subject: Load average for Emacs on SCO Unix 3.2.2?
q: How can I get GNU Emacs 18.57 to show the load average on SCO Unix 3.2v2.0? What type are the kernel's load averages?
a: Why dig through the kernel at all? Just call display-time. It puts the time on the mode line and the load average too, and it works fine on SCO. Read what Emacs already ships with.

subject: E-mail Privacy
q: A fired employee's e-mail memo might be needed as evidence. Is it legal or ethical for the sysadmin to restore their e-mail from backup and read it, or does the person still have rights to it?
a: Treat e-mail and files like an employee's desk: the company owns them, but if it led people to believe they were private, a privacy suit could stick. So publish a memo saying files aren't private. Sigh, get a lawyer and your policy straight before touching backups.

subject: Question about Internet access
q: What benefit would Internet access bring a large nationwide trucking distributor, and how does a company get connected?
a: Not much, and the Internet can't be used for business purposes; it's for research and education. Sysadmins and developers swap ideas and problems on it. You could use it for e-mail gateways, but don't trust sensitive business traffic to it. Know where you are.

subject: AIAI TR Report Request
q: How do I order a technical report, AIAI TR-65 "Survey of related AI projects", from the University of Edinburgh's AIAI?
a: Phone their enquiries number, (031) 650 2732, to learn the exact charge first. Then send a cheque or money order in sterling, payable to the University of Edinburgh, to AIAI Publications at the Artificial Intelligence Applications Institute, 80 South Bridge, Edinburgh EH1 1HN. Not hard.

subject: poetry analysis, pattern recogn.
q: I need to find differences between versions of a very long poem, ignoring insignificant ones like spelling variations and differing line lengths, preferably with a rule file. Is there software for that?
a: Use SNOBOL or SPITBOL. Vanilla SNOBOL4 is public domain, with plenty of sample programs, on Simtel20. The full SNOBOL4+ from Catspaw costs $95. A plain diff was never going to cut it, which any idiot with pattern matching experience knows.

subject: Natural language processing using genetic algorithms or neural nets?
q: Can anyone give a bibliography on applying genetic algorithms or neural nets to learning to interpret natural language, going from free text to a conceptual representation?
a: Look at Lee et al. on a symbolic/connectionist script applier (Cognitive Science Society 1989) and on learning distributed representations of conceptual knowledge (UCLA-AI-89-13). Also Miikkulainen on sequential paraphrasing of script-based stories (IJCNN-89) and extended backpropagation (IJCNN-88). Now go read them.

subject: overtraining backprop
q: Does anyone know good references giving a technical, mathematical description of overtraining in backprop? Hecht-Nielsen says the underlying cause is unknown.
a: The cause is the decision to find one "optimal" weight set measured on the training data. Plenty of weight sets do nearly as well, and you should average results over all the plausible ones. Any book on Bayesian statistics explains it, though none is newbie-friendly. Go read one.

subject: CGs on NN
q: How do people use conjugate gradient to minimize a neural net error function when the error function isn't known in advance? How do you get the Hessian H and h?
a: You don't compute the Hessian at all. Conjugate gradient here means approximating conjugate directions with a dynamic update, based on total error and the partial derivatives per weight, which you get by backprop. Read the conjugate-gradient section in Numerical Recipes.

subject: Help: Neural Nets/Cell-Automata/Dynamic Systems ...
q: I want to learn about computing with neural networks, cellular automata and dynamic systems, but my CS degree is weak on theory. Can anyone recommend books to build the background?
a: For cellular automata, get Cellular Automata Machines by Toffoli and Margolus, MIT Press, a good intro to CA and physical modeling. Then Theory and Applications of Cellular Automata, edited by Wolfram, which is heavier reading. Do some actual reading for once.

subject: bibliographic citation needed
q: What is the full citation for Hornik, Stinchcombe and White's paper Multi-layer feedforward networks are universal approximators?
a: You had authors and title right. It's Neural Networks, vol 2, number 5, 1989, pages 359-366. Next time use the library you're so keen on.

subject: Schools for AI&Neural-nets
q: Which schools should a friend with an MS apply to for a PhD in neural networks and AI?
a: The 1988 neural network society journal lists some: University of Tennessee, Boston University, Brown, Johns Hopkins, Caltech, Carnegie Mellon psychology, and MIT. There are many others. Go look at the research center directory instead of asking the net.

subject: shells & Windows
q: I'm looking for expert system shells that run under Microsoft Windows. Level 5 Object is the only one I can think of. Can anyone name others?
a: Neuron Data's Nexpert/Object runs under Windows. Inference's ART-IM/Windows is supposedly due within half a year, and it's the fast one. Most of the rest are toys that don't scale. Sigh, read a trade rag once in a while.

subject: pdp-11/55
q: Did anyone ever have a PDP-11/45 with some MOS or bipolar RAM in place of the core? Did it make much difference?
a: Read the time(1) manual page, it's been there since v7. On a PDP-11 the execution time depends on what kind of memory the program lands in, and user time in MOS is often half what it is in core. Not exactly obscure.

subject: VLSI Implementation of ECC
q: Does anyone have a fast method for encoding Hamming check bits in a CMOS VLSI design? We use a chain of transmission gates for the parity bits, and want something around 30-40ns in 3 micron technology.
a: Use a parity tree, not a chain. One 1Mb ROM with 64-bit word ECC did 33-bit parity in two levels of dual-rail pass-transistor XOR gates with sense amps, about 10 nsec in 1.5 micron CMOS. Read the ISSCC paper instead of daisy-chaining gates like a beginner.

subject: Tightly-coupled, multi-processor UNIX systems?
q: Has anyone built a tightly-coupled multiprocessor UNIX where one processor runs the kernel and the others send it system calls? Where can I find references?
a: Purdue did it by replacing the SBI terminator on a VAX 780 with a second CPU: the master runs most of the kernel, the slave runs user processes. Gould reused the code for their Powernode. Also look up the CMU Mach paper from Usenix. Master/slave is an old idea.

subject: How fast are your disks?
q: Why does Unix seem limited to about 30 disk I/Os a second on random access, and are there reasonably priced systems that do better?
a: It's just seek plus rotational delay plus transfer. A 20 ms drive gets you around 30 per second, a 40 ms one about 20. Overlapping seeks, multiple disks and bigger blocks help. Not a law of Computer Science, it's physics.

subject: Where to archive admins post
q: Where should an FTP site admin post a notice that a package is now available, especially when no newsgroup matches well or it fits ten groups?
a: For MS-DOS applications, post to comp.binaries.ibm.pc.archives, period. Otherwise crosspost with reasonable coverage. What counts as reasonable is the moderator's judgement and experience. Not a perfect answer, but there it is.

subject: Followup-To: in comp.archives articles
q: Why does comp.archives put the Newsgroups line into Followup-To instead of the original Followup-To header on reposted articles?
a: Bug in the program. It was supposed to use the original Followup-To line but the header name was misspelled as "Follup-To". Which suggests "foul up" to me. Fixed now.

subject: How much of 2bsd src could be "free?"
q: How much of 2BSD source could be made free, like what's happening with 4.3BSD to 4.4BSD?
a: Alas, not much. Bits of the kernel, mostly networking, and some apps like ftp, rsh and login are ported from liberated 4.3 sources. Even 4.4 isn't free of AT&T code, and PDP-11 folk can't afford lawyers. Sigh.

subject: rx, dz, kermit
q: On my 2.10BSD system the DZ11 lines don't work: echo to /dev/tty00 hangs, and ps shows ? for the tty of their gettys. The DL11 lines work. What's wrong?
a: That's modem control. The DZ11 honors modem signals, so open() hangs until it gets carrier, and getty shows ? since it never opened the device. For hard lines you need DTR out and CD in, not just pins 2, 3 and 7. Jumper them in the DB25.

subject: Question re inodes
q: Why does the 2.10 BSD file system use 64 byte inodes but only 21 of the 40 address bytes, with just 4 direct blocks, instead of using the leftover space for more direct blocks?
a: Because 2.9BSD shipped with that wart, and fixing it meant changing the file system. Conversion tools would need heavy testing, so we talked ourselves out of it. Using those blocks would be reasonable, and while you're at it, rip out the 3-byte inode compression. Not rocket science, just tedious.

subject: Possible "lseek()" bug
q: Is it a bug that System V 3.1 lseek() doesn't return a negative value when given a negative offset?
a: No, that's what it's supposed to do. The manual page for lseek says a non-negative file pointer value is returned on success, otherwise -1 and errno is set. Read the man page before you call something a bug.

subject: vi(1) bug - defunct processes
q: On System V/386 3.2.1, every time I pass part of a file through a filter with ! in vi, it leaves a defunct process that can't be killed until I exit vi. Is this a known bug?
a: Yes, it's an old bug. It was in Microport and is on the SVR3.2 source tape, so of course AT&T ships it. A workaround on ISC is to run something like :!ls afterward, which makes vi do the wait calls and clears the zombies.

subject: lint pass2 error
q: Running a big program through lint on SVR2 gives "lint pass2 error: Too many names". What does it mean and how do I work around it?
a: An array of source file names overflowed; it's 150 elements in vanilla SVR2 and SVR3.0. Either recompile lint with bigger NSZ and FSZ, or run lint -c on each file and then lint *.ln. Sigh, tiny fixed tables, the classic.

subject: Parallel Parsing?
q: Does anyone know of theoretical or practical work on parsing context-free languages with parallel algorithms?
a: Anton Nijholt made quite a study of it. Best reference is probably An Annotated Bibliography on Parallel Parsing, Memoranda Informatica 89-67, 1989, University of Twente. Go read it before asking the net again.

subject: Lexers in YACC?
q: How can I use a first-stage YACC grammar as a filter between the lexer and the parser to handle non-LALR(1) parts, given that C has no coroutines to make the first stage return tokens?
a: Don't. Queue the tokens, insert magic tokens that make the grammar LALR(1), then call the second stage. Often lex with right-context rules or start states is enough anyway. Look into those first.

subject: Hash specifics
q: How do I build a hash function with a minimal table size and minimal collisions for a known set of strings, such as the 386 opcodes?
a: That's perfect hashing, and it's been studied for years. Algorithms exist but they're all very slow. Start with Cichelli's minimal perfect hash functions paper in CACM, January 1980. Go read a journal instead of endlessly tweaking parameters.

subject: YACC, going the other way
q: Is there a YACC-like tool that goes the other way and generates strings from a BNF grammar? Has anyone done this cleanly?
a: Use Prolog. A BNF written in Prolog is an executable recognizer, and swapping the low-level test rules for generators turns it into a generator. Attributed grammars for test data generation are also a known technique. Do your homework.

subject: .HQX on Unix or Dos ?
q: How do I decode a Macintosh .HQX file under Unix or DOS?
a: Sigh. .hqx files are ASCII-encoded like uuencoded ones, made by BinHex on the Mac. Grab mcvert from sumex.stanford.edu, info-mac/unix/mcvert. It's BSD source code, so you'll have to compile it yourself.

subject: Question about patents and copyrights on algorithms...
q: If an algorithm is patented or copyrighted, how much of it can programmers use? Can we write a version without its tricks, and why copyright it at all, as with LZW in GIF?
a: Algorithms can't be copyrighted. Software implementations of them can, but not the algorithms themselves. Sigh, basic stuff, and it comes up every week.

subject: What is LZFG?
q: What is the LZFG compression method, and where can I find papers describing it?
a: The reference is Fiala and Greene, Data Compression with Finite Windows, CACM 32,4 (1989). Variants showed up in portable zip 0.8 and LHA 2.12. Oh, and it's patented, so mind that before you go using it.

subject: Clipper 5 and COM1: ???
q: Can a Clipper 5 routine read data from the RS232 serial port of a PC (COM1 through COM4)?
a: Writing to the port is easy from Clipper, but receiving is best done at interrupt level, so Clipper alone won't cut it. Find a public domain or shareware C library, or buy a commercial one. Telepathy from Extrasensory Software seems to be the favorite. Don't reinvent it.

subject: Long Transactions
q: Can anybody point me to publications and recent work on long transactions in databases?
a: Look at "Concurrency Control in Advanced Database Applications" in ACM Computing Surveys, Vol. 23, No. 3, September 1991. It discusses long transactions. Go use a library; that's what they're for.

subject: Wish: Windowing software for CLIPPER
q: Does anyone know of a windowing package for Clipper, for menus and data entry?
a: Why bother? The built-in DBEDIT and ACHOICE functions, plus judicious use of SAVE SCREEN TO and RESTORE SCREEN FROM, give you the same windowing effect. Everyone wants to buy a package for what the language already does.

subject: Who uses Z39.50 Information Retrieval Application Protocol?
q: Does anyone know of any relational database systems that conform to the ANSI Z39.50 protocol? So far I only know of WAIS.
a: Don't count on it. You could bolt Z39.50 onto an RDB, but relational databases don't support the access full-text retrieval needs, so performance would stink. Z39.50 came from the library crowd and doesn't do generalized text retrieval yet.

subject: FoxBase 2.1.1 Locks Up Under Xenix
q: FoxBase 2.1.1 under SCO Xenix and Unix freezes all sessions when a fourth copy of an application with four databases and several indexes is started alongside three running ones. Any ideas?
a: Probably a deadlock from running out of system file resources. Relink the system with linkkit and raise the files parameters, such as maximum files open and locked; I just doubled them all. SCO's support said to re-read the manual. Typical.

subject: Foxbase DOS->XENIX
q: Has anyone ported a FoxBase system from MS-DOS to FoxBase under SCO XENIX 386? Any quirks I should be aware of?
a: A beta tester ported a 200K-source app with 10+ databases and it went without a hitch. Quirks were reportedly fixed by SCO, though multi-user records weren't getting unlocked before 2.1.1. The sys() free-memory function is gone, since it's pointless in multi-user. Read the manual.

subject: Accessing ORACLE from a diskless workstation
q: How can I connect to an Oracle database on a server from a diskless workstation without the password showing on the command line, where ps -ef displays it?
a: Set the TWO_TASK environment variable, e.g. setenv TWO_TASK T:depot:A in csh. Then just type sqlplus and Oracle prompts for your login name and password. Putting passwords on the command line is amateur hour.

subject: Need DBase III Report Help
q: How can I print the odd pages of a 100 page dBase III+ report first, then flip the fanfold paper and print the even pages? Is there a simple way?
a: Not with the report writer, it can't be cajoled into anything out of the ordinary. Use SET ALTERNATE to send the report to a file and work from there, or write custom code to generate it your way. Sigh.

subject: dBase/FoxBase question
q: How do I detect a control character keypress in dBase, in FoxBase under SCO? WAIT ' ' TO var gives me 0 for all control characters.
a: Use INKEY() instead of WAIT. The manual says it picks up non-printable characters too. Loop until it returns nonzero, and you get the ASCII decimal value, which you can convert with chr(). Works fine on SCO. Read the manual, it's in there.

subject: Informix DBMENU variable
q: How do I set DBMENU in Informix SQL so that I can run isql with just -u instead of giving the database and 'main' menu on the command line?
a: You had the idea right, you just dropped a letter. Set DBMENU to the first menu you want, and 'main' is the default anyway. Then run isql databasename -ur. The r means User_menu Run. Read the manual next time.

subject: DBase source code
q: I heard Borland is going to release some of the dBase source code because a judge wants to stop a monopoly on DOS databases. Is there anybody who knows if, when and where I can get the sources?
a: Rumor mangled, as usual. To get antitrust clearance for buying Ashton-Tate, Borland agreed to drop the legal attempts to control the dBase language. Their copyright on their own implementation stays. No source for you, but clone writers can stop worrying about lawsuits.

subject: Clipper 'S87 TYPE MISMATCH
q: In Clipper S87, I have a database containing only deleted records that is not yet packed. A SELECT JUNKY sometimes gives a TYPE MISMATCH error, but SELECT 8 works. What could be wrong?
a: That's not Clipper's fault, it's something in your code. Always reference files by alias. You probably lost the alias because the file got closed. Test with @ 0,0 SAY JUNKY->(USED()) before the SELECT, and make sure JUNKY isn't a string variable. Trace your code, it's not magic.

subject: index date field in Clipper 87'
q: In Clipper Summer 87, I did INDEX ON DTOS(DATE_FIELD) and printed records from an array, but they came out in the order I keyed them, not sorted by date. What's wrong?
a: The index expression looks fine. Check that you actually opened the index file when you print, and that it's the controlling index if you have several. Also, loading everything into an array just to print is unnecessary. Check the basics.

subject: R&R Report Writer help needed
q: In R&R Report Writer, how do I conditionally total a field, such as counting all invoices that have been paid and also all that haven't, when a query filter won't do?
a: Make two calculated fields, one for paid and one for unpaid. Each uses iif on dtepaid to give 1 or 0, like iif(dtepaid>blank,1,0). Then put a Total Count on each. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: General ESQL question.
q: In embedded SQL on RTI INGRES 5.0, can I make the select list a variable so I can choose attributes at run time, instead of selecting every attribute?
a: You need embedded dynamic SQL, and INGRES 5.x doesn't support it. RTI says 6.x does, but that's unconfirmed. Embedded QUEL in INGRES 5 does allow that kind of dynamic retrieve, so code it in EQUEL and switch to ESQL later.

subject: SQL-schema to C generation
q: Is there a stand-alone tool to turn an SQL schema into C declarations, or can awk do it?
a: If you're on Ingres, use DCLGEN. It generates C structure declarations for any table, command line driven, so you can script it. Make the table in Ingres and port the output to your DBMS. Awk, meh.

subject: Rename Database in Informix
q: Is there an easy way to rename a database in Informix SQL 2.1? I can rename the database_name.dbs directory, but I suspect the DB dictionary tables have hard-coded full pathnames.
a: Usually it's as simple as renaming the .dbs directory. Only if you put tables elsewhere with CREATE TABLE ... IN [pathname] do you need to fix the dirpath column in systables with an UPDATE, carefully. Check the catalog before whining that it's broken.

subject: dBase/Clipper
q: My dBase III+ index on (1-H/AB) works even when AB is 0, but Clipper dies with a division by zero. How do I avoid it?
a: Guard the division: INDEX ON iif(ab=0,0,1-h/ab) TO BA, replacing the 0 with whatever suits you. Sheesh, dBase III+ letting a divide by zero slide without a peep is the real bug here.

subject: Oracle Primary Key Constraint
q: Oracle SQL doesn't enforce a primary key constraint, so I can insert duplicate ids. How do I make sure the primary key is upheld on inserts and updates?
a: As of V6 that's correct, the kernel doesn't enforce most constraints, only NULL/NOT NULL. Some of the tools do. Rumor says V7 will. Meanwhile a unique index will do the job. Nice database, huh.

subject: database machines?
q: What can you tell me about Teradata database processors? Has anyone used them, or where can I read up on them?
a: Phone Teradata for brochures if you want colorful marketing materials. For substance, ask database machine researchers, such as Andy Lowry at Columbia. The best book is "Database Computers: Principles, Architectures, and Techniques" by S. Y. W. Su from McGraw-Hill, 1988. Britton Lee also builds custom database processors.

subject: What the hell is Codebase???
q: What is CodeBase? I heard it's a set of C functions that let you program in the xBASE style.
a: Yes, a set of C functions for manipulating xBase and index files, with screen handling utilities. Codebase++ is the C++ version and supports dBASE IV .MDX indexes. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: Clipper's SET RELATION question
q: When using SET RELATION in Clipper and I issue a DELETE, does it also mark the record in the related file as deleted?
a: No. Relations just link files, so deleting a transaction record doesn't touch the customer record it points to. You can delete both easily if you want, but the system won't assume it. Any idiot would hate it if it did.

subject: SQL standards document
q: Where can I get the current ANSI SQL standard, or the syntax for IBM's SQL/DS and DB2? I need to parse SQL for those systems.
a: Get the SQL Reference manuals for DB2 and SQL/DS from IBM; that's the authoritative source. The ANSI standard comes from ANSI itself for around $50. Since you're international, ISO matters more, and its SQL standard is very close. This is a FAQ, you know.

subject: Ingres and referential integrities
q: Why doesn't Ingres provide referential integrity as part of the data definition?
a: My guess is performance. In hierarchical databases referential integrity comes almost free with the model, but in a relational database checking it is real computational work. An IBM techie said even without it, relational lost a factor of about three. Think about it.

subject: Compatibility of Clipper Summer '87 w/ Clipper 5.0
q: Will a program that compiles under Clipper Summer '87 compile and run correctly under Clipper 5.0, or will I need major changes?
a: Mostly you can just compile it. Fixed bugs and standardized behavior will bite if you relied on the odd behavior, and your own functions may collide with new names. Third-party libraries need updating, and there's no NDX driver yet. Upgrade immediately and don't look back.

subject: Dbase IV compiler
q: Will a program written and compiled in dBASE IV run outside the dBASE IV environment?
a: No. The dBASE IV compiler is a pseudo-compiler producing .dbo files that only run inside dBASE IV. Ashton-Tate has announced a Professional Compiler that makes standalone .exe files, but it isn't available yet. Marketing again.

subject: DBASE III HELP
q: dBASE III keeps giving "Syntax Error in Field Expression" when I print my report. All my field expressions are date or character fields. Could a character field that starts with digits and ends with letters cause it?
a: Look for an empty column in the report template, a skinny one with no heading or expression, and delete it. Also, field names must start with a letter, and III says "syntax error" for nearly any bad expression, mismatched parentheses and memory variables included. Check each one.

subject: Fax modems v/s "regular" modems ...
q: What is the essential difference between regular modems and fax modems? If I have a 9600 baud modem, can I use it to send faxes?
a: No. Fax uses different modulation: V.21 for negotiation, then V.27ter, V.29 or V.17 for images, while data modems use Bell 103, V.22, V.32 and so on. Fax is also synchronous, so the modem must strip start and stop bits. Only third-party services like CompuServe do the faxing for you.

subject: Class 2 protocol info wanted
q: Where can I get a copy of the proposed Class 2 fax protocol, hardcopy or preferably on line?
a: It's now in balloting within TIA as Standards Proposal SP-2388-A, so it's copyrighted. The only legal place to get it is TIA, through EIA Standards Sales. Don't expect it free on line. Sigh.

subject: Why FAX send-only?
q: Why are some computer FAX modems and software send-only? What's the technical difficulty in producing send and receive?
a: Transmit-only is much easier to build. You can modulate the signal with an 8-bit controller, but demodulating needs a DSP chip. That's the whole story; the vendors just cheap out.

subject: AT&T ISN system and self maintenance
q: AT&T maintenance on our ISN site is over $65,000 a year. Does AT&T offer a board repair or swap service so I could keep spares and fix a faulty AIM myself?
a: AT&T does time and materials support, which might do if repairs are rare. Also try their National Parts Sales Center at 1-800-222-PART: parts marked Customer Installed can be bought outright or swapped at a lower price. Not sure about ISN, so call and ask. Sigh.

subject: 10Base-T hubs
q: Are cheap passive 10Base-T hubs OK for a small network of about 30 nodes?
a: Passive isn't the issue. The cheap hubs from Asante, SMC and the like have no management and cut other corners. And don't believe the hype, everyone claims to be on 10Base-T but net managers I talk to aren't moving that fast.

subject: Netting via Ethernet 15pin-15pin
q: Can I connect two computers, a Symbolics 3650 and an Amiga with an A2065 ethernet card, directly through their DB-15 connectors, or do I need transceivers or a hub?
a: No way. The interface isn't symmetrical, so you need electronics in the middle. Use thinwire coax with terminators and BNC Tees if the Symbolics has a port, or buy a multiport transceiver. An ANC-10 AUI-AUI device costs about half as much. Read up on networking.

subject: DECserver multisessions through ISN
q: Can I get multiple simultaneous DECserver sessions (SET MULTISESSIONS ENABLE) from a PC connected through an AT&T ISN network over a COM port? If so, with what software?
a: Think of the ISN as a very fancy, very long RS232 cable. Your PC is effectively hardwired to the terminal server, and that's where the multiple sessions live. Enable multisessions on the server, then use a key sequence like BREAK-ESC to back out and pick another session. RTFM, though good luck finding it.

subject: Macs on Novell Advanced 2.15???
q: Can Macs on a Novell Advanced 2.15 network store executables on the server, use network printer spoolers, remote boot, and how well does it perform?
a: Executables on the server, yes. Printing works through NetWare for Macintosh queues, but only for LaserWriters and ImageWriters. Remote boot isn't provided. NetWare for Mac has been buggy for a year, so don't pay a dime until your dealer has ANW 2.15C and Mac VAP 1.1.

subject: Request: Fiber optic networking references
q: Can anyone point me to a good book, survey or standards document on fiber optic computer networking?
a: Codenoll puts out The Fiber Optic LAN Handbook, ISBN 0-9626933-3-2. They were giving it away at Networld '91. Free, so no excuse.

subject: Thinnet cable choices
q: Choosing between Belden 8259 (66% NVP) and 8219 (cellular polyethylene, 78% NVP) RG-58A/U for thinnet: will the second give more distance, and is it too stiff to handle?
a: Velocity of propagation isn't the critical factor; attenuation limits thin Ethernet length, so check those numbers. As for stiffness, one user says the foam-core stuff is actually less stiff than solid polyethylene. Kinks in coax are NOT good. Obvious, really.

subject: Cabletron vs. TCL
q: Does anybody have real-world experience with TCL network products compared with Cabletron? TCL offered a lower price for apparently equivalent products.
a: Both work very well. Cabletron transceivers cost a bit more but have activity LEDs, which help. Installation is about the same, though TCL is harder to mess up. Cabletron is about a quarter inch smaller on a cable in tight conduit. Hardly earth-shattering.

subject: Specification For NetBIOS Driver
q: Does anyone know where I can find the specification for writing a NetBIOS device driver?
a: NetBIOS isn't a device driver. It's a spec, IBM's original PC Net Tech Ref, with a different implementation for every network. If you have a network, a NetBIOS program probably came with it. Learn what it is before you try writing one.

subject: pt200 term. emulator over TCP/IP
q: Does anyone make a pt200 terminal emulator over TCP/IP for PCs on a Sytek network, to talk to a Prime?
a: If you have PC/TCP v2.03, TNGLASS works with any emulator loading as a DOS console driver, like ANSI.SYS. From 2.04, it also emulates BIOS serial services on INT 14. But the emulator itself, I can't supply. Go shopping.

subject: Connecting 3com to tcp/ip or ethernet
q: Has anyone connected a 3Com PC network to a Unix or Xenix network using TCP/IP or Ethernet? What problems come up?
a: First you have to get past XNS versus TCP. Drivers that load on demand are in the works to convert those packets. Expect a speed drop and likely a host gateway, which you pay for in speed but get back in functionality. Welcome to networking.

subject: Twisted pair (StarLan) to ThinNet
q: How can I bring ThinNet into a StarLan twisted pair network? The Synoptics adapters didn't work with the Dec stuff. Is the problem a lack of a twisted pair standard, and is LatticeNet the same as StarLan?
a: You're mixing two things up. StarLan is 1 megabit twisted pair, while Synoptics is 10 megabit, heading toward 10baseT, so they are not the same. Simplest fix is a thin Ethernet transceiver plugged into a 15-pin connector on the StarLan hub, with the thin machines on that.

subject: appletalk <-> cbx
q: How can I give an AppleTalk network four asynchronous connections to our PBX data switch? Is there a terminal server that speaks AppleTalk that I can hang off the network?
a: Shiva makes a NetSerial that does this. You plug any RS232 device into it and it shows up on the AppleTalk net. Users pick it in the Chooser. Runs about $300 mail order. Not exactly exotic, you know.

subject: NCSA TELNET / BANYAN
q: How can I run NCSA Telnet concurrently with Banyan Vines on the same PC? Telnet works until I log into the file server, then the network communication dies.
a: Get the NDIS driver patch 1W from Banyan, then the dis_pkt packet driver adapter from ftp.vax.com. That combination lets Vines and KA9Q or CUTCP run together on one workstation. Sigh, the secret is just patches, as usual.

subject: performance analysis of fddi routers
q: How does CPU speed, SPECmark and memory affect the performance of a high-speed IP router between FDDI and token rings? Would a 41.7 MHz box with 64 Mb beat a 25 MHz one with 32 Mb, and what calculations are involved?
a: SPEC wasn't designed for routing, and a 2x difference in CPU and RAM is small next to the real differences between FDDI hosts. The people who know won't tell you. The only real analysis is measuring, not sales hand waving.

subject: Wiring for FDDI
q: How should I wire an FDDI vertical building backbone so FDDI can later reach the desktop, with a wiring concentrator on each floor? Are concentrators available yet?
a: Contact AMP in Harrisburg for their fiber optic cabling catalog and guide. For concentrators, try Unisys, the only outfit I know of that has even announced a product. Announced, mind you, not shipped.

subject: Ethernet utilisation
q: I heard Ethernet's CSMA/CD access can't get past about 50-60% utilisation. Is there any evidence for or against that?
a: Hogwash. Van Jacobson and Mike Karels tuned the 4.3BSD TCP/IP code and got a bit over 8 megabits per second between plain Sun 3/50s, which is 80-85% from one host. They even crashed some VMS hosts that couldn't buffer it. Don't believe forgotten sources.

subject: Thick or Thin Ethernet?
q: I'm installing an OS/2 LAN for under 20 users, well within thin-net limits. The network specialist advised thick-net because BNC connections go bad. Is that worth the expense and hassle?
a: Depends on your environment. Thick is more robust because the cable doesn't run to the back of each machine to get yanked. If users are careful, thin is fine. Otherwise use thick or twisted pair with a hub. Well-made BNC ends beat those slidey-clippy transceiver connectors anyway.

subject: Help with Mac to Sun Ethernet connection.
q: Is EtherTalk an Ethernet driver or an AppleTalk one? Do I need it on a Mac IIsi to talk TCP/IP to a SparcStation, or should I use MacTCP?
a: EtherTalk is AppleTalk over Ethernet, so it's not what you want for TCP/IP. Use MacTCP. And yes, the Ethernet address in /etc/ethers looks correct, but check the card's ROM or the assigned numbers RFC. Sigh, read the docs.

subject: Cabling beteen BNC T-connector and workstation?!
q: Is it legitimate to run a fly-run cable between a thin Ethernet BNC T-connector and the workstation instead of attaching the T directly?
a: Don't. Beyond collision detection trouble, you no longer have 50 ohm impedance, which causes reflections and standing waves. One salesman did it with an analyzer and took down the whole thin-net segment. I recommend against it, HIGHLY.

subject: 1024 stations on 1 ethernet?
q: Is the 1024 stations limit on an ethernet active stations or adapter connections, and why? Do bridges give us 1024 on each side?
a: The limit comes from the collision backoff algorithm, which picks one of 1024 time slots. Past about 800 active devices things go foobar. A bridge starts the count over; a repeater doesn't. So yes, per segment. Read the spec.

subject: cheap-net
q: Is there a cheap, simple network for several PCs and maybe Atari STs, with file transfer and no central server?
a: Look at Lantastic from Artisoft, about $100 per node. Its proprietary network runs at a respectable speed, around 1 MB, and Ethernet or Cheapernet costs extra. Source code? Don't count on it.

subject: LAN Manager APIs
q: Is there a good book on programming for LAN Manager? Can the Microsoft C libraries be used with Turbo C++, and where do I find what each routine does?
a: Get the AT&T StarGroup LAN Manager API Programmer's Reference, or the Microsoft LAN Manager Programmer's Guide, wherever better computer books are sold. And yes, Turbo C++ works just fine with them. RTFM.

subject: XNS
q: Is there an RFC-like document describing XNS packets, and is the Xerox document XSIS-028112 listed in the BSD 4.3 ns man page the one?
a: Probably. XSIS 028112 gives the format for IDP, SPP, PEX and some others. The useful stuff like Mail and Filing isn't in it. Order it from somewhere within Xerox. Good luck prying the rest out of them.

subject: Remote access to Ethernet Novell Clients from Unix
q: Is there software that lets me remotely access PCs on my Ethernet running Novell from a Unix host?
a: Novell sells a TCP gateway, I believe. It lets one host on the TCP side reach the Netware at a time. That's all I've got, and it's hardly generous.

subject: NCSA telnet and tn3270
q: NCSA telnet's telbin.exe spews garbage on IBM PS/2s, though tn3270.exe runs but CRAY and VAX hosts don't understand its 3270 keyboard. Anyone solved this?
a: I've heard you need to set the BIOS option to yes in CONFIG.TEL for PS/2s. And tn3270 is a superset of telbin and can act as a vt102 instead, so check tnmode in CONFIG.TEL. Read the config file, for pity's sake.

subject: Problems with DEBETs and ARP
q: Some DEC DEBET bridges had the broadcast address in their forwarding tables and didn't always forward broadcasts, which broke ARP. Is there a rev level where this is fixed?
a: Rev D, a step down from your rev E, doesn't have the problem and answers RBMS correctly about registered multicast addresses. Rev F doesn't have it either, but it doesn't like being asked about registered multicast. Rev E is the broken one.

subject: netware and Vaxes
q: We want to move to NetWare to use data that lives on a VAX. How would NetWare work with a VAX, and is there a card for it?
a: Novell sells Netware VMS, which lets a VMS VAX act as a NetWare V2.0A file and print server. To the PCs it looks like any other server, and it uses standard DEC Ethernet hardware, so no special card. Read the product sheet.

subject: Ethernet Controller Chips
q: What are the relative merits of the Ethernet controller chips from Intel, AMD and NS? Does anyone else make similar products?
a: Only one data point here: AMD's Lance, the Am7990. It runs fine under a 32016, needs two chips plus a few passives and bus interface chips, takes little board space, and makes the software easy. Not a survey, but it beats asking vaguely.

subject: When to bridge?
q: What's the maximum optimal load on an Ethernet before you should think about bridging? I heard 15-20 percent utilisation is about the most you can expect before overload trouble.
a: Wrong question, kid. Collect usage data and plot it. The moment the trend points upward, put in a bridge on an experimental basis. Then when you really need one, you and your staff already know how to do it.

subject: recommendations wanted
q: Where can I get TCP/IP for SCO Unix 3.2, and where is a good place to buy ethernet cards?
a: You can't yet. SCO is developing its own version, which isn't ready, and it will support 3Com and Western Digital cards. Excelan promises a port for their card a few weeks after SCO ships something usable. Vaporware for now, so wait. Nobody answered about card vendors.

subject: tcp/ip terminal servers with slip support?
q: Which TCP/IP terminal servers support SLIP, for connecting a bank of V.32 modems? I know Cisco has one.
a: The Annex II terminal server has SLIP and full IP routing support. Certainly, and it's hardly a secret.

subject: writing from buffers
q: Can vi write out the contents of a named buffer? Trying ":'aw filename" doesn't work.
a: No. 'a is a mark, not a named buffer, and in ex the double quote starts a comment. Named buffers are vi-mode only, so you can't use them in :w. Edit the new file and put the buffer into it. Learn the difference.

subject: Editor design, information sources?
q: Has anyone read good design texts or published papers on editor design, especially extensible editors? I don't want code examples.
a: Read the paper Stallman wrote on editor design, probably for his PhD at MIT. It covers buffering, windowing and binding of functions. Whatever you think of Emacs, it should be required reading before you write an editor. Do try to find a copy, kid.

subject: vi this file dammit
q: How can I make vi quit if the file I name doesn't exist, instead of helpfully creating a new one? Is there a vi command for that?
a: Skip vi's internals and do it in the shell: alias vv 'test -f \!:1 || vi \!:*'. It only checks the first argument, but you get the idea. Honestly, it's not hard.

subject: Yet another vi question
q: How do I start vi on a file and have it read in a template file on entry? I tried vi +'r template.rpt' myreport and it thinks I'm editing two files and core dumps.
a: Try vi "+:r template.rpt" myreport. Or skip vi's feature set entirely and write a tiny shell script that copies the template to the file and then runs vi on it. Amazing what a little quoting fixes.

subject: VI showmatch option
q: I'm using vi to type programs in a Lisp-like language that uses [ and ] as delimiters. Showmatch only works for ( and ). How do I get it for brackets too?
a: Get a newer vi. On the System V port I use, % matches parens, brackets and even braces. Sigh, your vintage version is just old. Go hunt down a current one.

subject: vi: search for or go to a line not of length n
q: In vi, how can I search for a line that isn't 61 characters long, or invert a search, like finding the next line that doesn't begin with a capital M? I'm trying to fix a mangled uuencoded file.
a: No easy way to do the length check in vi, so use awk or perl like a sane person. For lines not starting with M, /^[^M] does it, and :g or :v will run ex commands on matches. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: SunOS 4.1 & vi
q: What's the difference between the SunOS 4.1 vi and the old SunOS 4.0.x vi, and is there any way to persuade vi not to use tabs to indent?
a: The sys5 vi reads TERMINFO instead of TERMCAP, so you have to run the termcap-to-terminfo converter. To avoid tabs, :set tabstop=1234, so vi never generates one, though it gets mad at tabs in your file. Or just filter through expand.

subject: a question about vi
q: When I define too many vi macros, vi gets very confused. I suspect I'm running out of some internal table. Is there a solution?
a: Check whether you're editing in your HOME directory. Then your home .exrc gets read twice, once as the home file and once as the current directory's, which blows out your macro space. Setting noremap helped. Learn your tools.

subject: Can you write complex vi macros?
q: Why can't I put more than one undo-able command, like a replace and a yank, in a vi macro? I get 'Can't yank inside global/macro'.
a: Vi has a known bug with the unnamed buffer. Some blame the squeezing to fit on a PDP-11, since the innards share a buffer under horribly complex rules, so odd sequences blow up. Split it into smaller macros.

subject: Why oh Why "Cannot put inside global/macro"
q: Why does the vi macro 'map q dd1GP' give the error 'cannot put inside global/macro', and is there a workaround for moving lines around in my .newsrc?
a: Known bug, and it's been there forever. Workaround: learn ex commands. Use the move command instead of delete and put, like map q :m0^V^M to send a line to the top. Sigh, RTFM.

subject: High Performance Computing course
q: I'm planning a graduate course on high performance computing. Is there a decent textbook covering computer architecture for high performance machines?
a: Try Ibbett's The Architecture of High Performance Computers (1982). It's a good comparative look at the machines that held the high ground, through the CRAY-1, with the design tradeoffs. Hwang and Briggs drags and is dry; use it only as a reference. Pick a better book.

subject: Need some info on Northeastern University
q: What's Northeastern University like for a Masters in Computer Engineering: difficulty, student life, housing, the coop program? I heard it's a Christian Scientist school.
a: You heard wrong. It's a private non-denominational school in Boston, and the TV program isn't theirs. The engineering center is fairly new and the school is well regarded for EE and CE. The coop is excellent, and on-campus housing is sparse, so rent off-campus.

subject: How do I tell freemacs my screen size?
q: Can I tell freemacs about non-standard screen sizes, other than the 43 and 58 line EGA modes? I want to use my card's 44x132 mode.
a: In theory you needn't. Freemacs reads the EGA BIOS for the screen size and uses the whole screen. If your card is EGA BIOS compatible, put it in 44x132 mode and it'll cope. Otherwise set the screen columns and max screen line in the init code yourself.

subject: Can scrolling be changed?
q: Can scrolling be changed in GNU Emacs? It repaints the screen and centers the cursor when scrolling is needed. Can it scroll one line at a time like a regular terminal?
a: Yes. Set scroll-step with (setq scroll-step 1). By default it's 0, which always recenters point. Try scrolling by one line, and if that fails, point is centered. Use C-h v next time instead of asking the whole net.

subject: ^Z
q: Control-Z won't suspend MicroEmacs 3.9e on my Sun 3/60. Did I install it wrong, or is it a key binding problem?
a: Control-Z is bound to something else by default, resizing the window I think. Put bind-to-key suspend-emacs ^Z in your .emacsrc and you get job control back. ^X-D is also the default suspend binding. Read the bindings.

subject: Does emacs provide programming environment?
q: Does GNU Emacs give any advantage over vi when programming in C? What would it do for me?
a: Are you kidding? It has a C mode that indents for you and catches punctuation errors, and it blinks the matching brackets. M-x compile puts error messages in a window, and you can run a shell or the debugger inside it. It justifies itself.

subject: name "emacs" owned by anyone?
q: Does anybody own the name emacs? Could a commercial vendor release a product named emacs?
a: Obviously they can. At least two already have: CCA and Unipress. This comes up every few months, and the answer is still that nobody stopped them.

subject: Examples of use of x-create-x-window and x-pop-up-window?
q: Does anyone have examples of using x-create-x-window or x-pop-up-window in GNU Emacs? Has anyone written Emacs Lisp code that creates new X windows?
a: They aren't user functions and shouldn't be used. They're the obsolete way of creating the initial window, and are disabled once it's up. RMS has rewritten the X interface for multiple windows. Stop poking at internals.

subject: How to kill a rectangular block using micro-emacs
q: Emacs has kill-rectangle and yank-rectangle. Are there equivalent commands in MicroEMACS 3.10, or macros to do it?
a: They ship with it. Hit F8 for the page loader, then B for the BLOCK page, and the shifted function keys do rectangular cut and paste. The macro code is in bpage.cmd. It's all in the standard command files, so look before you ask.

subject: Building Emacs for Apollo; runs sloooooow
q: GNU Emacs 18.51 built fine on my Apollo DN660 but runs incredibly slowly, taking minutes per command and eating CPU. Any ideas?
a: Works fine here with 18.48 on SR 9.7. Remote file locking is slow, and Emacs doesn't know about Apollo's own locks, so I built without file locking. Check ring or remote node response too, using ringlog or dspst. Try that first.

subject: Can't get GNUS to cancel my articles.
q: GNUS fails to cancel my article with 'Search failed: ^J^J' when I press C in the Subject buffer. What am I doing wrong?
a: Nothing you typed. Your .el files were byte-compiled with an earlier GNU Emacs. Re-byte-compile gnuspost.el, and everything else while you're at it. This comes up every time someone upgrades Emacs and forgets.

subject: Gnu emacs on Sun 4.0 OS?
q: Has anyone gotten Gnu Emacs working under Sun's SunOS 4.0, where the crt file changed for shared libraries? Linking with -Bstatic didn't help.
a: Works fine on 18.50. Set START_FILES to pre-crt0.o and /lib/crt0.o, and link with both -n and -Bstatic, since SunOS 4.0 defaults to dynamic linking. You only did half of it. Do the whole job.

subject: Cray version of Emacs?
q: Has anyone ported any flavor of Emacs to the Cray? Vi is the only real editor on our Crays and I dislike it.
a: MicroEMACS 3.9e and 3.9p have been run on UNICOS successfully. Don't expect the full GNU monster, but it beats whining about vi.

subject: GnuEmacs Query: scribe.el?
q: Has anyone written a Scribe Mode for GnuEmacs?
a: Emacs 18.33 includes a scribe mode. Look at what ships with the thing before asking the whole net.

subject: dired sorting by date
q: How can I sort a dired buffer by date in Emacs? I've checked the manual and the elisp archives and found nothing.
a: Set dired-listing-switches to "-algot" and let ls do the sorting. Sorting columns with sort utilities and month names is the hard way. Sigh, one line of elisp, and you searched the archives for that.

subject: Termcaps in Gnu Emacs
q: How can I use my own termcap for a terminal in Gnu Emacs without editing /etc/termcap? It seems to look only at TERM.
a: It already honors TERMCAP. If TERMCAP doesn't start with a slash, it's taken as the entry itself. If it starts with a slash, it's the termcap file name. So setenv TERMCAP to your private ~/.termcap path. RTFM.

subject: Gnu backup files
q: How do I tell GNU Emacs not to make a backup file, the file~ copy, when I save?
a: Set the variable make-backup-files to nil. For just the current buffer, do M-x set-variable RET make-backup-files RET nil RET. It's in the manual under Backup Files, which you evidently didn't bother to read.

subject: Can't build GNU emacs on DECstation 2100 under ULTRIX 3.1
q: I can't build GNU emacs 18.55 on a DECstation 2100 under ULTRIX 3.1 and get errors. Has anybody got a solution?
a: Sigh. A DECstation is NOT a VAX, no matter who sells it. Use s-bsd4-3.h and m-pmax.h in the config. Built it that way with no problems. Try reading the config files before asking the net.

subject: GNUS. Can one restart a suspension?
q: I suspended GNUS with z, left the workstation idle for several hours, then typed g in the Newsgroup buffer and got "Process NNTP not running...". Is that supposed to happen?
a: Sigh. Your idle time crossed a threshold, and nntpd gave up on you, packed it in, and closed the connection. It's not GNUS' fault. The server hung up on you, so stop blaming the newsreader.

subject: InfoTex
q: I tried to print the GNU Emacs manual from the infotex sources, but TeX wanted .tex files. How do I convert the infotex files into TeX sources?
a: You don't use the info files. Use the original texinfo sources, with texinfo.tex and texindex. In the Emacs man/ directory, just say 'tex emacs' and you get a dvi file. TeX doesn't care about extensions. Make texindex and re-TeX it for the index.

subject: micrognu or freemacs ?
q: I want an Emacs on my PCs that's close to GNU Emacs. What features does Freemacs have compared to micrognu?
a: Freemacs is 100% 8088 assembler, so fast but unportable. It's programmable in MINT, a funky but real language, not TRAC. The killer is the 64K file size limit, which decides it for most people. It was written to the TECO Emacs manual, not GNU, so don't expect miracles.

subject: Micro emacs
q: I want to hack an editor into having groupware functionality and need a public domain emacs. Is there one called micro emacs, and where do I get it?
a: Yes, MicroEmacs exists and runs on MS-DOS PCs and Sun 4s alike. It has an extension language, nothing like Lisp, but it does the job. One person got it by FTP from durer.cme.nist.gov. Go fetch it yourself.

subject: Building GNU emacs
q: I'm building a 1985-dated GNU emacs on 4.3 BSD and make dies on process.c at a function declaration. Is this version just too old?
a: Yes. Three years of concerted development by a lot of capable people has gone into Emacs since that tape was cut. Scrap what you've got and get the current version, 18.51. You'll save yourself a lot of trouble. Honestly, a 1985 tape?

subject: Jove distribution missing ttystate.h
q: I'm compiling Jove 4.12 on a Gould and the distribution is missing ttystate.h. Where can I find it?
a: Your 4.12 tarball is broken. Grab Jove 4.13 by anonymous ftp from cs.rochester.edu, pub/jove.tar.4.13.Z. If IPROCS won't compile, remove its #define from tune.h. Honestly, check for a newer version before posting.

subject: Shell-mode trouble in GNUmacs
q: In GNU Emacs 18.38 on BSD 4.2, M-x shell sometimes warns 'no access to tty; thus no job control in this shell'. How do I fix it?
a: Your pseudo-tty's are probably screwed up, which was the cause at our site. Use crpty(8) to create new ones, and read pty(4) to see how they work. Sigh, check your ptys before blaming Emacs.

subject: A regexp for blank lines
q: In GNU Emacs 18.44, how can I write elisp to remove lines matching a regexp, including blank lines? Using ^$ loops forever at the end of the buffer.
a: Use the built-in delete-matching-lines instead of rolling your own loop. For blank lines specifically, just remove every occurrence of newline-newline. Honestly, check the function list before reinventing wheels.

subject: help
q: In GNU Emacs 18.54 on a Sun 3/60, when scrolling through a file the bottom mode line scrolls up the screen and then back down. What variable fixes this?
a: It's not a bug. It's just the cheapest way for emacs to scroll given your termcap. The Sun console lacks the scrolling region capability (termcap cs) that vt100s have. Read SUN-SUPPORT in the emacs etc directory for improving your termcap.

subject: GNU emacs and the cntl-h key...
q: In GNU Emacs 18.54 over NCSA telnet, Ctrl-H is interpreted as backspace/rubout. Changing the erase character in the NCSA configuration doesn't help. Anyone else seen this?
a: Yes. In Telnet the Ctrl-H and backspace keys are coupled, so you can't redefine one without the other. Best with vanilla Telnet is to make backspace send DEL and use Ctrl-backspace for Ctrl-H to the host. You delete more than you ask for help anyway.

subject: Is there a cleaner way to check for a narrowed buffer?
q: Is there a cleaner way in Emacs Lisp to check for a narrowed buffer than widening and comparing point-min and point-max inside unwind-protect?
a: Simplest: a buffer is narrowed if point-min isn't 1, so (/= 1 (point-min)) does it, though that ignores narrowing only at the end. And for save and restore of narrowing, use save-restriction, and save-excursion for point and mark. Learn the special forms.

subject: Crypt
q: Is there an easy way in GnuEmacs to edit encrypted files, like vi -x file does?
a: Get crypt.el from tut.cis.ohio-state.edu, in pub/gnu/emacs/elisp-archives/misc/crypt.el.Z. It handles encrypted, compacted or compressed files with style and grace. Sigh. Nobody reads the elisp archives anymore.

subject: Help with Emacs (and a message to Max Ott)
q: On SunOS 4.0.1, emacstool compiles and runs under GNU Emacs 18.51 but I can't get a scrollbar. Also on the Sun-4 the documentation program won't build and I get "Cannot exec binary file". Why?
a: No scrollbar is drawn. It's just the right edge of each window, and mouse hits there follow the scrollbar assignments; check scrollbar-width. As for the Sun-4, make-docfile is probably a Sun-3 binary. Remove it and rebuild, and check CC in etc/Makefile. Sigh.

subject: quandary with GNU
q: On some terminals, such as att4425 and att4415, GNU Emacs 18.47 maps the delete key (^?) to ^G, but not on others. Where is that remapping happening?
a: Probably sign extension. The delete gets sign-extended, and with meta bits ignored it looks just like a ^G. Check your terminal characteristics and make sure it sends the right bits, 8 bit no parity is best. That's from memory, so don't stake your life on it.

subject: Is there a fix for "File tags not a valid tag table"?
q: What's the difference between ctags and etags in Emacs, and how can I run etags from a key or M-x instead of the shell?
a: Ctags only handles C files. Etags handles any mix of C, Fortran and Lisp, so one tags file covers a multi-language program like GNU Emacs. As for running it, M-! runs shell-command, so M-! etags *.[ch] does it. Don't write a command to do what the shell does.

subject: Nemacs (Re: 8 bit characters)
q: Why is the Japanese version of GNU Emacs called Nemacs and not Nimacs?
a: The N stands for Nihongo, which is Japanese. Not that hard to work out.

subject: Byte-compiling yer .emacs (was Re: How to enable flow control)
q: Why won't Emacs load a byte-compiled .emacs.elc? Is there a way to have a byte-compiled .emacs?
a: Easy. Move your .emacs to emacs.el, byte-compile it to get emacs.elc, then move emacs.elc to $HOME/.emacs. When you change things, edit emacs.el and recompile. Works like a charm; no need for those ridiculous C-shell aliases.

subject: tfm to [pk or pxl for xdvi] and [afm]
q: Can I convert TeX tfm font files to pk or pxl bitmaps for xdvi, and to afm files?
a: No. A tfm holds only character sizes and kerning, while pk and pxl hold the actual bitmaps. Run Metafont on mf files to get gf, then convert those. Afm is similar to tfm, so that direction might work. Learn what the formats are first.

subject: Converting PFB files to `standard' PostScript
q: Does anyone have a program that converts Adobe Type 1 PFB font files into standard PostScript, so I can download the fonts with my TeX document?
a: Use pfb2pf, posted to alt.sources. It's a filter that strips the PFB key bytes and hex-encodes the eexec section. Getting your applications to download the fonts is your problem, not mine.

subject: Khmer font for Macintosh
q: Does anyone know of a Khmer font for the Macintosh, or a program to edit or print Khmer text on a laser printer, and what would it cost?
a: Try Devonian Software in Los Angeles or Linguist's Software in Redmond; fonts cost no more than $150. To make your own, Fontastic does bitmap fonts for about $100 and Fontographer does LaserWriter fonts for about $300, both from Altsys. Any Mac program handling fonts will then work.

subject: Type 1 font esoterica
q: In a Type 1 font, if parallel vertical lines form a stem but the vstem hint that covered them was replaced earlier in the character, are they still compared to StdVW and StemSnapV in the Private dictionary?
a: No. Once the stem hint has been replaced there is no adjustment. The rendering algorithm can't work out on the fly which curves make up a stem. If it could, we wouldn't need hints at all. Think about it.

subject: Comments on Arts&Letters vs. CorelDRAW?
q: Is CorelDRAW worth $200 to $300 more than Arts&Letters Editor? I'd like comments from people who have used both.
a: What $300 more? CorelDraw cost me about $330 at a discount dealer; only the list price is silly. Version 2.0 has top reviews in the magazines. Nobody pays list, so why ask?

subject: Scalable weight fonts
q: Is anyone aware of any research into scaling the weight, not the size, of a font?
a: Metafont, obviously. Knuth's Computer Modern Typefaces introduction has a bibliography of such work. There's also a PC generator called Parafont that does non-linear scaling, and Addison-Wesley has Knuth's books on Metafont. Do some reading.

subject: LUCIDA for TeX ?
q: Is the Lucida typeface by Bigelow & Holmes available for use with TeX, commercially or by general distribution?
a: Last I heard, a PostScript version of Lucida was being made especially for use with TeX. Agfa ships at least a subset with their P400 PostScript printers, so contact Adobe for details. Stop pestering the secretaries.

subject: Swiss and Dutch fonts?
q: What commonly used fonts on the Macintosh are close to Swiss and Dutch? I heard Helvetica may be the same as Swiss.
a: Swiss is Helvetica, and Dutch is Times Roman. Dutch is just a Times Roman clone under a different name, since the name is trademarked but the font itself can't be copyrighted. Any idiot with a font catalog knows this.

subject: What is ?
q: What is the italic font National Geographic uses for its photo captions?
a: No idea if it has a name, but Matthew Carter designed it specially for National Geographic, originally for Linotype equipment. NG may hold exclusive rights. Check Linotype's specimen book or call them. Carter is at Bitstream now, so ask him yourself.

subject: font generation for Borland TC and TP6.0
q: Where can I find software to generate fonts for Borland Turbo C and Turbo Pascal 6.0?
a: Dig through the SIMTEL20 archive, in the MSDOS.BORLAND directory. One of the files starting with BG has a .CHR font editor in it. Fetch 00-INDEX.TXT first to make sure, instead of guessing.

subject: MS-DOS vs. IBM DOS, help wanted
q: Can I upgrade from MS-DOS 3.3 to IBM DOS 4.01 on my AT clone without reformatting the hard drive?
a: Yes, SYS will move the system to the hard drive without a reformat. But it won't repartition, so you're stuck under 32MB. If you want big partitions you'll have to reformat anyway. DOS 4.0 also eats more base memory, so plenty of people stay with 3.3. Back up first.

subject: Definition of a Fractal?
q: Can anyone give a plain definition of a fractal that quasi-intelligent people can understand, not Mandelbrot's Hausdorff Besicovitch one?
a: Stick with self-similar, and maybe partial-dimensional. Compare a straight line with a space-filling curve and point out that fractals resemble such curves. Not that the public will get it, but that's the best you'll do.

subject: how are gifs stored?
q: Does an 1150x900 TrueColor (24 bit) image really take up 24 Meg when loaded into an X pixmap? If not, how much does it take?
a: It's 24 Meg bits, not bytes. Sigh, do the arithmetic: 1150 times 900 pixels at 24 bits is about 24 million bits, so roughly 3 megabytes. You're welcome.

subject: "Flip Book" Animator for X/Sunview
q: Does anyone have a C program for a flip-book style animator that shows a set of images, such as Utah .rle files, at some speed on X-Windows or SunView?
a: Use getx11 from the 3.0 Utah Raster Toolkit. It has enhanced support for flip-book style animation, so read its man page. No need to write your own.

subject: HOOPS package
q: Does anyone use HOOPS, the graphics package from Ithaca Software? What phone number do I call to get it?
a: HOOPS comes from Ithaca Software at 415-523-5900. Call them; that's what the number is for.

subject: Ray Traced Bounding Spheres
q: Given a cluster of points in 3-space, is there a good method for finding the minimum radius sphere that encloses all of them, or at least a small one tighter than the box's sphere?
a: Don't just center on the line between two far points. An equilateral triangle shows that fails. Grow it incrementally: start at the midpoint of two points, and when a new point is outside, move the center halfway toward it so the sphere touches it and the old sphere. It's the 3D smallest enclosing circle problem, in Preparata and Shamos.

subject: Q: Films via ray tracing hacks?
q: Has anyone hacked a ray tracer to spend rendering time on a movie frame in proportion to how long its image is visible, so fast-moving things are traced poorly and static things well?
a: Not so fast. If you're doing motion blur, the opposite is true: heavily blurred parts of the frame need more samples to render accurately than the static areas. You could look at HDTV and MPEG compression for similar tricks, though.

subject: New Ed. Foley and van Dam...
q: Has the new edition of Foley and van Dam come out yet? I read it was in preparation with a third author.
a: Not yet, as far as I can tell. Chapters are being handed out hot off the presses for a class, and it doesn't seem to have gone to the publisher. Some chapters list four authors, so your information is already stale.

subject: Mathematica and terminals
q: How can I get Mathematica to do graphics on a Tektronix terminal, a VGA PC or a Mac SE telnetted into a DEC workstation whose default terminal type is X?
a: Easy. Just issue <<Tek.m and it switches to Tektronix mode. RTFM, it's right there.

subject: Signal/noise and sampling...
q: How can I measure a video camera's signal-to-noise ratio when my frame grabber only gives 8 bits, which limits me to about 48 dB?
a: Aim the camera at a smooth white wall lit by a shadeless lamp, with the lamp out of frame, and grab several frames without moving anything. A noiseless camera gives identical frames. If the camera beats the digitizer, you get agreeing bands and differing bands. Thinner differing bands mean better S/N. Assumes your digitizer meets spec, which is optimistic.

subject: 3D Rotations of 2D Bitmap
q: How can I rotate a 2D bitmap in 3D about all three axes using the shear transform method? I can't find the article the FAQ cites.
a: The original three-shear work is in the 1986 Graphics Interface proceedings. An extended version is in Graphics Gems (Glassner, Academic Press, 1990). For 3D rotation of a bitmap, see Krieger's Master's essay on 3-D environments for 2-D animation, a perspective technique that isn't shear-based. Do some reading.

subject: Convex hull of a set of 3D vertices
q: How do I compute the convex hull of a set of 3D points, including the polygons that make up the hull, not just the vertices?
a: Look up A. M. Day, "Implementation of an algorithm to find the convex hull of a set of 3-d points," ACM Transactions on Graphics, Jan 1990. It has Pascal code. It doesn't handle coplanar points, though. Nothing's ever complete.

subject: Hodgepodge (Computer Recreations 8/88)
q: How do I handle the division by zero hazard when A = 0 in the Hodgepodge algorithm from Scientific American's Computer Recreations column?
a: Count the cell itself in the infected cells total, which guarantees A is greater than 0. Dewdney's article is vague on g, but with n=128 values around 45 were interesting. An 8-connected neighborhood works; 4 neighbors gave nothing interesting.

subject: How do I draw a perspective view?
q: How do I take a point (x,y,z) in space and map it onto the screen as a single point perspective view in (x,y)? My cube draws fine but anything harder gets lines going everywhere.
a: Assuming a left-handed system, divide x and y by z and scale by the tangent of the field of view. That maps into -1 to 1, which you scale to your window. And clip any polygon with a vertex behind the eye, or weird stuff happens. Obvious, really.

subject: Postscript, ESPF
q: How do Postscript and Encapsulated Postscript differ? Is the latter a superset of the former? I want to import standard Postscript graphics into FrameMaker.
a: Sigh. EPS is not a superset, it's a restricted subset. You can't use some PS commands like initgraphics, and in exchange you get things like a bounding box so FrameMaker can size the thing. The spec lists the forbidden commands. Try comp.lang.postscript next time.

subject: Get a life!
q: I heard of a Life program that does 1103 generations of the r pentomino in 1.5 seconds on a Sun 1. Does that really exist, and how might it be done?
a: Standard Life visits every cell each generation. Look only at live cells and their neighbors, and add bit-bashing and lookup tables, and you get a constant-factor speedup. Beyond that, you need Gosper's algorithm: a quad-tree plus heavy caching. Think harder.

subject: 2-D clipping
q: I need an efficient integer algorithm to clip 2-D lines to a rectangle. Everything I've found uses world coordinates and floating point. Where do I look?
a: Cohen/Sutherland, as described in Newman and Sproull's Principles of Interactive Computer Graphics. It finds the boundary intersections and trivially rejects lines wholly outside, and an integer version works fine. Honestly, this is in every graphics text; read one.

subject: converting PAL to NTSC and back
q: I need to convert NTSC video to PAL and PAL back to NTSC for a European frame grabber and an American VCR. Does such a converter exist, and what does it cost?
a: Yes, it's called a digital standards converter, and a good one runs about $20,000. Cheaper models are supposedly appearing, but who knows about quality. Welcome to the world of non-standard video and big bucks, kid.

subject: An Easy Image Format
q: I need to create an original 24-bit RGB image that will end up going to a slide recorder. What is the easiest image format to create?
a: PBM, obviously. Failing that, RAW with no header, one file per colour plane, left to right and top to bottom. 24-bit Targa is easy enough too once you get past the header. Pick one already.

subject: TIFF LZW compressed (type "MM") pictures ?
q: I scanned pictures on a Mac with ImageStudio and saved them as LZW compressed TIFF, type "MM", but no other program on Mac, PC or Sun can read them. How can I convert them to something common?
a: You likely saved RIFF, ImageStudio's own format, which is basically TIFF with LZW. Most Mac programs use no compression or just PackBits. Read them back into ImageStudio and use Save As Other to write real TIFF. Nothing else reads RIFF.

subject: Amiga or PC-AT ?
q: I want to continue my ray-tracing work. Should I buy an AT clone with an expensive graphics card and monitor, or an Amiga?
a: Go with the Amiga. It has graphics support you'd pay oodles for elsewhere, HAM mode gives 4096 colors, and genlocks and digitizers are cheap. There's lots of freeware on Fish disks, and Sculpt 3D plus Animate 3D should cover ray tracing. Quit dithering.

subject: Looking for CATIA info
q: I'm looking for information on the CAD/CAM package CATIA. Who makes it?
a: It's put out by Dassault in France. Thanks to an exclusive marketing agreement with IBM it only runs on IBM mainframes. Best CAD package in the world, in one opinion, though you'll need a mainframe, so dream on.

subject: Looking for Floyd/Steinberg Dithering paper.
q: I'm looking for the original Floyd/Steinberg dithering paper, 'An Adaptive Algorithm for Spatial Gray Scale', from the 1975 SID symposium digest. Is there a more available reference?
a: Same authors, same title, in Proceedings of the Society for Information Display, volume 17 number 2, second quarter 1976. That's far easier to find than the symposium digest. Go bother a real library.

subject: PHIGS Information
q: I'm starting a PHIGS project and there's little besides the standards documents. Are there books or documentation that help with programming in PHIGS?
a: There's a little book called Understanding PHIGS, put out by Template, the software side of Megatek. Found it helpful. Call them for a copy. Slim pickings otherwise, which is what you get with committee standards.

subject: XGL Graphics Library
q: Is Sun's XGL graphics library compatible with Silicon Graphics' GL?
a: No. GL is for SGI machines, XGL for Sun machines running OpenWindows. Similar purposes, but neither binary- nor source-compatible. Compatible in name only, and I hear they're moving to copyright the name XGL. Marketing.

subject: visualization book
q: Is the book "Visualization: The Second Computer Revolution" worth buying?
a: Lotsa pretty pictures but short on substance. It'd look nice on a coffee table. Save your $49.50.

subject: IKONAS rds-3000
q: Is the company that made the IKONAS rds-3000 frame buffer really out of business? If not, where can they be reached?
a: They got bought out by Adage. So much for the company vanishing, though I wouldn't expect much support for that old iron. Somebody even offered to collect your Ikonas up in Waterloo.

subject: PostScript -> DVI or anything else
q: Is there a converter that takes a PostScript file back to DVI, or even to plain ASCII text?
a: No sure-fire way. PostScript is a programming language, so output can be twisted arbitrarily. If the application's prep script is sane, edit it so running the file spits out text. Some apps scramble their own fonts, though. Otherwise print it and scan it. TANSTFL.

subject: Sun Raster Conversion Utilities
q: Is there a non-Sun, non-Vax-dependent converter from TIFF, PICT or other Mac formats to Sun Raster? Everything needs the Sun libraries, and the PBM and FBM packages didn't work on my BSD machines.
a: Use the FBM package. It reads rast files fine with just a simple struct in the flsun.c routine, no pixrect include crud. The writing code should just work too. PBM is the one that needs the pixrect include file, so skip that.

subject: Digital terrain data
q: Is there anywhere in the US I can get digitized elevation data for 3-d terrain modelling? I wrote the USGS and all they sent was info on topographic maps.
a: The USGS has plenty of digital elevation maps (DEMs) on mag tape, in 7.5 minute quads and 1 degree DMA data. You asked for the wrong brochure. Ask for their USGeoData information; the Reston and Palo Alto offices can help.

subject: STB Powergraph S Vga
q: My STB Powergraph VGA works only in Windows. Which card do I select in cshow, and why does Deluxe Paint II Enhanced complain about 512K on the card in super VGA modes?
a: Use the driver for the STB EMM16+. That's the one that works on an STB card. Pick it in cshow instead of hunting for an orchid entry. Works fine here.

subject: 64K colors?
q: The Tseng ET-4000 chip supposedly can show 65535 colors using 2 bytes per pixel. How do I use that mode, and is it worth the trouble?
a: As I understand it, it's a HAM-style scheme: special mode, reserved color values act as instructions to interpolation hardware. Fine for CAD packages doing anti-aliased lines, useless if you want any pixel set to any of 65535 colors. Look at how Amiga HAM went and weep.

subject: Would like to know the meaning of an achronym
q: What is DXF, the "defacto standard" mentioned in an ad for a CAD tool called MICROGRAFX, and where can I get more information?
a: DXF is a drawing interchange format in plain ASCII, made by Autodesk so AutoCAD drawings can be translated to other CAD packages. It has five sections: Header, Tables, Blocks, Entities and EOF. Details are in Appendix C of the AutoCAD Reference manual. Read it.

subject: Kodak CD Specs, or what is YCC
q: What is YCC, as used in Kodak's Photo-CD, as opposed to YIQ or RGB? Does it help with lossless compression?
a: Probably YCbCr, a colourspace from CCIR-601. Like YIQ, luma and chroma are separate. No advantage for lossless: converting RGB to YCbCr and back is itself lossy. It helps lossy compression, since you can throw away more chroma than luma. Journalists, sigh.

subject: 8 and 24 bit color printers
q: Where can I find general information on 8 and 24 bit color printers under $20K that print X screen dumps or Sun rasterfiles well?
a: The October 1991 Byte covers many current printer technologies. Look at color thermal printers: very saturated colors, usually around 300 dpi, and fairly fast compared to ink jet or dot matrix. Color laser would run you over $20K. Dream on.

subject: Superquadrics
q: Where can I find information on superquadrics, including the equations and ray intersection with normals, since our library lacks the first IEEE CG&A issue?
a: The original paper is by Al Barr, in the first IEEE CG&A, so get your library to fix its missing back issues. A point is c(e1,u)c(e2,v), c(e1,u)s(e2,v), s(e1,u), where c and s are the cosine and sine raised to the power e. Differentiate for the normal. Pentland's 1986 paper in Artificial Intelligence covers it too.

subject: Where can I get the .BMP graphics file format specification?
q: Where can I get the specification for the .BMP bitmap graphics file format that Microsoft uses in OS/2 PM and Windows? I want to convert GIF files to .BMP.
a: Read the manuals. Both formats are documented in the development kit manuals, and the OS/2 one is a bit more enhanced than the Windows one. Charles Petzold's books on Windows and PM programming cover them too. Sigh, it's all in print.

subject: there are no CORE programs utilizing 3D?
q: Why can't I find any 3D application programs that use CORE graphics primitives? Did nobody write a wire-frame modeler with it?
a: Because CORE is dead. It's been subsumed by GKS and PHIGS, and those are what people use instead. Nobody bothers with CORE anymore, so stop hunting for it.

subject: TIFF better than PICT? Why?
q: Why does an image scanned in 24-bit color and saved as TIFF look much better than the same image saved as PICT? Someone told me PICT loses information.
a: PICT doesn't inherently lose anything. A 24-bit TIFF should look just like a 24-bit PICT from the same software. If yours looks banded or dithered, your PICT is probably only 8-bit, either because the scanner software predates 32-Bit Color QuickDraw or because it's not installed and it fell back to 8 bits.

subject: World Cordinate Resolution
q: With floating-point world coordinates in a raytracer, if I use a span of -10000 to 10000 instead of -10 to 10, does that convert spare exponent bits into extra accuracy bits, or just make the holes in floating-point space bigger?
a: Accuracy is accuracy. The mantissa is fixed length, so scale doesn't buy you bits. Trouble only comes from mixing very tiny and very large numbers, which rarely happens in image synthesis. Results also vary with the machine's mantissa and exponent split.

subject: Covering Scan-Conversion of Polygons?
q: How can I scan-convert a polygon so that all grid cells with any part inside the polygon are identified, rather than the best approximation? Any references?
a: No references, but recursive subdivision with a quadtree at pixel boundaries will do it. Clip your polygon against each quadtree element to classify it in, out or partial, down to the pixel level, then keep the in and partial ones. Not rocket science.

subject: Video from a Workstation Screen
q: How do labs record video from a workstation screen? A camera has frequency problems. I heard of a board that plugs into a SUN and records straight to VCR tape. Who makes it?
a: Look at RGB/Spectrum in Berkeley. They make RGB-to-video boards and external boxes for most systems and frequencies. RasterOps also has an SBus card, I think called PIP. Or ask your Sun office, if you can stand sales droids.

subject: Acoustic touch screens
q: At what frequency do acoustic touch screens operate, and could they interfere with other devices in a hospital environment?
a: My literature says the surface acoustic wave signal has a wavelength of 0.0226 inch. I doubt interference is a problem, but ask the technical people who design these touchscreens, like Elographics, instead of guessing on the net.

subject: Intel DVI
q: How well does Intel's DVI technology work on images that aren't typical video, and does anyone have ballpark prices for the chips, boards or systems?
a: It works best on fairly stable video. Lots of background switching gives you speed problems. Nobody's heard a price in two years, though Intel wants it cheap enough for consumers, so I'd guess around $1,000. Marketing hype, as usual.

subject: PAL/NTSC ?
q: I have an NTSC laserdisc player, a Sony LDP 1500, but the Ecodisc videodisc is recorded in PAL. Am I out of luck, or is there a way short of buying a PAL player?
a: You're out of luck, only a PAL-capable player will do. But some play both: the Sony LDP-3600 and MDP-515 with a multi-standard monitor, and the Pioneer CLD1450 on a PAL monitor. Pick your next player better.

subject: DVI questions
q: With DVI, once my application works on my hard drive, how do I get it into a format for CD-ROM pre-mastering? Does it need a special program?
a: If you have DVI you have the Production Tools. VLayout adds the padding for CD-ROM, then run a disk optimizer so the files are contiguous, and back them up to an archive tape with SY-TOS for the CD-ROM house. Read the docs, newbie.

subject: Postscript APL font
q: Has anyone created a PostScript APL font to print function listings from STSC APL on a Sun?
a: An APL font for TeX exists and is free. Get the metafont definition and .tex files by anonymous ftp, and build it at any size for just about any laser printer. Sharp APL for Unix also ships a nice PostScript APL font, but it's copyrighted, so ask first.

q: What do I need to write an IBM 3270 emulation on a PC? Which manuals should I have?
a: Start with a working emulation instead of manuals. Get the Clarkson University TCP Communications Package by anonymous FTP from OMNIGATE.Clarkson.EDU, or use KERMIT's VT-100 emulation to an IBM 7171 or 3172, which converts to 3270. Don't reinvent the wheel.

subject: Insecure hardware (was Re: gets(3) nonsense)
q: Could hardware be at fault in the recent Internet virus? Did it work because those machines let code execute in data space, and what could hardware do to make UNIX more secure?
a: No, the fingerd bug was gets() letting a long line overwrite the stack, return addresses and all, so splitting code and data space wouldn't have helped. Tagged-word machines could stop it by marking return addresses as code. Fix your gets() calls first, honestly.

subject: Sizes, alignments, and maxima (was: Contiguous Arrays)
