q: Is it legal in a conforming C implementation for sizeof(int) to be 8 while INT_MAX is only 0x7FFFFFFF, as reportedly on the Cray-2?
a: I think so. The standard only requires binary representation, matching nonnegative signed and unsigned values, that INT_MAX ranges be representable, and modulo unsigned arithmetic. Nothing forces every bit pattern to be a valid integer, and we didn't want that, since some architectures can't.

subject: ANSI header library out there?
q: Is there an ANSI C header library out there for use with gcc on Ultrix, ideally one with ifdefs for different architectures that I can distribute?
a: There's no such thing as a generic ANSI C header library. The headers are compiler-dependent and system-dependent in places. Sigh, that's how it is.

subject: ET++ - An Object-Oriented Application Framework in C++
q: Can anyone tell me about ET++, the C++ application framework?
a: There's an article on its architecture by the authors in Structured Programming, Vol 10. It was developed at the University of Zurich in original single-inheritance C++, looks a bit like MacApp but better, and ran on a Sun. Version 1.0 is probably on ftp somewhere. Go look.

subject: method definition question
q: In CLOS, how can I write one method applicable to two unrelated classes A and B, say with a deftype of (or A B)? I can't redefine A or B to add a mixin.
a: You can't; compound type specifiers like OR can't be method specializers because they create ambiguities in the class hierarchy. Best choice is to factor the common code into an ordinary function and call it from both methods. There's no really elegant way, so deal with it.

subject: delete an instance
q: In CLOS, how do I get rid of an instance I've created? I'm using VAXLISP and PCL.
a: This is Lisp, so you don't delete things by hand. Once all references to the instance are gone, the garbage collector reclaims the memory eventually. Sigh. If you really want a function for it, see The Art of the Metaobject Protocol.

subject: methods on no-applicable-method?
q: Is defining a method on no-applicable-method with an eql specializer on the generic function a portable and correct approach?
a: What you really want is a default method on that particular generic function. Methods on NO-APPLICABLE-METHOD are for MOP hacking, like new generic function classes with odd default behavior. Most EQL specializer use means your protocol or class hierarchy is broken.

subject: Assertion tags
q: What are assertion tags in Eiffel used for, besides self-documentation?
a: They name the violated assertion. When an assertion fails and raises an exception, the runtime's exception history prints the tag, such as non_void_widget on a precondition, so you know which one tripped. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: PC/Mac Implementations: Any Updates?
q: What's the status of Eiffel implementations for the Mac and PC?
a: Eiffel/S from SIG Computer in Germany is an Eiffel 3.0 for the PC, slated for August 1, bare-bones with no Windows support. Eiffel/Mac is a 2.3.4 port from CERco, integrated with MPW, in alpha late summer, final release 1992 at best. Sigh, vaporware season.

subject: Unformatted(binary) Fortran standard output
q: How can I get a Fortran program to write unformatted binary output to stdout so I can pipe it over the LAN with rsh? The write(*) and write(6) statements don't work.
a: The always-open unit is implicitly formatted. First try open(6,form='unformatted'). Otherwise, explicitly OPEN another unit as unformatted. Or write small temp files and cat each one to stdout with a system call. Some implementations have been known to eat nulls too. Such fun.

subject: Fortran for MS Windows 3.0?
q: What Fortran would you recommend for MS Windows 3.0? How do Lahey and Watfor compare?
a: You can't write a whole Windows program in Fortran right now. Do mixed language programming: MS C for the Windows part and MS Fortran for the number crunching. Microsoft supposedly plans a Windows-compatible Fortran next year. Marketing promises, naturally.

subject: IEEE FP NaNs = everything else?
q: Has anyone explored using IEEE floating point as a general representation in a manifestly-typed language, with everything other than flonums being NaNs?
a: Think it through. Any arithmetic involving a NaN must give a NaN, so (+ 3.0 1) would come out NaN instead of 4.0 if fixnums were NaNs. Use NaNs only for non-numbers, and signalling NaNs will make ordinary hardware trap on (+ 3.0 'a). Two minutes of idle speculation shows.

subject: exploratory system for unix system calls/facilities
q: Is there an interactive environment for playing with Unix system calls and IPC without writing, compiling and debugging C code?
a: Try Elk, the Extension Language Kit. It's Scheme with interfaces to Xlib, Athena and HP widgets, and some Unix system calls and C library functions. The interface is easily extended to cover most others. Beats writing C by hand, I suppose.

subject: XLISP memory limits
q: On a 640K PC running XLISP 2.1, ALLOC 2000 only gets me 2 segments of nodes while ALLOC 500 gets 9. What are the limits, and how do nodes convert to Kbytes? Could my TSR editor be the problem?
a: Each node takes 11 or 12 bytes on a PC. In 640K with minimal TSRs, about 20K nodes, roughly 250KB, is what you'll get. Your TSR editor is surely eating a fair chunk of memory. Drop it, genius.

subject: Allegro (was Re: Want references for ObjectLISP)
q: We bought Allegro Common Lisp before it went to APDA. Does anyone know of an upgrade, since the APDA product includes much more than the original?
a: APDA offers a 1.2.2 upgrade, and you'd better get it if you want any support on ACL. There's also a tech note on known bugs and patches. Should've checked with APDA before asking the whole net.

subject: Evaluating a form in a particular stack frame
q: How can I evaluate a form inside a particular stack frame in Allegro Common Lisp, for instance from an error break, to call a diagnostic on local variables?
a: Wrong group; Allegro CL is not Franz Lisp. Anyway, use :loc with the variable name, which sets the top level variable * to its value. Then use * in your diagnostic call. Learn which group you're in.

subject: A question and an offer
q: What is the current version of XLisP? I have 2.0 from an FTP archive, but heard 2.1 ships with X11R4.
a: There's a 2.1 around, shipped inside the WINTERP package on the MIT X11R4 contrib tape. It added defstruct and asin, acos and atan over 2.0, but no sign of ln. Get the latest WINTERP plus XLISP by anonymous ftp from expo.lcs.mit.edu, contrib/winterp. Poke around.

subject: Need "reduce" function under Xlisp!!!
q: Xlisp doesn't have reduce, find-if, or every. Can anyone write those for Xlisp, or tell me where to get them?
a: Don't bother writing them. The enhanced xlisp, xlisp21c, already has all three and plenty more. Grab it from glia.biostr.washington.edu or bikini.cis.ufl.edu. Sigh, people never look for the existing version first.

subject: Ray's creatures: Tierra
q: What can you tell me about Dr. Ray's Tierra creatures, such as references, code and papers?
a: Look in comp.theory.cell-automata, where about 100K worth of info from Ray was posted recently, and it may not have reached your site yet. Don't get too excited too fast either. Newspaper hype never matches the real thing.

subject: Printing plural forms.
q: When programming, how do you avoid output like '1 files were copied' when it should say '1 file was copied'? Do any languages make plurals easy?
a: Common Lisp's format can pluralize automatically, even print numbers as roman numerals or English words. In C the usual idiom is printf("%d file%s copied.\n", nfiles, "s"+(nfiles==1)). Not exactly rocket science.

subject: Who or What is Scheme?
q: Who or what is Scheme? Does someone have a quick summary of where it fits into the Universe?
a: It's a dialect of LISP that is applicative-order and lexically scoped. Unlike the other LISP dialects, it treats both functions and continuations as first-class objects. Go read the Revised Report instead of asking the net.

subject: lilith...
q: Can I buy an old Lilith Modula-2 system, and who do I talk to about it?
a: Believe it or not, Modula Corp. of Orem, Utah still sells a version of the Lilith. Prices are probably higher than you'd like, but they may deal or know someone who has a used one. They also sell Modula-2 compilers and books.

subject: TopSpeed C (and yes, I know where I'm posting!)
q: Can I buy only the Standard Edition of TopSpeed C and still get the Extended Edition's utilities like the DDL and profiler, if I already own TopSpeed Modula-2 V2?
a: Mostly yes. The C extended edition utilities all work with M2, and the reverse should hold too. What you miss is the M2 source files. The overlap is nice, and the vendor ought to discount multiple compilers instead of being stingy.

subject: Query:Speed of Mod2 vs C
q: How does Modula-2 on the Amiga compare to C in overall execution speed?
a: One user says it's faster than C, though not because of the language; the compiler and its linker, which prunes unused modules, are just nicer. Another says TDI sits between Lattice 3.03 and Manx, with no real benchmarks. Subjective, so don't bet your life on it.

subject: MS-DOS OBERON Demo ???
q: I ran the Abu demo of Oberon-M on an AT with EGA, DOS 3.3. It compiled fine, but flashes the screen and returns to DOS. How do I fix it?
a: ABU expects a filename argument, and it must be an existing file. It's not your EGA. Read what the program wants before blaming the hardware.

subject: JPI TopSpeed
q: Is there a new TopSpeed Modula-2 coming out to go along with TopSpeed C, and when?
a: JPI says TopSpeed C is out by end of November at the latest. The newsletter says the polished user interface will be part of TopSpeed Modula-2 2.0 too, but 1.17 is still what's shipping. Don't hold your breath.

subject: Modula 3
q: Is there a newsgroup on Modula 3? I'm trying to evaluate it against Eiffel and C++.
a: Yes, comp.lang.modula3 exists, so ask there instead of here. It's archived too, on gatekeeper.dec.com in pub/DEC/Modula-3/comp.lang.modula3. Try reading the archive before posting, for once.

subject: TURBO MODULA.
q: My friend with a CP/M Osborne needs a copy of Turbo Modula to recompile a comms program. Can anyone help?
a: Borland never released it; it was sold off with TP 3.0 for CP/M to some little company. It did appear once in a BYTE Ciarcia article on an HD64180 board, with addresses and sources. Go dig through the back issues. Sigh.

subject: MacModula2 SYSTEM sources
q: Where can I get the assembler source for NEWPROCESS and TRANSFER in MacModula2 by Modula Corp, like Wirth's published ones for the Lilith?
a: In the original interpreted M-code version they're 68000 assembly routines inside the Modula-2 interpreter. Modula Corp isn't doing much with it these days, and I bet they'd be reluctant to release the sources. Don't hold your breath.

subject: default values of all sorts of pointers (references, procedures)
q: In Modula-3, if a variable declaration has no default value, is the initial value guaranteed to be in the range of its type, or is it an arbitrary bit pattern? Are procedure variables and references set to NIL?
a: Not NIL by default. You only get an arbitrary value of the type: VAR v: [5..6] starts as 5 or 6, and a procedure variable is NIL or a valid procedure of that signature. Nothing says it's the same each run. If you need NIL, say so in the declaration. Read the report.

subject: Porting Objective-C code to Macintosh
q: I want to port Objective-C code that does no graphics from my NeXT to a Macintosh. Stepstone's runtime source is $25K, so can anything else work?
a: If you're not doing graphics, you don't need the expensive graphical library. NeXT's compiler no longer generates ANSI C as far as I know, but all of Stepstone's compilers do. Doing this on nearly any machine is quite possible. NeXT is the odd one, super-optimizing for their own reasons.

subject: novice
q: I'm new to Objective-C. Is there a good book, and is there a public domain Objective-C compiler or preprocessor for OS/2 or DOS?
a: Get Object-Oriented Programming by Cox and Novobilski, from Addison-Wesley. As for a free compiler, none that I know of. Stepstone's costs $249 for DOS or $495 for OS/2. Welcome, I suppose.

subject: Make II, The REVENGE!!
q: Borland's Make 1.3 from Turbo Pascal 4.0 wouldn't even execute COMMAND, but the Make 1.0 from Turbo C worked fine. Shouldn't programs get better with higher version numbers, not worse?
a: You'd think so, but not with this one. Borland's latest MAKE is, to put it politely, junk, and others also went back to version 1.0. Better still, use NDMAKE or something that works like MAKE should.

subject: OOP
q: Can anyone recommend a good book or source for learning Turbo Pascal 6.0 object-oriented programming?
a: Read the manual. The object tutorial in the 5.5 manual was quite good. Skip those books with one chapter tacked on the back that just rehash it.

subject: Strings - HELP
q: Does Turbo Pascal 3.1 have commands like LEFT$, RIGHT$ and MID$ from Basic for splitting strings? If not, are there routines to do it?
a: Use the Copy function for that. You can also index a string like an array of char, so A_String[1] gives the first character. Read the manual before asking, kiddo.

subject: Pascal Source Code Beautifier Wanted
q: Does anyone know of a Pascal source code beautifier that works like the cb command does for C?
a: There's /pc/pd2/pritprn.zip by anonymous ftp from chyde.uwasa.fi, and maybe others on Simtel20. Commercially, Turbo Professional from TurboPower has source formatting. Read the file lists before asking.

subject: Follow up to "redefine"
q: How can I redefine the appearance of characters in the ASCII or extended character set in Turbo Pascal, so a character prints as a triangle, and can that be done in text mode?
a: Interrupt vector 1F hex points to the upper half of the character set. Point it at your own redefined table and use that. Details are in Kent Porter, Stretching Turbo Pascal, chapter 16, Custom Characters. Read the book.

subject: Simple modem control in TP6.0
q: How do I do simple modem control in Turbo Pascal 6.0? I just want to dial a number at 1200 baud, capture a few lines of data, and hang up.
a: Wishful thinking; there's no few-lines solution to serial port control. Look at the PCTechniques June/July 1991 article, a 530-line terminal from Borland, or the demo in faquote.txt in tsfaq21.arc on garbo that reads and writes COM1 and COM2. Do some homework.

subject: TP: Exponentiation?
q: How do you do exponentiation in Turbo Pascal 4.0, 5.0 or 5.5? I can't find it in the manual and ** gives a compile error.
a: Nothing gives. Turbo Pascal has no exponentiation operator, so write a function. The usual trick is x**y = exp(y*ln(x)). Sigh, read the manual's operator list again, it isn't there.

subject: Getting the command line args
q: How does a running Turbo Pascal program get at its command line arguments?
a: ParamCount gives the number of parameters, and ParamStr(I) gives the Ith one. ParamStr(0) is the program's own name. It's in the Reference Guide, which you'd know if you'd read the manual.

subject: Modifying the DOS environment with TP
q: I'm writing a DOS shell in Turbo Pascal 5.5. I can read environment variables with GetEnv and EnvCount, but how do I change them? Exec'ing COMMAND.COM with /C SET doesn't stick.
a: Right, that exec trick is no solution. You have to mess with the PSP to change the environment, which is an advanced subject. Some Turbo Pascal books cover it, maybe Tischer's Turbo Pascal Internals. Go read one, sigh.

subject: Disable Control-Break in TP version 4
q: In Turbo Pascal 3 the {$C-} compiler directive disabled Control-Break, but TP 4 doesn't have it. How do I disable Control-Break in Turbo Pascal 4?
a: Set the global boolean CheckBreak to FALSE. That's what {$C-} did in TP 3.0, and it works in 4.0 through 5.5. It's been in the manual all along, so try reading it sometime.

subject: running other files? (help)
q: In Turbo Pascal 5.0, can I split off a big chunk of code used only the first time a user runs the program and call it only when needed, to save space and memory?
a: Use overlays, or the Exec procedure to run another program. Both are in TP 5.0 and documented in the manuals. RTFM, then come back with specific questions.

subject: Bug In Turbo Pascal v6.0 - crt unit/checkbreak
q: In Turbo Pascal 6.0 with the crt unit, setting CheckBreak to FALSE doesn't disable Ctrl-Break. It still breaks. Any suggestions?
a: You redeclared CheckBreak yourself, and crt already declares it. Remove your own declaration and it works. If you must reuse the name, say crt.checkbreak. Read your own code before blaming the compiler.

subject: REDIRECTING INPUT/OUTPUT WHILE USING "EXEC"
q: In Turbo Pascal, exec won't let me redirect input or output, and it won't run a batch file. How do I get around that?
a: Load a command interpreter to do it. Call exec(getenv('COMSPEC'), '/C sort <infile >outfile'). For a batch file, put its name in place of sort and skip the redirection. Basic DOS stuff, really.

subject: Turbo Pascal typecasting and the Mem array.
q: In Turbo Pascal, how do I store signed 16-bit integers with MemW[seg:offset], and do I increment the offset by one or by two?
a: Type cast when you read the value, as in temp_value := integer(MemW[seg:offset]). The offset has to be incremented twice to reach the next value. The reference guide is murky, I know, but try reading it first.

subject: Technojock's Turbo Toolkit V6.0
q: Is Technojock's Turbo Toolkit V6.0 available by ftp or download anywhere, and is it still shareware?
a: It's still shareware, registration around $70. You can download it from a board in Oregon, though I know of no ftp site, so somebody up there should post it to simtel. Reviews are in PC Techniques and Programmer's Journal. Do your homework.

subject: Turbovision for C?
q: Is Turbovision easy to use and efficient, is it standard with Borland's C and C++ compilers, and are there better DOS windowing packages from other companies?
a: No, it's very clumsy to use, though if you like LISP you might enjoy all the nested parens. It isn't standard with Borland's C compilers, nor sold separately. Try Object Professional by TurboPower, which is far easier.

subject: PC-Sig CD-ROM from the internet?
q: Is it possible to get the PC-SIG CD-ROM contents from the internet? I seem to remember someone saying it was.
a: Yes, by anonymous FTP at least. Go look at /pc/pd2/moder.lst and /pc/doc/ftpsites.lst, which you can get by anonymous FTP or mail server from the garbo archives. Sigh, read the lists before asking.

subject: pascal to c convertion utility
q: Is there a public domain Pascal to C source conversion utility?
a: Use p2c. It handles multiple Pascal dialects, including units and conformant arrays with gcc. Archives are at labrea.stanford.edu and mcsun.eu.net. Expect a few #define tweaks building it on a Sun-4 with cc; the error messages tell you what. This comes up constantly.

subject: Is there any ISO PASCAL other than level 0 ?
q: Is there any ISO Pascal other than level 0? I keep reading about "level 0" in ISO 7185 and wonder if there are other levels and how they differ.
a: ISO 7185 defines two levels, 0 and 1. The only difference is conformant arrays: Level 1 has them, Level 0 doesn't. Order the standard from ISO or BSI like everybody else. Sigh, it's not exactly a secret.

subject: Is there a known bug in the TP Database Toolbox 4.0?
q: My Turbo Pascal Database Toolbox 4.0 index goes corrupt around the 3170th record, hanging or giving a Disk Read Error. Is there a known bug?
a: Not a bug, it's your setup. When you run tabuild, it assumes a maximum of 1000 records, so the page sizes are wrong past that. Run tabuild /W+ file.typ and set the max records to something like 32000. The overhead is small. Read the manual next time.

subject: TPW debugger wont work.
q: The debugger in TPW won't run. When I pick Run|Debugger it compiles, says loading debugger, then says it can't find the debugger. Where should it be?
a: Make sure the debugger is in a directory on your DOS PATH. Or you moved it after installing TPW, and now TPW can't find it. Basic stuff; check your PATH before you post.

subject: round(-10.5) ?
q: What does the Pascal standard say about round applied to negative arguments like -10.5? Does round(-10.5) giving -11 conform to the standard?
a: Yes, it conforms, and it's required. Round(x) is trunc(x+0.5) for x >= 0, otherwise trunc(x-0.5), so -10.5 gives -11. See 6.6.6.3 in the standard. Not numerically proper rounding, but you can't do it right and stay conforming. Read the standard.

subject: Borland Forum on Compuserve
q: What is the Borland Forum on CompuServe and how can I reach it? Is there a Bitnet connection, do I need a phone number?
a: You have to join CompuServe, so ask them for the details. Once on, type GO BOR at most prompts. There are also GO BPROGA, GO BPROGB and GO BORDB for programming and database. No Bitnet magic, it's a commercial service.

subject: To what use is TP6.0's $X+ (extended syntax)?
q: What is the real use of the $X+ extended syntax directive in Turbo Pascal 6.0?
a: It lets you call a function and throw away the result, which is handy when you only want the side effect. Think of a ReadKeyWord that eats a keystroke and idles. It's C influence creeping into Pascal. Sigh, and the magazine's example was lousy.

subject: Turbo Pascal history
q: What were the significant improvements in each version of Turbo Pascal, and when were they released? I know 5.5 added object-oriented programming, but what about the earlier versions?
a: 3.0 was one 39k executable with editor and compiler, but a 64k limit and no separate compilation. 4.0 added units, dropped the 64k limit and overlaid better. 5.0 brought the IDE and integrated debugger, 5.5 added OOP. Then 6.0 and 7.0 went to flaky junk. Sigh.

subject: Extended Pascal Standard Question
q: What's the status of control variables in the upcoming Extended Pascal Standard? Will a for loop's control variable still be protected from being threatened, unlike in Modula-2?
a: The 1989-08-18 draft keeps the old position. The for-statement's control variable can't be threatened by statements in the enclosing block or its procedure and function parts. That's real standardese, so read it slowly. Sigh.

subject: Turbo Pascal/DOS Batch Heap Peculiarity
q: Why does a Turbo Pascal program print a different HeapOrg depending on whether the calling DOS batch file ends with a carriage return? Is it a DOS bug or a Turbo feature, and how do I handle it?
a: It's a property of DOS, not a bug or feature. The program loads lower in memory when the batch file has no more lines. Don't rely on the heap surviving between runs, since COMMAND.COM's transient part stomps on it. Use a file or a TSR.

subject: TP printer-unit bug ?
q: Why does sending an Escape sequence through the Turbo Pascal 5.0 printer unit print only the character after the Escape? Is it a bug?
a: Not a bug. Since TP 4.0 the LST file is opened in cooked mode, so ESC is filtered out, tabs expanded, and ^Z ends the file. Open PRN as a file of byte instead. RTFM.

subject: Ordering copies of the book
q: Can anyone recommend a company that takes emailed or faxed credit card orders for the Perl book and ships to Ireland?
a: Addison Wesley holds international distribution rights, so orders get forwarded to them, and they're slow. TECHbooks will ship the occasional single autographed copy abroad, but the freight will kill you. Write them for details.

subject: Compiling perl on a 286 Xenix box
q: Compiling perl 4.0 on a 286 Xenix box, my cpp chokes on lines beginning with '#' that aren't valid preprocessor commands, and %SIG doesn't catch any signals. What's going on?
a: Perl invokes sed to strip out the non-cpp comments; look in perl.c for that. As for %SIG, no idea. Throw some instrumentation into stab.c around signal() and see what it thinks it's doing. Go read the source.

subject: Config on APOLLO SR10.2
q: Configure on Apollo SR10.2 says dup2(), mkdir(), lstat() and other routines are not found, yet they exist, so I edit config.h every time. How do I get Configure to see them?
a: Apollo's cc has two C libraries, /lib/clib and /lib/libc, and Configure only searches one. Make it look at both, by giving the missing library with -l when asked, or patching Configure. Then delete the -l from the makefiles, since cc searches both itself. Apollo, sigh.

subject: Port Perl4.010 to SCO UNIX
q: Has anyone ported Perl 4.010 to SCO UNIX 3.2.2? I heard it's a terrible target, so I'd like some advice before I try it.
a: Whoever told you that was wrong. It built fine on 3.2.2 with nothing special. When Configure asks for the system type, pick the SCO_3_2 entry instead of the i386 default, take the defaults for the rest, and it works. Sigh, not everything is a horror story.

subject: makedepend
q: Has anyone written a makedepend in perl?
a: Look at the w4 program in the book, page 273. Yes, it's in the book. Don't make me sound like a Scientology ad.

subject: All patches applied
q: I unpacked the perl kits and applied all eighteen patches in order. Is it safe to compile perl the normal way, or did I need to do something between patches?
a: Should be fine. The patch instructions are just a subset of the README for people upgrading. If you're building from scratch, follow the README. The real test is a clean compile and clean regression tests, so run them.

subject: select(FILEHANDLE) in debugger - bug or feature?
q: In the perl debugger, after the script does select(FILEHANDLE), printing variables with print $foo fails but print STDOUT $foo works. Is that a bug or a feature of the debugger?
a: Neither, really. Use the "p" command, which prints to DB'OUT on /dev/tty. Plain print only works by accident, because the debugger evals unrecognized commands as Perl, and Perl honors your select. Don't rely on STDOUT for debugging anyway. If your fingers insist on typing print, alias it to p.

subject: Things found while looking for other things
q: My Perl code sets alarm 360 inside a function, but I expected it to go off after I exited the function. Are functions in Perl implemented differently for alarms? Why doesn't it fire?
a: Functions in Perl have nothing to do with alarms. Check whether $SIG{ALRM} is ignored or caught, whether you call sleep, which uses alarm, whether you exit early, or whether you call alarm again before 360 seconds, which resets it. Or alarm is busted.

subject: GCC and Perl v28
q: Perl 3.0.28 fails to compile doio.c under A/UX 2.0 with gcc 1.37.91, and make test shows errors. Does anyone know enough gcc internals to help?
a: Perl at patch level 28 builds fine with GCC 1.37.92 on a MIPS DECstation at all optimization levels. So it's the machine-dependent part of GCC or A/UX, not Perl. Don't expect much help from the FSF crowd, thanks to Apple's suit.

subject: Chapter 6 passwd program problem
q: The chapter 6 passwd program from the Programming Perl book sources gives a syntax error near an open and an unmatched () in a regexp. What's wrong?
a: It's a typo from when a long line got folded into two pieces. Rejoin them so the first regexp ends with june?)$/i, then the second line is the july? through dec alternation with $/i. Honestly, folded lines, every time. Fix it and move on.

subject: why doesn't "sort X" give an error
q: Why does Perl 3.0 accept the program "sort X" without an error? What does perl think X is?
a: It's a subroutine name. You gave sort an empty array, so it never evaluates the name and never finds it missing. List operators take an optional word first: print takes a filehandle, exec and system take a program name. Weird, but good for poetry. See the man page.

subject: trouble with syntax
q: Why doesn't print "seconds: ",$localtime(time)[0],"\n" work in Perl?
a: Because the syntax is wrong. You want print "seconds: ",(localtime(time))[0],"\n" — wrap the call in parens and slice the list. Read up on list slices before posting next time.

subject: Downloading Adobe fonts
q: Adobe says its fonts can only be downloaded to a PostScript printer from a Mac. How can I download them to my QMS PostScript printer from a Vax instead?
a: Adobe will tell you the fonts can be turned into a text form. Do that on a Mac as you initialize them for a printer, then carry the file to a PC or VAX for downloading. Might have changed since; ask Adobe, if they'll talk.

subject: Multiple %!s legal?
q: Are multiple %! lines legal in a PostScript file, and what purpose does %! serve? My LaserWriter only prints the pages after the last one.
a: The printer ignores everything starting with %, including %!. It's just a convention, only meaningful as the first two bytes. Either your spooler is slicing the file on %!, in which case it's broken, or there's a stray control-D ending the job. It's not your printer.

subject: Times Greek boldface/italic and Times vs Symbol
q: Are there Greek boldface, italic and boldface italic PostScript fonts that match Times Roman?
a: Just make them yourself. The Blue book has examples: compute a slant angle, change the fontmatrix entry in the font dictionary, and register the new font. Scale the characters a bit wider and you get a bold effect. It's about the best you'll do. Read the books.

subject: Postscript screen dumps
q: Are there screen dump programs for the PC that can dump EGA or VGA graphics screens to PostScript?
a: Inset is a TSR that captures a screen to a PIX file, lets you edit it, and sends it to a PostScript printer. Or chain an EGA/VGA-to-Epson MX-80 TSR with an Epson-to-PostScript one, though the result will be grainy and ugly.

subject: ATM/Windows & Softfonts
q: Can Adobe Type Manager for Windows build bitmap HP softfont-style downloadable fonts from outlines? The docs mention a Font Foundry program that I can't find.
a: Yes. Adobe's Font Foundry program builds HP downloadable fonts from the outlines. It comes with an update to the type library, which was even free. Check your update before whining.

subject: Imbed PostScript into MacDraw?
q: Can I embed PostScript code in MacDraw to put a faint "Preliminary" underneath a form?
a: Nope. MacDraw II takes no PostScript input at all. MacDraw Pro, announced at MacWorld, does handle EPS import and export, once it actually ships, which is vaporware until proven otherwise.

subject: Mac PS previewer wanted
q: Can anyone point me to a public domain PostScript previewer for the Macintosh? I'm just starting to poke around with the language and want to see the results on screen.
a: Try Freedom Of The Press Light 3.0.1. It has a screen previewer, B&W plus the standard 8 colors, and works with MacDraw and UltraPaint. It's no speed demon, but it's faster than the older versions. Beggars can't be choosers.

subject: Printing multiple pages on 1 sheet
q: Does anyone have a utility to print N pages from an ASCII text document on one sheet on a PostScript printer?
a: Grab psnup.tar.Z from goober.phri.nyu.edu in the ftp pub directory. It does exactly that, and people there use it a lot. Honestly, no need to write your own scale/translate/rotate hack when somebody already did.

subject: Wanted: Postscript to Sun rasterfile converter
q: Does anyone know of a PostScript to Sun rasterfile converter?
a: NeWS has everything you need. Render the PostScript into a canvas and use the writecanvas operator to dump it to a raster file in one line. The catch is picking a canvas pixel density matching your output device, which hung us up for ages. Read the manual.

subject: gif2ps
q: Does gif2ps convert a color GIF file to a color PostScript file?
a: Nope, not the gif2ps I've seen. It converts the colours to greyscale values and outputs those. Does a decent enough job of it, but don't go spending money expecting colour.

subject: Fill Patterns in PostScript?
q: How can I fill an area in PostScript with a color pattern from a bitmap swatch without using the setscreen operator, since setscreen is discouraged in EPS files?
a: Use the image operator. Set your clipping path to the boundary you want filled, find the bounding box of that path, and translate the origin to its upper left corner. Then tile the image. No setscreen needed.

subject: Non-DSC files and dxpsview
q: How can I force dxpsview to preview PostScript files that have no DSC comments? My program makes flashcards and doesn't know where the page breaks are.
a: You can't. Previewers need the DSC comments to know where pages end, and none of them stop at showpage. Learn to live with it. Add the %%Page comments or go without.

subject: Help: Overriding DIPS on LaserWriter IINTX
q: How can I override the dip switches on a LaserWriter IINTX with PostScript, so I can switch between LocalTalk and RS-232 without flipping switch #2?
a: There's a command for it: sethardwareiomode, where 2 is AppleTalk and 0 is RS-232, run via exitserver. Note the printer stops listening to the sending port afterward, so send an EOF from the new device. Read the red book.

subject: novice question - HP emulation
q: How can I switch a Dataproducts LZR 1260 PostScript printer into LaserJet emulation without the password or wearing out the EEPROM?
a: Somewhere in statusdict, serverdict or printerdict there's a procedure that starts the emulator. Older printers had hplj, so serverdict begin statusdict begin hplj. Hook up a serial terminal, run executive, dump the dictionaries with forall, and hunt for hplj or switchopen. Do the legwork.

subject: Fear and Loathing in Reverse Polish
q: How can I turn on Diablo 630 emulation mode on a PostScript laser printer via software, without burning EEPROMs?
a: Inside serverdict and statusdict, running diablo, hplj or hpgl will generally start that mode. Some printers use diabloexec instead. Connect over serial, type executive, then dump serverdict and statusdict with a forall and == to find what yours has. Do your homework.

subject: Using show inside a screen function...
q: How can I use show inside a PostScript screen function, so it prints the numerical gray-level value of each halftone cell instead of drawing the figure?
a: Go read Real World PostScript, the orange book. Pages 175-190 have a routine that prints the halftone dot patterns out clearly. Modify it slightly and you get the cell values. Read the book before asking the net.

subject: Configuring an Apple LaserWriter for 8-bit postscript
q: How do I configure a LaserWriter on a Sun printcap so all 8 bits get through to the printer? The parity bit seems to be stripped and I get garbage.
a: Try setting xc#040 in /etc/printcap. It turns on the tty driver's litout mode, meaning no output post-processing. Beware that certain control codes like ^D ^S ^Q ^T ^C can still get eaten on the serial line, and Adobe won't say how to get around it.

subject: Courier and ptroff.
q: How do I get Courier in troff with Transcript's ptroff on a LaserWriter? .fp 3 C and \fB don't work and everything comes out roman.
a: ptroff is bizarre. Courier isn't C, it's L, for Listing, so use \fL, with \f(LB and \f(LI for bold and italic. That's how it worked at our site; your mileage may vary. Welcome to troff.

subject: Sonata
q: How do I get Sonata? Is it public domain?
a: Public domain? Hardly. It's a commercial Adobe font package, one of their top sellers. Screen fonts may be on sumex.stanford.edu, but you'll want to buy it, and it's well under $100 from a mail-order house. Pay for it.

subject: Printing startup page on Laserwriters
q: How do I get an Apple LaserWriter to print its startup page on demand by sending PostScript?
a: Use the startpage operator, which lives in serverdict. Do serverdict begin, userdict begin, startpage, showpage, end end. Userdict is needed because serverdict is read-only and startpage needs dictionary space. Works on most printers, not all. Look it up yourself next time.

subject: Is there an MS-DOS world interactive enviroment for Postscript??
q: How do I get an interactive mode for PostScript working with a LaserWriter hooked up to an IBM AT?
a: Use any comm program like Procomm. Configure the port for parity and baud, then type executive in lowercase and press return. You're then talking to the LaserWriter's interpreter. Read the manual next time.

subject: How to include PS into Troff?
q: How do I include a PostScript figure in a Troff document? Is there a template?
a: Use Psfig, a free preprocessor like eqn. It needs PostScript with a %%BoundingBox line, and you must adapt your postprocessor to recognize its output. Alternatively, try the .cf command with a file ending in two dots. Experiment, it's not hard.

subject: Imagen w/ Ultrascript
q: How do I send PostScript directly to an Imagen printer running TURBO Ultrascript 4.1T? Magic first lines like %! don't work.
a: That's a spooler question, not a PostScript one. With the Imagen spooler software, use "ipr -Lultrascript". No incantation in the file header will help. Know your spooler.

subject: How does one debug PostScript?
q: How does one debug PostScript? I only have a Mac II and a LaserWriter Plus and I'm doing trial and error with writeln-like functions. Are there any tools that make this easier?
a: Get Lasertalk from Adobe; it's about the closest thing to a PostScript debugger, letting you step through interactively. GhostScript from GNU lets you preview on screen. Adobe's mail server also has ehandler.ps, which prints the error and an operand stack trace. Stop wasting paper.

subject: 8"x14" paper on LW IINT
q: I loaded 8x14 paper in a LaserWriter IINT and it jammed at the A4 position. The Mac driver only offers A4, B5, letter and legal. How can I print on 8x14 paper?
a: The printer notices the paper feed running long with no trailing edge and decides it's jammed. You haven't told it the paper is long. Send the command 'legal' or equivalent, and check you have a legal cassette. Or manually feed it with statusdict manualfeed true. Basic stuff.

subject: Converting GIF to Postscript?
q: Is it possible to convert GIF files to PostScript, and is there software to do it?
a: Sure, this comes up constantly. Try GIFTOPS, the Fuzzy Bitmap utilities (which even do color PostScript), or gif2ps from surya.waterloo.edu, which makes greyscale and nearly EPSF. You can also capture a displayed GIF with SCRtoPS.

subject: figuring out a bounding box
q: Is there a utility that finds a PostScript file's bounding box by intercepting the imaging commands and drawing just the box with its numbers?
a: You're thinking of BBFig. You can get it by anonymous FTP from ymir.claremont.edu, in the tex utilities psfigtex directory. Not wishful thinking, for once.

subject: Postscript to HPGL
q: Is there software to convert PostScript output to HPGL, so I can print on a LaserJet IIP or spool to HP plotters?
a: Wait a second. A LaserJet IIP is a PCL printer, not HPGL. HPGL to PostScript converters exist, but PostScript to HPGL is a step backwards: arcs differ and fonts become stick characters. You won't like the results.

subject: Real bottleneck 1200 bps on LaserWriter NTII
q: My LaserWriter NTII on a serial port from a PC (MODE LPT1:=COM2:) drops data at 9600 baud and only works at 1200. What's wrong?
a: Handshake, obviously. DOS can't do XON/XOFF through plain redirection, and LaserWriters ship set to software handshake. Send the printer the short command sequence from its manual to switch to DTR hardware handshake, and wire the cable for DTR/DSR. Or use a spooler like AST SuperSpool that understands XON/XOFF. Sigh.

subject: Getting printer to acknowledge End Of Job sooner
q: My PostScript printer on a network stays busy for about five seconds after a job finishes and drops new jobs sent in that time. How do I get it to acknowledge end of job sooner?
a: Send a control-D at the end of the job. It's part of the serial-line protocol, not PostScript, so the spooler should be adding it. You can also try the stop operator at the end of the file, which is portable. This comes up every week.

subject: HPIID laser printer problem with quotes (`')
q: On my HP IID laser printer the backquote and frontquote in Courier both look like tiny slashes. How can I fix this for Courier without rewriting every filter?
a: Two ways. Change the encoding vector in your fonts to remap the quote characters to the accent characters near octal 301 and 302, as the Blue book describes. Or put a sed filter before the printer converting quotes inside parentheses to \301 and \302. Not rocket science.

subject: 9600 bps bottleneck on Laserwriter Plus
q: Our Laserwriter Plus is on a 9600 bps serial line and big bitmaps take forever to send. Can the serial port run faster than 9600?
a: Yes, set the printer's baud rate higher with the command documented in your supplement, changing 9600 to 19200 or 38400. Don Lancaster runs his at 57K, though one-way only. Try it; you can always reset it. Rocket science, it isn't.

subject: Delays and PostScript printers
q: Plain text files sent to a PostScript printer right after a big, complex page get lost. How do I tell when the printer is ready for more input? Is there PostScript flow control?
a: Send a control-D after each job to mark end-of-job. Then wait for the printer to send a ^D back, which works on a serial connection. If none comes in 2 seconds, send another. When one returns, the printer is really ready. You'll need an output filter that does it. RTFM.

subject: PS file interpretation time
q: What's the average interpretation time of a PostScript file on a Dataproducts or Apple laser printer?
a: Can't be answered, PostScript is a full programming language. Roughly, a dense text page with a couple of line-art bits takes 2 to 10 seconds. A LaserWriter Plus needs 8 to 10, an NTX 4 to 6. Longer is your driver's inefficiency.

subject: Ghostscript residency?
q: Where can I FTP Ghostscript from, or any PostScript previewer for the IBM PC?
a: Try wuarchive.wustl.edu, in mirrors/msdos/Postscript. GS23.zip is there, plus the GS22 fonts, GS22fnta.zip through GS22fnte.zip. Next time, check the archive sites before asking the whole net.

subject: ? How to find ``Thinking in PostScript'' ?
q: Where can I buy Glenn Reid's monograph Thinking in PostScript?
a: It's from Addison-Wesley, by Glenn C. Reid, ISBN 0-201-52372-8. If your bookstore can't or won't order it, go direct to the publisher. Try that before posting to the net.

subject: PostScript fonts: German...
q: Where can I find PostScript fonts for old German script, the Fraktur or Gothic style? Adobe couldn't help.
a: The devps ditroff-to-PostScript translator from Pipeline Associates comes with converted Hershey fonts for Gothic German, English and Italian. They look quite good below 16 points and are passable up to about 20-24. Or roll your own with the public domain Hershey conversion programs.

subject: Looking for Arabic fonts
q: Where can I find an Arabic font, commercial or public?
a: Apple's Arabic system software 6.0.3 is $35 and comes with two PostScript fonts, part number M0008AB/C. You have to join APDA to order it, at 800-282-2732 in the USA. Bureaucracy, as usual.

subject: PostScript scaling off?
q: Why is a 5 inch line I sent to our LaserWriter Plus about 1/32 inch too long? Is that normal for these printers?
a: Yes, it's mechanical. The interpreter's 300 dpi frame buffer really is 5 inches, but feeding paper at a precise rate is hard, and engines are only nominally 300 dpi, within about 1 percent. Paper thickness matters too. Don't expect miracles from a cheap marking engine.

subject: Statusdict
q: Without the printer manual, is there any way to query a PostScript printer and print out what's in statusdict?
a: Easy. Run "statusdict {exch == ==} forall" to dump the contents to stdout. Or over a serial line, type "executive", then "statusdict {pop ==} forall" at the PS> prompt to list the keys. Contents vary by printer, so don't whine about it.

subject: Does Prolog have an unambiguous syntax definition?
q: Does Prolog have an unambiguous syntax definition? For example, with display(@ #), will it show @(#) or #(@), and why?
a: There is a document: the public-domain DEC-10 Prolog parser. Readers based on it give #(@), and nothing about it is ambiguous. A prefix operator followed by a right bracket, or by an infix or postfix operator of wider scope, is read as an atom. RTFM.

subject: inheritance in prolog
q: Does anyone have good Prolog code for managing objects with inheritance, especially multiple inheritance?
a: Look at Datr, from Roger Evans and Gerald Gazdar at the University of Sussex. It runs in cprolog or pop11, and as far as I recall it's free. Do your homework before posting.

subject: Definition of list_length/2
q: Is there a better or shorter definition of list_length/2 in Prolog that handles all cases and is deterministic for given calling patterns?
a: Your non-deterministic part isn't tail recursive. Use an accumulator instead: call a helper with 0 as the starting count, add one per element, and unify the count at the empty list. Always look out for that. Basic stuff.

subject: Journal of LP for Assoc. for LP members
q: Is there a discount on the Journal of Logic Programming for Association for Logic Programming members, and how do I get it?
a: Subscription for ALP members is $55 for the next year, and ALP membership is $25. Outside the US and Canada it's $76. I don't know the exact discount, and the price has been climbing steeply. Contact the ALP secretary for a form.

subject: unification in Prolog II
q: Is there a good description of the unification algorithm in Prolog II, especially how it deals with circular structures?
a: If memory serves, they keep a stack of equations as assumptions. Before unifying two trees, check the stack: if they're already postulated equal, succeed at once; otherwise push the equation and carry on. It's sketchy, but anyone who thinks it through gets the idea.

subject: Can I talk about Parlog here?
q: My Parlog parser from Conlon's book doesn't work consistently on the Sequent Symmetry, and I get segmentation errors after a few recompiles. Is it Parlog or me?
a: The parser is correct. The Parallel Parlog system on the Sequent forces deep guards, which the parser uses heavily, to be tried sequentially, not in or-parallel. Change the clause search operator to ';' in the procedures using deep guards. Take other questions to Imperial College.

subject: Hoary old question: Best Prolog for IBM PCs
q: What's the best Prolog for IBM PCs for teaching a logic programming course? We need a site license for about 20 PCs, nothing fancy, and not Turbo-Prolog or a typed Prolog.
a: Expert Systems International's offering is hard to beat for that. A public domain binary of their compiler is on FTP, and you only need to buy one manual. ALS Prolog is also decent, and there's an old free A.D.A. Prolog, if it still exists.

subject: where can I find...
q: Where can I ftp either NU-Prolog or SICStus?
a: You can't, at least not legally. Both need a license. Ask mip@munnari.cs.mu.OZ.AU for NU-Prolog and sicstus_request@sics.se for SICStus. Academic or teaching licenses run a few hundred US dollars. Nothing's free, kid.

subject: block and exit_block
q: Why were Prolog's exception-handling predicates named block and exit_block in the standard draft, rather than something more descriptive?
a: No idea where the names came from. The US committee recommended changing them to catch and throw, and the ISO committee agreed at its last meeting. The standards committees are part-timers, so even obviously bad ideas take ages to get cleared up. Hardly august.

subject: Anybody use KEDIT?
q: Does KEDIT for MS-DOS work like XEDIT? Can I write macros without buying the REXX interpreter, and will my XEDIT macros run unmodified?
a: It can be very like XEDIT, with extras like blocks. Macros work with the built-in small REXX called KEX; the REXX interpreter is optional, but must be resident. Whether your XEDIT macros run unchanged is a guess. Read the manual, not the net.

subject: REXX message answerer that eats CPU time...
q: Does anyone have a REXX exec that answers messages and eats CPU time every few minutes, so a student account doesn't get forced off the system while disconnected?
a: Your real problem is likely leaving the account in an interrupt state like VM READ while disconnected. After 15 minutes of that, it gets FORCE'd off. Use a program called GONE, or Eric Thomas' CHAT program, which has such an option. Or home-brew a loop around WAKEUP if you have IPF.

subject: Variable dump utilities?
q: Is there a utility that gives a complete dump of all variables in a Rexx program? Mine is over 4000 lines with lots of variables and arrays, and trace and say statements don't cut it.
a: There are public domain ones; look at MEMO REXX on VMSHARE. Or write it yourself: an assembly routine making EXECCOMM calls, asking for the next variable until none remain. They come back in random order, so sorting is your problem. That's VM/CMS only.

subject: Limitation with lambda
q: How can I create a recursive function on the fly with lambda in Scheme, such as a generator for the sum of squares, cubes or fourths based on an exponent? Lambda doesn't seem able to name itself.
a: Wrap it in a LETREC inside the lambda, with the body just calling the recursive function. Lisp 1.5 used LABEL for this, and Scheme's LETREC generalizes it to mutual recursion. You can even do it with the Y combinator, but that's inefficient. Read your history.

subject: Unquoting
q: In Scheme I defined operators as '(+ - * /), but ((car operators) 2 3) doesn't give 5. (car operators) evaluates to the symbol +, not the function. How do I get the function?
a: Your list holds symbols, not procedures. Write (define operators (list + - * /)), since list evaluates its arguments. If stuck with names, eval works, but it's roundabout and non-portable, as implementations disagree on the environment argument. Basic quoting, folks.

subject: ST-implementation scheme?
q: Is there an implementation of Scheme running on the Atari ST, and how and where can I get it?
a: Nobody here knows of an ST one. XScheme by David Betz is public domain, comes with C source, and shouldn't be hard to port. Grab xscheme-0.22 by FTP from gatekeeper.dec.com, orville.nas.nasa.gov or ftp.kth.se. Sigh, do the port yourself.

subject: Scheme for IBM PC compatible
q: Where can I get a reasonably cheap or free Scheme interpreter or compiler for an IBM PC?
a: Xscheme, the Scheme answer to Xlisp, is free by ftp from tut.cis.ohio-state.edu as /pub/Xscheme.tar. It's written in C and builds on PCs and Unixes. Or pay about $95 for TI's PC-Scheme, which is fast and well documented.

subject: Logic programming for Smalltalk-80
q: Does anyone have code for unification and deduction a la Prolog in Smalltalk-80?
a: Digitalk's Smalltalk/V, at least the Mac version, ships with a Prolog interpreter written in Smalltalk. Look in the box before asking the net, will you?

subject: Saving FORMs in Digitalk's Smalltalk V
q: How do you save a drawing (a FORM) to disk and load it back in Digitalk's Smalltalk V?
a: Use the object loader/unloader from Goodies #1 and elsewhere. Also look at the FREEDRAWING classes, which let you save FORMS to a dictionary; then save and reload that dictionary with the object loader. It's all in the Goodies, so read them.

subject: LaserMaster -- Any Ideas
q: What do people know about LaserMaster Corporation, which advertises 1000 by 1000 or 800 by 800 plain paper laser printers? Are they real?
a: They seem real. Around $18M revenue in nine months, and they bought an outline font supplier. They're PC and now Mac oriented, with Windows drivers. Halftones at 1000x400 is not a real typesetter, so ignore the hype.

subject: Wanted LSI simulator
q: I'm looking for a public domain LSI logic simulator or timing verifier. Also, what is Magic, and is it public domain?
a: Try the UC Berkeley tools. Magic is a layout editor where you draw poly, metal and contacts like the masks, with an incremental design rule checker built in. Berkeley distributes it for a fee, around $400, for shipping. This gets asked monthly.

subject: IC package acronyms ?
q: What do the various IC package acronyms mean: SOIC, PLCC, LCC? What is the black square package with small curved pins on all four sides?
a: SOIC is a small outline plastic package with gullwing leads on 50 mil centers, roughly a half-size DIP. PLCC is a plastic leaded chip carrier with J-shaped pins. LCC is usually a ceramic leadless chip carrier, probably what your 286 is in. Learn the alphabet soup before buying.

subject: A question on SPICE simulation
q: How should I model a very wide MOS transistor in a SPICE deck if I want to see the effect of source and drain diffusion contact width and spacing on the channel resistance?
a: Model it as a series of parallel transistors, with small resistors between the sources and small resistors between the drains. You can get fancier, but if source and drain resistance is all you care about, that's sufficient. Don't overthink it.

subject: PLA Benchmarks
q: Where can I get the Berkeley PLA benchmarks like ADD6, ADR4 and ALU1 used with espresso, or other common logic optimization benchmarks?
a: Try anonymous ftp to mcnc.mcnc.org, in pub/benchmark/synth89 and its subdirectories. The benchmarks from that book should also be on the Berkeley software distribution tapes. Use ftp, it's not hard.

subject: bad address problem
q: ELM extracts bad return addresses and dumps my reply into dead.letter without warning. Can ELM be changed to bring up the headers menu when the address is invalid?
a: Misunderstanding: your MTA rejected the address, not ELM. In config.h, undefine NOCHECK_VALIDNAME and DONT_TOUCH_ADDRESSES, define OPTIMIZE_RETURN, and play with USE_EMBEDDED_ADDRESSES. Test addresses with sendmail -bv. Know your own mailer.

subject: Need help with ELM on Apollo
q: ELM on an Apollo strips the initial slash from home directories like //node/users/foo, leaving /node/users/foo, which doesn't exist. Where should I fix ELM?
a: Something else is going on. ELM takes the home directory as is from getpwuid(3) and doesn't strip the slash. Check whether getpwuid on the Apollo removes the extra slash, or whether /etc/passwd has only a single one. Debug before blaming ELM.

subject: NFS mail spools with elm
q: Elm on an SGI 4D-320 running irix 3.3.2, with the mail spool NFS mounted from a Sun, complains of errno 46 (no lock available) when it flock()s the spool. Any fix?
a: Quit using BSD-ish flock() and switch to System V-ish lockf() or fcntl() locking. flock() doesn't work over NFS. Everyone trips on this eventually.

subject: Has anyone...
q: Has anyone compiled ELM on a NeXT machine? I want to read mail on it when I dial in.
a: Yes, elm 2.3 runs fine on a NeXT. Just try it next time instead of asking first.

subject: Multiply-defined alias
q: How do I create a mailing list alias in elm 2.1 like r_d = R & D Group = hostname!user1, hostname!user2? Elm bombs out with 'get_token calls nested greater than 20 deep'.
a: Read the Alias Users Guide. A group alias may only contain local names or prior elm aliases. Make individual aliases for each user, then build the list from those. And skip the & in the group name, since Berkeley mail rules may expand it.

subject: Problem with filters and aliases
q: I have a script called by an elm filter rule, and aliases don't work in it, though they work when I run it by hand. Absolute addresses work fine. Is there a trick to getting aliases to work in scripts called from filter rules?
a: Probably HOME isn't set, like scripts run from .forward on SunOS. Stick an "env" dump to a file in the script and look. If HOME is missing, elm can't find your .elm/aliases files. Basic debugging, really.

subject: Escaping '@' in Elm won't work on my UNIX-PC
q: I installed elm 2.1 on my UNIX-PC with the 3.5 software. At the To: prompt it treats '@' as the line kill character even when I escape it with a backslash. How do I enter user@foobar?
a: Known bug, fixed in 2.2, but that isn't out yet. Until then, change your line kill character to something else. Control-U is a decent pick, since lots of systems default to it anyway. Sigh.

subject: Elm needs update option.
q: I run elm in a suntools window and never quit it. Is there an update mailbox option that writes changes to the mailfile without leaving elm?
a: Elm already has one, so read the manual. Use the $ (resync) command. Alternatively, under 2.1, hit c to change mailbox and just press return at the name prompt. It prints resynchronizing file and makes all pending updates without exiting.

subject: Return receipt requested
q: In elm, when I request a return receipt it prompts for the mail path to return it to. Can I set something in my elmrc or use an alias so my return path is filled in automatically?
a: Put a Return-Receipt-To: line with your userid in your .elm/elmheaders file. Note it's mostly obeyed only by sendmail and can be switched off, and many sites do exactly that to cut the flood of extra mail. Don't count on it.

subject: Problems making documentation
q: When I run "make documentation" for Elm on my Xenix 2.3.3 system, troff says "Typesetter busy" and the make dies with error code 254. What is happening?
a: Your troff isn't set up for a real typesetter, and it's in the SCO FAQ already, so read it. Rerun Configure and, when it asks for the program to process manual pages, give /usr/bin/nroff instead of the troff default. The output is usable, if ugly.

subject: Where can I FTP latest version of Elm?
q: Where can I FTP the latest version of ELM that has all the patches installed?
a: Try anonymous ftp to wuarchive.wustl.edu and look under packages/elm. Honestly, this comes up every week, so read the archive lists before asking.

subject: Was there a vote on a new group comp.mail?
q: A newgroup message for comp.mail just arrived. I don't remember a vote on it, so should there be such a newsgroup?
a: Read the vote status and new groups summary files from news.announce.newgroups, available by ftp or the MIT mail server. They show no business for a group called comp.mail, so the newgroup is almost certainly bogus. Check before you believe every control message.

subject: Forwarding under VM
q: Can a VM user set up mail forwarding to a UNIX system like a .forward file? If so, how?
a: If the site runs XMailer, SM MAILER FORWARD user@host. If it runs Listserv, SM LISTSERV /FORWARD user@host. That one is an optional local mod. Your postmaster may have disabled either, so ask. Beware of forwarding loops.

subject: X400 mail to CompuServe ?
q: CompuServe has an X.400 gateway using c=us, a=CompuServe, p=CSMail and dda set to the user id with a dot instead of a comma. Is CompuServe only known as an ADMD to attmail, since mail from the UK failed?
a: CompuServe is a registered ADMD and connects to Attmail, with other connections in progress. CSMail is the only PRMD for now. Your address form is correct: c=us;a=compuserve;p=csmail;dda=100010.2464. If mail fails, show the non-delivery notice instead of guessing.

subject: Path To Griffith University, Australia
q: Does anyone have a mail path to Griffith University in Queensland, Australia?
a: Try au.oz.gucis, which is the Computer Science Dept. there. Next time check the maps before asking the whole net.

subject: Is there really no TURN command in sendmail's SMTP?
q: Does sendmail's SMTP really not support the TURN command? Has anyone hacked it in?
a: Sendmail really does not support TURN. I doubt anyone has hacked it in either, since it's a bigger deal than it looks: sendmail would have to read mail out of a mailbox and dig through headers. You'd be better off with uucp on the PC.

subject: How to find people, given their organization??
q: How can I find someone's email address when I know their university or company but not their machine? The PSI white pages and whois often fail.
a: Mailing postmaster at the domain works about 75% of the time, though don't expect a quick answer. Or phone the place, get the person's number, and ask. If they don't read mail regularly, forget email. Obvious, really.

subject: use of the maps for mailing list
q: I got junk mail from a company that clearly used the UUCP Maps, even though my map entry explicitly prohibits using it for mailing lists. Does anyone know who is extracting the data?
a: Nobody knows who. Companies have been mining the UUCP map entries for years. I don't see how anyone can forbid it, short of the map area coordinators putting disclaimers in the map files. Your little notice means nothing.

subject: how to use mail with preformatted file (including headers)
q: Is there a direct way with mail or sendmail to mail a preformatted file that includes its headers? Also, can I put comments in an alias file?
a: Feed it to sendmail directly: /usr/lib/sendmail -v user@site < mail_file. It adds From: and Date: lines for you. Comments in an alias file start with a hash in column one. Plain mail can't do the file trick, but mush can. Read the man pages.

subject: MHS (Novell) to SMTP Gateway available?
q: Is there an MHS (Novell) to SMTP gateway so a company LAN can take an internet news and mail feed securely? Off-the-shelf, public domain or shareware is fine.
a: Yes, SMTP to MHS gateways exist from Computer Mail Systems of Southfield, MI, and Da Vinci Systems of Raleigh, NC. For other MHS questions try the MHS hotline. Commercial only, I'm afraid; no freebie answer here.

subject: Sendmail 5.61/UK-1.4a
q: Sendmail 5.61 puts daemon in the top Unix From line for locally delivered mail, where 4.12 used the real sender. How do I get the old behaviour back?
a: It's a security fix. Add -r $f to the mailer args on your Mlocal line: Mlocal, P=/bin/mail, F=lsDFMmn, S=10, R=20, A=mail -r $f -d $u. That's the fix. Read your sendmail.cf, it isn't hard.

subject: Email IDs and Business Cards
q: What e-mail address should I put on my business cards so that people on all kinds of mail systems can reach me, given the many ways to address one account?
a: Put just the plain domain-style address, user@host.domain. It's pretty much the only universal format, and sites that can't handle it usually have docs for their users. Trying to list every possible route is a losing game, so don't.

subject: What is PROFS??
q: What is PROFS? Is it a public network, or just an IBM product name? Can I send e-mail to a friend whose company is connected to it?
a: PROFS isn't a network, sigh. It's IBM's office management and mail system running under VM, a calendar/mail manager/shell combo. Her company is likely on Bitnet, so mail her Bitnet address. Don't expect customer-to-customer mail through IBM's link.

subject: What is a Sponsor in Internet?
q: What is a sponsor in relation to the Internet?
a: Probably the old Arpanet rule: DARPA funded it, so an organization needed a DARPA contractee to sponsor its connection. Or maybe an internet forwarder, a site that gateways mail to a uucp site. Nowadays you just go through a regional network or a commercial provider. Ask them what they meant.

subject: Internet mail to JANET
q: What is the Internet address of NSFNET-RELAY for sending mail from the Internet to a JANET user?
a: Address it as user%JANET-site-name@nsfnet-relay.ac.uk. Yes, that's the way to do it. It's the percent hack; any idiot knows it.

subject: INTERBIT ADDRESS
q: What is the address format for sending mail through Interbit to BITNET? Is it user%node@interbit?
a: Interbit doesn't exist. It's a keyword some BITNET software uses to find a gateway, so there's no correct address. Let your Internet forwarding site choose the gateway, and ask its postmaster what it supports. user@node.BITNET is the usual form, if it handles that.

subject: Standard header for return-address
q: What is the standard mail header for a return address? I've seen Return-address, Return_address, Return-Path, Reply-To and so on.
a: Reply-To is the one that overrides From for human replies. Bounces go to the envelope sender or Sender. Return-Address and Return_address aren't commonly supported, and Return-Path is unreliable thanks to the way sendmail does it. A mangled From shouldn't exist in the first place, sigh.

subject: White Pages software
q: Where can I find currently available White Pages software, and who's selling X.500 code?
a: There's a distributed White Pages system on the Internet with hundreds of thousands of entries. Mail wp-info@psi.com, or telnet to wp.psi.net and log in as fred. It's built on ISODE, not Andrew. Reports are on uu.psi.com by anonymous ftp.

subject: Destination dependent name conversions And Smail 3.1.21
q: With Smail 3.1.21, how can I convert brinkema@funnynet to John_Brinkema@funnynet only when the destination is funnynet, without touching the name for other destinations? Alias files don't seem to fit.
a: If funnynet is a separate entity, it should do its own aliasing; nobody else needs to know. Otherwise hide it behind a gateway name and resolve through the gateway's alias file, or add a transports entry that calls an external program to do the translation. Don't make everyone else's problem.

subject: smail3.1.21: /usr/lib/aliases doesn't send mail to author of message
q: With smail 3.1.21, when I mail to an alias in /usr/lib/aliases that includes me, everyone gets a copy except me. Why, and how do I fix it?
a: smail defaults to "nometoo" behavior and strips the sender out of the alias expansion. Give smail the -m option, or set the generic director attribute sender_okay in the aliases director. Read the docs next time.

subject: mush used in news
q: Can mush create a my_hdr Reply-To based on the user's login directory, since userids truncate to 8 letters but home directories hold the full name? Also, how do I set up news to use mush instead of ucbmail for replying?
a: Sure: my_hdr Reply-To: "$home:t"@"$hostname:1". For news, ftp the Rnmush script from cse.ogi.edu:pub/mush, then read about MAILPOSTER in the rn man page. Not using rn? You're on your own.

subject: Wish list for "pick" and "mark"
q: Can mush's pick and mark commands be improved? I'd like to pick on To: and Cc: at once, match exactly, match just the local-part of an address, and have more than five priorities. How likely is that?
a: Multiple criteria is the likeliest, if anyone can come up with a syntax that isn't worse than find(1). You can already match exactly, since these are regular expressions, not file globs. Local-part would be slow, so write a regex. For more priorities, recompile with MAX_PRIORITY bigger, up to 10.

subject: Mush under SysVR4
q: Has anyone gotten the latest mush to work under SysVR4? I compiled it with the BSD makefile and some hacking of include files, but it sometimes aborts and asks to dump core.
a: Why on earth use the BSD makefile on a SysV box? Use the SysV one. The BSD compatibility package is just an add-on, and SysVr4 is SysV at heart. Also don't hack system include files, and use maillock(3x) instead of mush's own locking.

subject: Generating report headers with mush
q: How can I get mush's echo command to write to a temporary file so I can script a report banner and mail it, using only mush's scripting?
a: Use "sh echo ..." to get the /bin/sh echo, then redirect with >. For echo -h or -p features, try "eval -h sh echo ... > file" or the -p version. Custom headers with my_hdr and set edit_hdrs might already do it. Read the man page.

subject: replying to the From: line instead of the Reply_To: line
q: In mush, can I set up a macro to reply to a header other than Reply-To, such as the From line, like REPLY FROM in CMS Mail?
a: Sure, use cmd to set reply_to_hdr to the header you want and then reply. I define several commands that set it to from, the From_ line, or reply-to, and one that unsets it for the default. Silly names, but it works.

subject: Multiple address aliases
q: Mush 6.4 returns mail with an unrecognised address error when I send to an alias with several members. It seems to be the commas mush inserts. What's wrong?
a: Your MTA doesn't understand commas, and that's not mush's fault. Recompile mush with NO_COMMAS defined. It's described in config.h-dist and the README files, which you'd know if you'd read them.

subject: How to create a mail digest
q: Mush has a command to undigest a mail digest, but is there one to create a digest? If not, what do you use to build them?
a: The mush 7.1 distribution has a script called "digestify", with a cmd alias, that packs a folder of messages into a digest. No table of contents or lead-in, but undigest will read it fine. Read the distribution next time.

subject: Some green-user MUSh questions...
q: Some mush questions: can I remove the delete binding from the middle mouse button in Sunview, can mushtool re-read the folder directory without exiting, and can I increase the characters allowed in autosign2?
a: Middle button: no, unless you hack the code and recompile. Folders: with walking menus, the save command rebuilds the menus; folders made by other programs never get added automatically. Autosign2: the Options field scrolls, and editing ~/.mushrc directly allows up to 1024 characters. Read the man page.

subject: Forwarding and Resending Mail
q: What's the best way in mush to forward or resend a message to someone else, possibly editing it, with headers like Originally-To and Forwarded-From?
a: Use mail -Eef to edit headers, run the editor and forward, then delete most of the headers mush supplies so the original's headers below the forwarded line are used. Rename To: to Originally-To: by hand. Or write cmd aliases, though that only handles the current message.

subject: Creating a new folder by mistake - Minor suggestion
q: Wouldn't it be nice if mush asked whether to create a folder when I name a nonexistent one in the Cc: or Bcc: line, in case I misspelled it?
a: It's a dwim feature, do what I mean. Most of the time you know you're creating a new file and don't want nagged, which is what I dislike about elm. If you want prompting, there's a verify variable, so set it.

subject: Tools to analyze mail log
q: Does anyone know of tools that will analyze a sendmail log, with statistics like number of messages and bytes to and from by host or user? C, awk or perl, I don't care.
a: There's a perl script called fromto that lists from/to pairs out of the syslog file. It's not full statistics, so you'll have to hack it into what you want. It's on sh.wide.ad.jp by anonymous ftp, pub/fromto.0.1.shar. Do some of the work yourself.

subject: Getting a Return-receipt: line within mail headers
q: How can I include a "Return-receipt:" line in the header of a mail message? Xenix mail allows it, but most SYSV and BSD mail systems don't. Is there a way short of editing the D.* files in the spool directory?
a: Stop thinking the builtin mail command is the only way to make mail. Write the message in an editor with a Return-Receipt-To: header, then an empty line, then the body, and feed it to /usr/lib/sendmail -t. MH also lets you put any header you like.

subject: MX records for "random-host.bitnet", how?
q: How do some hosts return MX records for arbitrary bitnet nodes, like random-host.bitnet? How is it done?
a: They just have a wildcard MX pointing to a small number of Bitnet gateways. The root nameservers don't know about it, so you'd have to point at their server, which you wouldn't want. Set up your own with gateways closer to you. Understand nameservers first.

subject: sendmail for SCO Unix v3.2.2
q: I want to replace mmdf with sendmail on my SCO Unix 3.2.2 box. Does anyone have a sample sendmail.cf where everything non-local goes to a smart host?
a: Log in as root and run "mkdev sendmail-init", then follow the menus. The .cf is on target, though it favors uunet for mail it can't resolve locally. Note SCO doesn't support sendmail at all. Their MMDF docs are lousy, too.

subject: configuring sendmail for UUCP connection
q: I'm configuring sendmail for a UUCP connection on a Sun. Mail to the UUCP node works only from my machine, and from the UUCP node outward I get a uux -1 error. How do I get other machines' mail to go out?
a: Figure out where the error is generated. If it's local, your UUCP mail isn't reaching the host with the modem. Put in an S0 rule like R$*.$*.UUCP $#ether $@modem_host$:$1@$2.UUCP, which punts all UUCP mail to the modem machine over the ether. Basic stuff.

subject: sendmail and MB records
q: Is there a way to configure sendmail to look up users via MB records in the nameserver?
a: Not out of the box. You add resolver routines that look up MB and MG records and return a comma separated list of addresses, then make minor changes to alias.c. Umich has them in their bind 4.8.1 tarball. Do your homework.

subject: Pathalias & a local file
q: Is there a way with pathalias to have a local map entry that only my site uses, such as saying I talk to a neighbor ten times a day when the public map says once a week? Is that done with a local file?
a: Yes, make a file with your local information and feed it to pathalias as the first input. Put that file first in the pathalias run, usually from a weekly cron script. That's how it has always worked, so go read the pathalias docs.

subject: "remote from somewhere" -- I'm confused
q: On 4.3BSD, rmail turns the From line into things like somewhere!dce@host or uunet!hpda.hp.com!tnguyen, which is no good. How can I get a clean user@host address without using smail?
a: Rmail is only meant as the mailer your UUCP neighbors invoke. Make rmail a link to sendmail so it uses the From: header, and your sendmail config decides the form. Or add rules turning uucp-neighbor!domain-host!user into user@domain-host. Sigh, read your config.

subject: Unknown user forwarding?
q: Our uucp sites can't use our aliases file, so they must address mail to us explicitly. Can sendmail on those machines notice that a user isn't local and rewrite the address to user@ our domain, or must I wrap /bin/mail?
a: Don't reinvent the wheel with a wrapper, sendmail can do it. Keep a file class of local logins cut from /etc/passwd, then add a rule in ruleset 0 sending any simple username not in that list to the other host. Learn your .cf file.

subject: Problems with Sendmail 5.64+IDA (from UIUC)
q: Sendmail 5.64+IDA from UIUC builds a wrong route for a domain when pathalias has only a .bar.com entry and no foo.bar.com line. Does anyone have a fix?
a: That's a bug in ruleset 19, fixed a couple of weeks ago. Near the end of S19 there's a rewrite rule with an 'S+' instead of '$+' on the left side. Change the 'S' to '$'. Better still, pick up a new Sendmail.mc, since you're running stale code.

subject: looking at macros
q: When debugging a sendmail.cf file, how can I display the value of a macro, or of a class defined with an F line?
a: First, an F line defines a class, not a macro. Macro definitions can be seen with -d35.n, while class definitions only show up if you dump all the symbol stuff with -d36.n, where n is a small positive integer. Learn your terminology.

subject: Multiple recipients in smail/sendmail
q: Why does sendmail with smail as the external mailer make multiple copies of a message with many recipients, even with the 'm' flag set? Does the flag only work for the same host?
a: Ruleset 0 yields a mailer, host and user tuple, and tuples are sorted by mailer and host. Make every host resolve to the SAME CONSTANT STRING, with the full address in the user part. Then the multiple-recipient flag works. Read the config, not just the flag.

subject: mail and 'quit' problem
q: With /usr/spool/mail NFS-mounted from a server on AIX, mail freezes on the clients when users type quit. What's causing it?
a: Known bug, not your setup. It's tracked as APAR IX18805 and is being worked on. Meanwhile, expect to read mail somewhere else. Welcome to NFS and mail spools, where this sort of thing happens every week.

subject: How do I contact a friend at Penn State?
q: A friend at Penn State sent me mail from node psuvm with the login rps3. How do I reply from my UUCP site?
a: Try att!gatech!psuvax1!psuvm.bitnet!rps3. Given att's and psuvax1's connections, that route should work. Bang paths, who needs them, but there you go.

subject: 1/2-speed receiving!
q: After restoring my system, my UUCP inbound speed is half what it used to be, though outbound is fine. Why?
a: Probably a different dialer script or uucico got restored. Somewhere between SysVr3.0 and 3.2 the g protocol window default went from 3 to 7. With a spoofing modem, .xferstats only shows the time to fill your modem's buffer, so don't trust it.

subject: How & where is the uucp mapping project
q: Could someone point me to information on the uucp mapping project? I've seen the postings in comp.mail.maps but don't know where to go for more information.
a: Send an e-mail request to uucpmap@rutgers.edu, or ...!rutgers!uucpmap if you must. That should get you all the info you need. Try asking the people who run it before the whole net.

subject: uucico timeout
q: How can I change the timeout uucico waits after a failed call? Mine waits an hour and I want it to retry more often.
a: Put it in the time field of the Systems file. For HDB, add ";timeout" after the time; for L.sys, add a comma and the timeout, as in "Any,20". It's in TFM, as you claim to have read. One reply said it worked on SysIII.

subject: A Silly Question...
q: How do I split a 176k archive to send via mail? Will uudecode recognize the parts and append them into one file?
a: Use shar 3.49 with the proper flags; it compresses, uuencodes and splits, and you reassemble by running each piece with sh. Or just use split, then the recipient does cat x.a* into the file. Sigh, basic stuff.

subject: UUCP Documentation Wanted
q: I need detailed instructions for setting up UUCP, ideally a book that also covers UUCP internals. Anybody know a good title?
a: Get "Managing UUCP and Usenet" from O'Reilly, one of the Nutshell Handbooks. It's about $12, covers BNU (HoneyDanBer) as well as old Version 2 UUCP, and has material on debugging connections. Sigh, a book exists for this and you still asked the net.

subject: A Few more Questions...
q: Is there a list of all the public Usenet newsgroups, and where can I get it?
a: The List of Active Newsgroups is posted periodically in news.lists. If it has expired, FTP it from pit-manager.mit.edu under /pub/usenet/news.lists, or mail the mail-server there. Also read the periodic informational postings, which you should have done already.

subject: Is there a UUPC providing UUCP file transfer?
q: Is there a version of UUPC that provides UUCP file transfer? The one I have works for mail but has no uucp or uux command.
a: uupc just transfers files as directed by the job files in the spool directory. Write a small program that creates a simple C. job file naming the file to send, and optionally copy the file to a D. file. Look at the source or sample C. files for the format.

subject: Send vs receive times
q: My systems send UUCP data faster than they receive it, say 210 bytes/sec sending against 176 receiving. Anyone else notice this? Any thoughts?
a: Simple. Reads on existing files are nearly always faster than writes to new files, because writing means the filesystem has to allocate disk blocks. Same reason dumps run much faster than restores. Think a moment before posting.

subject: Forwarding Mail
q: On my Microport Sys V/AT, uucp's mail forwarding works one day and then the mailbox disappears and only holds one day's worth of mail. Any ideas?
