a: Look at /usr/lib/uucp/uudemon.clean. It runs daily from root's crontab and does rm -f $MAILDIR/uucp, so the mailbox vanishes no matter what. Comment out that line and forwarding will survive. Read your daemon scripts, for pity's sake.

subject: 2 SCO Unix HDB UUCP's aren't talking... Help?
q: On two SCO Unix HDB UUCP systems, one can send to me but not the reverse, and the log just says REQUEST FAILED. I found a one-byte A. file and a C. file with the same extension. What is going on?
a: That's normal. The A. file is uucico's own sort of lockfile while it processes the matching C. file, and it comes and goes with each outgoing job. The connection may simply have broken, which happens. Not a mystery.

subject: Sendmail-SMTP problem
q: Our 4.2BSD sendmail talking SMTP to some Internet sites sends the data and the terminating dot, then times out waiting for a reply with a 'read reply' error, and the message stays in the queue. Anyone seen this?
a: Likely the receiver doesn't send its 250 OK until it has successfully saved the message. If the receiving system is busy, or can't finish queuing, you time out. If you do get the 250 after the terminator, then my theory is wrong and the receiver has some other problem.

subject: Suggestions for assigning pathalias value for grey-area connectivity
q: What pathalias cost should I give a site I poll from cron each night only when there's a workfile? DEMAND seems wrong and so does EVENING.
a: It's EVENING. Don't go lower, like DEMAND plus LOW, or mail gets routed through you when another path would avoid a ten-hour wait. Also poll every day or two to keep minimal reverse connectivity. Read the pathalias docs again.

subject: HoneyDanBer uucp question
q: When I call System V HoneyDanBer UUCP sites they say "You are unknown to me", though they can call me fine. What do I tell their administrators to set up in Systems and Permissions? It seems tied to my long system name.
a: Some uucp implementations send only the first 6 or 7 characters of the system name. If yours does, that truncated name must be in the MACHINE and VALIDATE fields. LOGNAME is limited to 8 characters. Expect smail grief too, naturally.

subject: Which headers may Sendmail re-write?
q: Which headers may sendmail rewrite? Our gateway machine rewrites the To: and From: fields on forwarded mail, like user@toaster becoming toaster!user@gatebox. Is that acceptable, or should only Received: and Path: be touched?
a: Sigh. When a gateway sends mail into the Internet, every @host in the headers has to be a fully-qualified domain name that Internet hosts can resolve. RFC822 requires domain form, not bang paths. A bare uucp name like toaster is not valid, so the rewriting is rescuing you from broken replies.

subject: pathalias ignores fast Internet connections
q: Why does pathalias route mail to Internet hosts like user@machine.berkeley.edu through UUCP to ucbvax instead of the fast Internet connection?
a: It's not a smail flaw, it's the UUCP map data. Internet domains like berkeley.edu shouldn't be in the map at all. Delete them, and with a .edu uunet!%s line in your paths, you'll get the optimal route. Sigh, clean up the maps.

subject: Smail is a snail mailer?
q: Why were messages sent from West Germany to my site in the NTT domain delivered through a long chain of sites, including one in Japan? Is smail to blame?
a: Maps show a link from nttlab to nttca, so mcvax figures the best way is via nttlab and kddlabs. Mail then bounces back to the US. The cause is the Japanese network being split into three parts, and no routing software understands that.

subject: UUCP polling interval
q: With BNU UUCP, can I set a minimum idle interval between successful calls, so outbound mail goes on demand but doesn't make lots of 20-second calls all day?
a: No, there's no such thing. What you really want is not calling if another job is about to show up, which is much harder to deduce. The easy approximation: leave the -r on the uux and run uusched at the frequency you're willing to call.

subject: Increase the time-out in HDB uucico?
q: uucico in HDB UUCP times out before the remote modem answers, though it takes about 50 seconds when I dial by hand. Is there a way to increase the timeout?
a: Try the easy fixes first. Add commas to the end of the phone number, since each is worth 2-5 seconds on a Hayes. Then put some delay in your login script, like several \d's before the first expect. Sigh, basic stuff.

subject: International Character Sets
q: Can somebody point me to standards on international character sets?
a: Look at the ISO 8859 standards. 8859/n covers it, where n=1 through 4 give you four slightly different Latin alphabets and n=7 is Greek. Go read them, it's what they're for.

subject: Cray Research Cancels Chen's Project
q: Cray Research cancelled Steve Chen's project and he resigned. What was the project he was working on?
a: The Cray MP, a massively parallel machine with 64 or 128 processors versus 2 or 4 on current Crays. Cost estimates passed $100 million, so Cray pulled the plug. Needed several breakthroughs, so the estimates were guesswork. Probably the right call.

subject: 4mm DAT Tapes
q: Does anyone know a reasonable source for 4mm DAT tapes?
a: This comes up all the time. One shop that sells recording media to music studios sold a box of 50 Maxell 2-hour DATs at a decent price. Just ask what brands of 120 minute DATs they carry and the price at your quantity. Don't confuse them with details.

subject: BIX on the Network?
q: How can I reach someone on BIX from NetNorth, Usenet or the Internet? What gateway address do I use?
a: Look in the Inter-Network Mail Guide. It says to try user@dcibix.das.net. Next time read the guide before bothering the whole net.

subject: Pronouncing hexadecimals
q: How do people pronounce hexadecimal numbers like C00000 or FF000000? I said "CEE ZERO THOUSAND" and my co-worker thought I meant C0000.
a: Don't say "thousand", because it means three zeroes in English, Chinese and Japanese, and hex isn't grouped in threes. Say "Cee and five zeroes", or "cee zero", pause, "zero zero zero zero". Some folks use "blah" for enough zeros to fill out a 32-bit word, like "F blah".

subject: SoundBlaster device drivers for 386 unix
q: How does a SoundBlaster card interface to a PC, and will it need a device driver under 386 Unix? Which interrupts can it use, and is it worth the money?
a: It uses I/O ports, standard at 220H, and a selectable interrupt, plus DMA. You'll probably need a driver to make it work under Unix. Don't pay over $150, mail order price. Games folks swear by it, ugh.

subject: 68882 pronunciation?
q: How does one pronounce the name of the 68882 chip? "Sixty-eight, eight eighty-two" is unwieldy. Any better suggestions?
a: Just call it "the FPU", and if you must say which one, "eight eighty two", same as the 387 on a 386 box. Some say "six triple eight two". If the number scares you, stay away from electronics, everything has one.

subject: What kind of archive is .arc ??
q: I found a file called corewar.arc and can't find a de-archiver for it on my Sun3. What kind of archive is .arc?
a: It's from the IBM-PC world. Find PKPAK by Phil Katz, a shareware program on most BBSs or at Simtel20; it's distributed as the self-extracting PK361.EXE. Needs a PC, I'm afraid; no idea about a Sun version.

subject: Trouble accessing Cleveland FreeNet
q: I got an account on Cleveland FreeNet, but my machine doesn't recognize freenet-in-a.cwru.edu or the b and c variants when I telnet. What are the numeric addresses?
a: Try 129.22.8.82, or swap the last number for 75, 76, 77 or 78. Sigh, if your host can't resolve names, fix your nameserver setup instead of asking the net for numbers.

subject: Julian day numbers
q: In Numerical Recipes' Julian day routine, why is the constant 30.6001 instead of 30.6? Isn't the 0.0001 irrelevant?
a: Because 30.6, which is 153/5, has no terminating binary representation. Floating point might give you something slightly under 30.6, so INT(30.6*5) could come out 152 instead of 153. The small fudge factor prevents that. Basic floating point, people.

subject: Acronyms. Is is `1 MIP' or `1 MIPS'?
q: Is it `1 MIP' or `1 MIPS'? I thought MIPS stood for Mega-Instructions Per Second, so why do people drop the S?
a: Since MIPS is an acronym for a plural, MIP for the singular is an obvious back-formation. I've seen the same with irregular plurals like matrices and parentheses, which is far more annoying. Language rot, that's all.

subject: voltages
q: Is there a power converter in the UK to run 110 volt USA equipment on the 240 volt UK system? How much, and where from?
a: Just use a small autotransformer wired to halve the 240 volts. It cost about $20 at a local electrical store. The computer runs on DC with regulators, so it needn't be fancy. Even a small one is heavy, so don't whine about the weight.

subject: How to direct follow-ups ??
q: Once in a while someone posts to several groups with follow-ups directed to only one group. How is this done?
a: Edit the headers when your newsreader, like rn, brings up the followup in your editor. Put the group you want in the Followup-To line and change Newsgroups if needed. Yes, you can edit headers. Also trim the References line while you are in there.

subject: Free consulting service; what's the catch?
q: Someone phoned offering free computer consulting paid for by vendors like IBM. What's the catch?
a: The catch is he wants a look at your modems, password files and phone numbers, and the root password so he can install some software. It's a scam, seen it before. Don't let him in the door.

subject: Isn't that postcard kid dead?
q: Wasn't that kid in Surrey, UK collecting postcards for a record dead? Is the postcard thing legit or not?
a: Apparently legit. CBC news reported he got enough cards for the Guinness Book, over 1.4 million against the roughly million needed, and he thanked everyone. Stop passing faxes along.

subject: negative ion generator and computer
q: What effect will a negative ion generator have on my PC? Could it damage it? And has anyone had experience with them?
a: Nobody says it'll fry the PC, but it charges dust particles so they cling to the nearest surface. Everything near it gets filthy and caked with dust, walls included. Keep it far from the PC, use dust covers, and expect more cleaning.

subject: what does ascii ftp do to a binary file?
q: What exactly happens to a binary file when it is sent by ftp in ascii mode? It seems some bytes are removed, and I want to fix files that were sent wrong.
a: Oh, for crying out loud. Take a file dump program and compare a file sent in binary mode against one sent in ascii. Then you'll know what happens on your own configuration, instead of asking the net to do it for you.

subject: Ftp site list sought
q: Where can I find a list of ftp sites with a brief description of their contents? I remember one at 'pilot.odin.nj' but must have the address wrong.
a: Try the garbo archive, which has a copy of that list as /pc/doc/ftpsites.lst. There's also /pc/pd2/moder.lst covering MsDos sites and their moderators. Keep better track of addresses next time.

subject: Exabyte (8mm) versus DAT (4mm)
q: Which is a better backup device for a heterogeneous network, Exabyte 8mm or DAT 4mm? DEC argues DAT is inherently better because it was designed for digital data while 8mm is an analog video format.
a: The design origin argument is rubbish, since both just record flux changes on magnetic media, and DAT was designed for sound anyway. Both are new, so there's little known about long-term reliability. Ask whether you can get your data back after years, and whether the interface handles spacing and multiple images.

subject: HCI and VR newsgroups
q: Are there Usenet newsgroups dealing with Human-Computer Interaction and Virtual Reality?
a: Try comp.human-factors and comp.cog-eng for HCI, and sci.virtual-worlds for virtual reality. If you're feeling adventurous, alt.cyberspace. The alt.cyberpunk lot is the lunatic fringe. This comes up every week.

subject: Keyboard Recommendation Wanted
q: Can someone recommend a good MIDI keyboard for $1000 or less with at least 61 velocity-sensitive keys, multi-timbral, to use with a PC sequencer? I'm eyeing the Yamaha SY22 and Roland JX-1.
a: Get a Roland D-5, in the $550 to $600 range. Still love mine. Spend the money you save on other MIDI and studio gear instead of overpaying for the shiny one.

subject: FTP sites for soundblaster software
q: Does anyone know of any FTP sites that carry Soundblaster software, even just demos?
a: Try ccb.ucsf.edu, mostly .VOC voice samples, and sequent.mcs.kent.edu for lots of music and programs. chyde.uwasa.fi has a few things too. Stanford's kfps-roble6-dynamic is supposedly good, but good luck connecting. Read the archives next time.

subject: Silicon Graphics machine as audio workstation
q: I hear a new Silicon Graphics machine around $10k has audio better than the NeXT and a built-in DAT drive. What is it, and what do you know about it?
a: It's the Indigo. It has AES/EBU digital I/O, stereo 18-bit D/A, 16-bit delta-sigma A/D, up to 48 kHz, and a MIPS R3000. You can record CD/DAT quality straight to disk, and a DAT drive is available. Do your homework on the driver.

subject: Whats is a 'Quick Disk' or something sounding like that.?
q: What is a "Quick Disk"? A friend wants me to buy one for his musical group, something with "2 8" in the name. Is it a QD drum, or what?
a: It's a floppy disk format, double sided, 2.8 inch, used in some samplers and typewriters, not a drum. Roland-type keyboard gear used them, so try a music store. Around $30 for a box of ten. Sigh, ask your friend next time.

subject: Definition of "computer music"
q: What is the proper definition of "computer music"? Does it include "electronic music"?
a: Computer music is a label for audio signals that were in some way affected by computer technology. Sigh, it's a loose label, and the word music makes people think strictly of sound anyway.

subject: What compilers are there for Eiffel or Smalltalk?
q: Are there free or inexpensive implementations of Eiffel and Smalltalk for Unix or MSDOS?
a: A Little Smalltalk, from Timothy Budd's book, is one. GNU has a Smalltalk too, complete but with no windowing interface yet, ftp from prep.ai.mit.edu. For Eiffel, Sather is Eiffel-like, smaller and faster, at icsi-ftp.berkeley.edu. Try ftp before posting.

subject: Views in OO languages
q: How can a view on a class, like in database environments, be implemented in an object-oriented language?
a: For simple restriction, subclass the class and stub out the methods you want hidden, recoding the rest as needed. For complicated joins, multiple inheritance works better than single, and the usual tricks for faking it still apply. Not rocket science.

subject: OO Languages with "constraints" (Was: Subclassing vs. subtyping)
q: Which object-oriented languages let you formally specify constraints that keep the redundant information in a class self-consistent?
a: In Eiffel you write the constraint as a class invariant, though you still implement it and the system only does some checking. OBJ2 lets you express equational constraints. OO logic programming languages, where classes are sets of facts, might add clausal ones easily.

subject: Reading RT-11 format 5-1/4 inch disks in a PC/AT
q: How can I read RT-11 format 5-1/4 inch floppies on a PC/AT so I can get the data to our VAX?
a: Why bother with a PC/AT at all? If the goal is just getting data to the VAX, try VMS EXCHANGE with an RX50 drive. Think before you post.

subject: Gateway between internet and IEEE Compmail
q: How do I send email between IEEE Compmail and the Internet?
a: Mail to user INTERMAIL, at intermail@isi.edu from the Internet. Put a blank line, then Forward: ARPA or COMPMAIL, then a To: line with the destination address, then another blank line and your message. Not rocket science.

subject: How to Pay (Re: US$ drawn on a US bank)
q: USENIX won't take cheques on foreign banks, even in US dollars. What's the easiest and cheapest way to pay from Europe?
a: Get a traveller's cheque in the proper currency from your bank. It's the easiest and cheapest option, compared with wiring money, post office guaranteed cheques, or cash. Only the smallest denominations, around $10 to $15, can bite you. Bureaucrats.

subject: Getting to the Grand K
q: What are the options for getting from DFW airport to the Grand K hotel, some 30 miles away, besides a taxi?
a: Take a shuttle. Super-shuttle and other no-name limo services run regularly, and during prime time you just flag one down, marked North Dallas. On the red-eye, courtesy-phone them. It costs far less than a cab, though you'll tour scenic Carrolton on the way.

subject: FAQ?
q: Is there a FAQ for comp.os.aos, and where can I get it?
a: Are you kidding? There are no FAQs, no frequent postings here. Newbies expect everything handed to them.

subject: Coherent questions
q: Can Coherent use expanded memory, can I get around its 64K code segment limit, and is there an improved shared memory driver with shmat and shmdt?
a: Expanded memory is no good to Coherent. EXTended is, so learn the difference: motherboard memory is extended, add-in card memory is expanded. The 64K+64K limit is hard-coded in the kernel and the p3 kernel doesn't fix it. Read your manual.

subject: Copy from Coh to DOS
q: How can I read an MS-DOS disk from Coherent and copy files between them?
a: Use the dos command. For a 1.2M 5.25 disk, mount /dev/fha0 on /f0, then run dos xa for text or dos x for binaries, with a dot for the current dir. 360k disks are /dev/fh9a. It's in the Lexicon. Read it.

subject: bnews/cnews available?
q: Is there a news system, like bnews or cnews, available for Coherent to connect it to USENET? TASS looks like only a newsreader.
a: Cnews is available for Coherent, an older version that works okay. It's a 700K-plus tar file on mwcbbs. An older rn exists too. Be ready for LOTS of hard disk activity, which is what you get for running news.

subject: adding a hard disk to your floppy-only system
q: Can I add a hard disk to my floppy-only S100 CP/M system and boot from either the hard disk or a floppy, the way the Kaypro 10 did?
a: Yes, plenty of us have. Replace the boot ROM so it uses the hard disk controller, ideally trying the hard drive first and then falling back to a floppy. You'll probably have to roll your own, so you need the old ROM source and an EPROM burner. Welcome to S100.

subject: How "hard" is CR-LF
q: How "hard" is the CR-LF sequence in CP/M? I want to read a text file line by line and need a definite place to terminate the line. Can I count on LF being last and CR before it?
a: Quick and dirty: ignore the CRs and treat \n as the line terminator. Works in DOS and CP/M most of the time, and ports to Unix unchanged. Wastes a few CPU cycles checking for CRs that aren't there. Cry me a river.

subject: (none)
q: I heard a rumor that ArpaNet plans to cut its connections to the rest of the world, so archives like simtel-20 would no longer be reachable by FTP. Is that true?
a: Sort of. DARPA stops funding ArpaNet in April or May, but connectivity stays if each university or company pays to manage its own connection, rumored at $30k to $75k to start plus the same per year. Some will flee the net. Whether simtel-20 survives, who knows.

subject: Looking or CPM to DOS conversion...
q: I'm looking for software packages to convert from CP/M to MS-DOS. Any suggestions?
a: 22DISK from Sydex. It's shareware, on most bulletin boards, and converts, formats and copies CP/M and DOS disks for a huge number of CP/M machines. It's simple to use. This comes up constantly; go grab it.

subject: Kaypro and Spinwriter 7710
q: My friend's Kaypro 4 won't talk to an NEC 7710 Spinwriter. Output to LST:, PRN:, etc. hangs as if waiting on DTR, even with matching 1200 baud, 8 bit, no parity. What am I missing?
a: The 7710 uses hardware handshaking, so your cable matters. Run CONFIG.COM to set parameters and STAT.COM to reassign logical devices. Read the CP/M manual. Kaypro did strange things to its RS-232, as everyone does; "The RS-232 Solution" covers it.

subject: Kaypro 10 backup
q: What can I use to back up the 10M hard drive on a Kaypro 10, and where can I get a public domain C compiler for it?
a: The public domain sources have pretty well dried up. Small C exists for the Kaypro 10, but it's a real pig: slow, limited syntax, and no include function, so you recompile stdio.h every time. Beggars can't be choosers.

subject: Demise of Micro Cornucopia--What happened?
q: What happened to Micro Cornucopia? My user group got a letter saying it ceased publication with no explanation.
a: The last issue spelled it out, so read it. Subscriptions were fine; the editor simply burned out after a lifetime of publishing it. Groups offered to carry it on, but he wouldn't approve any deal over money and quality worries. Sigh, a good journal gone.

subject: nohup on Eunice?
q: How can I run a Eunice background job that survives logout of the login shell? Normal tricks with process groups and hangup signals don't work.
a: Use the VMS batch queue. From the Eunice prompt, "vms submit/noprint/nolog/notify/restart test.com" fired off and completed fine on Eunice 4.2. Don't expect real detached jobs, since VMS only allows that with DETACH privilege, which is a stupid security model.

subject: 486 support, ESDI configuration
q: Does Mach run on a 486 machine, and are there known incompatibilities with AT bus 486 boxes?
a: Yes. Mach 2.5 and 3.0 run fine on a 486 PS/2 Model 95 with no processor problems at all. The only trouble was the SCSI disk driver. An AT bus 486 should work too, all else being equal. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: What object format does mach use? BSD a.out? Coff? Macho?
q: What object format does Mach use? Is it BSD a.out, COFF, or Macho, and does it vary with architecture?
a: Mach ports normally support the native 4.3 object file format plus their own MACH-O format, which has directives to load register sets, create threads, and so on. NeXT dropped a.out loading in 0.9 and 1.0, but atom(1) converts a.out to MACH-O. Grumble.

subject: Mach RPC Throughput...
q: Why is Mach RPC throughput so much slower than other OSes in published comparisons? Are the RPCs too different to compare, or just not optimized?
a: You're comparing old Mach against newer competitors. Those figures come from Mach 2.5 or earlier. Mach 3.0 had its RPC completely rewritten, and a null RPC dropped from 210 to 125 microseconds. Read the revised IPC interface paper. Check your dates.

subject: mach_port_allocate_name
q: Why is mach_port_allocate_name in the kernel interface? It seems to only make implementations harder, and mach_port_insert_right should be restricted to previously extracted names. Am I missing the rationale?
a: Yes, you're missing it. A server can use mach_port_allocate_name so port rights match addresses of its data structures, saving a table lookup. The GNU emulator uses mach_port_insert_right to give a forked child rights under the same names, and your restriction would break that.

subject: Why isn't Mt. Xinu offering a Mach binary distribution?
q: Why isn't Mt. Xinu offering a Mach binary distribution? A binary kit would avoid the need for a UNIX source license, so the market should be bigger.
a: They are considering it but haven't announced anything. They have to work out whether the market is big enough, what price is right, and whether it'd be profitable. They want to hear what hardware and price make sense. Typical vendor dithering.

subject: V1.3 cat /dev/null != EOF ? (have you seen this?)
q: After building Minix 1.3 and rebuilding libc.a with the library script, the disk filled up. It came down to 'cat /dev/null > newfile' growing until the hard disk was full. Has anyone seen this?
a: Seen it. I never bothered working out what's broken in cat. I replaced the line in the run script with 'rm newfile ; touch newfile' to create the file. There's a second spot in the script that creates a file the same way, so fix that too.

subject: super_user in fs
q: After recompiling mm and fs on Minix, only root can mkdir, rmdir, link or unlink directories, and only root can su. What am I missing?
a: Permissions, genius. Make mkdir set-user-id and owned by root with chown root and chmod 4711. Do the same for mv_dir, which mv calls to move directories. Give su the same mode and owner.

subject: Modula-2, Pascal
q: Are there any Modula-2 or Pascal compilers that run under Minix on the Atari ST, something simple for learning programming?
a: There's a Pascal compiler for MINIX PC with full source, from Transmediair and UniPress. It's mostly written in Pascal, so you'd need another Pascal compiler to build it for 68000, then port it to Minix. Not plug and play; do some work.

subject: missing files in v1.3 upgrade?
q: Are usr/include/sys/dir.h, timeb.h, times.h and types.h supposed to be in the Minix v1.3 upgrade kit? I can't find them anywhere in the distribution.
a: They're not in 1.3 at all. What went in and what didn't was somewhat arbitrary. Others ended up fetching the diff set by ftp to get the sys include files. Complain to the distributors, not the net.

subject: Minix debugging tools
q: Booting Minix 1.5 from floppy gave "Unexpected Sftwr Int # 03h", and removing the int 3 in start.x fixed it. Where does that message come from, and how do you install a debugger?
a: That's the debugger trap. It does nothing on a standard 1982 IBM BIOS, but a few incompatible BIOSs print a message and never return, so take it out. For debugging, load a debugger before starting Minix, ideally much earlier, even in ROM. Don't expect hand-holding.

subject: IDE drives
q: Can I run vanilla Minix 1.5 on a 386 with an 80 or 120 MB IDE drive? What do I need to do, and will 386-Minix work with it too?
a: Yes, it runs fine on an 80 meg IDE drive. Load the original 1.5 onto the disk, then rebuild the kernel with at_wini.c to get protected mode and access to all your RAM. And yes, 386-Minix works with it too.

subject: tar for backup
q: Can I use Minix tar to back up onto several floppies, and pipe it through compress first?
a: Use vol together with tar. Vol splits a stream from stdin into floppy-sized chunks, 1.2M or 360k, and joins them back on restore. Clever, but VERY slow. Don't complain, it's floppies.

subject: Where is regerror() in MINIX-ST 1.5.10.3 ?
q: Compiling less on MINIX-ST 1.5.10.3, regcomp() and regsub() call regerror(), but it isn't defined anywhere in the library. Am I missing something?
a: No, regerror is supposed to be supplied by the application. Cawf, egrep and less each carry their own simple regerror.c with an fprintf, which should use "%s\n". If you want, drop a dummy version in the library to patch incomplete apps. Read the sources.

subject: Non-ST506 winchester driver for PS/2
q: Does MINIX work on a PS/2 Model 70 386? The ps_wini.c driver only handles ST506 drives, and the Model 70 has a strange drive on an edge connector. Is it IDE?
a: It's actually an ESDI controller, same in function as the ESDI adapter in other PS/2s, just built into the drive unit to save a slot. Use the ESDI driver posted a while back. If it scans POS adapter IDs, check for either of two. Easy fix.

subject: yacc and/or lex for minix?
q: Does anyone have a public domain yacc or lex for Minix or MS-DOS?
a: Bison, the yacc work-alike distributed with GNU emacs, is on prep.ai.mit.edu by anonymous ftp. Expect GNU memory appetite to hurt on small machines. A subset of lex also ships with ckermit. Go port it yourself.

subject: Elvis and Virecover
q: Elvis on Minix 1.5.0 only shows the first character I type in insert mode and then overwrites the rest on screen, and there's no "im" entry in /etc/termcap. Also, the optimizer "opt" crashes compiling virecover.c. Any fix?
a: Add ic=\E[@ to /etc/termcap; you don't need im/ei. As for opt, it chokes on big string constants, so split the big string in virecover.c into pieces under 80 chars. Sigh, a compiler that can't swallow a long string.

subject: minix_read/minix_write? Help
q: Has anyone developed DOS programs that can read or write Minix formatted disks, like the opposite of dos-read and dos-write?
a: The standard MINIX program readfs does exactly that. It reads a MINIX file system and creates an image of it on some disk. Compile it with any MS-DOS compiler and run it there. It was in the distribution all along.

subject: MINIX on amstrads
q: Has anyone gotten Minix working on an Amstrad PC 1512 with a hard disc? XT Minix boots but can't get past block 33 on the hard disc. How do I fix that?
a: Someone runs it with an OMTI controller under Minix 1.3 and had the same trouble. The controller couldn't get the right information from the disk. Give the winchester driver your drive's parameters directly, instead of begging for a new xt_wini.c.

subject: HELP NEEDED : How create a new filesistem on floppy with amiga.
q: How do I create a new MINIX filesystem on a floppy with an Amiga? mkfs seems to work, but mount complains and a second mkfs dumps core.
a: Use a PC-formatted disk, say formatted with messydos, not an Amiga-formatted one. That way disks are exchangeable between different implementations of MINIX. Yes, it's a waste of the Amiga's capacity, but that's how it is.

subject: 68K minix
q: How do I get Atari MINIX onto a Macintosh-readable disk, and is the Atari version on the 9-track tape offered by the card in the book?
a: Atari disks are standard 720K 3.5 inch disks. Compile readfs on the Mac and it reads the MINIX file system from the diskette, or hook up a PC and Mac with kermit. There's no tape version for the Atari, and don't call P-H for support.

subject: Minix 1.5.10 uptime/reliability
q: How long can Minix 1.5.10 stay up without rebooting? My AT&T PC6300 acts weird after two days and dies after three, even under little load.
a: Sounds like a memory leak. Mine ran a cron job every minute plus some uucp. After about two days nothing could run, out of memory. It was in 1.3 and 1.4a too. I gave up and rebooted every morning.

subject: ignorance about minix and EMS boards.
q: How much of EMS is software versus hardware, and can MINIX cope with an EMS board on an Intel clone? Will I need to write a driver?
a: MINIX copes by ignoring EMS entirely. Supporting it in the RAM disk driver would be a very useful enhancement and not very difficult, giving another 240K. No driver is needed just to run, so stop worrying.

subject: MINIX on PS/2 Model 25 !
q: I can't get MINIX 1.2 to boot on a PS/2 Model 25. It hangs or gives a trap < 16 message after I type '=' at the menu. Is this the same problem the Model 50 has, and what should I do?
a: No, different problems. Just try V1.3, which has been thoroughly tested on a Model 30 and has PS/2 fixes like the planar control register. The Model 50 trouble is suspected to be level-triggered interrupts from the Microchannel, which the Model 25 shouldn't have.

subject: dirent.h for clam
q: I have PC-Minix 1.3 and, trying to get Clam working, found I have no dirent.h in the obvious places like /usr/include. Where is it?
a: It's not in 1.3. dirent.h came with the 1.4a distribution. Upgrade, or quit grumbling and get a copy of it from there.

subject: Testers for utility
q: I have a sys admin utility I'd like to have volunteers test before releasing it to everyone. I remember a mailing list of testers. Can I submit my program to them, and how?
a: Yes, it's the Minix Referees Group. Mail your submission to minix-ref@plains.nodak.edu and it gets redistributed straight to all the testers. Keep it under 100K, because our sendmail eats anything larger. Read the rules before you whine.

subject: readclock.c and portio.c (minix 1.5.3)
q: I'm running Minix 1.5.3 and readclock.c calls port_in(), which reads /dev/port. I don't have a /dev/port and fs/table.c doesn't mention it. Am I missing something?
a: fs/table.c only sets major device numbers and tasks. /dev/port is the memory task's major device, minor device 4. Look at the MEM defines in minix/com.h, PORT_DEV is there for Intel chips. Read the header before posting, sigh.

subject: recompiling Copyrighted sources
q: If I have legitimate access to UNIX source code at my site, is it legal to recompile it under Minix and use it myself?
a: Only on machines named in your AT&T source license. If your Minix box is on the list, fine, whatever OS it runs. If not, moving even one byte of AT&T code there violates the license. Copyright is beside the point once you've signed a license. Read what you signed.

subject: Alarm handling in 1.5
q: In Minix 1.5, wouldn't keeping alarms in a linked list be faster than the clock task scanning the whole proc table for expired p_alarm entries?
a: Sure, it'd be faster, but the clock task takes about .0015% of the CPU on a 386, so who cares. A delta list would be faster still and truly O(1). Premature optimization, sigh.

subject: C-shell for MINIX-ST
q: Is there a C-shell (csh) for MINIX-ST, and where can I find MINIX-ST stuff by FTP?
a: There's a shell called Clam. It's not a csh clone, but has most of the features of both csh and tcsh, and it was ported to ST-Minix. It was posted to the net, so go dig for the sources instead of making someone repost it.

subject: Amiga Minix
q: Is there a public domain or shareware MINIX for the Amiga, and what hardware do you need to run it?
a: No. By the end of August there'll be a copyrighted version from Prentice Hall, with all the sources of everything plus a 700 page manual including a code listing. So no free lunch, kid.

subject: Amiga version of Minix
q: Is there a version of Minix for the Amiga, or is anyone working on one? I'm a beginner C programmer.
a: Two students have started on an Amiga port, but nobody knows how far along they are. And a beginner shouldn't make porting a multiprogramming operating system to poorly documented hardware project number 1. Learn to crawl first.

subject: Minix for the 68K (AMIGAs ?)
q: Is there any interest in or effort toward a Minix port to the Amiga, such as the A1000?
a: Yes, there's already an effort going. Contact amiga-minix-request@ulowell.uucp. Maybe check earlier postings before asking whether anybody's doing it.

subject: password encoding
q: Looking at the Minix source, the passwords look encoded rather than encrypted, and inverting the crypt function seems trivial. Is that so, and does Unix use the same method?
a: Yes, it's invertible; somebody posted an inversion program about a year back. Minix used to have a Unix-compatible crypt, and nobody seems to know why it got changed. I still use the old one, as any sane person would.

subject: Minix ar compatability
q: Minix ar is incompatible with Berkeley unix ar. Has anyone modified Minix ar to be compatible?
a: Wrong diagnosis. Minix ar is the same as the v7 and Berkeley format. Your Encore 4.2 box uses System V COFF object format, which Minix doesn't understand. For archiving files across systems, use tar. Sigh.

subject: System calls: particularly checking if input is available on stdin
q: On MINIX-ST I can't find fcntl, and gtty and stty aren't documented. Are they obsolete, and is there a manual on MINIX system calls?
a: gtty and stty are obsolete V7 backwards-compatibility wrappers around ioctl, and they can't do anything ioctl can't. MINIX is modelled on V7, so use the Bell Labs UNIX Programmer's Manual, Vols 1-2. Open modes are plain integers: 0, 1, 2. Read a book, kid.

subject: Some questions...
q: On Minix, what is chmem really for? Is the memory and stack the compiler allocates normally enough?
a: It's for machines with no memory management hardware. The full amount of memory a program needs has to be allocated in advance, and chmem is used to set that limit. Allocate more with chmem and you get more. Think about it.

subject: ST 1.5.0: patch(1) won't patch
q: Upgrading to ST Minix 1.5.0, patch fails on 8 of the cdiffs with "The next patch looks like a new-style context diff to me". Is there a quick remedy?
a: Recompile patch now that you've built the new libc.a. The original library had bugs that show up in patch. Follow the upgrade directions in order, as they were written for a reason.

subject: Ralf Wenk's M68K Kermit Patches
q: Were Ralf Wenk's patches to term and kermit, avoiding the shadowing bottleneck under M68K Minix, ever made public?
a: Only term and talk were patched, not kermit, since the author doesn't use it. Both patches were posted in April, and the later 1.6.* versions should include the term patches. Check your news spool before whining.

subject: EXTENDED/EXPANDED Memory on PC's
q: What is the difference between extended and expanded memory on PCs, and how does expanded memory matter for Minix on machines that aren't 286 or 386?
a: Extended memory is mapped above 1 Meg, so real-mode OSes like DOS and Minix can't touch it. Expanded memory uses hardware tricks: 64k chunks get mapped in and out of the 640k space. It works on a 286 fine too. Learn the difference already.

subject: MINIX on a 68000
q: What's the status of the MINIX port to the 68000 and Atari ST? Will Prentice-Hall sell it?
a: Minix-ST is really in the works and Prentice-Hall will distribute it. It won't be available until spring 88. Quit holding your breath, bated or otherwise, and be patient.

subject: Simple (?) question re signals
q: When I type the interrupt character (DEL) under Minix, what determines which processes get the SIGINT? On my system it only goes to the shell.
a: There's an implicit assumption that a tty line maps one to one onto the process owning it. For one terminal that's true, and the distributed version only worked for one, so no problems so far. Follow the chain of calls from tty.c. Hardly rocket science.

subject: cpp source, where is it?
q: Where can I find the source for cpp? I upgraded to Minix 386 with the patches but can't find the cpp source.
a: Use gnu cpp. The source is in the gcc source, and bcc doesn't quite compile it but the workaround is easy. A Minix-386 binary is in the uk subdirectory on plains. Fix the pipe bugs in Minix and use -traditional where needed. Sigh.

subject: upgrading
q: Where can I get an upgrade kit from Minix 1.3 to 1.5.x? The kit on plains.nodak.edu has no instructions and the files aren't in a format I recognize, so I think it's corrupted.
a: The files are compressed tar files, just named badly. Rename xxx.Z to xxx.tar.Z. The instructions are in pub/Minix/updates/pc.kit. They use 13-bit compression, which Minix-PC can handle. And did you set BINARY mode in FTP? Check the basics before blaming the archive.

subject: asld bug?
q: Why does sprintf() on Minix return the address of the buffer instead of the number of characters copied, as I thought it should?
a: BSD sprintf() returns a pointer to the buffer, inherited from V7, while Sys V returns the character count. So much BSD code depends on the pointer that nobody will change it. The stdio.h comment says it all: too painful to do right. Typical.

subject: DOS[READ\WRITE\DIR] on 3 1/2 etc etc
q: Why does the Minix DOSREAD utility use its own print_string stuff instead of just calling printf?
a: Disk space was tight when it was written. Dropping the stdio library and using a limited print_string kept the binary about 3 or 4K smaller. Not everyone had megabytes to burn, you know.

subject: tools/menu -whats the story?
q: Why does tools/menu in MINIX 1.5.9 contain so much unused stuff like brk, initvarv(), get_partition() and read_partition()? Is it half changed or an odd version?
a: It used to do file system checking, make empty file systems and other junk. It's being reduced bit by bit. If you want to strip the cruft, post a cdiff and it'll probably be adopted if it works. Patches, not complaints.

subject: MacMINIX
q: Why is MacMINIX going to be a hosted app rather than a real operating system like on the IBM PC, Atari, and Amiga?
a: Because IBM, Atari, and Commodore tell you how the machine works. Apple figures you're a user who can be trusted to point with the mouse. How the disk controller, clock, video, keyboard and DMA chips work is none of your business. Hard to write a native OS for a secret machine.

subject: need knowledge
q: Is there an operating system called MVS, and what machines does it run on? Also what machines does VMS run on?
a: MVS runs on IBM 370/390 types of machines and compatibles like Amdahl's. VMS is from DEC and runs on their own boxes. Sigh, basic stuff.

subject: DPS 6 Operating Systems ...
q: Is there any operating system other than GCOS available for the Honeywell DPS 6 systems?
a: I think Pick is, or at least used to be, available for the DPS-6. Beyond that, I've got nothing on Thoth. Go dig through the old vendor lists yourself.

subject: *.sfp and WP51
q: I have soft fonts (brd*.sfp) I want to use with WP51, and I've set the softfont directory path, but WP doesn't list them under Change Base Font. Why?
a: Hit Shift-F7 for the Print menu, select your printer, edit it, then go to Cartridges and Fonts. Check whether your soft fonts are in the downloadable list. Beyond that I don't know, and your manual should say.

subject: Repair of DOS backup files
q: Is there a utility that will repair damaged DOS 3.2 backup files, probably damaged because the floppy drives that wrote them were out of alignment?
a: Good luck. If misalignment is the cause, the same out-of-alignment drive should read the disks back. Otherwise you can adjust the heads on the fly, but don't unless you're a qualified technician.

subject: How do I determine memory needed?
q: How do I figure out the smallest amount of memory to allocate to a random program in DESQview? Is there a direct or indirect way to calculate it, and does Manifest help?
a: Easiest is the loadhi program that comes with QEMM and QRAM. Run the program with the /gs option, and when it finishes loadhi reports two numbers; the first is yours. No loadhi? Limit memory with EATMEM or shrink Change-a-Program until it dies. Exercise the program fully, or you'll guess low.

subject: zmodem in desqview.
q: Is there a way to make DESQview able to receive 19200 baud using zmodem? Zcomm as the single task still can't do it, though it runs fine outside DESQview on my 386SX 20MHz.
a: It's done every day, even at 9600 with compression, plus two other tasks running. Likely you lack a 16550 UART chip; without it you lose characters. Costs about $14. Read the ZCOMM docs, they list where to order. Sigh.

subject: QEMM and DesqView
q: QEMM keeps locking up on my 33 MHz 386 whenever I load DesqView, even with FRAME=C000 or C400. My line is device=qemm386.sys FRAME=C400 ON RAM ROM. What am I setting wrong?
a: Quarterdeck tech support suggested the "nosh" parameter on a similar machine, and that did the trick. Try DEVICE=C:\QEMM\QEMM386.SYS ram rom nrh nosh. Stop guessing at frame addresses.

subject: Quarterdeck and Quattro Pro SE
q: Why is Quarterdeck offering Quattro Pro SE with QEMM 6.0? Did Quarterdeck buy it from Borland, or do they have some kind of deal?
a: They must have some kind of deal. Quarterdeck has an upgrade offer for current DV-386 owners: DV 2.4, QEMM 6.0, DESQview Companions and Quattro Pro SE for $99. Nobody's said they bought anything. Rumors aren't facts.

subject: printing to a file??
q: Can I print to a file under DOS 3.3 instead of LPT1, without rewriting my program's print code?
a: If the program writes to stdprn, use the force-handle command to change it to stdout. Then redirect the output when you run the program. No need to rewrite anything, you didn't have to be so dramatic.

subject: How can I jump ...
q: How can I jump to a different part of my program using CodeView, skipping ahead and resuming execution elsewhere?
a: View the source as assembly or mixed, bring up the registers, and change IP, or CS:IP, to where you want to resume. It's handy for skipping subroutine calls. Point it somewhere stupid and you'll execute garbage and hang the machine, so don't.

subject: How to put CARRIAGE RETURN in Batch file
q: How can I put a carriage return in a batch file so I can run a series of mainframe download commands without typing a return after each line?
a: Use Ctrl-M, the ASCII code for CR. One trick is a file like Y.BAT containing Y followed by Ctrl-M, redirected into other batch files to answer the are-you-sure prompts. Works fine, though DOS makes it harder than it should be.

subject: switch char in DOS 4.0
q: How do I change the switch character and directory separators in DOS 4.0 to the UNIX defaults? The config.sys lines and programs from before 3.3 don't work.
a: Try switchar.exe in /pc/ts/tsutld18.arc from the garbo archives. No guarantees. And learn that Followup-To: poster doesn't mail replies to you, it just confuses the software. Sigh.

subject: Borland Educational Discount Info?
q: How does Borland handle educational discounts? My brother wants to buy their C++ compiler, and his computer store carries mostly hardware.
a: Borland has a Scholar Program for educational discounts. Call 408/438-5300 and press 2 for Customer Service, or mail their Educational Sales department at borlandEd@cup.portal.com. It's in the contact file in the archives, which you could have read yourself.

subject: Expanded/Extended mem. info needed
q: Is it possible to use expanded memory if you don't have extended memory? What would you need, and what goes in config.sys?
a: Yes. You need a hardware LIM board, or a disk emulator that'll be slow and not fully compatible, plus the EMS driver in config.sys. LIM bank-switches 16K pages into a 64K frame, and works even on XTs. Extended is a different animal entirely.

subject: Is it possible to write-protect a partition?
q: Is there any way to write protect a hard drive partition? I run computer labs and want the system and software partition read-only while a scratch partition stays writable.
a: Yes, if you use Disk Manager as your disk driver. One of its partition types is Read-Only, and it works great. Keep a small C: with DOS and boot software, make it read-only, and have autoexec.bat run d:\autoexec.bat to ease editing. Nearly crash-proof, I said nearly.

subject: Getting rid of "syntax error" from .bat files - how to?
q: My batch file tests parameters with if %1==param1 but gives a syntax error when no parameter is passed. How do I avoid it, and handle a parameter starting with a dash?
a: Wrong format. With no parameter it expands to 'if ==param1', which is invalid. Quote it: if "%1"=="param1". Or append a character to both sides, like if x%1==x-f. Either also copes with the dash. Basic batch lore.

subject: ASC II Zip files
q: What zip program do I need to unpack the ASCII Zip files I see in this newsgroup? Does PKUNZIP handle them?
a: This comes up every week. Those are UUENCODED zip files, binary turned into ASCII for transmission. Get UUDECODE from a local site or an ftp site, run it, and you end up with the ZIP file for PKUNZIP. Dumb question indeed.

subject: 4dos - where can I find it?
q: Where can I find the latest version of 4DOS?
a: Try /pc/sysutil/4dos30.zip by anonymous ftp from chyde.uwasa.fi. It's also on CompuServe in the IBM PC forums, and the publisher, J.P. Software, runs a BBS with the latest demo. Honestly, this comes up every week; go look before asking.

subject: MS-DOS 5.0
q: Will MS-DOS 5.0 fix all of DOS's problems? Does it kill the 640K limit and bring sturdy multitasking? What does it actually improve?
a: NOT! Whoever told you that is on drugs. The beta gave me about 630k free on a 286, with no multitasking to speak of. The new HELP command is the headline feature, and it even overrides 4DOS's better one. Marketing, sigh.

subject: ANSI.SYS colors
q: With ANSI.SYS loaded under DOS 4.01, how do I set the screen to yellow text on a blue background, and where?
a: Set a prompt. With ansi.sys in config.sys, use prompt $e[1;33;44m$p$g. That's bold on, 33 yellow, 44 blue, then the usual path and greater-than. It's all in the DOS manual, you know.

subject: Source for Borland Turbo C, C++ Libraries
q: Can I get the source to Borland's Turbo C and C++ libraries from Borland? I've seen mail-order houses selling a Turbo Developers Library; is that it?
a: Yes. The Turbo C package has a request form for library source in among the prolific documentation. It might be cheaper from a mail-order house. Search, and ye shall find; try reading the manual.

subject: Shared programs in Desqview
q: Can a DESQview shared program call DOS, especially Exec, to load a bunch of TSRs?
a: Dunno about calling DOS, but shared programs shrink the maximum window size by their own size. So loading TSRs that way hurts window size just like loading them low from DOS before DESQview. No free lunch.

subject: Borland Upgrade Policy (was Re: Borland Application FrameWorks)
q: Does Borland provide free or cheap upgrades when it ships buggy software, and do they send bug fix notices?
a: Generally not. Borland doesn't usually do maintenance releases. They sometimes publish free patches on Compuserve and their BBS, and if you report a serious bug you may get a fix. Don't hold your breath waiting for mailings, though.

subject: MSC 6.0 limits
q: Does Microsoft C 6.0 have the same limits as 5.1, such as the 512 byte maximum macro expansion?
a: No, 6.0 lifted it. The macro expansion limit is now 6k. There are other changes from 5.1 too, like more ANSI compatibility, based pointers and in-line assembly. About time.

subject: Graphical front end for PKZIP
q: Does anyone know of a graphical front end for PKZIP, with file selection and interactive archiving? Would there be demand for one?
a: Not graphics-mode, but you'll face iron-tough competition from SHEZ and AM, the two stars of the shareware scene. Go look at shez62 and am557 before reinventing the wheel, again.

subject: HELP: Access global variables in child process
q: How can I access global variables of the parent from a child process started with EXEC() in Turbo Pascal?
a: Pass the child a pointer to the data. Split it into segment and offset, hand both over as strings, and convert them back to words in the child. Better still, share one record so you pass lots of data at once. Not rocket science.

subject: Printer status
q: How can I check the printer status from a C program? I'm using Turbo C and didn't find anything in the manual.
a: Look at biosprint(). One of its options checks the printer status. It's in the library, you know; the manual has it if you bother to look past the first page. Sigh.

subject: Random Numbers
q: How can I get a random number on DOS machines when not all have clocks? I seed rand() from the system clock now.
a: Seeding from the clock is generally fine. With no clock, save the last random value to a short file and use it as the next seed. And rand() output isn't very random; read the Numerical Recipes in C chapter.

subject: Batch File "open" file detection
q: How can a DOS batch file detect that a file is in use on a LAN and show my own 'Application In Use' message instead of the share violation Abort, Retry, Fail error?
a: You're approaching it backwards. Have the batch file create a semaphore file before running the app, check if it exists first, and print your message if so. Delete it afterward. Or make the files read-only so share won't complain, unless the app writes to its executables.

subject: Spawning processes in DOS
q: How can my DOS program run another program and capture its output, the way an editor runs a compiler and shows the output to the user?
a: Redirect your stdout handle to a temporary file. The child inherits your handles, so dup stdout to save it, close it, open the temp file, exec, then restore stdout and read the file back. Or use popen() if your library bothered to include it.

subject: Info wanted: Copy protection
q: How did the various copy-protection schemes on the IBM PC work? I'm after general information, not cracking.
a: PC Tech Journal devoted most of an issue to this a year or two ago, and it's good reading. I can't tell you which one, since my back issues are gone. Try the public library.

subject: ASCII --> WP 5.0 mailmerge files
q: How do I create a mailmerge file for WordPerfect 5.0 from a dBase IV database? What format does the merge file have to take?
a: Fields end with control-R, carriage return, linefeed. Records end with control-E, carriage return, linefeed. Fields can span multiple lines. If dBase IV will embed those control characters in your report, you can do it directly. RTFM next time.

subject: How to disable ^P from outputting to printer?
q: How do I disable CTRL-P printer echo on DOS? I keep hitting it by accident and rebooting.
a: Why reboot? Just press Ctrl-P again to turn printer echo off, even at the Abort, Retry, Fail prompt. Or pick Fail. You can also zero the printer timeout at LPT1 0:0x78. That miserable excuse for an OS earns its reputation, but you're reading nothing.

subject: Number of drives on system, how do you find out the ...
q: How do I find out the actual number of drives on an MS-DOS machine? Turbo C's setdisk() returns 5 on my two-partition system, including a nonexistent E:.
a: Sigh. setdisk() just returns whatever LASTDRIVE= says, defaulting to 5. Test each drive up to LASTDRIVE with the IOCTL call for fixed or removable media. Bogus drives return an error, and it makes no disc access. It's documented, so read a book.

subject: Updating a file date
q: How do I update a file's date, like Touch, in Turbo C? I can't find a function for it and can't rely on Touch being on the user's system.
a: Turbo C has setftime(). It's on page 317 of the manual and indexed under Date, File. Sheesh. If you really can't use it, go to DOS interrupt 21Hex, function 57Hex.

subject: Borland patches somewhere besides simtel?
q: I can't get through to simtel. Does anyone have the Turbo C++ patches available by ftp somewhere else?
a: Try CS.CMU.EDU, 128.2.222.173. Go straight to /afs/cs/user/ralf/pub, since anonymous can't read anything above it, and grab tcppt1.zip. Honestly, simtel isn't the only machine on the net, you know.

subject: Stack Overflow
q: I ran an exe file and the computer said STACK OVERFLOW. What is happening?
a: Usually a programming error: the program uses more stack than reserved and was compiled with stack checking. Without the source to recompile with a bigger stack you can't fix it. Some programs also choke on a large environment, so shrink it, say with 4dos.

subject: Assembly language primers wanted
q: I want to teach myself 8086/88 assembly language to augment my C programming. Can anyone recommend books that assume you know nothing about 8086/88 assembler and take you through the basics?
a: Try Lafore's "Assembly Language Primer for the IBM PC & XT" from the Waite Group, but get a real reference like Coffron's "Programming the 8086/8088" too, since the primer skimps on the instruction set. "The 8086 Book" by Rector and Alexy is an oldie but a goodie. Do read them.

subject: Porting software to the PC, 64K data structure barrier.
q: I'm porting a UNIX program to the IBM PC with Turbo C++, and the compiler complains about a struct bigger than 64K. Is there a way to define large arrays, and will malloc() handle them?
a: Try the huge memory model, -mH on the command line. If a single element is over 64K, though, Turbo has no easy answer. Get Microsoft C 6.0A and use its huge model, which has no 64K limits. Welcome to the PC, kid.

subject: turning off banner in BC++
q: Is there any way to turn off the banner lines bcc and tlink print for every program compiled from a makefile? MASM has /t and Microsoft C has -nologo, so is there anything comparable in BC++?
a: Nope. The BC++ docs' comparison with MS C 6.0 shows no corresponding option to turn off the logo. Redirect the output to a file and write a little program to strip the copyright lines. Sigh, hardly rocket science.

subject: Undefined symbol in linking using BC++
q: Linking with BC++ gives undefined symbols FIWRQQ and FIDRQQ when I cast a constant to float with math.h included. What's going on?
a: Those connect to the floating-point library, so you need the appropriate MATHx.LIB. The compiler didn't notice you used floating point, the old floating-point formats not linked nonsense. Put a dummy float operation in, like float foobar = 42.42;. Classic Borland.

subject: choosing ramdrive's drive letter
q: On our 3Com network, ramdrive grabs drive C, which we want for the network disk. How can I choose the drive letter ramdrive uses? My driver.sys fake floppy trick crashes the machine on 'net use'.
a: Have you tried subst r: c:\ in autoexec.bat? Yes, that's about the whole trick. Fake floppies are a clumsy way to go about it.

subject: DOS file attributes 0xC0: who/why/what/when/where/how?
q: What software uses the two most significant bits of the DOS file attribute byte?
a: As far as anyone knows, nothing uses them. Alas, MS-DOS masks those bits out of everything, which kills the idea of using them for soft-links. Typical.

subject: How to program the SoundBlaster
q: Where can I get public domain source code for programming the SoundBlaster card?
a: Somebody got tired of seeing this request and put up SB.ZIP, a small set of assembly routines for calling the SB voice driver. It's on xanth.cs.odu.edu in the /sblaster directory, public domain. Try looking before asking next time.

subject: MSDOS Device Drivers: "Why?"
q: Why do MS-DOS device drivers use separate strategy and interrupt routines? It looks inefficient and bad for multitasking.
a: It's not a hindrance. It would help multitasking, since DOS could queue requests while the driver is busy, and a good driver could reorder them, like elevator seeking on disks. But DOS is single-tasking and never queues, so no driver ever used it. Typical.

subject: strange results from #define
q: Why does #define SEC_PER_DAY (24*60*60) give a number nothing like 86400 on Lightspeed C and Zortech C++, while 86400L works fine? Do parentheses in a define do strange things?
a: Not the parens, genius. 24, 60 and 60 are all ints, and with 16-bit ints the product overflows to 20864 before the cast to long ever happens. Write (24L*60*60) or 86400L. Any idiot knows int is not long.

subject: How to reset VGA? & Re: EGA/VGA ReadPixel function in C
q: Why does saving and restoring all the VGA registers not restore the video the way an int 10h mode set does? I've tried resetting the sequencer and the CRT controller, with no luck.
a: Are you reading the low-numbered CRT controller registers back to get your values? Often they're write-only, for some stupid reason. Write values from a table instead. Read the 6845 spec sheets, which are a good place to start even if the card doesn't use one.

subject: DJGPP vs 386max
q: With 386max 5.1, the new djgpp with VCPI support complains that an EMS driver used address 1B0000H, broken by handle_screen_swap(). Why is that location hardcoded, and how do I get it to work?
a: I just picked a location unused in a normal DOS system. The screen routines map primary and secondary screens there. 386Max is probably putting its big control program there, which it's allowed to do. Try giving 386MAX memory nearer the 1M border so it loads lower.

subject: Why isn't anybody fixing ansi.sys???
q: ANSI.SYS in the OS/2 1.2 DOS compatibility box forgets the country keymap and falls back to the US layout. Why hasn't anybody fixed it?
a: Nobody answered why, but stop waiting on the vendor. Use NNANSI.SYS, which was just posted in comp.binaries.ibm.pc. It works in the DOS box, though its copyright message can overwrite the vdisk message if listed after it in config.sys. Typical.

subject: NAMED PIPES?
q: Can an OS/2 netstation create a named pipe that another netstation or server process opens? What path do I give DosOpen()? I've tried \\SERVER\NETSTAT1\PIPE\NP1 and \\NETSTAT1\PIPE\NP1.
a: The path \\NETSTAT1\PIPE\NP1 is correct, but that machine must be a server, since a pipe is a shared resource and workstations can't share theirs. For workstation to workstation, use mailslots. Read the manual.

subject: HPFS and OS/2 2.0 windows compatability
q: Can someone describe how HPFS differs from FAT, with its directory and allocation strategy, or point me to a journal reference?
a: Read Microsoft Systems Journal, Volume 4 Number 5, September 1989: "Design Goals and Implementation of the New High Performance File System". It covers all of it, so go look it up.

subject: DosFindFirst with HPFS names ?
q: How can I get long file names on an HPFS partition with DosFindFirst under OS/2? Increasing the FILEFINDBUF structure doesn't work.
a: Your program has to promise the OS it can handle them. Set the LONGNAMES or NEWFILES bit in the .EXE header, via the module definition file or the markexe utility. Otherwise DosFindFirst only gives 8.3 names. Goofy, but it keeps old 1.1 programs from crashing.

subject: Mouse under compatibily box
q: How do I get the mouse to work for Microsoft Windows applications running in the DOS compatibility box under OS/2 1.1 EE? Will 1.2 fix it?
a: Set Windows up for EGA mode instead of VGA. OS/2 1.1 can't handle the mouse in anything above EGA. Version 1.2 fixed it for at least one user in standard video modes, though the mouse still dies in 800x600. Sigh, the usual.

subject: Microsoft NMAKE usage
q: I'm porting a UNIX program to Microsoft 6.0 C and NMAKE. The UNIX makefiles loop through a make variable of subdirectories with a shell for loop. Is there an easy way to do that in NMAKE without kludging up batch files?
a: Skip the for loop. Make the target depend on $(SUBDIRS), then give a rule for $(SUBDIRS) that depends on a do_always target and runs cd and make on $@. Any normal make handles this; any idiot knows loops belong in make, not the shell.

subject: Owned windows and WM_DESTROY in MDI
q: In the OS/2 MDI sample, why does the frame window procedure set the parent of the system menu and minmax windows back to the frame on WM_DESTROY? Aren't owned windows destroyed automatically?
a: No. On destroy, children are destroyed recursively, but owned windows just have their owner set to null. Controls left on the object window hang around and later touch freed frame resources like the heap, and poof. The documentation is simply wrong.

subject: OS/2 platforms
q: Is it true that OS/2 2.0 will be the last version to support the 80286, or the first that will not support it? Which rumor is right?
a: Neither rumor is right. OS/2 2.0 will not support the 80286 at all, though it will run apps written for 1.x and the 286. PC Week's contrary rumors were retracted. Supporting the 286 was a mistake in the first place.

subject: Appletalk for OS/2 and/or MCA
q: Is there a LocalTalk card for the MCA bus, so I can use AppleTalk on a PS/2 under OS/2?
a: Daystar Digital makes a microchannel LocalTalk card. One has run in a Model 80 for a year without complaints. Their ad is in just about any MacUser, so look before asking.

subject: HELP: CONFIG.SYS deleted & then powered OFF->Hard Disk Stuffed
q: Someone deleted CONFIG.SYS on an OS/2 machine and then powered it off without shutting down. Now we can't read the hard disk; DIR gives 'Invalid internal file key type' and CD gives SYS003. How do we recover?
a: Boot from the install disk and run CHKDSK /F C:. That fixes 90% of these messes. On HPFS you lost the IFS line with /AUTOCHECK, so you must run it by hand. Rebuild CONFIG.SYS by installing OS/2 on another machine with the same options and copying it over.

subject: ?? Increasing DOS box env. space in 1.3 ??
q: How do I increase the environment space for the DOS box under OS/2 1.3? The manual doesn't say much about it.
a: Put it in the shell line of config.sys: shell=...command.com /e:xxx /p, where xxx is your number. If you meant memory for the DOS box, you can't. Load fewer drivers, use one code page, skip ega.sys. Read the manual harder.

subject: Timer resolution in OS/2 2.0
q: In OS/2 1.x the clock resolution was limited to about 30 Hz, so data acquisition scheduled off the OS timer couldn't go faster. Has that restriction been lifted in OS/2 2.0?
a: Wrong question. OS/2 is NO real-time operating system, and neither are DOS or UN*X, so stop expecting one. If you need real-time data rates, buy an add-on card like the IBM RIC real-time interface coprocessor card. Any idiot knows this.

subject: OS/2 problems with DOS box
q: OS/2 1.3 won't open a DOS box and reports SYS 2064, not enough storage to create DOS mode, even after I removed all device drivers. Any thoughts?
a: Did you try ALL the obvious things? The DOS box is a device driver, and you removed it. Put it back. Think a bit, will you?

subject: gnu archives for os-9
q: Are there any FTP sites with GNU tools, especially GCC patches, for running on OS-9?
a: Try smilodon.cs.wisc.edu, 128.105.1.214. Look in pub/OSK/GNU for the many GNU utilities, and pub/OSK/GCC for GCC and G++, executables and sources. Not that hard to find if you'd bothered to look around.

subject: OS9000
q: Has anyone gotten OS-9000 running in a real world setup? Microware says it runs on any 386 or 386sx, but I don't want to be the first to try it with my own money.
a: Microware just started shipping the 386 PC/AT version. It's known to run on Compaq's 386sx, Gateway 2000's 25MHz 386, AST Premium 386 and a Leading Edge 386. You need an AT-compatible hard disk controller. Opinions will take a week or so, so don't whine yet.

subject: msdos -> os9
q: I transfer files by Kermit from an MS-DOS machine to a DEC Rainbow running OS-9, and all the returns turn into control-J characters. What can I do?
a: Control-J is a line feed, not a backspace, which is control-H. MS-DOS uses CRLF and OS-9 uses CR, and Kermit converts them unless you tell it not to. Don't set file mode binary or use -i on text files. RTFM.

subject: Windows-like Development Kit?
q: Is there a Windows-like or X-Windows-like development environment for OS-9 on a 68030?
a: Try MGR. It's much faster and has far less overhead than X, which doesn't yet run correctly on OS-9. It's a full GUI with multiple windows and pop-up menus, based on the client-server model.

subject: RCS for OS-9?
q: Is there a freely available newer uEmacs for OS-9 than the version 1.1 on my system, and a later RCS than 2.x for OSK?
a: uMacs 1.1 as shipped with OS-9 is just MicroEmacs 3.6, the last version without distribution restrictions. Newer ones aren't freely redistributable with commercial software. You can find MicroEmacs 3.10 in the TOP package on smilodon, or on CompuServe. Read the license next time.

subject: help!
q: On OS-9 Level Two, runb gives error 43 (unknown procedure) when the i-code module and runb aren't in the same block of memory. Any ideas?
a: Error 43 can happen when a procedure can't be loaded for lack of room, or in Level Two can't be mapped into the address space of the process running RunB. Look at the memory requirements of your procedures. Read the manual.

subject: OS-9 68k
q: What hardware does OS-9 68k need? Does it require an MMU, and what about timers and interrupts, for a 68020 single board computer?
a: No MMU required, though one lets you enforce access restrictions. For time-slicing you need a periodic interrupt, and 100 Hz is good. Figure at least half a megabyte of memory, and use interrupt-driven I/O, not bit-banger serial that hogs the CPU. Basic stuff.

subject: Porting Unix software to OS/9
q: What's involved in porting Unix software to OS-9? How close is it to Unix, with fork(), sockets and system calls?
a: Pretty close on processes, signals and files. OS-9's F$Fork is fork plus exec, so you can't precisely emulate Unix fork(). The Ethernet package gives you sockets. Expect to dig for _ss_*() or _gs_*() calls in place of ioctl(). Sigh.

subject: VMS-RSTS DECnet bug?
q: Accessing a RSTS account from VMS over DECnet fails with an RMS-F-SYN file specification syntax error whenever the account number has an 8 or 9, like [3,18]. Why, and is there a way around it?
a: It's not a bug, it's a restriction. VMS parses remote filespecs by VMS rules, and VMS UICs are octal. Quote the filespec, like RSTS::"[10,9]*.*". You lose wildcard transfers, but it works. This is in the manuals, remember those?

subject: File specification regularity (Was: Re: VMS vs. UNIX file system)
q: Did I make a syntax error in this VMS file spec: SYS$SYSROOT[UTILS.ANUNEWS.SRC.NEWS_SRC]NEWSADD.OBJ;1?
a: Yes. You left out the colon after the logical name. SYS$SYSROOT:[UTILS.ANUNEWS.SRC.NEWS_SRC]NEWSADD.OBJ;1 is the correct one. Complain about VMS file specs all you want, but get them right.

subject: How to disable Decwindows Pause Session?
q: How can I disable the Pause Session feature in the DECwindows session manager so students can't lock up a workstation and walk off?
a: Try setting the XtNsensitive resource for pause session to False in the app-defaults file. If the UIL file sets it to True explicitly, you're out of luck. Or hack a daemon that watches for the pause session full-screen window and destroys it. Ugly, but so is DECwindows.

subject: VMS MAIL (ISAM FORMAT) ---> ordinary text file
q: How can I get VMS MAIL out of its ISAM format into an ordinary text file from DCL, appending new mail to an ASCII file?
a: Use a command procedure. Run mail, select /new, then extract /all /append to your sequential file, delete /all, and exit. Not complicated, so skip the callable mail nonsense.

subject: How to Use DECterm's Status Line?
q: How do I use the DECterm status line in VMS? The VT300 escape sequences work on Unix but not from VMS, and my xterm termcap's status line sequences don't work on DECterm either.
a: You can't, apparently. DEC's engineers didn't want to write into the DECterm title bar because real hardware terminals don't do that, never mind that they don't resize either. Just use an xterm window with the xterm termcap, and avoid the vt300 termcap that turns the screen black.

subject: Uncompress and Gcc for VMS?
q: I tried to ftp the VMS compress/uncompress and Kermit sources from cu20b.columbia.edu but found no files in the ftp directory. What's going on?
a: That host runs some weird software that drops you in the middle of nowhere. Try 'cd k2:' then 'mget vmslz*.*'. That's the VMS port of compress, heavily modified. Ignore the .ARC extensions; they're just ASCII files concatenated with a one-line header each.

subject: Impact of DECwindows in VMS 5.2/5.3
q: If I just install VMS 5.3 over 5.1-1 and don't tailor DECwindows off, what happens? Do I lose disk space, and are new detached processes started?
a: Not exactly as you heard: the install asks whether you want DECwindows. It eats disk, mostly the server component, and VMS 5.3 plus DECwindows leaves about 50000 blocks free on an RD54. If you don't start it, no detached processes run. The install guide lists the sizes, so read it.

subject: File serving among VMS/Ultrix
q: Is it possible to use a VMS system as a file server for Ultrix workstations? How, and is it DECnet or Ethernet dependent?
a: Supposedly the VMS/Ultrix Connection (UCX), release 1.2 or later, does it, giving NFS access to ordinary VMS filesystems. It runs TCP/IP over Ethernet. Third parties like Wollongong sell TCP and NFS for VMS too. Ask your DECperson instead of guessing, and don't trust rumors.

subject: Need tape utility to read VMS BACKUP tape on Unix/Ultrix.
q: Is there a utility for reading a VMS BACKUP tape made on VMS 4.6 on a 4.3bsd or Ultrix Unix system?
a: The comp.sources.unix archives have a program for reading VMS backup tapes under UNIX. Go look there. This isn't hard.

subject: XtAddInput and VMS DEC Windows
q: XtAddInput hangs on VMS when I feed it from a pipe to a subprocess. Does anyone use it that way?
a: The VMS folks implemented XtAddInput in an OS-dependent way, with AST and STATUS arguments instead of the file descriptor and mask everyone else uses. Your Unix code needs hacking, sometimes extensively. Sigh.

subject: PC-Xinu large memory model problems
q: In PC-Xinu large memory model, the clock interrupt dispatcher's cs register comparison trick fails and the system locks up. Also, why must the BIOS clock interrupt routine be serviced before Xinu's?
a: In large model, check CS against both bounds, _TEXT and DGROUP in Turbo C, and allow a context switch if it's in range. The stack layout differs too. BIOS goes first because if Xinu switched away, the BIOS routine might not run for hours, leaving the floppy motor spinning. Think it through.

subject: Help: Parallel and Distributed Software Engineering.
q: Can someone recommend good readings on parallel and distributed software engineering?
a: Try Sol Shatz's IEEE Tutorial on Distributed Software Engineering, from IEEE Computer Society Press, ISBN 0-8186-8856-4. Not exactly light reading, so sit down.

subject: RP3 memory management
q: How does memory allocation like malloc work on the RP3 when memory can be interleaved across processors?
a: The interleaving can be configured so only some memory is interleaved, giving N+1 heaps: one per node plus one for interleaved memory. We wrote an extended malloc for user and kernel that lets the caller ask for node-local or interleaved memory. Burdens the programmer, but he knows best, or should.

subject: Need True Random Number Generator
q: We need a true random number generator, 32 bit, not shift-register based. Does anyone know how to build one using thermal noise?
a: Not aware of any ready-made ones. Start with a thermal noise source and a hard limiter; higher cutoff is better. Sample the square wave, take two samples, output 0 for 1-0, 1 for 0-1, nothing for equal pairs. That cures DC offset bias. Elementary.

subject: Read-Write CD's
q: Are there any vendors currently supplying read/write CD subsystems?
a: Sony has a CD recorder, a two-box affair with a separate encoder/decoder and recorder. JVC and Mitsumi have announced recorders too. Don't expect it to be cheap.

subject: SCSI & Q-bus
q: Can a SASI host adapter like the DTC 11-2 on an LSI-11 Q-bus control a SCSI disk? Can a SASI adapter that asserts a variable device ID control more than one SCSI device if I avoid overlapping operations?
a: A qualified yes to both. Performance will be poor because you can't overlap I/O. An old adapter likely has no arbitration, no ATN, no parity and sends only the target ID, which SCSI-1 allowed. Expect bugs, since vendors rarely test against SASI.

subject: Okidata Location & Number
q: Could someone give me the phone number for Okidata, or where they're located? I need to replace a hard to find part for one of their printers and I have no manual.
a: Try 1-800-OKIDATA. It's their universal customer support number, and they sorted out a part for an old 83A for me. Oki also has a healthy minimum on parts orders, so don't expect them to mail you one screw.

subject: Info requested about SCSI tape drives
q: I want to connect a 1/4 inch SCSI cartridge tape drive and a hard disk to my 68000 Unix box. Will any SCSI tape drive work with my tape drivers, and what problems come with multiple devices?
a: Not necessarily. SCSI is only a transport, so the tape controller must support the right standard like QIC-24 or QIC-02 and your drivers must too. Multiple devices need the attention bit. Many tape controllers won't disconnect during slow operations, which defeats streaming. Learn it.

subject: SCSI 2?
q: Is anyone doing anything with SCSI 2? Any comments on the CAM Committee proposals or the latest revision of the standard?
a: Go find the SCSI BBS run by someone from NCR Wichita. It's where the standards committee people hang out, with the SCSI 2 working draft, SCSI 1, ESDI, figures and a big message base. Registration is free. Read the drafts instead of asking the net.

subject: Seeking experience/info about helical scan tape drives
q: What's the difference between the CY-8200 from Cybernetics and the EXB-8200 helical scan tape drives? Does anyone have experience with them?
a: The differences are mostly packaging. Cybernetics, for one, charges a ridiculous amount for an optional LCD panel. If you don't need gadgets, buy the OEM Exabyte, and with lots of data the 8500 beats the 8200. Don't pay for shiny panels.

subject: VME-to-UNIBUS
q: Where can I find an adaptor to connect a VME device to a UNIBUS or QBUS bus? It's a one-time need; performance and packaging don't matter.
a: Performance Technologies in East Rochester, New York sells the PT-VME903, a two-board set that connects a VMEbus chassis to a QBUS chassis. Doesn't solve the UNIBUS half, but there you go.

subject: Extending Amiga Keyboard Cable
q: Why can't I use a longer cable between my Amiga keyboard and the computer? A 25 or 12 foot cable leaves the caps lock LED solid red.
a: The 5 volt signals drop to about 2 volts after the round trip, and plain phone cable is too wimpy. Use a beefier cable or add a 5 volt supply at the keyboard. Early keyboards also seem worse, which is Commodore's problem.

subject: Feeding labels thru HP Thinkjet?
q: How can I feed standard labels through an HP ThinkJet when the tractor feed won't adjust down to 3.5 inch width?
a: Buy labels in sheets that are two-across. If your software can't do two-up printing, run half the labels through, then reverse the paper to print the other half. Not hard, just use your head.

subject: Farallon StarController restictions
q: Has anyone installed the Farallon PhoneNET StarController, and what are the practical limits on devices per branch? Farallon only supports one device per branch, which seems extremely conservative given the ports are electrically isolated.
a: You can hang as many devices off it as you like, bandwidth permitting. A fair rule of thumb is 6 to 8 devices per port. Farallon wants to sell you more boxes, naturally. And it's just a fancy repeater, so for traffic problems you want a bridge.

subject: National Ethernet chip "DP8390"
q: Is the DP8390 ethernet chip on the Apple EtherTalk cards a custom chip or a standard one?
a: It's a standard part, National Semiconductor's ethernet controller, and it's pretty easy to program apart from some chip bugs. Other boards use it too, like the Western Digital WD8003 for the PC. Not exactly a state secret.

subject: NBP Lookups - case sensitive, or not?
q: Should AppleTalk NBP lookups and zone names be case sensitive or not? Some of my UNIX AppleTalk implementations differ.
a: Case-insensitive. Inside AppleTalk says entity names are case-insensitive by definition, so zone and NBP names must match regardless of case. Diacriticals do matter, though: n and n-hat don't match. Your uab code is broken, so go read the book.

subject: (none)
q: Someone once posted a small PostScript file that reboots the LaserWriter. I lost it. Can someone send a copy?
a: No file needed. Send "systemdict begin quit end" and the LaserWriter resets, wiping the prep file and any loaded PostScript. A test page prints if that's enabled. You must be in PostScript batch or interactive mode, of course. Ten seconds of typing, honestly.

subject: Appletalk wire specs
q: We run AppleTalk with the standard Apple connectors. What kind of wire must be used, or does it really matter?
a: It matters, and anyone who's debugged it knows. Wrong wire means a pile of miscellaneous network problems, worse as the network grows. Use the standard shielded cables, or look at PhoneNet or similar, since phone-jack systems have fewer loose connections. Don't say nobody warned you.

subject: address finders / white pages
q: We want a "white pages" at our university so someone at a Mac composing e-mail can look up a colleague's address. Is there server and client software for this?
