a: The White Pages name server that comes with CE Software's QuickMail does it. The server is an INIT on any Mac, and the NameFinder INIT is the client. It can rescan mail center user lists and lets you add your own fields.

subject: Mac TCP/IP Packages
q: We're standardizing on a Mac TCP/IP package at a university, considering NCSA Telnet, TCP/Connect, SU-MacIP and MacPathway Access. Have we missed any contenders?
a: Yes: MacUWS from Ungermann-Bass, which is based on SU-MacIP with a new interface. Also, TCP/Connect is discontinued and replaced by a rewrite, TCP/Connect II, and MacPathway Access is not HyperCard based. Get your facts straight before shopping.

subject: DECNet from a Mac
q: What's available for making a Mac software package talk DECnet? A DECnet driver that used the EtherTalk board would be ideal.
a: Look at TSSnet, which gives Macintoshes DECnet support. I think it comes from Alisa Systems in Pasadena, but check before you go calling people. Honestly, this is what a vendor list is for.

subject: What's cap.etalk?; aufs under AFS
q: What's the difference between ru-cap and ru-cap-etalk on rutgers.edu, and which version of CAP should I get?
a: ru-cap is the normal CAP distribution for KIP-implementation gateways, like KIP-only, FastPath with KStar, or old GatorSystem GatorBoxes. ru-cap-etalk is the UAB version, recompiled for UAB libraries. Pick based on your gateway. Obvious enough.

subject: latest version of CAP
q: What's the latest version of CAP and where can I ftp it?
a: CAP 6.0, by anonymous ftp from rutgers.edu. Get all the patches too, or don't come crying later.

subject: Printer Access Protocol (PAP)
q: Where can I get the include files or libraries for Printer Access Protocol (PAP) to write a Mac server that looks like a printer? Are they public or from ADAP?
a: There are none. No official server PAP library exists, so write your own on top of ATP. PAP is a simple protocol with only a few commands, so quit whining. A good test is having a Mac try to print to it.

subject: HyperCard doesn't work with Aufs
q: Why does HyperCard fail to read stacks on an Aufs shared volume on a Sun, asking for a file name with every other character capitalized like hOmE? Does it work with a real AppleShare server?
a: HyperCard really does change the case of the filename on lookup. Mac file lookups, real AppleShare included, are case-insensitive, so it works there; Unix under AUFS is case sensitive, so the lookup usually fails. Fundamental OS difference, and nobody's sure how to fix it.

subject: (none)
q: Is it illegal to send a 0x00 to a 3270 terminal? Is there another character that just gets eaten by the terminal?
a: Nul is perfectly legal. The 3270 eats it up without complaint, storing it as a data character at the current buffer address. It has the same effect as an erase/write for that location. Read the manual next time.

subject: ISO standards sources...
q: Where can I get the ASN.1 ISO standard specs, which I believe are ISO 8825 and 8826? Machine-readable would be nice.
a: Get your numbers straight first. ASN.1 itself is ISO 8824, and 8825 is the basic encoding rules. That's what the replies tell me; they don't say where to buy them or whether there's an electronic copy.

subject: CCITT T.51 (ISO2022?) and multiple-byte codes designated to GR/GL?
q: With ASCII designated into G0 and invoked to GL, and a multi-byte set like JIS kanji designated into G1 and invoked to GR, can ASCII and kanji be mixed with no escape sequences? What should happen with a lone byte that has the 8th bit set?
a: Yes, you've read the standard correctly. Error cases are outside the scope of ISO 2022 and T.51. Every implementation I've seen just takes the next byte as the second half of the pair and does something. Don't expect the standard to hold your hand.

subject: PElementID
q: The ISODE psap.h says ASN.1 tag numbers (PElementID) range 0 to 16383, but an overflow happens above 8191. Do only 13 bits (PE_ID_BITS) fit?
a: Sounds right. Two bits go to the Class and one to the Form, leaving 13. Getting 14 means working out the Form at encode time, which can't tell a zero-length primitive from an empty constructor. The comment in psap.h is probably out of date.

subject: X400 problems between DEC's MRX and DG's
q: Is there a limit on the number of addressees in X.400, since large distribution lists break mail between a DEC MRX and a DG system?
a: Limits aren't documented in the X.400 (1984) standards. They come from the profile the implementations are built or configured for. With the NIST profile the limit is 32K-1 recipients. Check with your vendors, as usual.

subject: looking for kerberized "xdm"
q: Is there a kerberized version of X11R4's xdm, and is it available from MIT somewhere?
a: Somebody already did it. The kerberos patches to X11R4, xdm included, plus a paper called "The Secure X Window Server", are on anonymous FTP at cs.duke.edu in dist/papers/khera. Not from MIT, so quit pestering them.

subject: Fibre Channel Draft Standard
q: Can someone give me the title of the ANSI draft standard for Fibre Channel?
a: The draft I have is titled "Fibre Channel Physical Layer (FC-PH)", Rev 2.1, May 25, 1991, a working draft proposed American National Standard for Information Systems. Look at the cover sheet next time.

subject: XTP
q: Does anyone know where I can find a description of the XTP protocol? Email or FTP is preferred, but a reference to a paper would do.
a: Send your surface-mail address to the xtp-request address at pei.com and they'll mail you a free copy of the XTP spec. Surface mail, mind you, not FTP. Some of us still read paper.

subject: How good is CRC-32 at burst error detection?
q: How good is CRC-32 at detecting burst errors, for checksumming the contents of an encryption?
a: A 32 bit CRC detects all burst errors up to 32 bits, meaning the distance from the first bit in error to the last is 32 bits or less. Textbook stuff.

subject: Searching through top level domains?
q: Is there a defined protocol in the DNS for finding information about a company, say MegaWidget Corporation, in the top level domain servers? Otherwise I have to phone them to learn their registered domain name.
a: Not in the DNS, no. That's what nicname, or whois, is for: it asks other machines such as nic.ddn.com to search their databases. It usually gives you enough to start a mid level search. Read up before building your own databases.

subject: About Protocols for File Transfer
q: Using ordinary asynchronous RS-232 full-duplex serial lines, can an error-detecting and correcting file-transfer protocol be as fast as or faster than a non-protocol transfer?
a: Strictly, no. You have to send checksum, CRC or ECC data along with the payload, and that takes longer. Though with no errors and a decent window, acks are small and cost almost nothing. Dedicated error-correcting hardware like MNP modems helps too.

subject: NFS for MAC OS
q: Does anyone know of NFS software for the Macintosh that runs under the native Macintosh OS?
a: Apple holds such a program, developed by CITI, but hasn't released it. It was due June 12 and didn't show, with blame going to either politics or bugs. Typical vendor behavior. Maybe more news at Interop.

subject: Forcing a umount
q: One of my six intermounted NFS workstations crashing hangs all the others, even when I'm not touching the dead machine's data. How can I avoid this, since a forced umount isn't available?
a: Use the automounter. It cuts down on dead-host problems, since you only get hurt by the crash of a machine you currently care about. Sigh, it's single-threaded, so it's slow to give up on a dead server. Symbolic links from /{mach} to the mount point make the /{mach}/{mach} scheme tolerable too.

subject: Racal NI5210 drivers for PC-NFS
q: PC-NFS 3.5 with a Racal NI5210 hangs at NET START on a 386 with a 16-bit VGA card. I think the shared memory defaults to C000. Any ideas?
a: With most VGA cards the first usable NI5210 address is C800, not C000. Setting it wrong makes NET START hang. If it hangs while searching for a YP server, check for an interrupt conflict instead.

subject: Disk Thrashing when using PCDOS standard I/O
q: Using a pipe in a DOS command line with an NFS drive as the default makes our Sun server's disk thrash and eats network bandwidth. We run PC-NFS 3.0. Is it sending one byte per packet, and can that be changed?
a: That's fixed in PC-NFS 3.0.1, which has been shipping since the summer. Call Sun's CSD for the upgrade. Sigh, running the old release and then wondering why it misbehaves.

subject: problem with rsh under PC-NFS
q: Using rsh under PC-NFS, a dummy account works but my own login gives "Permission denied. rcmd: Too many open files." Raising the file limits doesn't help. What's wrong?
a: The open files message is a red herring. It just means you lack permission for remote shell on that machine. Add the PC hosts to hosts.equiv or to .rhosts in your home directory. Only valid users can run remote commands, so check that too.

subject: PC-NFS - What is it?
q: What is PC-NFS? Can I use it to make a PC hard drive accessible via NFS from an SCO Xenix box, and what does it do to the PC's performance?
a: No, unless Sun changed it lately, PC-NFS is client-side only; it gives PCs access to big shared disks, not the reverse. Transfers run about like disk to disk, but you need ethernet, and it eats around 200k. Typical PC networking weirdness, especially on 386s.

subject: login hangs when server dies
q: When an NFS server dies, login on all its clients hangs after displaying /etc/motd, even though nothing needs files from the dead server. Why does this happen at login time?
a: It wasn't $PATH, dfspace, or getwd() stat()-ing a mountpoint. It was the mount option noquota, undocumented in the poster's manuals but essential. Use it on the NFS mounts. Typical: the manuals leave out the one option that matters.

subject: Barry Shein's nfsstone Benchmark
q: Where can I get Barry Shein's nfsstone benchmark? I have nhfsstone, but I'm told it isn't the same.
a: Both the benchmark code and the original paper are available by anonymous ftp from encore.com. Next time, check ftp before bothering the whole net.

subject: PC-NFS SLIP at 19.2 kbaud?
q: Why is PC-NFS SLIP limited to 9600 baud, and can anyone get 19.2 kbaud working?
a: Don't know why Sun limits it, but it can be done. One person ran PC-NFS over SLIP at 38.4 Kbps from a 286 PC. They needed a small program of about 15-20 lines of C to tweak bits in the serial port interface. Hardly rocket science.

subject: Speed difference using cp over NFS
q: Why is copying files over NFS between two SparcStation 2s about five times faster when pulling the data than when pushing it with cp?
a: Pulling means an NFS read and a local write. Pushing means a local read and an NFS write. NFS writes are synchronous, so they crawl next to a local asynchronous write, unless your server has NVRAM to speed it up. Basic stuff, really.

subject: Old Telebit vs New 9600 baud modem
q: For running PPP, should I use an old Telebit Trailblazer with PEP at 19.2k, or a new 9600 baud V.32 modem? Would I see better interactive performance from the 9600?
a: The V.32 one. TCP/IP, whether SLIP or PPP, wants a full-duplex channel, and PEP is half duplex. PEP only wins on seriously bad lines. Without header compression it's a disaster. We ran both, and V.32 is better. Sigh.

subject: (none)
q: Can someone suggest good references on ASN.1, and is there an e-mail mechanism like for RFCs to get ISO and CCITT documents?
a: Get The Open Book by Marshall Rose, ISBN 0-13-643016-3. ISO and CCITT documents are copyrighted, so there's no free distribution like RFCs. That's how the standards process gets funded. Wish it were otherwise, but it isn't.

subject: IBM AADU and Clarkson packet drivers
q: Can IBM's AIX Access for DOS Users (AADU) drivers and Clarkson packet drivers share one ethernet board so I can run TN3270 at the same time?
a: A packet driver already supports multiple applications using different protocols at once. The -n option is only for converting IPX packet formats, which is irrelevant here. What you need is an AADU driver that calls a packet driver. Then both can talk concurrently. RTFM.

subject: Novell 802.3
q: Does Novell's "OSI Support" just mean tunnelling IPX inside 802.3 packets, swapping the Ethernet type field 8137 for an 802.3 length field? Have I got the wrong end of the stick?
a: Yes, you do. Novell has an FTAM product giving a full seven layer OSI stack for NetWare 3.11, so FTAM clients can reach the NetWare file system. IPX inside 802.3 is something they've done for years and was never called "OSI Support". Get your terms straight.

subject: PPP on STREAMS
q: Does anyone know of an implementation of PPP or SLIP for STREAMS, preferably for AT&T 386 and preferably with source?
a: There's a ppp-streams.tar.Z floating around on ftp.ee.lbl.gov, so go fetch it. If you want SLIP on AT&T SysV/386 R4, Win/TCP R4 includes a SLIP driver. Spider TCP/IP is also STREAMS based, if you're paying. Learn to use ftp.

subject: (none)
q: How can I cheaply connect small off-campus sites with a few PCs, Macs and Unix machines over 9600 bps leased lines using TCP/IP? Is there a public domain IP router between Ethernet and SLIP, or localtalk?
a: Use SLIP. A free SLIP for the Mac is at dustbin.cisco.com, A/UX ships with it, and slattach is the tool on Ultrix and A/UX. For Ethernet to Localtalk you need hardware, like a Kinetics Fastpath. No miracle freebie there.

subject: SENDMAIL configuration
q: How do I get sendmail on a Sun 4 to accept mail addressed to user@foo.net on host A.FOO.NET, which has an MX record, without hacking ruleset 8?
a: Quit fighting sendmail's config. One reply pulled smail 3.14 off uunet and had it running in about three days, and recommends it highly. Just clean out the logs in /usr/spool/smail weekly. Sendmail rules are a swamp, everybody knows that.

subject: Wanted : ethernet protocol list...
q: I see unknown ethernet protocol types on our network, such as x0808, x3c01 and xaaaa. Where can I get a list of what they are?
a: No list from me. But be careful: if your ethernet is throwing errors, bad packets show up with garbage types. Check the FCS (CRC), overrun, collision and runt counts first. Analyzers capture what they can from bad packets, so don't trust the type.

subject: ftp file type extenstion
q: I'm adding a non-standard contiguous file type to my ftp server and want standard clients to use it. Should I encode it in the path or add a new file structure via STRU?
a: Not STRU, that's the wrong tool; contiguous is orthogonal to the STRU attributes. Do what some IBM MVS implementations did and use the SITE command to pass the options before a STOR. Read the protocol spec before inventing things.

subject: Calling the NFSPROC_ 's in the Sun Network File System Protocol Specification
q: I'm reading the Sun NFS Protocol Specification version 2 and see calls like NFSPROC_GETATTR(). How do I generate these calls? Is there a header file or library that resolves them?
a: Read the RPCL and rpcgen docs so you can parse nfs_prot.x, then look at that file in /usr/include/rpcsvc. Then read the man pages for clntudp_create, clnt_call and clnt_destroy. After that it should be pretty clear. RTFM.

subject: can a Bridge do null padding
q: I'm trying to get a uucp link working through a Telebit modem to a Microcom AX/2400 that talks to a Bridge, then to a Decstation. An octal 15 is getting a spurious NUL after it and the protocol fails. Could the Bridge be doing this padding?
a: Yes, very likely. Your "bridge" is probably a terminal server, maybe from Bridge Communications, running as a Telnet client on that serial port. It maps <CR> to <CR><NUL> on inbound characters, assuming a human is typing. Think before you call things bridges.

subject: Shutting down sockets - HELP
q: If I bind an address to a BSD socket and the program crashes, how can I release that address so I can reuse it next run, without rebooting the node? Or can I force a bind to an apparently used address?
a: Quit hardcoding the port. Bind with INADDR_ANY and let the OS pick a port, then rendezvous at a well known port using datagrams to exchange the real one. That way nothing stays tied up. Not Apollo specific either, so stop blaming the box.

subject: bug in BSD tahoe res_send()?
q: In BSD tahoe res_send.c, with several nameservers in resolv.conf, only the first gets queried on the early retries because of connect() and send(). Is this a bug, and how do I fix it?
a: Yes, it's a bug. Change the test from nscount == 1 OR retry == _res.retry to AND, so the connected-send path is used only with one nameserver on the first try. The tahoe BIND is ancient anyway, so check 4.4-reno before whining.

subject: Question on Fusion Software
q: Is the Fusion TCP/IP package used on Fujitsu FMR PCs in Japan the same Fusion software we have in the States? We need documentation to do testing.
a: Yes, same thing, though the Japanese version is a bit older and somewhat modified. The program interface and docs should be the same. Don't expect a full match on every detail, and send the customer support guy a note rather than posting.

subject: Looking for traceroute for SunOS4.0.3
q: Is there a traceroute for SunOS 4.0.3 on Sun3s and Sun4s that someone has running?
a: Yes, grab traceroute_pkg.tar.Z from uunet.uu.net in /networking. It has the new kernel .o's and all the sources you need, with the patched ip_icmp.c and raw_ip.c plus traceroute.c. Needs kernel mods, so don't whine about it.

subject: Ethernet 'null transceiver'?
q: Is there such a thing as a null transceiver, a way to connect two thick-wire Ethernet machines without real transceivers?
a: Yes. American Network Connections makes the ANC-10 Ethernet AUI-AUI Direct Connection Device. It behaved very well for us, and it even has LEDs. Buy it from a distributor.

subject: Proteon's behaviour
q: Our Proteon router sends small test packets to itself through both Ethernet interfaces every so often, eating bandwidth. Can the frequency be reduced?
a: It's two packets every 3.5 to 4 seconds, hard to see that eating real bandwidth. You can order the software with the maintenance feature disabled per interface, but then the gateway can't tell if the Ethernet is down and may advertise dead subnets via RIP.

subject: DNS ghost server
q: Our old nameserver 'ghost' and its former addresses live on in BIND 4.8.1 even after TTLs expire and we removed all delegations. Why does the ghost persist?
a: Most likely the root nameservers were never asked to delete the old NS and glue records, so the stale data keeps circulating until that's fixed. And post real names instead of phony ones, or nobody can look it up for you.

subject: Telnet's ECHO option
q: Per RFC 857 I send DONT ECHO and get WONT ECHO, yet a BSD host keeps echoing anyway. Am I misreading the Telnet ECHO option, or is BSD broken?
a: BSD gets it right. DONT ECHO is not DONT OUTPUT. What looks like echo is program output, like login printing the name you type character by character. The Telnet echo options have nothing to do with that.

subject: Encrypted SMTP Mail?
q: RFC1113, 1114 and 1115 describe encrypted SMTP mail. Are there any implementations out there to test and evaluate?
a: Trusted Information Systems has software based on MH mail that does this and plans wide distribution. Catch is, the public key algorithms are licensed from RSA, who patented them, and you pay $25 per user for two years for certification. Enjoy that.

subject: NCSA KA9Q
q: What do the acronyms NCSA and KA9Q mean when people talk about tn3270?
a: NCSA is the National Center for Supercomputing Applications at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. KA9Q is nobody's guess here, and ignore the joke expansions. Sigh, look it up before asking the net.

subject: What is SNMP
q: What is SNMP? My Fastpath IV registers itself as a gateway and also as an SNMP when I check the network.
a: Simple Network Management Protocol. That's what the letters say, so it's hardly a mystery. For more, get Marshall Rose's book, "The Simple Book", Prentice Hall, ISBN 0138126119. Read it before asking again.

subject: Configuration Test Protocol
q: What is the Configuration Test Protocol that uses ethernet type 09000 packets? Is it documented in any RFC, and is it a kind of ethernet ping?
a: Yes, it's a sort of Ethernet ping. It's in the DIX Ethernet spec, Version 2.0, not an RFC. Controllers reply to test packets or forward them on. IEEE 802.3 dropped it, so only DEC still supports it much. Read the spec.

subject: WIN/TCP for VMS, ping and privileges [repost]
q: What privileges does ping need under WIN/TCP for VMS, since it uses raw sockets?
a: SYSPRV does it. That's all. Not exactly hard to remember.

subject: rlogin -> character per packet ?
q: When I rlogin over TCP/IP, is each typed character sent in its own packet? Can I control this? My link has a half second round trip and typing is painfully slow.
a: Typically yes: one character costs three packets, the character itself, the remote host's echo, and an acknowledgement. I'm not sure you can change that, or would want to. It's how remote echo works, so live with it.

subject: Hitchhikers Guide to Internet, Intro to Internet Protocols
q: Where can I get the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Internet and Hedrick's Introduction to the Internet Protocols by ftp?
a: Anonymous FTP to uxc.cso.uiuc.edu. The Krol guide is pub/hgi.me and the Hedrick paper is pub/tcp-ip-intro.me. Both sit in the same place, so a quick look would have saved you a posting.

subject: TCP/IP Between PCs and Mainframes...What Physical Layers?
q: With IBM's mainframe TCP/IP and OS/2 Extended Edition's TCP/IP, what physical layers can be used? Ethernet surely, but what about token ring and SDLC, since that's how most PCs link to mainframes?
a: Ethernet and token ring both go via the 8232 (PC AT with an Ungermann-Bass card), the 3172, or the 9370 with its 802.3 card. Devices that speak the CETI channel protocol work too. No announced 3174 token ring support or SDLC for PCs. Don't hold your breath for it.

subject: TCP flow control query
q: With TCP flow control, when the receiver advertises a zero window, are the ACKs from the stalled host valid probe responses, and when should the receiver advertise that its window has opened?
a: The ACK is just the answer to the sender's zero-window probe. The ACK doesn't matter much, the window size in it does, because that lets the sender resume. When the receive window goes from zero to non-zero, the receiver should send an update on its own. It's in the RFCs.

subject: Zone transfers for "."
q: Do zone transfers work for the root domain "."? How do the root servers stay in sync?
a: Berkeley bind 4.8.1 makes a total mess of root zone transfers, and 4.8.3 reportedly has the same problem. So the argument is about buggy software, not the idea. Presumably the real root servers don't run Berkeley bind.

subject: Question about sending email from bitnet & internet host
q: I can send mail from a BITNET VAX/VMS node and an Internet VM/CMS host, but I have trouble mailing people whose addresses have bangs (!). Does handling these address types depend on the system (VAX, IBM VM) or on the network (BITNET, Internet)?
a: Depends on the mailer software, not the box. Plain JNET on a BITNET VMS VAX can't handle bang paths, since those come from UUCP and vanilla Unix. Get PMDF or MX on the VAX and they translate bang paths reasonably well. Sigh, read up on it.

subject: Bind mods to call a program
q: I want to hack BIND 4.8.3 to add a PROG record type that runs a program and returns its output as an A record, for load balancing. Has anyone done this?
a: Don't fork and exec a process for every A query, that's wasteful. Have a separate server process, RPC or AF_UNIX, wait for requests from your modified BIND and answer them directly. Saves the overhead, in case that wasn't obvious.

subject: questionable resolver code
q: Isn't res_search wrong to append the local domain whenever a name doesn't end in a dot? Typing ping jimi.cs.unlv.edu generates queries like jimi.cs.unlv.edu.cs.unlv.edu.
a: That's standard behaviour and correct. The default domain is added if there's no trailing dot, and if that fails it retries without. Multi-level domains like abc.ocf would otherwise fail, and the extra queries resolve locally and cost little. Think before you patch the resolver.

subject: Problems with packet drivers and mouse
q: After loading packet drivers and starting a mouse app, running NCSA Telnet makes the mouse stop working until I restart the app. I have a serial Microsoft mouse and a WD8003EBT board at IRQ 3. What's the conflict?
a: Your serial mouse is on COM2, and COM2 uses IRQ 3. The ISA bus can't share interrupt lines, so move the WD8003EBT off IRQ 3. This comes up every week.

subject: Any terminal emulators that run under FTP's Software????
q: Are there terminal emulators that work with FTP Software's package and allow complete keyboard mapping like NCSA Telnet's?
a: Any emulator that supports BIOS Int 14h will work with FTP's TNGLASS. For NCSA-style mappings, use MS-DOS Kermit, which is where the NCSA keyboard material came from. Not exactly hard to find.

subject: KA9A What is it?
q: Could somebody explain what KA9A NOS is?
a: It's KA9Q NOS, not KA9A. Sigh. It's a network operating package mainly for the IBM PC, ported to Amiga, Atari ST, Mac and UNIX, bringing TCP/IP to amateur packet radio. It has an IP router, telnet, ftp, smtp and finger servers and clients. Source is free by anonymous FTP.

subject: PC/TCP speed
q: Does PC-NFS run faster than PC/TCP from FTP Software? PC/TCP accesses files on our Ultrix system slower than our current 3COM server, and I thought NFS would be at least as fast as anything written by a DOS software company.
a: 3Com protocols are designed specifically for DOS. NFS servers blast data as fast as possible, the dumb PC ethernet cards drop packets, and then everything gets retransmitted. Read and write sizes and checksumming matter too: PC-NFS does 8K unchecksummed writes and 1K reads, InterDrive does 1K checksummed both ways.

subject: RPC on sockets on MSDOS?
q: Has Sun's RPC been ported to MSDOS on top of a socket layer over TCP/IP? If not, what's a good socket layer to use?
a: Don't port it yourself. Look at Netwise RPC, which runs over many TCP/IP packages for DOS. RPC is their main product, so it had better be good. Saves you the grief.

subject: BootP Server
q: Has anyone written a BootP server for the PC/IP package that runs on a PC?
a: Port the CMU public-domain Unix bootp server to a DOS socket library like PC/TCP or PC/NFS, as long as it doesn't lean on Unix-only functions. DOS socket libraries only do read, write and close on sockets, and have no dbm. Don't expect Unix miracles.

subject: Accessing the Packet Drivers
q: Has anyone written a standard C library for accessing the packet driver directly?
a: Not yet, but the 8.x release of the packet drivers will include public domain C code donated by Phil Karn. Don't hold your breath, it's not quite out. Patience, kid.

subject: POPMail 2.3 won't work.
q: I got POPMail 2.3 and it claims it can't find the packet driver, though 2.1 and 2.2beta3 worked fine for me. Anybody got it working?
a: Works fine here, even alongside Novell. Check your packet driver's interrupt, mine is at 0x61, and some programs search for it while others don't. Some PDs are flaky too; swap to a plain WD or NE card and it's fine. Sigh, basic debugging.

subject: IPXPKT
q: I have two different IPXPKTs, one from an in-house source and one from the Clarkson packet driver collection, and they seem to work in opposite senses. What's going on?
a: Name collision. Clarkson's IPXPKT is a packet driver that uses IPX to do its work. Your in-house source made a packet driver shell and carelessly gave it the same name. Most people call that one pdipx, or plain ipx, though some say ipxpdi.

subject: RFC's by mail
q: I tried to get RFC1147 by mail from service@sri-nic.arpa but it bounced as undeliverable. Is there a different address to request RFCs by mail?
a: SRI-NIC.ARPA is now known as NIC.DDN.MIL. Use that host. This is what happens when you never read the announcements.

subject: Clarkson Packet Driver for Cabletron cards?
q: Is there a Clarkson Packet Driver for Cabletron cards that has the -n option for 802.3 packet conversion with dual Novell and TCP stacks?
a: No, and the author is tired of being asked; Cabletron is welcome to the little snippet of code that implements -n. But you don't need it: use the card's own packet driver with an IPX.COM from NSHPD.OBJ 1.05EC, which does 802.3 by default.

subject: packet driver for Cabletron TP card
q: Is there a packet driver available from Clarkson or Cabletron for the Cabletron E1020 8-bit 10BaseT Ethernet card?
a: Not from Clarkson. Get it from Cabletron, though, who are an enthusiastic packet driver supplier. Honestly, you could have just asked them.

subject: And yet more NCSA Telnet V2.3beta and 3C503 questions
q: Is there an FTP client that works with NCSA Telnet V2.3 and a 3C503 card in packet driver mode?
a: You're using the wrong FTPBIN, obviously. NCSA's 2.2 version didn't support packet drivers. Clarkson University made those changes, so look on their grape.ecs.clarkson.edu archive.

subject: ka9q performance?
q: My 8088 PC running ka9q with a 3c501 and Clarkson packet driver only gets about 12 kbps over ftp to a NeXT, and large files time out. Is that expected, or can it be tuned?
a: The 3c501 can't handle back-to-back packets, and your NeXT will send them if the PC advertises a big enough TCP window. Make the TCP window the same size as the TCP MSS. Blame the cheap card.

subject: NCSA Telnet and FTP to VAX/VMS
q: NCSA Telnet and FTP to our VAX/VMS running Wollongong TCP/IP are unreliable, slow and choppy, and sometimes can't connect, though PC to PC works fine on thin wire ethernet. What's wrong?
a: The fix was to disable heartbeat on a multiport repeater. After that, Telnet and FTP worked fine with the default config.tel settings. Check your ethernet hardware before fiddling with software parameters for weeks.

subject: HELP! my lpd dies!
q: The KA9Q PC lpd hangs my PC when I start it, though the ftp server and the other servers start fine. Why would lpd die?
a: Don't start lpd from autoexec.net. Start it by hand at the net> prompt instead. It's a hassle to retype after every reboot, but nobody has found a real fix, so quit whining.

subject: Packet drivers (what is it ?)
q: What are packet drivers? Can NetBios and TCP/IP coexist on top of one, and will it let our Lantastic PCs reach mail and news on our UNIX hosts?
a: Packet drivers hide the differences between Ethernet cards behind a software interface, so several protocols such as IPX, NetBios and TCP/IP can sit on one card. They can coexist. But Lantastic doesn't support the packet driver spec, so it won't work for you. Complain to Artisoft.

subject: pointer to CHARON?
q: Where can I FTP CHARON, the PD/shareware bi-directional print spooler between UN*X and Novell Netware?
a: Try splicer.cba.hawaii.edu or sun.soe.clarkson.edu. Mind there are several versions: the newest one is an SMTP gateway for Pegasus Mail and won't do the print spooling you want, so dig up an older one. Read the docs before you grab the wrong one.

subject: Looking for a WD8003 ODI driver
q: Where can I find a WD8003 ODI driver? Why didn't Novell include one for such a popular board in LAN Workplace for DOS?
a: The Western Digital ODI driver wasn't certified until recently, which is why it wasn't shipped. It exists now, and it may make the next LAN WorkPlace release. Getting one little file onto a distribution is more work than you'd guess.

subject: TCP-IP SOFTWARE VENDORS
q: Where can I get names, addresses and phone numbers of vendors of TCP-IP software for DOS PCs, such as FTP Software and Wollongong?
a: FTP to nic.ddn.mil and get netinfo:vendors-guide.doc. It's the definitive reference, updated every six months or so. Comes up every few weeks; use it.

subject: Use of Wollongong Win/TCP for DOS with AT&T StarLan 10 NAU
q: Will Wollongong Win/TCP for DOS work with AT&T StarLAN 10 Network Access Unit or the StarLan-10 EN100 boards in AT&T 6386 computers?
a: Clarkson has a packet driver for both of those boards, and Win/TCP supports packet drivers. So yes, it works. Funny how the vendor never knows its own product.

subject: Cabletron card & NCSA Telnet
q: Will the Cabletron E1010 twisted pair Ethernet card work with NCSA Telnet, natively or with a packet driver? I think it's based on the WD8003 chipset.
a: Cabletron writes their own packet drivers, so call them and ask. That's the only way Ethernet card makers learn that people want drivers. Tell them you won't buy a board without one.

subject: Getting Win/QVT/Net to work.
q: WinQVT/Net 1.53 gives me the error "Packet Driver error 11 SetRcvMode" with the packet driver that came with my Everex Ethernet card. Should I use a different one?
a: You're running a pre-9.x packet driver; the current release fixes that. Grab the latest qvtnet16.zip from cica in pub/pc/win3/util too. And since you can continue past the error and it works, it's hardly a catastrophe. Sigh.

subject: Novell on top of Packet Drivers under MS Windows
q: Windows 3.0 says it cannot load vnetware.386 when I run Novell on top of a Clarkson packet driver with PDIPX. Is there a working vnetware driver, or am I doing something wrong?
a: Heresy, but it works: comment out the netware lines in system.ini so Windows stays ignorant of NetWare. Start NetWare and log in outside of Windows, then everything works inside it. Works fine here with a packet driver on a WD8003E. Stop fighting the vendor drivers.

subject: NTP/XNTP under SunOS 4.1?
q: Has anyone tried NTP/XNTP under SunOS 4.1? Any problems?
a: Yes, it runs fine under SunOS 4.1, no problems that I can see. Sigh, try it before asking the whole net.

subject: printing RFC1129
q: How can I print RFC1129 on a NeXT printer? It fails with limitcheck, OffendingCommand printerdevice.
a: Put /letter { } def, /legal { } def and /note { } def at the start of the file. The error means it's setting a paper size that confuses the NeXT interpreter. If that fails, find and remove any page size setting. It's device-dependent anyway. Ugly hack, but fine.

subject: OBIOS Questions
q: I have questions about the OBIOS P1256 spec. Is there a proposed way to include built-in self test for modules and units, to handle digital and analog I/O, and to handle general hardware configuration like timeouts and interrupts?
a: Self test, not really; a driver can test itself at initialization and return an error code. Analog and digital I/O aren't covered yet. First come SCSI, network, async serial, timer/counter and time-of-day clock, then experts can write specs for other device types. Config is part of the spec, supposedly.

subject: Specifications
q: Where can I get ASCII copies of software specs and standards, like DoD-STD-2167A and its DIDs? Is SIMTEL a likely source?
a: Yes, SIMTEL is it. The Ada Software Repository at WSMR-SIMTEL20.ARMY.MIL has 2167A and the DID templates in PD2:<ADA.DOD-STD-2167A>. The Ada Clearinghouse BBS has piles more ASCII files, and the CALS BBS has the CALS standards. Sigh, ask where to look first next time.

subject: looking for digital compass
q: Does anyone have details on digital compasses that can be interfaced to a mobile robot?
a: Radio Electronics ran an article on interfacing the Radio Shack flux-gate compass; you need two A/D channels. Marine compasses with RS-232 interfaces exist too, for around $500. Go read the article instead of asking for ANY information.

subject: I need a Scientific American refrence
q: I remember a Scientific American article a few years back about simple robots that sensed light bulbs and drove toward or away from them according to neuron-like programming. Does anyone remember the date or author?
a: Can't give you the issue date, but the author is Valentino Braitenberg. His book "Vehicles: Experiments in Synthetic Psychology", MIT Press, 1984, elaborates on the same topic. Read that instead of squinting at indexes.

subject: Torque control of motors
q: I'm new to robotics. Are there motors where I can specify the torque directly, by feeding in current instead of voltage?
a: Sigh. In most DC and torque motors, torque is proportional to armature current, so you servo the current. Back EMF fights a plain voltage drive as speed rises, so use a current loop or a PWM amplifier. It's elementary motor theory.

subject: Insuring data integrity in dirt
q: My shop is too dusty for 3 1/2 inch MS-DOS disks. What do people use to carry programs to CNC machines, other than sealing a drive in a steel case or using paper tape?
a: Keep the drive out of the shop. One setup uses a 40 foot cable between the robot and its controller, and the controller talks RS-232 to a PC for up to 50 more feet. Put the PC in the clean room. Sealing drives in steel is silly.

subject: The project that inspired the newsgroup
q: We're setting up a lab with at least 7 robotic workstations. Any suggestions for safety equipment, such as light curtains or safety mats?
a: Skip the pricey light curtains. Cheap infrared sensors from the home-security market do nearly the same job. If you use invisible barriers, post a BIG sign, because people will keep tripping the system by pointing at the cute little robot. Sigh.

subject: Suggestion wanted. HERO 2000 programming environment.
q: What programming environment would you suggest for writing C software for a HERO 2000 robot from a PS/2 Model 50 running MS-DOS 3.3?
a: Borland's Turbo C works fine on that setup, and it should download to the HERO over a serial port without trouble. Microsoft C is the other choice if you need Windows hooks, but it costs plenty. Don't overthink it.

subject: Polaroid Ultra Sonic Ranging Sensors
q: Where can I get the Polaroid ultrasonic ranging sensor, or a designer's kit, or a cheap used version?
a: Polaroid's own ad in NASA Tech Briefs lists the Designer's Kit at $165, and their applications engineers take questions. A cheaper route is the Circuit Cellar sonar ranging kit with transducer, about $79, which hooks to a parallel port. Read the ads, they're right there.

subject: X11R5
q: Has anyone tried using the Andrew distribution with the recent release of X11R5?
a: Yes. PL10 binaries built against X11R4 patch level 18 run fine under the MIT sample server on a Sun 4 with SunOS 4.1.1. They end up statically linked against the X libraries, which is annoying, but it works.

subject: How do you measure code quality?
q: How do you measure code quality? Is bugs per line of code any good, and is there a simpler method than the complex methodologies?
a: Many define quality as adherence to specification, but better to take the customer's view. Does the product work for them? A defect nobody finds isn't a defect. Bugs per line is management's toy. You can't test forever or ship junk, so find the middle.

subject: using Halstead effort equations
q: I implemented Halstead's effort equations and calculated the numbers for various functions. Are there guidelines for interpreting them like there are for McCabe's cyclomatic complexity, and how are they used?
a: No handy thresholds, so don't go making grand claims. Look for correlations between your Halstead numbers and real things like faults found or the cost to produce the code. Basili's papers in IEEE Trans. on Software Engineering, 1983, are where to start.

subject: DOD-STD-2167A
q: Is there a book on developing under DOD-STD-2167A? The standard is useless as a tutorial and I can't tell what a 'capability' means.
a: Never seen a 2167 tutorial book. A 'capability' is just a rubric for requirements: performance, features, and so on. IEEE 830/1984 is a decent outline for requirements specs, but the DoD wants extra reviews and paperwork on top. Welcome to the God-given lifecycle.

subject: Is it Art or is it Engineering
q: Programmers say software development isn't really engineering. What do real engineers do that we don't? Is there anything in programming analogous to tolerance?
a: Yes, there is. Numerical analysis has convergence criteria, which is tolerance as measured with micrometers. Routines that check their inputs, or the return code on close(), are the old overbuilt-beam safety margin. We call it paranoia. Heuristics fit too, if you must romanticize it.

subject: WANTED:testing coverage analysis tools
q: What tools are there for branch-level test coverage analysis of C programs on Unix workstations?
a: Try tcov, which comes standard with SunOS. Use the -a flag to cc and you get code coverage figures. SunOS also has performance tools. Mind you, the poster is still evaluating it, so no guarantees.

subject: specification problem using Estelle
q: In a sliding window protocol every unacknowledged message needs its own retransmission timer. Using Estelle's delay statement it seems I can only specify one periodic timer. Is there a nice way to specify multiple independent timers in Estelle?
a: Sure, just make a separate transition for each timer. Use an any clause over the window index, a provided clause for sent and not acked, and a delay on each. All the delays run independently. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: Making the preprocessor substitute a '#'
q: Can an ANSI C preprocessor macro like #define FOO # pragma bar expand to a '#' directive? The # seems to be treated as stringizing.
a: No, can't be done in ANSI C. Stringizing only applies in function-like macros, so that's not your problem. Replaced text is never rescanned as a preprocessing directive, even if it looks like one. Read the standard.

subject: HELP for unbuffered terminal IO needed !
q: How can I recognize keystrokes immediately with unbuffered terminal I/O in C in a standard, portable way? The FILE definitions differ between our VAX/VMS and Ultrix systems.
a: There is no standard solution. ANSI C doesn't even promise a keyboard exists, let alone unbuffered input. Curses is the closest de facto standard you'll get, and POSIX is the written one. And stop peeking at FILE; a portable program shouldn't care.

subject: Boolean values...
q: Is the expression (X == Y) guaranteed in C to give either 0 or 1, so I can portably use it as an array index like y[param == 1]?
a: For ordinary relational operands, yes, the standard gives 0 or 1. For function pointers or null pointer constants the standard guarantees nothing, sigh. Beware isa*** macros, which often return merely non-zero. If you need a sure 0 or 1, use !!.

subject: system() length bound?
q: The system() function is in ANSI C. How long can its argument be, and how can a conforming program find out?
a: The standard gives you nothing. System() just returns an implementation-defined value, so the implementor is supposed to document any length limit. Can a program portably find out at run-time? No. Read the compiler docs, like everybody else.

subject: POSIX reference
q: What is the relationship between Standard C and POSIX compliant C? Is there a good POSIX programmer's reference?
a: POSIX defines two kinds of C conformance, Standard C support and Common-Usage C support. A system with the first fully supports ANSI C, and Standard C plus POSIX ports far more easily. As for a reference, the Posix Programmer's Guide by Donald Lewine from O'Reilly. Read section 1.3.3.1 first.

subject: ISO Latin 1? (was Re: design by committee)
q: Does ISO Latin 1 address oriental languages like Kanji? Do trigraphs?
a: Neither addresses it at all. ISO Latin 1 handles small-alphabet languages with 8 bits and hasn't a prayer with large alphabets. Trigraphs just let you write C in the ISO 7-bit set. Danish proposals don't help either.

subject: List Library functions...
q: I'm new to Borland's C++ and want to list the functions in a particular library. Is there a way?
a: Sure. TLIB.EXE comes with Turbo C, Turbo C++ and Borland C++. Run it with no parameters and it tells you how to list modules, extract them, and insert, delete or replace them. Try reading what it prints.

subject: constant expressions
q: Should a C++ translator identify 1-1 as a constant expression evaluating to zero, even without optimization?
a: Best guess: it needn't compute it at compile time, but it must remember the expression is constant. If it's converted to a pointer, the code must check for zero and make a null pointer. The result has to be as if optimization were done.

subject: Dutch IJ
q: In a Dutch phone book, how are the surnames Meijer and Meyer sorted? Should they be mixed together or kept apart as separate spellings?
a: Scholars would insist on listing all the Meijers first, then the Meyers. Phone books, though, mix them together by first name for practical reasons. Sigh, theory versus practice, as usual.

subject: ISO 8859
q: What exactly is defined by ISO standard 8859?
a: It's the standard for single-byte 8-bit encoding of graphical character shapes, currently six subsets. The most popular is 8859/1, covering most Western European languages. Every subset carries 7-bit US ASCII in its bottom half. Not hard to look up.

subject: French Standard Character Set.
q: My French article written on a Macintosh shows garbled accented characters on an IBM-PC. Which machine uses the international standard character set, and is there a French standard?
a: Neither one. Mac and PC code those characters differently, and neither directly supports ISO Latin-1, the closest thing to an international set for French. Write import-export routines that translate through Latin-1 as the common exchange format. Welcome to character sets, kid.

subject: Where can I get ISO standards documents?
q: Where can I get ISO standards documents, like the 9646 OSI conformance testing parts? I'd prefer ftp, then email, then buying.
a: Dream on about ftp. ISO documents are copyrighted and neither ISO nor ANSI allows electronic distribution, since sales fund the standards work. Buy them from ANSI in New York or from ISO in Geneva. Write and ask for the catalog.

subject: POSIX 1003.1 and <sys/types.h>
q: Does POSIX 1003.1 forbid including <sys/types.h> inside other headers such as <grp.h>? I couldn't find it in the book, and if true, why?
a: There's no specific prohibition in the standard. But it's non-trivial to implement safely, since the header mustn't surprise the programmer with unexpected typedefs or prototypes. A portable program should include <sys/types.h> itself anyway, so gid_t is there. Do your homework.

subject: POSIX.1 requires shell???
q: Does POSIX.1 require that a shell interface exist? Could dot 1 simply allow a shell, conforming to POSIX.2 if present, without requiring it?
a: No. POSIX.1 doesn't require a shell. Honestly, read the standard before posting.

subject: Question re: International UNIX
q: Is there a standard under development for International UNIX supporting different foreign languages?
a: Not as one thing. Start with POSIX, where the 1003.2 working group handles internationalization with help from /usr/group and EUUG, and ANSI C, which also covers some of it. Learn those two efforts first.

subject: problem - keyboard input becoming intermittent
q: After three years my 3b1 console started losing keystrokes intermittently, about every other one, though not at the shell prompt. Is it the keyboard or a board problem?
a: Test the keyboard on an otherwise quiet system first. If it's still flaky it's the keyboard, maybe a keycap spring that needs readjusting. Or two machines running gettys to each other on tty000, which floods the console. Don't guess, test.

subject: BITFTP
q: BITFTP works when my mail goes to a machine directly connected to UUNET, but when the path has two more machines it won't send me files and won't answer HELP. Why, and can I specify the path?
a: Likely your return address. BITFTP wants a fully-qualified domain address, and there's no official .uucp top-level domain, so replies to a .uucp address usually die. Use a real FQDN from another machine. Also, plenty of sites trash BITFTP traffic because it spews files and hammers uucpNET. Grumble.

subject: HDB and async_main
q: How do I use async_main on my 7300 UNIX PC with HDB UUCP? I need the vt100 emulation.
a: Don't sweat it, it works with HDB present. async_main doesn't depend on the uucp tables or programs, since it uses the ph system's databases. The only thing shared is the lockfiles, and HDB was set up to keep them in the old location. Sigh, nothing to fix.

subject: Is it possible to hang a scanner off the 3b1?
q: Is it possible to hang a flatbed scanner off a 3b1?
a: If the scanner has a serial output and you have software that can interpret it, sure. The RS-232 port is the only general-purpose I/O on the 3B1. No SCSI, IEEE-488 or ADC cards exist for the expansion slots. Don't expect miracles.

subject: ksh broke my vi (repost)
q: The new ksh broke my vi: from vi, ':!ls %' passes the filename with the high bit set on every character, so ls can't find it. The old ksh and /bin/sh don't do this. Any fixes or workarounds?
a: Vi sets that high bit to quote the filename; older shells masked down to 7 bits, newer ones allow extended character sets. Workaround: reinstall the old ksh as /bin/oldksh and set SHELL=/bin/oldksh in your .exrc. Or use a modern editor, like Jove.

subject: Seeking modem pinouts
q: What are the recommended cable pinnings for connecting an external modem to a 3b1?
a: Straight through on pins 1 through 7, then 20, 15, 17, 22 and 24, so TD, RD, RTS, CTS, DSR, ground, DTR and the rest. CD on pin 8 is the odd one. Honestly, the manual would have told you.

subject: file modification date reset on "mv" to floppy filesystem
q: Why did mv to a floppy filesystem reset the file modification date to today? Is that a bug?
a: Yes, it's a documented bug. The bugs section of newer Unix manuals like SunOS lists this, and the UnixPC manpage implies mv behaves differently across filesystems. Read the manpage next time.

subject: 16 bit sound samplers.
q: Are there any 16 bit sound samplers for the Archimedes?
a: Try Armadilo Systems Ltd. in Uppingham. They do a stereo 16 bit record/playback system with an object oriented front end. It takes over the whole machine instead of running in the desktop. Price? Ask them, I'm not your secretary.

subject: SoundTrackers
q: Does a SoundTracker module creator exist for the Archimedes? All the modules around seem to be Amiga ports, and I'd like to write some myself.
a: Yes, Tracker, from The Serial Port, makes 8-channel soundtrackers. Check Acorn User for the price. Get the latest version, since two are floating about and one's better. Honestly, look in the magazines first.

subject: ftp & newcastle
q: Everything I've downloaded from Newcastle by FTP refuses to de-arc, giving 'Bad header in file' errors in Sparkplug. Is it my link or something else?
a: Not your link. Albert is converting all the Sparked files to .tar.Z.uu, so Sparkplug can't read them. Nobody announced it, naturally. Upside: you can now extract just the bits you want before downloading, which beats the incompatible arc formats.

subject: Highnote, A448b sampler software
q: Has Highnote, the sampler software for the A448b, been updated beyond version 2.03? Can I get an upgrade from Armadillo?
a: Forget it. Armadillo's receivers were called in, so they've folded. There may have been a later release in '89, but nobody is left to send it to you. Next time, buy from a company that lasts.

subject: anybody ported GNU Emacs?
q: Has anybody ported GNU Emacs to the Archimedes? I know of the port by David Pilling, but I hear it isn't very good and doesn't run in the desktop.
a: Pilling's thing is MicroEMACS, not GNU Emacs, whatever his adverts imply. Real GNU Emacs is so full of Unixisms that people gave up on it. It'd take months unless someone writes a Unix lib for RISC OS with pipes and fork. Sigh.

subject: MEMC and video DMA question
q: In an Archimedes with two or more MEMCs, can one MEMC's RAM handle video DMA while the other runs at full speed? Does MEMC do general-purpose DMA, say for winchesters?
a: No. One MEMC is master and the rest are slaves, and the CPU and video DMA share the same data bus, so one holds up the other no matter how many banks you add. MEMC does DMA for video and sound only, no general DMA. The rumour was right.

subject: Double precision on Beeb
q: Is there any way to do double-precision arithmetic in BBC BASIC on a Model B or Master?
a: Not out of the box. Get The BASIC ROM User Guide, which details how BBC BASIC does floating point, and write your own routines. Use a disassembler on the BASIC ROM and work from that. Sorry, nobody's handing you a ready-made library.

subject: Whatever happened to AIM?
q: Whatever happened to AIM, the picture processing software that came out when the Archimedes first appeared? Is it still PD and does a copy exist?
a: It's on Archive magazine's shareware disc #21, along with QRT and an old version of !Translator. It's not a RISC OS application, and I don't know of a later version. Went off *Configuring all over the place, so don't expect polish.

subject: 68030, cacheing, DMA devices
q: A DMA device will screw up a system running a data cache, and the 68030 has an onboard data cache. Can the MMU be told that certain pages of memory are not to be cached?
a: Yes, the chip designers thought of it. Each translation entry has a cache inhibit bit, and there is also a cache inhibit input for external hardware, cycle by cycle. So the OS should mark DMA-target memory uncacheable. Whether it works in the Amiga is another matter.

subject: ARP 1.3 ARes and AmigaDOS 1.3 More don't get along well...
q: ARes from ARP 1.3 refuses to use the resident copy of AmigaDOS 1.3 More v3.27, claiming the checksum has changed. Is there any way to fix this?
a: Use the undocumented NOCHECK switch when you ARes More, and the checksum complaints stop. No crashes or gurus so far, either. Why it happens is unknown. Of course, it's undocumented because the documentation still isn't out. Typical.

subject: loadwb delay
q: After installing Post 1.1 I kept getting 00000004 gurus, but everything worked when I used loadwb delay instead of loadwb. Can anybody explain this?
a: LoadWB re-initializes most of the Workbench screen data and returns before it finishes its work, so anything attaching to the screen too soon gets trampled. The delay option just waits a while, which fixes it only some of the time, since a busy startup can outlast the delay.

subject: .lzh files
q: All the LZH unpackers I found on abcfd20 are themselves compressed with LZH. How do I unpack the unpacker?
a: Chicken and egg, yes. Get zoo-2.01.pak from /amiga and run it, since it's self-extracting. Use zoo to unpack lharc-1.0.zoo, then use lharc to unpack LZ090.lzh. Laborious, but that's life.

subject: Problems with TeX on Amiga
q: AmigaTeX and TeX 3.0 use environment variables set with set or setenv. They work from the CLI, but after I enter SKsh I can't change them and TeX can't find its inputs. Why, and what's the fix?
a: TeX uses the Manx C way of handling environment variables, and your shell's built-in set and setenv don't touch the same global variables. Alias set to tex:c/set so you override the built-ins, if your shell lets you. Obvious, really.

subject: Binaries/Alt-Sources
q: Are comp.binaries.amiga and alt-sources working properly? I haven't seen anything new in either for at least three weeks, and I'm in Australia.
a: No, comp.binaries.amiga is broken at the moment. The archives are being moved to a new machine, and the moderation tools aren't finished moving yet. Submissions are still accepted at the old address and will be processed once the move is done. Be patient.

subject: DevCon Notes
q: Are the latest DevCon Notes available yet, and will the disks be available too?
a: Not yet. Notes and code disks are still in final revision and typesetting before going to the printers. Whether disks ship with the book is undecided. Stay tuned for price and availability, and quit pestering.

subject: Complex Numbers in C
q: Are there library functions for complex math in C, or will I have to write them all myself?
a: Get Lattice C++. It ships a complex number library with cos, exp, log, pow, sqrt, abs, real, imag, polar, conj and the usual operators, so you can write a = (b + d) * c like in FORTRAN. Quit whining about writing it yourself.

subject: A couple of dumb questions
q: Can I create my own Keymap files on the Amiga, and can I hook a 2000 to an Apple Mac II color monitor?
a: Yes to keymaps. The format is in the Rom Kernel Manual, though it's no picnic for a novice. No to the monitor. The Mac II uses a different scan rate, and the Amiga's display hardware sets resolution, not the monitor. Everyone confuses that.

subject: Amiga bridgeboard card and VGA card
q: Can a VGA card work with a Bridgeboard XT/AT in an Amiga 2000, or does it need a second monitor?
a: Any video card on the IBM bus side needs its own separate monitor, since it has no connection to the Amiga's display. The standard Amiga monitors manage CGA at best, so anything beyond that wants a multisync. Obvious, really.

subject: Commodore Announces Hard Disk Controller Upgrade?
q: Can an A2090 disk controller be upgraded to an A2090a, so it can boot under Kickstart 1.3, by swapping a chip or two?
a: Sounds unlikely. The 2090a has ROMs with the autoboot code, and the 2090 has no sockets for them. Sigh, dealers and their rumors.

subject: Math Games Wanted
q: Can anyone recommend an Amiga program for teaching and practicing basic arithmetic? It's easy to write a random-number drill, but kids expect more in the way of special effects.
a: Try Discovery Math, and there's Spelling and Trivia too. Yes, the Sesame Street generation wants fireworks with its arithmetic. Sigh.

subject: Question on the 286 Bridge card
q: Can the Amiga 286 Bridge card run OS/2, or Xenix or Microport?
a: Mostly a BIOS and hardware compatibility issue. If the software only uses BIOS calls and the bridgecard BIOS implements them, it should work. If it pokes the hardware directly, you'd have to beat on the low-level drivers. Too soon to tell. Don't hold your breath.

subject: Sonix problem and comments
q: Certain Sonix instruments, like HighHat and most of the IFF ones on the Data Disk, won't load with 'Can't load instrument from disk' on my single-drive Amiga. My own instruments load fine. Any ideas?
a: Sonix needs some system resource to load IFF files. Copy one IFF instrument to RAM: and load it while the System disk is in the drive. Once the resource loads, the rest load until reboot. Also check your RAM; samples are hungry.

subject: Way to go, CBM advertising! (and a silly wish for 1.4)
q: Could the Amiga have a WriteRastLine(rp, x, y, n, buf) routine to replace many WritePixel calls, and maybe a column version? Would it be faster in the system code than in ours?
a: Yes, there'd be a good performance advantage doing it in the system code. I believe it was implemented for 1.4, with horizontal and vertical versions of the routines. Maybe wait for the release before whining.

subject: DMCS & MIDI guru problem
q: Deluxe Music Construction Set crashes the machine when exiting, but only after using the MIDI interface. Is this a known problem, and is there a fix?
a: Known problem, yes. The 1.3.2 serial.device is to blame, so back-fit the 1.3 serial.device. DMCS does an illegal RemoveDevice with the io_Device pointer after CloseDevice, which only worked before 1.3.2. Don't flame CBM, the program is the broken one.

subject: VT100 v 2.9
q: Did I miss the release of VT100 v2.9 for the Amiga? I remember a message saying it was coming soon.
a: You didn't miss it. The author's day job got in the way, so 2.9 is at least a month from beta testing, maybe six weeks to release. Meanwhile, the 2.8A patch fixing the Kermit BYE guru has been sitting with the moderators for months.

subject: Tin Toy
q: Did anyone catch the Academy Awards? I heard Tin Toy from Pixar won something. What was it about?
a: It won the Oscar for best animated short subject. It's about a small one-man-band toy and his adventures with a baby. Can't describe it properly, you have to see it. Quit asking if it was an Amiga.

subject: HP DeskJet and AmigaTeX
q: Do I need a font cartridge or RAM expansion to use an HP DeskJet with AmigaTeX, and are there font limits?
a: No cartridge needed. TeX uploads its fonts to the printer, or composes a page bitmap in memory, so buy more memory instead. The DeskJet has none of the font size limits some 300 dpi machines have. You can also make your own sizes with AmigaMETAFONT.

subject: Linking amiga.lib before lc.lib (Lattice)
q: Do the C-like functions in amiga.lib (fprintf, fgetc and so on) behave exactly like real C functions when linking amiga.lib before lc.lib with Lattice?
a: No, they don't. They use a different stdio FILE pointer than Lattice, and expect 16 bit ints, so use %ld for Lattice ints. There's no floating point in their printf. Link with TWStartup.o instead of c.o, and put Amiga.lib before LC.lib. RTFM, the AutoDocs cover it.

subject: Power Supplies in Amigas
q: Do you Amiga users leave your machines on all the time, and have power line glitches ever eaten your machine?
a: Leave them on. Mine ran 24 hours a day for nearly two years, and others report the same. They shrug off glitches and brownouts that upset VAXen and Suns. Only a dropout mid-floppy-write hurts. Retry, what did you expect?

subject: Sprites (Mindwalker)
q: Does Electronic Arts really have a policy of upgrading their badly behaved Amiga games, which won't run with 1.2 and fast ram, for $7.50 plus the original disk?
a: Yes, they do. They'll replace it for $7.50 if you send in the complete package, or free if the warranty hasn't expired and you've got proof of purchase date. Next time, ask them before whining on the net.

subject: A3000 and a C compiler
q: Does Lattice C 5.10, or any Aztec C, really run on an A3000 with Workbench 2.0? Which should I get?
a: SAS/C 5.10, the Lattice successor, has the 2.0 sticker and ships with 1.3 and 2.0 include files. Any 5.x runs under 2.0, but older ones lack the includes. Commodore built Workbench 2.0 with it. I can't speak for Aztec.

subject: Does RAM: ever retry?
q: Does RAM: ever retry allocating memory after an Out of Disk Space requester? Hitting RETRY after freeing programs returns immediately.
a: Yes, but it wants a contiguous chunk of about 30K. Unload one big program rather than lots of little ones, and RETRY works. I've had over 100K free in pieces and still got the requester. Fragmentation, genius.

subject: An Emulator for the Amiga
q: Does a VT240 or similar graphics terminal emulator exist for the Amiga? VT100 and VT220 emulators don't work for GKS graphics on our VAX.
a: No. And it'll stay that way unless CBM decides a VT240 emulator is a strategic product for the Amiga. Don't hold your breath.

subject: UW status ??
q: Does anyone at Commodore have any official word on the rumored trade-up policy from the Amiga 1000 to the 2000?
a: No official word yet. Keep your ears to the net, and the official word will be posted. Be patient.

subject: amiga ==> 1581
q: Does anyone have a program that can write 1581 disks on the Amiga, like dos2dos but from Amiga format to 1581 format?
a: The "Transfer" program that comes with C64 Emulator II does 1581 and 1541 format. It will even let you use a real 1581 or 1541 drive for the copies if you don't trust the Amiga drives. Funny, nobody checked their own disks.

subject: Boot-Picture on HD
q: Does anyone have a utility that copies a boot sector from a floppy to a hard disk's boot sector, so I can use a BOOTGIRL picture boot block on my hard disk?
a: One of the fish disks has a program called TrackBack, or some variant, that copies boot sectors to files and back. It works with hard disks too, so back up the boot record and restore it to the other disk. Sigh, not hard.

subject: GNU CC
q: Does anyone have the source code for GNU CC, and has it been ported to the Amiga?
a: Someone has GCC itself running on the Amiga and is converting ld to produce Amiga hunk format, but no Unix-compatible libraries yet. Another says it's a memory hog, so don't expect much without several meg of RAM. Port the libraries yourself.

subject: RGB to HSV Colors
q: Does anyone know a formula for converting an RGB color value into an HSV one? I'd like the correct method.
a: Get "Procedural Elements for Computer Graphics" by David Rogers (McGraw-Hill, 1985). Pages 401 to 406 have pseudo-Pascal for RGB to HSV, HSV to RGB, and the HLS conversions. Took about an hour to turn into C, and they work. Read a book for once.

subject: Amateur Radio Software
q: Does anyone know of ham radio software for the Amiga? I'm thinking of writing Morse, RTTY and AMTOR programs but don't want to duplicate existing work.
a: Try the BBS-JC Amiga BBS in California, at 415-961-7250. It's run by a ham and has a collection of public domain ham software. Call before you reinvent the wheel, for once.

subject: PD Make for Amiga.
q: Does anyone know where to get a public-domain make for the Amiga? I use Lattice C 3.03 and can't build larger programs without it.
a: There's one on a very early Fred Fish disk, maybe disk 2. Don't expect much: it lacks many Unix make features and doesn't notice a failed step, blindly plowing on. Sigh, it's PD, what did you expect.

subject: Transformer (again)
q: Does the official Commodore upgrade of Transformer do everything PSTrans does, such as running under WB1.2, using expanded memory for 640K, and working with a 68010/20?
a: The official CBM Transformer 1.2 runs under the 1.2 OS and works with expanded memory, so 640K is available. A 010/020 you're out of luck on. Typical Commodore.

subject: Fonts? Phooey!
q: FF won't accept my proportional font with the IBM extended character set on the Amiga, and I don't have SETFONT. How can I get it to work?
a: FF is wrong about it. Load the font into FED, make sure it's fixed width, save it again without bothering to rename, then run FixFonts on it. FF worked like a charm after that. Tedious, but it works.

subject: SetRGB4CM() from AmigaBasic??
q: From AmigaBasic, calling SetRGB4CM() gives 'illegal function call'. What is Basic telling me?
a: Don't DECLARE FUNCTION it, since it returns no value. Use CALL SetRGB4CM&(sColorMap&,n,r,g,b). But it only sets the ColorMap and doesn't remake the display, so you probably want LoadRGB4(). See LoadACBM on the Extras disk.

subject: Handshake w/ dMouse problems :^(
q: Handshake 2.8a with DMouse 1.1, the lineart handler and ConMan gurus when the screen blanks during a Kermit download and I move the mouse. Anyone seen this, and what can I do?
a: Yes, it's a known clash. DMouse seems to interfere with the background task Handshake runs for the blinking cursor. Quit dmouse and turn the monitor off by hand, or use dnet. Or use another terminal program with its own screen blanker, like Mach II.

subject: Debugger for Benchmark Modula-2
q: Has Avante-Guard released the source level debugger mentioned in the Benchmark Modula-2 manual? Has anyone used another Amiga debugger with Benchmark M2 programs?
a: Not as of three months ago, when I bought it. I was told LDebug is a source level debugger that works with Benchmark, though I haven't tried it. Vaporware again, sigh.

subject: Need help, Balance of Power run from RAM?
q: Has anyone modified Balance of Power to run from RAM? It's unbearably slow from overlays, the game refuses to run with FAST memory, and my old fixhunk said it can't treat overlay files. Is there a newer version?
a: FixHunk 2.0 is out and it does work with BOP. I know it's on Plink, and maybe on Fred Fish's latest disks. Next time check for a newer version before whining about the old one.

subject: VLT TeX Docs Out anywhere?ga
q: Have the VLT docs been released in TeX format? The manual that ships with VLT is just okay, and I hear the TeX version is better written.
a: Can't help with TeX; nobody here has a TeX or ASCII copy. The real manual is SLAC-370, 114 pages, and you order a printed copy from the National Technical Information Service in Springfield, Virginia. Sigh, paper, how quaint.

subject: Using RF Modulator
q: How can I run an Amiga RF modulator to a TV and still use Digi-View at the same time? A Y-cable seems too weak to drive both.
a: First, your composite setup is probably broken, since RF loses detail. Try a simple two-position video selector switch with phono jacks, or a cheap external modulator from Radio Shack. A monochrome composite monitor, around $100, might be better. Or ask Newtek for a new manual.

subject: attaching a CLI to a window.
q: How do I attach a CLI to a custom window on the Amiga? I can attach a console device by passing the window to console.device in OpenDevice, but I want a CLI.
a: Make a FileHandle that uses that console.device unit, then pass it as the 2nd and 3rd args to Execute(). Fish disk 38 has a Window example that does this; run something like NewCLI with the handle. RTFM, the DOS manual covers it.

subject: Clipping within a window.
q: How do I clip text or graphics output to within the borders of a simplerefresh window? I know SuperBitMap with GZZ works but that's overkill for text only. How do I set up my own clipping rectangle in a window?
a: Use GZZ. You don't need a superbitmap just to clip inside the window borders. If you want arbitrary clipping rectangles, make a layer with layers.library; the ROM Kernel manual has an example. Read the manual, it's all in there.

subject: Recovering files
q: How do I recover an unclosed file on AmigaDOS? My raytrace crashed at 94.7 percent and DiskX has never recovered anything for me.
a: Never looked at it closely, but try DiskSalv 1.4x. Run DiskSalv DXX: RAM: FILE FileXX. It scans the device and saves only files matching that name. It certainly won't hurt to try. Maybe save your work more often.

subject: Assemnbly help needed
q: How do I use WindowToBack and WindowToFront in assembly on the Amiga? A0 needs a name for the window, but what do I point at for another program's active window?
a: No names involved; it's the window pointer, same as OpenWindow returns. Open a window of your own, follow the next and previous pointers in the screen's window list (LockIBase first, you *must*), then call WindowToBack. It's rude to do to other people's windows, mind you.

subject: GenLock info
q: How does a genlock work on the Amiga, and what does my program have to do to sync with it?
a: Nothing. Kickstart 1.2 checks for the genlock at boot, flips the direction of some video signals and sets a bit in a base structure. Your program needn't do a thing, though you can arrange your palette so it stays usable when color 0 is external video. Common misconception, sigh.

subject: Commercial compiler comparisons...
q: How good is Lattice's C++ compared to their normal C compiler, and is Manx better than Lattice or vice versa on the Amiga?
a: Not much difference between Manx and Lattice overall, though Lattice has had better service. Lattice's C++ is an AT&T front end that spits out C for another compiler, so the development cycle is slow. Nobody I know uses it.

subject: Lattice 5.05 say 5.04
q: I applied the Lattice 5.05 patch to 5.04 with no errors, but the compiler still says version 5.04. Is that my problem or Lattice's?
a: Normal. The lc driver still says 5.04 after the patch, while lc1 and lc2 should say 5.05. If those still say 5.04, you've got the broken 5.04 disk, the patches to lc1, lc2 and lc1b failed, and nothing got patched. Check before whining.

subject: A2000 + Janus + copy-write problems??
q: I can't get certain Electronic Arts copy-protected disks like Arcticfox and Archon to boot on my A2000 with the Janus bridgeboard. Is the Janus board the problem?
a: Probably not Janus. Those programs don't work with extra memory or Kickstart 1.2, which is EA's problem. Try noFASTmem to disable the extra memory temporarily, or fixhunk for some programs. The real fix is developers doing it right in the first place.

subject: arc, Computer Language magazine
q: I can't unpack clfeb90.arc on my Amiga because the newest ARC I can find says I need a newer version. What's wrong and what do I use?
a: The file was made with PKXARC, which uses Squashing, and no Amiga version of ARC supports that. Get PKAX from PKWARE for the Amiga; it extracts these files, and much faster than ARC 0.23. Learn your archivers.

subject: Help, need pointer to PasTex3.0
q: I couldn't find the TeX 3.0 package for the Amiga (PasTeX) via ftp at abcfd01.larc.nasa.gov. Where can I get it?
a: Typo in the original post, nothing more. The server is absfd20.larc.nasa.gov, not abcfd01. Check the hostname before you go bothering the whole net, sigh.

subject: Problem with Amiga Word Perfect
q: I have WordPerfect 4.1 for the Amiga, which only reads IBM 4.2 files. Is there a conversion program to import IBM WordPerfect 5.1 files?
a: No converter needed. IBM WP 5.1 can export to 4.2 format. It works fine unless you use the odd features 4.2 has and 4.1 doesn't. Honestly, read your manual.

subject: Editor for terminals
q: I have a terminal (HP2628A) connected to my A500. Is there an editor, maybe public domain, that supports it?
a: Stevie, an Amiga port of vi. Public domain or shareware, I think. vi sounds hard, but you get fast once you stop whining. Should do the trick.

subject: Mac Emulation.
q: I heard someone can run Mac system 6.0.3 on the A-Max emulator on an Amiga. How do I install it?
a: Just copy a system disk from a Mac and boot it. It worked as 6.0.3 for me. Microsoft Works' word processor locks up on menus, and ReadySoft's file export utility won't recognize files going Mac to Amiga. No magic involved.

subject: Simple Example Desired
q: I need to get what I type at the keyboard into a window on my own screen on the Amiga. Should I use console.device or the Text() command?
a: Text() only draws text, so using it for input is deep trouble. Console.device works but is complex. Easiest is requesting VANILLAKEY IDCMP messages when you open the window; when Message->Class is VANILLAKEY, Message->Code holds the key. Not hard.

subject: ethernet, slip etc
q: I want to connect an Amiga to a campus Ethernet. What cards, SLIP or TCP/IP software are available, and what do they cost?
a: Commodore's A2065 Ethernet card works in 2000s, 2500s and 3000s, with thick and thin connectors, for about $349 list. The TCP/IP package is $149, in beta, with the usual apps plus an NFS client. KA9Q uses SLIP. Read the announcements.

subject: how to port programs which use curses/termcap?
q: I want to port the spreadsheet sc to the Amiga, but it uses curses and termcap. Should I port a curses clone or rip the curses out and hard-code it for the Amiga?
a: Write your own curses library with just the functions you need. Keep a virtual map of what you think the screen looks like and update what changed. Optimizing it can wait, since nobody cares on a dedicated machine. It isn't hard.

subject: Scroll Bars in SuperBitMaps
q: I'm adding proportional gadget scroll bars to a SuperBitMap window on the Amiga and get Gurus. What am I doing wrong?
a: You need to provide an uninitialised Image structure for each scrollbar gadget. Why it can't allocate one itself, who knows. One of the great mysteries of the modern world. Maybe 1.4 will be less dumb about it.

subject: VT Emulations for A2000
q: I'm looking for an Amiga 2000 terminal program that uses the new keyboard fully for VT100 emulation and also handles IBM-style ANSI color and an IBM-style font. Any suggestions?
a: A PD program called COMM handles the ANSI color commands. The next A-Talk, called A-Talk III, covers the VT100 keypad, IBM ANSI.SYS and an IBM graphics font. When it ships? Ask OXXI. Vaporware again, what a surprise.

subject: 11 point fonts & VLT
q: I'm trying to get a custom 11-point font to work with VLT. The docs say to run ff with the -1 switch to replace topaz 11, but VLT still comes up with topaz 11. How do I replace the 11-point font?
a: Edit the topaz 11 file directly with FED. Then the catch: running almost any application before VLT, or re-invoking VLT, makes it substitute topaz 8. So reboot and run a startup script with ff -1 and then run vlt. Works most of the time; it's buggy software.

subject: RS-232 & MIDI Interface
q: I'm trying to read MIDI data from my keyboard through the Amiga serial port, but 9600 and 19200 baud give different garbage. How should I set the RS-232 to get the right data?
a: MIDI runs at exactly one rate, 31250 baud, so set the serial port to that. The interface doesn't buffer anything, it just isolates the computer from the instruments. It's also not electrically RS-232, so you need a MIDI adapter. Basic homework.

subject: CMI board, and IBM monitor woes
q: I'm using QRT for ray tracing on my Amiga and thinking of buying the CMI board with the math processor. Can anyone guess how much of a speedup I'll get?
a: Depends on whether QRT is compiled to use IEEE functions so the 68881 can actually cruise. If it is, expect roughly an 80% speedup in the preliminary tests on the accelerator at 14MHz. Don't buy the thing before checking how your binary was built.

subject: a500 around the world
q: If I run a 60Hz A500 on 220V/50Hz power in Israel, will the display flicker get worse? And is PAL versus NTSC relevant for the A500 RGB output, or only for the composite adapter?
a: Flicker depends on the machine's video rate, not the power frequency. RGB is RGB. PAL and NTSC only matter for the A510 composite adapter, and the RGB difference is just 50Hz versus 60Hz refresh. A European machine gives more scan lines. Basic stuff.

subject: AmigaOS is real-time?
q: Is AmigaOS truly a real-time OS? Does it guarantee system calls finish within a defined amount of time?
a: No. Real-time means bounded response to real-world events, and Exec disables interrupts for arbitrarily long periods, for example while Enqueueing a task on the ready list. It's responsive, thanks to lean design and no virtual memory, but not real-time. Stop calling it that.

subject: Psound 3.0 (was Re: PSound_3.0 hates Sonix 2.0 (and vice versa)
q: Is Psound 3.0 freeware like version 1.0 was, and is there any way for an A1000 owner to get the upgrade?
a: Perfect Sound 3.0 is NOT public domain. It's now a commercial product, so stop asking for it on the binaries group. Contact Sunrize Industries, Perfect Sound's distributor, if you want it.

subject: SID 1.06 ??IS it
q: Is SID 1.06 the latest version for the Amiga? If there is a newer one, where can I get it?
a: As far as anyone knows, 1.06 is the latest. Send the author $25 and he'll mail you v2.00 once he finishes it, plus BBS access. Sigh, and pay the man, shareware doesn't write itself.

subject: Can I get Zoo for VMS?
q: Is Zoo available for VMS? I know it exists for Unix.
a: Yes, it exists for VMS. The Zoo source distribution has instructions for compiling it. Note it only supports Stream_LF files, a problem only on old VMS before V4.4. Go find an FTP site.

subject: Amiga & Mathematica
q: Is a version of Mathematica produced or planned for the Amiga?
a: At a demo last fall, when asked, they said yes. The kernel is the same everywhere, but porting the graphical interface will take time. Expect to need a couple more megs and a hard drive, so don't hold your breath.

subject: MyMenu with IconX scripts?
q: Is it possible to get MyMenu to run IconX scripts? It says "Can't open info file" when I try.
