a: Sure, just treat the IconX script as a CLI startup script in the MyMenu command, using CLI NewCLI "CON:0/0/0/0/" from the script. NewShell works too but won't allow the tiny window size. Honestly, read the MyMenu docs.

subject: Agnus Woes
q: Is it possible to put a Fat Agnus in an Amiga 1000? My dealer said it couldn't be done. Does Commodore plan a fat Agnus upgrade for 1000 owners, or is it a hardware constraint?
a: Your dealer was wrong. Somebody has done it and posted instructions on BIX. Commodore, of course, did nothing for 1000 owners. Go read BIX instead of asking the dealer.

subject: Mac Fonts-->Amiga?
q: Is it possible to use Macintosh fonts on an Amiga, and is there a program that does the dirty work of converting them?
a: Somebody wrote a converter, and the fonts work in Notepad and DPaint. But they fail elsewhere: the space character vanishes in SetFont and Vizawrite, and FED doesn't see them as fonts. It's half-baked, and the author moved on. Don't hold your breath.

subject: ATalkIII and Diga! upgrade
q: Is the ATalkIII upgrade price $34.95 or $39.95, and does it differ if I'm upgrading from Diga! versus another comm program?
a: OXXI says $34.95 for A-Talk and A-Talk Plus owners, and $39.95 for users of other comm programs like Diga!, Online! or Dr. Term. So you pay the $39.95. Sigh. Call OXXI directly next time instead of asking the net.

subject: Limit on ROM size
q: Is the Amiga, other than the 1000, limited to 256K ROMs? How easy is it to install larger ROMs?
a: A500s and A2000s take a pin-compatible 512K ROM. Nobody ships one mainly because A1000 owners would suffer. Beyond 512K you run out of address lines and address space, so that's the limit.

subject: IMGScan...
q: Is the Sunrize IMGScan scanner for the Amiga any good? Is it worth the $100?
a: No. After many hours, nobody could get an image anywhere near the quality of the demo picture. An Amiga magazine calls the image quality mediocre, color scans poorly, and it is slow. Save your money; the demo was marketing.

subject: DeciGel (was Re: UNIX on the Amiga)
q: Is there a DeciGel-like program for the Amiga that traps and ignores divide-by-zero errors? They're the most annoying GURUs.
a: Get GOMF. Version 1.0 is PD and is on every BBS. Version 2.0 is commercial, $39.95 from HyperTek. Version 1.0 has worked fine for me. Honestly, this should be easy to find.

subject: GIF format
q: Is there a GIF reader or a GIF to IFF converter for the Amiga? I'd like to put some digitized Star Trek pictures on my A1000's screen.
a: Yes, one exists. There's a package with a reader/displayer and a GIF-to-IFF converter, plus a bit of documentation and two sample pictures. It's been on the BBSes and GEnie for ages, something like GIF.ARC. Go look before asking again, sigh.

subject: Swaping windows
q: Is there a PD program that lets a key combo send a Workbench window to the back or front, so I don't have to take my hands off the keys?
a: Not PD, but Commodities Exchange by Jim Mackraz does this, and so does the Funkeys program in MicroSmiths' Fast Fonts package, which can also start a CLI with one keystroke. Both are highly recommended, so quit pestering people about docs.

subject: 1000 SCSI
q: Is there a SCSI interface for the Amiga 1000 that supports SCSI direct commands, and who makes it?
a: Use an A590 on the A1000, just plug it in back to front. Not an official CBM statement, it just happens to work. CBM makes the A590. Honestly, not rocket science.

subject: Amiga Hard Drives
q: Is there a bug in the first release of the Microbotics HardCard when paired with a Quantum 40 drive in an A2000, and has it been fixed?
a: Yes, it came from unclear hardware docs for the A2000 and A2620, and it's fixed. The fix is a PAL socket mod with a wire between pins 15 and 11. Microbotics supplies a modified socket, and new boards ship with the mod. Be VERY careful.

subject: Dual Mac/Amidos drive for AMAX use.
q: Is there a drive that works as both an Amiga drive and a Mac drive for AMAX use on a 500? Where can I get one and for how much?
a: One was advertised, but the fine print says it only runs AmigaDOS stuff with extra software, so the Amiga side is good for maybe half of what you'd want. If you find one that doesn't need that, tell everyone. Read the fine print.

subject: Mice
q: Is there a good optical mouse that is compatible with the Amiga mouse?
a: Amiga mice are fairly generic. Any mouse that gives X and Y quadrature signals and contact closures for the buttons should work, though you may have to make an adapter cable or plug yourself. Sigh, read the signals before you buy.

subject: Sculpt 4D Jr
q: Is there a major feature difference between Sculpt 4D Jr and the full Sculpt 4D, given the big price gap? What else is out there for modelling and animation on the Amiga?
a: As far as I know, Jr is basically a 3D modelling program and doesn't do ray tracing. Byte by Byte also has a Sculpt 3D upgrade coming RSN, so you might wait. Know what you're buying before you hand over money, kid.

subject: Public Domain Pascal Compiler?
q: Is there a public domain Pascal compiler for the Amiga?
a: Try PCQ Pascal. Check the ftp site abcfd20, 128.155.23.64, in incoming/amiga/PCQ. I don't remember if it's PD or shareware, but it's comprehensive and painless. Next time look before asking.

subject: ROM based 68000 cross developement
q: Is there a way to cross-develop for a ROM-based 68000 on an Amiga, with a cross compiler, assembler and linker?
a: Just use the standard Amiga C compilers, 68000 assemblers and BLINK, then convert the executable to Motorola S format with absolute addresses. You must write your own printf and scanf, can't initialize changeable variables in ROM, and statics aren't zeroed. Live with it.

subject: AMIGA ==> IBM ?
q: Is there a way to transfer Amiga hi-res pictures from DPaint III and Photon Paint II to an IBM and display them there? Any PD or commercial programs?
a: A commercial program called D2D copies Amiga files to an IBM 3.5 inch disk. Reduce IFF pictures to 16 colors with an IBM palette in DigiView first. For HAM pictures, use HAM2IFF to convert to IFF. Nobody knows the ftp site. Figure it out.

subject: Terminal Emulator in Window
q: Is there an Amiga terminal emulator that runs in a resizable Workbench window, so I can dial a mainframe in one window and edit in another?
a: A-Talk III works fine with Workbench windows. It recomputes columns and rows on every resize, so under UNIX you can write a termcap or terminfo for a small window size and run emacs in it.

subject: IEEE-488
q: Is there an IEEE-488 interface available for the Amiga? How much, and where from?
a: ASDG is showing an IEEE-488 module for its Twin-X iSBX host adapter at AmiExpo in Chicago. The module and driver are done and developer units are shipping. Final pricing isn't set yet. Ask them, and spare us the vapor.

subject: Object-oriented drawing IFF spec? (and other q's)
q: Is there an IFF format for object-oriented drawings on the Amiga? The registry in the 1.3 Autodocs and Includes doesn't list one.
a: Yes, DR2D, a new IFF FORM for 2D object-oriented drawings. The spec should be in the Nov/Dec 1990 Amiga Mail, and several commercial products are supposed to support it soon. Of course the old registry doesn't list it, it's old. Read the newer docs.

subject: Simulation of analog computer
q: Is there an analog computer emulator for the Amiga? I have a set of linear differential equations I want to see graphically. If none exists, is there a cheap real analog computer I can buy?
a: Never heard of an analog computer simulator for the Amiga. Doug's Math Aquarium will plot differential equations, though it isn't PD. As for a real analog computer, just wire one up from op-amps. Grab a cookbook and a bunch of 741's. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: HD Backup info wanted
q: Is there any hard disk backup software for the Amiga that preserves file dates, so make doesn't recompile everything? PD or commercial is fine.
a: There's an alpha port of the Unix bru (Backup and Restore Utility) on a recent disk. It's quick and dirty, and the alpha does not preserve dates. The beta, using the new 1.2 facilities, is due within a week or so. Not PD, but freely redistributable.

subject: Fish Contents On-Line Index
q: Is there interest in an on-line every-word index to the Fish disk contents files, or does one already exist?
a: One exists, a program called Aquarium. It started on one of Fred's disks, and the copy on abcfd20 is updated to Fish 360. Go ftp it before you reinvent the wheel, grumble.

subject: Old Lattice Poblem.
q: Linking with old Lattice C 1.2 from Commodore, I get undefined symbols like memcpy, memset and strupr from lc.lib when I use printf. What's wrong?
a: Those routines are supposed to be in lc.lib, so your library is probably trashed. Try another copy and recheck your Blink command. That version had no librarian, so verifying it is hard. It's ancient; Commodore should be ashamed of still selling it.

subject: undelete
q: My Amiga file got deleted and I have nothing to undelete it. Where can I get something to undelete lost files?
a: FixDisk. Version 1.2 is on Fish disk 403. It undeletes files, checks the directory structure, and repairs bad disks. Sigh, grab it before you lose the rest of your scripts, and make backups next time.

subject: Hard Drive Whine and Dust?
q: My SCSI hard drive has started making a faint high-pitched whine, even when idle. What's causing it?
a: Probably a small metal strap on the bottom of the drive that rests against the spindle to bleed off static. It squeals as the spindle rotates, and it's harmless though annoying. Clean the contact point and hold the strap snug with scotch tape.

subject: 2090A Question
q: My minimal Amiga boot disk with a 2090A hard drive keeps asking me to insert dh2:, and BindDrivers doesn't seem to mount it. What else is needed?
a: BindDrivers needs icon.library. Put it in the Libs drawer, which you left empty. Basic stuff, you'd have seen it if you'd checked what it opens.

subject: A2000->B2000 upgrade?
q: My rev 4.0 A2000 has worse video than an A500. Will Commodore upgrade it to a rev 4.2, or is something else wrong?
a: Probably just a wrong-type ferrite bead on the video connector. Have a tech replace the beads on R, G and B with a plain wire jumper, FCC notwithstanding. Also check if you have a German A2000 with the single 28-pin connector, because then all bets are off.

subject: NoClick3.5 problems
q: NoClick 3.5 gives a Guru error 4 on my A1000 with a 68010. Anyone else have problems?
a: Blame a stupid manual that claimed the 68010 and 68020 share the same stack frame. They don't. If you have a 68010, go back to NoClick 3.3 or 3.4 until the author puts out 3.6.

subject: ARP 1.3 Bug or Feature?
q: On Amiga with ARP 1.3, 'list #? lformat "bar %s" | execute' works from execute and run but fails under arun. Is that a bug or am I misusing the pipe?
a: Not a bug. The pipe syntax is parsed by the ARP Shell, which gets the command line via Execute and Run but not via Arun. It wouldn't work from a standard AmigaDOS CLI or CBM 1.3 Shell either.

subject: DF1: format problems.
q: On my Amiga, disks formatted in the external drive DF1: can't be read in DF0: and vice versa, though already formatted disks work in both. Is something inside the Amiga dying?
a: Not likely the Amiga, which makes no distinction between formatting and normal writing. It smells like mechanical misalignment, just enough that fringes of old data let the other drive read them but not a clean new disk. Pretty weird, but check the drive.

subject: Problems with trig functions and SDB
q: On the Amiga, asin and acos return garbage, cotan and atan2 are undefined, and SDB prints garbage for floats and doubles. What's the fix?
a: Use one of the mt.libs, since they contain the transcendental functions. SDB wants IEEE format, so compile with cc +fi and link with -lma. Read the manual, it's not hard.

subject: SETCPU with the AT bridgeboard
q: SetCPU 1.4 with FASTROM gives "Software error - task held" requesters when an AT or XT bridgeboard is installed. Any ideas?
a: It's some kind of protection violation, and the bridge card people are still looking into it. The fix is SetCPU V1.5, which installs a handler for level 2 exceptions so the bridge software gurus go away. Wait for it to be posted.

subject: Zorro III (Re: Wishlist for A3000)
q: Since NuBus slots are at fixed addresses, is it technically a bus?
a: Sure. It's a geographically addressed bus, and that makes far more sense with a 4 gigabyte address space than a 16 megabyte one. For the smaller space, Amiga Autoconfig is the best way I've seen to configure cards.

subject: BKDC *.WRP files
q: Some badge killer demo contest entries come with a .WRP file and a program called warp. What am I supposed to do with them?
a: Warp unpacks the .WRP files onto whole diskettes. Run something like "warp write ram:sentinel1.wrp" and it prompts you for a disk in df0:. Run warp with no arguments for a synopsis. Try that before asking.

subject: Compress
q: The Amiga compress/uncompress from Purdue says "file not in compressed format" on the Purdue archive files. Is there a version that works?
a: The Purdue version only handles 13-bit compression, and the archives use 15-bit. Use binary mode in ftp, obviously. A newer compress that allocates memory dynamically and reads a default bit count from an environment variable is coming real soon now. Patience, kid.

subject: graph.zuu
q: The Amiga program graph.zoo says it can't open graph and that digits.font is missing. Where can I find that font?
a: Not on the normal distribution disks. Use FED from the extras disk to save topaz.font out as digits.font, or NewZap the binary and replace the string digits.font with topaz.font plus a NULL. The binary release looks incomplete. Sloppy packaging.

subject: ST has Borland Turbo C, why not Amiga?
q: The Atari ST has Borland Turbo C, so why doesn't the Amiga?
a: It's not really Borland's work. A small European company wrote a very good Turbo C clone and Borland agreed to market it where the ST sells better. So quit writing to Borland's president.

subject: newtek1.wrp too large
q: The newtek1.wrp demo is too large for my Amiga floppies; one warped file is 1704 blocks and won't fit even on an empty disk. How can I get this demo?
a: Quit whining, it got rewarped with LHWARP, which compresses much better than old WARP. The new pieces are small enough for a disk and sit on xanth.cs.odu.edu by anonymous ftp in /amiga/demos/newtek-1/. You'll need the newer LHWARP 1.02 to unpack them.

subject: VT100 question
q: Using VT100 v2.3 on an Amiga to a Sun, the backspace key just shows control-H. How do I get the Sun to see it as a backspace, and delete as forward delete?
a: Two ways. Issue the right stty on the Sun, man stty. Or upgrade to a newer VT100 and put SWAP ON in vt100.init, or use the SWAP item in the Utilities menu. It swaps BS and DEL. RTFM.

subject: 2.0 Weirdness - WBPattern
q: WBPattern doesn't work on my A3000 under 2.0, and I can't find the FKey Commodity. Any ideas?
a: Check you haven't mangled your startup-sequence, and that ENV: is still assigned to RAM:Env. As for FKey, it simply isn't part of the 2.00 and 2.01 releases. The manual pictures it anyway, naturally.

subject: arp bindings
q: Was part 4 of the ARP 1.1 bindings ever released? We missed it.
a: No luck here either, we missed it too. When we get all four parts we'll make them available by anonymous FTP from uunet. Don't hold your breath.

subject: Fish Disk database (Going crazy!)
q: Wasn't there a program in a recent Fred Fish disk that was a database of the whole Fish collection?
a: No, you're not crazy. It's called Aquarium, with a decent Intuition interface. I believe it's on Fish disk 301 and covers disks 1 through 300. Check the disk before you bother the net.

subject: ARexx question
q: What exactly is the point of having an ARexx port in a program? What could I use it for?
a: Two things, and it's not hard. You get a nearly full macro language for free, with loops, conditionals and recursion, which most micro apps lack. And you can glue together whatever programs you like, say your own choice of editor with AmigaTeX, instead of being stuck with the vendor's pick.

subject: PAL grounding
q: What happens if you add a second SOTS box, like a C Ltd. SCSI interface alongside a StarBoard II on an A1000, and don't ground the PALs? What problems should I watch for?
a: Expect it to refuse to boot, or get as far as asking for Kickstart and then fail to read it. Everyone told me to buy the J&K PAL upgrade from C Ltd. for two boxes. Cheap hardware, cheap grief.

subject: A2000 and CPU slot
q: What happens to the A2000's 68000 when a 68020 board goes into the CPU slot? Does the 68020 run everything, or does the 68000 act as an I/O processor?
a: Nobody here answered the hardware question, only the name. Someone voted for AMIX over AMIUNX, since it's easier to say and spell. Sigh. Read the board's documentation instead of speculating about I/O hounds.

subject: A few more dumb questions....
q: What is UUencoding and when do you need it? Can I download a .zoo file by FTP and just unzoo and run it, and do I need to do anything to a ZOO or ARC file before uploading?
a: Uuencoding turns eight-bit binary files into seven-bit text. It dates from when email couldn't carry eight-bit characters, and many newsfeeds still need it because news was meant for readable stuff. Sigh, history lesson over.

subject: FTP & Telnet
q: What is required to run FTP and Telnet on the Amiga? Are they available, and if not, what needs to be done in programming or hardware?
a: You need at least an ethernet connection to the host. After that it's just a matter of hacking the software to run under AmigaOS. Nobody's going to hand it to you on a plate.

subject: high-speed file transfer
q: What's a good method for high-speed binary file transfer between an Amiga and a Sun over a pair of USR Courier HST modems at 9600? Kermit's error checking clogs the link.
a: Standard Kermit is a pig, so stop using it. Use ZMODEM, which is easily 4x faster, and sources exist for both Amiga and UNIX. If your modem link does error correction, YMODEM-G should be faster still. This comes up constantly.

subject: How to read the keyboard?
q: What's the best Intuition-friendly way on the Amiga to tell whether a key such as z is currently held down? I'm using Modula-2, but C or assembler pointers are fine.
a: Not sure it's the best way, but open keyboard.device and send it a message. You get back a bit pattern showing exactly which keys are down. The RKM Libraries and Devices volume has a chapter on it. Read it.

subject: Random Number Generation
q: What's the best way to generate random numbers on the Amiga? My public domain C compiler has no library call for it.
a: Get the book Numerical Recipes. It covers the issues and the algorithms and even gives code, and it's a great book. Stop hunting for a library call and learn how generators actually work.

subject: Min. Amiga system for Unix
q: What's the minimum Amiga configuration to run AmigaUnix? Will a 2000 do, or do you need a 3000?
a: It's been said on the net before. You need an MMU, but a 2000 will do if you put a '030 in it. The least is basically an A2500. Read the group before asking.

subject: Leaving Computer On
q: What's the net's wisdom on leaving a micro like an Amiga 1000 turned on all the time versus switching it off? Does power cycling do more damage than continuous running, and what about hard drives?
a: Power-on shock is constant per cycle while wear grows with time, so the break-even is a few days; just leave it on. Turn hard disk machines off overnight. Turn the monitor video off, and ventilate properly, unless you like burned-in phosphor.

subject: AT bridge card
q: When will an AT bridge card be available for the Amiga 2000?
a: No date, but fully functional prototypes were shown at BCS and Comdex. Since the A2000 and XT Bridgeboard only just began shipping, expect at least a three month delay. It will have the high density 1.2 Mb floppy that still reads 360K. Be patient.

subject: Purchasing Amiga Chips
q: Where can I buy Commodore Amiga custom chips, in particular the 8520 I/O and timer chip? My local dealer refuses to help.
a: Go right to the source and order direct from CBM in Westchester. One buyer got an 8520 for around $23 including shipping in under 14 days. And dump any dealer who won't help, they understand economics.

subject: Where are IFF2Ps and DiskChecker?
q: Where can I find IFF2Ps (the color IFF to PostScript converter) and DiskChecker for the Amiga via FTP? I lost mine in a disk crash.
a: Anything posted to comp.sources.amiga or comp.binaries.amiga is archived on xanth.cs.odu.edu. Look under /usenet/comp.sources.amiga/volume89: iff/iff2ps20.1.Z and dos/fs/diskchecker.1.Z. A quick grep would have found that, and next time make backups.

subject: Nethack Amiga,where can I get it?
q: Where can I get Nethack 3.0 for the Amiga? I have the source but not the patience to compile it.
a: Don't bother with the current patch levels. Compiling takes Manx 3.6, a custom make util and lots of fixes, and pl6 is buggy anyway. Wait for patch level 7, which should compile cleanly with stock Lattice 5.04 or Manx 5.0. Sigh, patience.

subject: Where is the Workbench?
q: Where exactly is the Workbench on an Amiga? Is it one file, part of loadwb, or a collection of files, and where does the version number come from?
a: The version number comes from the file version.library in the libs: directory. To really know what you have, check file sizes and checksums. I've never found a list of correct checksums, though. Typical Commodore.

subject: PopCLI (and regular CLI) Question
q: Why can't I bring up a CLI window from the Workbench icon or PopCLI without the Workbench disk inserted, even with NewCLI and CLI in VD0:?
a: Workbench CLI uses the AmigaDOS Execute() call, which needs the RUN command and only loads it as C:RUN. Whatever directory C: is assigned to must contain RUN, or it won't work. Basic stuff.

subject: asdg rrd, no vd1?
q: Why can't I set up a second recoverable ram disk, vd1:, with the ASDG RRD? Mount works but touching vd1: gives a not a dos disk error.
a: The code allows no more than one vapordisk per machine. VD0: can be up to 8 megabytes, and ram has no head movement latency, so there was no need for more. Also the semi-fast ram hack won't work, since the code tests against 0x200000 to split fast and chip ram.

subject: vlt 4.834 question
q: Why do all my old VLT scripts fail in the new VLT 4.8 release? The command send "ATDP5447787*R" no longer dials my modem.
a: Script handling was fixed in the new VLT, since it was a hodge-podge from pre-history. The syntax changed, so all your scripts must be rewritten. Painful, but it shouldn't change again soon. Welcome to progress.

subject: whats the story with st-506 drives on the 3000
q: Why does BindDrivers hang when I use my A2090 with ST-506 drives in an Amiga 3000, and how can I fix it?
a: The A2090 driver never expected Fast memory it can't DMA into at boot time. Run the NoFastMem program before mounting the A2090 so it gets its buffers in Chip RAM. A revised driver would be the real fix, but nobody supplies one. Typical.

subject: Self-repairing SCSI disks!
q: Why does my Amiga SCSI hard disk seem to repair itself after a crash, taking minutes to hours on reboot? What causes it, what is it doing, can it cause trouble later, and does 1.3 change it?
a: That's the AmigaDOS disk validator, not magic. The disk was left inconsistent when the system went down, so it walks every file and directory and works out which blocks are free. Usually only the file being written is lost. The fast file system makes it much faster.

subject: Atalk III & Kermit
q: Why does the A-Talk III transfer window report a Kermit file size about 50% bigger than the actual file?
a: The built-in Kermit counts the bytes transferred including encoding, so you get more than the file size. Get the XPR Kermit that ships with release 1.3 and up; it's more powerful and shows the right size. They won't bother fixing the built-in one. Upgrade, already.

subject: Zoo
q: Why does zoo crash and guru my Amiga when I unpack or list zoo files from my hard drive, though it works on floppy, rad:, ram: and vd0:? I'm using Supra 5.01a software with FFS mounted on both partitions.
a: Sounds like you have a pre-release 1.3 FFS, which had a bug that showed up beautifully under ZOO. Developers were told about it in AmigaMail. It might also just be that your stack isn't set large enough.

subject: Disney Animation Studio
q: Why is a professional package like Disney's Animation Studio copy protected, and why is the sound-playing animation player "flicker" not freely redistributable?
a: Disney absolutely positively demanded the copy protection, over objections from the developers. Flicker isn't freely distributable because of some weirdness in the licensing agreement for the Sonix music drivers. Blame the suits, not the programmers.

subject: Male parallel port?
q: Why would a brand new Amiga 2500/030 come with a male DB-25 for both the parallel and serial ports?
a: It shouldn't. Sounds confused for sure, so have your service center return the motherboard for one that isn't screwed up. Somebody wasn't paying attention on the assembly line.

subject: MSH disk errors & text conversion...
q: With MSH on the Amiga, an AmigaDOS ASCII file comes out on MS-DOS with its CRs changed to LFs. Is there a quickie program to fix that?
a: Sigh, the old end-of-line problem. The Amiga uses LF while MS-DOS wants CR+LF. You need utilities to add and strip CRs; Matt Dillon's addcr and remcr are on Fish 168/169, one disk has the executables.

subject: REZ & Shell
q: With REZ 0.3 and shell 2.07M, I do "rez run" and then run a command, and it executes but leaves me in a new CLI. Why does that happen?
a: Don't rez run at all. Just keep run in a directory like vdk:c with c: assigned to it. You'll still type endcli to get the shell back, which is the same annoyance. Or make ARP's arun resident, which leaves you in the shell. Nobody knows why run does this.

subject: Bridgeboard, CrossDOS & virtual drives...frustration
q: With a Bridgeboard and CrossDOS, I can copy programs with AREAD but they are unreadable on the IBM side. What's the secret?
a: Use the /B switch on AREAD and AWRITE. Without it they transfer as ASCII text, which is useless for programs. Binary files need /B. CBM forgot to tell anyone, naturally.

subject: Whither Zorro?
q: With the A2000 coming out with its own expansion bus, what happens to Zorro? Will third-party boards be obsolete and will we have to wait months for compatible products?
a: Sigh, read the specs. A2000 slots are electrically Zorro, so no six-month wait. Existing boards, such as all the ASDG products, go on sale the same day the A2000 does.

subject: PasTeX 240dpi fonts anywhere ?
q: Does anyone have the 240dpi fonts for PasTeX? I don't want to generate them with MetaFont on a stock Amiga 500.
a: Get the gf fonts, which come in many resolutions, by anonymous ftp from labrea.stanford.edu. Run them through gftopk, which should come with PasTeX, to make the pk format it uses. Works very well. Honestly, this is what ftp is for.

subject: Decent Looking Output (Excellence/Postscript)
q: How do I get decent PostScript output from Excellence? The text comes out too wide even after resizing fonts to 11 point.
a: RTFM. Set the page pitch to 15 in the page setup requester, as the manual addendum says, around pages 51 and 52. PostScript fonts look right after that, and you can fine-tune with the pitch. Did you even buy the thing?

subject: HP deskjet 500 printer drivers
q: I got an HP Deskjet 500 and the Amiga printer driver gives real blocky characters in ProWrite, Notepad and Deluxe Paint. Is there a better driver?
a: Those programs basically do screen dumps scaled up to the page, so every screen pixel becomes a big block. Turn on antialiasing and use density 3 or 4, or use software that renders at printer resolution. Or spend $40 on a proper driver like the one in DJ Helper.

subject: ProPage print bug fixed?
q: My ProPage 2.x doesn't print to a dot matrix printer, only PostScript. Has this print bug been fixed in the new version?
a: It's never been broken for me. Check you're picking Output/Dot Matrix and not Output/Postscript. Version 2.1 even prints landscape to dot matrix, and registered 2.0 owners were sent an upgrade. Try it off floppy to rule out your startup junk.

subject: Star NX-1000 Rainbow, Bold NLQ?
q: My Star NX-1000 Rainbow prints bold in draft mode from ProWrite 2.0 but not in NLQ with the EpsonX driver. Is it the printer, the driver, or ProWrite?
a: Check your manual. The NX-1000 simply does not do bold in NLQ mode, and no italics either. It does underline, which is small consolation. It isn't a bug, so quit blaming ProWrite.

subject: IBM Proprinter and Panasonic KX-P1124 drivers
q: Where can I find a driver for a Panasonic KX-P1124 printer on the Amiga?
a: Don't bother hunting FTP sites. Use the NEC-Pinwriter driver that comes with your Amiga. It works great. Read what's already in the box before you go begging the net.

subject: ZX Spectrum Emulator
q: Where can I find the ZX Spectrum emulator for the Amiga? Does it really exist, is it public domain, and where is it available?
a: It exists, it's PD, and it lives on ab20.larc.nasa.gov. A guy in Wellington, New Zealand wrote it. On a 2500 it runs about as fast as a real Spectrum. Getting software across is the hassle, naturally.

subject: A3000 CG fonts... where to get more?
q: Where can I get more CG scalable fonts for AmigaDOS 2.04 on the A3000, or how do I create them?
a: Any CG fonts that come with DTP programs like Pagestream and Pro Page work fine, and both companies sell font packs. Gold Disk also sells Compugraphic fonts, including the Outline Font Collection. Pay up; fonts aren't free.

subject: Pagestream2.0 with CG fonts printing Postscript
q: Why does PageStream 2.0 print Helvetica instead of my extra Compugraphic fonts like Palatino-style ones on a PostScript printer? Is there an alias file I need?
a: Read your manual, pages 1.28 to 1.33. CG fonts have different widths than their PostScript counterparts, and only the bundled CS fonts have PostScript equivalents. For a PostScript printer, get real Type 1 fonts or the PageStream Fonts Plus Pak.

subject: PD Matlab on fish disk 499
q: With PD Matlab from fish disk 499 on my Amiga, plot(x) asks if I've set my stack to 100000, and answering yes exits with error 3. How do I fix it?
a: Set the stack to 150000. That got it working on a 2.5 meg A1000. It opens two hi-res screens, so expect horrendous flicker. Read the docs.

subject: PerfectSound?
q: Approximately how many seconds could I digitize with PerfectSound on a 1 meg Amiga 500?
a: It's all down to sampling rate. At 20 KHz you burn 20K per second, so with roughly 800K free you get about 40 seconds. Halve the rate and you double the time, but you lose highs, and stereo halves it again. Basic arithmetic.

subject: Instruments...
q: I can't load soundtracker modules in Protracker and I need to rip samples out of modules or find a source of instruments. Any ideas?
a: Try MED. It has a pretty comprehensive suite of sample tools and will save samples as IFF or RAW. Go use it before asking the net again.

subject: Looking for...
q: I'm taking a music composition course and need some PD scoring software for the Amiga. Where can I find it?
a: Only freely distributable thing I've seen is the old Sonix demo, formerly MusiCraft, maybe on old AMICUS disks; try ux1.cso.uiuc.edu first. Honestly, mail-order DMCS is far better and cheap. Real composition wants Dr. T's Copyist, which costs real dollars. Free doesn't get you far.

subject: New Sound Board
q: What's the story with the new AD1012 and AD1016 that go with the Studio 16 from SunRize? The ad in AmigaWorld has no price listed. Any guesses?
a: Retail is roughly $400 to $500 for the AD1012, the 12 bit digitizer, and about $2000 for the AD1016, the 16 bit one. Sigh, ads that hide the price always mean it hurts.

subject: Token ring or apple talk
q: Are there token ring or AppleTalk cards for the Amiga?
a: I know of no Token Ring cards for the Amiga. DigiFeX sells an AppleTalk card, but its software only talks to printers or other Amigas, not Macs, so no shared hard disks. It also tends to crash when printing to a powered-off printer. What a surprise.

subject: A500 data overrun using a v.32bis/v.42bis modem?
q: Can a stock A500 take full advantage of a v.32bis/v.42bis modem, or is the extra expense over v.32 wasted?
a: Opinions vary. One says the A500 can't reliably handle a continuous stream above 9600 baud, so don't buy v.32bis for it. Another says 2.04 and fast RAM make 19.2K and up workable. Keep the modem anyway, it'll outlive the 500. Sigh.

subject: Ham Packet Radios - who makes 'em?
q: Can anybody give me the name and phone number of a manufacturer of ham packet radios?
a: Hundreds of radios can do packet, so there's no single maker to call. Whatever you buy, you need an Amateur Radio license to operate it. It's earned, not bought. Learn that before shopping.

subject: Extended packet size with Handshake Kermit
q: How can I make Handshake 2.20c's Kermit receive extended packet lengths?
a: If Handshake follows the usual XPR conventions, use the XPR Setup menu item or send a setup string starting with O. 'OP500' sets the packet length to 500. You can also set the XPRKERMIT environment variable beforehand. RTFM for XPR.

subject: JRComm -- Text attributes?
q: In JRComm's vt100 mode I can't get underline or boldface to work, and the scrolling is awful. Am I missing something simple?
a: Yes. Put the fonts that come with JR-Comm in your FONTS: directory, since they're needed for reverse video and underlining. Scrolling is fine here in VT100 mode, so something's wrong on your end. Read the docs.

subject: VT Terminal Software
q: Is there a better VT220 emulation for the Amiga than Handshake, and are there any VT graphics capable emulations like VT240 or VT340?
a: Meshugena also advertises vt220, but I think it only has vt200 menu options. It does multiple sessions and has a nicer interface than dnet. VLT handles vt102 quite well, I think. As for VT240 or VT340 graphics, nobody has one. Sad truth.

subject: UUCP versus SLIP connection
q: Is there any real reason to choose SLIP over UUCP for dedicated serial lines between Amigas and UNIX systems? One line is very long, with delays near a second. Is SLIP out of the question?
a: If you can run SLIP, you should. TCP/IP over SLIP has no trouble with long delays, since it uses a time-adaptive algorithm. Half-second lag is hardly news to TCP. Go read about it.

subject: Supra 9600
q: The blurb on the Supra 9600 says to just set your computer to 9600 and let the modem handle the speed. But with v.32 and v.42bis, doesn't that bottleneck you at 9600? Is the article wrong?
a: The article is wrong. Set your serial port to 19200 or 38400 and let the modem do the rest. Sigh, that's the whole point of v.42bis, and the blurb writer should know better.

subject: Downloading from radio/satelites?
q: What does it take to download weather satellite images and other broadcast information by radio, and is it allowed? Is it ordinary AM/FM, or does it need special hardware?
a: Not ordinary AM/FM. Satellite reception needs a dish, LNA or LNB and downconverter gear, while weather FAX, news FAX and slow-scan TV live on HF, roughly 3.5 to 30 MHz. In the US receiving is unrestricted. Subscribe to rec.radio.amateur.* and learn something.

subject: ASCII code for BREAK ???
q: What is the ASCII code for BREAK? I can't find it in my ASCII table.
a: There isn't one. That's why you can't find it. BREAK isn't a character, it's a line condition, a continuous mark or space held longer than a character time, typically 100 to 300 mS. Some old software faked it by dropping the baud and sending a NULL, a kludge. Basic serial stuff.

subject: Current Atalk III version?
q: What's the current version of Atalk III, and is it AmigaDOS 2.0 compatible?
a: Version 1.3e, as far as I know, and yes, it's 2.0 compatible. Check the version yourself before you go bothering the net again.

subject: SLIP -- do YOU know where it is?
q: Where can I get SLIP for the Amiga?
a: Sources to AmigaNOS 1.9 are archived as AmigaKIT19.lzh and amiganos-src19.zoo on one UUCP site, and nic.funet.fi in Finland has some stuff too. Think twice before fetching transatlantic. Folks keep asking this.

subject: VLT zmodem
q: Zmodem downloads in VLT keep overflowing my buffer, giving garbage and aborting the transfer. Any suggestions?
a: Change the buffer size. It's under the external options in the transfers pulldown menu. With a hard drive, set it higher. Without one, set it lower; 8K worked for one user. The buffer overflows before it can be written to disk, so go read your menus.

subject: Bridgeboard and the Parallel Port
q: Can a Bridgeboard use the Amiga parallel port instead of buying a card with parallel ports? How?
a: Yes. Run the lpt1 program from the original Bridgeboard disks, in the PC drawer. Click its icon and the PC side owns the parallel port; close the window and the Amiga gets it back. It's on the disks, so RTFM.

subject: apple ][ emulations?
q: Does anyone have experience with the public domain Apple ][ emulators on the Amiga? None I've tried compile under Manx Aztec. Do I need a ROM dump?
a: Don't bother with the C versions. One I got going under Lattice was painfully slow, as any 6502 interpreter in a high-level language is. On a 7.14 MHz Amiga you need assembly. Honestly, write it from scratch.

subject: A-Max & parallel PostScript printer+
q: I have an Amiga 2000/2091 running A-Max 2.06 and System 6.0.5, with a PostScript printer on the parallel port. Choosing the LaserWriter driver in Chooser doesn't print. Am I doing something wrong?
a: Probably not you. The latest FAQ notes that MultiFinder and System 6.0.5 aren't 100% compatible with A-Max. Try a lower system version if you can. Sigh, read the FAQ before blaming yourself.

subject: Transformer--where?howmuch?when?
q: IBeM won't run on my 68000 Amiga, so do I need the Transformer? Where do I get it, and how well does it perform?
a: Hang on, don't go buying Transformer. IBeM's author is working on an upgrade for any Amiga with any memory. On a 68000 it'll be as slow as Transformer was, around 0.1 Norton SI, but reliable and multitasking, with hard disk partitions.

subject: Info on Atari ST emulators anyone?
q: Is there an Atari ST emulator or program for the Amiga that can read ST format disks, so I can move text files from a friend's ST without using the modem?
a: You don't need an emulator, any idiot knows ST disks are nearly MS-DOS format. CrossDOS (commercial), Dos-2-Dos, or the shareware MSH will read, write and format them. I've copied files both ways with Dos2Dos. Try it before posting.

subject: Looking for good Atari ST emulator
q: Where can I find a good, working Atari ST emulator for the Amiga that runs on a 68010?
a: Don't count on it. I doubt any ST emulator runs on anything above a 68000, since early TOS did illegal things that break on later CPUs. And if it has the ROMs on disk, it's illegal; buy them from an Atari dealer. Think before you ask.

subject: Why not Hardware?
q: Why aren't there hardware add-ons for the Amiga to emulate machines like the C64, instead of all software emulators?
a: Cost, naturally. A little board with a 6502 also needs all the special peripheral chips of the emulated machine. The processor is the easy part. Handling peripheral registers is hard, so you'd end up with about 70 percent of the original hardware. Not worth the money.

subject: Waiting FOREVER for AMAX-TWO-PLUS
q: Will AMAX 2+ ever be released? Does anyone know when it's supposed to appear?
a: ReadySoft told me last week it would ship mid-November. It gives 7.0 compatibility and built-in Amiga drive compatibility. Colour has to wait for Amax III. Vapourware promises, so don't hold your breath.

subject: Deskjet Inkmun Full Color Kit?
q: An ad advertises an Inkmun Full Color Kit for the HP Deskjet at $34.95. How does it work, what software do I need, and does it affect buying a used Paintjet for around $600?
a: It's just a kit to clean empty DeskJet cartridges and refill them with coloured ink. You print colour-separated output, feeding the paper through three times, and only PageStream handles it. The registration is horrible. It's no substitute for a PaintJet.

subject: Other than color 0 in screen border for genlock?
q: How can I get something other than color 0 into the screen border on the Amiga, so my SuperGen genlock doesn't let video through at the very edges of an overlay frame?
a: Get an ECS Denise. It lets you turn border transparency off, or set the border blank instead of color 0, either of which fixes it. Commercial software doesn't support it yet, so you'll need Kickstart 2.0 and a small utility you write yourself.

subject: HP-Deskjet Color ?
q: I heard HP has a new color DeskJet with a 4-color ink cartridge. Does anyone know more about it, or whether there's an Amiga driver?
a: Nice printer, thousands of colors at the full 300 DPI, but slow: up to 7 minutes per full color page. It holds only one cartridge, so you swap between black and color. With the black cartridge it's basically a DJ500. No word on an Amiga driver.

subject: wasp and dynamic, sliced modes
q: I made sliced hires images from GIF files with wasp and viewed them with mostra, but they show lots of thin horizontal color bands. Is the problem wasp or mostra, and is there a viewer that handles sliced hires?
a: It's wasp, not your viewer. Nice program, but mostra, dyna-show and full-view all choke on its dynamic-hires output. Not much you can do about it yet. Sigh.

subject: Looking for Imagine Objects
q: Is there an ftp server or BBS with 3D objects for Imagine or TurboSilver? Lightwave comes with an object library but Imagine gives you nothing.
a: FTP to hubcap.clemson.edu and look in /pub/incoming/amiga/IMAGINE/OBJECTS. Imagine and Turbo Silver share the same object file format, so they work in either. Quit whining about libraries and go build something.

subject: 24 bit boards
q: Only DCTV seems to offer animation among 24 bit boards for the Amiga 3000. Is that right? Does anything else animate?
a: Wrong. HAM-E, DCTV, and Colorburst can all animate. HAM-E and DCTV aren't true 24-bit displays, just simulating colors. Colorburst does 24-bit but can't really animate in it, though you can animate on top of a 24-bit background. Read the specs.

subject: MegaMidget and ICD's Flicker Free Video
q: Are the MegaMidget and ICD's Flicker Free Video compatible? Can they be piggybacked on an Amiga?
a: They plug in at different points: the MegaMidget in the CPU socket, the FFV in the Denise socket by the video port. The FFV fits around the two big capacitors. Whether the MegaMidget physically fits, measure it yourself.

subject: Can I boot off of DH2: instead of DH0:?
q: Can I boot off my SCSI drive DH2: instead of DH0: on an Amiga 2000HD with a 2090A controller?
a: Use the prep utility that came with your 2090A. It has a boot-from-this-drive (y/n) option. But be warned it might format the drive, so back up first, genius. RTFM.

subject: 68020 Question
q: Can I just drop a 68020 into my Amiga in place of the 68000? I know a 68010 works. Are there any problems, and is the chip the same size?
a: No, the package is still different. You need extra circuitry for the CPU to sit on, especially to run above 7.16 MHz, because the rest of the system must believe a 7.16 MHz 68000 is attached. Why do you think 2620 and 2630 boards carry all that? To confuse buyers?

subject: Does FFV (Flicker Free Video) work in PAL & NTSC?
q: Does FFV (Flicker Free Video) work in both PAL and NTSC? I don't want to buy two flickerFixer boards just to use both.
a: Forget FFV. The Commodore A2320 display enhancer does PAL, NTSC and ECS modes automatically, and even works with some genlocks. It lists at $299 against $499 for FFV. Sigh, read a price list once in a while.

subject: Supra 500RX
q: Does anyone have experience with the Supra 500RX external memory expansion for the Amiga 500, compared to ICD AdRAM, Baseboard and others that use the A501 slot?
a: It'd almost certainly be faster, since the trap door expansions all have wait states, though on an unaccelerated 500 that hardly matters. Supra advertises zero wait state and promised autoconfig of everything. Whether it actually ships is another matter. Vaporware, probably.

subject: A501/GVP Impact A500 incompatibilities?
q: Has anyone seen incompatibilities between the GVP Impact A500 memory expansion and the Commodore A501 expansion? Guru crashes happen with both installed but not with either alone.
a: Check your GVP jumpers. The newer 4 meg model has different jumper instructions than the 2 meg one, so call GVP and verify yours are set right. Read the paperwork next time.

subject: A silly question...
q: Has anyone tried using the IBM-PC slots in an A2000 or A3000 without a Bridgeboard, say by putting a cheap clone motherboard inside the Amiga? Does the A2000 even supply power to those slots without the Bridgeboard?
a: Doubtful. As I recall, power isn't connected to those slots unless a Bridgeboard is present, so about all they're good for is mounting hard drives on dead boards. Also, a 286 board needs support electronics and a keyboard. Think before you post, kid.

subject: CLTD controller
q: Has anyone used the C-LTD SCSI controller with a Lucas/Frances combo on an A1000? Formatting a 150MB drive gurus or hangs.
a: Yes, it works. I had to ground the A1000 PALs and install SCSIDOS 3.0 from Microdyn, who took over the line. Don't run the Lucas above 16MHz with it, and on some drives disable block read or the bus hangs.

subject: New Fat Agunus
q: How can I tell whether my new Amiga 500 has the new Fat Agnus without voiding my warranty? The store said no, but a friend was told his has it but not activated.
a: The replies don't pin down a clean test, and you'd be a fool to trust the store clerk. One owner with the Obese Agnus says it still can't use 1Mb of chip memory. He can only switch PAL to NTSC through hardware registers. Whatever.

subject: HELP! - Problem w/ 1Mbx4 SC Zips
q: I put 8 1Mx4 zips in my A3000 but Workbench only shows 1MB. Is there some jumper I need to change?
a: Yes. Without changing the memory sizing jumper on the A3000 motherboard, a 1Mx4 part is treated as a 256Kx4 part. It's an 800-something jumper listed in the manual and on the first schematic page. RTFM before you blame the chips.

subject: UNIX drivers for 3rd party hardware
q: If I have a Microbotics HardFrame and want UNIX on the Amiga, am I out of luck without a CBM controller? Could I move the drive to a 2091 without reformatting?
a: GVP says it will supply Unix drivers, but Microbotics grumbles Commodore tells them nothing. HardFrame and 2091 both follow the RDB spec, so the drive should boot on the 2091 without a low-level format. You'd only reformat a partition for UNIX, I think.

subject: A2300 Genlock
q: My A2300 genlock over-saturates colors when I use it to output digitized images to a VCR. There are no apparent adjustments other than the overlay ones. Any thoughts?
a: The manual lists trimmers: VR1 brightness, VR2 color, VR3 FSC, VR4 hue, VR5 H-position, VR6 burst blank, and L6 for the VCO. It doesn't say where they are. Hope it's obvious. Typical documentation.

subject: 150ns DRAMS
q: My A500 has 150ns DRAMs in its half meg expansion. If I reconfigure it as chip RAM, will the extra timing constraints cause trouble, given I read the Amiga wants 120ns parts?
a: Relax. Chip bus cycles take 280ns, and Commodore wouldn't use 150ns DRAMs if they didn't work. Chip-bus timing is the same whether it's mapped Fast or Chip. Whoever said only 120ns works is spreading bogus information.

subject: read/write error
q: My Amiga 500 gives a READ/WRITE error on most disks as I load them, though usually they load fine. Could it be the drive or something else?
a: Could be interference from your monitor. One fellow cured it on a 500 with a 1084 monitor by wrapping aluminum foil around the internal drive as a shield. Only truly bad disks fail now. Crude, but cheaper than a new drive.

subject: GVP 68030 22/33/50MHz SIMM memory
q: What does GVP mean by "custom" SIMM32 memory modules on their 68030 accelerator? Do I have to buy memory from them, or are they the same as SIMMs sold in stores?
a: Here we go again. It's a SIMM pinout they dreamed up themselves, so yes, you buy from them, and no, store SIMMs won't fit. The JEDEC standards are 30-pin x8 and 72-pin x32 modules. GVP chose their own 64-pin x32. Check old articles.

subject: Hard Disk for A500
q: What hard disk interfaces are available for the Amiga 500? SCSI preferred.
a: Plenty, so go look. GVP Impact Series II, Supra 500XP, Dataflyer, Trumpcard 500 and Pro, Grand Slam, Rapid Access Turbo 500, and the XETEC Fast Trac. Most come with memory expansion boards. Your dealer only knowing PCs is no surprise.

subject: Max Bandwidth of Zorro
q: What is the maximum bandwidth of Zorro II and Zorro III?
a: Zorro II does about 3.5 MB/s. Zorro III is theoretically about 50 MB/s with full cycles, 150 MB/s in burst. The A3000 gets about 20 MB/s practically without burst. Don't believe the marketing numbers.

subject: A3000 CPU Wars!!
q: Why was everyone so worked up about the A3000 040/030 multiprocessor thing if no OS will take advantage of it soon?
a: I doubt everyone was worked up. People kept asking what separates the accelerated 16MHz and 25MHz systems, and the multiprocessing feature is the only difference. That's all it was.

subject: Compatibility info requested on 15" tall Packard-Bell monitor
q: Will a 15-inch Packard-Bell monitor with a 62.75 kHz horizontal rate work on an Amiga with a deinterlacer or ECS Denise? How do its scan rates compare to NTSC, CGA, EGA and VGA?
a: Those numbers look way out of line. A multisync has to drop down to about 15 kHz and go up to about 30-31 kHz horizontal, and handle 60 Hz vertical for NTSC modes and 50 Hz for PAL. A fixed 62 kHz monitor won't cut it. Check the specs before buying.

subject: Disk icons
q: Can I change the icon Workbench puts on my disks when I format a new floppy?
a: Workbench uses either the Disk.info in the disk's root directory or the system default icon. So find a Disk.info and edit the image. IconEd ships with your system, but IconMaster is much nicer. That's for WB 1.3. 2.0 is only rumor, so don't ask me.

subject: zoo drives me nuts
q: How do I unzoo a big file on my Amiga when I run out of disk space? Piping to df1: just makes zoo think df1: is a file in the archive.
a: cd to the blank disk you want to expand onto, then type zoo x// followed by the archive path. Without the // modifier zoo won't keep the directory structure. Copy zoo to RAM disk first so you can pull out your Workbench disk.

subject: Preferences Postscript Driver
q: I just hooked my Amiga up to an Apple Laserwriter. Is there a preferences-style printer driver that automatically converts text files to PostScript, so I don't have to run each one through PageStream? What's it called and where do I find it?
a: It's called PostDriver, a commercial program from a company called Soft Service. So no, you won't find it lying around in FTP-land, free. Pay for it like everybody else. Nobody here knows if it's sold in the USA.

subject: MEmacs with undo?
q: Is there a version of MEmacs for the Amiga with undo? If not, who do I contact to get it added?
a: Have you tried MicroEMACS 3.10? It's the general release that appeared as source in comp.sources.*. Grab it from an Amiga BBS or a suitable ftp site. Look before you wish.

subject: HELLPP!!!
q: The corners of my 1084 monitor screen have gone much lighter and the Workbench blue looks bright purple. Is the picture tube ruined?
a: Probably not. It looks like a magnetic field, same as bringing a magnet near a color TV. Check for speakers, fans or anything electrical near the monitor and move it away. Any idiot who has wrecked a TV with a magnet knows this.

subject: Close box probs in 2.0 under Wshell
q: Under 2.0 on an A3000, the Wshell close box needs five clicks before it closes. Is this a bug?
a: Not a bug. WShell needs ConMan to recognize the close gadget. The standard 2.0 CON: sends an EOF, and five are required as a safety against accidental ^\ hits. Install ConMan and point your WShell windows at it. RTFM next time.

subject: why can't the Amiga talk properly
q: Why can't the Amiga speech software talk Danish or German with u umlaut and decent r's? Why was that phoneme standard chosen, and what can be done?
a: You're right, and Commodore knows it. There's been internal discussion but no result yet. It's a money question: would it pay, and how many apps would even use speech? Even English apps mostly don't. CDTV will go straight to digitized speech.

subject: hardware shipping
q: I'm selling my Amiga 2000 and need to ship it. Other than price, is there anything I should know about choosing between UPS and the regular postal service?
a: UPS has the better record for tracing lost or late packages. That's the difference that matters beyond price, so go use it. Don't ship a CPU without being able to track it.

subject: Virus checkers
q: I run VirusX 4.0 from my Startup-Sequence on my Amiga. Is there any known virus it misses, and should I have another virus checker?
a: Yes, VirusX doesn't recognize all viruses, so you're not covered. Get Virus_Checker from the usual Amiga archive sites. Zero_Virus is also worth running alongside it, since its brain file can be updated for new viruses and boot sectors.

subject: Amigavision with multiple videodisks?
q: Can Amigavision be convinced to control multiple video disks? Will the current device drivers handle that?
a: No. I checked with Commodore: AVision doesn't support multiple discs and the drivers have no capacity for it. The ASCII control codes for the Pioneer 4200 are easy enough, so you could write a custom driver or a program. Typical vendor limitation.

subject: Request for information DCTV devise Amiga
q: Can the DCTV device give me NTSC output from an Amiga 2000 for broadcasting animations, in low resolution and without flicker?
a: DCTV turns 24-bit RGB into NTSC. It works in low-res or interlaced and is flicker-free, but only for programs that output 24-bit RGB, like Imagine. It does nothing with Workbench or other non-24-bit output. Read the fine print before buying.

subject: MONDO problem in AmigaVision
q: In AmigaVision, my mouse interrupt with several hit boxes runs and then the program quits, sometimes depending on timing. What's wrong?
a: Check that "Any Click" is turned off in the Mouse wait requestor, or an invalid response can kick you out. Also make sure your if-then boxes test response()=="x", with x the value from the mouse interrupt. Why it's intermittent, nobody knows.

subject: Oberon or Modula-3 Amiga versions ?
q: Are Modula-3 or Oberon available for the Amiga? If so, where can I ftp them?
a: There's a demo of a supported Oberon compiler on Fred Fish disk 380. Grab it by ftp from ux1.cso.uiuc.edu as amiga/fish/ff380/Oberon.zoo, or something like that. The file explains ordering the full version. Nobody mentioned Modula-3.

subject: Hacking in a 68020
q: How hard would it be to build a 68020 board with an MMU that drops into the 68000 socket of an Amiga? What problems would I face?
a: Just buy a 68030, the MMU is expensive for a 020. The interface is simple: read Commodore's expansion board docs. We built a synchronous 020 board in six weeks. Asynchronous is messier and needs a datalatch on the databus.

subject: String Gadg Colors
q: The text entry box of a string gadget always uses the screen's background color. Is there any way, simple or hard, to set it to something else?
a: Under 1.3 and earlier the editable text is hard-coded as color 1 on color 0, and there's no real way to change it. Under 2.0 use the StringExtend structure. Sigh, read the docs.

subject: Memory Alloc during Duplicate (WB)
q: Why does the Amiga Workbench Duplicate function grab all available memory to duplicate an empty directory?
a: Yes, that was a Workbench 1.x problem. Workbench 2.04 doesn't do it. Copying was redone to use only the memory it needs, and the system stays stable even at 0 bytes free. Upgrade already.

subject: NEC 2A and 2000
q: Can I hook a NEC 2A monitor up to my Amiga 2000? A friend said I need a buffer box. Is that needed for all multisyncs, and does the 2A handle interlace?
a: No. The 2A is only a Super VGA monitor, syncing at 31.5kHz and 35kHz, so it won't take the Amiga's RGB output without a flickerfixer. Beam alignment on the units seen was lousy too. Read the spec sheet before buying.

subject: Auto-configing...
q: Can a device that isn't autoconfigured by hardware be configured by using the Expansion directory? I want novice users to run an install program and never worry about it again.
a: No. Executables in the expansion drawer only start when a matching hardware device is found, and non-autoconfig hardware never matches. I wish there was a "match always" too, but there isn't. Sorry.

subject: using Kodak 3.3M/6.6M floppy drives
q: Can the Amiga's built-in disk controller handle a Kodak 6.6M floppy drive that spins at 600 RPM, with index pulses every 100ms?
a: No. The Amiga chipset's disk controller is limited to the standard 3.5 inch data rate. Anything faster needs SCSI, the PC bus, or your own controller card. Should've been obvious from the specs.

subject: Multiple Amigas on a SCSI Bus.
q: Can two Amigas, a 500 and a 1000, each with a 590 hard drive, share SCSI devices on one bus? Is it feasible?
a: Possible, sure, if you enjoy pain. You need a new device driver, one 590 set to a different SCSI ID, and some arbitration. Best bet is to make one machine act as a drive server for the other, since otherwise who may read, write, or cache what is a mess.

subject: Aztec-C and stack size
q: Do programs written with Manx Aztec-C need a minimum stack of 8000 bytes? Mine works at 8000 but crashes at 4000.
a: Not an Aztec requirement; look at your automatic variables, which live on the stack. A big local array blows it. Compile with the +m switch for stack checking, and define __stkover() to exit gracefully. Don't put huge arrays on the stack.

subject: FF - FastFonts
q: Does anybody know what FF (FastFonts) does on the Amiga? I know it's supposed to speed up text displays, but what does it actually do internally?
a: Can't speak to the internals, but the 1.3 enhancer manual never tells you that FF can replace the default Topaz system font with any 8-bit font. Put 'FF myfont.font' in your startup sequence. And don't put a comment on the same line, or it won't work. RTFM, if it were in there.

subject: ILBM Hunks
q: Does anyone have a current list of the ILBM hunks registered with CATS? I have FF185 but want as much current information as possible.
a: Throw out FF185, it's stale. The 1.3 RKM includes and autodocs are far more current, with extra specs in the IFF chapter appendices like PAN, DPDV and CHAN. Read the manual before you go begging the net.

subject: DevPac/MonAm2
q: Has anyone got DevPac's MonAm2 single-stepping working on an Amiga 3000? The address indicator doesn't move when I step, on either Kick 1.3 or 2.0.
a: Check your version numbers, genius. GenAm and MonAm have separate ones. The early 2.0 MonAm2 choked on 030s, but 2.05 works fine on a 2500/030, which is effectively the same as a 3000. Get an upgrade from HiSoft if you need one.

subject: ARP include files
q: Has anyone heard when the ARP include files and programmers docs will be available? It's a pain not being able to recompile programs without them.
a: They're coming. There's a set of includes for C and the standard assembly includes, glue and pragmas for Lattice 5.x are tested, and the docs are about done and should land on a net somewhere. Patience, it's not an official statement either.

subject: How serious is memory fragmentation?
q: How bad is memory fragmentation on the Amiga if I do lots of small allocs and frees, like a new line buffer on every change? Should I manage my own pool, and does the system merge adjacent free blocks?
a: Not as bad as you fear. With little other activity you'll be fine, but another task's freed 32K chunk stays a fragment while your buffer sits in it. Your own allocator is probably faster than AllocMem for line buffers. Yes, adjacent free blocks merge. Don't stomp the memory list or FreeRemember(,0) leaks 8-byte headers.

subject: Am I even or odd?
q: How can I tell during the vertical retrace on the Amiga whether the next field shown is even or odd, so I can swap 3D shutter glasses lenses correctly?
a: A bit in a video register identifies the current frame, long or short. It's documented in the Hardware manual, probably the high bit of the beam vertical position register. Use the custom register base passed to you and Commodore's symbolic names. RTFM.

subject: dual playfields under Intuition
q: How do I set up a dual playfield display under Intuition on the Amiga? The Intuition manual hints it's possible and the RKM shows dual playfields without Intuition. My DUALPF window hack flickers and leaves me with only 8 colours.
a: All the code you need is in the Amiga Enhancer Software manual, version 1.2, pages 69 through 75, courtesy of Jim Mackraz. Read the manual instead of hacking the window setup and wondering why the colors break.

subject: Noclick on the A3000
q: How do I turn off the clicking of the internal floppy drive on the A3000?
a: Stick a floppy into the drive. Costs nothing, and uses no memory or CPU time from your Amiga. Sigh, you're welcome.

subject: SetFunction
q: How do I use SetFunction() on the Amiga to replace DisplayBeep with my own code? I called SetFunction(IntuitionBase,(long)-60,&MyFunction) since I think -60 is the DisplayBeep offset, but it doesn't work.
a: Your offset is wrong. Library vector offsets are hexadecimal, hex, hex. Check the real DisplayBeep offset in hex, not decimal -60. Honestly, RTFM.

subject: How do you disable DOS requesters ?
q: How do you disable the DOS requesters, like the "Insert volume env:" prompt, on the Amiga?
a: Look in your Process structure for pr_WindowPtr. Point it at a window and requesters appear there; set it to -1 and they never come up, you just get the error back. Put it back how you found it afterward, because DOS won't reset it. RTFM.

subject: How does an A590 disk work ?
q: How does the A590 hard disk adaptor work? Can I replace the XT drive with a bigger SCSI disk, and do I need to change straps on the board?
a: It has two connectors, one for the XT drive and one for SCSI drives. Just plug the SCSI drive in with power and SCSI cable and configure it with HDToolBox. No strapping needed, and you can run both together.

subject: ???? Lattice Update Availability ???? (was Re: Lattice C 5.02 BUGS)
q: How will we know when to call Lattice and ask for the 5.04 update of Lattice C? If they mail registered owners, why not just send it?
a: Probably the patches go on the Lattice BBS, which is standard practice, and get sent to people who call in about bugs fixed in that update. One poster recalls you must call the BBS and download the fixes. Report your bugs, then.

subject: Memory protection
q: I have an A2000 with an A2620 card. Can I run the memory protection tool on it, or is it tied to the 68030?
a: Yes, it'll follow you into an A2620 just fine. Whether you can actually get hold of the thing, I couldn't tell you. And the TRAP option of the cpu command is obsolete in the A3000 software release, so read the notes before asking again.

subject: <None>
q: I know the CLI process limit on AmigaOS 1.2/1.3 is 20. What is the task limit when started with CreateProc(), and does 2.0 have a CLI limit?
a: No limit on non-CLI processes, and processes are supersets of tasks, so learn the terminology. 1.3 capped CLIs at 20; 2.0 has no cap. I've seen CLI #300+ under 2.0 stress-testing with scripts. Sigh, 256 is just rumor.

subject: Lattice 4.0 and MicroEMACS 3.10
q: I'm trying MicroEMACS 3.10 from the fish disks with Lattice 4.0. It runs, but the cursor won't move and typed text isn't displayed. Has anyone fixed this?
a: The typeahead routine is broken in the real release, so you get no display. That's the actual problem. Someone fixed it along with other stuff and is mailing the sources off, so wait for those instead of hacking at it.

subject: need good digitized sound compression scheme
q: I'm writing a game with lots of digitized samples on the Amiga. Is there a better scheme than Fibonacci delta encoding plus zero-run compression to squeeze sounds onto the disk?
a: Not really. Fibonacci delta, as in IFF 8SVX, gets 2X while adding distortion, though it's listenable. Skip run-length coding: edit the zeros out with Audiomaster and play two sounds with a timer wait between. Apple's talk of 6X is vapor until someone shows how.

subject: Apple SCSI not compatible with standard SCSI?
q: Is Apple's SCSI not compatible with the standard? Will Mac SCSI drives work with Amiga controllers?
a: Depends. Apple used a 25-pin connector instead of the standard 50-pin, losing the extra grounds and reliable long cables, which is why they say one meter max. Many Amiga controllers have an Apple-style 25-pin port, and the rest is pretty standard, so Mac drives should work fine there.

subject: Is 14.32MHz too fast for my expansion RAM?
q: Is a 14MHz 68000 speedup board wasted with my Micron 2MB expansion RAM? Will the fast processor just wait on the memory?
a: Mostly wasted. Speedup boards run expansion bus memory at normal speed, so you only gain on internal CPU operation, cache hits and special fast memory on the board. Without that you get a little. Basic hardware, folks.

subject: Need help w/ SCROLLING
q: Is there a faster way than ScrollRaster() to scroll a 30-pixel high strip of text on an Amiga hires-interlaced screen?
a: Skip ScrollRaster(), it cares about RastPorts and layers. If you have no windows on your screen, call BltBitMap() directly. Rewriting the caller in assembly while still calling the same slow routine was never going to help.

subject: sun c to amiga
q: Is there a utility to run C programs compiled on a Sun on my Amiga, or move them over from the Sun to the Amiga?
a: Programs compiled on a Sun won't run on an Amiga, any idiot knows that. Copy the source over with kermit or sz/rz and a terminal emulator, then recompile with an Amiga C compiler. Amiga gcc might also do it.

subject: Mac sounds to Amiga IFF sounds... KILLER!
q: Is there a way to convert Mac sounds to Amiga IFF sounds, or at least play them on the Amiga?
a: Trivial. Read the Mac file a byte at a time and flip the high bit, which is XOR with 128 in C. That gives you Amiga dump form; load it in a music program and save as IFF. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: FastFileSystem
q: Is there a way to get the Amiga FastFileSystem driver to work with trackdisk so I can mount an FFS floppy? Does 2.0 allow this? I have 1.3.
a: Under 1.3, mount it with a mountlist: copy the RAD: entry, set device to trackdisk.device, and add Mask=0x7ffff so all device access goes through CHIP buffers. Under 2.0 the ROM filesystem is FFS with extras and switches between OFS and FFS disks automatically. Try reading the docs.

subject: Static limits (Re: AmigaDos directory knowledge + (new) BENCHMARK I DID)
q: Isn't the Amiga also subject to static limits, like the 32 SigBits limit for an AmigaOS task?
a: Sure, but sigbits can be shared between multiple event generators. It's somewhat harder to share file handles between multiple files. Not the same thing at all.

subject: Bridgeboard & A3000 problems again!
q: My A2286 bridgeboard in an A3000 under 2.0 can't find the Janus libraries again after I added an internal modem, though it works fine under 1.3. Any ideas?
a: Try 'cpu nodatacache' before the binddrivers command. Also check the bridgeboard manual and make sure your memory and IO addresses don't conflict. Sigh, read the manual before blaming the A3000.

subject: LUCAS FPU LOGIC ERROR
q: My Amiga accelerator shows an "FPU Logic Error" in SetCPU, and I have no MMU. What does this mean and should I worry?
a: It means the FPU address isn't fully decoded, so the FPU answers at the MMU's coprocessor address too. Harmless today, but a future OS looking for an MMU might get fooled. Not a big deal now, but sloppy hardware design.

subject: Catching free memory violations
q: My Amiga program seems to use memory it doesn't own. Would zeroing memory on FreeMem and periodically scanning free memory for non-zero bytes catch it? What are the pitfalls?
a: It would work, with caveats. The first eight bytes of each free chunk hold the next-chunk pointer, so you can't zero those, and a stray write may have trashed them, so don't trust walking the free list. Programs may also free memory without clearing it, so non-zero isn't proof. Easier: wrap AllocMem and FreeMem with #defines and track every block.

subject: Flicker Fixer and AmiGen
q: My Flicker Fixer loses sync and the video is trashed when I attach an AmiGen genlock to my B2000. Is that normal, and can it be fixed?
a: Yes, it's normal. The Flicker Fixer works with a composite adapter but not a genlock, and it won't sync while the Amiga is in genlock mode. Microway is beta testing a cheap piggyback compatibility board, so wait for that. Should've been documented.

subject: DME and vanishing text
q: My assembly program writes text with DOS Write() and linefeeds. It looks fine with TYPE, but DME drops the latter half of lines I continue with a second Write(). Why?
a: You're writing a null byte at the end of each string. TYPE ignores nulls, but DME treats them as end-of-line, like C does. Subtract 1 from the Length you pass to Write() so the terminating $00 isn't written. Classic off-by-one.

subject: INTUITICKS Problem!
q: My ray tracing program runs 10% faster when I put the calculation inside a CASE INTUITICKS loop, but then it hangs whenever the window isn't selected. What's going on, and is there a way around it?
a: INTUITICKS only go to the active window, so of course it stalls when deselected. Sigh. You don't need them: the Amiga is pre-emptive, so just do your work. Use Wait() or WaitPort() when you're actually waiting for something, and timer.device if you need timed events.

subject: DisplayBeep()
q: On the Amiga, DisplayBeep() flashes the screen, which is annoying in telecommunications. Is there a way to change it to a real beep, like the Macs?
a: SetFunction() the DisplayBeep() call. Plenty of utilities do it already. Fish disk 217 has InstallBeep, which plays an IFF 8SVX sound in a background task instead of flashing, binary only. Didn't take much digging, did it?

subject: Amiga clocks
q: Our Amiga runs a slideshow around the clock, and the clock misbehaves: it runs fast, resets to 1-1-1978, or is weeks off. What causes this?
a: Either your clock battery is dead or your CIAs are bad, since they provide some system-dependent timing. That's about it. Replace the battery before you go blaming the cable TV headstation.

subject: AutoBoot Under KS 1.3
q: Under KS 1.3, can I still boot from a floppy in DF0: if I have an autobooting device in one of the A2000 slots?
a: Yes. A bootable floppy in DF0: overrides autoboot devices, because the system checks the floppy first.

subject: TCP/IP FTP
q: Using Commodore's TCP/IP on my A3000, I get 'network unreachable' trying to FTP to a site that isn't in my local hosts file, even by number. All the listed sites work. Any ideas?
a: Your Amiga knows nothing beyond its local net. Use the route command, like route add default vax 1, to send unknown networks through that machine, and check with netstat -r. There's no name service software either, so use the number or put it in the host table.

subject: Free memory available
q: What is the acceptable way to find out how much free memory there is on the Amiga from a C program, without AllocMem'ing until it fails? I want to test it with IF in a startup script.
a: Call AvailMem(type), for example AvailMem(MEMF_CHIP) or MEMF_FAST, shifted right 10 for K. Free memory isn't the largest contiguous chunk, though, since AllocMem needs contiguous blocks. For IF, have your program return 0 or 5 and test with WARN. RTFM.

subject: The Pure Bit...
q: What is the pure bit on an Amiga executable for, and what must a program do to be legally pure?
a: It marks the executable as residentable, meaning reentrant, so multiple instances can share one code image. The linker sets it, never you by hand. A program with BSS or DATA hunks usually isn't pure. Forcing it gets you wrong filenames and Gurus. Don't.

subject: Double Click
q: What is the standard way to handle double clicking on a gadget on the Amiga, and what is the best timing value?
a: Don't roll your own. IDCMP messages carry time stamps, so save the one from the first click and compare it to the second with intuition.library's DoubleClick function. It uses the preferences interval, and you must respect that setting.

subject: What CRT (Monitor) for ECS
q: What kind of monitor do I need to use the promised ECS hi-res modes on an Amiga, in the 16 to 20 inch range?
a: You need a monitor that handles 31.5 KHz horizontal as well as 15.75 KHz, and many in that price range won't do the low one. The Mitsubishi HA3905 does, for about $1800. Don't expect too much from ECS; get a flicker fixer.

subject: Help: Agnus/Denise pinout differences on 500/2000 and 1000
q: What would Agnus pin 34 and Denise pin 35 on an Amiga 500/2000 correspond to on an Amiga 1000?
a: If you mean the 28MHz clock input, there's no equivalent on the old Agnus. Fat Agnus makes all system clocks from 28MHz, while the old ones take CCK and CCKQ from discrete logic. On old Denise those pins are no-connects, later wired to _CDAC and _CSYNC.

subject: Help with Execute()
q: When my program uses Execute() from Workbench, the executed program gets a stack of 4000 regardless of the .info file. Can I set the stack size for it from within my program?
a: Tack a stack command onto the front of the string you pass to Execute(), with an embedded newline. For example, pass "stack 123456\nram:doit arg1 arg2" instead of just the command. Simple enough, no startup-sequence hacks needed.

subject: autodoc reader
q: Where can I get a good autodoc reader for the Amiga, better than more or less?
a: Fish disk 297 has the DevKit, which includes a stand-alone program called GetAutoDoc. Just type GetAutoDoc OpenWindow and you get that autodoc. It works off an index, so it's quick. Better than more, anyway.

subject: IEEE libraries
q: Why are the Amiga IEEE libraries always set to -1 whether being used or not, so I can't flush them? I'd like to know which program is using them.
a: Check what startup code your compiler or linker attaches. These days it does too much, opening and closing libraries behind your back. Or you're looking at the trans library, which opens the bas library when loaded, so flush twice. Look at what gets bolted onto your program.

subject: Why put Kickstart on A3000 ROM? (was Re: 512K FastRam)
q: Why did they put Kickstart in ROM on the A3000, when the machine has a hard disk and loading it into RAM would be cheaper and faster?
a: Because ROM costs more only up front for the masks. The per-unit cost is very low, and in the quantities Commodore orders, ROMs are quite a bit cheaper than RAM. ROMs are also quite a bit faster than the RAMs. Think before you assume.

subject: A-Max Stuff
q: Why doesn't the A-Max cartridge work on the back of the 1010 drive, and can the Apple drive read and write disks while in Amiga mode?
a: The cartridge is poor design; it doesn't work on a 500 either, but works on a 2000. As for the Apple drive, forget it: the Amiga uses one fixed speed while Apple drives use variable speed, as the A-Max manual says. Read it.

subject: A68k and Manx AS
q: Why is the object code from the PD A68k assembler about 30% smaller than what Manx's AS produces? Is there something AS puts in its .o files that A68k leaves out?
a: A68k optimizes as it goes. It turns Bcc into Bcc.S for backward references, makes backward references PC-relative, converts ADD, SUB and MOVE to the quick forms, and turns 0(An) into (An). Hardly magic, Manx just doesn't bother. Watch your jump tables, though.

subject: Sitting Ami on end
q: Will standing an Amiga on its end mess up drive alignment? I want to put it under a desk with a noisy fan.
a: No problem at all. I've run mine on its end almost since I got it. Get a tower stand to keep it above any spilled water, and cable lengths shouldn't be a problem. Stop worrying about it.

subject: PropGadgets and IDCMP
q: With an Amiga PropGadget, I get a GADGETUP on mouse-down in the container plus a stray SELECTUP on release. Why do I get the SELECTUP, and how can I stop it confusing my code?
a: You can't count on SELECTDOWN and SELECTUP arriving in pairs or in any order. There are lots of ways to get one without the other. Write your code to cope, and watch INACTIVEWINDOW events, since then all bets are off on the mouse.

subject: Where Oh Where is the ECS Chipset?
q: With the new Enhanced Chip Set, could I use 2MB of RAM on an 8-UP! board as chip RAM in an A2000 or A500, and could an MMU remap the first megabyte?
a: Forget it. Without major hacking you'll never get more than 1M of chip RAM in an A2000 or A500, since the upper address bit isn't wired to the custom chips. And an MMU only remaps the CPU's view, not the custom chips' addresses.

subject: zoo troubles
q: Zoo on the Amiga takes forever to add even a single file to an archive in a directory of 150 files. It seems to be reading every file. Has anyone else seen this?
a: Yes, this comes up. AmigaZoo searches the whole directory for matching files for every name on the command line, even without wildcards. Globbing is slow on the Amiga file system, so you wait. And wait. Pathetic.

subject: 8mm Tape Drives on Apollo 10k
q: Any advice on 8mm tape drives for an Apollo 10K using wbak and rbak, such as the ExaTape EL and HC? Will the drive work from a foreign system over NFS?
a: The 8500 with quick-restore is very nice; it cut our restores from hours to minutes. For a remote drive try wbak -stdout piped to rsh, or the -rem host:dev option. But backing Apollo files up over NFS may lose the object type of executables, so you'd restore it manually. Grumble.

subject: Possible to mount others disks onto DN10000?
q: Can I NFS-mount disks from my Convex onto a DN10000? I found /etc/nfsd but no /etc/biod. Is Apollo's NFS only a one way deal?
a: NFS is a two way deal. The Apollo NFS manual is the best I've seen. Read it to get it running, and if it doesn't behave as documented, use your service contract. Honestly, RTFM.

subject: ntpd software for SR10.3
q: Can anybody give me a pointer to the ntpd sources for SR10.3?
a: Read the file Readme.xntp in the Apollo archives at archive.umich.edu. It points to the source and has patches to run it on Domain/OS. Sigh, the pointer was sitting in the archive all along.

subject: jove on apollo?
q: Has anyone got jove working on an Apollo running 10.2? It builds but doesn't run properly under bsd4.3, and won't build under sys5.3.
a: Jove won't run properly on Apollos because it doesn't understand pathnames starting with //. The code is full of hardcoded '/' and "/", so nobody sane would touch it. Typical Unix-centric sloppiness.
