subject: MIT Xdm on Apollo.. Has anyone had success with it?
q: Has anyone gotten the MIT xdm to work on an Apollo? I log in, it looks like the session starts, then the xdm screen comes back, and it ignores the foreign systems in Xservers.
a: Use the explicit machine name instead of just :0 in the Xservers line, like opal_3:0 secure /bin/nice --10 /etc/Xapollo.R4. That fixed it for me. Hardly a mystery, just read your config more carefully.

subject: 425e Disk Brackets
q: Has anyone seen the disk mounting brackets in the HP Apollo 425e? Are they the same as in the 400s and 400t, which matters for third-party drives?
a: No, it's yet another bracket design, unlike the 400t or 400s. It's a small tray sitting on a frame inside the cabinet. HP doesn't offer them yet, as with the 400t, so some third party will have to make their own again. Typical.

subject: Filename completion in Apollo's C shell
q: Hitting ESC to complete a partly typed filename doesn't work by default in Apollo's C shell. Is there a workaround?
a: RTFM. It's in the csh man page under filename completion: it only works when the filec shell variable is set. Put "set filec" in your ~/.cshrc and stop bothering the net.

subject: Using the same IP class C adress with a domain-ring and an ethernet
q: How can I use one IP class C address for both a domain ring and a plain ethernet? I'm no TCP/IP expert and the documentation didn't help.
a: They have to be two separate networks, and the Apollo gateway runs /etc/routed to route between them. Split your class C into subnets with the mask option to /etc/ifconfig, or get a second class C for the token ring. Read up on subnetting, it's not magic.

subject: Tape format for Apollo
q: I have big data files on a Unix VAX and want to move them to a network of Apollos running Domain. A plain copy to tape couldn't be mounted on the Apollo. What's the best way?
a: Apollos read tar tapes and ANSI tapes. For ANSI tapes use the Aegis command /com/rwmt. Tar is nicer since you can send whole directories at once. Use that instead of a raw copy.

subject: Problem with setuid shell scripts under Aegis
q: I made a setuid-to-root script under Aegis on Domain 10.2, but it fails with "no rights to change acl". Why doesn't my setuid script run as root?
a: Aegis doesn't support setuid scripts. It never really changes the UID, which is a security feature, so stop assuming Aegis is UNIX. Otherwise anyone could slip in their own edacl via the path and be root. Sigh.

subject: Need info on stack frames and offsets from interrupt routine..
q: If a function is interrupted by a signal like SIGALRM on an Apollo, where do I find the return address and registers? I'm writing a small preemptive teaching kernel using timer interrupts.
a: Look at the context structure passed as the third argument to the signal handler. Did you read the manual before posting? You can also use pfm directly instead of signals; see man pfm.

subject: Apollo Pascal and Modules
q: In Apollo Pascal, why can't non-main modules call procedures in the main module, and is there a better workaround than a one-line main?
a: Procedures declared in a program are implicitly and un-overridably internal, so other modules can't call them. Better workaround: use all modules, put the main code in a procedure called main, and bind with the -entry option, like bind -b myprogram mymod1.bin mymod2.bin -entry main. Ugly, but that's Apollo.

subject: Ingres 6.2 on DN10000 - TCP/IP problems
q: Is anybody running Ingres 6.2 on a DN10000 successfully? I get lots of localhost connections hanging in FIN_WAIT and CLOSE_WAIT, and TCP/IP often hangs completely.
a: Count yourself lucky it doesn't hang without Ingres. Ours hung weekly for years; the Ethernet controller has a known lockup bug. Things improved with SR10.3.0.6 plus patch pd91_p0230, a new tcpd and tcp manager. Anything less was big trouble. Still locks up now and then, cause unknown.

subject: Ethernet board for Apollo3000 Actually a 3Com503 Board?
q: Is the Ethernet board Apollo sells for the DN3000 really just a 3Com 3C503, so I could skip paying $700 for it?
a: Yes, it's a 3Com board with an Apollo PROM. But Apollo adds a special chip that derives the 48-bit Ethernet address from the node ID, and early DN3000s only understood token ring until a boot PROM on the motherboard is replaced. Not as cheap as your tight-fisted boss hopes.

subject: Is a 68020/68030-based version of Domain/OS available?
q: Is there a 68020/68030-based version of Domain/OS? Are all the SR10 commands compiled to run on the 68000, and doesn't that cost performance?
a: Kernels for the newer machines use 68020 features, but user-space software is built to run on all 680x0. Shipping separate 68000 and 68020 copies of /bin/ls for a low payoff would be a headache. Build your own with -cpu 68020 if you care.

subject: SL/IP with SR10.2 - possible ?
q: Is there a SLIP driver in Apollo SR10.2, or something in the public domain?
a: Yes, you can specify an sl0 device with ifconfig and run slip on a separate subnet to the far side. Apollo doesn't support proxy ARP, so you lose a whole subnet. Not fast, but it works. Read man ifconfig.

subject: GIF ???
q: Is there a program that can display GIF format pictures on an Apollo?
a: There are three that I know of: gif to postscript, gif to x, and gif to gpr. They all came off Usenet at some point, and the source is available if you ask. Sigh, it was posted here already.

subject: More on STDIN and EOF & Redirection
q: Is there a way to use stream_$errin on an Apollo? What is error input, and can I redirect standard input to a file while sending error input to the keyboard?
a: stream_$errin was a nice idea, but the SVID demands only three streams open at startup, and errin made four. COFF objects only get three now. Open /dev/tty instead and read and write that. Users can't redirect it, which is the price.

subject: nfs/rpc question
q: On Apollo 400s, execve and chdir hang on deeply nested NFS directories under NFS 2.1. Is NFS 2.2 any better?
a: Yes, 2.2 is much better and I'd highly recommend it. It's not the best NFS around by a long shot, but it beats 2.1 easily. What did you expect from 2.1?

subject: cp -rs vs. /com/cpt
q: On Apollo Domain/OS 10.3, cp -rs and /com/cpt treat files differently. After moving a tree with cp -rs, a program complained about invalid record length, but a /com/cpt copy works. Which should I use?
a: Be suspicious of copying Aegis-ism trees with plain cp. We use 'cp -rsp' to preserve date and time, but only with standard UNIX text and COFF files. Try the -oP options, which may handle the weird file types and ACLs. Otherwise, use /com/cpt.

subject: berzerkly lpd probs
q: On Domain 10.3 with the BSD environment, the lpd daemon dies within seconds of starting, and I have to delete lpd.lock. Is it fighting with prsvr and prmgr?
a: Probably it's your /usr/spool/lpd setup. If you've linked /usr/spool/lpd and are starting lpd on multiple nodes, it refuses, since it only wants one registered via NCS. Follow the Managing BSD System Software book. For once they got it right.

subject: DSP90 w/CDC 500MB Drives: Disk Errors
q: Our two DSP90 servers with CDC 500MB drives under SR9.7 get disk block header errors, and invol loses the bad blocks I add, then SYSBOOT isn't found. What do I do?
a: Stop using the SR9.7 invol. The newer ones can't handle an extended bad block list of about 200 entries, so they forget what you add. Replace all your invol programs with the SR9.2.3 one and redo the disks. Apollo broke a fix, naturally.

subject: HELP! rbak aborts
q: Running rbak to restore a directory on an Apollo SR9.704 system, it gets about halfway through a tape file and aborts with a heap_$get Heap table full error. What is happening and how do I get around it?
a: Known rbak bug on DN10000 nodes: if any component of the path is a single character, it dies with a segmentation fault partway through the restore. Apollo claims it's only the 10Ks, but who believes vendors? Look at your path names.

subject: 8 mm video cassets
q: We bought Sony 8 mm video cassettes for our Exabyte drive, though they aren't sold as data media. Are they reliable?
a: We've used Sony P5-90MP tapes for a year and a half with no problems, and they cost half as much. We scrap each tape after at most five uses. Data-grade marketing tax is mostly nonsense.

subject: function prototype mystery?
q: What do the &'s mean on arguments in the Apollo prototype for proc2_$get_info()? Passing addresses gets a type conflict, but passing the plain variable works.
a: It's pass by reference. You hand it the object and the compiler passes the address for you. Standard ANSI C, so quit blaming Apollo.

subject: News from ADUS on DN10k?
q: What is HP offering now to DN10000 owners as an upgrade or trade-in deal?
a: There's a trade-up program giving an extra 40% off the normal price of an HP 750, and you keep the DN10000. A 64 MB, 2.6 GB 750 drops from $95000 to $35000 Canadian. It ends October 31, 1991. Marketing at its finest.

subject: xterm via remsh - need a better font
q: When I start an xterm with remsh and display it on my Apollo, it uses a tiny unreadable font and wrong stty settings, and my .Xdefaults on the host seems ignored. What do I need?
a: Use xrdb on the Apollo to load your defaults into the server, so every xterm started there uses them unless overridden on the command line. That's the easy way. Works with plain rsh xterm -display too.

subject: load
q: Where can I find the load average on an Apollo DN3000? It's not in /dev/kmem, but uptime and xload know it.
a: Run nm on uptime. It calls proc1_$get_loadav(), which seems to take an array of 3 ints and maybe a status_$t. Experiment to find the scaling. It's an unreleased call, so it may break in a future release. Your problem.

subject: /com/cc questions and where can I get emacs
q: With the Aegis C compiler, how do I stop it from defining __STDC__, and how do I key off the -systype setting in the source?
a: For __STDC__, use -U__STDC__ or -A nansi, though the latter may have other effects. You're doing the systype thing backwards: define your own symbol like BSD and let it select the #systype and includes. And why write for both universes? Pick one.

subject: //gs printing
q: A lady with an Apple //GS and an ImageWriter II can print from Multiscribe GS, but old 8-bit programs like Newsroom won't print. Any suggestions?
a: Many programs, especially graphics ones, bang the hardware directly instead of using the slow official firmware calls, so the GS serial port breaks them. Try configuring for a //c port or a generic serial card, or else ask the publisher. Sigh, lazy programmers.

subject: ORCA/C and returning GSString's...
q: After a GS/OS DInfo call in ORCA/C, I can pull everything out except the device name. How do I copy the name from DInfoRec.devName, a GSString32, into my own string in a few simple steps?
a: It's a class-1 string, so just copy it. Use BlockMove from the Memory Manager, and cast the last parameter to a long, or use a C library routine like memcpy(). Not exactly rocket science, kid.

subject: //C --> Hard disks / SCSI devices
q: Are there any hard drives that work with the Apple //c, and any way to get a SCSI port on it?
a: As far as I know the ProApp 20 and 10 are the only hard disks that work with a //c. They also have a SCSI interface and can be shared with other computers. A+ ran an issue full of hard disks, so go read it.

subject: Apple ][c modem port
q: Can I hook a regular RS232 modem to the modem port on my Apple //c? Are there adapters that turn Apple's modem port into a standard RS232 port?
a: Yes. The //c port is a DIN plug, so you just need a cable going from the DIN to a DB25. JDR Microdevices' catalog has them, along with plenty of other junk. Honestly, check a catalog before asking the net.

subject: Apple //gs printer drivers
q: Does anyone have generic printer drivers for an Apple IIgs that work with an Epson FX-series printer? Apple only seems to support the ImageWriter and LaserWriter.
a: Get the C/Mac/GS printer interface from Orange Micro. It makes your FX printer, and a host of others, emulate an Imagewriter. Apple's driver support is poor, as you suspected.

subject: UNIDISK AND //GS?
q: Does the Unidisk 3.5 drive have serious compatibility problems with the Apple IIGS, as a dealer told a friend?
a: Nope, the dealer is just trying to sell a GS. UniDisk 3.5 drives work just fine on a GS. The newer unified drive's only extra is that it also works on a Macintosh. Typical dealer nonsense.

subject: RamFactor
q: Has anyone got words, good or bad, on the RamFactor versus RamWorks III for an Apple II? I already have an extended 80-column card and my most urgent need is more memory.
a: Get the RamFactor. It's bootable, works in the //gs, and can be battery backed for instant boot from the RAM disk, and it won't leave you with another orphan board. Downsides are no Appleworks/RAM disk partitioning and its odd, pricier RAM chips. RamWorks only makes sense if you lack an extended 80-column card.

subject: Apple II Hi-res picture conversion?
q: How can I convert Apple II Hi-res screen images into some format displayable on an IBM PC? I can get them into Hires memory and BSAVE them, but I don't want to write code to unscramble the pixel layout.
a: Nothing I know of for the IIe and below. On a IIGS, SHRConvert loads Apple II Hires, converts to Super Hires and saves a GIF, which VGIF and friends view on a PC. It's on the usual anonymous ftp sites. Go look.

subject: Saving SHR screen from p8
q: How can I save the SHR screen from ProDOS 8 so I can load it into a paint program? My saved file shows about six small copies of the screen and a messed up palette.
a: You forgot to linearize the screen buffer. Store $41 in $C029 before moving the picture from bank $E1, then save as type $C1. That fixes the tiny repeated copies. Turn the interlacing off, as it's the same mistake every time.

subject: ProDOS Version # - How does my program find out?
q: How can a program find out which version of ProDOS 8 it is running under?
a: You can't get the version string the user sees, like 1.1.1 or 1.8. Peek location $BFFF, KVERSION, instead. For ProDOS 8 1.8 it holds 8. That's all you get, so live with it.

subject: Pro-Beagle FTP?
q: How do I FTP to pro-beagle.cts.com? I get 'Unknown host'.
a: FTP is not magic. Both ends have to run it, and I don't think Proline software supports it, nor rlogin, finger, talk or the rest. So there's nothing to connect to. Sigh.

subject: GS modem port
q: How do the Apple IIGS modem port's mini-8 pins, with their plus and minus signals, correspond to an RS232 DB25 connector?
a: Use the minus pins, since the GS is RS-422 on the same serial controller as the Mac. Pins 3 and 5 are TxD and RxD, which map to 232 pins 2 and 3, and signal ground goes to ground. The handshake pins and the plus pins have no 232 equivalent. Cables should come with a swap-2-and-3 switch.

subject: problems downloading/unpacking "Fontasm"
q: I get a checksum error unpacking Fontasm 1.0 from the Apple2-L archive, and it crashes with a system error. I tried twice and with ShrinkIt. Does anyone have a good copy?
a: It's not you. The fontasm.A.sys16 file is bad. Somebody downloaded it four different ways and got nothing, and the original senders never answered. Typical archive neglect, so don't waste more time unpacking it.

subject: GS Shell Applications
q: I got ROGUE from an ftp site and it comes out as a GS Shell application. How do I run one of these from the Finder?
a: You don't. It's a *SHELL* application, so it says right on the tin that you need a shell to run it. Use APW if you own it, or ECP16, which is just as easy and free. Read the label next time.

subject: Applesoft Manual Question
q: I have an Apple IIGS and want to program in Applesoft with my kids. Are the Addison-Wesley manuals meant for the IIe or IIc also right for the GS?
a: Yes, those are the ones. Applesoft is still Applesoft, even on the GS. Don't overthink it.

subject: Weird cards and assorted other things
q: I picked up a strange card for my Apple II, a Heuristics, Inc. Model 20A-1, that looks like some kind of sampling card. What is it?
a: It's probably a voice recognition processor. Heuristics made at least one for the Apple II. It works like the spectrum display on a graphic equalizer, tuned for speech analysis. With the right software it does voice ID or voice commands. Look up your own hardware next time.

subject: Help needed with HR Graphics
q: I'm writing an Apple IIe game and can only find how to plot single hi-res pixels in machine language. Any books or articles on hi-res animation?
a: Look for a book something like Designing Arcade Level Graphics on the Apple II, by Jeffrey Stanton or Staunton. It picks up where the usual Apple graphics books stop around shape tables. Find the author in Books in Print.

subject: IIGS programming question
q: In my IIGS toolbox program a small window closes when the user presses the mouse button, but the main event loop then sees that same click. How do I keep it out of the event queue?
a: You can't stop the mouseDown from being queued. Sigh. Consume it from the queue instead: call GetNextEvent until it returns a mouseDown, rather than polling Button(0). Use $ffff as the mask and ignore the events you don't want.

subject: ROM 1 upgrades
q: Is Apple still offering the ROM 2 upgrade for a ROM 1 Apple IIGS, or am I stuck without GS/OS?
a: Where do I start. There is no ROM 2; ROM 01 is the latest upgrade for the original IIGS. ROM 03 has a different motherboard, so no upgrade. GS/OS runs on all of them, given about 1.25 MB of RAM. Read up before buying.

subject: ShrinkIt bug?
q: Is ShrinkIt 2.01 buggy? It stops extracting files from a Binary II file after about 30 files, when I tried to extract 75.
a: Yes, it's a known bug, and it's been discussed to death. The workaround is to just press return and it keeps going. Try reading the net before posting next time.

subject: wordperfect for the gs
q: Is WordPerfect available for the Apple IIgs, and what does it cost?
a: Apparently yes; a friend says it retails for $199. Whether it's 5.25 or 3.5 inch disks, nobody knows, though 3.5 is the obvious guess on a GS. That's secondhand, so check a dealer.

subject: IIGS and CD/ROM
q: Is it true it costs about $2200 to master a CD, with the per-disc cost then around $4 in volume?
a: Depends on the shop. The best deal I found was $1600 for 1000 discs complete, from Phillips Dupont Optical, which is about $600 for mastering plus $1 a disc. That's half what I was quoted a year ago, because the plants have serious overcapacity.

subject: FPE/GS
q: Is the data path between the FPE floating-point card and the cpu of an Apple IIgs 8 or 16 bits? Does the GS fetch data from memory 16 bits at a time?
a: Eight bits. The FPE is a slot card, and the Apple II has an 8 bit data bus, so all memory and slot access is 8 bits at a time. The 65816 is 16 bit only like the 8088: 16 bit registers, 8 bit bus. Marketing noise.

subject: backup programs
q: Is there a hard drive backup program that works with the data and resource forks supported by GS/OS 5.0?
a: Try Glen Bredon's ProSel-16 backup program. It backs up resource files, extended files, and does error correction too. Pretty cool, and ShrinkIt/GS won't get anything like it anytime soon.

subject: Mac PICT ---> Apple PICT
q: Is there a reasonable way to convert Macintosh PICT files to a format the Apple IIGS paint module in AWGS can load?
a: Not that anyone knows of. PICT is a series of QuickDraw commands, and Mac QuickDraw and IIGS QuickDraw II differ structurally. A converter would be tricky to write, and nobody has done it. APDA sells the PICT notes, and IIGS Tech Note #46 covers the other format.

subject: comma input
q: Is there a way to have the INPUT statement in Applesoft BASIC not give ?EXTRA IGNORED when a comma is typed along with the other characters?
a: Stop using INPUT. Read the keyboard one character at a time with GET and tack each character onto an input string yourself. ON ERR won't catch that error anyway. The manuals even had an input-anything routine, if you'd bother to look.

subject: (none)
q: Is there an AT command to set the interrupts on my Datalink 1200/2400 modem for my Apple, so I don't have to open the computer to change them?
a: No. The interrupt setting is a DIP switch or jumper on the card, so it's purely hardware and no software command will change it. Some software can fake interrupts, but the card stays as it is.

subject: Adapter Needed
q: Is there an adapter to connect an RGB monitor to the Apple IIc?
a: Yes. Computer Direct sells one for $19.95, or any local adapter cable shop can make one. The poster said it works great and the colors are much sharper. Not hard, people.

subject: Multitasking & the IIgs
q: Multitasking on the IIgs seems nightmarish, since neither the tools nor GS/OS are reentrant and applications can do anything with the I/O space. Is it really workable?
a: You're assuming multitasking needs preemption. It doesn't. Voluntary relinquishment of the CPU works fine. The AT&T 630 terminal I'm typing on multitasks with no preemptive scheduling and no memory protection. Think before you call things folly.

subject: More GS Source Examples??
q: On the Apple IIGS, can I make a window with data height greater than $FFFF, and how do I do hierarchical menus, tear-off menus, and menus inside a window?
a: For tall windows, do what MacApp does: keep your position as a longint in your own data and map the top 16 significant bits to coordinates and scrollbar values. Menus in a window are covered in IIGS Technote #3. Hierarchical and tear-off menus need serious reprogramming; no tricks exist.

subject: Appleworks GS communications module
q: The AppleWorks GS communications module shows a garbled font that looks like Shaston 14 or 18 point, with overlapping characters in the edit line, session record and status bar. How do I fix it?
a: You don't have the right font. It needs Monaco 9, or it scales Shaston-16 down and does a miserable job. AWGS ships with Monaco 9, but System 5.0 doesn't, so copy the font off your original system disk. RTFM.

subject: ROM 03
q: What happens if I plug a ROM 03 chip from a new Apple IIGS into an old IIGS with only 256K on the motherboard? Does it check it's in the right machine?
a: ROM 03 machines use two ROM chips, so you can plug in one or the other but not both. As for what happens, it would certainly void your warranty. Think before you start swapping chips.

subject: System Error $1101
q: What is System Error $1101 on the Apple IIgs? It has something to do with the loader but the Toolbox Ref doesn't list it. What about GS/OS Error $0002?
a: System error $1101 is a Segment or Entry not found error from the loader. Nobody had an answer for GS/OS $0002 in the replies. Next time, look harder at the manual before asking.

subject: reference manual/6502 specs
q: Where can I get specs for the 6502, and the reference manual for the Apple IIe? Can I order directly from Apple?
a: Try a local electronics distributor for 6502 data books from NCR, Rockwell and Western Design Center. WDC only sells direct. Jameco sells specs for 50 cents, with a $20 minimum order. For the IIe reference, try an Apple dealer first. Do your legwork.

subject: Split of divisions?
q: Why did Apple start shipping tech notes separately to Mac and Apple II developers? Is it money, or does it signal a split of the divisions?
a: The Apple II developers asked for it. They were tired of paying the full fee and getting mostly Mac stuff to throw away, so splitting the mailings lets the cost come down. It's no sign of a company split. Quit reading tea leaves.

subject: BASIC.SYSTEM v1.4 (was Re: BASIC.SYSTEM v1.3 Bug)
q: Will BASIC.SYSTEM 1.4 display and allow lowercase in filenames, like ProDOS 8 1.8 does?
a: Nope. ProDOS 8 1.8 was not changed to really allow lowercase filenames. It just doesn't barf on the bits in a subdirectory entry that tell GS/OS's ProDOS FST which letters are lowercase. Read GS/OS Technical Note #8 before asking again.

subject: GSRam chips
q: Will the RAM chips from my GSRam card work in my old Apple II Memory Expansion card, which I figure uses the same 32K chips?
a: Your premise is off. The chips in the GS RAM are 256k by 1, 120 ns recommended, not 32K per chip, unless the universe just inverted. Check your facts before swapping chips around.

subject: SX212 info sought
q: Can the Atari SX212 modem connect directly to the 8-bit without an interface, does it come with a cable and terminal program, and will it work with Chameleon?
a: Yes, it has an SIO connector and works with an R-verter type handler. The cable comes packaged with SX-Express, which is sold separately. Chameleon is unconfirmed, so use it via an 850 like any Hayes-compatible modem. Read the spec sheet.

subject: US DOUBLER SLOWER SOMETIMES??
q: Does SpartaDos with the US Doubler really read and write slower on non-binary files, like Action source code, than other DOSes?
a: No. The speed comes from track buffering and custom disk formatting, not file type. As long as standard CIO calls are used, it's fast. SpartaDos is the only DOS that gets the special interleave right. The rumour is nonsense.

subject: MEDIT/AMAC under SpartaDOS
q: Has anyone used AMAC and MEDIT under SpartaDOS? It chokes and assumes the default drive is 1.
a: Never got it to work. It reads the first file and hangs on the first INCLUDE, probably because AMAC opens more than 7 files and twiddles low-level I/O. It does run under MYDOS. The drive 1 fixation is the copy protection, naturally.

subject: Word Processor question, using At 800 and 1025
q: How can I print a file that is too big for my AtariWriter cartridge's memory? Also, is there a public domain word processor better than AtariWriter?
a: AtariWriter has a merge file command, I think ^V. At the end of the first piece, give it D:FILE and chain the next one. Best PD editor is Textpro. The best editor overall is probably Paper Clip. Read your manual.

subject: Atari 800 Monitor Connection
q: I got an old Atari 800 and want to hook it to my Commodore monitor through the five-pin DIN monitor port. What are the pin-outs for that port?
a: Pin 1 is composite luminance, not connected. Pin 2 is ground, pin 3 audio out, pin 4 composite video, and pin 5 composite chroma, also not connected. On a mono monitor the picture may look skipped, so try video on pin 1 or 5. Read a manual sometime.

subject: Adding a Hard Drive
q: I salvaged a 10M Tandon full-height hard drive. Can I use it with my Atari 800XL, and what interface and DOS do I need?
a: Yes, it's possible. Get an ICD Multi I/O or Black Box interface, and the Black Box is likely what you want. MyDOS and SpartaDOS handle it. You'll also need a SCSI controller, and it'll cost you, lots of bux.

subject: Ethics in programming....
q: Is it ethical or legal to distribute, for free, commented source code I made by disassembling a copyrighted program like TextPro 3.2R when I can't find the authors?
a: Don't. A copyrighted program belongs to its author, and disassembling the binaries, commenting them and handing them out violates the copyright. There may be good reasons the source isn't public domain. Without the author's permission, keep it to yourself.

subject: 8-bit VT100 emulator needed
q: Is there an 80 column VT100 emulator for the Atari 8-bit? I have a 130XE and an SX212 modem.
a: Kermit65 does exactly that, and someone posted a version that works with the SX212. There's also a vt10sq.arc on CompuServe that does 80 columns with no extra hardware, though it botches graphics control characters. Sigh, search before asking.

subject: Indus Info Wanted
q: My Indus GT drive for the Atari 8-bit needs a new belt, and I've lost track of Indus. Do they still exist, and where can I get it repaired in New York City?
a: Probably not still around. But the Indus mechanism is nearly identical to the one in the 1050, made by Tandon, so anyone who repairs Atari disk drives should be able to fix it. Hardly a tragedy, so quit fretting.

subject: Z mag?
q: What is Z-mag? Someone mentioned it and I'm still clueless.
a: Zmag is a weekly online Atari newsletter, distributed to BBSs for years by its editor, who did it for free. A printed version with advertising now goes out to Atari user groups. Sigh, it used to be posted here weekly.

subject: ATR8000 info wanted
q: What is an ATR 8500, as mentioned in the MyDOS posts? I have an ATR8000.
a: It's a smaller ATR8000 with a DMA controller and an SIO chip in place of the acre of TTL used for disk and serial ports. It handled higher data rates and had more accurate RS232 baud rates. Software support had dried up when it shipped, of course.

subject: Monitor question
q: What monitors do you recommend for an Atari 8-bit, color preferably, but I'd like to hear about mono too?
a: I've run a used NEC green-screen for years, cost $80, and 80 columns come out clear and crisp. Catch: if chroma is hooked up, colors show as line shading and 80 columns is unreadable. Disconnect chroma, but then colors don't differ. Blame the blue default background.

subject: Daisy Dot II
q: Where can I get Daisy Dot II? A company address or a BBS number would do nicely.
a: Check the Antic issue with Newsroom for the 8-bit Ataris on the cover, around August. It has an article on DaisyDot II and an address. Honestly, dig through your back issues before asking the net.

subject: Atari 800 Power
q: Where can I get a power supply for my Atari 800? Radio Shack and an Atari store both said it's hopeless.
a: All you need is a transformer delivering about 9V AC at 3A. If you still have the old brick, crack it open with a vise to break the glue joint, replace the blown 3A fuse, and glue it back. Or try Best Electronics. Hopeless, my foot.

subject: Crashing Megafile at STE
q: A friend sold a Megafile 30 to another friend with an STE, and now the combination crashes frequently. AHDI 1.7 is in use. Is there a known problem?
a: Try AHDI 3.01, and skip 3.00, which is buggy and destructive. Back up first. Otherwise the drive may have been ruined by shipping without parking it, or the STE has the DMA hardware problem, which nobody noticed without a hard drive.

subject: gcc ?????
q: After installing gcc on my Atari ST, hello.c works with printf, but adding fprintf(stdout, ...) fails with undefined symbol _stdout. Why does this happen?
a: You've got a library and include file mismatch. There are two families of gcc libraries. The older one from gcc 1.23 has _printf_guts and stdout, and the 1.37 family has _doprnt and _iob[]. You're probably pairing headers from one with a gnu.olb from the other.

subject: A few questions on CAD 3D II and Cyber-animation
q: Can CAD 3D II use more than 1 meg of memory for more and bigger objects, and can Cyber-animations be played from a hard disk?
a: Yes to both. CAD 3D II is pretty crippled in 1 meg unless you strip nearly everything out of C:\AUTO. And there's a program on Compuserve that plays big .DLT animation files straight off the hard drive. Buy the memory already.

subject: Atari Minix and ICD
q: Can I run Minix on an Atari ST with an ICD host adapter when Minix only sees 4 partitions but ICD allows more? Is a layout with TOS, Minix and Spectre partitions past the fourth a problem?
a: Works fine. Someone runs Minix and Spectre on an ICD adapter with the same layout, just one Minix partition. Maybe you could rebuild Minix for more than 4 partitions, but nobody's tried, and I wouldn't depend on it. Keep it simple.

subject: ST to Multisync Adapters
q: Can anyone recommend the Practical Solutions Monitor Master as an ST to multisync adapter? Does it have an audio jack?
a: Wrong box entirely. The Monitor Master has no multisync support. All it does is switch between two Atari monitors. Read the spec sheet before buying, and don't trust the marketing blurb.

subject: gcc & parse error in stdio.h
q: Compiling a hello world with gcc on the Atari ST gives "stdio.h:60 : parse error at null character". How do I get rid of it?
a: This comes up now and then. Define __NO_INLINE__, or whatever the macro is called, and the problem goes away. I think it's absent from the new mintlib. Stop hacking up stdio.h.

subject: Looking for Go
q: Does anybody know of a good Go game for the Atari ST, PD, shareware or commercial, with rules, a few strategies, and a computer player?
a: There's a GNUGO.ARC file at terminator, the atari.archive site, so go fetch it. Or try Goliath, which won last year's computer Go world championship, if you're willing to pay for it. Works in high and medium rez.

subject: Looking for STMIDIEX.LZH or MIDIEXCL.LZH!!!
q: Does anyone have STMIDIEX.LZH or MIDIEXCL.LZH, which stores system exclusive files from MIDI devices? Also, is WINXV13.LZH, which allows up to 127 windows, any good?
a: Don't bother with the MIDI one. I got it off GEnie and it only runs on German TOS 1.4, not US TOS 1.4. Sigh. It can go in atari.archive if anyone's curious. Nobody said anything about the window thing.

subject: adress of Mark Williams Co.
q: Does anyone have an email address for Mark Williams Co. in Chicago, for C compiler support and new ST products?
a: Don't bother. Mark Williams is out of the ST compiler business, as one caller was told. They never liked the ST numbers. Their compiler is non-ANSI but still fine for portable Unix-style code, though not for commercial ST products.

subject: Atari SC212 modem: yea or nay?
q: Does the Atari SC212 1200bps modem have a standard DB25 RS232 port? Is it any good for $25?
a: Yes, it has a DB25 port plus an SIO port for the old 8-bit Ataris. One user's had it three years with no trouble, apart from the dead internal speaker. It's only 1200, not 2400, so don't expect miracles for $25.

subject: Magic Sac Compatible with LightSpeed Pascal Yet?
q: Does the updated LightSpeed Pascal run on the Magic Sac, or should I go with Turbo Pascal?
a: No. Both LightSpeed C and Pascal need the 128K or later ROMs, so they won't run on the current 64K ROM Magic Sac. The Mac II update had nothing to do with ROM requirements. Turbo Pascal doesn't need them and runs fine.

subject: Large format graphics on the ST (specifcally .GIF).
q: Has anybody seen a program for the ST that loads large format pictures like GIFs and lets you scroll around to see the whole picture?
a: Yes, the GemView accessory does that. Picture comes up in a standard GEM window and you use the scroll bars to see the parts off the screen. I think you can ftp it from atari.archive.umich.edu. Sigh, go look before asking next time.

subject: Mega Mega?
q: Has anyone expanded an Atari Mega ST beyond 4 MB for things like GNU Emacs, big RAM disks, Scheme and Smalltalk? Is there any commercial expansion?
a: Going to 8 MB is easy enough if you can build a RAM board for the 68000. The catch is getting the DMA controller to handle the upper 4 MB. Germans sell expansion boards, but they're very expensive, around 689 pounds for 4 MB in England, chips extra. Typical.

subject: Using a Seagate ST225 w/ ATARI 520ST
q: Has anyone used a Seagate ST225 hard drive off an IBM with a 520ST?
a: Of course. Atari shipped plenty of them in the old SH204 shoebox, along with a host adapter, power supply and an Adaptec 4000A controller. I swapped the adapter for ICD's. Hardly exotic.

subject: Question: send mail from Internet to UUCP
q: How can I send mail from an Internet node to a UUCP address like Darek@microsoft.UUCP? What do I type at the To: prompt?
a: Depends on your site's mail setup, and on how competent your admin is. Try user@host.uucp first. For brain-dead systems, route through uunet, like darek%microsoft.uucp@uunet.uu.net, which covers about 98 percent of cases.

subject: 520ST : 2 urgent though simple questions
q: How can a 520ST be expanded to 1024k or more, and can it use a serial printer without a parallel-to-serial interface?
a: Piggyback soldering only works with 256K chips, and since 1M chips are cheaper, just buy a board that takes the 1M. As for the printer, select the serial port as your printer port and you have a serial printer. Not rocket science.

subject: TeX'ing gulam.tex
q: How do I TeX gulam.tex? It says it can't find texinfo.tex, which the first line includes.
a: texinfo.tex is the macro package distributed with the Gnu software documentation. If you have the emacs sources it's probably already on your machine. Otherwise ftp it from prep.ai.mit.edu or atari.archive.umich.edu in gnustuff/tos/Doc.

subject: ESDI hard disk on 520ST
q: How do I attach an ESDI hard disk to my Atari 520ST's hard disk port? I have a Micropolis ESDI drive and an Emulex MD21 adapter.
a: You need a host adapter, which interfaces the Atari to SCSI. For an ESDI drive you also need an Adaptec SCSI-ESDI adapter. BMS makes a host adapter, the BMS-200. Call them and see what they recommend.

subject: .PC1 files....
q: How do I view .PC1 files on the Atari ST, and where can I get a utility for it?
a: They're the Degas Elite compressed form of .PI1 files. Load them into Degas Elite, which converts between .PIx and .PCx. There may be PD viewers too. Read the extension, people.

subject: SWITCHBACK
q: How does the Switchback product for the Atari ST work, and which programs won't work with it?
a: It hooks an interrupt off the printer port, and a button press triggers a TSR that saves the whole RAM image for restoring later. It fails on programs that abuse the printer port or load into all of memory, like boot-disk games that never reach TOS.

subject: Drawing on the ST
q: I find the mouse impossible to draw with on my 1040ST. Is there a software package or a drawing pad or better mouse that makes drawing bearable?
a: Get a graphics tablet. The ProTablet ST from Quantum Microsystems replaces the mouse in just about every package via a little desk accessory driver. Runs about $400. Sigh, pay up if you want to draw.

subject: HARD DRIVES FOR STs
q: I have an Atari 1040ST and want a cheap, large hard disk. Can I just buy a Seagate SCSI drive from an ad, or must it be made for the ST?
a: Buy an ICD host adapter, a bare SCSI drive and a power supply. Seagate and Miniscribe drives work, and the adapter comes with all the software. Set the drive select to zero. Choose the adapter first, then the drive. SCSI beats the rest, obviously.

subject: KERMIT!?
q: I have an Atari ST with 512K and need to download files from a VAX/VMS 5.2 system, and my xmodem routines don't work there. Where can I find a Kermit for the ST and the VAX?
a: Use Uniterm on the ST; it includes Kermit among other protocols and works fine against VMS 5.2. For the VAX, ask your system manager, it may already be installed. Otherwise get it off a DECUS tape or another VAX site. Redistribution is unrestricted, so quit whining.

subject: Languages!!!! (cont.)
q: I heard some versions of GFA BASIC are in the public domain. Is that true, and where can I get one legally without paying?
a: NO. There are no versions of GFA BASIC in the public domain. Being published in a magazine doesn't make it so. Pay for the January 1989 issue of START, or buy version 3.0 from ANTIC. Get your facts straight.

subject: ELVIS questions
q: I installed Elvis on my 1040ST and get "can't read back C:\tmp\w._e_" even though I set the temp directory to F:\tmp. What am I doing wrong?
a: Dunno, nobody here got Elvis working either. Use STEVIE 3.9 instead; it's on atari.archive and has worked fine for weeks. Elvis on an ST, sigh.

subject: Basepage problems
q: I load a C program from GFA-basic with EXEC and call the address at basepage+8, but the computer crashes. What am I doing wrong?
a: Stop hand-rolling it. The GFA 3.xx compiler can link GFA modules with Turbo C modules directly. Just use the option line $X followed by the function name. RTFM next time.

subject: MIDI beginner, STart disk, Sampsyn
q: I'm a MIDI beginner with an ST. Is there a cheap or public domain sequencer, and are the programs on the STart magazine disk public domain?
a: STart disk programs are not public domain, except ST Writer. Super Conductor was a commercial Michtron program, so buy the disk. For cheap sequencers, there are PD ones, Alchimie Jr. for mono and a color one called MIDISEQ, or Dr. T's Tiger Cub for under $100.

subject: Object Tree Help Wanted
q: I'm building a GEM dialog box with a G_BOX root and a G_BOXTEXT child. If I add more G_TEXT objects inside the box, are they children of the G_BOX, and what Obj_Next, Obj_Head and Obj_Tail values do they get?
a: Yes, anything inside the box is a child of the root, and the G_BOXTEXT button is just another sibling beside them. Numeric order doesn't matter much. Better yet, use a resource construction program instead of building GEM resources by hand like a masochist.

subject: What archiving format?
q: I'm confused about archive formats like arc, lharc and zoo. Is one more efficient or reliable than the others, and which should I use for my files?
a: Arc is fast and reliable but can't pull single files out of a directory. Zoo is slower and bigger but very reliable and flexible, with versions and comments. Lharc compresses best but is slow, unreliable and comes in incompatible versions. Just say NO. Read the zoo manual.

subject: Kermit
q: I'm getting errors from Kermit on my Atari ST with my .kermrc file, and I think it dislikes my setting packets to 1024. What should the file include?
a: Sigh. The ST Kermit software really sucks, and that's from someone at the home of Kermit. Skip it and use UniTerm 2.0e, a far better implementation and much easier to deal with. It's freeware, so look at your nearest anon FTP site.

subject: "C" on the ST - Public Domain
q: I'm looking for a good C compiler for the Atari ST, preferably public domain, and one that would accept Turbo Pascal stuff from IBM ports.
a: A C compiler that swallows Turbo Pascal wouldn't be good, it'd be magic. Try gcc from atari.archive.umich.edu. Otherwise Prospero C is rock solid, about $100, and the docs alone are worth it.

subject: looking for matrix math package
q: I'm looking for a matrix math package for the Atari ST that handles matrices with complex entries. What is it called and where can I find it?
a: There's a shareware program called MATRICKS.TOS with a 22K manual. Contact its author for the current version and whether it handles complex numbers. Or get Numerical Recipes in C and bolt on a complex struct, if you can't be bothered. Not hard.

subject: External 360k 5.25" floppy
q: I've got a 360k 5.25 inch floppy with cable for my Atari ST. The drive spins when I access B: but asks for a disk in A:. How do I get the ST to use it?
a: Remove the resistor terminator pack, and swap the 150 ohm resistor tied to +5V for a 1K, since the Atari needs 0V. Run PCF554.PRG to slow drive B to 6ms, format with DC Format rather than the desktop, and fiddle with the jumpers. Hardware hacking isn't for the timid.

subject: RTX question
q: Is it possible with RTX on the Atari ST to create processes within a GEM application and redirect stdout to a self-written device driver, say for two shells running concurrently in two windows?
a: Yes, it's possible. That's exactly how VSH Manager works. You can also fake multitasking GEM with messages, or have apps send GEM requests by remote call to a server that handles the process-sensitive GEM stuff. Think a little before asking.

subject: Mac-->Atari Sound Converters
q: Is there an FTP site with a utility to convert Mac format sound files into Atari ST format?
a: You don't need one. Take the Mac .data file, get it onto your ST, and try it with play.prg to get the playback rate right. Then use it with Digital Keyclick, Beep and Digivec. Many archive sounds are Mac samples anyway. Sigh.

subject: TOS 1.4 upgrade problem
q: My 1040STF with TOS 1.0 was told its board can't take the TOS 1.4 upgrade. There are 6 socketed ROM chips. Can I just buy the 6-chip set and install it myself?
a: There are two sets: a 2-chip set for the original Megas and a few 1040s, and a 6-chip set for everything else. Nothing stops you using the 6-chip set. The dealer probably just didn't want to sell a set without making a profit.

subject: bizarre problem
q: My 520ST shows nothing on a monochrome monitor, though I hear keyclicks. The mono works on my Mega2 and the color works on the 520. What's wrong?
a: Your 520 is broken. Likely the connector is damaged, since the mono signal is on a different pin, or a monitor is asserting a signal making it think it's always color. Or the mono signal dies on the motherboard path. Go fix it.

subject: SM124 monitor down, help!
q: My Atari SM124 monitor keeps blowing replacement 2.2uF 25V capacitors after a couple of hours, and the originals were physically bigger. Any suggestions?
a: Keep the value and use a higher working voltage, say 75 to 100 WV, which should hold up better. Going larger is usually fine unless the cap is for timing. If it still fries, something else is killing it. Basic electronics, folks.

subject: Help! Hot memory?
q: My ST with a 2MB expansion board locks up with vertical lines and eleven bombs after about 1.5 hours, and on reboot I only have half a meg. What's wrong?
a: You most likely have a bad bit in the add-on memory, one bit in each of the 16 chips. TOS sizes memory at boot, sees it doesn't read back, and truncates to half a meg. Write a little C program to find the bad bit, then replace that chip. Ancient hardware does that.

subject: gnu again !!
q: My email request to the atari archive server for gnustuff files got nothing. Is something wrong with my send request?
a: The file is no longer there. The gnustuff directory is being rearranged and changes almost daily. Check the index before requesting anything: send gnustuff/Index gets just that directory's index. Read the index first; saves everyone grief.

subject: Problems using Overscan with SM125
q: My overscan mod on a 260ST with an SM125 shows strange bit patterns and vertical lines and the keys change them oddly. Is the SM125 incompatible, or is something else wrong?
a: Common problem. Check the transistor: a near equivalent just gave diagonal black stripes over a distorted desktop. Use the specified part and keep the leads as short as possible. Cutting corners on a soldering job, tsk.

subject: FILE I/O
q: On the Atari ST, Fseek and fseek, Fread and fread seem to do the same thing. Is there a preferred choice, and is there something subtle I'm missing?
a: Capital F are GEMDOS OS calls, like Unix read and lseek. Little f are stdio library calls. For portable code use the little f's, but GEMLIB's have debilitating bugs and newline translation. For control, use capital F. Parameter order differs too, naturally.

subject: Misc Questions
q: On the Atari ST, how can I find out how much memory is left while a program runs, preferably without mallocing until it fails? Also, what are .cnf files?
a: Just call freemem = Malloc(-1L). It returns the largest free block, so a fragmented heap gives less than you'd expect. Nobody answered the .cnf part, so figure that one out yourself.

subject: Gemini with Quick ST 2.x
q: Quick ST II with Gemini keeps stdio from appearing in the Mupfel window and takes over the whole screen. Is this incompatibility being fixed?
a: Use Quick ST 2.1G or 2.2G. The G versions don't hook the GEMDOS text output functions, so redirection works, and you still get the text speedup. If you haven't upgraded to 2.1 or higher, you're missing out.

subject: TOS 1.4 bug?
q: Since installing TOS 1.4 on my 1040ST, double-clicking a GEM application sometimes gives me the show/print/cancel dialog instead of running it, and it works the second time. Anyone else seen this? Any fix?
a: Yes, it's a known desktop bug. It seems tied to the full path name length, around 18 or 30 characters depending on who you ask. Rename the file or directory so the path isn't that length and it mostly goes away. Atari hasn't said a word, naturally.

subject: Read bits and ST files/directories
q: The directories from a botched installation are all read only on my Atari ST and I have no utility to remove them. Is there a chmod for the ST that works on directories?
a: The gulam shell supports chmod +w file, which sets the write access bit. Try that. Mark Williams msh wasn't going to cut it, was it?

subject: Source-level debuggers for C?
q: What C compilers for the Atari ST that are still supported come with source-level debuggers, and do any also work at the executable level?
a: Laser C comes with a fantastic source and assembly level debugger, ldb, so good the package is worth buying for it alone. I hear Turbo C 2.00 has a good source level debugger too. That's all I know, and the docs may be in German. Tough.

subject: What is the 520STe?
q: What is the 520STe? I thought Atari only released the STE in a 1 meg version.
a: It's the STe with half a meg of RAM. They're real, and some even came bundled with games. Better buy if you plan to upgrade to 4MB: cheaper than the 1040, and you only waste two 256K SIMMs instead of four. Not exactly hard to figure out.

subject: ascii code
q: What is the ASCII code for the Delete key? I need it to set key codes in a term program running in Mac mode on my Atari ST.
a: Delete is ascii 127 and backspace is ascii 8. Any idiot with an ASCII chart could tell you that.

subject: VideoKey
q: What power supply comes with the Practical Solutions VideoKey? I lost mine and the manual doesn't say.
a: It's a 12VDC, 300 mA plug-in transformer. Get a replacement from Radio Shack or a similar store. Honestly, keep track of your parts.

subject: formatting with 10 sectors under tos 1.4
q: What's a good formatting program for 10 sectors per track disks under TOS 1.4? My disks formatted with Twister or Neodesk stop working after a short time.
a: DC Formatter 3.2 does 82 tracks and 10 sectors fine under TOS 1.4, no problems. If your disks still die, it could be a whacky drive or just really bad disks. Not what you wanted to hear, I know.

subject: MINIX
q: What's the status of the MINIX port to the Atari ST?
a: It'll be available from Prentice Hall around June 88. It's being wrapped up now into a set of diskettes for reproduction. Patience, children.

subject: Whatever happened to comp.sys.atari.tech?
q: Whatever happened to comp.sys.atari.tech? People crosspost to it but I don't see it here. Can someone re-create it?
a: Wrong name. It's comp.sys.atari.st.tech. It passed, got created, and should be on your system. If it isn't, bug your local sysadmin or a net.god. Honestly, check the name before demanding groups be re-created.

subject: UW on the ST...
q: Where can I find the Unix side of UnixWindows (UW) for my Atari ST setup? I only found the Atari side.
a: It's in the same directory as the Atari UW stuff: uw.tar.Z, a compressed tar file with the complete Unix source and documentation. The Atari source and binaries are in a separate arc file. Look around the directory before begging for binaries.

subject: patches to TOS 1.4
q: Where can I find the patches for TOS 1.4, like poolfix, and which is the latest version?
a: Get PoolFix 4, it's been posted here before. The patches are on the panarthea archive server as volume8/rainbow, and hopefully under Binaries at atari.archive.umich.edu. There's also an Atari patch program from Rainbow TOS Fix. Use the archives.

subject: GULAM with german keyboard
q: Where can I get a version of GULAM that respects the German keyboard?
a: Grab 'keyfix', posted to comp.binaries.atari.st, with source in the sources group. Run it on gulam.prg and it writes a gulamnew.prg for your keyboard. No need to hunt for a special version, for crying out loud.

subject: Flight Sims.
q: Which flight sims for the Atari ST don't come on copy-protected floppies that can't be backed up? Falcon was recommended.
a: Sublogic's Flight Simulator II has no protection at all and installs on a hard disk. Falcon and F-19 Stealth Fighter were also suggested, though protection wasn't confirmed for them. Proflight is new and feature-packed, but its protection is unknown. Check before you buy.

subject: Question on use of Interleaves
q: Which interleave should I use when formatting a hard disk on the Atari ST for the best response time, and how can I tell what interleave my disk already has?
a: Use 1 with the Adaptec 4000 controller most MFM systems have. With 17 sectors a track, interleave 1 uses all 17 while anything else uses only 16, so you get more capacity. The controller caches, so there's little penalty. Nobody answered the detection bit.

subject: resource files
q: Why do some ST programs use .rsc resource files that need a configure program, instead of cleartext files that you edit with an editor?
a: Because those resource files come from a resource editor and the user has no say in the internal format. There's a standard GEM layout: a tree structure describing dialog boxes, menus and so on. It's not a text config file. Read up on GEM.

subject: GEMDOS bug (attn -- Alex)
q: Why does GEMDOS fail to find files in subdirectories after I swap disks, returning error -33? Fischer's workaround doesn't work for me.
a: It's a GEMDOS bug. The directory-structure cache didn't check for media change and assumed its internal tree was still right, mostly when the first disk's root, FAT and so on are small enough to cache. Fixed in the upcoming new ROMs. Typical.

subject: Gemini on old STs
q: Why doesn't Gemini work on TOS versions before 1.2, and is there any chance of it being released for older TOS?
a: Gemini uses the BIOS character I/O vectors that only appeared in TOS 1.2, so there never will be a version for older TOS. Sigh. You can run MUPFEL.PRG, the standalone shell, with VENUS.PRG, the standalone desktop, on TOS 1.0.

subject: GEM HELP
q: With GEM, how do I put the mouse at a specified location on the screen, and how do I bound it to a box?
a: initmous does it, but I wouldn't recommend it. Every program using it drove me crazy because the mouse runs out of room and you have to pick it up and put it back down. Check the position and re-init if you exceed the limits, but there's probably a better way.

subject: Fast Raster Routines Needed.
q: How are the bit planes set up in the Atari TT graphics modes? In 320x480x8, does one byte equal one pixel?
a: No. The 320x480x8 mode is just an extension of the 2- and 4-plane modes. Two bytes hold plane 1 for the first 16 pixels, then two bytes of plane 2, and so on. Chunky pixels would have been nice, but Atari didn't care.

subject: How can I format floppies fast?
q: How can I format a 720k floppy fast on the ST? Using the xbios commands, 10 tracks take about 6 seconds, and playing with interleave only made it worse.
a: Your timing's about right. The floppy spins 5 times a second and each track takes about 3 rotations: format, verify, and a missed timing mark after the head step. Also the Atari driver always waits a 30ms head-settling delay. A smarter driver would skip it.

subject: Default Font specs....
q: How can I reliably get the width and height of the default system font in GEM, so I can scale my resource file coordinates in both ST color and mono? vqt_attributes fails under MultiDesk.
a: Look at rsrc_obfix(). It does everything you need. Or do what I always did: call graf_handle() for the character width and height and fix up the resource with those. Honestly, this is in the docs you say you read.

subject: Ste fix for 2.5 meg upgrade?
q: I upgraded my STe to 2.5 megs with SIMMs in slots 1 and 3 and the 256k ones in 2 and 4, but a memory checker says I have 4 meg. Where do I find the simmfix program that is supposed to fix this?
a: SIMMFIX is only 248 bytes and the machine won't always recognize it as a program, so you get TOS Error #35 now and then. Skip the hack: go with two megs or four. And SIMM prices are rising, so quit dawdling.

subject: TOS 1.4
q: I was given a disk copy of TOS 1.4 as a developers version. Can I blow it into EPROMs and plug them into my TOS 1.2 ST, and what size are the chips for a two-ROM set?
a: The disk version can't be used for a ROM copy, and I hear it's very buggy. The ROM version is position dependent code. A two-chip set takes 1 meg PROMs, not EPROMs, since I doubt you can get 28 pin 1 meg EPROMs. Sigh.

subject: Resource Construction Kit for Prospero C
q: Is there a resource construction utility that works with Prospero C on the Atari ST?
a: Prospero sells one in their Toolkit, which is just K-resource, and you can get that from Prospero or Kuma. Really, any resource construction program will work. Someone posted a good one here too, if you bothered searching.

subject: Ram expansion questions....
q: My 520ST has an AERCO Easie ST solderless RAM board giving 1 Meg. How many 1M-bit chips do I need to expand it to 2+ meg?
a: The board's docs say you install 16 TC511000P drams, 120 ns or faster, to get a total of 2.5 meg. Dig out the manual first next time. Word is the board isn't exactly plug and go, so don't expect miracles.

subject: Cookie Jar
q: What is a cookie-jar on the Atari ST? I can't work out its function from the messages discussing it.
a: It's an area of memory where any program drops its cookie so others can scan for it. Resident code uses it to see it's already installed and not load twice, or to check a needed resident program is there. Sigh, read the docs.

subject: <None>
q: Why are there two Portable Math Libraries for GCC on the Atari ST, PML and PML16, and what is the difference?
a: I'd guess one is 32 bit and the other 16 bit, meaning the int size. Check the docs that came with them instead of asking the net. Sigh.

subject: Ack! STe DMA sound problems?
q: Why do my sign-converted .SND files play with a 2.2-second burst of noise at the start on my STe, when MOD players sound fine?
a: Sounds like your .SND files have some screwy header that isn't raw sound data. Either convert them correctly or strip the offending bytes. Verify with a known good sound file from the archive. Check your files before blaming the hardware.

subject: COFF & ELF
q: Can I convert COFF C++ libraries to ELF with coff2elf on SV/386 R3.2.2 with the V5.0 ANSI C compiler?
a: Yes, if you only need to relink them, coff2elf does it. The catch: AT&T's C++ depends on ar for symbol table data, and the V5.0 ar output is incompatible with earlier C++ releases. Early 2.1 distributions fix it with a shell script change.

subject: 2 floppy drives on the Unix PC (was: 3.5 inch drives on Unix PC)
q: Can a Unix PC run two floppy drives, the 5.25 inch plus an added 3.5 inch? And are high density 3.5 inch drives just more tracks, or more sectors per track?
a: There's no drive select logic on the motherboard or in the driver, so two drives needs a hardware hack and a loadable floppy driver. High density drives, 3.5 or 5.25, double the data rate to get more sectors per track. Same hack needed. Sigh.

subject: Can several windows be smgr/wmgr/phmgr?
q: Can several windows each be smgr, wmgr or phmgr by issuing that ioctl?
a: No. Each system window type gets exactly one window. Otherwise how would the system know where to send the hot key? To take over a hot key, run your own program in place of ph or smgr and use keyfix to redefine the key. See <sys/kbd.h>.

subject: 99 pin connector for unix-pc bus
q: Has anyone found a source for the 99 pin connector on the Unix-PC expansion bus?
a: It's a custom part, but not proprietary, and AMP can supply it with the dreaded minimum purchase quantity. The numbers are AMP 2-532431-0 for plug-in boards and 2-532433-0 for the motherboard. A distributor listed it with zero stock, naturally.

subject: Bernoulli on AT&T 6300?
q: Has anyone put a Bernoulli Box on an AT&T 6300? Any problems, and does the ROM revision matter?
a: Tried Bernoulli 10/10 drives on Olivetti M24 and M280 machines, which are the same breed. The headache was configuring the various interface cards, and that's over now. No trouble with older BIOS versions 1.21, 1.36 or 1.43.

subject: Hard Disk Help
q: Has anyone successfully added a Seagate ST251 40 meg hard disk to an AT&T 6300 PLUS in place of the CDC WREN II?
a: If you can low-level format with non-standard parameters, you just need the geometry: the ST251 has 6 heads and 820 cylinders, with precomp and reduced write set to none. A utility like Disk Manager from Ontrack helps when formatting balks.

subject: INT 19H in AT&T 6300 ROM BIOS
q: How can I reset an AT&T 6300 from a batch file? INT 19H in a little DEBUG program doesn't reliably reboot the hard disk.
a: Do a far jump to FFFF:0000, where an 8086 or 8088 starts after a hardware reset. On many machines that acts like a power-on boot and clears problems a DOS boot won't. Some hardware may need resetting, so try it before whining.

subject: big disks for 3b2
q: How many internal drives can a 3B2/600 hold? Don't the 600s have three?
a: I only find room for 2 internal hard disks, 1 floppy and 1 tape drive in the 3B2/600. After that you go external, as far as I know. Count the bays before you daydream about 2Gb.

subject: Convergent MiniFrame (Help)
q: I got a Convergent MiniFrame with no hard disk or cables. What cables do I need for the hard disk and floppy, and which connector is which?
a: Ordinary PC hard disk cables work, no twists. Looking into the drive bay, left to right: hard disk 1, hard disk 0, the floppy, and last the one for both hard drives. Install drive 0, almost any ST-506 drive, 40 megs or more. Read the board.

subject: Newcomer to the PC7300 Group !!
q: I just got a PC 7300 and got rid of the Mac-like interface, but all I can do is ls and mail, with no cc. Where can I get PD compilers and software, and what is going on?
a: You don't have cc because the foundation system lacks the development set: cc, as, ld, libraries, lex, yacc, sdb. You need more manuals too. There's a unix-pc newsgroup including unix-pc.sources, with lots of software distributed for the machine. Read before you rip things out.

subject: 3b1 unixpc 7300 newsgroup archives, where are they?
q: Is the 3b1 / unixpc 7300 newsgroup archived anywhere? Where can I find past information?
a: Watch comp.sys.3b1 and comp.sources.3b1, not this group. The archive site is cheops.cis.ohio-state.edu (osu-cis), loaded with five years of contributed stuff, and uunet archives comp.sources.3b1. Don't expect miracles overnight.

subject: Extended memory for 6386?
q: Is there a product or public domain software that lets a 6386 WGS running DOS use extended memory, so StarGroup software gets out of the 640k base? QEMM has given me nothing but problems.
a: QEMM works fine on a 6386 with DOS 3.3a. StarGroup 3.3 can run the redirector in extended memory (switch in lanman.ini) and the ISO stack in expanded memory (switch in protocol.ini). That cuts conventional use from about 110k to 40k. Maybe the problem is your setup.

subject: 3B2/300
q: My 3B2/300 running System V won't boot and says NVRAM SANITY FAILURE, DEFAULT VALUES ASSUMED, check the battery, and then DISK SANITY FAILURE. What's wrong?
a: The NVRAM error probably just means it sat unplugged longer than the battery could hold. It gets rebuilt once you get past the disk problem, so only blame the battery if it repeats. The disk lost its sanity track, which devtools or dgmon may rebuild. Or the disk or interface is dead.

subject: IPC 802 in 386?
q: My AT&T 6386's IPC intelligent ports card locks up about every other day. Is there a fix other than rebooting?
a: Get driver version 2.1 from AT&T. Call the hotline and they'll send it. The lockups were in the 1.2 and 2.0 drivers and seem fixed in 2.1. Should have been right the first time.

subject: Voice Power problems with 3.51m
q: My Unix PC with a Voice Power card shows 'play' in the voice editor (ve) but plays nothing and the time stays at zero, though the diagnostics work fine. Any suggestions?
a: You MUST use the handset to listen to anything from the Voice Power card. It won't play until the handset is off the hook. Sigh, everyone trips on this one.

subject: VT Initialization
q: My login shell is ksh, but when I switch virtual terminals with Alt-SysRq-Fx I have to start ksh by hand. How do I get it to come up automatically?
a: Edit /etc/default/login and add the line ALTSHELL=YES. That tells login it's OK to put your real shell's name in the environment instead of pretending to be something else. It's in the docs, you know.

subject: link of directory
q: On System V without symbolic links to directories, how dangerous is it to make a second hard link to a directory as root, say to get around a DOS program that can't see a lowercase name?
a: Plenty. The .. entry in the linked directory always points to the original parent, unlike BSD. You can't remove the link with rmdir without first emptying the directory, with startling results. fsck complains too, and circular links are a no-no. Don't.

subject: ATT6300/BASIC timer problem
q: On my AT&T 6300, the BASIC timer values in seconds past midnight sometimes go above 86400, at random times a few times a day. I'm on ATT DOS 3.1 and ROM BIOS 1.21. What's wrong?
a: It's a bug in the 1.21 ROMs that causes those bad timer values. It was reportedly fixed in the 1.43 ROMs, and replacing the 1.21s made the problem disappear for others. Replace your ROMs. It's not your code.

subject: UNIX PC Graphics Questions
q: On the UNIX PC, can I access screen memory directly instead of doing pixrect ops for each pixel in a vector draw routine?
a: Not without pain. Screen memory sits at $420000, and the only way in is a loadable driver. You'd still make a system call, and it would trash the window manager's view of things. Good luck, you'll need it.

subject: CPLU4.2 vs C-FP+
q: Our 3B2/400s run the old ATT C-FP+ compiler. Is it discontinued, does CPLU 4.2 support the MAU hardware floating point and ANSI C prototypes, and is it any good?
a: C-FP+ is surely not sold anymore, and CPLU 4.2 does everything it does and more. Hardware floating point works with the -Kmau flag, and the optimizer is better. ANSI? No, not at all. Wait for SysV Release 4.0. It's solid, no bugs found.

subject: 3b1 screen print
q: Screen print on my 3b1 leaves white space between the lines because of carriage return and line feed handling. Could the lp program be the cause?
a: Quite possibly. Try /dev/rlp instead of /dev/lp, since lp adds a form feed after 66 lines. Then you may have to resend the printer its CR/LF interpretation instructions. Check how sprint does newline and how the printer is set up, for pity's sake.

subject: Network choice for the Future?
q: Should I choose Starlan or TCP/IP Ethernet for Unix-to-Unix connections among ATT 3B2s, 6386s and perhaps a VaxStation 2000? I need remote shell, remote copy and 8-bit transfer.
a: You want Starlan-10. It has all the wiring convenience of Starlan with the software tools of Ethernet. You can even put your Vax on it with a Starlan-10 cable tap for the Ethernet controller. Not a hard choice.

subject: Test plug configuration?
q: The UNIX-PC diagnostic disk says I need a special plug to test the serial port at /dev/tty000. How should one wire it, and where can I get one?
a: It's essentially a loop-back test: the output lines run into the input lines and it handshakes with itself. Build one with a ribbon cable that has male and female connectors, and put a null-modem adapter between them at the far end. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: Fast/Slow 6386s
q: Two nearly identical 6386 16MHz systems run ix386 and VP/IX with the same applications, but the one with the 40MB ST506 drive runs much faster than the one with the 135MB ESDI drive. How do I make the 135 run as fast?
a: Check the controllers first. There are 3:1 and 1:1 versions of both ESDI and ST506, and a 1:1 ST506 can beat a 3:1 ESDI. Upgrading means a backup and a fresh low-level format. Also tune the System V/386 parameters for 4MB, and check file system layout. Basics, people.

subject: Question about AT&T Graphic Adaptors
q: Why can the AT&T 6386SX/EL's built-in VGA do 800x600x256 while the VDC600 in the 6386/25 only goes to 640x400x256? Both report 256k of display memory.
a: The VDC600 is basically a Paradise VGA+16 with 256k RAM, so its 256-color limit is low. The 6386SX/EL's video is more like a Paradise 1024, with 512k RAM and 800x600 in 256 colors. Memory, genius, memory.

subject: CBM <---> CP/M
q: How do I get files from C128 mode over to a CP/M disk on my Commodore 128? 64CONVRT doesn't read the CP/M directory right.
a: 64CONVRT works fine, but the CP/M disk must be formatted as 64 SINGLE SIDED. Format it from CP/M, convert a terminal program onto it, then copy that to double sided. Then download CP/M programs directly. Read the format options next time.

subject: Ultima V
q: When is Ultima V going to be released for the Commodore 64/128?
a: Late June or early July. I had it on back order since mid-February and called to find out. Origin has advertised it since December, the dorks. Another two months to wait.

subject: Problems after installing f77 on 3100
q: After installing FORTRAN for RISC 2.0 on a DECstation 3100, the loader complains about stamp mismatch, and the f77 libraries are links to 3.1 version libraries. What's wrong?
a: Removing the old Fortran 1.0 with setld left /usr/lib/libF77.a, libI77.a and libU77.a as symlinks to the old 1.31 libraries. Remove those links and re-make them to the 2.0 libraries in /usr/lib/cmplrs/f77. Then it works. Check your links.

subject: Black vertical line on VR299 display (DS3100)
q: All my xterm windows on a DS3100 with a VR299 display have a one-pixel black line next to the scroll bar. Anyone know the cause or a fix?
a: Looks like the first row of pixels from the first row of characters, and it shows up when the scroll bar gets added. Running clear seems to take care of it. Hardly a mystery.

subject: Can I safely remove a SCSI device from a running DEC3100
q: Can I safely remove a SCSI device, like an Exabyte, from a running DECstation 3100 that's acting as a fileserver?
a: No. SCSI isn't set up for hot connect or disconnect, so you'll likely trash disk transfers in progress and probably zap a driver or receiver. Power down both sides first. Not rocket science.

subject: DECStation 3100
q: Can ULTRIX 3.0 be installed on a DECstation 3100 over the network from a VAX server, given the different byte ordering? Do I need a TK drive?
a: No TK drive needed. The MIPS chip's byte order is chosen at board-construction time, and DEC picked little-endian to match the VAX. Install from the VAX works fine once you update the server software. Your rep should know this.

subject: DECstation bootable off RZ5x (650meg) disks?
q: Can a DECstation/DECsystem 3100 server boot off the RZ56 650meg disk (RZ5x)? The salesmen say it's not a supported boot device. Is that a real barrier?
a: Not a real barrier. It's "not supported" only because ULTRIX V3.1 shipped before the RZ56 existed. There's an easy workaround, so order it and have your sales rep check with ULTRIX support. Sigh, salesmen.

subject: Rev levels for hardware maintenance of VAX Nodes
q: Does DEC publish or sell the current rev levels and Field Change Orders for VAX hardware, so we can check that a third-party maintainer is keeping our nodes up to date?
a: Yes. DEC puts out the current revision levels in a quarterly, free publication called the VAXcluster Systems Quorum. Use it to keep your field service people honest. The other option is a paid guide through your sales rep, and it is NOT cheap. Be insistent, they won't know it exists.

subject: Iverson 11/750 accelerator
q: Has anybody used the Iverson accelerator card for the VAX-11/750 that claims a 15-25% speedup with a variable clock? Does it actually work?
a: It works. We ran it on four 750s, VMS and UNIX, and benchmarks showed 15-25% depending on the test. It's transparent, with a switch to take it out of the system, and installs easily. Price was about $9K, which is steep, but that's vendors for you.

subject: EMail Addressing for someone at DEC.FRANCE wanted
q: How can I send email from a bitnet site to someone at DEC France, at an address like hamnqvist@casee.enet.dec.com?
a: If the name and node are spelled correctly, that syntax should work just fine. Check your spelling before blaming the network.

subject: VS2000 operator console
q: How do I redirect the console of a VAXstation 2000 (OPA0:) to an async port so I can use it as a plain MicroVAX with no monitor?
a: Get a MicroVAX console cable and plug it into the printer port, then cold boot. The machine will use your terminal as console. It is basically a printer cable with certain pins shorted. Otherwise open the box and move a jumper, which is a pain.

subject: DECnet task-to-task programming
q: How do I set up a DECnet task-to-task connection between two existing processes on VMS without using named objects, since those need SYSNAM privilege?
a: Use a PROXY account, and the connection will start a command file in the user's directory, no SYSNAM needed. Or just use sockets, since even UCX 1.2 supports them and your code stays portable. Why fight DECnet at all?

subject: Short Question
q: How does a VAXstation II/RC differ from a VAXstation II/GPX?
a: The RC was a standard VAXstation II in a BA23 box, with 3 MB instead of 2, cheaper at $15,000 vs $25,000, and no DECnet license. The last three backplane slots were filled with epoxy, honest. RC meant Restricted Configuration, marketing at its finest.

subject: help needed setting up a VAXStation 3100
q: I can't get my VAXstation 3100 to see an ANDATACO SCSI disk daisy-chained with the TK50. Each shows up alone, but together neither appears in show device, and test 6 gives error 84. Has anyone fixed this?
a: Sounds like both devices are set to the same SCSI address. Could be a termination problem too, but that's less likely. Check the address settings first, sigh, it's the oldest SCSI mistake there is.

subject: Information on DEC LN3 A3 needed
q: I got a DEC LN03-A3 laser printer with no manuals. Can I get PostScript for it, what toner does it use, and can it print graphics?
a: An LN03-A3 is just an LN03. You'd have to upgrade to an LN03R to get PostScript. It takes LN03 toner cartridges, apparently with a Chinon engine. Graphics are done with SIXEL. Paper just has to survive the bends. Manuals, honestly, would've told you all this.

subject: Setting up a remote print queue
q: I have two VMS systems at different sites, each running an application that prints to local print queues. Can I set up a queue on node A that the application on node B can print to, and vice versa, over LAT and DECnet?
a: Sure. Buy DECprint or the old Remote Print Manager from the company that sold you the boxes. Or skip the software: COPY to the spooled device through logical names like NET$PRINTER_NODE_A pointing at A::LPA0:. Pull DQS too. Sigh, no extra software needed.

subject: DEC 6430
q: I want to learn about the DEC 6430. What machines does it run on, what is it like, how old is it, and what's the newest version?
a: You're confused. It's a VAX 6000-430, which is itself a CPU, so asking what it runs on is redundant. It's a CMOS, DEC-proprietary, symmetric multiprocessing box of about 20 VUPS, released only months ago. The 6000 line started with the 210. Get the naming straight.

subject: VAX/EWS
q: I want to use VAX EWS on old VAXstation 2000s to turn them into X terminals. How much memory does it need, and how is the performance?
a: It doesn't emulate a VT1200, it makes an X window terminal. As little as 4 Mb works, but under 6 Mb you can't open many windows. It runs under VAXELN, so performance is quite good, even on an old 2000.

subject: f77 array size limitation
q: My Fortran program with a large array, A(2*N,N) with N=400, gets a segmentation fault on a DECstation 5000 running Ultrix 4.1, but works for smaller N. What do I change?
a: It's your stack, genius. The RISC Fortran compiler puts big arrays on the stack, and the default csh limit is tiny. Compile with -static, or run limit stacksize with a bigger number, and put it in your .cshrc. Yes, the segfault is a dumb way to say so.

subject: MicroPDP-11 clock
q: My MicroPDP-11 prints "clock disabled" at boot, just before booting from disk. How do I enable the clock?
a: If it's in a BA23, the switch is on the control panel. Pop off the front and you'll find a PC board behind the bezel with a 2-position DIP switch, and one of those is the clock enable. Try them both; the processor board isn't where you were looking.

subject: VAX 730 stuff
q: My VAX 730 complains that SYS$SYSTEM:RSX.EXE is missing when I run compatibility mode software. I thought compatibility mode was built into all the VAX 700 processors. How do I get a replacement?
a: Hardware runs PDP-11 instructions on the 7xx, but the RSX software emulation isn't part of VMS since V4.0. It's a layered product called VAX RSX, so send DEC more money. An old V3 RSX.EXE won't work on V4, too much changed.

subject: LAT printers
q: Print jobs from our Ultrix 4.1 machine to LAT printers on a terminal server sometimes hang and print over and over. What causes it?
a: It's a known bug and the release notes even mention it. The only fix I've heard of is restarting the print daemons every now and then. Sigh, typical vendor quality.

subject: f77 compiler on DS3100 is missing falloc(), malloc(), free()
q: The f77 compiler on my DECstation 3100 under Ultrix 2.0 is missing falloc, malloc and free even though the manuals document them. Why, and how can I make my own?
a: MIPS 1.31 FORTRAN has no POINTER type, so those routines were never supported, whatever the manual claims. Version 2.0 of the compiler adds POINTER, malloc and free. Meanwhile, write the routines in C and interface FORTRAN to them.

subject: KDA50-QA configuration for VMS as DUBx:
q: What are the standard CSR address and vector for a KDA50-QA configured as controller DUBx on VMS?
a: Stop guessing and ask SYSGEN, whose rules are subtle and change often. Run CONFIG in SYSGEN and it tells you the CSR and vector. The second UDA comes out at 760334 with vector 300 here, but it depends on your other hardware.

subject: Seeking software for Rainbow
q: What software is available for the DEC Rainbow besides the standard DEC issue? Are there commercial or public domain packages, and are there any user's groups?
a: Join the INFO-DEC-MICRO mailing list at SU-SCORE, which covers Rainbows. Ask your local DECUS chapter about a PC SIG for a user's group. There's also plenty of public domain stuff on Rainbow-oriented FIDO BBSes and on the LCG.KERMIT system. More than you'd think.

subject: PDP-11 Assembler
q: Where can I find books on PDP-11 assembly language programming?
a: The classic is Richard Eckhouse's "Minicomputer Systems: Organization and Programming", from Prentice-Hall, maybe also via Digital Press. There's also "Assembly Language Programming for the PDP-11" by Harvey Lee Shapiro. Go read them, kid.

subject: Where can I find the SCSI specs?
q: Where can I find the SCSI specs? Is there any other reference that explains Async vs. Sync SCSI busses and their compatibility?
a: Order the SCSI-1 spec from ANSI in New York, document X3.131, about $25. The SCSI-II draft comes from Global Engineering Documents in Irvine. There's also a Prentice-Hall book titled "SCSI". Sigh, reading the actual spec beats guessing about sync and async.

subject: DECnet protocols (was Re: UNIX to VMS via DECNET)
q: Where can I get copies of the DECnet protocol specifications? The old documentation I found didn't match what I saw on the Ethernet.
