a: Get the DNA functional specs from DEC. The network architecture general description is AA-N149A-TC, and the layer specs include AA-X440A-TK, AA-Y298A-TK, AA-X435A-TK, AA-X439A-TK, AA-K182A-TK, AA-X437A-TK and AA-X436A-TK. Order them like everyone else.

subject: Wanted: NFS for VMS
q: Where can we find NFS for VMS 5.x to connect our unix systems and PCs to the VMS filesystems, and what are the caveats?
a: DEC's is the poorest TCP/IP you can get, with no mail and flaky links to Suns. Skip it. WINTCP from Wollongong is the most widely used. MULTINET is cheapest, often rated best, and the only one that does VMS as NFS client. Pick one, grumble.

subject: DECSYSTEMS
q: Which DECsystem 5000 model would support up to 50 users running small and large applications under Ultrix?
a: Not the little ones. One user's DECsystem 5140 dies with a couple of hefty background jobs. For 50 users plus background work, buy a VAX; you get the same users per dollar. Don't expect miracles from a workstation.

subject: RM02 on MASSBUS advice wanted.
q: Will an RM03, an RM05 and an RM02 work together on one MASSBUS controller on a PDP-11/70? Are there any problems with that configuration?
a: It can be done, though DEC field service had never seen it. The last drive on the chain must be an RM05 or the timing breaks. On RSX you also answer the mixed massbus question in sysgen. Took us an hour of trial and error, because nobody reads anything.

subject: Auto Start Rainbow 100A?
q: Can I get a Rainbow 100A to restart automatically after a power outage, past the startup screen that asks to select drive A? I could burn new PROMs.
a: Bummer, but no. You need a 100B motherboard for that. Burning PROMs on the 100A won't save you.

subject: DecMate II
q: I bought a DecMate II at an auction. Is it a Rainbow or PC compatible in any way?
a: No, it's neither. The DECmate II is basically a PDP-8 based word processing system. Some had a Z80 board added for 8-bit CP/M, but without that it's pretty useless by modern standards. Should have checked before bidding.

subject: Rainbow 100 Info?
q: I just got a Rainbow 100. Which MS-DOS and BIOS calls work, and where can I find technical info?
a: Get the Rainbow Technical manual, which IRUG sells. MS-DOS calls work fine, but hardware-dependent BIOS calls don't: below 20H or above 2FH fail, 2xH works. INT 18H is the Rainbow BIOS, with VT100 emulation in ROM. It's not a PC, so quit expecting one.

subject: winchester hard drive formatting program
q: Is there a public domain formatting program for a Rainbow's Winchester hard drive? I want something legal and free.
a: Last I looked, DRYCAS had a PD formatting program called WUTIL. You practically answered your own question. Go look there, it's been a while though.

subject: Problems with biff/comsat notifying wrong people
q: After our Multimax has run for weeks, comsat/biff sometimes notifies the wrong user of new mail, apparently reading wrong info from /etc/utmp. Has anyone seen this?
a: Comsat isn't rereading /etc/utmp. It's a bug in the 4.2BSD sleep(3): it goes to sleep and never wakes up. Fixed in 4.3BSD, and a quick diff makes it painfully obvious. The 4.2BSD interval timers also have a bug that shows up on multiprocessors with the same symptom.

subject: default routing in Annex
q: How do I set a default route in an Annex running release 4.0? The gateways file only seems to handle specific networks.
a: Add "net 0 gateway 128.83.1.1 metric 1 hardwired" to the gateways file, /usr/spool/erpcd/bfs/gateways, using your own gateway address. It's picked up at boot, just like a BSD default route. From R4.1 you can write "default" instead of 0.

subject: HP 28S Battery Replacement
q: Can I change the batteries in my HP-28S without losing memory? The HP-41 could go a few minutes without batteries.
a: Read the manual. The appendix on batteries says you have about a minute to swap them. Honestly, this is what manuals are for.

subject: Mail-order Casio B.O.S.S. source?
q: Does anybody know a mail-order source for the Casio B.O.S.S.? I can't find any ads in the computer magazines.
a: You're looking in the wrong magazines. Try the photography ones, like Popular Photography. One place in New York, Executive Photo, treated me fine, though you could probably do better by hunting around.

subject: Variable word length math
q: Does anyone know of a calculator that supports variable word length (8, 16, 32) math, like the old HP 16C?
a: The HP48SX does variable word size for binary integers. The 28S probably does too, I suspect. Nobody needs to haunt the used market for a 16C when HP sells this.

subject: Free EQ LIB offerd by HP for 48SX
q: HP offered a free Equation Library card for buying the 48SX, and I sent in the coupon but heard nothing. Who should I call?
a: It's an independent company, Direct Mail Projects, not HP. They have no modules to send because HP badly underestimated the response and ran out. They said modules should arrive around the end of January, so you wait. Typical marketing.

subject: Serial cable for HP48sx to PC
q: Has anyone made the serial cable for the HP48SX to a PC? Do I need HP's software for up/download, or will any communication program like Procomm do?
a: You don't need HP's software. The PC disk just has a plain-jane kermit.exe, and every kermit I tried worked. Any decent Kermit does the job, so quit paying for fluff.

subject: Atari Portfolio (was Re: Casio Boss models)
q: How do I link the Atari Portfolio to a Mac or a PC? Is the $190 cable and software package worth it, or would standard cables and MacKermit do?
a: For a PC, just get the Parallel Interface Unit. The Portfolio has in-ROM software for it, and the PC disks come with it. For a Mac you need the Serial Interface Unit plus a terminal program, and Atari gives one away free, so don't waste money on a commercial one.

subject: D/L problems
q: I got the Joust game into my HP48 and used ASC->, giving me a string starting with Joust by Zoom. How do I actually start it?
a: That's not a program, it's a string. Another program, Super-Chip, uses it. Call the string onto the stack, then execute Super-Chip. Latest revision I've seen is 1.1. Not as easy as Tetris, tough luck.

subject: HP95LX Games
q: I tried making an APNAME.LST file to run the built-in Hearts and Bones game on my HP95LX with ALT-H, but it doesn't work. What do I need to do to run it?
a: The apname.lst file has to be in _dat, so save it as c:\_dat\apname.lst. Each line is a key binding. Reboot afterward, then press the bound key, such as ALT-FILER. Details matter, you know.

subject: Units Problems...
q: On my HP 48SX, entering 1 degree C twice and adding gives 275.15 degrees C. Is that a bug?
a: Not a bug, RTFM, page 201. A plain C value is a point on a scale, not a difference, so the 48 adds absolute temperatures: convert to kelvins, add, convert back. Convert to K before adding, or combine with other units so it treats them as relative.

subject: HP28 screen memory
q: On the HP28, I tried #FF840 #FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF POKE to change screen memory and nothing happened. What am I doing wrong?
a: You reversed the arguments. It's the value first, then the address: #FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF #FF840 POKE. Get it backwards and Bad Things can happen. Also check your word size; 32 bits is one display column. Read the manual.

subject: Question about HP48SX units.
q: On the HP48SX, what units do "ct" and "t" under MASS and "F" under ELECTRICITY in the UNITS menu stand for?
a: ct is carats, a carat being 0.2 grams. t is metric tons, 1_t = 1000 kg. F is farads, the unit of capacitance. All of this is in vol. 2 of the 48SX manual, in the appendix with the command summary. RTFM.

subject: hp48 reset button
q: There's a little hole labeled 'R' under the top right rubber foot of the HP48. Is it a reset button?
a: This is a FAQ. Yes, it's a reset button. Use it before ON-C when in trouble and you avoid the dreaded 'Restore memory?' question. It resets cleanly with no memory loss, unless the memory is actually damaged.

subject: Alternative Operating Systems...
q: Which palmtops let you boot an alternative operating system? I'm thinking about the Poquet PC and wondering about DOS in ROM.
a: The Portfolio boots from a card in A:, but no OS files show up, so it likely can't boot another OS unless it launches from DOS. The Poquet boots from cards the same way and loads DOS, so it ought to be possible. Unverified, naturally.

subject: kermit problem??
q: Why do I get an Invalid Syntax error transferring a program to my HP calculator by Kermit? It stops at line 9, and the log shows FREEX where I'd expect another token.
a: That #M#J is just Kermit's encoding of CR/LF. The two Kermits may disagree on encoding control characters. Also, the tokens after it should be FREEZE STOF, not FREEX. Fix your transfer settings and compare the text.

subject: Name resolver?
q: Does HPUX 6.5 support Internet name resolution, so telnet to a hostname.domain.edu finds the IP address?
a: Not officially, 6.5 has no domain name service. Grab the resolver by anonymous ftp from me10.lbl.gov in /pub/bind and you get some DNS capability. Typical vendor, making you do it yourself.

subject: 3rd party SCSI tape on HP9000/375??
q: Has anyone connected a third-party SCSI tape drive to an HP 9000/375 running HP-UX 7?
a: Yes, I've hooked Exabyte 8mm drives to several HP 9000/3xx boxes. HP-UX 6.5 and 7.x include an unsupported SCSI tape driver; look in /etc/master. The vendor's own driver worked best, though.

subject: Looking for LaTeX...
q: Has anyone ported LaTeX to HP 9000/300 series machines? Also, were TeX, texx and texx2 only for the 800 series?
a: That's incorrect. The HP TeX package has TeX 2.93, METAFONT, LaTeX, PiCTeX, xdvi and texx in C source, and it builds and runs fine on both the 300 and 800 series. Some compiled binaries are included too. Texx2 is missing, but xdvi and texx cover it.

subject: Advice sought porting Sun RPC to HP-UX
q: Has anyone ported Sun RPC 3.0 to HP-UX on the HP9000/300? Any advice?
a: HP already did it. NFS is an optional product on HP-UX 6.0, and the RPC library calls live in libc. Check with nm /lib/libc.a | grep callrpc before you waste time porting something you already own.

subject: File transfers from HP1000
q: How can I transfer files from an HP1000 running RTE-A to an MS-DOS PC? Kermit on the PC trips over the HP's ENQ/ACK flow control, and I can't get Kermit onto the HP.
a: HP sells AdvanceLink, which runs on both the PC and the HP1000. You can also turn ENQ/ACK off on the HP, though the exact command depends on your MUX. And if you can't move Kermit's sources over, how do you expect to move a binary? Think.

subject: Traps
q: How can I use control Y traps in PASCAL3000 on an HP 3000? The manual doesn't seem to mention them, and I wondered about calling an SPL subroutine from PASCAL.
a: Look in the MPE V Intrinsics manual. XCONTRAP enables or disables the CONTROL-Y trap, and traps are covered in Section 5, pages 5-37 to 5-49, with control-Y on 5-46 plus a sample SPL program. Haven't tried it myself, so don't blame me. Read the manual.

subject: LaserJet II & III
q: How compatible is the HP LaserJet III with the LaserJet II? Will every file that prints correctly on a LJ II print correctly on a LJ III?
a: No, not always. One user's GnuPlot-generated bitmap files printed fine on a LJ II but came out a bit garbled on a LJ III, after eliminating interface and configuration problems. Compatibility claims are marketing fluff, naturally.

subject: ksh (SECONDS or PS1)
q: I put a prompt script from the Korn shell book in my .profile to show the time of day, and when I sourced it the terminal hung on every HP. What is the problem?
a: My guess is your PS1 exceeds COLUMNS. We saw ksh hang when a colleague tried a fancy way to set COLUMNS and LINES. Export COLUMNS and PS1, set a long PS1, then set COLUMNS=10, and ksh hangs. Ugly bug, but there it is.

subject: x11twk problems
q: I'm running HP Teamwork's x11twk from a Sun 386i with X11/NeWS instead of an HP machine, and it starts, then complains it can't find the font files with a DM_GPR_FAILURE error. Can I even do this, and what am I doing wrong?
a: Sigh. The fonts x11twk uses have to live on the X-server machine, here your Sun, not just on the dc_server box. Copy them over or NFS mount them at the same full path. Uncompress them if they're .scf. Watch out that the .snf format may differ between HP and Sun.

subject: root over NFS (again)
q: Is there a patch for NFS on HP-UX 6.5 that lets root act as root over an NFS mount, say for 0700 files on the remote machine? Is it fixed in 7.0?
a: You can patch the kernel with adb to remap nobody's UID to 0, but then root on any machine gets in, which wrecks security. Newer NFS lets you grant root per machine at export time, like root=zen on the export line. Upgrade, and think about security.

subject: bad m/o disks?
q: My HP 6300 650A optical drive on an HP-UX 7.05 350 panics on backup writes and leaves unreadable blocks, even after mediainit. Is there a SCSI patch, or a better way to spare bad blocks?
a: Install the 7.0 SCSI patches (scsi_if.c, scsi.c, scsi_ccs.c, ac.c). If that fails, HP may need to swap the controller PROM, an old C1700-89000 CCP 2.13 for the new C1700-89601 CCP 3.02, since firmware error recovery caused it. Typical HP.

subject: Cognos PowerHouse 5.26
q: My PowerHouse update came with 5.26 tapes but 5.06 manuals. What's the difference between the two versions on MPE V/E?
a: You should have gotten a document called PowerHouse for HP 3000 MPE/V New Features, Version 5.26. It has exactly what you want. If it's missing, ask your Cognos sales rep. Check the box before you post.

subject: stty : : Operation not supported
q: On HP-UX 6.5 with X11R3 I get random stty errors like Not a Terminal or Operation not supported on socket when reading mail or starting X clients. What causes it?
a: Stty commands in .cshrc instead of .login. It looks random because mailx only spawns a shell for the pager when a message exceeds the crt length. Keep stty out of .cshrc, or skip it when the csh isn't interactive.

subject: yp & remote printing
q: Remote printing on HP 9000s doesn't work with yellow pages netgroups in hosts.equiv. The queue says it's waiting for the remote host to come up until I add the host explicitly. What's wrong?
a: It's not hosts.equiv, that would give access violations. The problem is inetd failing to start rlpdaemon as the manual says. Start /usr/lib/rlpdaemon from your rc file instead, at the end of localrc(), and it works. On clusters, guard it by hostname so discless nodes skip it. Sigh, the manual is wrong.

subject: Cron twice on standard time
q: Since the switch to standard time, our HP-9000/550 running HP-UX 5.21 ran cron jobs twice, once an hour early and once at the right time. Any suggestions?
a: Known cron defect: it runs scheduled jobs twice on the day of the switch from Daylight to Standard Time. It was fixed in the 5.3 release for the Series 500, so get 5.3. Maybe read the update notes before you wonder.

subject: IMAGE problem
q: Under MPE V, DBGET reports a 'broken chain' error after DBFIND, yet QUERY reads the chain fine and nobody else is accessing the database. What's happening?
a: You probably still have a broken chain. QUERY often reads serially and ignores chains, so it never complains. Try the utilities on the Contributed Software Library tape, or Adager or DbGeneral. Otherwise it's a serial DBUNLOAD/DBLOAD to rebuild. Sigh.

subject: 720 without bitmapped display?
q: We're thinking of buying an HP 720 as a compute server and have no room for a big display. Can we run one without a bitmapped display, from a serial port or over the network?
a: Yes, HP sells a 720 std server config with no display. Don't ask me what's in it, I don't remember. Call your HP rep and read the price list instead of asking the net.

subject: Hp version of PBMPLUS package?
q: Where can I find an HP-compatible version of the PBMPLUS package? Altering the source hasn't worked.
a: You don't need to alter the source. With HP-UX 7.0, all you need is a decent makefile. Use imake from X11R3 with the Imakefile. Get the latest pbmplus.tar.Z by anonymous ftp from expo.lcs.mit.edu in contrib. Sigh, not hard.

subject: Fortran Libraries ???
q: Why do the Fortran library functions in the archive have an underscore after the name, when Fortran calls them without it? Does the Fortran compiler append it?
a: Some vendors muck with names: underscores prepended or appended, names capitalized, whatever. They think it's a favor. Isolate yourself from it in a header file, and expect to do the final link from f77 on some machines. Vendors, honestly.

subject: Using an 8mm Exabyte Drive on a 400s
q: Why does rdump on an HP/Apollo 400s give far less capacity on an 8mm Exabyte than the rated figure? Is the rmt writing 512 byte blocks, and is there a better backup program?
a: Blame dump's small block size. The Exabyte is most efficient in both speed and space with blocks that are multiples of 8K. Try ftio, which is about the most efficient option and lets you set the block size to nearly anything. Honestly, read the drive docs first.

subject: TIOCNOTTY on HP9000/300 series?
q: Why is TIOCNOTTY defined in sys/ioctl.h only on the HP9000/800 series and not the 300 series? What should I use on the 300?
a: Why, no idea. But I just call setsid() instead of the TIOCNOTTY ioctl and haven't noticed any problems. Whether that's the best replacement, you tell me.

subject: No C-Compiler after upgrade from 7.0 -> 8.0 ?
q: Will we lose our C compiler when upgrading HP-UX 7.0 to 8.0? I heard it only ships a stripped-down one for linking the kernel.
a: Seems HP unbundled the full ANSI C development system, supposedly to be cost effective. They kept the traditional K&R cc, which should be enough to get gcc running. So pay up for ANSI C or build gcc. Typical vendor nickel-and-diming.

subject: utimes() and other bsd routines not on 7.0
q: utimes() and other BSD routines aren't on HP-UX 7.0. Is there any way to implement utimes() there?
a: Use utime() instead. You can even write a utimes() emulation on top of it and just throw away the microsecond fields, which 4.3 does inside the kernel anyway. Some other BSD routines are in libBSD, if you'd bothered to look.

subject: How to reset CMOS configuration that prevents booting?
q: A bad 'extended setup' on my C&T 386 motherboard means it won't boot, just beeps, and the CMOS battery is soldered so I can't clear it. How do I reset the CMOS?
a: Hold down the INSert key while turning on the machine. That makes it ignore or reset the CMOS settings, so you can then change them back. Someone remembers the DELete key working the same way, so try both. Next time don't fiddle with what you don't understand.

subject: Distribution of shareware for profit without permission
q: A company is distributing my shareware program on disks for a few dollars each without asking me. Is that legal?
a: Probably yes, grumble. If they charge only for copying and the disk, they're not selling your program for profit. And shareware carries a notice encouraging copying, which is permission to distribute. Unless you ban clubs and companies explicitly, you can't stop them.

subject: Mixing DRAM speeds
q: A friend added 2 meg of 1Mx1 80ns DRAM to a 286 NEAT chipset clone that already had 1/2 meg of 256Kx1 120ns, and set the controller for 120ns, but it hangs and won't boot. What's wrong?
a: Not the speed. The NEAT chip set can't handle mixing bank sizes, thanks to its bank interleave feature. You need 36 chips of one kind before you can put in a different kind. Sigh, read the chipset docs before buying RAM.

subject: Supramodem?
q: A friend is looking at a 2400 baud Supramodem for $149. Has anybody heard about it or used one?
a: Folks report nothing but good things. One user has run it six months with heavy uploading and downloading, flawless, as reliable as a Hayes and fine with anything wanting Hayes compatibility. You can find it cheaper by mail order, too.

subject: need info on Leading Edge Model D2
q: A friend is thinking of buying a Leading Edge Model D2, a 286 with 30 Mb disk for about $2000. Any feedback on reliability and compatibility?
a: One owner found the price good, the machine well-built and the guarantee about the best around. The catch is that Leading Edge makes dealers pay before shipping, so you may have to put 10-25% down and wait a few weeks. Typical vendor nonsense.

subject: UNZIP program and PC archives?
q: All the popular PC archives are swamped with FTPs. Is there another site with UNZIP and a good selection of PC software?
a: Try chyde.uwasa.fi, under /pc/pd2/pkz102.exe. It's less swamped than the usual suspects. Honestly, every semester the students come back and the big archives choke.

subject: PostScript Add-ons for HP LaserJet+?
q: Are there PostScript add-ons for the HP LaserJet+, who makes them, and can I buy memory upgrades from anyone other than HP?
a: Yes, plenty of boards exist. PC Magazine reviewed four or five recently, and one RISC-based board needs no downloading or special driver. Check Pacific Data Products before buying from HP. Get a 1M+ board since it's upgradeable. Read the magazine.

subject: DOS memory allocation
q: Can DOS be persuaded to allocate memory from the top down, so a TSR can allocate memory while an application runs without fragmenting memory?
a: DOS past 3.0 has INT 21h function 58h, which sets the memory allocation strategy, and one option is to allocate top down. Consult a DOS technical manual for the parameters. Read the manual, it's all there.

subject: Those beautiful new Zenith flat screens vs. multiscanning monitors
q: Can I get a VGA card that works with the Zenith ZCM-1490 analog monitor, or should I buy a multiscan instead?
a: Yes. VGA cards have a nine-pin D connector for RGB, EGA and Multisync monitors, and a fifteen-pin D for VGA monitors like the ZCM-1490. Plug into the right one. Not hard.

subject: Installing Hard disk on Compaq Portable
q: Can I install a hard disk on an old 45-pound Compaq Portable with an AST board? I expect I'd have to replace the controller card.
a: Skip the controller swap hassle and get a Plus HardCard. They come in several capacities and access times, so you shouldn't have trouble finding one to suit. Plug it in and be done with it.

subject: Leaving PC on - Hard disk
q: Can I install a switch to turn off just the hard drive while leaving the rest of my PC on when it won't be used for a while? Is that feasible?
a: This has been done to death before. Consensus was it'd be a good idea for the disk, but too hard to do, since DOS, the BIOS and the rest of the hardware can't support it. Sigh.

subject: Remapping the EVIL Caps-Lock Key!
q: Can I remap the Caps-Lock and Ctrl keys on my AT clone within DOS, or do I have to do surgery on the keyboard?
a: Look on the underside of the keyboard first. A surprising number of enhanced keyboards have a switch that swaps Ctrl and CapsLock. Everex ATs even include new keycaps to match. No soldering required.

subject: Using EGA with Zenith Z-151 PC
q: Can I use an EGA card and Multisync monitor with a 1985 Zenith Z-151? I get an orange border and flashing center and an unresponsive keyboard.
a: You need the latest ROM, which any Heath/Zenith store can tell you about. It cost only about $12. Also disable the old video card with its jumpers. Try getting IBM to upgrade a PC 1 ROM, whiner.

subject: Where to post "for sale" stuff (was Re: For sale: 330Meg Priam...)
q: Can I use the distribution field to keep a for-sale posting inside the USA instead of sending it to the whole world?
a: No. The distribution field is for keeping articles of local interest local. Something for sale belongs in a different group altogether, and the distribution question comes up there. Sigh, read the docs before posting.

subject: ZOO enhancement suggestion
q: Can ZOO do CR/LF translation when extracting, so I can move portable sources between MSDOS and XENIX? Is there a better way?
a: The 2.0 manual says a revised zoo with automatic end-of-line conversion is in the works, and "in the works" should be read very liberally. Meanwhile write a trivial program that strips carriage returns or adds one before each linefeed. It's ten lines of C, for crying out loud.

subject: Seeking recommendations for WordStar to WordPerfect converters
q: Can anyone recommend a program to convert WordStar 3.3 files to WordPerfect 4.2? The CONVERT utility that came with WP doesn't do a good job.
a: Word-Link from M/H Group. I tested it on all sorts of conversions, including DCA(RF) to WP 4.2 against WP's CONVERT, and it converted everything. It only swaps tab characters in where the file had explicit spaces. Centering came out the same.

subject: Owners of Sony 1304HG... any comments?
q: Can owners of the Sony 1304HG comment on its performance and quality compared to the NEC 3D?
a: It works nicely in VGA mode and runs hot. It doesn't go as low as the 3D, so 15KHz is out of range. The 3D has more glare. Whether 1024x768 on a 14 inch screen with a dumb adapter is useful is your call.

subject: GoScript
q: Can someone send me info on the latest GoScript and where to get it by anonymous ftp?
a: You can't. GoScript is a commercial product, not PD or shareware. You're probably thinking of Ghostscript, the PostScript previewer from the FSF. Sigh, learn the names.

subject: Kraft Joy Stick
q: Can the Kraft joystick look like a mouse to PC application software that expects a mouse? Is there software that will do this?
a: There's a program called PMM on a local BBS whose description says it turns your joystick into a mouse. I haven't tried it myself, since I have a real mouse. Next time leave a usable path, junior.

subject: File creation error
q: Copying 300 small files from the hard disk to a 1.2 meg floppy gave 'File creation error' after 224 files, though DIR shows plenty of space. Why, and why is the copying so slow?
a: You ran out of root directory entries: a 1.2M floppy root holds exactly 224 files, and it's fixed in size. Make a subdirectory and copy into that. Slow is normal for floppies, and XCOPY buffers in memory so it beats COPY. RTFM.

subject: Compaq disks are non-standard?
q: Dealers say the disk interface on my Compaq 386/20e is non-standard and I must buy Compaq's expensive drives. Is that true, and is there any way out?
a: Yes, it's common knowledge: Compaq uses a modified ST-506 between controller and disk. The way out is to replace the controller and drives with an aftermarket kit, which exists in the states. The CPU-to-controller side is standard AT WD1003. Typical vendor lock-in.

subject: Tape Backup Units
q: Do floppy-interface tape backup units like the Colorado work well for backing up a 70meg hard disk on a 386 AT clone under DOS 3.3?
a: One user put a Colorado Jumbo on the second floppy port and is happy with it. Formatting a tape takes forever, 38 minutes, but backup runs about 10MB in 6 minutes, and the software works well under DOS and Xenix. Not bad for the price.

subject: Heap manager in C?
q: Do you know of a heap management system in C, with malloc() and free(), for an embedded system whose C compiler lacks them? The MS-DOS library sources all contain 80x86 assembly.
a: There's one in the classic K&R book. Compilers do it in assembly because customers care about size and speed, not portability of the runtime library. Sigh, did nobody read K&R?

subject: Turbo Pascal 5.x
q: Does Turbo Pascal 5.x have EGA/VGA drivers? I need a language that can access EGA/VGA modes.
a: Yes, BGI drivers cover EGA and VGA, plus CGA, Hercules and others. But it's one driver for both EGA and VGA, so you get 16 colors, no 256-color mode. Borland's documentation on building the drivers in is scattered all over, as usual.

subject: PS/2 70-E61 Queries.
q: Does anyone besides IBM make an 8514/A card for the PS/2 model 70? What would a 2400 baud MCA modem and 3 megs of memory cost?
a: A few outfits, Hedland and Paradise among them, are cloning 8514/A chipsets, faster than IBM, but they're AT-bus. MCA versions are months off. An MCA modem runs about $200, so get an external for $100 to $150. SIMMs about $120 per megabyte. Wait for it.

subject: How do you turn off the PC's BEEP?
q: Does anyone have a utility, maybe a TSR, that turns off the beep on a PC? Occasionally I'd like to silence the sound, and IBMs have no on/off switch on the front panel.
a: Grab silence.com from /pc/pd2 by anonymous ftp from 128.214.12.3. Or do it the old way with a cheap single-pole switch on the speaker lead. Honestly, a utility this trivial shouldn't need asking about.

subject: 386 Board for AT&T 6300
q: Does anyone have experience with 386 processor boards for the old 8086-based AT&T 6300? Does the Intel one work?
a: One user ran the Applied Reasoning Elevator 386 Board in two 6300s for about 1.5 years. It was the only one found that works in the 6300, since most others assume an 8088 socket. It's around 2K plus a 387, DOS only. Your $1500 is wishful thinking.

subject: Info needed: 12MHz 0-wait AT clone from Computer Products United
q: Does anyone have experience with Computer Products United and their 12MHz 0-wait AT clone for $995?
a: One person ordered one for a friend. Helpful people, on-time delivery, no trouble, and they overnighted missing software. But they had no 0-wait machines then and offered a 12MHz 1-wait one. So the company seems on the level.

subject: Software Carousel
q: Does anyone have experience with Software Carousel, a simple context switcher for the PC that's lighter than Windows or DESQview?
a: It doesn't really context switch like Windows or DV. You switch memory partitions manually by hotkey, using high memory, EMS or disk for swapping, and everything in the other partitions stops running. Fine if you know what you're buying. Read the box.

subject: CursOff?
q: Does anyone know how to stop the IBM PC cursor from blinking on and off, especially in WordPerfect?
a: You can't, not really. The blink is generated by the hardware. The BIOS interrupt only changes which scan lines the cursor occupies. Some package fakes it with an invisible system cursor plus its own software one, but it's slow. Read a book, sigh.

subject: Splitting large files
q: Does anyone know of a program that splits large files, over 1MB, across diskette boundaries? DOS BACKUP does it but has problems.
a: Grab FRAGMENT.ARC from the public util directory on bluefront.cc.umich.edu. It was written to move around huge files and does what you want. Use FTP instead of asking.

subject: looking for an 80286 disassembler
q: Does anyone know of a public domain or otherwise free 80286 disassembler I can get hold of?
a: PC-SIG disk #309 has a table-driven disassembler written in Basic. I know, I know. It's probably 8088 only, but you can modify the source to taste. It's cheapware at best. Beggars can't be choosers.

subject: vi for MS-DOS?
q: Does anyone know of an MS-DOS version of vi? I work in both UNIX and MS-DOS and want one editor for both.
a: There's STEVIE, posted to comp.sources.unix, and pc_vi on simtel20 by ftp or the sixhub archive server. There's also a commercial pc-vi, and MicroEMACS runs everywhere. Two versions sit in PD:<MSDOS.EDITOR> on simtel20. Go look, it's not hard.

subject: Dos Func. 4B emulation
q: Does anyone know of public domain code to emulate DOS function 4B, Exec, for a DOS shell that plays with Interrupt 21H?
a: It's not as hard as it looks. Read the DOS technical reference for the .EXE header format and how it's loaded. The EXE2BIN replacements on SIMTEL are nearly identical to an .EXE loader. And DOS already has function 4B, so why emulate it?

subject: Norton SD program problem
q: Each time I use the Norton SD program I get 'Invalid COMMAND.COM cannot load COMMAND, system halted' when it finishes, though it works fine the next time. I'm on a Compaq Plus 2. Any suggestions?
a: Speed Disk moves files around to make them contiguous. If COMMAND.COM was fragmented and was moved, anything remembering its old cluster location, like fastopen, a disk cache or buffers, now points at the wrong place. A warm boot fixes it. Don't run it with such stuff active.

subject: SOLOMON?
q: Has anybody heard of or used a software package called SOLOMON? It's either a database or accounting software that runs on networked PCs, and I want to know what it is.
a: It's an accounting and inventory control package, and a good one by all reviews. It's meant to run on a network, not one lonely PC. Expect roughly $3000 for the base system and $1000 per module, from memory. Quality costs, kid.

subject: CompuAdd
q: Has anyone had good or bad experiences dealing with CompuAdd? A friend is ordering a 286 PC from them.
a: Mixed. One shop used CompuAdd 386s exclusively with no problems and helpful tech support. Another got 286s with lots of trouble, slow warranty service, and a monitor that belched blue smoke. Prices are good, quality's a gamble. Shocking.

subject: How to match up directories on different drives - query
q: How can I back up a hard disk subdirectory to a floppy so it lands in the matching subdirectory, ideally from a batch file?
a: Get DOS 3.2 or 3.3 and use XCOPY with /s for subdirectories and /m to copy only files with the archive bit set. Then wrap it in a batch file. Otherwise you're hard coding batch files, so read the manual.

subject: Full pathname of file wanted
q: How can I get the full pathname of a file given relative to the current directory, for example ..\SUB2\MYFILE.EXT from C:\SUBA\SUB1, to pass to another program?
a: In C it's trivial: grab the current directory with getcwd() and append the supplied path, adding a backslash if needed. Or change to that directory and get the working directory, which returns the full path. Tell us the language next time.

subject: How may I print full IBM char set on QMS PS 810?
q: How can I print a text file with the full IBM extended character set on a QMS PS 810 laser printer? Emulations didn't work.
a: If the file's small, use SCRtoPS. It grabs the PC screen and converts it to encapsulated PostScript, with the full IBM character set. It's a screenful at a time, so not elegant, but it works.

subject: Windows/386 & Lotus 1-2-3 Version 3.00
q: How can I run Lotus 1-2-3 Version 3.0 under Windows/386 Version 2.11?
a: You can't. Lotus 3.0 wants protected mode, and Windows/386 only gives you a real mode virtual machine. Drop back to 2.2, run 3.0 under OS/2, or wait for the Unix version. Complain to the vendors, not me.

subject: Interleave factor on a 6300
q: How can I tell the current interleave factor on my AT&T 6300 hard disk? I have Norton Utilities. Is 1:4 recommended, and how do I change it?
a: Run the Norton SI program. If the hard disk performance ratio against the XT is below 1.0, your interleave is probably wrong. Changing it means a low level format; keep trying factors until it reaches 1.0 or better. 3 to 6 is usual for 10 and 20 meg disks.

subject: serial port problems... HELP!
q: How do I get 3 COM ports working on a PC with a modem and a two-port serial card? I've tried everything in TFM.
a: COM1 and COM3 share IRQ 4, while COM2 and COM4 share IRQ 3. That's your trouble. Your software has to let you pick the address and interrupt; Qmodem has an install for it. Basic PC stuff, sigh.

subject: from 1 to 2 hard disks.
q: How do I go from one hard disk to two on my PC? My controller has one 34-pin and two 20-pin connectors, and one of each is already cabled to the drive.
a: Exactly as you guessed: clamp a second 34-pin connector in the middle of the ribbon cable. The end drive becomes drive 2. Change the drive-select jumper, and pull the terminating resistor from the middle drive. Not rocket science.

subject: MSWord 5.0 <-> BITNET <-> MacWord 4.0 -- Help Needed
q: How do I move MS Word 5.0 documents from a PC over BITNET to MacWord 4.0 and keep the formatting? Is uuencoding and mailing the file reasonable?
a: Use Microsoft Rich Text Format, the only way that keeps all the formatting. Don't confuse it with the DCA(RFT) option. In Word 5.0 the RTF converter is an external program, so look in your Word directory. RTF is plain ASCII, so mail it directly. Sigh.

subject: Nestled Batch Files Under MS-DOS
q: How do I run a batch file from inside a for loop in another batch file under MS-DOS? The second batch runs once and never returns to the first.
a: Precede the call with command /c, which loads another copy of the command interpreter that returns to the first when done. Like so: for %%1 %%2 %%3 in (*.plt) do command /c f001. Standard DOS; look it up.

subject: How do you do concurrency?
q: How do Windows or GEM run several processes concurrently under MS-DOS? Are there software procedures I could use to do this myself?
a: Not as you think. GEM isn't multitasking at all, as far as I know. It lets several tasks sit resident but runs only one at a time, so it's more a shell and program manager. Can't speak for Windows. Check your definitions before asking.

subject: Norton si - how does it determine the cpu?
q: How does the Norton si program decide which CPU you have? On my V30 machine it sometimes says V30 and sometimes V20.
a: Don't know how SI does it, but one way is prefetch queue length. Run a bunch of identical short instructions, use self-modifying code to change one n bytes ahead, and see if the change executes. Queue length is unique per chip. Disable interrupts first, obviously.

subject: Invalid drive problem
q: I boot my PS/2 Model 55 SX from a PC-DOS 3.3 floppy, but DOS says "Invalid drive specification" for C: and D:, where OS/2 1.1 EE lives. Why can't I use the hard disk when booting from diskette?
a: Because the OS/2 1.1 partitions use a bigger FAT than DOS 3.3 understands. It only knows 12 and 16 bit FATs, and the partition ID byte tells it which is which. Try DOS 4.01 or Compaq DOS 3.31. Basic stuff.

subject: changing AT's clock
q: I bought a used 8 MHz NEC AT-compatible whose memory looks rated for 12 MHz. Can I just swap the CPU and clock to 12 MHz for cheap speed?
a: Probably won't work. The expansion bus takes its timing straight from the CPU clock, so your slots would run at 12 MHz too, and at least one card will likely choke. The glue chips may cope, but the cards won't. Read the other thread on it.

subject: Trouble getting files from SIMTEL20
q: I download .ARC files from SIMTEL20 with Unix ftp and then move them to my PC, but PKXARC says the archives are all screwed up. Are they pre-compressed or a new archiver?
a: Probably not the files. Bad transfers happen maybe 5% of the time, and re-downloading fixes it. But more than five in a row points at your un-arc utility being suspect. Check your tools first.

subject: Question Re: 386 memory
q: I have a 386 clone with a Micronics 20 MHz board and 1 MB RAM, but programs show 0 expanded and 0 extended memory. How can I use this RAM?
a: It's set up as expanded memory, so you need the EMS driver that came with the board. That's micemm2c.sys, and it uses the 386 page mapping to emulate EMS. Put device=micemm2c.sys 0 (384) in CONFIG.SYS. RTFM next time.

subject: looking for Microsoft-compatible Z-80 cross-assembler
q: I need a Z-80 cross-assembler for MS-DOS that's compatible with Microsoft's macro assembler for CP/M. The PD one on simtel20 isn't. Any suggestions?
a: Try the MSDOS Z-80 cross assembler from the C Users' Group. There's also HI-TECH C, an MSC 5.1 compatible Z80 cross-compiler, supplied by Grey Matter in the UK. They advertise in BYTE. Look around before you ask, sigh.

subject: Loading Device Drivers at the DOS prompt
q: I need to write a program that loads device drivers from the DOS prompt. Character drivers work, but I'm lost on block device drivers and which DOS tables need updating. Is there a reference?
a: Get the DOS Programmer's Reference, 2nd edition, by Dettmann and Kyle, published by Que. It has extensive info on installable device drivers. Go read it instead of guessing at tables.

subject: Memory upgrade - WHAT IS WRONG?
q: I replaced 18 64k drams with 18 256k drams in my AT and set the switch for 1 meg, but I get 'Memory no match - Run SETUP' and only 512k plus 512k extended. How do I get 640k base?
a: Do the math. 18 chips of 256 kbits is only 576K, or 512K with parity, so your board won't take more without more banks. Run SETUP and tell it you have 512K and the message goes away. Sigh.

subject: C: not a valid drive
q: I replaced the 10 MB ST-412 in my IBM PC-XT with a 20 MB ST-225. C: says invalid drive specification and Fdisk says error reading fixed disk. Does it need a low-level format?
a: Yes, swap in a drive from a different maker and a low-level format is in order, any fool knows that. Also be wary of that old IBM controller, which probably only supports 10 meg. A newer controller runs $100-$150 and handles bigger drives.

subject: How do ya when your FATs corrupt?
q: I use the Norton utilities to save a copy of my FAT table, but how do I know if the FAT was good to start with?
a: There are two copies of the FAT, so run a binary compare on them. Both being identically corrupted is unlikely. Norton DT will also check your FAT area. A bad FAT is usually catastrophic anyway, so DOS will loudly tell you.

subject: PK ARC version 3.5 Help
q: I uudecoded PK ARC 3.5 from comp.binaries.ibm.pc and got PKX35A35.EXE instead of the .COM the instructions mention. I moved it to my PC with kermit and it just locks up DOS 3.1. What's wrong?
a: The .EXE is correct; the .COM in the instructions is a typo. Your lockup is almost certainly because you didn't set FILE TYPE BINARY in Kermit before transferring. Basic stuff.

subject: Tape Drive Suggestion?
q: I want a tape drive for my PC under US$400, usable in MS-DOS and SCO Unix. The Colorado drive takes up a floppy connector. Can I still have two floppies and the tape drive?
a: Yes. The newer Jumbo models with rev 40 firmware work without a separate controller even with a B drive, since it runs in parallel with B, though not at the same time. Rev 39 supposedly works too. Read the Computer Shopper ads for prices.

subject: Data Transfer - Laptop to PC
q: I want to type notes on a cheap laptop or a Tandy 102 and move them to my XT at home. Can I use the serial port, and how do I transfer the data?
a: Connect the two machines by serial ports and run a transfer program such as Procomm or Telix. Detailed instructions are in tspfon29.arc on chyde.uwasa.fi by anonymous ftp. Once set up, it's no sweat. Read the file instead of asking.

subject: Drive controllers
q: I'm building my own PC with three or four floppy drives, mixed 5 1/4 and 3 1/2. How are the extra two drives addressed, by device number and by drive letter?
a: DOS gives A: and B: to the first two floppies, then the hard disk takes C: and D:. The others must be installed as external devices in CONFIG.SYS and end up as E: and F:. Also, your BIOS has to support four floppies, and some don't.

subject: Novell & Microsoft Windows
q: I'm out of memory running PageMaker and a scanner program under Windows on my Novell network. Is there a program that loads the Novell ipx and net drivers into high memory?
a: On a 386 there's Hi386 from Rybs Electronics, which works well unless your hardware is funky. Mine choked on an expanded memory card and a hard drive's ROM. Without a 386, get the HiCard2, a board with 256K for buffer space for drivers. Buy hardware, I guess.

subject: Keep PC on constantly?
q: I'm setting up a BBS and want to leave my PC running constantly. Is it better to turn the monitor off or just blank the screen, and will turning it off hurt the VGA card?
a: Turn the monitor off. That won't hurt anything, and it saves the monitor from sitting there burning. Get a UPS or some other power protection for the whole box too, since power glitches are a fact of life. Sigh, basic stuff.

subject: "pc-compatible" printers
q: Is a 24-pin dot-matrix printer worth it over a 9-pin, and what about the Epson LQ series or Panasonic 1124?
a: Graphics are much nicer on 24-pin, and prices are low enough that there's little reason to buy a 9-pin. The Epson LQ 500 is a nice printer. Without a driver for the LQ, graphics get stretched, so don't whine later.

subject: Hard Cards
q: Is it better to install a hard card, or an internal hard drive in place of the B: floppy?
a: There's no real difference. Many cheap hard cards are just a standard WD controller with a 3.5 inch drive bolted to a card. The card spares you the floppy mounting and screw-thread nonsense, and you keep your floppy for backups. Any idiot can see that.

subject: drive interface speeds
q: Is synchronous SCSI different from asynchronous in terms of cables and controllers? An article says synchronous SCSI uses different controllers and cables.
a: No, you're confusing synchronous with differential SCSI. Synchronous and asynchronous are logical protocols with nothing to do with cabling. Differential is the hardware option, with different drivers and termination for longer cables and better noise immunity. Learn the difference.

subject: Seagate ST225 D.O.A.
q: Is the Seagate ST225 20 meg drive any good or a perennial troublemaker? Ours made bicycle-in-the-spokes noises, needed power switch fiddling and now gives seek errors.
a: Mixed opinions. One report says Seagate made a big batch of marginal ST-225s and the recent ones are fine again. The old ones were the VW Bugs of hard disks. Yours sounds like one of the bad batch. Surprise.

subject: Are there Font-manipulation utilities for DOS?
q: Is there a DOS utility that lets me examine my current default font, make small changes, and reload it?
a: Grab FONTEDIT, a PC Magazine utility, which should be on SIMTEL with the rest of the PC Mag stuff. It captures whatever font is currently displayed, supports global changes, and can save and load font files. Honestly, you'd have found it if you'd looked.

subject: Need Imagen Driver for MS/DOS or MS Windows
q: Is there a PC word processing package or MS Windows driver that supports Imagen impPRESS, or a PostScript or LaserJet to impPRESS or troff translator?
a: Elan Computer Group sells EROFF for MS-DOS, a TROFF package with support for Imagen printers, the HP LaserJet and PostScript. It includes TROFF, NROFF, PIC, EQN, TBL, GRAP and a rough previewer. It's derived from AT&T DWB 2.0, the real thing, not a rewrite.

subject: Cache programs
q: Is there a PD, shareware or commercial disk cache program for PC clones that can use extended or expanded memory, like Compaq's?
a: Mace Utilities includes three programs that cache a hard disk in conventional, extended or expanded memory, from Golden Bow Systems. Lightning is another. Both are commercial. Nothing free that I know of; pay up.

subject: VME <=> PC bus
q: Is there a device that links a PC bus to a VME bus so my PC can be a peripheral on the VME bus? If not, is there a fast, simple, short-haul link?
a: Ajida Technologies sells a unit that gives the PC lots of control of the VME bus. Drawback: it's master-only, so no VME master can address your PC. If that won't do, there are 386 PC compatibles that plug into VME and do both master and slave.

subject: Is there such a thing as a serial port expander?
q: Is there a serial port expander, a smart switch that plugs into one serial port and connects several devices by an escape code? I can't add a serial board.
a: Nobody sells exactly that in this thread. The usual answer is a multiport serial expansion board such as Arnet's, which gives you extra ports. Under DOS you need drivers to get COM4 and up. Do your homework on what your OS and application support.

subject: chip speed
q: Is there a simple relationship between microprocessor speed and memory chip speed? What chips do I need for a 10MHz 80286 and a 4.77MHz 8088?
a: In general there isn't. It depends on board design, other chips and clocks. 100ns is probably fine for the 286 and almost surely for the 8088. If it works, don't worry. Otherwise read the manual or buy the fastest, though 80ns is surely enough.

subject: Ever heard of a mac emulator?
q: Is there a software Mac emulator, possibly public domain, that runs Macintosh software on an XT-class PC?
a: Never heard of one, and it would be ungodly slow. It would need a clone of the Mac Toolbox, so it surely wouldn't be public domain, and Apple's lawyers would descend. The Amiga's AMAX does it with real Mac ROMs and costs around $600.

subject: "script" for MS-DOS?
q: Is there a utility for MS-DOS that behaves like the UNIX script command, writing everything that goes to the screen into a file?
a: Crude option: run a second COMMAND.COM with its output redirected to a file, then exit with ^Z. You won't see anything on screen while doing it, which is a rotten disadvantage. Another approach hooks int 21, but misses BIOS or direct hardware output. DOS, what do you expect?

subject: desperately seeking vt100 emulator
q: Is there a vt100 emulator for the PC that uses the keyboard to send the same escape sequences as a real vt100 keyboard in application mode? PC-VT uses function keys, and Qmodem isn't true vt100.
a: Have you tried Procomm 2.4.2? It was the only suggestion offered for VT-100 emulation. Try it before whining about every other emulator.

subject: Switching from Protected to Real Mode
q: Is there a way for a program to switch a 286 from protected mode back to real mode without rebooting the machine?
a: Supposedly yes. Rumor has it there's an undocumented 286 instruction that does it, and Microsoft likes it so much they wanted Intel to leave it in the 386. Another report says it involves a double fault, and Microsoft wants to patent it. Patenting a hack, sigh.

subject: hooking PC's together
q: Is there a way to hook two PCs together via the parallel ports to transfer files quickly? The serial ports are used.
a: Yes, there are parallel-port file transfer programs. One reply bought The Interchange for $39.95, and others named Direc-link, Paranet and File Shuttle. PC Magazine, January 12, 1988, has a whole section on data transfer programs. Go read it, not every one supports parallel.

subject: Searching for 8514-compatible Adapter
q: Is there any company making a graphics adapter compatible with the IBM 8514/A that fits the standard AT bus? Headland, Genoa, Tseng?
a: Not yet, but several are expected to announce at Fall Comdex for delivery before year end. Hints have come from Headland, Paradise, Genoa and STB. Paradise or Headland will likely be first, being the chip developers. Real soon, in the cosmic sense. Be patient.

subject: Standing a PC on Its Side and a Mouse Question
q: Is there anything wrong with running an IBM PC standing on its side? Also, any pros and cons of a bus mouse versus a serial mouse?
a: Standing it on end is fine. Drives are mounted both ways and there's no evidence it matters, and you get more table space. The only con anyone knows of is none. Ignore the folk wisdom about data falling off the platters. Didn't answer the mouse bit.

subject: AT&T 6386 WGS / 16mhz / 1mb Config. Problem
q: My 16MHz AT&T 6386 WGS shows 640k base, 0k extended and 384k dedicated memory, and MS-Windows 3 won't run in standard or 386 mode. What do I need?
a: You can't run enhanced mode without at least 1Mb of extended memory. That 384k "dedicated" memory is most likely shadow RAM for the BIOS, so it doesn't count. Add more memory, or just run 286 protected mode. Basic stuff.

subject: A question about hard disk
q: My 60 Mbyte Seagate ST-277R-1 RLL drive with autopark makes a strange sound for about 5 seconds after power off, like a stick in a fan's blades. Does anyone know what it is?
a: That's the autopark. It apparently uses the disk's momentum in some mechanical operation to park the heads, and the noise is that action. Other Seagate drives do it too. Nothing to worry about, so quit fretting.

subject: expanding memory?
q: My 8 meg motherboard has 1 meg installed as 36 256k x 1 bit chips and not enough sockets to add 3 more meg. Do I have to replace all the 256k x 1 chips to get to 4 meg?
a: Yes, more or less. A row of RAM is one 32-bit word plus parity, and every chip in a row must be the same size. You can probably add 36 megabit chips to reach five meg. Cheaper than you'd fear, so quit whining.

subject: Compaq Deskpro 8086
q: My 8086 Compaq Deskpro with a 20 MB hard disk won't boot from the hard disk since I reformatted and went from MS-DOS 2.11 to PC-DOS 3.3. It boots fine from a floppy and the disk works afterward. Any ideas?
a: Run FDISK and activate the hard disk partition. It almost certainly shows the partition but not as active, so the machine never looks for DOS on it. Copying boot records around with the debugger? Sigh. Read the manual first.

subject: Kermit and Procomm
q: My Procomm 2.4.2 with Kermit transfers text fine, but when I receive a binary like an exe or arc file it adds about a third more bytes and the file is ruined. I haven't changed any Kermit defaults. Any ideas?
a: Eight-bit quoting, most likely. The BBS claimed 8 bit no parity but sent the quote characters anyway, and Procomm wasn't looking for them, so it stuffed them into the file. A Fido was the root of it. They shouldn't quote on a true 8 bit path. Sigh.

subject: 80386 Bug - Does anybody else have it?
q: My Proteus 386 box has a 386 that fails the 32 bit integer multiply test. Does anybody know when Intel will clean up this mess and ship good chips?
a: Blame the clone maker, not Intel. Others have been getting good chips for months, and Proteus knowingly sold you a chip that didn't work properly. Intel has handled the buggy 386 as well as can be expected. Quick-buck vendors, sigh.

subject: Turbo Pascal / Wordperfect /Laserprinter
q: My Turbo Pascal graphs grabbed into WordPerfect 5.0 come out with black as black and white as white, which prints a mess on the laser printer. How do I fix it?
a: Load the WPG file, then choose Graphics Edit and INVERT it with the Switch key, usually Shift-F3. Also try grabbing the picture with black/white or white/black colours. Using WordPerfect is the right way, not screen dumps.

subject: Help with ANSI escape sequences
q: My Turbo Pascal program writes text containing ANSI escape sequences, but instead of clearing the screen or changing colors, ESCAPE shows up as a left arrow. How do I get Turbo to do the right thing?
a: The PC-DOS version of TP writes through the BIOS screen handler, bypassing DOS and ANSI.SYS. Try the {$P1} compiler directive, which forces DOS i/o calls for screen output. And use write, not writeln, unless you want the CR-LF. Sigh, read the compiler directive list.

subject: Help needed
q: My XT clone switches to 8MHz turbo from the keyboard but drops back to 4.77MHz after a software reset to text mode. How can I lock it at 8MHz?
a: Highly machine dependent, genius. Mine has a dip switch that locks it at 8 MHz, and the manual also described a software method. Open the case and flip the switch, and stop pressing three keys like a newbie.

subject: Bios upgrade for old AT
q: My old AT only supports 4-bit drive types, and IBM will only sell the BIOS upgrade with an overpriced drive. How can I get my AT to accept a 40 meg Miniscribe type 36 drive?
a: Burn your own ROMs. With an EPROM programmer and two 27256s, overwrite an unused drive table entry (sixteen 16-byte entries starting at 0xE401) with your drive's values, then fix the checksum byte. Otherwise the machine will sulk. Not for the faint of heart.

subject: set system clock?
q: My old IBM PC AT with DOS 3.0 forgets the time when I turn it off. How do I set the actual hardware system clock?
a: Run the SETUP program that came with your AT. The clock lives in the CMOS setup, same place you set display type, memory and disk types. The TIME command only touches DOS. And a GTO is a Pontiac, not a manual feature. Honestly.

subject: Ancient IBM PC wants more memory
q: My old IBM PC, model 5150, has 256k and I want to add memory, but dealers keep asking whether it's a PC 1 or PC 2. How can I find out which I have?
a: Look at the motherboard. If it has 16K RAM chips, it's almost certainly a PC-1. If it has 256K total on the motherboard, it's almost certainly a PC-2. Dealers who can't remember the machine are hopeless.

subject: NEC Multisync monitor and VGA adapter
q: My original NEC Multisync's video cable doesn't fit a VGA adapter, and NEC wants $49 for the pinout converter. Does anyone know a cheaper source for one?
a: Try Fry's Electronics in Fremont, California. They sold one for about $18. Forty-nine bucks for a cross-wiring gizmo is robbery; typical vendor nonsense.

subject: truncate() for MS-DOS
q: Neither Turbo C 2.0 nor Zortech C 2.06 has a function like Unix truncate(). Is there an equivalent for MS-DOS?
a: Position the file where you want EOF, then write zero bytes to it with the DOS call. It won't work through stdio fseek() and fwrite() because of buffering, but lseek() and write() might, if they pass straight to DOS. Don't count on it.

subject: Norton Utilities locking up PS2 55 SX
q: Norton Utilities 4.5 locks up on a PS/2 55 SX, for example the directory sort utility. Is there a special version for these machines?
a: No special version needed. Norton runs fine on a 55SX if IBM's XMAEM and XMA2EMS drivers aren't installed. Use another extended-to-expanded converter instead. IBM's drivers fight with Microsoft's, like HiMem.Sys. Typical.

subject: Problems with Compaq SLT/286 and QuickBasic 4.5
q: On my Compaq SLT/286 with Compaq DOS 4.01, running Microsoft QuickBasic 4.5 on battery power turns the screen completely white, but never on the AC adaptor. Microsoft and Compaq blame each other. Any ideas?
a: The DACs in the SLT VGA are turned off on battery, since they're power hogs. The app reads FF from them at startup and writes it back, giving white. Compaq has a little program that turns the DACs on. Ask support properly, and the blame game ends.

subject: Do OTHER hard drive brands fail to spin up?
q: Seagate drives are always reported failing to spin up at boot. Do other brands of hard drives fail the same way?
a: Sure. Apple had Quantum HD40s seizing from a spindle lubrication defect, a Priam RLL drive had spin-up problems, and a Miniscribe 8450 sometimes fails to spin up on first power-on. Seagate may just be the most popular, so its failures show up more.

subject: Telix 3.11 bug?
q: Telix 3.11 sends a garbage 4-character string whenever my BBS sends a Ctrl-E (ENQ), even when the ENQ answerback string is empty or changed. My own copy doesn't do it. Is this a bug?
a: Not a bug, a feature. Turn off the auto-CIS download feature, since CIS uses ENQ as a protocol initializer and Telix answers it. Read the docs before you cry bug. Fine on CIS, a nuisance everywhere else.

subject: Logitech Mouse Driver & Microsoft Word 5.0 Incompatibility
q: The Logitech mouse driver release 3.43 seems incompatible with Microsoft Word 5.0, and the screen fills with garbage colors and characters. Is there a fix?
a: Get the newer Logitech driver from their BBS; it was written to fix exactly that. Someone reports beta version 4TI works fine. You may have to be registered. Maybe read the vendor's docs before whining at Usenet.

subject: NS16550 ACE question
q: The NS16550 ACE docs say it asserts THRE only when the transmit queue is empty. That makes no sense if the FIFO is supposed to be transparent. Is the spec wrong?
a: Spec's fine, you're missing the point. The chip exists to cut system load: interrupting on every free slot would mean an interrupt per character. It interrupts when the queue is nearly empty instead. And use the 16550A, not the 16550.

subject: pc vt100 terminal emulation and IBM mainframe's
q: Using Procomm 2.1 with VT100 emulation on an IBM mainframe, I'm stuck at the MORE... prompt. What key clears the screen, or what's the escape sequence for the VT100 keypad ENTER?
a: It depends on what your async gateway maps to the 3270 clear key. Try ESC followed by a period to clear the screen. For PF1 to PF12 use ESC 1 through ESC 0, then ESC minus and ESC equals. Procomm's VT100 emulation isn't perfect, so grumble at it.

subject: PC WatchDog problem
q: WatchDog security software on my PC-AT locks the hard disk when I boot from floppy, and I get "invalid drive specification". Can I boot from the floppy and get at my files?
a: WatchDog marks the partition as non-DOS, so DOS programs won't touch it. If the disk is encrypted, you're stuck with a low-level format. If not, use BIOS calls, not DOS calls, to read the blocks, find the autoexec file, and edit out the offending program.

subject: Virus help
q: We have a virus outbreak on our PCs. What's a good detector and eradicator, and where can I get it and an unzip program without simtel ftp?
a: Dial John McAfee's BBS. It has scanners for standalone PCs and networks, removal programs, and an unZip utility. The files come with validation programs so you can check them for contamination. Hardly mysterious.

subject: CMI DRIVE
q: What AT drive type should I use for a CMI CM6426 hard drive with 4 heads and 640 cylinders?
a: Type 2. The CMI-6426 is a 20 megabyte unit, the same drive IBM first put in the AT, and type 2 only formats 615 cylinders, but you get no other choice. Don't trust it with data you care about, since those early CMI drives were lemons.

subject: What is a .BOO file?
q: What archiver makes .BOO files, and where do I get it? ZOO doesn't work on them.
a: It's not an archiver, genius. BOO is like uuencode but incompatible, and the files come out longer, not compressed. Grab msbpct.bas, .pas or .c from /kermit/a, or the executables from /kermit/bin, and unBOO it.

subject: ibm ps/2 error 163
q: What causes a 162 and 163 error at boot on a PS/2 Model 60? Is it the battery, the external 5 1/4 drive, or dasddrvr.sys?
a: Could be the battery, but one machine's old battery measured fine and worked after reinstalling. Maintenance said dasddrvr.sys or external high-density 5 1/4 drives can cause similar errors. Try pulling the battery so the config memory is lost, then reinitialize. Sigh.

subject: What do YOU KNOW/THINK of POWER C by MIx Software Inc.
q: What do users think of Power C by Mix Software? Is it comparable to Quick C and Turbo C, and what about its windowing package?
a: It works great for one user. The library is a superset of Turbo C's, so Turbo C programs compile fine, while MSC programs need some name changing. The Magna Charta windowing package looks nice, but its manual could use pictures. Not bad for fifty bucks, I suppose.

subject: Lost clusters, chains, and files
q: What does "1 lost cluster found in 1 chain, convert lost chains to files?" from CHKDSK mean, and can I recover without reformatting?
a: A file is a chain of clusters. When a chain gets unhooked from its directory entry, say a crash before close, it's still allocated but belongs to nothing. Run CHKDSK /F and it makes FILEnnnn.CHK files in the root directory. No reformat needed. Read the manual.

subject: Dos disk buffering schemes
q: What does BUFFERS= in config.sys do? DOS seems to hit the disk on every read when I seek around a COFF file.
a: The buffers are only used for partial-sector reads and writes. Read or write a complete sector and DOS transfers directly between your buffer and the disk. Every MS-DOS C I've seen uses a 512 byte buffer, exactly one sector. So no, there's no crude cache to rescue you.

subject: Layered M/B?
q: What does it mean for a motherboard to be "layered", like a 4-layered motherboard? Are all motherboards layered?
a: It means what it says: several layers of glass sandwiched together to fit more conductor paths into less space. Most motherboards are 3 or more layers these days. Watch for interference and capacitance effects, though.

subject: Which Word Processor in 1987?
q: What editor or word processor would you pick for C code development on a PS/2 Model 50? Is there one that knows the new displays and the mouse, and what was the Atex look-alike editor for MS-DOS?
a: Don't use a word processor for code, any idiot knows that. If you know EMACS, get Epsilon from Lugaru, which has a C-like language and a C mode with source. The Atex look-alike is XyWrite, I think.

subject: WHat happened to Norton's SA?
q: What happened to Norton's SA (Screen Attributes) program? It was in every version of the Norton Utilities up to 4.0 but is missing from 4.5. Why was it removed?
a: It wasn't removed, you just didn't read the docs. SA got folded into BE, the Batch Enhancer, so you now type BE SA followed by the same old arguments. Same usage, extra prefix. Read the manual next time.

subject: pd:<msdos.games> on simtel20
q: What happened to the games directory on simtel20? I went to ftp nethack and the directory is gone.
a: The games got axed, DOS and UNIX both. Word is a new boss decided they had to go. Some are still scattered through the pd1:<pc-blue> volumes, and you can get nethack, omega and moria source from uunet.uu.net. Then compile it yourself, like a grown-up.

subject: What is PROFS?
q: What is PROFS?
a: It's an office mail and scheduling system that runs under VM/CMS. Big IBM mainframe stuff, nothing to do with your PC. Wrong newsgroup, too.

subject: Publish-It Lite
q: What is Timeworks Publish-It Lite like, and how does it differ from Publish-It? What are its drawing tools and import formats?
a: Lite is a subset of Publish It, which has only primitive tools: pixel, line, box, circle, rounded box. The big difference is that Lite won't generate 300 dpi output, so even on a LaserJet you get dot-matrix quality. Pay for the real one, for crying out loud.

subject: archive bit
q: What is the archive bit on a DOS file for, and is there a way to copy protect specific files?
a: Backup sets it, and DOS sets it whenever a file is modified, so backup programs can archive only changed files. No easy copy protection without odd formatting. To keep novices out, mark files hidden and system. Read the DOS manual.

subject: UUCP software for a p.c.?
q: What programs exist to turn a PC into a UUCP dial-up node?
a: Uuslave is the most complete uucico clone. It does variable window size for the G protocol, master and slave modes, and it's been ported to MS-DOS. UULINK is another option. The public domain Uclone is only a half-working dialout toy. Sigh.

subject: Sound Boards - Speaker Recommendations
q: What speakers should I use with a PC sound board like the Sound Blaster or AdLib? The board puts out only a few watts, and I wonder if a 10W 8 ohm Radio Shack speaker is okay.
a: Skip the plain speakers; use a pair of amplified ones. Amplified AIWA speakers sound a lot better on an AdLib than ordinary ones, and amplified Bose were fantastic. Take your walkman along to try them, since that's what they're designed for. Obvious, really.

subject: Best Version Control Packages for PC?
q: What's the best version control package for a PC AT, preferably something behaving like RCS or SCCS?
a: PVCS from Polytron. It works well, is easy to set up, and has good vendor support. The commands map from RCS, with get like co and put like ci. It also handles binary files, which RCS won't. Polytron sells direct.

subject: v20 vs 8087
q: What's the difference between the V20 and the 8087 chips?
a: They're different animals. The V20 is a replacement CPU for the 8088 and highly compatible with it. The 8087 is a math coprocessor handling 32-bit integer and 32 or 64-bit float arithmetic. Basic hardware knowledge, folks.

subject: PROCOMM PLUS problem
q: When I use a Procomm Plus script file to log on to another computer, it gets impatient and sends the next step before the prompt arrives. Any suggestions?
a: Use the timing argument on WAITFOR. The default is 30 seconds, so WAITFOR "string" 60 gives you a minute, and FOREVER waits indefinitely. Other timed script commands take the same syntax. It's in the manual, chapter 11. Try reading it sometime.

subject: Phoenix BIOS and NMI problem
q: When compiling with Turbo C I sometimes get an NMI error asking to shut off NMI, reboot or continue. I was told the processor is going too fast for the compiler. What causes it?
a: Somebody is pulling your leg. Compilers don't care how fast the processor is. An NMI on a PC is usually a memory parity error, meaning a bad memory chip. Run the diagnostics that came with the machine and test your memory.

subject: Zmodem for 7-bit paths wanted
q: Where can I find a Zmodem that supports 7-bit paths?
a: You can't. ZMODEM requires 8-bit transmission, period. Unless somebody has hacked the original code into something foreign, it isn't an option. Read the protocol spec before asking.

subject: Info on Microsoft OMF
q: Where can I find an online description of the Microsoft OMF object file format used for .OBJ files from Microsoft C? Would reusing MS C 5.0 libraries under QNX work?
a: Microsoft OMF is a hacked version of Intel's, so Intel docs won't do. Ask Microsoft support, though it's probably quicker to buy the MS-DOS Encyclopedia, which defines it. I've never heard of an online version. Sorry, didn't touch the QNX part.

subject: word perfect format & writing a conversion prgm.
q: Where can I find documentation on the WordPerfect 5.0 file format so I can write a conversion program to XyWrite?
a: Ask WordPerfect Corp directly. They have a technical information package and documentation on the formats. Mind that 5.0 is quite different from 4.2 because of the graphics features. Honestly, try the vendor first before posting in caps.

subject: compression algorithms wanted
q: Where can I find source code or algorithms for data compression routines, mostly for ASCII text but maybe binary too?
a: Go read the book Data Compression by James Storer, from Computer Science Press. That's the pointer you get. Next time hit a library before bothering the net.

subject: Window development
q: Where can I get RC.EXE, the Windows resource compiler, and which C compilers work with it? Is there a development package from Microsoft?
a: It's in the Microsoft Windows Software Development Kit, around $450 to $500 and wildly overpriced. You need a Microsoft language, MSC 4 or later, Pascal or MASM. QuickC won't do. Nobody competes with it yet, so grumble and pay.

subject: IBM ROM BIOS upgrade kit
q: Where can I get an IBM PC ROM BIOS Upgrade Kit, part number 1501005? My neighbor's PC won't use the hard disk without it, and IBM and local dealers don't stock it.
a: The kit itself is gone, but the ROM chip is still floating about. Ask for part MK36C35N-4, program number 1501476. Mail-order outfits advertise it in Computer Shopper and PC Week, from about $25 to $50. Read the ads once in a while.

subject: modifying executables
q: Where my brother works they have a Fortran program with an error in it, reading wind direction off by 180 degrees, and no source code. Is there a way to modify the executable?
a: Get Sourcer, the commercial program advertised in PC Magazine. It turns binaries back into semi-commented assembler, and you work out the intent from context. Sigh, it's not magic, you'll be reading assembly, but that's what patching without source costs you.

subject: Who is Packard Bell and why are they making clones?
q: Who is Packard Bell and why are they making PC clones? Are they any good?
a: They're an old TV maker who built a neat 22-bit mini around 1960, sold it to Raytheon and went back to TVs. The current PC is a Korean clone. Their modems and monitors drew poor reports, so be wary.

subject: New Microsoft Word Question
q: Why do fonts like TMSRMN change between Microsoft Word printer drivers when I switch from the HPLASPS to the OKILASER driver? Is it a Microsoft screw-up?
a: Microsoft doesn't try hard to put corresponding fonts in the same slots across printer files, and documents store the font's position, not its name. Fix it with MAKEPRD: convert the PRD to text, change the font numbers like {F16 to {F24, and convert back. An hour's work, thanks Microsoft.

subject: DOS 4.01 and SHARE.EXE
q: Why does DOS 4.01 insist on SHARE.EXE for large partitions, and how do you stop it complaining about the lack of SHARE at boot?
a: DOS 4.01 loads SHARE automatically on large volumes. To stop the squawking, load it yourself in CONFIG.SYS with INSTALL. SHARE is for file and record locking in multiuser setups. DOS assumes anyone with a disk over 32 MB must be on a network. Typical.

subject: expansion of *FOO.* = *.* ?!?
q: Why does DOS treat *FOO.* the same as *.*, and is there a patch to fix it?
a: DOS expands * to ???????? in the name and ??? in the extension, so *FOO.* becomes ????????FOO.??? and the FOO falls off past eight characters. It's a CP/M kludge, and MS calls it documented behavior. Replace command.com with a real Unix-style shell, like the MKS Korn shell.

subject: Microsoft C 4.0 spawn is a memory hog
q: Why does a program that spawns another one under Microsoft C 4.0 show 70K less free memory than running it from DOS, and is there a way around it?
a: Small model programs get 64K of data space by default. Use the linker's /CP switch, as in /CP:1, and LINK will work out how much to actually allocate. Reading the linker docs would have told you that.

subject: ARC standards
q: Why isn't there a standard ARC file format that works across DOS, UNIX and VMS, maybe with built-in uuencoding?
a: ARC from SEAware is a standard of sorts, and UNIX programs handle it reasonably, plus a VMS reader exists. For real portability, zoo runs on BSD, SysV, MS-DOS, SunOS and VMS. Use that and quit whining.

subject: NEC V30
q: Will the NEC V30 really run 80186 code?
a: Yes. Assembling 80186 mnemonics and converting them to NEC ones produced identical object code, so the V30 runs 80186 code and the V20 runs 80188. It even has extras, like executing Z80 code. Obvious to anyone who read the spec.

subject: Are there better PC power supplies
q: Are there better PC power supplies? Mine died and took the motherboard, modem and tape drive with it, and I want a quality 250W supply for a tower case.
a: Get a PC Power & Cooling supply, about the only name brand around. The Turbo-Cool 300 runs in a tower, goes for around $165, and is quiet. Not cheap, but cheap no-name junk is what killed your machine in the first place.

subject: Non-standard text modes on VGA and SVGA?
q: How do I set the non-standard text modes like 132x43, 132x25 and 80x50 on VGA and SVGA cards? Does it depend on the BIOS or card?
a: It depends on the chipset. On a Paradise card, an INT 10H call with AX of 0054 hex gives 132x43 and 0055 hex gives 132x25. For 80x43 and 80x50, use an ANSI.SYS-type driver's escape codes, or on MSDOS 5.0 just type MODE CON: 80 50. RTFM for your card.

subject: 386-33 Motherboard
q: If I buy a 386-33 whose motherboard maxes out at 16 MB and has no 32-bit memory slot, am I limiting my upgrade path? Is there any need for more than 16 MB on an 80386?
a: Not if all you run is DOS. But with UNIX or OS/2 you'll happily use more than 16 megs, and X terminal servers eat all the memory you give them. Sixteen megs of DOS is just a 15.5M ramdisk, ha.

subject: S.I. index of 386SX
q: My 386SX scores an S.I. index of 7.1 at 8MHz and 15.3 at 16MHz, while my cheap XT-286 at 8MHz gets 8.4. I was warned the 386SX is slightly slower MHz for MHz than a 286. Any comment?
a: The warning was correct. But one benchmark proves nothing about your uses, and Norton's SI is skewed toward more powerful CPUs; a 386/22 gets 23.0 when 10-15 would be saner. Stop worshipping a single number.

subject: Is there a virus in QEMM Ver. 5.1 ??
q: A hex string showed up in QEMM 5.1 files that looks like a virus signature. Is there a virus in QEMM 5.1?
a: No, it is NOT a virus. The hex string turned out to be part of the warm boot instruction, which install.exe and optimize.com both use. Scanners and CRC checks found nothing. Somebody jumped to conclusions again. Sigh.

subject: 'Divide Overflow' Error
q: A student gets a 'Divide Overflow' error whenever she accesses a certain database in dBASE through Assist mode. Any clues?
a: Only a guess: dBASE recalculates field and entry information when a file loads, so the database file is probably corrupted. Write a program to extract whatever data you can and rebuild the file. It's tedious. How it got corrupted is the real question.

subject: MS Word 5.5 mouse problems
q: After installing MS Word 5.5 on a DEC VAXmate, touching the mouse freezes the whole machine. It works fine without a mouse driver. Has anyone fixed this?
a: Take VSHIELD out of memory. Someone had the same freeze, pulled the virus shield TSR, and Word ran fine with the mouse. Your driver was never the problem. Learn what your TSRs are doing before you blame the vendor.

subject: Dos 5 -- Where did all these hidden files come from ?
q: After upgrading to DOS 5 I found hidden files like FILENAME._XE, ._OM, ._YS and ._RV, 77 bytes each, for every EXE, COM, SYS and DRV on my drive. What are they and do I need them?
a: Not DOS 5. Those are almost certainly from Norton Antivirus or a similar inoculation program. They're control files holding each file's length, CRC and other info to check it hasn't been tampered with. Yes, they eat clusters. Install a virus checker, pay the price.

subject: Kermit 3.10 C-p problem using no emulation
q: After upgrading to MS-Kermit 3.10 with no terminal emulation on an Olivetti M24, pressing control P in GNU emacs sometimes inserts a flood of ^Q characters until I press ^Q. What causes this?
a: Probably your keyboard, not Kermit. M24 keyboards are notorious for wearing out and not debouncing quickly, so autorepeat kicks in even though the key looks released. The new Kermit just reacts faster. Take it apart and thoroughly clean the Ctrl, P and Q keys.

subject: coherent and windows3
q: Are Coherent and Windows 3 incompatible? I'd like to use Windows 3 as a windowing manager under Coherent on a 386.
a: They're incompatible. Windows 3.0 is a DOS application that runs on top of DOS, and Coherent doesn't support DOS applications. The vendor said a flat no when asked. Did you really expect otherwise?

subject: ZIPfiles and a 386/25
q: Are there problems unZIPping on a 386? Borland C++ install on my ALR 386/25 gives random CRC failures in UNZIP, and different files fail each time.
a: Try copying the files to the hard drive and unzipping them there. That cured the same flaky floppy unzipping on my 286 at 1.2 meg. Then see if the zip files pass the -t test. Check the drive before blaming the CPU.

subject: making 720K floppy 1.44M
q: Can I write a device driver for DOS that bypasses the BIOS and talks straight to the drive controller, so a 720K floppy drive treats disks as 1.44M? Does one already exist?
a: Yes, it can be done and has been. Many drive makers ship such drivers with the hardware. One guy even disabled the 1.44M hole check with a soldering iron. Honestly, a 1.44 disk costs next to nothing, so it isn't worth the bother.

subject: How do I determine the clock speed?
q: Can anyone give me code, preferably in Pascal, that will determine the clock speed of a PC?
a: You can't determine the CPU clock speed of an arbitrary PC. Best you can do is time an instruction mix against a known system like the PC/XT, and that number says little about the real clock. Look at INFOPLUS in Turbo Pascal source on SIMTEL20. Sigh.

subject: Looking for a good version of nroff for MS-DOS
q: Does anyone have a suggestion for a good version of nroff for MS-DOS, something that just works without a lot of testing?
a: Elan sells eroff for the PC, with both nroff and troff built from licensed AT&T code. It's solid and runs on PC, Sun, VMS and SCO too. Pay for it instead of testing freeware junk.

subject: FTP sites
q: Does anyone know of good FTP sites for public-domain PC software?
