a: Read the FAQ on FTP sites, /pc/ts/tsfaq18.arc, available from garbo.uwasa.fi. Or stick around and read the news first, starting with comp.binaries.ibm.pc.d. This comes up every week; try reading before asking.

subject: reading system timer?
q: How can I read the PC system timer channel 0 counter without stopping the timer and the 18.2 per second interrupts?
a: You issued a load command, 36h. Send a timer latch command, 00h, instead. The timer keeps running and you read the count as of the latch. Use it for fine timing all the time. RTFM next time.

subject: FTP help
q: I FTP a .ZIP file and download it to my IBM PC with Kermit through Procomm, but pkunzip gives an error. Do I need to convert it first?
a: First, are you ftping in binary mode? Of course not, probably. Second, if you're kermiting from a VAX/VMS system, you may have to convert the file type between Stream/LF and Fixed 512. I forget which way, so check.

subject: IBM XT dip switch settings
q: I can't find my Guide to Operations for the IBM XT. What are the dip switch settings?
a: Switch 1 is normal operation and must be off. Switch 2 is the coprocessor, 3 and 4 are system board memory, 5 and 6 are the display type, and 7 and 8 are the number of 5 1/4 inch drives. Keep your manuals, hmph.

subject: XT's and big hard drives -- PROBLEM
q: I have an XT with a 40 meg hard disk, and Ontrack's Disk Manager works under MS-DOS 3.2 but crashes under 4.01. How can I get DOS 4.01 to use the 40 meg disk?
a: DOS 4.01 handles disks over 32 meg natively, so skip the disk manager. Low-level format with the controller's formatter, partition with plain FDISK, then do a normal format, as the DOS manual says. Works fine on my XT for a year.

subject: RLL Interface
q: I was given a Western Digital RLL controller for an AT. Does it need special software or drivers, or is it treated like a normal MFM controller?
a: If you have an RLL drive, just connect the sucker up and off you go. No special drivers. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: Hard Disk Setup Problem - I Need Help
q: I'm installing a Miniscribe hard disk (771 cylinders, 4 heads, precomp 128, 26 sectors, 39 meg) on a 286 board, and the setup software's presets don't match. Can I enter the parameters manually?
a: No manual entry needed, maybe. The Miniscribe 20MB had a jumper that made the 4 head, 26 sector layout look like 6 heads by 17 sectors. That wastes a little space but matches BIOS type 2, I think. Dig out the drive documents and check the jumper.

subject: Seagate 1239A, Diskmangager, and DOS 5.0
q: Installing a Seagate 1239A IDE drive with DiskManager 4.20 under DOS 5.0, the machine locks up on boot when the DiskManager driver is in config.sys. What am I doing wrong?
a: DOS 5.0 ships an updated DiskManager driver, and the README says so, so use that one. Better yet, if the BIOS lacks the drive type, get a BIOS upgrade with a user-definable type and just use FDISK. Read the README.

subject: Hard drives
q: Is it possible to have two different hard drive controllers in one machine, like an RLL controller and an IDE controller, each with a drive?
a: Under UNIX you can mix MFM, RLL and ESDI. With DOS you can if the BIOS can be readdressed and the controller supports a secondary address. How DOS gets to the second one, no idea. Wouldn't bet on it.

subject: Upgrading *PCDOS* 3.30 to MSDOS5.0
q: Is it possible to use the MS-DOS 5.0 upgrade package to upgrade from PC-DOS 3.30?
a: Yes, it works, and it went smoothly on the first try. The old hidden IBMBIO.COM and IBMDOS.SYS stay behind and waste space. Unhide them with ATTRIB, delete them, then boot a DOS 5.0 floppy and SYS C:. Back up first, obviously. Don't trust dealers, but he was right this time.

subject: Looking for a PC-based mail front-end for IBM PROFs
q: Is there a PC-based mail front end for IBM's PROFS that pretends to be a 3270 connection and gives a friendly interface with local message filing?
a: PC/PROFS, from your local IBM rep. It's not bad if PROFS turns you on, especially if your word processor understands DCA and the mainframe has DISOSS up. Sigh, it's IBM, so expect to pay.

subject: How can I make ms-dos as much like unix as possible?
q: Is there a complete unix-like replacement for the MSDOS shell, and how can I make MS-DOS as much like unix as possible?
a: You're thinking of the MKS Toolkit from Mortice Kern Systems. It costs around $250, with a 50% educational discount, and gives you grep, awk, sed and vi, which MSDOS simply doesn't provide. Anyone who's used them won't go back.

subject: Is a 387/40 available?
q: Is there a math coprocessor for the 386/40? Has anyone heard of or used one?
a: Yes, there are. Cyrix makes one, and AMD perhaps too with their 386/40 clone. One user reports Checkit giving about 3087.9K Whetstones with a 40MHz IIT 3C87. Not exactly hard to find.

subject: vga fonts???????
q: Is there a program for VGA that changes the fonts in DOS, or one that lets you design your own fonts and load them?
a: Yes, there's a shareware thing called vfont. It loads a new font and stays resident to put it back when a program resets the font. Expect it to clash with some TSRs and drivers, and it died on a 486. Compaq DOS also ships two fonts, for 25K of driver.

subject: Help With Compaq Deskpro 386/20 Error Message...
q: My Compaq Deskpro 386/20 gives "162 - System Options Not Set (Run Setup)" and asks for a diagnostic disk. Do I need to buy one, and will it fix the soft reboot problem?
a: The CMOS battery has probably died, so the checksum is invalid. Replace it, then run a Compaq setup diskette or a shareware AT setup program like GSETUP31. You'll need to know your hard drive geometry. Honestly, the battery is the first thing to check.

subject: Memory Check
q: My PC's memory check at power-on now takes twice as long. It used to zip through. How can I make it fast again?
a: Check your CMOS settings. Sounds like you've got more wait-states than before. Basic stuff.

subject: Help needed for Norton Disk Doctor Usage
q: Norton Disk Doctor turns lost chains into files with a ._dd extension. What should I do with them, delete them or save them?
a: Delete them. Unless the lost clusters were part of a text file that got mangled, there's nothing useful to be done with them.

subject: extended memory
q: On a 286 AT with 640k conventional and 384k extended memory at 1 Megabyte, can I load TSRs and device drivers into extended memory to free up DOS memory? We don't have the C&T chipset.
a: Memory at FFFF:0010 starts at 1M, so enable A20 and put your TSRs there, leaving A20 always on. Adjust the CMOS extended memory size too. Anything else using extended memory will break it. Or just buy Quarterdeck's QRAM, for about $60, instead of hand-hacking.

subject: Lotus 123 v3.1, Netware, and HP IIIsi problem
q: Printing from Lotus 123 v3.1 over Netware 3.11 to an HP IIIsi gives garbage when printing special fonts, shading or graphics. Plain spreadsheets and local printing are fine. Why?
a: Likely a time-out on the Netware spooler. Lotus can spend more than the default 30 seconds between parts of a graph. Run CAPTURE /NA or CAPTURE /TI=60 before starting Lotus. That was my experience on older versions, anyway.

subject: 386 BIOS shadowing/remaping
q: QEMM386 can shadow or remap the BIOS into RAM. Could I write my own BIOS routines and have a 386 program use mine instead of the built-in ones?
a: Yes, two ways. Steal the BIOS interrupts and point them at your own code, or write your own BIOS and burn it to ROM to replace the chips. Writing into QEMM's shadow RAM is doubtful, since it probably protects it. Remapping memory yourself is hard, as most memory managers don't give you that control.

subject: BlueMax 5.1 & standard mode
q: Qualitas BlueMax 5.1 reportedly supports Windows only in enhanced mode. Do I have to change CONFIG.SYS and reboot every time I want standard mode, or is there a newer version that supports it?
a: BlueMax doesn't do Windows standard mode, period. You run enhanced. And you need himem.sys for both standard and enhanced anyway, so nothing changes there. Supporting UMBs in standard mode is possible, but BlueMax and 386MAX don't do it.

subject: Novell Crashes my PS/2
q: Running NCSA Telnet over token ring and logging into Novell, a couple of my PS/2s give "Invalid COMMAND.COM. Cannot load COMMAND, System Halted" when I run an application from dosshell. What causes this?
a: Probably Netware misjudging your DOS version. Mine thought I had DOS 4.00 instead of 4.01 and set the comspec to the wrong directory. Check with ver, compare the size and date of your boot DOS against what comspec points at, and set up a separate DOS directory on the server. Kludgy, but it works.

subject: UUEncode question
q: What is the mode number on the begin line of a uuencoded file? Is it a checksum, and how does uudecode use it?
a: It's no checksum. It's the Unix permission mode in octal, three digits for user, group and other. Meaningless on single-user MS-DOS. If your Prime has no mode, hack the code to ignore it and write something like 0640. Honestly.

subject: QEMM ?
q: What should I put in config.sys or autoexec.bat to load command.com and DOS into high memory with QEMM? I have 591K free on DOS 4.01 and want to break 600K.
a: You're stuck, since DOS 4.01 can't be loaded high. Upgrade to DR-DOS or MS-DOS 5.0 and load the kernel into high RAM. Also ditch COMMAND.COM for 4DOS to save some memory. Read the manual before whining about 591K.

subject: Looking for a text viewer.
q: Where can I find a good text viewer via anonymous ftp? I want users to call it from a menu, page back and forth through a DOS text file, and return to the menu without damaging the file.
a: List version 7.5 is pretty good. Grab list75i.zip from garbo.uwasa.fi in the /pc/fileutil directory. Not hard to find, you know.

subject: DBASE file format ?
q: Where can I get the file format description of dBASE III Plus and/or dBASE IV?
a: The dBase III format is described in dbasefil.zip, available by anonymous FTP from chyde.uwasa.fi in the pc/doc/ directory. Nobody mentioned dBase IV. Get off your lazy duff and fetch it.

subject: WordStar5.0 Professional hangs inexplicably
q: WordStar 5.0 on my PC often hangs when I hit a cursor key. The machine is still alive, since I can print the screen or warm boot, but no WordStar commands work. Any fix other than upgrading to 5.5?
a: Try raising the STACKS setting in your config to a much higher number. Someone with a similar WordStar hang found that fixed it, after WordStar tech support pointed at the DOS setup. Sigh, check your config.sys before blaming the word processor.

subject: Telnetd/Ftpd for a PC on a net.
q: How can I let other hosts on an Ethernet telnet or ftp into a PC that isn't dedicated as a server? Is there a TSR or Windows process that serves incoming ftp and telnet?
a: Look at the public domain NCSA program. That's all anyone offered, so go read its docs and find out whether it does what you want. Don't expect miracles from a PC.

subject: How to set keyboard lights?
q: How do I set the keyboard lights on a PS/2 or AT when I've replaced the interrupt 9 handler and the lights no longer track capslock and numlock?
a: Write 0EDh to port 64H, then write a light mask: 1 for Scroll Lock, 2 for Num Lock, 4 for Caps Lock, OR'ed together. You can't read them back, so keep track of the state yourself.

subject: Unix-like SCCS wanted
q: Is there a Unix-like SCCS project maintenance utility in the public domain?
a: Check your system first, since SCCS ships with many Unix systems. Otherwise get RCS from archive sites like uunet. It's functionally the same as SCCS, and MKS sells versions for DOS and OS/2. Simtel may also have something for PCs.

subject: POST error code 164...
q: After adding a second 2MB SIMM to my PS/2 55SX, I get POST error code 164. What does it mean?
a: 164 means memory size setting incorrect, so run SETUP from the Reference disk. Change anything on a PS/2 and you have to run it again. RTFM, it's a PS/2 thing.

subject: 4mb SIMMs for 55sx
q: Can 4mb SIMMs be used on the motherboard of a PS/2 55sx?
a: Yes, they can. You can get up to 8mb on the motherboard, and it's much faster too. As for the fastest chip, I don't know, so go ask your memory vendor instead of the net.

subject: IBM 8513 monitor problems -- all 20 of them
q: We got about 20 IBM 8513 monitors that all show a blue blotch on the left and a brown blotch on the right when the screen is white. Is anyone else seeing this?
a: IBM ran a poorly announced recall on 8513s with serial numbers 72-0000000 through 72-0640000. Call your local IBM Service Center and ask about ECA-017. If yours are outside that range, call anyway and see if there's another recall. Check your serial numbers before posting.

subject: PL/M
q: Is PL/M really suitable as a systems programming language for the iAPX processors compared to C? What makes it uniquely suited?
a: Nothing, really, except Intel designed it and had compilers for it long before buying someone else's C compiler to call "Intel C". It has SEG and OFFSET hooks and three levels of optimization, plus PL/M-80 compatibility. There's no contest; C wins. Use C.

subject: Recovering from system crash
q: Does ISIS recover from a crashed machine, or only from crashed ISIS programs? The docs on the recovery manager seem to say only programs.
a: You read the V2.1 manual right. It restarts programs but can't work out the last group member to fail unless ISIS stayed up. In V3.0.3 rmgr restarts after process or machine crashes and starts the fresh-log process first. Upgrade.

subject: COCO 128->512K
q: I'm upgrading my CoCo III from 128K to 512K. What about Tandy kits, other companies' kits, or bare boards? What chips do the piggyback kits use?
a: Most 512K upgrades are plug-in boards that suggest clipping a capacitor on the motherboard, no piggybacking at all. The B&B 256K upgrade is a piggyback one, using 64K x 4Bit chips. Heck, the CoCo3 runs fine on 128K with the cap clipped.

subject: fast clock for 6809
q: Is there a faster version of the 6809 than the 2 MHz MC68B09? We ran one at 3 MHz without trouble but don't know the long-term effects.
a: Hitachi makes a 3 MHz CMOS version, and it reportedly runs at 4 MHz too. Ask your local Hitachi office for the part number. Also, the chip itself is the easy part; bus timing is what bites you, since setup and hold times don't shrink, so your peripherals must be faster. Think before overclocking.

subject: dead coco
q: My CoCo died: at powerup ampersands and such appear on the screen, with a normal black border and green background. Is it the ROM, and can I tell whether it's the extended BASIC ROM?
a: Wrong guess. I've never seen a ROM in a CoCo go bad. Sounds more like the SAM chip or the CPU. A bad memory chip is possible too, but that tends to make most characters come out the same, like an &, with only a few different.

subject: coco 1, memory
q: My old gray-box CoCo 1 says 32K on the bubble, but diagnostics show 16K and TSEDIT reports over 47500 bytes free. Do I really have 64K, and should I look for Level 1 OS-9 or Deskmate?
a: Yes, you have 64K. BASIC and RS-DOS can't see it all because the ROMs sit in the upper 32K, while TSEDIT switches the ROMs out and does its own thing. Level 1 OS-9 is hard to find, but don't pay over about $20. Read the docs, it's not magic.

subject: CoCo3, Disto Controller, OS-9
q: The WD-1773 chip on my Disto Super Controller for the CoCo3 doesn't seem to read or write single density, so I can't read an OS-9 Standard Format disk. Is there a chip replacement that gives me single density back?
a: The 1773 definitely does read and write single density. Your vendor probably doesn't program it correctly. Sigh. Fix the controller, not the chip.

subject: Hard Drives
q: What's the difference between an RLL and a non-RLL hard drive system, and what does RLL stand for? How do the controllers differ?
a: RLL is a newer encoding method than MFM, the older one used on floppies and hard drives. It squeezes up to 48 or more sectors per track versus about 32 for MFM. You need a drive certified for RLL, though. Read the spec sheet before you buy.

subject: Motorola FREEWARE BBS: available via FTP ?
q: Are the files on Motorola's FREEWARE BBS, such as the source for the TUTOR monitor (TUTORBUG.ARC), available by FTP anywhere?
a: No FTP. The BBS runs on a pair of PCs, and nobody's in a hurry to move it to anything *nix, so don't hold your breath. But someone keeps an archive server that mails out the uuencoded, split tutorbug.arc, so use that.

subject: Source for VME prototyping cards
q: Does anyone know a source for wire-wrapping cards compatible with VMEbus specs, with J1 and possibly J2 connectors, that fit a VME chassis?
a: Try AUGAT, whose V Series has singles and duals with full power and ground planes. Spendy, but good quality. Radstone Technology in Britain also sells a VME card with wire-wrap space and a gate array VMEbus interface. Use the slip-on pin labels too.

subject: the 68070 - has it left hyperspace yet?
q: Has the 68070 (a 68000 with an MMU, serial ports and timer for under $25) shown up yet? Is it pin compatible, and is the MMU like Motorola's?
a: Not sampled yet; samples are expected by end of 1987. Expect a price well over $25 at introduction. It has too many pins to drop into a 68000 socket, and the MMU is a Philips design, not compatible with Motorola's. Don't hold your breath.

subject: 680x0 Price/Performance...
q: I'm building a parallel computer with 68000 processors on each node and paying out of my own pocket. Where can I get 10 to 16 680x0 chips with the best price/performance?
a: Go to a hamfest. Dealers in used chips show up with 10MHz 68000s around ten bucks, some 68010s too. Check the yellow pages for ham radio dealers to find one. Entry is about five bucks. Sigh, nobody checks the surplus guys first.

subject: PD 68K-assembler wanted ...
q: I'm looking for a public domain 68000 assembler. Long distance calls to a Motorola BBS from Europe are too expensive. Is there anything I can get by ftp?
a: Get the Sozobon C compiler or the Mark Johnson C compiler. Both come as C source and include a separate assembler and linker. The compiler emits plain assembly text and the assembler turns it into linkable objects. No need to phone Motorola, for heaven's sake.

subject: Is anyone shipping a 68030 UNIX box?
q: Is anyone shipping a 68030 UNIX box now or soon?
a: A Dallas company, Logic Process Corp, has a 16MHz one and promises 25MHz when parts arrive. Atari is showing a System V one at Hannover. Beware: a bare 030 in a 68020 design gains little, maybe double only if designed for it. Marketing hype.

subject: 68882 Exception Handling
q: On the 68882, is FSAVE/FRESTORE on every exception or interrupt an absolute requirement, or just an easy way to solve a complex problem? When can I skip it for performance?
a: You only need it if the handler touches the coprocessor, and that includes FMOVEM instructions your compiler may sneak into prologs and epilogs. Also reset it if you won't return cleanly. Otherwise ignore the FPU. Protocol violation traps tell you when you got it wrong.

subject: 68040 not object code compatible?
q: The 68040 manual says it's user object code compatible, but CALLM is listed only for the 68020. What gives?
a: Only the 68020 implements CALLM and RTM. Nobody used them, so they were dropped by the '30; they raise an unimplemented instruction exception. They're OS instructions anyway. The real incompatibility is the missing 040 floating point instructions. Marketing, sigh.

subject: 68230 specs
q: Where can I get the Motorola specs for the 68230, or a book with a chapter on it? I'm moving from a 6821 PIA and have to rewrite driver code.
a: It's in chapter 8 of the M68000 Family Reference manual, Motorola publication FR68K/D. Get it from your local Motorola Semiconductor sales office or their Literature Distribution Center. Also ask for the advance information data on the 68230 PI/T, since the register details are there. Try the phone book before posting.

subject: New Low End Aviion Workstation?
q: Is it true Data General has announced a new low-end Aviion workstation?
a: Yes, the AV 200. It came out a day after Sun's SPARCstation SLC, with a 19 inch monochrome monitor at 1280x1024, 8 MB of memory, Ethernet and local disk connectors, at reportedly the same price as the SLC. Rumors, always rumors.

subject: Flags and shift
q: On the m88k, if one instruction does x := shift_left_by_1_bit (x+y), what happens to the carry flag? Does the shift clear it or does the add leave it set?
a: Moot, because that takes two instructions. The 88K has no dedicated condition code register and sets no flags on arithmetic unless you ask. Carry-out in the PSR needs addu.co, and shift left is mak. Read the architecture manual.

subject: porting ksh on DG/UX
q: Porting ksh to a DG 6220 with gcc 1.37.23, the assembler chokes on msg.s with an operand type mismatch for 'set .,.+2'. Any ideas?
a: Your gcc code generator is broken; it should have emitted align 4. Fix the compiler source, or put a sed script between the compiler and assembler turning set .,.+2 into align 4, or better yet half 0. Old gcc, what did you expect?

subject: Baseline 88K Mask under BCS
q: Which version of the 88100 silicon do software vendors consider the baseline, given the silicon filter workarounds for earlier masks?
a: Data General uses E.1 as the baseline for DG/UX 4.10 and will use E.2 for 4.20, and I'd expect E.2 for quite some time because re-spinning chips costs. D level silicon is NOT acceptable unless you never use double precision floating point. I don't speak for DG.

subject: screen size fluctuates on plus
q: A Mac Plus screen's active area grows or shrinks by a pixel or two when a moderately large window is opened or closed. What's going on?
a: That's monitor bloom. It varies with the ratio of light to dark on the screen. It points to a poor power supply design, but it's only an annoyance, nothing to worry about. Other workstations do it too.

subject: New Mac Owner-type Needs Help
q: A friend is buying a Mac Plus and needs a word processor with a spelling checker and a paint program. MacWrite is $99. Anything cheaper or better, and is FullPaint a good deal?
a: Spend the money and get Microsoft Word 3.01 and SuperPaint. Word has a spelling checker, and so many users that help and books are easy to find. SuperPaint is about $59 at discount outlets. Cheap isn't the point, kid.

subject: Hard Drived & JCLOCK init
q: After adding the JCLOCK init, my Mac hard drive isn't recognized. The disk saver utility won't fix it. How can I save my disk without reinitializing?
a: Use MacZap, about $35 mail-order. Don't let any disk saver utility fix it: Disk First Aid and MacTools can erase the directory. If it won't boot, write a new SCSI driver, use MacZap to recover what you can, then reformat. Learned that the hard way.

subject: Black Apple
q: After installing System 6.0.2 on my Mac II with the Installer's minimal Mac II/IIx system, the Apple in the menu bar is solid black instead of multicolored. Dragging the System folder fixed it. What's going on?
a: The minimal II/IIx install script assumes a bare, probably black-and-white system. Use the regular Mac II installer script from the System Tools disk instead. Or flip the Monitors cdev to B&W and back to color. Read what you're installing.

subject: Telnet 2.2 - [driver e] -?
q: After my Mac II hard disk crashed and I reinstalled the System and Finder, NCSA Telnet 2.2 over Ethernet fails with "Network Initialization Failure! Couldn't open driver [e]". What do I do?
a: Reinstall the EtherTalk driver with the Installer, not by just dragging the file into the System folder. Apple's docs say to use the Installer, and that fixed it here. Nobody could explain what the [e] means. Sigh, RTFM.

subject: Disappearing files and other that won't work
q: After rebuilding the desktop on my Mac to pick up changed icons, programs in the system folder stop working or vanish. Why, and is there a better way?
a: Rebuilding the desktop over and over is a bad idea, as you found. Just switch the Inited Finder flag off with ResEdit or DiskTop. The Finder then re-reads the bundle when you open the folder and takes the new icon. Sigh, no pretzel needed.

subject: Unrecognized SE/30 drive
q: An SE/30 with the 80meg Apple internal hard drive suddenly doesn't see its disk and waits for a floppy at startup. Disk First Aid doesn't list the drive. What happened, and can the data be recovered?
a: Probably one of the infamous drives with sticky lubricant, mostly in SE/30s and IIcxs. Try booting from an Apple system disk, and if the drive shows up, reinstall the system with the Installer. Otherwise take it to a licensed Apple dealer. Jerking the machine to unstick it is voodoo, so back up fast.

subject: Can PS/2 1M SIMMs be used in a Mac?
q: Can 1M SIMMs made for the IBM PS/2 be used in a Mac?
a: Yes, they're the same as Mac SIMMs except for one extra parity chip. Don't go hunting for them, since you'd pay for a chip you can't use, but if the deal is good there's no reason it won't work.

subject: Finder "Clean Up"
q: Can I make the Finder's "Clean Up" the default, so I don't have to hold option on "Clean Up Window"?
a: Set the always-grid-drags bit in the Finder's LAYO resource, and icons will always be gridded, so you'll never have to clean up again. There are other interesting bits there too. Poke around in ResEdit a bit harder next time.

subject: Can a DA specify what area it is opened in?
q: Can a desk accessory specify whether it gets opened in the application's memory or the system's under MultiFinder? Or can it at least find out where it was opened?
a: It's decided by where the DA lives. Font/DA moved or ResEdited into an app, it opens in that app's world and layer. In the System File or via Suitcase, it opens in the system heap and the DA Handler's layer. A DA should only care whether it's in the app heap or not. Sigh.

subject: reminders & appointments
q: Can anyone recommend a Mac desk accessory that displays repeating reminders at a given time, and ideally has an appointment calendar? Smart Alarms crashed my system.
a: Try Comment 2.0x from Deneba Software. It does reminders nicely, with far more flexible repeat settings than Smart Alarms, and also lets you add Post-It type notes to documents and spreadsheet cells. Reasonably cheap, too.

subject: Hard disk back-up on a VCR ?
q: Can you back up a Mac hard disk onto a VCR tape? I saw an ad for a product doing about 1MB/min, and wondered if the SCSI port plus some electronics into the PCM input of an 8mm VCR would work better.
a: It's been done: Corvus had a Mirror interface that backed up its hard disks to VHS tape. But the Sony PCM adapters want constant data at roughly CD rate, far too fast for a Mac hard disk with no DMA. You'd need a stop/start scheme. Not trivial, sigh.

subject: Minor problem with Suitcase (1.2.4 and II) and ApplicationMenu
q: Choosing the DA layer from ApplicationMenu also runs the last DA in the menu when Suitcase 1.2.4 or II is running. Is this a known bug, and can it be fixed?
a: It's a bug in ApplicationMenu, fixed in the upcoming version 3.3. Meanwhile, rename ApplicationMenu so it loads after Suitcase and the problem goes away. INIT load order, people.

subject: Cirrus Volumes incompatible with Suitcase II
q: Cirrus Volumes, the DA that comes with La Cie hard disks, reboots my Mac when I invoke it with Suitcase installed. Anyone seen this?
a: Older versions of Cirrus Volumes didn't work if installed via Suitcase. Get the newer one, version 5.15 from the Silver Lining distribution, which works fine here. Update your stuff, it's not Suitcase's fault.

subject: Mac IIv - inexpensive Mac II box
q: Could Apple make a cheap expandable Mac II, a "Mac IIv", by taking a Mac IIcx and swapping the 68030, MMU and math coprocessor for a plain 68000?
a: Won't work. Color QuickDraw needs instructions the 68000 doesn't have. And Mac II pricing is based on value, not production cost, so don't expect Apple to hand you a cheap one. Sigh.

subject: Portable yes, Mac NO !
q: Crystal Quest 2.2 crashes the new Macintosh Portable but not the SE, SE/30 or Mac II. Why?
a: Probably because Crystal Quest checks for Color QuickDraw by looking at the machine number. The Portable's number isn't recognized, so it guesses wrong. Apple obviously would never ship a machine without color QuickDraw, right? Plenty of programs have this problem. Sigh.

subject: New Portables Soon?
q: Do I need a 68030 to run System 7? I'm wondering when a 68030 portable will come out.
a: A 68030 is NOT required for System 7. It runs on a Mac Plus or better with 2 MB of memory. Only virtual memory needs a 68020 with PMMU or a 68030. Sigh, this myth refuses to die.

subject: SE Accelerators and Sound
q: Do SE accelerators generally include software to fix the sound speed-up, like the Radius did, or is Radius the exception?
a: Radius is the exception, it seems. My AOX DoubleTime in high-speed mode makes sound come out as static or distortion, and no fixing software was provided. Typical cheap accelerator vendors. I live with it.

subject: Alternate sounds on Mac Plus?
q: Do the Mac SE and Mac Plus support alternate SysBeep sounds via the control panel, or is that only the Mac II? Can it be added?
a: None of the others do it with an Apple-supplied cdev. Grumble. Someone wrote CheapBeep, a cdev that works on the 512KE, Plus, SE and II with System 4.1 or later. It cycles through a range of sounds from SoundCap files.

subject: MacSprint II
q: Does anyone have a MacSprint II cache board for the Mac II? Can you feel the improvement, and does it work with a PMMU?
a: Yes, I have several. You feel it at first, then it fades into the background, though the improvement is real. It comes with its own cdev and no unusual problems. It failed miserably with A/UX, but that's fixed now. Four-year warranty, which is rare in this racket.

subject: Fullwrite 1.1 bug
q: Does anyone have a list of bugs for FullWrite 1.1? I crash my Mac every 15 minutes with it, for example by typing two decimal points in the superscript size in Style.
a: Can't say there's a list. I couldn't reproduce your two-decimal-points crash on FullWrite 1.1. I just got an alert saying it's not a valid number, on a Plus with System 6.0.2 under MultiFinder. Maybe your setup is the problem.

subject: MS Word books
q: Does anyone know of a Microsoft Word book or tutorial other than the standard docs, like the third-party Excel books?
a: Try Microsoft Word 3.0 (for the Macintosh) Made Easy. It's a decent intro that teaches things the MS tome doesn't, but the title lies. Some parts are slow enough for a yuppie, others are intuitively obvious style. Still no real reference manual, sigh.

subject: Multi-user reminder calendar
q: Does anyone know of a reminder program like Remember? that several people can use for scheduling meetings and appointments?
a: SmartAlarms has a multiuser version, from ComputerWare for $149. The single-user one is convenient enough. Cough up the money.

subject: Mac II Video Expansion Kit
q: Does anyone know what chips make up the Mac II Video Expansion Kit for the 4-bit card?
a: It's just 8 VRAMs, video DRAMs. The board ships with 8 chips on it and 8 empty sockets, so the kit is nothing but a set of chips. Don't pay Apple prices for a handful of RAM.

subject: MACTCP
q: Does anyone know where one can get a copy of MacTCP?
a: APDA sells it, part number M0230LL/A. It's a single-user license and costs a whopping $100. Typical, charging real money for a driver.

subject: Upgrade II -> IIci?
q: Has Apple announced an upgrade path from the plain Mac II to the new IIci? I'd pay big bucks for the performance.
a: Nope, can't be done. The ci uses the IIcx form factor, which differs from the II's box. An upgrade from the cx to the ci is planned, but nothing for the II. Wait for something new in the II form factor, and expect it to cost an arm and a leg.

subject: Mouse Freezing on Mac IIci
q: Has anyone had the mouse freeze on a Mac IIci? It's unpredictable and happens in Word 4.0, Canvas and the Finder, and it isn't the desktop bus cables.
a: Yes, I had it too, mostly right after starting Word 4.0. Removing the watchCursor 2.0 INIT fixed it. Blame your INITs first, as usual.

subject: need help to print screen using Lightspeed Pascal
q: How can I dump the screen to the printer from Lightspeed Pascal?
a: A bit sleazy, but FKEY 3 and FKEY 4 hold the screen dump code. GetResource one, check you actually got it, dereference the handle, cast it to a procedure pointer with no parameters and no result, and call it. Don't skip the check, genius.

subject: Apple Desktop Bus info wanted
q: How can I get information on building devices for the Apple Desktop Bus used in the new Macs and the IIGS?
a: Get Inside Macintosh Volume 5 from APDA. Somebody even reported a copy being in stock, so you should get it quickly. It's called reading the documentation, try it sometime.

subject: Word 4.0 to WordPerfect for DOS???????
q: How can I move a Microsoft Word 4.0 file from a Mac to WordPerfect on an IBM clone? Word's Save As Word/DOS and a binary transfer didn't work, and WordPerfect's convert utility doesn't see it as a Word file.
a: Save it as RTF on the Mac and let WordPerfect's conversion routine read that directly. Or use Apple File Exchange to translate onto a 720K AT-formatted 3.5 inch floppy. Expect stray hard returns either way, so go hunt them with reveal codes.

subject: Determining Machine Configuration
q: How can I tell 64K ROM, 128K ROM and newer Mac ROMs apart without SysEnvirons glue in LightSpeed C? ROM85 reads the same on an SE as a Plus.
a: ROM85 matches on the Plus and SE because they run virtually the same traps, patches on the Plus and ROM on the SE. That's a sane choice. Lower ROM85 means a more capable machine. It's in IM Vol 5 or a tech note. Go look.

subject: Imagewriter I vs. II and clones
q: How compatible is the Imagewriter I with programs written for the Imagewriter II? Also, how do the Imagewriter-compatible clone printers compare?
a: Apple's ImageWriter II software is 100% compatible with the ImageWriter I. The only difference is color: the I prints every non-white color as black, same as a II with a black-only ribbon. Clones, no idea. Not my problem.

subject: Device driver for Mac Emacs -> Laserwriter
q: How do I get a file from Mac Emacs (the nicer version with bells and whistles) to an old Laserwriter over Appletalk? I just want plain ASCII on paper, and the system bombs on both the Mac Print menu and the emacs lp command.
a: Printing code in that thing is ancient and was ripped out because duplicating what hundreds of other programs already do is pointless. Just open the text file in Microsoft Word and print it from there. Not rocket science.

subject: LW II NT Startup Page
q: How do I get rid of the startup page on the new LaserWriter II NT, now that its ports don't allow the old serial-terminal fix?
a: I can't say it works on the LW II, but the Widgets program included with DiskTop has a function that enables or disables startup page printing. A call to CE Software might be in order. Check before blaming Apple.

subject: Autoreceive in White Knight ZMODEM???
q: How do I make ZMODEM autoreceive in White Knight, the way ZTerm does?
a: Turn on the Auto_Receive checkbox in the File Transfer Options dialog, down next to Final Report. Then WK autoreceives ZMODEM just fine. It was sitting right there in the dialog, so try looking first.

subject: HFS/MFS
q: How do I prepare an 800k MFS disk and a 400k HFS disk on a Mac? I thought you hold down the option key while initializing, but it hasn't worked.
a: For the 800k MFS disk, boot a pre-HFS setup, System 2.0 with Finder 5.3 or earlier, and initialize it there. For the 400k HFS disk, hold option while clicking One-sided in the Initialize dialog, and keep it held the whole time. Read the manual next time.

subject: Switching of SE's internal harddisk
q: How do I switch off the internal hard disk on a Mac SE? It involved holding down several keys, and it's useful for playing old floppy-based games.
a: Hold Command-Option-Shift-Delete while booting. Grumble, you can reboot with one hand and move to the Delete key quickly; you don't need your nose for the power switch.

subject: GetMouse et al.
q: How do the Mac mouse routines like WaitMouseUp, Button, StillDown and GetMouse get their information? Do they read the mouse directly or use the event queue?
a: Not the event queue. A look in Macsbug shows Button and GetMouse read the low memory globals, and the others, like WaitMouseUp, call the lower level routines. OSEventAvail and GetOSEvent also use the low memory globals. Fire up Macsbug yourself.

subject: White Knight throughput
q: How does White Knight compare with Red Ryder 10.3 at high baud rates above 9600? Screen display is a bottleneck for me at 19.2K.
a: White Knight is significantly faster than Red Ryder 10.3. It keeps up at 9600 without problems, and at 19.2K there may be some lag. It depends on how fast your Mac is, and on color. Try it, instead of asking.

subject: THE COLONY
q: How does one get out of the spaceship in the Macintosh game The Colony? I've tried everything.
a: Put on the power suit, then enter the security code at the airlock console and open the door. Walk in, close it behind you, then exit the outer door. Only one airlock door may be open at a time, or you die. Read the manual.

subject: Stats on 68881
q: How fast can the 68881 do a multiply-add?
a: It depends. On clock rate, operand format and addressing mode; FMUL alone runs from 71 to 908 cycles, not counting fetches. Get the Motorola MC68881 user's manual and read chapter 6, or benchmark your own app on a real Mac. Obvious, really.

subject: PC Drive (What good is it???)
q: I bought a 5.25 inch PC drive for my Mac II, but MacOS doesn't recognize it as a standard drive. Is it only useable with third party stuff like SoftPC?
a: Use Apple File Exchange, which is on the 4-disk System Tools and Utilities set. It can talk to that drive. The Finder won't mount it, so quit expecting that. Read the disks you already got.

subject: trouble downloading from Simtel20
q: I can't unstuff Mac files I ftp'd from Simtel20 and moved over with kermit; StuffIt complains of bad headers. What am I doing wrong?
a: Download on the Mac side using Versaterm's MacBinary Kermit setting, then follow the rest of the Using Simtel instructions. Plain Kermit binary mode with the data fork mangles it. Pick the right mode, kid.

subject: ".sit" Unpacker Needed
q: I got a packed file ending in .sit from the net after BinHexing it, and my PackIt can't read it. What program unpacks it?
a: It's a StuffIt archive, so you need StuffIt. PackIt won't touch it. This comes up every week, and the suffix is a dead giveaway.

subject: inits running off the right side of a 9" screen
q: I have 19 INITs and the icons run off the right side of my 9-inch screen. Can I do anything about this?
a: Only the X coordinate gets passed from INIT to INIT, and patching QuickDraw to lie seemed too risky. Use the little INIT called CR, which does a carriage return on the INIT display. Name it alphabetically between the INITs to start a new row. Crude, but it works.

subject: background ImageWriter printing?
q: I have a Mac SE with 1 meg of RAM and no MultiFinder. Is there a way to print MS Word 3.01 files in the background on an ImageWriter?
a: Yes, folks do it with 1 meg. Keep your system small: eliminate fonts you don't use and get rid of all screen fonts larger than 12 point. Stop hoarding fonts and it works.

subject: Appending files
q: I have about 100 MS Word documents and want to merge them into one large file in Word 4.0. Is there a quick way besides opening each one and cutting and pasting?
a: You'll have to open them all anyway, but you can skip the cut and paste. Open all but the last file, and in each one name the next file as the 'next file' in the document dialog box. Then mail merge to a new document. Voila, and no manual labor.

subject: print several files at once
q: I have about 40 Lightspeed C source files on a Mac. Is there an easy way to print them all with one or two commands?
a: Shift-click to select all the files on the desktop, then choose Print from the File menu. No command line needed. Not that the DOS crowd will ever admit it.

subject: CDC Wren IV's on A/UX
q: I initialized a CDC Wren IV with SF&I and want to use it as an A/UX system disk. Do I need a commercial driver, and how do I find the drive's exact size?
a: SF&I predates the A/UX partition map, so it's Mac OS or A/UX, not both. Use dp under A/UX to build the map; Apple's generic driver should do. For size, do a Read Capacity with SCSI Tool, remembering it returns the last block, not the size. Sigh.

subject: TeX Question
q: I installed TeX on the 780 and want to preview the .dvi file on my Mac. I sent a test file over with macput, but the previewer didn't recognize it. How do I download a .dvi file for previewing?
a: Set the file's creator and type to match the previewer, using a setfile tool like DISKTOP, and copy them from a document that already works. Also, some previewers floating around are demo versions that only read the bundled documents. Check that before wasting more time.

subject: Interferon 3.0 question
q: I looked at Interferon 3.0 in ResEdit and found a resource called =VIR with a message mentioning interferon application 2.1. What is it for, and why does it say 2.1 when it's supposed to be 3.0?
a: It's just the signature resource, the creator string for the application. Do a Get Info in ResEdit and you'll see it. The author likely forgot to change it going from 2.1 to 3.0. Nothing to worry about. Stop being paranoid and RTFM.

subject: Font Translation Problems
q: I made a custom font from Zapf Dingbats but the LaserWriter substituted the real Zapf Dingbats when printing. How can I force it to send my screen bitmap font?
a: I haven't tried it, but the FOND resource is the culprit. Cut the FOND with ResEdit, then install the font with Font/DA Mover 3.8, which makes a new FOND. With no printer font referenced, the driver should download the bitmap. Fonts 101.

subject: Need an accelerator for a SE
q: I need an accelerator for a Mac SE. How much do they cost and how much faster are they? Should I go with a faster 68000 or a 68020?
a: Go 68020, so you can run the optimized Mac II versions of software like StatView II, Mathematica and WingZ. A Radius 16 with 68881 ran $725 and works smoothly; the Dove MSE3 was $589 but has quirks and breaks Turbo Pascal. Speed seemed about the same. You get what you pay for.

subject: Accounting package for small business
q: I need an accounting package for my home business on the Mac with general ledger, receivable and payable, that doesn't hide double-entry bookkeeping. What do people recommend?
a: Rags to Riches by Chang Labs has run fine for six months here, and it's cheaper than Insight. G/L, A/P, A/R and billing came to under $300 mail order. One caveat: it doesn't work properly with Suitcase installed. Typical.

subject: Language wanted
q: I teach a file access course using COBOL and the students find it a drag. Is there an alternative language for sequential, hashed and indexed sequential files, on Unix or Mac, that isn't Pascal, C, Ada or FORTRAN?
a: First ask whether your students are headed for commercial programming. If they are, stay with COBOL. Many, many sites still use it, and a student who knows it gets the job over one who doesn't. Boring, but true.

subject: Any Linkers which take arb. length names?
q: I understand the MPW linker and Mac linkers in general only take 31 character external names, which isn't enough for C++ mangled names. Why is that, are there linkers that get around it, and where can I find the object file format?
a: Not true, so quit griping. MPW object format uses plain Pascal strings, so identifiers can run up to 255 characters, and MPW Pascal already keeps 63. The format is documented in an appendix of the MPW Shell manual, available from APDA. RTFM.

subject: using OpenDeskAcc()
q: I use OpenDeskAcc() to bring my program to the front after launching another program and waiting for it to finish. It works under MultiFinder 6.1.b9 but not under 6.0.3 or 6.0.4. How can I do it under 6.0.x?
a: Did you try Launch()ing yourself? Not the hack you're using, but it might even stay compatible with future releases, which is more than you can say for your trick.

subject: Using Compuserve
q: I used XMODEM to download a .sit file from Compuserve to my Mac, but it comes across as a text document so StuffIt ignores it. What's the right way to do this?
a: Your terminal program is doing plain XMODEM instead of MacBinary XMODEM, so the file lands as TEXT. Switch it to the MacBinary setting if it has one. Otherwise run the file through BinHex to get a real StuffIt file. Read your terminal program's manual.

subject: Shareware fees for overseas
q: I want to pay a $10 shareware fee to an author in Australia. Cash is risky, a personal check gets eaten by cashing fees, and an international money order doubles my cost. Any ideas?
a: Send a US cheque. One Australian author says his bank's conversion cost is about $2 Aus, and $10 US is roughly $10 Aus, so he nets about the full amount. You could also split a money order with other users. Cash is a pain for them, so skip it.

subject: Printing Mac->Unix->LaserWriter
q: I'm printing PostScript from a Mac through a Unix machine to a LaserWriter IINT, and special characters like curly quotes and dashes turn into junk. I suspect the eighth bit is lost. How do I fix it?
a: First find where it breaks. Look at the uploaded file on the Unix machine with less or vi; the 8-bit characters should be there. Usually the problem is in the upload path, not the Unix-to-printer path. Check before you blame the printer.

subject: Responder/InterPoll Update
q: InterPoll lists my IIcx, IIx and IIci as just 'Macintosh' while recognizing the SE/30. Is this InterPoll itself, or a change in the Responder between System 6.0.3 and 6.0.4?
a: Responder was revised to version 1.1 to handle the newer Macintoshes, and the system now contains the name strings. Inter*Poll 1.0.1 also fixes bugs and includes any device whose type starts with 'Macintosh'. Update your stuff.

subject: Lightspeed/Just Enough/ MacPascal...
q: Is Just Enough Pascal a rehash of MacPascal, and will there be a trade-in for those of us stuck with MacPascal?
a: You've been misinformed. Just Enough Pascal is a tutorial system that works with Lightspeed Pascal 2.0, not a new MacPascal. MacPascal itself is still sold through EduTech, Symantec's education distributor. Check before you spread rumors.

subject: SuperMac dying?
q: Is SuperMac dying? Dealers advise against buying from them for the next couple of months. Can anyone say what's going on?
a: Shipping and service slipped because the parent was going down the tubes, but a reorganization is underway and they have solid products and management. If everyone shuns them, the rumor becomes self-fulfilling. If you need the product now, buy it. Otherwise buy from IBM, coward.

subject: PostScript files under Multifinder...
q: Is it impossible to generate a PostScript file from the print dialogs under MultiFinder? The Command-F and Command-K switches seem to work only under Finder.
a: Turn off Background Printing in the Chooser. Then Command-F and Command-K work fine under MultiFinder. Three people had to tell you the same thing, which says plenty about reading the manual.

subject: OK to use Mac RAM cache?
q: Is it safe to use the Mac General CDEV's RAM cache? I heard it defers writes and coherency isn't guaranteed at shutdown.
a: Yes, it's safe. Use Shut Down from the Special menu in the Finder and your disk's integrity is assured, and the Mac starts faster next time. Only a sudden power cut is risky, and then your data is a crap shoot anyway. Old wives' tales.

subject: $129 1MB SIMMs for end users - a lie?
q: Is the $129 price for 1MB SIMMs real for end users, or only for resellers? Has anyone bought four or fewer at $129 or less?
a: It's real, no lie. Mail-order ads in MacWeek show Chip Merchant at $129 a SIMM, and others a bit higher. Nobody local will sell at that price, but mail order will. Read the ads before telling people it can't be done. One vendor was a nightmare, so shop carefully.

subject: Is Supramodem any good?
q: Is the 2400 baud Supramodem any good? A friend found one for $149.
a: People like it: small, fast, cheap, front power switch, and SmartCom treats it like a Hayes. One catch: on a Mac II with software-controlled power, switching the modem on can instantly shut the Mac off. Leave it on, or turn the Mac off first. Sigh.

subject: Hebrew word processor
q: Is there a Hebrew word processor for the Mac that doesn't need the Hebrew System software and Script Manager?
a: Two options. Mac-in-Hebrew was a DA that gave right-to-left entry in MacWrite and Word, but it's old and may not work on new systems. Or ask Davka about Achbar, which is ugly, buggy, copy protected and overpriced.

subject: Graphics package request
q: Is there a Mac graphics package, preferably PostScript, that can distort text or shapes as if wrapped around a can?
a: Try Smart Art I or III from Emerald City Software. They specialize in PostScript special effects. Their PostScript environment might help too, whatever the darn thing is called. Look it up yourself.

subject: Question on Turbo Pascal.
q: Is there a compatibility problem between the Mac II and Mac Plus for code generated by Turbo Pascal? My program using the window manager and QuickDraw runs on the Mac II but crashes on the Mac Plus.
a: Check whether you're calling anything Mac II specific, like Color QuickDraw or the new Menu Manager. Also see if the Plus is running a System older than 4.1. Can't say more without details, and frankly, Turbo, what did you expect?

subject: Sun raster file => Macintosh raster file
q: Is there a converter that takes a Sun raster file and outputs a Macintosh readable raster file, so I can look at Sun graphics on a Mac?
a: Get the portable bitmap (pbm) utilities that come with X. They convert Sun raster and MacPaint to and from pbm. Go raster to pbm, then pbm to macpaint. If you don't have them, ask the author. Learn the tools.

subject: Printing multiple files in Think C...
q: Is there a less painful way to print all the source files of a Think C 4.0 project? Selecting each file and printing is a pain, and selecting them all in the Finder and choosing Print just opens the project.
a: Select all the source files in the Finder, then choose Print from the File menu, and Think C should print them all. Mind you, that's only a guess that Think C follows the interface, and you said it just opens the project. Sigh.

subject: Program to view cdevs/inits?
q: Is there a program, a cdev maybe, to view the inits (startup documents) running on my Mac? It's easy to lose track of them.
a: Yes, it's called the Finder. Pick View by Kind from the Special menu and the startup documents are grouped together. Honestly, look at what you already have.

subject: Changing MultiFinder's default memory size?
q: Is there a simple way to change MultiFinder's default memory size for programs with no SIZE resource? Also, why is it 384K?
a: It's not stored in any resource, so you'd have to patch the constant in the Finder code. Just use Get Info on your apps instead. 384K is what a typical app got on a 512KE, which was still a supported platform when MultiFinder shipped.

subject: Internet to America Online?
q: Is there a way to send e-mail from the Internet to America Online?
a: No. There is no link from the Internet to America Online, and they told us they have no gateways to any other email service, just snail mail and fax. Welcome to the walled garden. Sorry.

subject: Calendar INIT WANTED ! (and various others)
q: Is there an INIT that displays the events stored by the Calendar DA at startup? I think it's called Calendar Init.
a: Never heard of that one, but there's a program called Remember? that does the job nicely. The newest version is 1.3, while sumex has 1.2. Try looking before you beg for files.

subject: Anonymous FTP site where I can get TechNotes?
q: Is there an anonymous FTP site where I can get Apple TechNotes?
a: ftp to apple.com, also known as apple.apple.com. Look in pub/dts/mac/tn, where the notes are in subdirectories of 50 each plus one for the TN Stack. This comes up every week.

subject: Envelope printing on IWII or LW?
q: Is there an easy way to print envelopes on a Laserwriter or Imagewriter with MS Word, preferably using Print Merge?
a: Feeding and indexing is much easier on the LaserWriter. Make a FullWrite file with two sidebars, one for the return address and one for the addressee, and set the top to (8.5 minus envelope height) over 2. Or print sticky labels, which are tractor-feedable. Envelopes are irritating either way.

subject: any reason NOT to buy a 512K mac cheap?
q: Is there any reason not to buy a used 512K Mac with 800K internal and external drives plus MacWrite, Paint and Draw for about $1000? It's for word processing and a bit of spreadsheet.
a: Questionable deal. A new Mac Plus with 1 meg and SCSI runs $1249 at university prices, and upgrading a 512KE to a Plus costs about $600. Someone saw an old-ROM 512 with an external drive go for $600. Haggle.

subject: Can MultiFinder turn itself on?
q: Is there any way the Set Startup option could switch to MultiFinder by itself, without the user doing it manually?
a: Yes. When a System and Finder are moved to the hard disk, the boot blocks get written there. I think Installer also rewrites the boot blocks on a System upgrade. So it's not a cosmic joke. Check what got installed.

subject: Public Folder and hierarchy
q: Is there any way to open a folder inside Public Folder on the Mac so I can copy just one file out of it, instead of copying the entire folder?
a: Not in the current release. It won't let you look into subfolders, only tells you file counts and megabytes. Workaround: run multiple Public Folders, each customized to point at a different directory, one per subfolder you care about. Clumsy, but that's what you get.

subject: Internet access over modems (sortof like SL/IP) on Macs...
q: Is there software that makes a Mac a real Internet host over a 9600 baud modem, something like SL/IP on Unix?
a: SLIP just wraps IP packets for serial lines, and it isn't Unix-specific. What you want is a TCP/IP suite with SLIP drivers: Phil Karn's KA9Q package for PCs and Macs. It's freeware with source, on ftp at various sites. It ain't easy, but it's been done.

subject: 32K limit
q: Lightspeed Pascal on my 512KE Mac says 'Program segment longer than 32K' and won't run. How do I avoid this, and what exactly is over 32K?
a: A code segment can't exceed 32K in most environments, so segment your app. In Lightspeed Pascal, view by segment in the project window and drag source files between segments. It works per source file. Read the manual, it's all in there.

subject: MacNosy help???
q: MacNosy 2.01 gives me errors trying to access files, trying to open filename.src when the name is truncated to 10 characters, and sometimes bombs when combining blocks. Is the latest version more robust?
a: You've got an antique version. The name length bug was buried in ugly old code and has been gone for at least a year, along with the other problems. The current version is fairly unbreakable, windowed and menu driven. Upgrade, for pity's sake.

subject: macintosh prodigy mods for telebit modems?
q: Macintosh Prodigy doesn't support Telebit Trailblazer modems. Does anyone know how to modify modem.txt, or how to use a Trailblazer at 2400 baud with it?
a: Don't bother hacking modem.txt. Tell it you have a Hayes 2400 and it talks to a Trailblazer Plus just fine. You may have to tell it to dial again, since it sometimes gets confused on the first try.

subject: System 4.3/6.0 & MultiScrap is sloooow!
q: MultiScrap is awfully slow after I installed System 4.3 and Finder 6.0 on my hard drive. Is there a fix or a better replacement?
a: Yes, everybody hits this when they get a hard drive. No new MultiScrap fixes it. Buy SmartScrap, which is basically a very fast MultiScrap that saves in standard ScrapBook style and shows a catalog of the contents. It costs, naturally.

subject: Imagewriter II -and- Programming
q: My Imagewriter II sometimes spits out reams of hex code in columns instead of printing text. What causes that?
a: You bumped the select button next to the power switch. Turn the printer on while holding it and it prints everything in hex, a service tech feature. Power off and on without touching it. Sigh, read the manual.

subject: Imagewriter LQ Print Spacing Problems
q: My Imagewriter LQ loses some spaces between words, mostly before capitalized words, and ignores top margin settings. Driver software is V 1.0. Any clues?
a: That's your problem: the old driver. It's fixed in version 2.0. Upgrade, and stop fiddling with dipswitches.

subject: LaCie 80 meg drive
q: My LaCie 80 meg drive in a Mac II won't boot after most program crashes. I have to boot from floppy and run Disk First Aid. Is this fixable?
a: It's a known Mac II quirk. A bad crash wipes the PRAM, so the Mac forgets what drives are attached and won't boot from the hard drive. An INIT called PramFix is supposed to fix it. Blame Apple, not the drive.

subject: Hard disk
q: My Mac SE doesn't see its hard disk at boot, though I can boot from floppy and the red light keeps flashing. How do I get the disk back?
a: Clear the parameter RAM. Boot from the floppy, hold Command-Option-Shift while opening the control panel until the dialog asks about clearing PRAM, and click yes. That usually brings the disk back after a restart. Back up immediately, since this can be a symptom of worse to come.

subject: Mouse multiple clicks
q: My Mac SE is under 2 months old and the mouse sometimes sends two or more clicks, selecting whole words or scrolling continuously. What causes it, and is there a fix besides replacing the mouse?
a: The cure is to take it back to the dealer for a new mouse, since it's under warranty. Test the replacement by slowly clicking in a dialog box where there are no buttons, and count the beeps. Too many beeps, get another. Dead simple.

subject: Interesting Mac Crash
q: My Mac SE on System 6.0.3 crashed with system error 3, then 10, then 29 after using Font/DA Mover. What is error 29?
a: Error -29 is unit table full, though how it became a system error is unclear. Reinstall the system and try with fewer DAs and drivers. Resume doesn't do much; the application provides it. Sigh.

subject: Mac SE Keyboard -- Whither ON/OFF switch?
q: My new Mac SE keyboard is supposed to have an ON/OFF switch for the whole system, but I can't find one. Is it there?
a: The key marked with a triangle is the ON key, but it only works on the Mac II. Press it and the power comes up. Shut down with the Special menu's Shut Down command. Your SE doesn't get it. Read the fine print before believing MacUser.

subject: LSC, Mac limitations?
q: On the Mac with LSC, my array of pointers for a 250x250 window is 62500 bytes, and the Mac can't handle a segment over 32K. Also, does my NULL test on a linked list fail unless I set the last next pointer to 0L?
a: Static variable space can't exceed 32K, a Mac limit, so allocate the array at runtime with malloc, NewPtr or NewHandle. malloc'd nodes contain garbage, so use calloc or set the next field to NULL yourself. Basic C hygiene.

subject: Jasmine megafloppy
q: Our Jasmine megafloppy cartridges have gone bad, and Jasmine seems to have died. Where can I get more cartridges?
a: Jasmine isn't dead; I called and they're still selling the MegaDrive and cartridges. Bad ones can be exchanged by getting an RMA number from tech support. The mechanism is made by DTC, so other OEM cartridges may work. Rodime is the one in trouble. Check your rumors.

subject: Using Printer with LSC
q: Output from Lightspeed C to the Imagewriter via fopen on .BOut prints, but the paper never advances, and each line overwrites the last. What's wrong?
a: You opened with mode "a", which is text mode. The C library converts your newlines into carriage returns, the Mac text file convention, so the printer never gets a line feed. Open it in binary mode, "ab". Read the library docs sometime.

subject: Laserwriter Message
q: Printing to a Laserwriter Plus, I sometimes get a message that a screen bitmap version of Geneva is being created since the printer font isn't available. Why, and how do I stop it?
a: The LaserWriter doesn't know Geneva, so the Mac has to draw the font itself. Rule of thumb: fonts named after cities aren't LaserWriter fonts. Turn on font substitution in Page Setup, or better, use a real LaserWriter font. Word processors with headers or footers trigger it too, so match their font to the body. Read the manual.

subject: H E L P ---> Red Ryder + SE30 (Scott are you there ?)
q: Red Ryder 10.3 freezes with a dead arrow cursor when dialing on an SE/30 with system 6.03 and an Everex modem, though it worked on a regular SE. Is that a software problem?
a: Not a Red Ryder 10.3 problem, since others run it fine on the SE/30. The port probably isn't responding, maybe from an INIT on the 030 that the other SE lacks. Everex modems have had trouble too, so try another modem. Bisect your INITs.

subject: Red Ryder problems
q: Red Ryder 10.3 in vt100 mode on my Vax account garbles the screen: lines break in half, and vi alters the wrong text and deletes the wrong lines. What's wrong?
a: Red Ryder doesn't handle the VT100 screen escape codes properly. Use Kermit instead; that fixed it for the one who replied. And go read the manual that came with the program, since legit copies include one. Sheesh.

subject: Screen Savers
q: Screen savers like Pyro and Dimmer behave oddly on our big-screen Mac monitors. Are there newer versions or other screen savers that work on bigger monitors?
a: The latest Moire cdev works fine on every large monitor around, though you may have to rename it !moire or zmoire to fix INIT load order. Pyro 3.3 also does just great on big screens. Read the version numbers next time.

subject: Font trouble on Mac II
q: Some of our favorite fonts misbehave under FullWrite and MacDraw II on a Mac II but not on SEs, with the same System 6.0 software. The FOND resource seems to lack width information. Why the difference, and is there a workaround?
a: The fractional width info is bad because Font/DA Mover before 3.6 didn't move it correctly. Copy the fonts out to another file, remove them from the system, and reinstall with 3.6. It has nothing to do with SE versus II. Read the FullWrite insert page next time.

subject: 605i-network-products-installer.hqx (Is the image corrupted?)
q: The 605i-network-products-installer.hqx file gives a CRC error in BinHex on two downloads while the other 6.0.5 images decode fine. Is the file corrupted?
a: The file is fine, BinHex 4.0 is buggy. A file name over twenty-odd characters trips that error. Decode it with StuffIt's BinHex option, which doesn't have the bug, or shorten the name. Slower, but at least it works.

subject: Dos Mounter demo does not work on the IIci
q: The Dos Mounter demo from sumex crashes my IIci during bootup even with all INITs and CDEVs turned off. Has anyone else had this problem?
a: Yes. Smart Alarms installs itself in the System and can't be switched off like a normal INIT, and that's what kills it. A clean floppy System ran the demo fine until Smart Alarms went on. Sigh, check your own System before blaming the demo.

subject: Manual for HPDJ Driver is bad (???)
q: The HPDJ DeskJet driver manual downloaded from sumex and rascal won't open in any application and has type and creator "nX^D". What is wrong with it?
a: Nothing's wrong. It's a WriteNow document, and that creator code is the WriteNow signature. Open it with WriteNow or the demo, Sample WriteNow, on sumex. Read the creator code before you cry bad file.

subject: Blitter and graphics performance
q: The Mac II doesn't seem to have a blitter. Can video cards have blitters, and is there any way to speed up QuickDraw's line, dot and area fills on a Mac II?
a: Sure, you can add one. Write an init resource that swaps out the references to the normal line, dot and area drawing routines and patch in your own bottom-level routines. Tricky, but possible. Try it before whining about hardware.

subject: Global blowing away Mac II?
q: The Megamax C library stores a long word at low-memory location 694 decimal (2B6 hex), and programs built with it crash a Mac II. What is at that location, and could that cause the crash?
a: You guessed right. That location is reserved by Apple. It was BasicGlob for the never-released MacBasic, and as of System 4.1 it holds the ExpandMem pointer on all machines. Trash it and the Mac II dies. Nobody said you could use it; read the docs.

subject: Problem with Tech Note #176 (SIMMs)
q: The Tech Note #176 SIMM installation files for the Plus, SE and II won't open in MacWrite, Word or Teachtext. What format are they in?
a: They're diagrams in MacDraw format. You need MacDraw to look at them. Not exactly a mystery.

subject: Blinking Apple
q: The apple in my Mac Plus menu bar blinks between regular and inverse once a second, and the Apple menu still works. What is it and how do I stop it?
a: Someone set the Alarm Clock desk accessory. The alarm setting lives in battery-backed parameter RAM, so a system disk without the DA can't turn it off. Get a disk with the Alarm Clock DA and shut the alarm off. This comes up all the time.

subject: 6.0.4 and Monitor Convergance Tests
q: Under System 6.0.4, how do I display the color convergence test pattern that was a button in the Monitors cdev in 6.0.3?
a: Apple dropped the button, and 6.0.5 lacks it too. Apple's workaround: open a painting program, paint the screen black, and draw some white lines. It's a lame fix, but it works. Somebody also wrote an app that replaces it.

subject: LightSpeedC and assembler
q: Version 1.0 of LightSpeedC had a poor assembler interface. What does the current LSC provide for using assembler?
a: An inline assembler, since 2.01. It's integrated into the compiler through a new asm statement, not passed to some assembler pass, so you can reference C functions and variables by name and get A5 or A6 relative references. Break, continue and return all work, and #defines are honored.

subject: Resources, Resource Compilers, and Resource Editors
q: We inherited an old Mac app with RMaker input files. What's the best way to bring this up to date and edit the icons without using RMaker anymore?
a: Run RMaker one last time, then use DeRez on the resource file to get Rez source. Include types.r so menus, windows and dialogs are readable. Or keep the compiled resources and edit with ResEdit. Read up on Rez and DeRez.

subject: What is minimum needed on startup floppy?
q: What are the minimum files needed on a Mac floppy to use it as a startup disk, leaving the most space free?
a: All you really need is System and Finder. Fonts and desk accessories can go, though keep the Chooser, and a printer driver if you print. Move System and Finder onto the disk together so it becomes bootable. Or use the minimal-system Installer scripts from System 6.0 onward. RTFM.

subject: MPW Pascal
q: What does MPW stand for, and why would anyone pay $400 for a Pascal compiler when Turbo Pascal exists? What does it do, and how does TML Pascal II differ?
a: It once stood for Macintosh Programmer's Workshop. You're paying for more than the compiler: tools for the whole programming process, like the Unix programmer's tools, far beyond what Borland gives you. Turbo Pascal is fine for small programs; for big team projects you'll want MPW.

subject: Anyone knoe what DM_FIX appl does?
q: What does the Mac application DM_FIX do? It adds code resources to the Finder and says "Desktop Manager Finder Patcher".
a: It's a patch installer, as Get Info would tell you. It patches the Finder to close the Desktop DB and DF files on unmountable volumes so you can unmount them. Only for users of the Desktop Manager INIT. And don't ask what that is; read old news.

subject: Equation editor
q: What equation editor should I use on the Mac for medium complexity integrals, linear equations and ratios?
a: Expressionist and MathType are the favorites around here. I like MathType, since it's more logically laid out. Word's built-in math is fine for simple stuff, but it gets painful as expressions grow. This comes up every week.

subject: What disk drives work with LaserWriter II NTX?
q: What hard disk, say 20MB, can I connect to a LaserWriter II NTX? Apple drives work and Dataframe drives reportedly do not.
a: A Rodime 100M drive works just fine on an NTX, with about 30 Adobe fonts on it. Or buy Adobe's Type Catalog disk with all 300 fonts, if you've got the cash. Try a higher SCSI address on the Dataframe before giving up.

subject: Undocumented Result code -120. Help!
q: What is Mac result code -120? It isn't in Inside Macintosh, and I get it reading a file from a large HyperCard application.
a: A -120 is dirNFErr, directory not found. It's not a Memory Manager error as you guessed, so quit pattern-matching on error numbers and check the paths.

subject: Tape DIsk INIT
q: What is the Tape Disk INIT that comes with Apple Tape Backup 2.0.1? Is it optional, obligatory, or only for special cases?
a: TapeDisk lets you mount volume backup tapes as a regular disk, though much slower than a real one. It's entirely optional. Don't use it with MacroMaker, as the README says. Read the README before asking the net.

subject: Hypercard version?
q: What is the latest version number for HyperCard?
a: 1.2.1. Not exactly a hard one; this comes up every time Apple sneezes.

subject: Fedit+
q: What is the most recent version of Fedit+? I have 1.0.7, but MacUser lists 2.0.
a: 1.0.7 is still current. The company says 2.0 might be available in October, maybe. Don't believe everything a magazine prints; vaporware is vaporware.

subject: Imagewriter I Cables?
q: What kind of cable do I need to connect a new Mac SE to a very old Imagewriter I?
a: It's a null-modem cable wired DIN-8 on the Mac end to DB-25 on the Imagewriter. Same cable you'd use for a Hayes-type modem. Apple sells adaptors for $20, and third parties for less. Don't pay Apple's markup, sigh.

subject: DOS EMULATION
q: What's a good DOS terminal emulation program for the Mac, so I can connect to a cheap PC clone by cable and also reach a remote PC by modem? I've only heard of MacChuck.
a: Try PC Anywhere III on the PC and PC-MacTerm on the Mac. It's supposed to work with any PC, clone or PS2, and there's a network version for AppleTalk. That's the rumor anyway, I lost the flier.

subject: System 6.0 SERVER installations/Network CDEV
q: What's different about a Macintosh II SERVER System 6.0 install compared to a standard System install on an AppleShare server?
a: As far as anyone can tell, the server configuration raises the maximum number of users on a Mac II from 25 to 50. It also bumps the max open files and locked ranges, per the recent tech notes. RTFM, Apple documented it.

subject: HP LaserJet IIP Use
q: What's it like using an HP LaserJet IIP with a Macintosh, and what other hardware and software do I need?
a: It works fine, but you need a printer driver such as MacPrint or JetLink, around $100 to $150. Add at least 512K more memory for a full page of graphics at 300 DPI. HP's memory is overpriced, so buy third-party. And no PostScript-only programs, obviously.

subject: drawing changes when pasting MacDraw -> Scrapbook. ?.
q: When I paste a MacDraw drawing into the Scrapbook, the characters shift position and the circle looks smaller. Why, and what can I do?
a: Turn off fractional character widths in your preferences. That's the cause. Hardly a guru-level problem.

subject: Direct PS files to a specific folder. How?
q: When I print to a PostScript file on the Mac, the file lands in the current folder, the application folder, or the System Folder depending on the program. Can I direct all PostScript files to one specific folder?
a: Use ResEdit to enable the Disk File checkbox in the LaserWriter dialog and turn on Background Printing. Then every PostScript file goes into the Spool Folder inside the System Folder. Beats fumbling with Command-F, too.

subject: Orbit 2.1 Posting Corrupt?
q: When I run the BinHex of Orbit 2.1 from comp.binaries.mac through BinHex 4.0, I get a CRC error. Is the posting corrupt?
a: Probably not. Someone unbinhexed it fine, so the error is likely at your site. Check your own end before demanding a repost, and don't waste the net's bandwidth.

subject: System 7 -- When?
q: When is System 7 scheduled for release?
a: Sigh. Apple announced many System 7.0 features, and MacUser's September 1989 line was that it ships sometime before the world ends. Don't hold your breath, and don't ask vendors for dates.

subject: system 6.0.1
q: When will the bug-fix System 6.0.1 for the Mac be released, and will 7.0 be delayed? My dealer refuses to release System 6.0 and cites Apple policy. Is that right?
a: The latest Apple Viewpoints says 6.0.1 is due August 15, and 7.0 is rumored for January. Your dealer sounds like a bozo, and 6.0 is very good anyway, unless you want sound to work nicely on a Plus.

subject: dialing # and * in HyperCard
q: Where can I buy the device that hooks a telephone up to the Mac speaker for HyperCard's dial command?
a: Data Desk of Seattle sells the "Hyper Dialer," around $30. It's the same little interface box Borland sells with their Sidekick DA, MacDialer. It hooks up to your phone. Honestly, a phone call to them would've been quicker than posting.

subject: Apple DTS tech stack?
q: Where can I find the large HyperCard technical support stack from Apple DTS?
a: That's the Tech Note stack, normally on apple.com, AppleLink and APDA, and also at SUMEX, Rascal, PUCC and SIMTEL-20. Don't grab the current V3.1 though, a new version is due within two weeks. Be patient.

subject: Where can I purchase Yeager's AFT
q: Where can I purchase Yeager's Advanced Flight Trainer for the Mac II? My usual source won't have it for a few weeks and I want it now.
a: ComputerWare sold it for $38, and I couldn't find it anywhere else. The lowest price I saw was $36. A $25 quote turned out to be the IBM version. It runs on an SE too, so stop whining about the wait.

subject: Flight simulators for the Mac
q: Which Mac flight simulators are out there, and do Falcon, JET or Chuck Yeager's work in color on a Mac II?
a: JET isn't Microsoft's, it's SubLogic's, and it won't run on a Mac II. Falcon forces 1-bit mode. Chuck Yeager works at any depth, but the RAM version won't run under Color QuickDraw on a IIci. P-51 is wireframe, and Air Warrior on GEnie does color but eats money.

subject: article about jGNEFilter in MacTuto
q: Which MacTutor article talks about jGNEFilter?
a: It was the article that implemented a screen blanker. I can't recall the issue, but it's in the Best of MacTutor Volume 1. Go look it up instead of scanning contents lists.

subject: High-Density floppies
q: Which brand of high-density 3.5 inch floppies should I buy, and where? Kodak ones run $24.95 a box at a photo store, but I don't want disks that die in a few months.
a: Skip the photo store and call MEI/Micro Center. Somebody bought 300 double-density disks there and not a single one has failed. HD runs about 89 cents each, so a box is $8.90. Shipping is slow, but you'll live.

subject: Magazine query
q: Which major Macintosh magazines are there, and what are their orientations? I want an even mix of technical and user articles.
a: Macworld, MacUser and MACazine are user, software and hardware. MacWEEK is news, Macintosh Today is news and user, and MacTutor is Mac programming. InfoWorld and Byte also cover it. For a mix, read two of them.

subject: TeleCommunications
q: Which protocol is fastest for uploading BinHex'ed files from a Mac? Is there any reason to use something other than plain text transfer, or is Xmodem faster?
a: Plain text is fastest, but there's no error checking, so one glitch ruins the whole BinHex file and you won't know until you unBinHex it. Use ZModem, then 1K Y-Modem and X-Modem, and last the original 128-byte Xmodem. Not a huge difference between the X and Y ones.

subject: Who's got the ANSWERS?
q: Who answers all these questions on the net? I read 50 questions and only one response.
a: Many people mail answers straight to the poster, who is supposed to summarize if it's of general interest. That cuts down on duplicate postings, and there's already way too much traffic here. So post a summary yourself, and answer a question before asking one.

subject: What's that thing in my Disk Window?
q: Why can HFS disks be recognised by a single pixel in their window that separates them from MFS disks?
a: Presumably so the distinction is imperceptible except to users who really care. It's easy to see if you look for it and invisible casually. Did you expect a profound reason? Sigh.

subject: Mac only has 90-day warranty
q: Why does the Mac only carry a 90-day warranty?
a: The only logical explanation I remember hearing is that it gives Apple dealers a form of income through AppleCare. The warranty is pitiful, we all know it, and it's been talked to death. Squeak at Apple if you must.

subject: Curiouser and curiouser...
q: Why does the resource manager in the 128K Mac ROMs seem to contain support for Suitcase, like InitResources looking in the system folder for an INIT file with creator 'dMob' and running INIT 128 out of it?
a: It doesn't. There's nothing in the ROM that does that. Suitcase patches InitResources and OpenDeskAcc, so you're looking at its patches in RAM. Check the address: the Mac+ ROM starts at 400000 hex, and anything lower is RAM. Look before you theorize.

subject: Where is ASCII 205?
q: Why is ASCII 205 and other two-key combination characters missing under System 4.1 and Finder 5.5? I need the set-inclusion symbol in Symbol Font for math manuscripts.
a: Characters 204 and 205 were inadvertently left out of the US character table in systems 4.0 and 4.1. They come back in the MultiFinder system release. Sigh, a bug, not a conspiracy.

subject: Slow Laserwriter Halftones?
q: Why is my halftone program so slow on the LaserWriter? A 420x320 greyscale takes 20 minutes, and larger files take up to an hour.
a: There's more than one way to print a greyscale. Some programs image it into a bitmap and download that. Hold F after clicking OK in the print dialog to dump the PostScript file and see. A 512x512 4-bit takes about 1.5 minutes on a LaserWriter Plus, so 20 is absurd.

subject: Laserwriter sales to students
q: Why won't the campus computer store sell LaserWriter NT or NTX printers to students? Is that Apple's policy or just local policy?
a: Sounds like local bureaucracy, or maybe something in the student discount contract. Other schools do the same: students can buy an SC but never an NTX, and an NT only with a letter from the department head promising no resale. Bureaucrats love to complicate things.

subject: MacWrite II/Word 4.0 (Claris Translater 1.0?)
q: Will MacWrite II be able to import Microsoft Word 4.0 files? I saw a file called MicrosoftWord 4.0 with a Claris Translator 1.0 version.
