a: Yes, MacWrite II 1.1 handles Word 4.0 documents. That file is an XTND translator module. Drop it in your System Folder or Claris folder and it shows up in a popup in the open and save dialogs. Other products will use XTND later.

subject: SoftPC and Color Emulation
q: Will SoftPC run color applications, like a PC game designed for CGA/EGA/VGA, on a Mac IIcx with a color monitor and 8 bit color card?
a: Yes, SoftPC emulates CGA graphics very nicely. The new SoftPC 286 is supposed to do EGA or VGA too, though I'll believe that when I see it. Marketing always says that.

subject: A repost for comp.binaries.mac?
q: Will anyone repost the hex files for the Pyro and Suitcase II updaters on comp.binaries.mac? The ones that came over had lines missing.
a: They were already reposted several days ago: Pyro! Updater 3.3, and Suitcase II Updater 1.2.2 in two parts, on Dec 30 and 31. If you haven't seen them, ask your news feed why. Not our problem.

subject: ]Moire and GateKeeper
q: With GateKeeper, GateKeeper Aid and Moire, my Finder is always reported as damaged at shutdown under 6.0.4. Removing Moire fixes it. Does anyone know why?
a: Don't jump to conclusions, they work together fine. Moire has a run on shutdown option that will bomb an SE or a Plus, since it seems to only work on 68020 and up. Turn it off. RTFM.

subject: 6.0.2 laserwriter bug (and slowness)
q: With System 6.0.2, turning on unlimited downloadable fonts makes LaserWriter printing slow and sometimes switches to Courier. How can I optimize pages for printing?
a: Nobody had a real fix. One person with the fonts on a hard disk saw no slowdown, so the bottleneck is evidently sending fonts over the wire. The Courier switching is a known bug. Blame Microsoft, as usual.

subject: 6.0 What works - what doesn't?
q: Word 3.01 and Excel 1.5 crash at the first menu click under plain Finder on System 6.0, though they work under MultiFinder. LS-P 1.0 does likewise. What works with 6.0?
a: Get the 3.02 upgrade of Word. It runs with 6.0 under either Finder or MultiFinder, and the upgrade should be free. Running outdated software on a new system and then complaining, honestly.

subject: MacTCP and NCSA Telnet
q: MacTCP NCSA Telnet won't connect through a MultiGate that allocates IP addresses dynamically to LocalTalk Macs, though the non-MacTCP version works. What's wrong?
a: You're making it harder than it is. Select the zone and choose Server, not Dynamic, in the assign section. The net class and subnet settings are meaningless because the MultiGate already knows them.

subject: Battle Mac 1.0
q: Battle Mac 1.0 from comp.binaries.mac crashes repeatedly on my Macs and gives odd game information. Has anyone else had this problem?
a: Yes, it's a bug in the game. It seems to never dispose of the memory from the previous game, so it grows until it eats its whole partition and crashes with an out of memory error. Raising the MultiFinder partition only buys a few more games. Sloppy programmer.

subject: Do you need color for SimEarth?
q: Do you need a color Mac to play SimEarth? I have a Classic and am wondering whether it works in monochrome.
a: No, it plays fine in monochrome, I've done it on an SE. Color is definitely a plus, though. Not everything needs a rainbow, but fine.

subject: Darwin's Dilemma
q: Has anyone heard of the Mac game Darwin's Dilemma? What is it like?
a: Rented it, glad I didn't buy it. You push life-form icons around, and two like ones merge into a higher form. Moves are horizontal or vertical only, with limited teleports, and I gave up around level 4 or 5. If you like that sort of thing, just get Polar from sumex.

subject: MS Flight simulator (where is it?)
q: Has anyone heard when the new version of Microsoft Flight Simulator for the Mac is coming out? Rumor said this summer.
a: The demonstrator at the Expo said this September. Registered users are supposed to get an upgrade notice too. Believe it when you see it, vendor dates being what they are.

subject: Lode / LodeRunner
q: How do I beat level 50 of Lode Runner? I can't get the two bags of money in the upper right and get back out.
a: Go straight for those two bags, and if you've already buried a bad guy who fell in that pit, forget it. Otherwise fall into the pit, grab both bags, move to the left half, dig right, fall in and move DOWN. The bricks below are invisible trap doors. Patience, kid.

subject: Glider+ 3.0 cat screen
q: How do I get past the cat on the last screen of Glider+ 3.0? The cat keeps swiping my paper plane out of the air.
a: You win by flying the plane out the window, right where the paw can hit. Use the rapid back-and-forth trick to drop the plane almost onto the cat's back, then lower the tail so it coasts backwards over his head and out. Timing, kid. Practice it.

subject: net Trek
q: How or where can I get the latest version of NetTrek for the Mac?
a: Buy it. NetTrek "The Real Version" is now a commercial product from Premier Technology, and mail order outfits like MacConnection carry it. Free ride's over, folks.

subject: Games On The Iisi
q: I just got a IIsi and games like PT-109, Sargon IV and SubBattle Simulator crash or freeze. Has anyone found a way to make them play on an SI?
a: Likely the System, not the machine. If crashes hit where a digitized sound plays, run the game's 'snd ' resources through Sound Master 1.62: remove them, put them back, and they get a new format. So I hear. Try it before whining.

subject: Fire-Brigade - anyone played it?
q: I want a real strategic wargame for the Mac, like the SPI or Avalon Hill board games. Fire-Brigade looks interesting, but are there other worthwhile computer implementations of board games?
a: Look at the SSG pair, Halls of Montezuma and Panzer Battles. They keep the boardgame feel while the Mac does the bookkeeping. You assign divisional actions and the computer moves the units, so don't expect to push individual units around. Grumble, grumble.

subject: Appletalk
q: I'm looking for AppleTalk network games that multiple users can play. Any suggestions?
a: Try Spectre, a multi-user tank game made for playing over a network. This comes up every week, so check the archives next time.

subject: Curse of the Azure Bonds
q: I'm stuck in Curse of the Azure Bonds. Is there any way to kill off that massive party of beholders, dark elf lords, high priests of Bane, and rashashkas?
a: Cast mass invisibility, enlarge and haste on the whole party before the fight; invisibility matters most. Then chop the beholders down with fighters, clerics and backstabbing thieves while fireballing the priests, elves and rashashkas. Two or three tries. Sigh, it's not that hard.

subject: Leather Godesses of Phobos: HELP!!
q: In Leather Godesses of Phobos, how do you kill Thorbast after taking his sword, what is the answer to the sultan's question, and how do you get past the Large Machine by the canal without being fried?
a: Don't kill Thorbast. Give the sword back and get him to give up. The answer to the riddle is "Riddle". For the machine, send the barge downstream alone, wait till it passes the beam, then enter the black circle in the well bottom. Think a little, will you?

subject: Pool of Radiance
q: In Pool of Radiance on the Mac, my dwarf fighter can't unready the +1/+3 sword from the graveyard quest, and another +2 sword makes whoever wields it lose hit points. What's going on?
a: The first is a bug in the original program; the sword's name is too wide for the List Manager. SSI replaced the 1.0 disks with a newer version. The +2 sword has an alignment and burns followers of other alignments. Alas, there's no warning.

subject: Uninvited : Help? <some minor spoilers>
q: In Uninvited, how do I get past the family of zombies in the garden maze? Also, is the unreachable ceiling light in the upstairs bathroom important, and can the fireplace fire be put out?
a: Sigh. For the zombies, just try going another way. The bathroom light will matter once you can actually reach it. The fire I don't think is important, but it's been a while since I solved the game.

subject: Solarian and System 6.0.7
q: Solarian 1.03 has sound problems since I installed System 6.0.7. Is it the new sound manager?
a: Not generally. Solarian II runs fine on 6.0.7 on a IIcx and IIsi. A Mac II is slower and a sound can block the next one. Current release is 1.04, which you get by paying the shareware fee. Pay up.

subject: Tetris questions
q: Tetris music sounds fine on an SE but garbled on my Mac Plus running under MultiFinder. Is that the Plus?
a: It's MultiFinder, not your Plus. Running Tetris under MF garbles the music, because Tetris lets MF do its housekeeping and the sound drags for a split second. Turn MF off if it bugs you. Hardly a big deal.

subject: Mac Baseball Games?
q: What are people's impressions of the baseball games for the Macintosh, especially very statistical ones? Is Earl Weaver Baseball out for the Mac, and how is it?
a: Earl Weaver Baseball 1.5 is out and quite good. It tracks stats, injuries and standings, with 32 old stadiums, but you can't make your own teams or play in color, and speed depends on your machine. Hardball II tracks stats well and lets you create teams, for around $46. Pick one already.

subject: exit
q: What is the latest version of NetTrek for the Mac, and what's improved? Are there other good network shoot-em-up games for the Mac?
a: Latest I've seen is 2.0. You can play solo against the computer, ships get damaged more ways, keyboard controls are better, and there's destroy base. Not a huge improvement. Falcon is the only other good action game I know of, if you both skip autopilot.

subject: Simcity 1.1 vs 1.2
q: What's the difference between SimCity 1.1 and 1.2? I think the copy protection changed.
a: Not much difference. Version 1.2 makes you look things up on a very dark sheet that's hard to read, and it supports MultiFinder. Unless you're sick of inserting your master disk or want MultiFinder, don't bother upgrading.

subject: Where's Blade??
q: Where's Blade? What's the status of that 256-color Mac game announced here months ago, and what's it about?
a: It was delayed to about the end of the month for last-minute fixes. It's basically a run/jump/kill game for the Mac. There's a screen shot in the back of the latest Macworld. The author brags the main character animation alone eats over a meg of disk.

subject: Wizardry II and game sequels in general
q: Will not having played Wizardry hamper my enjoyment of Wizardry II? Can sequels generally be enjoyed without the original?
a: You can't play Wizardry II without Wizardry I at all. You can't create characters in it; you must build them in the first game and transfer them, ideally at 13th level or so. Many sequels are less strict, but start with Wiz I.

subject: printer (postscript) cheap in Comuter shopper
q: An ad in Computer Shopper offers a PostScript printer, the LX29000, for $1295 with HP LaserJet emulation and an AMD RISC processor. What's the catch?
a: The catch is it's not true PostScript, and the ad doesn't claim it is. Read it again: it says PostScript compatible. The price is believable and an excellent deal, but learn to read marketing.

subject: Help with color Deskwriter
q: Can a DeskWriter be upgraded to a color DeskWriter? How many colors, where is it done, and how's the output?
a: Yes, but only an authorized HP repair shop can do it, for $450 plus tax. You get 24-bit color, though it won't add AppleTalk if you lack it. You need 32-bit QuickDraw, which the IIsi and LC have built in. It's a lovely printer.

subject: Using HP Deskjet 500 (for IBM) with Mac
q: Can a Mac SE drive an HP Deskjet 500 over serial, using the DeskWriter driver? Does that driver speak PCL, or has someone written a driver that does?
a: Can't say if the DeskWriter driver works, but there's a driver made specifically for the HP Deskjet, source included. Get it by anonymous FTP from rascal.ics.utexas.edu in misc/mac/printing-support. Try that first, sigh.

subject: SE/30 video (Micron Technology?)
q: Does anyone have the address, telephone or price for Micron Technology's 8-bit video card for the SE/30 that drives the internal monitor?
a: Micron Technology is at 800 642-7661 in the US or 208 368-3800. Suggested retail is $339 for the 8-bit card, $89 for the internal grayscale adapter and about $569 for 24 bit. The 8-bit card isn't out for a couple of weeks. Try calling next time.

subject: Printing Mailing List Faster
q: How can I print an 8000-name Filemaker Pro mailing list faster on an Imagewriter LQ? It takes 8 hours and I can't use the fastest print option.
a: Fastest mode sends only characters, not bitmaps, so the application can't control formatting. That's incompatible with your 4-across layout, and many programs don't support it anyway. 8000 labels in 8 hours sounds pretty good to me. Want speed? Buy a faster printer.

subject: Mac IIci cache card
q: I installed the cache card Apple sent for my Mac IIci. What do I have to do to use it? Do I adjust the RAM cache in the Memory control panel?
a: Nothing. Just plug it in, which you already did. It's a memory cache, not a disk cache, so leave the control panel alone. You should see about a 20% speedup, especially on memory-intensive work. Honestly, that was in the manual, such as it is.

subject: StyleWriter Ink cartridge: other sources?
q: I ran out of ink in my StyleWriter. Is the Apple dealer really the only source for new ink cartridges?
a: No. The StyleWriter uses a Canon BJ-10e engine, and that cartridge seems to be the same. Bookstores also sell refill kits with two ink-filled syringes you jab into the old cartridge. Two refills cost about one Apple cartridge. Apple's markup, again.

subject: hardware questions
q: I'm buying a Mac IIci. How can I speed it up, does it need a cache card or a math coprocessor, and what is a SuperDrive?
a: Accelerators exist that bring a IIci up to IIfx speed, but if you're buying new, just get a Quadra 700. Every IIci already ships with a cache card, and Mac II-series machines have an FPU except the IIsi. A SuperDrive reads 800K and 1.44M floppies, and with third-party software, MS-DOS disks too.

subject: Stylewriter & Deskwriter prices
q: Is $383 for a Stylewriter with a student discount reasonable? Can I get a Deskwriter with a student discount, and at what price?
a: That's about the best you'll do for a Stylewriter. HP edu discounts via dealers are for faculty and some staff, not students. Deskwriters were around $375 to $399 in NYC and under $500 by mail order, and worth the extra for two to three times the speed.

subject: Hard Disks that take power from floppy port
q: Is it wise to buy hard disks that take their power from the Mac floppy port for our Plus and SE users? Will the power supply burn out from the extra load?
a: Don't do it on a Mac Plus. Its power supply is under-specified; it doesn't even provide SCSI termination power, supposedly because the margins are so thin. An SE would probably be safe, I think. Buy proper drives with their own supply.

subject: Device to allow your CD player to be used to read data ?
q: Is there a SCSI device that lets a conventional CD music player read data into a Macintosh?
a: No, never heard of one, and it would probably cost as much as a CD-ROM reader anyway. Those run $400 to $800, usually around $600. Going the other way is easy, though, if you're desperate.

subject: Micropolis 1303? Anyone? Anyone?
q: What capacity is a Micropolis 1303 5 1/4 inch hard drive, and can it work on a Mac SE/30 over SCSI?
a: Micropolis says the 1303 is a 35 Mb MFM drive, so no dice for a Mac. Next time, call the manufacturer first instead of wasting bandwidth, sigh.

subject: Quadra MEMORY configurations
q: What memory configurations does the Quadra support? Can I install 2 or 4 SIMMs of 1MB or 4MB, and is it the standard SIMM and not the FX version?
a: Not all of those combinations will work. The Quadra has a 32-bit address bus, so you need to add memory in groups of four SIMMs. That rules out the two-SIMM combos. I'd assume, anyway; read the manual.

subject: Silverlining?
q: Where can I find a low-level formatting routine like Silverlining for an SE?
a: Silverlining itself, genius. I've run it on SE/30s, Plusses and IIsis, so an SE should be no problem.

subject: Ethernet throughput on Mac
q: Why is Mac-to-Mac ethernet file transfer only 2-3 times faster than LocalTalk, around 25,000 bytes per second, when NeXTs get 250,000? Can I speed up the Mac?
a: Something is broken on your end. Large file transfers over Ethernet should be at least 10 times faster than LocalTalk. One Mac pulled a 3569K file off an AppleShare server in 22 seconds, about 169K per second. Go fix your setup.

subject: SE --> SE/30 upgrade discontinued?
q: Will Apple keep selling the SE to SE/30 upgrade, or is it being discontinued?
a: Nobody outside Apple knows for sure. They've dropped the Mac Plus logic board kits, but still sell SuperDrive kits for the SE and II. Old upgrades linger on the price list for years, so expect it for a year or two. Don't panic.

subject: hypercard & TOPS
q: After I installed the 3/18/87 TOPS upgrade on our Mac Pluses, HyperCard freezes while opening. What's going on?
a: HyperCard isn't the problem. The old TOPS installer replaces system resources with older ones. Get a fresh system file, drag-copy the TOPS files and use Font/DA Mover for the DA. Sigh, installers that stomp your System are a tradition.

subject: Creating custom ICONs for use with HyperCard
q: Can HyperCard use ICN# resources for icon buttons? Is there a utility to turn an ICN# into an ICON resource?
a: No, you're right, HyperCard can NOT use ICN#s. Use the IconMaker DA or ResEdit instead, since both produce plain ICONs. Read the docs next time.

subject: How can I...
q: Can I embed a program in HyperCard that calculates where planets are and positions buttons accordingly? Can HyperCard call outside code?
a: Write an XFCN. Your compiler should ship a HyperXCmd header; HyperCard calls your subroutine by name from a script. XCMDs return nothing, XFCNs do. The catch is no globals. Or do the math in HyperTalk if you're patient. Not hard.

subject: Typing Something into HyperCard
q: Can I get HyperCard to execute a command key equivalent such as Cmd-A from a script? Typing "A" with the command key down didn't work.
a: Don't try to fake keystrokes. If you have Macro-maker or another macro program, write a macro that types the combination you want, then put a doMenu command in your script. Sigh, the menu command is what you wanted all along.

subject: Setting card size via HyperTalk
q: Can I set the card size via HyperTalk in HyperCard 2.0? I can only change it in the Stack Info dialog.
a: Yes: set the rect of this card to "0,0,342,512", same as the Resize button in Stack Info. To change only the window size, without losing ornaments and paint outside the rectangle, set the rect of card window instead. It's in the manual.

subject: Do Hypercard and Sys 7 fit on a small machine?
q: Can System 7 run HyperCard on a Mac 512ke or Mac Plus with 2 megabytes of RAM?
a: If System 7 runs on a given Mac, HyperCard runs alongside it. With 2 megabytes it's about like HyperCard under 6.x single Finder on a 1 meg machine. Cramped, but that's what you get.

subject: Can HC 2.0 move files in the finder?
q: Can a HyperCard 2.0 stack copy files from a floppy to a folder on the hard disk, or the other way around, like the Finder does?
a: Yes, but not with plain HyperTalk. Use one of the XCMDs in the support tools, which you can fetch from the mac.archive.umich.edu site. Honestly, go read what's in the archive before asking.

subject: get pixel state command?
q: How can I get the on/off state of a pixel at a given X,Y coordinate in HyperTalk?
a: You can't get there from HyperTalk. The Toolbox call GetPixel(h,v) returns whether the pixel is black or white, so you need an XFCN wrapping it. It's been done before, but I don't remember by whom. Not a hard XFCN to write.

subject: hypercard printing mailing labels
q: How can I print HyperCard fields as mailing labels with first and last name on one line, instead of each field printing vertically down the label?
a: Get "Reports for HyperCard", a set of scripts and XCMDs sold, I think, by Activision. It gives you far better custom report layout and handles your problem. Print Report was never going to do it. Pay up, or hack it yourself.

subject: Two simple (TRIVIAL!) questions
q: How can I select all the text in a single HyperCard field from a script, and what's the best HyperTalk book for advanced programming?
a: Use "select text of fld <fldname>". As for books, Winkler and Kamins, "HyperTalk 2.0: The Book", has been very helpful, though it's one of only two I've bothered with, so "best" is your problem.

subject: system messages
q: How can a HyperCard stack log data every N minutes while the user does something else in the stack? I want a timer message without busywaiting, preferably without waiting for MultiFinder.
a: Use an on idle handler. Store a target time in a global at openStack, and in on idle check whether the seconds have passed it, add the interval and do your work. Keep the code light, and pass idle. Put it in your Home Stack script. Not rocket science.

subject: Constant Pitch Text?
q: How do I change the text in a HyperCard field to constant pitch, where every character occupies the same space like a line printer?
a: Use a monospaced font. Monaco shipped with your Macintosh, and Courier comes with the LaserWriter. Font vendors sell others. Honestly, this isn't hard.

subject: abort process
q: How do I detect that a HyperCard process was aborted with Command-Period, so I can reset variables and run clean-up routines? It isn't sent along the message path.
a: Set a global variable when the process begins and clear it when the process ends. Then install an idle handler that checks the global. If it's still set there, the process was interrupted, so do your cleanup. Basic bookkeeping, really.

subject: How to unlock a stack?
q: How do I unlock a HyperCard stack once I've selected Protect Stack from the File menu?
a: Hold down the command key, I believe, while you mouse into the File menu, and the protect option shows up so you can undo it. It won't beat an unknown password, naturally. Sigh.

subject: HC 2.0, XCMDs, THINK C, globals
q: How does HyperCard 2.0 handle XCMDs and their globals? Does it jump to the real resource or a copy, and how can I keep globals between calls?
a: HyperCard copies the external and jumps to the copy. Externals have no globals off HyperCard's A5. Either pass values in from script globals, or follow tech note 256 and make a private A5 world. Restore HyperCard's A5 before any callback or kablooey.

subject: R/Ws to disk
q: HyperCard does disk I/O whenever a script puts text into a field, which makes it miss mouse clicks. Can I defer that disk I/O?
a: No. In idle time HyperCard writes RAM back to disk until the stack on disk mirrors the stack in RAM, so a power failure loses almost nothing. You CANNOT DEFER THE DISK I/O. Live with it.

subject: Getting complete HC 2.0 Pkg
q: I bought a Macintosh Classic and got a disabled HyperCard with hardly any stacks or documentation. How can I get the complete HyperCard 2.0 package?
a: Many user groups distribute the full five-disk HyperCard 2.0. BMUG in Berkeley sells the set for $15, takes VISA by phone, and you needn't be a member. Quit waiting on your dealer, who clearly knows nothing.

subject: Merging Stacks
q: I have two address stacks I want to merge without ending up with two backgrounds. Does anyone have a script for that?
a: No script needed. There's an XCMD that merges any backgrounds together, however different they look or however many fields they have. It was posted with a stack to comp.binaries.mac. Go fetch it instead of hand-hacking HyperTalk.

subject: HyperCard 2.1
q: I hear HyperCard 2.1 changed the Picture XCMD so it behaves differently from what Goodman and other manuals describe. Is that true?
a: Rumor, and a persistent one. Picture got only two changes in 2.1: a bug fix so mouseUpInPicture is sent only if the mouse is still over the picture, and a sixth parameter for floating windows. Goodman is still current. Winkler and Kamins was wrong all along.

subject: Importing Text ?????
q: I import about 3000 names from a Word text file into HyperCard in stages. After deleting the imported names and re-saving the file, HyperCard starts again from the very first name. How can it import something that isn't there?
a: Because Word keeps the document open even after you've closed it, until you quit. Microsoft tech support says it tracks clipboard selections as pointers into the document. Quit Word first. Typical.

subject: How do I unprotect my own stack?
q: I protected my HyperCard stack and set userlevel to 1, and now the file menu doesn't show Protect Stack. How do I unprotect my own stack?
a: Hold down the command key while pulling down the file menu. Then Protect Stack shows up and you can fix things. Basic trick, but nobody reads the manual.

subject: Arrowkeys and HyperCard
q: I set textArrows to true in HyperCard, but my stack-level arrow key script still runs instead of acting as real arrows inside an editable field. What am I doing wrong?
a: Pressing an arrow key always sends an arrowKey message to the card, whether textArrows is true or false. The property only affects what HyperCard does with that message. So check in your script for an insertion point and pass the message on. RTFM.

subject: Palettes in hc2
q: In HyperCard 2, my palette has buttons that stay highlighted until another is selected. When I open the palette, how can I highlight the default choice from a script?
a: Use the hilitedButton property: set the hilitedButton of window "paletteName" to buttonNumber. It's a one-liner, and the property list in the docs would have told you.

subject: Trouble saving report format in 2.0
q: In HyperCard 2.0, I converted an old stack and want to save the report format, but after printing, the report and its name vanish even though I said yes to saving. What am I missing?
a: Start the print job so it prompts you to save the report, click OK, then cancel before printing gets underway. That got around it for me, from memory. The manual is useless on this, naturally.

subject: French Accents in Hypercard
q: In HyperCard on a Mac SE, making an accent grave with option and tilde can fire a command-key shortcut and send students back a card. Can I disable those speed keys?
a: Trap it in your stack script with an on commandkeydown handler: if the key isn't the tilde, pass commandkeydown. Otherwise, try fonts that put accents on other keys, or a key remapper, though that messes with HyperCard's own keys. Think a bit.

subject: "Repeat with...." question
q: In HyperCard, "repeat with the number of cards of this bkgnd" fails. How do I loop over only the cards of one background, or find the number of cards in a single background?
a: "The number of cards" only works for the whole stack, so you can't tack "of this bkgnd" onto it. Go to the first card of the background, remember its short id, then step with "go next card of this bkgnd" until you're back at that id. It's slow, but that's HyperCard for you.

subject: Strange behaviour (dare I say bug)
q: In HyperCard, a find next button whose script just does returnKey finds the same occurrence again, but pressing Return finds the next one. Why, and how do I build a find next button?
a: Clicking makes HyperCard drop the find rectangle, so the returnKey restarts the find from scratch and hits the same spot. Either teach users to press Return, or script a button that does go next, do msg box, and go prev if not found. Fiddly, but there you go.

subject: MacTCP problem
q: In MacTCP Toolkit 1.0, TCPRecvChars only returns the first buffer of about 1500 chars when I ask for 25000, instead of waiting for all of them. TCPCharsAvailable returns only 1500 to 2000 at first. Is this a bug?
a: TCPCharsAvailable only reports what has already arrived locally, not what's still waiting at the far end. Pass that number to TCPRecvChars and it returns right away. Waiting for the full 25000 should work, so it sounds like a bug. But freezing the machine for it is what makes users hit the reboot button. Read a buffer at a time, you lazy bum.

subject: Goodman's HC2 book complete?
q: Is Goodman's HyperCard 2.0 book complete with respect to HyperTalk? I'm looking for a book with a full HyperTalk 2.0 reference and the new HyperCard features.
a: Can't speak for Goodman's, but get "HyperTalk 2.0: The Book" by Dan Winkler and Scot Kamins, from Bantam. Written by the HyperTalk creator, so it's thorough, with plenty of example scripts. Not for beginners, so don't whine if it's over your head.

subject: Extract text from fields in HC?
q: Is there a simple way to extract the text from all the fields in a HyperCard stack? Copying and pasting into a word processor is too slow, and printing from HC is too slow for a big stack.
a: Grab the Import/Export stack, import-export-tools.hqx, from the info-mac/card directory on sumex-aim.stanford.edu. It lets you pick the background, fields, delimiter and field order. Without HC 2.1, fields over 16384 characters won't import right. Read the docs, too.

subject: Creating Reports
q: Is there a way in HyperCard to build up report templates from scripts, creating an item, positioning and sizing it, giving it commands and default font, size and style info?
a: Unfortunately, no. You can't do that from scripts. Sigh, go ask for it in the next release like everyone else.

subject: How to tell when really idle?
q: Is there a way in HyperCard to tell when it's really been idle for, say, five minutes, so I can run a keep? Counting idle messages needs a reset whenever anything else happens.
a: Don't count messages. Save the ticks each time your idle handler runs, and if the gap since the last call is bigger than your handler's normal interval, something interrupted it, so restart the timer. Otherwise do the keep once five minutes' worth of ticks have passed. Crude, but it works.

subject: Address Stack Import
q: Is there an easy way to import an old Address stack into the HyperCard 2.0 background?
a: Yes, use the import button or menu item. It offers text or old-style address stack. Works nicely, but it only finds the zip on the city, state, zip form, chokes on apartment numbers, and dumps unparsable stuff in the notes field. Don't expect magic.

subject: Interface between HT and Relational DB?
q: Is there an interface between HyperTalk and some relational database?
a: There's an Oracle/HyperCard XCMD set that hooks into a multiuser database on a remote non-Mac server. It's "only" $999, and the single-user version is, I think, $199. Vendors do love their prices.

subject: Why no 'case' statement in Hypertalk? Suggestions?
q: Is there really no case statement in HyperTalk? I'm stuck writing ugly nested if-then-else for keypress trapping.
a: There's no case statement, and you don't need one. Chain it with plain else if and a single end if at the end, or send the key as a message to handlers named a, b and c. It's not nesting. Read the manual.

subject: Problem with videodisc XCMD and P6000
q: The Apple videodisc XCMDs work fine with a Pioneer 6000A but pause over a second per command on a plain Pioneer 6000. Is that the cause, and can the source be changed to fix it?
a: The HyperCard Videodisc Toolkit simply doesn't work properly with the 6000, only the 6000A. The 6000 lacks several commands the A has, and some are critical. Some commands fail outright, others just glitch like your pause. Buy the A.

subject: debuggers for XCMD's
q: What debuggers can I use for XCMDs written in THINK C? The THINK C source-level debugger needs more memory than I have and seems to only run from within the project.
a: HyperCard 2.0 lets you debug XCMDs written in MPW Pascal or C with SADE. Nobody else offered anything better, so don't hold your breath for THINK to follow suit. Time to learn MPW, I suppose.

subject: Claris Phone Humber for Hypercard 2.0 Upgrade
q: What phone number do I call to get the HyperCard 2.0 upgrade from Claris?
a: Claris Customer Relations, (408) 727-8227. They're sending out a free bug-fix upgrade from HC2.0 to the newer 2.0 version. Whether 1.x owners get a deal, I can't say. Go ask them instead of the net.

subject: System 6.05 (crash) & HyperCard 2.0
q: What's special about System 6.05, which HyperCard 2.0 needs? What differs from 6.04?
a: Two things: TextEdit 3.0 and Sound Manager fixes. HC 2.0 uses TextEdit for field text, and TE 3.0 gives full Script Manager compatibility, so multi-lingual text works. HC also needs the Sound Manager changes. Read the release notes next time.

subject: how to get field from specific card
q: What's the HyperCard syntax for getting a field from a specific named card? Or should I send that card a message to set a global from the field?
a: There's no way except to go to that card. Lock screen, push card, go to the card, get the field, pop card, unlock screen, then use it. Locking the screen makes it faster. That's HyperCard for you.

subject: Hypercard 2.1 and Developers Kit, differences?
q: What's the difference between the $49 HyperCard 2.1 upgrade and the $140 Claris Development kit? Is the upgrade crippled?
a: No crippling. The Development kit just adds more documentation and maybe a couple of extra stacks, reports differ. The HyperCard application itself is the same in both. Paying $90 for manuals, how nice for Claris.

subject: Memory loss when browsing
q: Why does a HyperCard stack produce free memory and lose space while just being browsed at user level 1, and is there a workaround?
a: Scripts probably put data into fields. HyperCard then moves the card to the end of the stack file so it can grow, leaving a hole. Set cantModify in the stack info box to stop it, at some cost in speed. Learn how your tools work.

subject: compression makes stack bigger!
q: Why does my HyperCard stack get bigger when I compress it, and why is there such a large overhead loading 221k of text into a stack?
a: Sigh. HyperCard builds hint info so FIND runs fast, and Compact Stack grows it once you have hundreds of cards, so the stack gets bigger but finds faster. The overhead comes from moving cards around and leaving holes, which only Compact Stack coalesces. Append to the end and the slop shouldn't be there.

subject: Windoids: Where for art thou?
q: Why has nobody posted Windoid newsletters after issue 6? Could someone post issues 7 and later?
a: There's nothing to post. Issue 6 is still the latest as far as anyone watching AppleLink can tell. They're probably busy with HyperCard 1.2 and 2.0. Patience, kid.

subject: Hypercard FIND problems...
q: Why is HyperCard's find so slow for strings like XX.XX.XX with short pieces, while a three-character search is instant? How do I get around it?
a: It's designed in. HyperCard keeps hint bits, a trigram hash of the text, and anything under three letters is dropped from the hints, so it falls back to a slow card-by-card search. Make your search targets three characters or more. Live with it.

subject: System 7 / Inside Mac Question
q: Will there be an Inside Mac volume 6 for System 7, or will the new programmer information just trickle out as tech notes?
a: Inside Mac VI, obviously. System 7 would need about 800 tech notes, and nobody sane wants to write those. No word on when it ships, so quit pestering and wait.

subject: Compactor (Where is it?)
q: Where can I get Compactor for the Mac?
a: Try nic.funet.fi, 128.214.6.100, in the pub/mac/arcers directory. Compactor lives there with the other archivers. Use archie or look around before asking the whole net, sigh.

subject: TEGetText and TESetText
q: After TEGetText, how do I dispose of the old text handle without nullifying hText in the TextEdit record when I plug in my filtered copy with TESetText?
a: Either munge hTE^^.hText in place and call TECalText, or copy it with HandAndHand, dispose the old hText, assign your copy, and call TECalText. TESetText copies the source, so you end up with three copies in RAM. The first way keeps one copy, so use that.

subject: Color Quickdraw and RBGBackColor
q: After my app calls RGBBackColor with other colors and then back to white, dialog buttons in other apps turn black once it quits. What am I doing wrong?
a: Do a proper SetPort before RGBBackColor. It sounds like you set the desktop background, not the window background. For a black window, make a 'wctb' resource with the same ID as your WIND and use GetNewCWindow. Basic stuff.

subject: system 6.0 upgrade problem
q: After upgrading to System 6.0 and running the boot block fixup program, my 80meg hard drive won't boot by itself and I have to boot from a floppy. Suggestions?
a: You trashed the boot blocks. That fixup program is for an older system release, so you wrote the wrong version. Use the Installer or boot from the upgrade disk and recopy System and Finder, which rewrites them. Next time read the readme.

subject: profiling and speeding up Mac code
q: Are there standard speedup tricks for Mac code, and is there a profiler to see where my code spends its time?
a: MPW ships with code profiling libraries, and they work well. Use them instead of guessing where the time goes. Some of us profile before we whine about speed.

subject: HyperCard Suggestion - a closeField even when no change
q: Can HyperCard send a message when someone tabs or clicks out of a field without changing its contents? Maybe a new message like leaveField.
a: Already done. HyperCard sends exitField when the user leaves a field without changing it. RTFM before asking Apple for features it shipped long ago.

subject: Loading and running XFCNs
q: Can I GetResource an XFCN, lock the handle, and call the dereferenced pointer as a ProcPtr with my own XCmdBlock, outside HyperCard?
a: Yes, it should work. Just save your critical CPU registers before the JSR and restore them on return, in case the XFCN trashes A5. Do the same around callbacks. A5 at minimum; I save D0-D7 and A0-A6 to be safe. Basic hygiene.

subject: Faster keyboard processing from HyperCard
q: Can I install a routine in HyperCard that traps keyboard input and sends characters straight to the Communications Toolbox, since the keyDown handler is slow?
a: Yes, if you go the XCMD route. With HC 2.x and XWindows, an XCMD can make a BeginXWEdit callback and get all the keystrokes. You'll get an xGiveUpEdit event if someone takes the keyboard back, which you can ignore, though that's obnoxious.

subject: MDEF code in Pascal
q: Can anyone send me Pascal code for a tools MDEF and a patterns MDEF in Lightspeed Pascal? My attempt draws only some cells, highlights random shapes, and returns no meaningful numbers.
a: Look at the ObjectDraw sample that ships with THINK Pascal 3.0. It has three custom MDEFs in Pascal, for tools, patterns and colors, built into the program source. Read the samples that came in the box before you post.

subject: Virtual 2.0 and DiskExpress
q: Can virtual memory utilities like Virtual 2.0 coexist with automatic disk optimizers such as DiskExpress II, given that Virtual needs contiguous disk space?
a: I believe you can lock down files so DiskExpress won't touch them while optimizing, and you'd do that for the VM swapfile. Personally, optimizing the disk every day is compulsive, and the constant disk access while you're trying to think is annoying.

subject: Correct handling of PixPatHandles
q: Cloning a PixPatHandle before every PenPixPat or BackPixPat call fragments the heap under A/UX, which doesn't seem to compact. How can I cut down on all those allocations?
a: Don't worry about it. A fragmented heap isn't really a bad thing under A/UX, since there's a virtual memory system underneath it. Stop fretting over nothing.

subject: missing bits of ioFlAttrib field (HParamBlkRec)
q: Do the undocumented odd bits of the ioFlAttrib field in HParamBlkRec mean anything? And is the resource-fork-open bit always a reliable sign the application is busy?
a: Dunno what they mean, and you shouldn't care. Undocumented bits, bytes and words are reserved by Apple and subject to change without warning, so never rely on them meaning anything. Stick to the documented ones.

subject: MPW and inline "Assembly"
q: Does MPW support inline assembly, like an asm block, without hex and without a separate assembly source file? Just a yes or no, please.
a: No. Not that you need it, since the compiler does a fine job on trap calls and the code is hard to beat. For real hand-tuning, use a separate .a file with the full assembler and macros. Inline asm is a maintenance nightmare anyway.

subject: Munging the Munger
q: Does _Munger respect the size of the handle when deleting a chunk of bytes from the middle? What ends up at the physical end of the handle?
a: It uses GetHandleSize and SetHandleSize to get the output handle the right length, so the handle gets truncated. It's in the last note of the Munger entry in Inside Mac. RTFM.

subject: Appletalk Confirm
q: Does an AppleTalk NBPConfirm generate network traffic? If the target is in my own zone, can my machine's names table confirm it without any traffic?
a: Yes, it generates traffic. Your names table only lists names your own machine registered. A confirm works like a lookup, except it's sent straight to the NBP socket of the node that registered the name, rather than broadcast zone-wide. Across cables it goes through the bridge. Learn how it works.

subject: develop magazine subscription
q: Does anyone have a number to call about subscription problems with develop magazine? I'm trying to subscribe but getting nothing.
a: All subscriptions go through the fulfillment house: 800/443-9637 outside CA, 800/331-4164 inside CA. If that fails, write the editor, who is reportedly responsive to this sort of thing. Try the phone first.

subject: VBL or patch traps?
q: For an INIT that pops up an alarm dialog after a set time, should I use a VBL task or patch WaitNextEvent/GetNextEvent?
a: Patch the trap, not the VBL. You run when the foreground app is looking for something else to do, you get far more freedom with memory and the toolbox than at interrupt level, and you can take your time. It's called WAITnextEvent for a reason.

subject: x windows on the mac 2
q: Has X Windows been ported to the Mac II, and how good is the performance?
a: A port under A/UX is reportedly in the works and should be out sometime this fall. No word on the price or the speed yet. Don't hold your breath on vapor.

subject: Mac<->Nintendo PowerGlove Interface?
q: Has anyone figured out how to hook a Nintendo PowerGlove up to a Mac? What sensors does it actually have?
a: Don't bother expecting much. The PowerGlove instruments only one index finger joint, giving 4 values for roughly 0, 30, 60 and 90 degrees. It has no real position sensor, just a little wrist button box. Mattel won't even tell VPL the data format, so you'd be reverse engineering it.

subject: MIDI Manager question
q: Has anyone gotten MIDI Manager 1.2 working on a Mac Plus? My programs work on my SE/30 but send and receive no MIDI packets on a friend's Plus.
a: Word is MIDI Manager 1.2 doesn't work on a Plus, thanks to bugs in the Apple Serial Drivers, though the MIDI Manager proper is probably fine. Version 1.1 of everything works. Typical Apple software, shipped without testing.

subject: Can LSC call a Pascal function pointer?
q: How can I call a Pascal function through a function pointer in LightSpeed C 3.0? The pascal keyword and parameter list in the typedef work in MPW but LSC won't accept them.
a: Use the CallPascal family: CallPascal, CallPascalB, CallPascalW and CallPascalL, depending on the return type. Pass the pointer to the Pascal function as the LAST argument. Check the manual, since you evidently didn't read it. Or write an ugly front-end caller in plain C.

subject: Detecting 3rd Party Math Co-Processors.. How?
q: How can I detect a third-party FPU, like the SuperMac SpeedCard's, when SysEnvirons() doesn't report it?
a: The trouble is boards using a fast 68000 or 68010 with a memory-mapped FPU, and SysEnvirons() can't see those. Unless the maker supplies an INIT to patch SysEnvirons(), or some alternate mechanism, you're out of luck. It does catch normal 68020/68030 boards.

subject: Need sample code for folder/file lookup.
q: How can I find out whether the blessed System folder exists on a volume, and whether a prefs-like file exists inside it, without using SFGet/PutFile?
a: For the boot volume's System folder, call SysEnvirons and read the sysVRefNum field. Then try to create your prefs file. If you get an already-exists error, open it; otherwise open and initialize it. Don't make this harder than it is.

subject: A-Trap length
q: How can I find the length of a ROM trap on the Mac so I can copy it to RAM?
a: Don't try it. ROM traps aren't sorted by trap number, you may get somebody's patch instead of the real thing, and the code has PC-relative jumps to ROM utility routines. Tell us why you want it, and we'll find a saner way.

subject: Purge or Revert Resource?
q: How can I revert a resource already loaded in memory to the version on disk while keeping the same handle? LoadResource does nothing if it's already loaded, and I can't find a PurgeResource.
a: There's no clean way to keep the same handle. You should be making provisional changes on a COPY of the resource anyway, so you can revert at will. Only if you keep the changes, copy it back to the Resource Manager's handle and call ChangedResource. Design it right the first time.

subject: How do I tell if I'm *inside* MacsBug?
q: How can I tell whether the code I've interrupted or the trap I've intercepted is running inside MacsBug?
a: RTFM, Appendix C of the Macsbug 6.1 reference. MacJmp holds the entry point with flags in the high byte in 24-bit mode, or flags at $BEE in 32-bit mode. Bit 7 is set if Macsbug is running.

subject: How can a desk accessory find application windows?
q: How can a desk accessory find the application's window, or its title? FrontWindow returns nil because the WindowList global is nilled out when a DA is launched.
a: Open your DA's own window and read the nextWindow field of its window record. That's the window right under yours, which is probably, though not guaranteed to be, the application's window. Not pretty, but the Desk Manager nilled the list on you.

subject: System CLUT's weird pallette
q: How did Apple choose the layout of the system color lookup table? It seems heavy on some shades and weak on others, and not obviously regular.
a: It's not mysterious. The first 216 colors are every combination of 6 values each of red, green and blue, since 6 cubed is 216. The last 40 are 10 reds, 10 greens, 10 blues and 10 grays. Do the arithmetic.

subject: blinking caret
q: How do I blink the insertion caret in a dialog edit text item without calling ModalDialog or DialogSelect?
a: Look at the DialogRecord. It has a textH field, which is the TEHandle the dialog uses, so call TEIdle() on that. Don't use GetDItem(), because for text items it returns only a CharsHandle, not a TEHandle. Read Inside Mac.

subject: How to calculate number of lines for a text box?
q: How do I calculate the number of lines a string will take in a dialog text box, given word wrap? Do I have to simulate it with FindWord and TextWidth?
a: No. Make a TextEdit record with a dest rect of the right width, install the text, call TECalText, then read the nLines field. The Dialog Manager uses TextEdit anyway, so the answer matches. Obvious, really.

subject: Changing THINK C default font
q: How do I change the default font for the THINK C editor? I think it needs ResEdit on the THINK C application.
a: RTFM, page 98. Use ResEdit to modify the CNFG 0 resource in the THINK C application. The second, third and fourth words specify font number, font size and tab width for new Untitled windows. Someday they'll index those manuals properly.

subject: Which HFS calls are avaiable?
q: How do I check whether PBOpenDF is available on the Mac? I can't tell what the gestaltFullExtFSDispatching flag means or what it will be under System 6.0.7.
a: That flag only matters to external file system writers, so ignore it. HFSDispatch is still trap $A060 as far as I can tell. Check for the FSSpec calls instead: call Gestalt with gestaltFSAttr and look at bit 1. Read the docs properly.

subject: Popup Menus
q: How do I generate the little downward arrow that the new HIG recommends to mark a popup menu? It isn't in the Chicago font, and I'm using a PICT for now.
a: A PICT is a decent way to go, but it's drawn in one color, so matching the menu text color is a pain. You could also use a FillPoly. Do try to keep up with the toolbox.

subject: How to get a 1-byte byte in Think P?
q: How do I get a 1-byte byte in THINK Pascal? sizeOf(byte) says 2, and I want to read DITLs without splitting integers into high and low bytes.
a: Sigh, Byte is a 0..255 subrange and Pascal has no unsigned, so it takes two bytes, a LisaPascal holdover. SignedByte, Boolean, small enumerations and packed arrays of Char are one byte. Use a packed array of byte over the DITL handle.

subject: How to get arrow cursor in cDev?
q: How do I get an arrow cursor in a cdev? The Control Panel keeps setting it to the cross-hair.
a: Add a 'CURS' -4064 resource to your cdev file. Its contents don't matter; its presence tells the Control Panel to send you cursorDev messages instead of setting the cross. You still set the cursor yourself. It's in a tech note, TN 215. RTFM.

subject: ENTER/Return in Modeless dialog
q: How do I make Return/Enter act like button item #1 in a modeless dialog, so it doesn't put a newline into a TextEdit field? I'd like to see the key event too.
a: Call IsDialogEvent each time through your event loop. If it returns true, do your special key processing first, so check for a keyDown and the key. If it's return, treat it as item 1. Otherwise pass the event to DialogSelect. Inside Macintosh I, page 417 covers it, so go verify it.

subject: How does one save/restore clipping?
q: How do I save a port's clipping region and restore it later on the Mac?
a: Use GetClip() and SetClip(), IM-I-166,167. Preserving the current clipRgn is exactly what they're for. If you're on MacApp, use GetFocus and SetFocus, and allocate the clipRgn in the FocusRec first. It's in Inside Mac, you know.

subject: How to send DDP packets LARGER than 600 bytes???
q: How do I send DDP packets larger than 600 bytes on AppleTalk? I'd rather not split a 1200 byte buffer into my own multipacket protocol.
a: Don't use DDP. Under about 4624 bytes, ATP works: 578 bytes in the request, up to 4624 in the response. Beyond that, use ADSP, which is symmetric and takes any amount of data, and it comes with System 7 or an INIT. DDP means doing everything yourself.

subject: Setting Fonts in Dialogs
q: How do I set the font of an editText item in a dialog? Setting the txFont field through the item handle gets ignored and it keeps using the system font.
a: Make the item a user item and maintain your own TEHandle for it. That's easy if it's the only editText, but with other Dialog Manager fields you jump through hoops to avoid two blinking insertion points. Too bad ictb's don't work on the Plus or SE.

q: How do I use and parse the data fork of the application I'm developing on the Mac? I saw PBGetFCB mentioned, but how is the data parsed?
a: Parsing is your problem. Put anything you like in the data fork, in any format you please. Only the resource fork has an enforced format. And get a set of Inside Macintosh; programming the Mac without it is nearly impossible.

subject: Fax Modems and sending files to them.. INFO Wanted
q: How do I write a program that sends text files to an ADB fax modem on a Mac? Is the fax modem treated like any other device?
a: Yes, treat it like any other device. If it has a Chooser device, just raster your text as if printing to any printer. I print to mine with the THINK Class Library and never wrote any printing code. No toaster needed, thanks.

subject: changing screen depth
q: How do you change the screen depth in code on the Mac? It's late and I don't want to search Inside Mac.
a: Read Tech Note 276, which covers the calls and techniques. Beware, some new hardware and third-party video may not work with SetDepth. Sigh, searching docs is the job, late or not.

subject: System 6.0 breaks my cdevs! revisited
q: How do you detect MultiFinder's presence or absence under System 6.0, now that the WaitNextEvent trap is always implemented?
a: You don't, and the Tech Notes said so all along. Apple doesn't want code depending on MultiFinder, since features may migrate. You can test only for WaitNextEvent and temporary memory allocation. Read the Tech Notes before whining.

subject: Chooser Name
q: How do you get the name of the machine as specified in the Chooser? Can my application set that name too?
a: Try GetResource('STR ',-16096). It lives in the System File, which your resource lookups can always reach unless you've been playing games. Under System 7.0 it hands back the Owner Name, not the Macintosh Name, so read the fine print.

subject: Rotating Text
q: How do you rotate text under QuickDraw to write characters along a vertical baseline? My plan is to draw to an offscreen bitmap and rotate the pixels by hand. Is there something more elegant?
a: Nope, your hack is the right way under current and past system software. MacTutor had an article with source that remapped TextEdit to do all four 90 degree rotations. Quit looking for elegance in QuickDraw.

subject: ViewEdit grid size -- how to set it ?
q: How do you set the default grid size in ViewEdit to 8 in each direction instead of 16, without setting it every time?
a: You can't, as far as I know. Nobody's going to tell you otherwise. The request got passed to the ViewEdit guy, so maybe some release after MacApp 2.0 gets it. Don't hold your breath.

subject: Folder Icons
q: How does one create new folder icons on the Mac? For instance, the System Folder has a different icon from other typical folders.
a: The folder icon lives in the Finder's resource fork. The Finder only knows two folder icons, one for the System Folder as a special case and one for everything else. You can edit both with ResEdit, but you can't add new ones. Learn how the Finder works.

subject: AppleTalk Zone names
q: How does the Chooser get the names of the AppleTalk zones? I figured NBPLookup with Zone and Name set to *, but what would the ObjType be?
a: Wrong guess. It isn't NBPLookup at all. The Chooser sends a special ATP request to a nearby bridge to get the zone list. Go read up on ATP instead of guessing.

subject: Messing with TE and Dialogs
q: How exactly do TextEdit records work in dialog boxes? Is there only one TE record for all edit items, and what do editOpen and ParamText storage do? I want to write my own dialog-like thing that still uses the Dialog Manager item lists so I can use ResEdit.
a: You don't need the internals. Just read the Dialog Manager chapter of Inside Mac for the DLOG and DITL formats and how it behaves. The only non-obvious bit is that the editText box sits 3 pixels outside the text, and clicks within 2 pixels count. RTFM.

subject: NuBus Interrupts
q: How long must the interrupt line for a Mac II NuBus slot be asserted? My 10 usec pulse isn't recognized, but holding the line for a second gives lots of interrupts.
a: You must hold the line until your software services the interrupt, and the service routine clears it. The OS dispatcher polls the line state, and if it's still asserted on exit it assumes you want another. Usually a flip-flop on the board does it. This comes up constantly.

subject: Cycles available to program on a IIsi
q: How many cycles are available to a program on a Mac IIsi? What steals cycles and which interrupts preempt a program?
a: The IIsi runs at 25 MHz. Built-in video can add wait states on bank A accesses, depending on depth and screen. Interrupts for VBLs, Time Manager, SCC, VIA and NuBus can fire any time and take as long as they like. The Mac isn't a real-time machine. Read Designing Cards and Drivers.

subject: Required Apple events
q: I added the four required Apple events (oapp, odoc, pdoc, quit) to my app and they work from the Finder, but other apps bomb on the quit event, and mine isn't brought to front before dialogs appear. How should I handle this and test it?
a: Only the Finder is supposed to send the required events, so test with the Finder. On quit, just set a flag and shut down from the idle loop. Calling ExitToShell from the handler will smoke you. For dialogs, use AEInteractWithUser, which waits until you're foreground.

subject: No THINK C 4.0 in this corner of the Great White North
q: I bought THINK C 3.0 and never got an upgrade notice for 4.0. Can I get the upgrade, and who do I ask?
a: Call Symantec customer services at 1-800-441-7234 and ask. You should be able to get the upgrade free if you bought 3.0 recently enough, though I forget the cutoff date. Quit whining on the net and pick up the phone.

subject: keyUp events in THINK C
q: I can't get keyUp events in THINK C's TinyEdit sample even though I call WaitNextEvent with everyEvent set to 0xFFFF. What's wrong?
a: It isn't THINK C. The system event mask in low memory is set up to drop keyUp events by default, since most apps don't care. Call SetEventMask to change it, and RTFM: Inside Mac says so right there.

subject: Custom Icons
q: I changed my application's icon with ResEdit, but the Finder desktop still shows the old one. What makes it use the new icon?
a: Rebuild the desktop. Option-clover restart does it, or just delete the Desktop file on the disk and let the Finder build a new one. It's one of the classic Macintosh gotchas, and you'll lose some custom icon info, so deal with it.

subject: HELP-scanf mystery.
q: I copied unmodified code from Unix to the Mac. It works on Unix and under the ThinkC 4.0 debugger, but with the debugger off it crashes with an application quit error when scanf reads input. I've run the scanf patches. Is this a scanf bug?
a: It's not scanf. You're trashing memory, probably by assuming ints are 4 bytes, or that sizeof int equals sizeof char *. Sigh. Blaming the library is what newbies do. The debugger just hides your bug.

subject: InvalRect proc for dialogs?
q: I have a modeless dialog box and need one section redrawn without redrawing the whole thing. Is there something like InvalRect for the Dialog Manager?
a: Yep, it's called InvalRect. A dialog is a window, so the same call works. Windows is windows. Sigh, think before you post.

subject: balloon help
q: I hear you can add balloon help to a Mac app without programming, just by adding resources. How do I do it?
a: Get BalloonWriter and put its INIT in the Extensions folder. Launch it, attach it to your application file, load a balloon for each resource, and edit the balloons for MENUs, DLOGs and WINDs. Then have it write a new application with the help built in.

subject: 7.0 Released?
q: I heard that System 7.0 has been released. When will it be in the stores?
a: It's out. Dealers have already got copies, and Apple is throwing a party for some 2200 developers at the San Jose Convention Center. Wait till Friday for the big fun. And you get your news from a radio talk show host? Sigh.

subject: PICT format
q: I need to read the information in a PICT resource, like a drawing program puts on the Clipboard. Tech note 21 doesn't say the format of Regions or of PICTs from newer ROMs. What else is missing?
a: Skip parsing it yourself. Replace the QuickDraw standard routines with SetStdProcs, then do a DrawPicture, and you see every operation. It's likely slower, but easier and friendlier across system versions. Nobody here knows how regions are stored, so stop poking at internals.

subject: AppleTalk - ATPCloseSocket
q: I open and name an ATP socket with ATPOpenSocket and PRegisterName, but ATPCloseSocket gives me badATPskt (-1099). Why?
a: Long shot, but change the ATPCloseSocket entry in Appletalk.h to pass a short instead of a char. The library pulls a 16-bit word off the stack. I saw the same with DDPCloseSocket. Apple's headers being wrong again, sigh.

subject: LSC 3.0 & signal
q: I ported a small program from a VAX running Unix to the Mac using LSC 3.0. It uses signal() to break out on control-C, but on the Mac control/command-C and period never break out. Is this a bug in LSC 3.0?
a: Not a bug. Unix is not the natural universe. The C standard never says control-C generates a signal; that's a tty driver feature on some Unixes, running off serial interrupts. Write your own terminal driver for LSC's stdio if you want it. Professors missed that, sigh.

subject: transfer mode that doesn't clobber black bits?
q: I'm drawing arrows on the Mac with PenMode(patXor) for the shaft, but when I add the arrowhead in patXor it knocks out pixels where the head meets the shaft. Is there a transfer mode that draws over existing black pixels and can still be erased by redrawing?
a: Use srcOr for the head, which won't drop pixels, and srcBic to erase it. Four steps: srcXor draw shaft, srcOr draw head, srcXor erase shaft, srcBic erase head. Works only if the head covers nothing but the shaft. Inside Macintosh I-157 has pictures. Read it.

subject: Patching
q: I'm trying to write an INIT that patches the shutdown trap to empty the trash. How do I find where the real trap is and change its address to mine?
a: You don't need to patch _ShutDown at all. Install a shutdown procedure that gets called when the machine restarts or shuts down, and skip the GetTrapAddress/SetTrapAddress mucking about. It's all on page 588 of IM V. Try reading it first.

subject: FKEYs and resources
q: I'm writing an FKEY that may bring up a dialog. Where's the best place to keep its resources, given I don't know which resource files are open when it runs?
a: Put a file in the system folder and, if the user renames it, show an alert saying it can't find the file. Better still, make the pref file a cdev so users can change options in the control panel. Also, Apple may stop supporting FKEYs. Sigh.

subject: Macsbug and DRVR Puzzles!
q: In MacsBug 6.1 the drvr command shows the unit 4 Sony driver entry repeated in unit 1, which IM says is the Lisa HD driver. Why is it repeated, and why did the log command say MacsBug was damaged?
a: The two aren't related. Unit 1 was the old HD20 serial disk driver, and Apple combined it with the Sony driver to save space, so two unit table entries point at one driver. As for log, it calls the file system, which can fail if the file system or OS below it is damaged, or if you call it at interrupt time. Not a mystery.

subject: Problem with menu resources.
q: In THINK C 3.0 my menu resources vanish or load oddly after GetNewMBar. What could be wrong with my menu resources?
a: Check with ResEdit that the menu ID inside the MENU resource matches the resource ID. They are distinct things, and if they don't match your menus won't load. Everybody forgets this one, and it's a classic newbie trap.

subject: Creating THINK C code that uses 68881 if available
q: In THINK C, can I generate code that uses the 68881 only if it is present, or likewise for the 68020? And how do I cast 96 bit doubles to SANE's 80 bit doubles?
a: No. The coprocessor option applies to the whole project, not per source file. Your best bet is MPW: write two versions of the routine and fiddle the make file for each compiler option. Awfully nice feature, but not happening. The cast question went unanswered.

subject: ? THINK C CArrayPane subclass ?
q: In THINK C, my CArrayPane subclass only draws column borders as far as the existing rows, not the full length of the ScrollPane. Is there an easy way to make the borders draw the entire length?
a: Borders only get drawn where cells actually exist, true enough. Overriding DrawBorders should work, so the bug is probably in your code. The grafport is a red herring; TCL panes share the enclosing window's port. Go debug your override.

subject: MacTCP DNR problems
q: In Think C 5.01, OpenResolver(nil) from Apple's dnr.c returns -1 instead of 0 for my MacTCP program, though NCSA Telnet works fine on my machine. What's wrong?
a: OPENRESOLVER is #defined as 1 rather than 1L. The dnr code expects a 32-bit value but THINK C passes a 16-bit int. Make all the selector constants long, and declare rtnCode in the hostInfo struct as long too. Apple changed them back to ints, naturally.

subject: Fake a KeyDown as MouseDown in Modal Dialog
q: In a modal dialog with two TextEdit boxes, how can I make the return key move to the next box? Faking a mouseDown from the filter function doesn't work.
a: Stop faking mouse events. When your filter sees return, call SelIText to select the next box and turn the event into a nullEvent. Or change the key in the event to Tab and let the Dialog Manager handle it.

subject: Missing key-up events
q: In my Think C program, sometimes a key-up event is never generated for a key-down event. Why would that happen?
a: You have to tell the OS Event Manager to report key-up events with SetEventMask. It's in IM II-70. Key-ups are masked off by default, so read the manual before blaming the hardware.

subject: Device drivers : must they be written in assembler?
q: Inside Mac says device drivers are normally written in assembler. Is that still true, or can I write a driver in THINK C?
a: No, write it in whatever language you like, since it all ends up as assembly anyway. Just get the header right. Assembly gives you more control over generated code where timing is critical. Not a dumb question, but read the manual.

subject: Is AppFile.vRefNum always WDRefNum???
q: Is AppFile.vRefNum always a WDRefNum under HFS? I need to find the parent dirID of each file opened from the Finder.
a: No. It's certainly not a WDRefNum for files on an MFS volume, and likely not for files at the root of an HFS volume. A Technote covers it: WDRefNums are -32768, -32767, -32766, while normal vRefNums are close to zero. Read your Technotes.

subject: Think C 5.0 and MacApp
q: Is MacApp supported under Think C 5.0? And how is the new MacApp, which I hear gives serious segmentation errors with MPW 3.2?
a: No current MacApp works with any current THINK C. The segmentation problem under MPW 3.2 is minor: a standard MPW library segment is left locked mid-heap, so merge it into your Main segment. Honestly, that's trivial.

subject: MacTech Journal dead?
q: Is MacTech Journal dead? Their phone number was disconnected and my faxes got no reply.
a: It's alive and well as far as anyone can tell. They had a booth at MacWorld Expo in San Francisco, and someone picked up their latest issue there. Disconnected phone numbers aren't proof of death, you know.

subject: Debuggers
q: Is SADE out, and does it need 4 meg? How is Jasik's debugger, and is MPW a good platform where I can swap in my own editor?
a: SADE is out and doesn't need 4 meg, but it's slow and a hack. Jasik's Debugger is mouse and window driven with source, assembler or mixed levels. MPW isn't fast, and the editor is integrated into the shell, so no swapping. What it offers is power and good code generation.

subject: Pascal compilers
q: Is TML Pascal II, at $79 with basic MPW, worth getting as an MPW Pascal alternative? Does anyone have experience with it or know of problems?
a: It's an excellent product. Code is on par with Apple's MPW compiler, often better, and it compiles far faster. Differences: no constant string indexing, and no packing beyond the byte level. It ships only with MPW. Good price, so quit dithering.

subject: HFS Help
q: Is a vRefNum assigned at runtime, or is it a number I can trust to find the same file on that volume the next time I open it? Is it a reliable way to find a file?
a: No. The vrefnum is dynamic, handed out starting at -2 and counting down. Use the volume name, directory ID and file name to find a file across launches. Within one run, vrefnum plus dirID plus name is safe. Read the book again.

subject: How to do a LEGAL tail-patch
q: Is it a legal tail patch to reset the trap address to the original, call the original trap, then set the address back to my patch?
a: Nope. If the trap checks its return address, it sees your patch instead of the real caller. Apple's come-from patches break the same way. Do a come-again patch: call the original trap yourself, run your code, then jump to the original address. The trap just runs twice.

subject: Safety of using async _Control from ioCompletion?
q: Is it safe to make an asynchronous _Control call from an ioCompletion routine, say an AppleTalk SendResponse from the completion of a GetRequest, if all buffers are preallocated?
a: Yes, it's safe, and many drivers do it. Use a different parameter block, though. Don't let completion routine A start B while B starts A, or you'll recurse until the stack blows. Sigh, I've seen it happen.

subject: Mac SIMMs vs. PC SIMMs
q: Is it true that nine-chip PC SIMMs work in a Mac as well as eight-chip Mac SIMMs, so I can use spare 1 meg PC SIMMs in my SE/30?
a: Doesn't matter much. PC hardware costs the same or more than Mac stuff. There's no point hunting for parity RAM unless you're upgrading a IIfx, and eight-chip SIMMs will keep their resale value. Quit fussing with it.

subject: Editor in C
q: Is source code available for an editor in C that can handle reasonably large files on the Mac? THINK C's Mini-Edit and Tiny-Edit choke past 10k because of TextEdit.
a: I published the text of an editor kernel in MacTutor, February and March 1990. Honestly you'd probably be better off with a commercial product like Word Solution Engine instead of rolling your own around TextEdit's limits.

subject: MPW 3.2?
q: Is the MPW 3.2 update available other than through ETO?
a: Yes. It ships on E.T.O. #4 in early June, and mid-June as a stand-alone product through APDA on disks or CD, with a special update price for MPW 3.0 or 3.1 owners. It isn't orderable yet, so quit pestering them.

subject: rowBytes for a pixmap
q: Is the rowBytes computation for a pixmap in Knaster's Macintosh Programming Secrets wrong? For an 8-bit 200 pixel wide pixmap it gives 208 rather than 200.
a: With Color QuickDraw you want long-word alignment, not word alignment, since ColorQD goes much faster that way. Use rowBytes := (depth * (Right - Left + 31) div 32) * 4. In C that's (depth * (Right - Left + 31) >> 5) << 2. Don't count the bytes, it's about speed.

subject: how can I reach Applelink?
q: Is there a bridge between the AppleLink MacApp.Tech$ and MacApp.News$ groups and the Usenet newsgroups? What is the group called?
a: MacApp.Tech$ shows up as apple.mac.app on my machine, and CPlus.Dev$ as apple.lang.c++. I don't know about MacApp.News$. The apple prefix may mean limited distribution, but check your own feed.

subject: screen memory address
q: Is there a memory location or system call to find the start address of the memory-mapped video RAM on the Mac, so I can poke the screen directly without hard-coding it for different machines?
a: The global variable ScrnBase holds the start of the main screen buffer. It's in Inside Mac II, page 19. Hard-coding the address was a dumb idea anyway, so go read the book.

subject: Low Level File Editors (Debug)
q: Is there a public domain hex editor for the Mac, like debug on MS-DOS, that can edit all file kinds? Also is there a Peter Norton style utility that can recover deleted files?
a: MacSnoop 1.1.4 edits all files. For recovering deleted files or crashed hard disks, buy Symantec Utilities. Yes, buy it, some of us pay for software.

subject: Any sort of DIFF utility exist?
q: Is there any program for the Mac that lets you diff two files to see the changes between them, like on the PC and UNIX?
a: There's a freeware one called TextDiff, release .9 dated 1986, from a Delphi users group in MA. It should be out there somewhere. Go look instead of asking the net first.

subject: Using THINK C 5.0.1 opt on ANSI lib
q: Is there any reason not to recompile the THINK C 5.0 ANSI library with optimizations on, now that 5.0.1 is out?
a: No reason not to, but there's little to gain. Much of the ANSI library is inline assembly, and the rest doesn't lend itself to optimization. It has nothing to do with the optimizer's reliability. Don't waste your afternoon.

subject: 'mctb' and DA's
q: My DA adds a menu item to the menu bar with an 'mctb' resource for color, but Font/DA Mover renumbers the resource so it no longer points to my menu. Can the DA fix this itself, or is there another solution?
a: Forget the 'mctb' resource, it won't survive the mover's renumbering. Set the menuColorTable manually from the DA with calls like SetMCEntries and SetMCInfo, described in Inside Macintosh volume V, page 239. RTFM.

subject: OpenResFile, 6.07 and 68000s
q: My INIT reopens its own file with a WD and OpenResFile. It works everywhere except the Plus and Classic under System 6.0.7, where it gets an address error in SetHandleSize. What gives?
a: It's a bug in the ROMs and System. Your Tech Notes describe a workaround. Read them before wailing for help.

subject: My games crash under 6.07 - Help?
q: My Mac games, which are heavy on offscreen bitmaps, clip regions and 'snd ' resources, crash under System 6.07. Are there technotes on what changed, and any obvious pitfalls?
a: It's the new Sound Manager biting you. Start one sound before the previous finishes, with sounds in too-rapid succession, and it crashes. Stop the current sound explicitly before starting the next. Sigh, basic hygiene.

subject: LSP 2.0 ("Smallest code ever?")
q: My program compiled with Lightspeed Pascal 2.0 is 7K bigger than with 1.11, despite the ads claiming the tightest code. Has anyone else compared sizes?
a: Compare the right numbers first, genius. The built application includes runtime libraries, and the more Pascal intrinsics you use, the more gets linked in. Overflow and range checking also bloat things. One user's medium-sized program came out 1% smaller than MPW Pascal and about 25% smaller than with 1.11.

subject: jGNEFilter
q: My tail patch of GetNextEvent via jGNEFilter calls the previously installed filter with Jsr (A0), but it crashes on 7.0b4. Is that the right way, and why does it fail?
a: Most bad. jGNEFilter procs expect the event record in A0, and you clobbered A0 with the next procedure's address, passing it to itself as the event. Also, _GetNextEvent calls the filter near the start, so it's no tail patch.

subject: NewHandle & No Memory
q: NewHandle never returns when my heap runs out, even though I check MemError after each call. I set up SetGrowZone to call SysErr(25). Shouldn't NewHandle fail gracefully?
a: You're shooting yourself in the foot. When the memory manager can't allocate, it calls your grow zone routine, and yours bombs the system with SysError(25) before NewHandle can return. Don't set up a grow zone routine like that.

subject: Problem printing to Apple Personal LaserWriter.
q: PrPicFile on the Apple Personal LaserWriter returns -192 resNotFound, though it still prints fine. Should I ignore the error?
a: You shouldn't be calling PrPicFile at all. The Personal LaserWriter does draft printing, not spooled. Check bJDocLoop in the print record, as Inside Mac II shows. Ignoring the error breaks on an ImageWriter. RTFM.

subject: Small Printing Bug between THINK Pascal 3.0 & PrintMonitor
q: Printing All Files in THINK Pascal 3.0 with PrintMonitor lists every file under the name of the top window, though they print fine. Why?
a: Older versions did this too when printing from the Finder. The printer driver picks up the name of the frontmost window, and THINK doesn't change the window as it switches documents. Harmless. Don't blame the beta MF.

subject: SwapMMUMode? or GetPixBaseAddr?
q: SwapMMUMode crashes my Mac IIcx under Think C 4 when I try to use GetPixBaseAddr to alter pixels in an offscreen GWorld. What's wrong?
a: There's a tech note on this. The PC looks like XXYYYYYY, and those XXs send the machine off into lala land when you swap MMU modes. You need inline assembly to make it 00YYYYYY first. Read the tech notes, people.

subject: LSC 3.0 Debugging problem
q: The LSC 3.0 debugger says illegal instruction when I step through a simple statement like if (var) ptr->member = var; and then hangs the machine. Is it a debugger bug?
a: Probably not the debugger. Likely ptr has a bad value and the assignment is smashing useful memory. Look at the Data window. Check your pointers before blaming the tools.

subject: Horizontal scrolling in List Manager
q: The List Manager scrolls horizontally a whole cell width, showing blank space for a single column. Is replacing the scroll action procedure the preferred way to scroll by pixels, or is there another way?
a: Yes, that's what it does. Set the list up with no horizontal scrollbar, supply your own, and have its action scroll the list while a custom LDEF compensates for the offset. Or use THINK C's CCellGrid or CScrollPane. The List Manager is for simple lists, and Apple never claimed otherwise.

subject: MPW 3.0 Installation
q: The MPW 3.0 installer bombs out saying it can't find a script file that is definitely there. What's going on?
a: Two known causes. Your hard disk name has an illegal character, like a quote or apostrophe, which is noted on page 44 of the manual. Or you're running TOPS, so reboot holding the keys that keep TOPS from installing. Also don't install over an old MPW folder; do a fresh install.

subject: LSC >> 3.0 <<
q: There's an ad for LSC 3.0 on the back cover of MacTutor, mentioning a symbolic debugger. Is it really out yet?
a: No. The ad was premature, and Think apologized when called. So you get to sit and wait patiently like the rest of us have been doing for ages. Typical vendor vapor, advertising before shipping.

subject: Opening same file from two applications
q: Two Mac applications opening the same file for reading give me zero bytes read and no error. Shouldn't opening one file from two applications work under MultiFinder and System 7?
a: It works only if both open the file with readonly or shared read/write permissions. Plenty of applications use exclusive read/write and weren't written for sharing. It takes more than changing permissions to make an app sharing compatible. Sloppy programmers, as usual.

subject: sprintf problems under LSC 2.15
q: Under LSC 2.15, strcpy works in my HyperCard XFCN but sprintf crashes it. Is the printf library incompatible with HyperCard, or am I missing libraries?
a: The printf family works by setting global variables and calling core formatting functions. Under LSC 2.15 you can't have globals in code resources, so sprintf blows up. Any idiot who read the manual would know that.

subject: Reading a resource from an already open file
q: Under MultiFinder the Desktop file is always open, so OpenResFile gives error -49. Must I write code to read the resource fork by hand to get a resource out of it?
a: No, open it read-only with OpenRFPerm from Inside Mac volume 4. It's not on 64K ROM machines, though. Finder still has it open read-write, so your resource map can go stale if Finder changes the file. Open it only when you need it, and RTFM.

subject: Forced Switching under MF
q: Under MultiFinder, how can my program force a switch to another running application, like HyperCard, at a given point?
a: Call OpenDeskAcc() with the application's name. It switches to any other opened application. Think about why that works for a minute, it's obvious. Not exactly in the Interface Guidelines, but neat.
