subject: DA questions, the second time around...
q: Under MultiFinder, my desk accessories loaded into the application heap never get their goodbye kiss when the application quits. How do I get them to close themselves?
a: Install a head patch on ExitToShell that fires when the app quits and removes your patches or closes things down. Apps returning from main still get an ExitToShell from the OS. Sigh, it may not undo everything if something re-patched the trap, so use small islands in the system heap.

subject: Weird Update with System 7
q: Under System 7, calling SetCTitle on my button causes an unexplained update event that redraws the control. Did the Control Manager change, or do I have a hidden bug?
a: Can't say what causes it, but the workaround is to save the current port, set it to the window, call ValidRect on the window's portRect, and set the port back. That keeps the window from getting updated. Ugly, but it works.

subject: Exactly What Does one need to begin MAC programming?...
q: What do I need to begin Mac programming? Do I have to buy all the volumes of Inside Macintosh, or which are mandatory?
a: Start with volumes 1 and 2, the basics of the Toolbox: windows, drawing, menus. Volume 4 covers the new file management. Skip the rest and you'll wish you hadn't the minute you do real work. Nobody memorizes it, so buy the books.

subject: TextEdit as a paragraph engine
q: What does it mean to use TextEdit as a paragraph engine? Is that one small TE record per editor window with text copied in and out?
a: TextEdit stores values as signed 16-bit integers, so it's limited to 32K bytes and about 2000 lines. You can give each paragraph its own TE record, but you position and scroll them yourself and selections can't cross paragraphs. Or feed one record chunks as lines scroll. It's a lot of work.

subject: LSC 3.0.?
q: What is the most recent release of Lightspeed C 3.0, and is 3.0p4 the same thing?
a: 3.01p4 is the latest patch, and if no more bugs turn up it will probably be remastered as 3.02 soon. The patches are minor upgrades, but worth having. Honestly, just install them.

subject: Toolbox Patching
q: What is the right way to patch a Toolbox trap on the Mac so my code runs first and then the original routine finishes and returns to the caller, instead of resetting trap addresses all over?
a: Do a head patch. Point the trap at your patch with SetTrapAddress, do your work, then JMP to the original trap so it returns directly to the original caller. No re-patching on every call. Learn the difference between head and tail patches first.

subject: four leaf clover character
q: What keys do I press to get the command (four leaf clover) character on the Macintosh? I see it in menus but can't find it in KeyCaps.
a: Press CONTROL-Q in the Chicago font. Select Chicago in Key Caps and hold down CONTROL to see the hidden characters, like the check mark, diamond and apple logo. Not exactly hard to find if you'd looked.

subject: multiwindow editor on AU/X
q: What's a good multiwindow, mousing, grepping text editor for program development on a Mac IIci running A/UX 1.1.1? I hate ed and vi, and don't want to install all of X11 and ATK just for ez.
a: Throw out A/UX 1.1.1 and get 2.0. It has an MPW Shell-like multiple window editor, plus MultiFinder, so you can run whatever Mac editor you like. Honestly, upgrading is the obvious answer, and you could have figured that out yourself.

subject: Macintosh handles
q: What's the best way to allocate a chain of Mac handles without fragmenting memory, given the master pointer problem with MoreMasters?
a: Determine your master pointer needs empirically, per Tech Note 53. Exercise the program, break into MacsBug and count the nonrelocatable blocks of size $108, $10c or $110, then call MoreMasters in CODE 1 for that many plus 20 percent. Scale it to available memory.

subject: Question - Use VBL or Def. Task?
q: What's the best way to write incoming data to a file on the Mac without losing any, using THINK C? A VBL task I tried that called SysBeep stopped beeping shortly into the application.
a: Your card probably doesn't interrupt, so poll with a VBL task and use two buffers, writing one out while the other fills. Have the VBL set up a deferred task for the actual write. SysBeep at interrupt time is a no-no since it loads a resource and allocates heap memory.

subject: best way to detect command-. interrupt?
q: What's the officially approved way to detect a command-period interrupt on the Mac so a user can stop a long operation, without slowing the inner loop too much?
a: The proper way is to run your event handler so other apps and windows keep working. Otherwise people poll GetKeys() for command and period, but you must call it very often or you'll miss the keypress, and it slows your loop. Frankly there's no good way.

subject: RAM DRVRs, resLocked, dNeedLock
q: What's the relationship between RAM DRVRs, resLocked and dNeedLock? When does a Mac driver need which bit set?
a: RAM and ROM drivers differ in one thing: RAM ones supply a handle in dCtlDriver, ROM ones a pointer. Set dNeedLock if you're ROM based. Unset it if RAM based so the Device Manager locks you. Ignore resLocked. Read page II-188 carefully, it's not intuitive.

subject: DisposHandle
q: When calling DisposHandle on a Mac, does it matter whether the handle is locked or purgeable?
a: Nope, doesn't matter. But don't call DisposHandle on a handle with its resource bit set, since that wreaks havoc with the Resource Manager. Call ReleaseResource instead. Basic stuff, really.

subject: AFP/ASP/.XPP???
q: Where can I find documentation on AppleTalk ASP and AFP so I can use .XPP to start a connection to an AppleShare server? Inside Mac only says look elsewhere.
a: Get the AppleTalk Filing Protocol Engineering Technical Notes from APDA. XPP itself is documented in AppleTalk Manager Update, also from APDA. The part numbers are KNBAFP and KMSAMU. Inside Mac was never going to cover it.

subject: LSC and MPW C ansi?
q: Which versions of LSC and MPW C are ANSI compliant?
a: MPW 3.0 and up. None of the Lightspeed C versions are, and the differences will drive you crazy. For example, sizeof doesn't return size_t. Sigh.

subject: Why can't I build MacApp examples?
q: Why does MPW hang at the link step when I try to build MacApp sample programs like Nothing with MABuild? I'm on an SE/30 with MPW 3.2 and MacApp 2.0.
a: Sounds like the old MPW and Vaccine INIT conflict. Remove Vaccine from your System folder and you should be able to link. Stomping on the floppy is optional but recommended. Those anti-virus INITs cause more trouble than viruses.

subject: DA loses resource file on accRun
q: Why does my desk accessory get ResError -193, resource file not found, on UseResFile when it receives accRun events in the background?
a: You guessed right. The file was opened when the DA Handler was running, but at accRun time another app may be running with a different resource chain, so the Resource Manager never finds your map. Get your resources at startup, when you know your opener is running.

subject: Why doesn't TEUpdate do an update?
q: Why doesn't TEUpdate do an update, and why do TECalText and TEUpdate reset the teLength field I set?
a: NO! Never set teLength yourself. TE guarantees teLength equals GetHandleSize of hText, so you should NEVER change it. And TEUpdate always works fine, even for printing. Fix your own code first.

subject: Will our tools break with 32-bit mode? was Re: SwapMMUMode in graphics
q: Will our debugging and programming tools like MPW, TMON and MacsBug break under System 7.0's 32-bit mode? Will they be made 32-bit clean?
a: Apple writes the ROMs and System Software using MPW, so a 32-bit clean version is a foregone conclusion. TMON 2.8.4 was made for the IIci and later, and TMON Professional is imminent. Your MacsBug is probably just out of date. Check your versions before whining.

subject: TEXT and styl Resources
q: With Think C 5.0 and TCL 1.1, I load a TEXT resource into an EditText with SetTextHandle, but the styling stored in the styl resource doesn't show. How do I get it?
a: A styl resource handle is what Inside Mac calls a StylScrapHandle. Use TEStylInsert, if memory serves, to insert text and style together. SetTextHandle only gives you raw text. Read Inside Mac.

subject: Anyone seen a talking moose?
q: Does anyone know where I can get the Talking Moose desk accessory that makes rude comments on the screen?
a: It's still around, version 3.0, sold by Baseline Publishing in Memphis for about $40 or $45, and it includes MacinTalk. Don't send money to the original author. There's also Zippy the Talking Pinhead on simtel20, loosely based on it.

subject: Info on new Mac
q: I hear Apple is coming out with a new Mac with an 030 priced near the Classic. What's the release date and price?
a: It's the Classic II, the 030 based Classic. Per MacLEAK the roll-out is Oct 21, at $1,899 for the 2/40 and $2,399 for the 4/80. Rumour sheets again, so don't bet your lunch on it.

subject: wanted: info about macro program "Frontier"
q: Is the Mac macro program Frontier by UserLand out yet, how much does it cost, and has anyone tried it?
a: It's supposed to be released within the month. It's not a macro language but a scripting language, using IAC and AppleEvents. Price unknown. Read the review properly before calling it a macro program.

subject: Unix diff
q: Is there a Mac utility that does what Unix diff does, taking two files and showing only the differences?
a: Compare 0.9 works well, and you can grab it from sumex in info-mac/util as compare-09.hqx. There's also compareall, but it only says how much differs, maybe not what. Go fetch it yourself.

subject: If Monks Had Macs...
q: Where can I find a copy of the HyperCard stack "If Monks Had Macs..."?
a: You can get it from BMUG. I think it's also in the index at the University of Michigan ftp site. Log in anonymously and GET PC2:!INDEX to see the listing. Try looking before posting next time.

subject: ethernet bridge on masscomp
q: Can I use a Masscomp 5500 as an ethernet bridge or gateway between two ethernets? Is Dual Net what I need, and can the Lance chip on the motherboard serve as the second interface?
a: DualNet is NOT what you want; it's redundant ethernet for fail-safe use. Running two interfaces is no problem, and the Lance chip plus the Excelan board should work, with the Excelan board using in-kernel protocols. Expect it to chew CPU, and it's not officially supported.

subject: RS-2030's and 4Mb SIMMS
q: Can an RS-2030 be upgraded with 4Mb SIMMs for more memory than 16 Mb?
a: No. The 2030 board only takes 1M-by-9 SIP modules, fitted in multiples of 4 Mbytes, up to a maximum of 16 Mbytes. Sorry to spoil the dream, but that's the hardware.

subject: duplicate cron jobs, who is responsible?
q: Cron on our MIPS machines runs some jobs twice, within a second of each other. What's causing it?
a: That was a known problem report, a race condition in cron. It's fixed in RISC/os 4.50. Sigh, upgrade, it wasn't your crontabs and it wasn't timed.

subject: Does MIPS have an ISV program?
q: Does MIPS have an Independent Software Vendors program with hardware and software discounts for RS2030 machines?
a: Yes, there is one, but for the current discounts, call your local MIPS sales rep. In the Bay Area, call (408) 720-2900 and ask for a sales rep. Did you really need the net to tell you to call sales?

subject: Using alloca
q: Does alloca work on MIPS, and are there any potential problems with using it?
a: The 2.10 compilers include alloca. Include <alloca.h> and you get a machine-dependent builtin alloca; leave it out and you get a portable emulation. Reading the man page's warning would have cost you nothing, but there it is.

subject: Files mysteriously disappearing
q: Files are mysteriously disappearing on our MIPS machine. The name shows in ls but the file can't be accessed. Any ideas?
a: Seen it on an M/2000. Mips told us to upgrade to RISC/os 4.01, and nobody has complained about vanishing files since. NFS mounts can vanish too, and the cure there is unmounting and remounting. Annoying, but that's vendor software for you.

subject: Register access from a C program
q: How do I access CPU registers from a C program on a DECstation 3100 under Ultrix 3.2? man -k register failed. Do I need an assembly routine?
a: What are you really trying to do? The compiler is using all the general-purpose registers, so you have no business touching them. If you must, GCC lets you bind a variable to a named register with asm. Specify your problem next time.

subject: 4.52 is it reliable?
q: Is MIPS 4.52 reliable? We're still seeing mbuf exhaustion and panics on our M120s and 3240 after installing the 4.52 kernel.
a: 4.52 is fine here except for one thing: rpc.lockd has a huge memory leak. It eats all physical memory and plock()s it so it can't page out. Check rpc.lockd's memory use. MIPS has been told and is supposedly working on it.

subject: How to add dbx names for .o files?
q: Is there a way to get GCC to put dbx debug symbols into .o files on a MIPS machine, through assembly, or must I build a names-only .o and merge it with ld -r?
a: No, the assembler only lets you set the filename and line number. I put the debug info in as assembly comments, then a program reads the object and source and writes a new object with the debug data. A cover program runs both. Ugly, but that's what you get.

subject: ld problem
q: On an RC3240 running RISC/os 4.30, linking a program that uses gethostbyname() and a local library gives "jump relocation out-of-range, bad object file produced" for select. Is this a known bug?
a: Not a system bug, your bug. Something in your code defines a data item called select, so libc's jump to select() lands in .data and is out of range. Find the external data item named select and rename it.

subject: .livereg pseudo-opcode
q: What is the .livereg pseudo-opcode in R3000 assembly code? It isn't in the Kane book.
a: It tells the assembler which integer and FP registers are live at a jump, call or return, so its global dataflow optimizations and the reorganizer don't do unsafe things. It's emitted by the compiler; assembly programmers needn't write it. Read the MIPS assembler programmer's guide.

subject: slattach "load", e.t.a. for 4.50B
q: When is the 4.50B release due for the RC3230, and does it fix the modem controls on the tty ports and the ISA serial adapter that never shipped?
a: 4.50B is already shipping, as far as I know. It fixes the tty modem controls and gets the AT bus serial card working. The adapter was switched to edge-triggered interrupts late in development and the driver changes missed 4.50. Sigh, keep up with your vendor.

subject: Can some one explain this compiler output?
q: Why does the MIPS cc allocate 24 bytes of stack for a non-leaf procedure with no locals that calls a function taking no arguments?
a: A non-leaf always gets 4 words of argument build area, because the first four parameters pass in registers 4 through 7 and the callee might be a vararg function that homes them there. Add a word for the return address in r31, and the stack pointer stays double word aligned, so 6 words. Basic calling convention stuff.

subject: virtual memory
q: Why doesn't virtual memory grow across the network? Could a job that runs out of swap grab disk on another node temporarily?
a: Sun already does it: swap to a file that doesn't have to be local, and you can add swap any time. Anything fancier means checkpointing, which mainframe people have had for 25 years. Unix hasn't invented it yet, apparently.

subject: Mips assembler question
q: Why won't the MIPS assembler accept .word b-c for the difference of two labels, and is there a way to do it?
a: The MIPS COFF format has no relocation for b-c, and the assembler handles .word long before instruction scheduling, so it doesn't know how many nops get inserted. The .struct directive may help for data offsets. Otherwise, sorry. One person had GCC compute the offset.

subject: indent core dumps on 4.51
q: indent dumps core under RISC/os 4.51. Is this a known problem, or just local to our site?
a: Wasn't known, but it's been found and fixed. The fix arrives in release 4.52. Until then grab the fixed indent by anonymous ftp from mips.com, as tmp/indent. Try the ftp site before posting next time.

subject: Protecting computer equipment
q: How can I protect computer equipment from lightning through the power and phone lines? Is line conditioning enough, or do I need a UPS, and can a UPS signal the computer to shut down?
a: A UPS is better and costs more, but nothing is certain if lightning hits close. Some UPSs have a relay that closes when the battery runs low, but you must wire it to a port and write the monitoring yourself. It usually isn't pretty. The phone company's protector should be enough for the modem.

subject: Copyrighting Software
q: How do you copyright software, and is each revision a separate copyright?
a: Slap a notice on it: "Copyright 1989 Yourname" and you're covered. Registering with Form TX costs $10 and gets you treble damages. Copyright each revision to be safe. And "(c)" alone is invalid, use the word. Read up, newbie.

subject: Altos 586 and V20
q: I put a 10MHz NEC V20 in my Altos 586, which has an 8086, and it won't boot. Why? Too fast, bad chip, or do I need other parts?
a: Wrong chip. The V20 replaces the 8088 and has an 8-bit bus with a different pinout. The V30 is the 8086 replacement with the 16-bit bus. Drop in a V30 and it should work. Somebody screwed up telling you V20, but you should've checked.

subject: VT100 emulators
q: I want to use a cheap computer like a C64, C128 or Apple IIx to reach the UNIX machines at school. What VT100 emulation is available for them, and will it give a true 80x24 screen?
a: On a C64, grab one of the VT100 emulators talked about in comp.sys.cbm, Kermit being one. Or get VIP Terminal and write a termcap or terminfo entry. Either gives 80x24. Kermit also gives you the Kermit protocol, if you even need it.

subject: Intergraph Interpro 120 : TCP/IP under UNIX SYS V, need help
q: On an Intergraph Interpro 120 running UNIX System V, I keep getting 'DOD_INC DOD TCP/IP not initialized' when trying to bring up TCP/IP. How do I get it going, and what is the clearinghouse?
a: The executable that activates the protocols is /etc/dodini. Run it with the -a switch and it'll tell you why initialization fails. The clearinghouse handles the XNS protocols and updates Intergraph host files. With one Intergraph box, edit /etc/host to add the non-Intergraph nodes yourself.

subject: System 3000 backup (no devices)
q: After upgrading our NCR System 3000 to NCR's SVR4 2.0 release 1.01, a full backup through sysadm only saved directories, files and pipes, not devices. Is that expected?
a: Yes, that's how it behaves. For a real full system backup you have to use cpio or modify the backup script yourself. Typical vendor shipping, sigh.

subject: NCR Multi-processor unix
q: NCR says applications developed on SVR4 will run unchanged on its multiprocessor SVR4 MP if they use standard system calls. Does that mean there's no common ABI between SVR4 and SVR4 MP, so programs must be recompiled?
a: No. Neither the APIs nor the ABI will change. The warning was just a reminder to use standard calls, so customers can start developing on today's uniprocessor SVR4 systems. The MP version is built on the shipping uniprocessor one. Read the sidebar less nervously.

subject: cpio error restoring to /stand
q: On an NCR System 3000 running SVR4, extracting a cpio archive into /stand fails with 'Cannot create temporary file, errno 89, Operation not applicable', though cp and mv work fine. What's going on?
a: Use truss to trace the system calls of the cpio process. You'll see which call fails and why. SVR4 ships it for a reason, so use it instead of asking the net.

subject: news software and uux -z option
q: The news 2.11 docs patch uux with a -z option to suppress success messages, but my Tower manual says -z enables a success message. Are the two options opposite?
a: You're not imagining it. HDB defaults to the old behavior, and its -z flag now means the opposite of the news hack. Read the man pages first, or enjoy the flood of mail.

subject: SLIP On Towers
q: We have several NCR Tower 500s running win/tcp that allow SLIP connections, but NCR won't give us manuals. What is the cable spec for the connection, and where do I find SLIP documentation?
a: Order NCR publication number D1-1081-B07. It has the SLIP specifications and the recommended modem settings. Next time ask your NCR rep for the right pub number instead of complaining.

subject: streams primer
q: What are the document numbers for the NCR STREAMS Programmers Guide and STREAMS Primer, so I can order them?
a: STREAMS Programming Guide is D1-1559-A and the Primer is ST-2111-52. They're the same as the AT&T manuals with those titles, and any decent Unix bookstore stocks them. Check the manual before asking.

subject: Next doesn't recognize uncompressed?
q: After I uncompress kermit.Z, my NeXT treats it as a text document and not an application. What am I doing wrong?
a: Set the executable flags. Run chmod +x on the file from a shell, which is required after uncompressing a binary on any UNIX machine. Basic stuff, kid.

subject: buy cube or station and third party harddiscs?
q: Can I put a third party hard disk, like a Quantum, Fujitsu or Seagate, inside a NeXT machine in place of the stock drive?
a: Yes, it works. Plenty of NeXTstations ship with Seagate ST1480 or Quantum drives; just query the disk with /etc/disk -q and look. Not exactly a secret, though I suppose NeXT might tell you if you ask the right person.

subject: USING OD's to backup other boxes
q: Can I use a NeXT with its optical disk to back up other machines, like our A/UX box, without reinventing the wheel?
a: Check whether A/UX has remote dump and restore. Berkeley released rmt, which the NeXT already has, but not the dump facility itself. With remote dump you can back up a filesystem across the network. Go read up.

subject: Diagram! and word processing
q: Can drawings made with Diagram! on the NeXT be incorporated into documents produced with WriteNow, TeX and Frame?
a: Yes. Diagram! generates Encapsulated PostScript files that you can place or include in WriteNow, Frame or TeX documents. In WriteNow you can even copy and paste graphics straight in. Basic EPS, folks.

subject: Browser auto-update
q: Can the NeXT Browser be configured to update automatically whenever something changes in its directories? Manually updating is a pain.
a: Not as far as the replies go. Just type cmd-u, what's so hard about that? The browser already notices when it's out of step with the filesystem. An option to update itself is something to hope for in the future.

subject: Mixing 4MB and 1MB SIMMS
q: Can you mix 4MB and 1MB SIMMs in a NeXT? We have 8 1MB SIMMs and want to add some 4MB ones without pulling the old ones.
a: Yes, but not within a bank. The SIMMs sit in 4 banks of 4, 16 total, and each bank must be all one size. Each SIMM is 8 bits wide, so you need four to fill the 68030's 32-bit path. Think about it.

subject: Renderman
q: Does anyone know a credible reference for what exactly the Renderman model is like?
a: Get the book "The Renderman Companion" by Steve Upstill, published by Addison-Wesley. Not hard to find, people. Read it before asking the net.

subject: NeXT printer: weight of paper query
q: Does the NeXT laser printer have an upper limit on paper weight, and can it print on transparencies?
a: Yes to transparencies, but only film specifically designed for laser printers. Any decent office supply store or university bookstore carries it. And don't feed it random junk like aluminum foil. Obvious, isn't it?

subject: Ensemble hanging
q: Ensemble, the NeXT 2.0 MIDI/DSP demo app, hangs regularly during multi-voice MIDI I/O or DSP synthesis on my cube with a 68040 upgrade board. Is it a known problem?
a: It's a timing bug in 2.0 that only hits 68040 systems. NeXT has already fixed it, and the fix should arrive in an update, maybe 2.1, very soon. Your DSP is fine, so stop poking at it.

subject: Slow when on a network?
q: Even under 1.0, BreakApp is slow and jerky on my NeXT, which sits on a network with many Suns and has a few dozen NFS filesystems mounted. Why is the machine so plodding?
a: Probably some system daemon going wild, perhaps over something on your network. I have 36 NFS mounts and BreakApp runs fine. Run ps in a Terminal to find what's eating cycles, and check whether someone's logged into your box over the net.

subject: compiling BaSH-1.05 on NeXT (2.0)
q: Has anyone compiled bash 1.05 on a NeXT running 2.0? I couldn't get past the first two files with the generic BSD makefile.
a: Don't bother; bash 1.07 is due within a couple of weeks. Hopefully it will be just a matter of typing make on the NeXT. Patience, kid.

subject: ML
q: Has anyone found or made an ML interpreter or compiler that builds on the NeXT? SML/NJ doesn't compile for me and looks like it would need major reconstruction.
a: Sigh. It's a 68040 cache problem, probably self-modifying code. Somebody put a prebuilt SML/NJ 0.69 executable on ftp.cs.cornell.edu that runs on '030 and '040 under 2.0. You can't build it from the distribution, since the NeXT patches didn't make it in. Set binary mode, for pity's sake.

subject: rrn on NeXT
q: Has anyone gotten rrn, the remote rn that reads news over NNTP, to run on a NeXT? I can read news fine, but when I try to post I sometimes get "%interp buffer overflow" and rrn exits.
a: Build rrn with the compiler option -fwritable-strings. That got rid of our interp buffer overflow. If it doesn't, try -traditional instead. Sigh, old K&R code scribbling on string constants again.

subject: BSD Games
q: Has anyone ported the BSD4.3 games like wump and rogue to the NeXT? NeXT claims a complete BSD UNIX.
a: Someone installed Nethack on a NeXT cube with no trouble compiling and installing. That's the sort of CPU wasting you wanted. Go build the others yourself instead of waiting for a handout.

subject: HELP reading NeXT files from UNIX and X11
q: How can I view the on-line Shakespeare on the NeXTs from my NCD X terminal with the fonts and formatting, instead of seeing all the formatting instructions?
a: Believe it or not, yes. If you have ATK, grab the RTF to ATK translator from the info-andrew list. Run it and view the result with EZ, the ATK editor, under X. Works on NextStep docs. Sigh, nobody uses ATK, which is a shame.

subject: How to obtain object id's loaded with loadNibFile
q: How can a NeXT application find out which objects were loaded by loadNibFile, so it can set text fields and sliders at run time?
a: Easy. The id loadNibFile returns is the new panel. Get its view hierarchy with contentView, then use findViewWithTag to find the controls. You need unique tags assigned in Interface Builder, which is trivial for sliders and buttons.

subject: PS to EPS: HELP!
q: How do I convert PostScript to EPS on the NeXT so I can import diagrams into WriteNow? Scene only does TIFF to EPS and back.
a: PS to EPS isn't always possible. Try Glenn Reid's distillery plus something that computes bounding boxes, maybe. EPS to PS is a null conversion since EPS is a subset of PS. TIFF is resolution-dependent, so it'll look awful on a laser printer. Ask in comp.lang.postscript.

subject: Multiple EPS images in a single file
q: How do I create an EPS file containing more than one EPS image, for use with NXEPSImageRep's newListFromFile:?
a: You can't. For today's EPS files that method just returns a List with one element. It only exists to parallel NXBitmapImageRep, since TIFF can hold multiple images. Doesn't make sense for PostScript. Sigh.

subject: How to get uucp received file stats?
q: How do I get uucp to log statistics for received files in SYSLOG? It only shows transmitted files on NeXT.
a: You can't. It's a known bug, and NeXT said it would be fixed in NeXTstep 2.0. Whether they actually did it, who knows. Vendors and their promises, sigh.

subject: Printing long (legal) pages
q: How do I print legal-size pages with manual feed on a NeXT so the bottom isn't cut off, when the page comes from emacs as PostScript or text rather than from an app with PageLayout?
a: Put the legal paper size in your PostScript header, with a DocumentPaperSizes: Legal comment. Easiest is to Print/Save a legal-size WriteNow document to a file and copy its header. Not every PostScript printer supports legal, and the NeXT laser printer may not. Read the manual.

subject: hostname change. stupid question?
q: How do I properly change the hostname of my NeXT from localhost? I tried rc.boot and NetInfo, and NetInfo crashed.
a: Use the /NextAdmin/NetManager application. It edits /etc/hostconfig through a whiz-bang interface. Or just edit that file directly, as any sane person would, instead of poking NetInfo until it breaks.

subject: UUCP
q: How do I set up and maintain UUCP on my NeXT? I've never used it and the documentation seems lacking on installation.
a: RTFM. The Network and System Administration manual covers it quite thoroughly, with sample chat scripts and modem configurations. Every new NeXT ships with it in hardcopy. Other UUCP books exist too, probably as clear as NeXT's.

subject: Floptical ejection snafu
q: How do you eject the optical disk on a NeXT when it crashes on eject, and is the machine usable with one optical drive and no hard disk?
a: There's a small oval hole at the upper right of the optical drive; poke the NeXT screwdriver in to pop the disk out. One optical drive is usable but feels slower than a Mac Plus with a SCSI hard disk. Standard software fills the disk, so throw stuff away. Read the manual.

subject: dumb terminal dumb
q: I can't get a dumb terminal working on my NeXT. A good null-modem cable sends data from the NeXT to my adm3a, but nothing comes back the other way. Is it a hardware problem?
a: The NeXT port is RS422, not RS232. It swings between about +5 and ground, while your terminal wants +5 and -5. Some RS232 receivers tolerate that and others don't, so try another terminal. Sigh, check your signal levels first.

subject: hex tool
q: I got my NeXT cube through the fire sale and it came without a hex wrench, and I need one to get the back panel off to install RAM. Two sets of standard hex wrenches didn't fit. Where can I get the right one?
a: RTFM. Appendix C of the User's Reference says to buy one from an Authorized NeXT Service Center, or use a three-millimeter ball-tipped hex wrench from a hardware store. Standard sets won't do, as you found out.

subject: NeXT Motorola 88K Machine?
q: I heard NeXT will be releasing a Motorola 88K-based box later this year. Has anyone heard similar rumors, and what else can you tell us?
a: It's hardly a secret. The latest InfoWorld cover story says the new NeXT will have Moto's 96002 plus the new superscalar 88K, and it should be out about this time next year. Read the magazines before asking the net, newbie.

subject: Floppy Drives for NeXT ???
q: I need to transfer largish files (300K+) from a home Mac to an office NeXT, and the phone is too expensive. Is there a floppy drive that does the job?
a: We had good luck with Dayna's DaynaFile system, unless the NeXT has an accelerator disk. At least that's my impression. Dayna is investigating the problem. Buy the hardware, quit paying for phone calls.

subject: RFS on NeXT ?
q: I ran strings on the NeXT kernel and found a number of RFS symbols. Does that mean the kernel has hidden RFS support, or is it junk left over from CMU?
a: Probably neither. That's just NFS support, full of subroutines and error messages prefixed rfs, meaning remote file system, not AT&T RFS. Run nm and grep on a Sun without RFS and you'll see the same symbols. Think before you panic.

subject: How to make Floppy bootable?
q: I want to make a floppy bootable on my NeXT while my hard drive is parted. What can I do with it? Is there a Unix shell or the Workspace Manager?
a: Don't expect much. A bootable floppy is there to rebuild the hard disk, so it has minimal functionality, probably just the utilities to copy files and not much more. No Workspace Manager, so quit dreaming.

subject: Copy extended 2.0 to external drive
q: I'm getting an external drive for my NeXTstation and want NeXTstep 2.0 on it so I can boot from either drive. Can I have my school's NeXT support center build it on their machine, and how do I switch the boot drive?
a: You're legally entitled to copy it, and I can't see why the support center would refuse. Switching is easy: the internal drive is SCSI ID 1, so set the external to 0 to boot from it, or to 2 or higher to boot internal. Keep the internal bootable, genius.

subject: Alternate as META key?
q: I'm writing a terminal emulator for emacs on the NeXT that treats the Alternate key as meta. When a keyDown has NX_ALTERNATEMASK, how can I get the charCode it would have had without the mask, in a hardware-independent way?
a: Open /dev/evs0 and read the keyboard mapping with the EVSIOCKM ioctl. Then look up the charCode for the keyCode yourself. It's not perfect if the display server runs on a machine with a different keyboard, but it beats hardcoding tables from the manual.

subject: SIMMS: parity or non?
q: If I mix parity and non-parity SIMMs in my NeXTstation, will I lose autoboot? Is parity worth bothering with at all?
a: No, mixing doesn't lose autoboot. Two people have done it with no problems at all. Parity costs about a dollar more per SIMM, so buy whatever is cost effective, or skip it and wait for ECC, which your machine probably won't support anyway.

subject: next the next NeXT
q: If the 68040 is the last 680x0 chip, what will come after the next NeXT? Will NeXT survive?
a: Don't panic. There have been rumors for over a year of a 68050 supporting fine-grained parallel processing, possibly via the Tomosulo Algorithm. And 68040 samples were due by the end of the quarter. Quit worrying about the chip rumor mill.

subject: MATLAB for the NEXT
q: Is MathWorks planning a version of MATLAB for the NeXT? If not, why not?
a: Nope. MathWorks says they won't bother until they see a significant NeXT market. Meanwhile, run MATLAB on another CPU and use X for the graphics, which is distasteful. If you want it, call or write them and clamor.

subject: GNU C compiler
q: Is the GNU C compiler for the NeXT available via anonymous FTP, or can someone supply the executable and libraries? I'm learning C on an 8/105 NeXTStation.
a: GNU CC is on prep.ai.mit.edu in pub/gnu, and also via anonymous UUCP from osu-cis or from uunet. But those are source distributions only. Doesn't your NeXT already have a /bin/cc? Check before begging for binaries.

subject: Mac software on a NeXT???
q: Is there ANY way to run Macintosh software on a NeXT? I have a ton of Mac software and don't want to give it up.
a: No. There's currently no way to run Mac software on a NeXT, and I wouldn't hold my breath waiting. Sigh. Keep your Mac and run the old apps there, and buy the NeXT for new apps. Not rocket science.

subject: SMALLTALK for the NeXT?
q: Is there a GNU Smalltalk, and where do I ftp it so I can use it on my NeXT?
a: It's with all the other GNU stuff in all the usual places. Get prep.ai.mit.edu:pub/gnu/smalltalk-1.1.tar.Z. You'll also want to subscribe to gnu.smalltalk.bug. Try looking before asking.

subject: need a better Date
q: Is there a better calendar application for the NeXT than the Date program in /NextDeveloper/Demos? It has serious bugs that make it unusable.
a: Try Cassandra on Purdue, a $20 shareware date program with a notebook and calculator. A commercial alternative is Calendoscope, about $95, which is more powerful but garish. Yes, the name is silly.

subject: resizing windows
q: Is there a way to resize windows on the NeXT?
a: Yes. Look for the two-tone square box in a corner of the title bar. Click it, then grab an edge or corner and drag it. Might be a limit on which edge. Try looking before asking, will you?

subject: How to check SIMM(RAM) by Electrical Intsrument ?
q: Is there any way to check whether the rest of my NeXT's SIMMs are OK using an electrical instrument?
a: You won't like this: you pretty much can't. RAM is too complicated to judge without testing in-circuit under dynamic conditions. You need a program running as root that reads every byte, or better, one that writes test patterns, which nukes UNIX. The authorized-service diagnostic kernel does that.

subject: Station to Monitor Cable.
q: Is there anything special about the NeXTstation-to-monitor cable? Could I make my own from DB-19 connectors and six feet of regular cable instead of paying $80?
a: The pin-out is in the User's Reference, around page 382. It looks like a 9 pair cable, so match every signal with its own ground. Nobody's cut one open, so don't blame me if it fizzles. Read the manual first.

subject: Kermit 5A(165) ALPHA fails to transfer .Z file
q: Kermit 5A(165) alpha fails to transfer a .Z binary file between my NeXT and remote hosts, complaining about too many NAKs. Kermit 4E on the remote works. Is this a bug?
a: Sort of. Workaround: use 'set parity space' to force 7-bit transfers, which handles binary files. It's slower than real 8-bit, though. I've hit it myself and am looking into why 8-bit transfers fail. RTFM on parity next time.

subject: Another KErmit problem!!
q: Kermit on my NeXT downloads files but uudecode sometimes fails and uncompress or tar reports checksum errors. Doesn't Kermit checksum every packet and resend?
a: Something is corrupting the data and there are many suspects, even with clean MNP-5 modems. One person got better results by uncompressing before the kermit transfer. Nobody knows where the fault is, so don't expect magic.

subject: CC Bug discovered ?
q: My #if defined(OSK) || defined(BSD) didn't work with NeXT's cc, but defined(NeXT) did. Is this a cc/cpp bug or a documentation error?
a: Very unlikely a bug. It just means BSD isn't defined by the system compiler. Run cc -v and look for -DBSD on the cpp line. Only if it's there is it a preprocessor bug; otherwise the docs are wrong. Less than a second's thought.

subject: Mathematica/C query
q: My C program for Mathematica needs the file mdefs.h, but I can't find it on my NeXT. Does it need a source license, and where do I get it?
a: It's already on your machine, at /NextApps/Mathematica.app/Kernel/Utilities/mdefs.h. Look before you post. No source license needed.

subject: HELP! CAN'T GET MY '040 TO WORK!
q: My NeXT '040 upgrade hangs at a 'Loading from Network' window after the 2.0 upgrade and boot block fix. Any suggestions?
a: Use the p command in the ROM monitor to set verbose test mode to yes. The default is for people with IQs slightly above room temperature. You need the real UNIX console window visible to see what's happening at boot.

subject: SLIP Help!
q: My NeXT SLIP link dials and connects fine, but pinging the gateway gets nothing even though the TD and RD lights flash. Could this be a routing problem, and what do the IF flags and SOFT flags in the SLIP log mean?
a: Check the soft flags with duioctl slip0 GSOFTFLAGS. A live line reads 0x320; if LDOWN or FAILEDCALL got set (0x360, 0x3a0), root can reset it with SSOFTFLAGS 0x320. Then read netstat -r and netstat -i, and turn off XON/XOFF in the modems. IF flags are just interface flags. Basics, kid.

subject: taking cube off the network
q: My NeXT cube hangs at "Starting system services..." when I take it off the network. Is there an easier way to switch between networked and standalone?
a: Check your NFS mounts. Hard mounts make the machine hang until it finds the remote filesystems, so use soft, interruptable ones. Yellow Pages may also be hunting for its server. Boot verbose to see where it hangs. Basic stuff.

subject: Serial Port A configuration???
q: My modem on NeXT serial port A comes up 7 bit at login, which breaks vt200 mode until I run stty pass8. Can I make the port permanently 8 bit?
a: The culprit is getty. Its output is even parity unless you specify otherwise, and the terminal driver limits what it can do about it. Sigh. You need a better getty, since this one won't give you a clean 8 bit port.

subject: Mail application and its bugs
q: NeXT's Mail application bounces addresses like giacomet@gb.ecn with more than one item after the @. What's going on?
a: Sounds like a hosed sendmail configuration. Mail just hands the message to sendmail and doesn't care what addresses mean. NeXT also ships an archaic BIND, but a properly tweaked sendmail.cf can do just about anything. Go learn it.

subject: Host option
q: On NeXT OS 0.9, the -Host hostname option fails with 'DPS client library error: Could not form connection'. How do I get it to display on another NeXT?
a: Someone has to be logged into the destination machine, and their PublicWindowServer bit has to be set to YES. Otherwise remote programs can't open windows there. Basic stuff, which the docs should have said.

subject: Printing problems in v0.9
q: On NeXT v0.9 printing fails; npd is up, but the logs say 'couldn't create public context' and 'problem creating PS print context'. What's the problem?
a: The dreaded Public Context problem. Someone without Public Window Server set in their preferences printed, so npd made its context private to that user's job, and after logout nobody could use it. Make everyone set Public Window Server, and reboot meanwhile.

subject: Dead printers...
q: Our early NeXT printer keeps jamming, printing about half a page and then stopping with the paper stuck in the out rollers. Anybody know what to do?
a: Yes, everyone has it. All the mechanical problems with the NeXT laser are the same as any HP LaserJet Series II, because it's the same engine. Nothing magic about it, so don't blame the cube.

subject: sendmail trouble
q: Sendmail on the NeXT drops the domain name of the sender in the From field, so mail shows mccalpin@masig3 instead of the fully qualified name. How do I fix it?
a: First, the recipient never sees the SMTP from, you mean the header From. Sendmail itself is fine. If domains get dropped, the problem is in sendmail.cf, so go fix your config. Bribe the local sendmail hacker with Cheetos and beer.

subject: Power Surge protection & Terminal use
q: Should a NeXT be unplugged during a thunderstorm, can I initialize a floppy in DOS format, and can I eject a diskette from Terminal?
a: Always be careful about surges, and get a UPS. NeXT is Unix and caches writes, so losing power loses files. For DOS floppies, look in /NextAdmin for BuildDOS. For eject, check the man pages for unmount. Honestly, read the docs.

subject: mouse buttons on XNeXT
q: The XNeXT docs say the right mouse button should act as Button3 and both buttons together as Button2, but under twm both buttons just give Button1. How do I fix that?
a: Sigh. Change the "Right Button" default in the Preferences app. I forget which way it has to be set, but the docs will say. Read them next time before posting.

subject: The NeXT laser
q: The output from the NeXT laser printer here is streaky. Is that common? It didn't live up to what I expected from 400dpi.
a: Probably your school is using recycled toner cartridges, which is a no-no. NeXTlasers with original toner almost never streak. Cheap administrators, what a surprise.

subject: playing an arbitrary part of a soundfile
q: The playFrom selector in the NeXT sound object docs isn't implemented. How can I play an arbitrary part of a soundfile without SoundView?
a: Use copySamples:at:count: to copy the wanted portion into another sound object and play that. Don't say it's inefficient: Mach magic means little data is really copied unless you write into it later. Think before complaining.

subject: Application access to Webster?
q: Under NeXT System 1.* my programs used the text library to look up Webster's Dictionary. How do I do that under 2.0?
a: Contact NeXT Technical Support for the missing pieces. You could also check the pub/webster and pub/webster/NeXT-2.0 anonymous FTP directories on iuvax.cs.indiana.edu. That stuff may be all you need. Try reading before asking.

subject: Macintosh Fonts
q: We have Type 1 fonts for a Macintosh and want to install them on a NeXT. How is it done?
a: Convert the LWFN files to plain TEXT with the PD program unAdobe. Put the result in /LocalLibrary/Fonts/outline under the full PostScript name, and the AFM file in /LocalLibrary/Fonts/afm. Then run buildafmdir /LocalLibrary/Fonts to update the index. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: Recommendations for an Objective-C book?
q: What book should I get to learn Objective-C? I plan on writing programs for the NeXT computer.
a: Start with the Stepstone User Reference Manual for Objective-C, chapters 2, 3, 4 and part of 5. Mind that Stepstone's dialect differs from NeXT's. Pinson and Wiener's Objective-C book from Addison-Wesley is due in May, if your bookstore ever gets it. Sigh, read the manual first.

subject: Interface Builder strategies?
q: What's a good strategy for using Interface Builder to modify as well as build user interfaces, instead of decompiling and hand-editing the generated source?
a: Don't decompile. Do that only for instruction or when the app is final. Generate a .nib archive and edit that without recompiling. The skeleton code is just a starter, so add new methods and variables by hand and never regenerate it.

subject: Aufs for the Mac <-> NeXT
q: Where can I find the patches to run NeXT Aufs (Apple Unix File Sharing) with the CAP package from Columbia? I have the five patches that came with it, but there are more needed for NeXT. An anonymous ftp site would be best.
a: The NeXT patches are on anonymous ftp at sumex-aim.stanford.edu, in the info-mac/unix directory. Look for something like cap50-patches.shar. It's literally in your own back yard, so try looking next time.

subject: NeXT file system vs. standard ones
q: Where do people put public domain software on a NeXT, like emacs .el files and filters? Is there a standard way, or is everyone winging it?
a: I build a copy of /usr under /usr/local: bin, src, lib, include, man, etc. You have to add them to your path, libpath and manpath, but it's the cleanest. For NeXT-specific stuff I use /LocalLibrary, /LocalApps, /LocalAdmin and /LocalDeveloper. There is no sacred Tao, so stop winging it.

subject: Where does the mail go???
q: Where does my NeXT mail go when it disappears from Active.mbox for no reason?
a: It's probably not gone. The table_of_contents file in Active.mbox can get corrupted. Quit Mail, delete the table of contents, and restart Mail. It rebuilds it and the missing mail reappears. Yet another bug nobody's fixed.

subject: BUG (?) in 'ftpd' for 'mget' handling ??
q: Why does NeXT's ftpd expand 'mget *' into files one level down in subdirectories? Is that a bug or a feature?
a: It's a feature, and not NeXT's doing. Newer BSD ftpds glob internally and list directory contents, per RFC 1123, and the old client trick of stopping at a blank line no longer works. Short answer: use 'mget .' instead of 'mget *'. This comes up every week.

subject: NeXTMail
q: Why does NeXTMail put a ^M at the end of each line?
a: It doesn't. I checked. Go look at your own setup before blaming the mailer.

subject: tarring to a remote Exabyte
q: Why does tar cbf 20 /dev/nrxt0 work to a local Exabyte, but tar cbf 20 - | dd of=/dev/nrxt0 bs=20b gives directory checksum errors when read back?
a: Use obs=20b, not bs=20b. You only want to set the output block size, not input and output, because of how Unix buffers pipes. Any idiot with the dd man page could see it.

subject: Services Menu problems..............
q: After installing CopyPath2, my NeXT Services menu shows only a couple of entries instead of all my apps like Mathematica and mail service. Can I fix it?
a: Destroy ~/.NeXT/services/.applist and .cache, then log out of Workspace and back in. Run make_services from a shell, then log out and back in again. Yes, it's tedious, welcome to NeXT.

subject: Mma 2.0, Sybase, and ACL upgrades...
q: Has anyone heard when the Mathematica 2.0, Sybase and Allegro Common Lisp upgrades will arrive for NeXT?
a: Mathematica 2.0 is shipping; one person got a copy from NeXT on 8-30-91 and another picked it up at a campus store. Sybase and ACL weren't with it. Mma 2.0 needs a host license. Go bug your computer store.

subject: Is S an alternative to MATLAB?
q: Has anyone ported the S language to the NeXT, and could it be an alternative to MATLAB?
a: New S is available for the NeXT from AT&T, and S+ with more time series and graphics functionality is expected next year. S is very much matrix oriented, and as a data analysis and graphics package it beats MatLab, which is stronger in engineering stuff. Read up before guessing.

subject: Misc. questions.
q: How can I convert large numbers of WriteNow files to ASCII on a NeXT, and is there a simple rule for stripping the formatting?
a: Use the command line: pipe the file through /NextApps/WriteNow.app/wn-rtf and then /usr/lib/indexing/rtf-ascii into your output file. It usually works, though fancy formatting can add stray line breaks. Or save as ASCII from WriteNow itself, which is impractical for lots of files.

subject: CD-ROMs on NeXT
q: How can I get DOS programs under SoftPC on a NeXT to recognize a CD-ROM as a CD-ROM drive instead of another hard disk?
a: Put the CD in and wait for it on the browser. Pick the FSA option in the SoftPC preferences panel, then select the CD from the target panel. It mounts as drive E. Microsoft extensions need the newest SoftPC. RTFM.

subject: Reading SUN (Sparc) floppy disk on a NeXT Station (FAQ?).
q: How can I read and write a floppy on both a NeXTStation and a Sun SPARC?
a: Raw format is the best way: write with tar to the raw floppy device on one machine and read it with tar on the other. MS-DOS format also works but slowly, using mtools on the Sun. NeXT/unix format isn't mountable on the Sparc. Device names differ, so figure them out.

subject: How do you edit NeXTMail you receive?
q: How do I edit a NeXTMail message I've received so I can edit it before forwarding it? Mail lets me call vi, but NeXTMail doesn't seem to.
a: Click Send, then click Forward. The message gets duplicated into a Send window where you can edit it, then click Deliver. Honestly, you shouldn't be editing other people's mail anyway; excerpt or forward it instead.

subject: Problems posting from NG using NNTP
q: I'm having problems posting from NG using NNTP. I hit the post button, the window disappears and NG goes on its merry way, but it seems nothing gets posted. Is the problem my NG setup or the NNTP posting host?
a: Probably your server. Somebody saw the same thing and found their NNTP server was way behind on updates. Check that before you go blaming the software, sigh.

subject: Multi-window support for modem line (Question)
q: Is there a tool that allows multiple sessions over a single modem line on a NeXT, for NeXTstep or X? I know there's one for the Mac.
a: SLIP or PPP will do it. That's what they're for; do your homework.

subject: s: RTF export-filter
q: Is there an RTF export filter for the NeXT that strips RTF to plain ASCII, usable in pipes and in the background?
a: Use /usr/lib/indexing/rtf-ascii from the extended software release; it reads stdin and writes stdout. Pipe it through sed 's/^ //', then nroff, then uniq to word wrap and drop extra blank lines. Not hard, you just had to look.

subject: Mail.app font problems
q: Mail.app's send panel gives me Courier 12 for NeXT-Mail, attachments show as a '<' instead of an icon, and the cursor stops tracking text after changing fonts. Any ideas?
a: Set the font to Helvetica Medium 12.0 pt with the Font Panel, Command-t. Change it to anything else and you get exactly the weirdness you describe. Annoying bug, but there it is.

subject: The Mouse That Squeaks
q: My NeXT mouse squeaks. Would a squirt of WD40 in the mouse-ball hole be bad for it, and what's the right remedy?
a: Read the docs that came with your NeXT. They cover taking the mouse apart and cleaning it. Put the WD40 down, for pity's sake. Honestly, RTFM.

subject: Memory in new NeXTs
q: The monochrome and color NeXTs take different SIMMs. What memory will the new NeXTs use?
a: Nobody outside NeXT knows, but my guess is the color machine's SIMMs, since interleaving gives higher performance. Go ahead and upgrade your slab anyway; Mac owners will want the old SIMMs. It's a guess, so don't quote me.

subject: Color Icons!
q: Why are all the major icons on the NeXTstation Color still 2-bit black and white? Why can't color users have color icons?
a: NeXT's policy is that apps that do something in color get color icons, and the rest get greyscale. Want color icons anyway? Use size -m to find the icon's section, then fsectbyname to read and write it. Do the work yourself.

subject: Double-Click default interval
q: How do I get the double-click interval set in the Preferences application on the NeXT? NXGetDefaultValue with Preferences and DoubleClickInterval didn't work.
a: Run "dread -l" and look. The value lives under the NeXT1 owner as ClickTime, so use atoi of NXGetDefaultValue("NeXT1","ClickTime"). Not "Preferences", obviously. Poke around before posting.

subject: HELP: Using RIGHT Button
q: My NeXT app needs to process right mouse button events, but I get none unless I enable the menu button in Preferences. How do I enable it from my own application?
a: Change the event mask of the window you're receiving events through. A window only gets events its mask lets through, and the right mouse button is probably masked off by default. It's in the Window class documentation and event.h in dpsclient. Read it.

subject: Storage Object broke?
q: My NeXT program segfaults inside Storage's write method when I archive a Storage object with NXWriteObject. Why, and does archiving the root also archive other Storage objects referenced from its data?
a: Did you specify a description string? Without one the object cannot be archived, which is your crash. Sigh, RTFM. With a correct description, the referenced objects should get archived too.

subject: Inline functions in cc document pointer needed.
q: Where can I find documentation on inline function generation in NeXT's cc 2.0, and on the asm() call? Neither is in K&R or the NeXT docs.
a: Fire up emacs and type control-h i. The whole gcc manual is on-line in the GNU emacs info browser, along with the emacs manual. It's been sitting there the whole time, you know.

subject: Bug in execve and #! handling?
q: Why does a #! line in a script get cut off after a certain number of characters on NeXT? Is that a bug in execve?
a: Not a bug. It's inherited from 4.3 BSD: the line is limited to 32 characters, with a single argument allowed. That's why #! is a hack, not a real solution, and it needs a full pathname. If your path is longer, use a symlink. RTFM.

subject: Problem with uploading binary files through modem
q: I can't upload binary files from my NeXT to my university UNIX account with kermit 5A over a 2400 modem. Text works fine, but the transfer hangs. What's wrong?
a: Somewhere the eighth bit is getting trashed. Try "set parity space" to force 7-bit transfers, though that costs efficiency. Or compress and uuencode, then send as ascii. The right fix is finding where the bit dies. Haven't managed that myself.

subject: 8/9bit memory on NeXT-Station
q: I have a NeXTstation with 8MB RAM. Can I mix 4 x 4MB 9-bit memory with my remaining 4 x 1MB, or do I have to buy the more expensive 8-bit memory?
a: Yes, you can mix 9-bit with 8-bit if you skip the parity bit. Put the 1MB 8-bit SIMMs in the upper banks and the 9-bit ones in the lower, then set "enable parity" to "no" in the ROM Monitor. Otherwise no. Read your monitor settings before whining.

subject: Won't let me set the time
q: My NeXT has never been on a network, yet Preferences says the network time daemon is running and won't let me change the clock. How do I set the time?
a: Check your hostconfig file and make sure you have TIME=-NO- in it. Then in NetManager, under Network Time Configuration, uncheck the Time service enabled box. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: outgoing news
q: My outgoing news never gets posted elsewhere, though UUCP sends the batches. Is my sys line, with the feed name and to.feedname, correct, or have I overlooked something?
a: The to.mixcom entry is usually just for testing the path. Add the distributions to the list, like va,usa,world, changing va to your state and adding any others. Makes little sense, but the distribution must be in the list. RTFM next time.

subject: Root Can't Login
q: Root can log in on the NeXT configuration server but not on the served NeXTs. I get a Workspace error, internal error (signal 10), and other users are fine. What is special about a root login?
a: This comes up every few weeks. NetBooted clients that lack root access to / through the server's /etc/exports, via root= or anon=0, hit this Workspace Manager misfeature. Log in at the real console, or log in as a normal user and su. Root isn't needed for normal user operations.

subject: Question for memory banks and chips
q: To add memory to a NeXTstation, do I have to change all four banks? Will 2 meg SIMMs work in place of 1 meg, and what speed must the memory be?
a: NeXTstations have 8 slots in 2 banks of 4. The four SIMMs nearest the power supply are bank 0. You need 100ns if you win the tolerance gamble; 80ns is what's sold now. Faster buys you nothing. Read the NeXTanswers file and the FAQ.

subject: My signature was >5 lines so here it is....
q: Are there any reasonable books on programming the Series 32000?
a: Yes, the Series 32000 Programmer's Reference Manual, Prentice-Hall, 1987. It covers architecture, registers, instruction set, addressing modes, memory management and exceptions. NSC customers can order it through their account, everyone else through a bookstore. Not that hard.

subject: GENIX compiler 'feature' (bug)
q: Why does the GENIX 4.2 C compiler align structures within a structure on quad boundaries, even though the 32xxx doesn't care? Is there a way to turn it off?
a: You answered it yourself: aligned ints, pointers and structs run faster, and compilers favor speed over space. That's a feature, not a bug; VAX 4.3 does it too. No way to force byte-alignment in that compiler. National's newer GNX 5.3 compiler will have a packing option.

subject: Throughput Accelerator problems ?
q: Has anyone had reliability trouble with throughput accelerators on a Pyramid 9820? We've had several hardware crashes since they were added.
a: Ours on a 9825 has been very reliable. One board failed right after the TA went in, but it has run for months since with 50 to 70 heads-down users and a pile of news feeds. Never needs rebooting. Check your board revisions.

subject: Pyramid's sendmail
q: Is the sendmail shipped with Pyramid OSx 4.1 vulnerable to the recent Internet virus, and if so, what do I do?
a: Yes, the same bug that let the worm spread through SMTP is in all stock OSx releases. Get the PTF from RTOC, or if you're in a hurry use the adb patch from comp.bugs.4bsd.ucb-fixes, with "ucb strings - -o" rather than "ucb strings -o". Should have patched already.

subject: comsat and biff
q: On one of our Pyramids users get biff messages meant for other users. Is comsat at fault?
a: Probably comsat, in its scanning of /etc/utmp. One site found the SIGALRM that keeps its logged-in list fresh stops firing, freezing the list. A kill -ALRM to the comsat pid puts it back in sync. Fix your own daemon, then.

subject: Problem with inetd - stops forking in.telnetds
q: Our Pyramid's inetd occasionally stops forking telnetds, though it still listens on port 23 and rlogin works fine. Any suggestions?
a: Just a shot in the dark: are you overrunning the TOOMANY limit? If the problem clears in about ten minutes, you've probably started more than 40 in a specified amount of time. Basic inetd behavior, so check before blaming the vendor.

subject: Upgrade to 5.0
q: Why does upgrading a Pyramid 90x to OSx 5.0 require a faster 10MHz processor? Why would an operating system care how fast the processor runs?
a: It doesn't care about clock speed. OSx 5.0 won't run on the 90x SP processor set, so you need to upgrade to an AP processor, which happens to be 10MHz. Sounds like a garbled communication problem. Also, 5.0 is probably a pig, so expect to want at least 8M of memory.

subject: Could we run a C++ program on several processors in parallel ?
q: Can I run a C++ program on several processors of a Sequent in parallel? Combining C++ with the Parallel Programming Library chokes on keywords like "shared".
a: Look at Presto, from Brian Bershad at UW, available by ftp from cs.washington.edu. It does what you want and more. Fair warning: you need AT&T C++ 1.2.1 on the Sequent, since g++ isn't supported yet. Sigh.

subject: timed on Dynix V3.0?
q: Does anyone have a version of BSD 4.3 timed that runs on a Sequent running DYNIX V3.0? The source I got from uunet has too many 4.3-isms to compile.
a: Yes, someone has versions of both timed and ntp for it. Fair warning: they're not well tested and involve some rather strict compromises. Welcome to porting 4.3 code to a 4.2 box.

subject: Large Tape Drives Availability
q: Does anyone make a very large tape drive for the Sequent Symmetry, like 2.3GB on a Video 8 cartridge?
a: Yes. Sequent itself offers a 2GB 8mm tape drive for the Symmetry line. Go bother your local Sequent sales rep for the literature, since the asker apparently couldn't be bothered to check.

subject: did Sequent really pull Unisys plug?
q: Is it true that Sequent has stopped selling S27s and S81s through Unisys because Unisys fell behind on payments? What happens to Unisys servicing and to PTX?
a: Not so, far from it. Sequent just won't pursue NEW OEM deals and is building its direct sales force. Unisys is still a valued partner, selling U6000/70 and /80 boxes, which are S27s and S81s. DYNIX/ptx is written by Sequent, not Unisys. Quit believing rumors.

subject: mv not atomic in dynix
q: Why isn't mv atomic under DYNIX? Two mv commands renaming the same file or directory to different names at the same time left me with two hard links to one inode. Has this been reported?
a: It's a multiprocessor with a re-entrant kernel, genius. On a uniprocessor rename() is atomic only because no other process can be in the kernel at once. On DYNIX several CPUs can run rename() together, and hardware locks on the link counts won't stop that. Sigh.

subject: 2 Gb cartridge tape drive
q: Will the EXABYTE EXB-8200 8mm tape drive work with a Sequent system, and does anyone have experience with it?
a: It more or less does. Someone ran it on a B8K in place of the cartridge drive with the DYNIX cartridge tape driver, and read and write worked without significant changes. The Exabyte looks like an Archive streamer with a very long tape. Sequent worried about reliability, though. Test it yourself.

subject: problem with edge in 3.3.1?
q: After installing IRIX 3.3.1 on our 4D/20, running edge gives "Could not find window slot in shared memory: Error 0". What does this mean and how do I fix it?
a: That message comes from 4Sight. Log out of 4Sight and log back in again, and see if that clears it. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: tcsh problems on Personal IRIS...
q: After installing tcsh on a Personal IRIS and making it the login shell, the console vanishes and I can't start a wsh. Switching back to /bin/csh fixes it. Why?
a: wsh can't find the command tcsh. Symlink it into /bin with ln -s /usr/local/bin/tcsh /bin/tcsh and it works. Check the SYSLOG, it tells you so. Obvious if you'd read it.

subject: NeWS can't find host information for "cinnamon"
q: After setting up yp on a new Iris, NeWS dies saying it can't find host information for my own host name, though /etc/hosts and the yp hosts database both have proper entries and networking works. What's wrong?
a: That's a bug in IRIX 3.2. Check /usr/etc/yp for a resolv.conf file, delete it and reboot, and the NeWS server should come up. It's fixed in 3.3, so upgrade next time instead of whining.

subject: Problems with system tools in 3.2
q: After upgrading our SGI 4D/220GTX to 3.2, WorkSpace says it can't connect with the File Access Monitor (fam), and Transfer Manager and System Manager do nothing or vanish. What's wrong?
a: Your yp server needs the sgi_fam and sgi_toolkitbus lines in its inetd.conf, pointing at fam and rpc.toolkitbus. Then bounce inetd with kill -1. This comes up every time someone upgrades. Read the release notes.

subject: VGX and setmonitor(3g)
q: Calling setmonitor on a 4D/340VGX under IRIX 3.3 can hang the graphics pipe if other graphics processes are running. Will this bug be fixed in the 3.3.1 release?
a: Yes, it's fixed in 3.3.1. Under 3.3.0 it's only safe when no other program is doing graphics, and that's hard to guarantee, so it's never really safe. Sigh, ship it right the first time.

subject: Can you compile tcsh without gcc?
q: Can tcsh be compiled on an SGI Personal Iris without gcc? Linking fails with a usplit error about not being able to read or write ucodes.
a: Yes. I got linking errors too with tcsh 6.00.00. Fetch 6.00.01 and it built fine. The meta key still doesn't work, and nobody has told me why. Grab the newer source before whining about the compiler.

subject: fortran compilation error
q: Compiling any Fortran program on our Personal Iris 4D25 gives undefined symbols __trap_fpe_override and __checktraps. Where are these routines and how do I get them included?
a: They don't turn up in standard releases unless you've mixed system libraries from different releases. In 3.3, __trap_fpe_override is referenced in libF77.a and defined in libc.a, and _checktraps is referenced in libI77.a and defined in libc.a. 3.2 has neither. Fix your library mix.

subject: Bash for the Iris
q: Has anyone ported GNU's bash to the Iris with job control working? We can compile it only by disabling job control, which is frustrating since the Iris supports it.
a: Yes, it's been done. The changes go into bash 1.06, but they were only tested on pre-release Irix 3.3. Under 3.2 you'll need some changes, though it shouldn't be too hard. Sigh, read the release notes next time.

subject: sgi to PCX ???
q: Has anyone seen a public domain SGI image to PCX converter?
a: The San Diego Supercomputer Center has a set of image format conversion tools that I believe are distributable. Try mailing consult@y1.sdsc.edu. Honestly, ask them instead of the whole net.

subject: Dog (Flight)
q: How can I isolate SGI machines running dog (flight) so its packet storms don't hit other machines on the network?
a: Fixed in a future IRIX release. By default dog will use UDP/IP multicasting instead of broadcasting. Same amount of traffic, but only the machines playing dog receive the packets. Live with it until then.

subject: how to attach a modem for dial-in/out
q: How do I attach a Telebit T2500 modem to an SGI Personal Iris running IRIX 3.2.1 for both dial-in and dial-out at 19200?
a: Set up a dx_19200 getty in /etc/gettydefs and run the fix-telebit script in /usr/lib/uucp on the port with the modem on, then start your getty. For both directions, run uugetty on ttyf with hardware flow control. Get one direction working first, don't be greedy.

subject: Writing Low Density Tapes from a Personal Iris
q: How do I write low density tapes from a Personal Iris so a GT can read them? The Personal Iris writes high density that the GT can't read.
a: This has been said many times, but fine. The Archive 2150S (QIC-150) drive can't write QIC-11 or QIC-24, only read QIC-24. If you need to write QIC-24 on the PI, you need the 2060S QIC-24 drive. Read the group before asking.

subject: sgi screen dpi
q: How many dpi is the Iris screen, and does it change with different monitors? I'm using 118 dpi mode TeX fonts and they don't look quite right.
a: On a 4D with a 19 inch monitor it's a hair under 96 dpi; a 14 inch monitor on a PI gives about 108. When in doubt, get out a tape measure, measure the scanned area and divide by the pixels. Not rocket science.

subject: emacs
q: I built emacs 18.55 on an Iris running Irix 3.3.1 with an NFS-mounted home directory. It says "error in init file" on my .emacs, though the same file works on Suns and Sonys. Any ideas?
a: It's Yellow Pages, of course. Emacs doesn't consult the YP passwd when hunting for ~/.emacs. Relink with -lsun, or put your own entry in the local /etc/passwd after the plus entry, or add a dummy plus entry at the bottom. Read the 3Y man pages.

subject: Monkey Wrench in apE?
q: I started apE 2.0 on an Iris with the wrench command, and the window just sits there reading Wrench with no icons. What's wrong?
a: Nothing's wrong, it's a feature. apE would swallow your whole screen, so the icons don't come up automatically. Pick Palettes from the Windows pull-down menu in wrench. And go through the tutorials, which you'd have known if you'd read them.

subject: External tape drives
q: I want to put a 760 Mb drive in my Personal Iris 4D/20's full-height slot, so what do I do with my internal 150 Mb SCSI tape drive? Is there an inexpensive external cabinet?
a: The SGI option is the external 150 Meg SCSI tape drive, P5-T4C3A, which sits on top and is externally powered. It's the logical choice only if you're buying another PI without the tape. Ask your sales rep; no cheap cabinet was named.

subject: NFS problems...
q: I'm mounting a file system from a Sun 4/330 running SunOS 4.1 onto an SGI 4D210/VGX. Files I write onto the NFS file system are dated an hour behind, though both clocks are right and touch sets the date correctly. Any ideas?
a: Daylight savings, most likely. IRIX and SunOS keep time in GMT and convert for display, so if the two disagree about the timezone or whether DST is in effect, you get exactly this. The server picks mtime on normal writes, while touch passes all the times over the wire. Check TZ, and try man timezone.

subject: Parallel printing from 4D/70G ?
q: I'm trying to make a parallel printer cable for a Tektronix 4692 on an Iris 4D/70G. The pinout SGI gave me is for a DB25, but my machine has a DB37 and it doesn't work. What's going on?
a: That pinout is for the PI's DB25 connector. The IKON Centronics board needs a 37-pin Sub-D to Centronics 34-pin cable, the P4-PX01, which you apparently never ordered. Order it. Your hotline gave you the wrong sheet twice, which is hardly surprising.

subject: Question about 'man' on Irix 3.3.2 (4D/210GTX)
q: Irix 3.3.2 on a 4D/210GTX ships without troff, so I can't read unformatted man pages. Building groff needs g++ and gcc and gave me trouble. Is there an easier way than buying troff from AT&T?
a: We skipped porting roff entirely. We mounted the local/man hierarchy from a Sun and ran catman there. Faster than fighting groff, g++ and gcc on an Iris, and you didn't have to pay AT&T either.

subject: Is there a CPU meter for the SGI?
q: Is there a CPU meter for the SGI that works like the CPU performance meter on the Sun?
a: Try gr_osview. Use a ~/.grosview file with cpu strip, gfx strip, wait strip and rmemc lines. It's been there all along, you know. Look before you ask.

subject: SEIKO printer documentation
q: Is there any documentation on how to control page size, setup, etc. for the SGI Seiko printer filters? There should at least be a man page.
a: The Seiko 2.0 driver has the features you want. The hardcopy manual and the online release notes document them. You didn't say which release you run, so check that you're not stuck on the old 1.0. RTFM.

subject: Loss of CR/LF in wsh window??
q: My wsh window sometimes loses its CR/LF handling so that output staircases across the screen. How do I reset it without killing the window?
a: Type control-J, then stty sane, then control-J again. Works most of the time and puts the default settings like the erase character back. Only an amateur kills the window. This comes up every week.

subject: .4sight and X
q: On IRIS release 3.3, X applications won't start for users with ~/.4sight, user.ps and startup.ps, though they work from an xterm. xSGINeWS is on in chkconfig. What's going on?
a: Release 3.3 changed X autostart. The array basicRestartActions in /usr/NeWS/lib/NeWS/init.ps calls startXsgi, which runs xstart. Your user.ps is redefining basicRestartActions without that call. Fix that, and stop redefining things you don't understand.

subject: mailbox
q: On IRIX 3.3 my mailbox icon appears, but my window scrolls 'mailbox: Bad file number' continuously. What's happening?
a: Mailbox prints that when it can't connect to fam. Check whether famd is running. And try 'Mail -v' to see where your mail is actually going. Read the messages, they tell you things.

subject: bug in reading from disk partitions
q: On IRIX 3.3.1, how can I find the raw size of a disk partition? A read that runs past the end of the partition fails instead of returning a partial buffer.
a: RTFM. The partition info lives in the disk label, the first 512 bytes of the volume header partition. See /usr/include/sys/dvh.h and vh(7m) for the layout and read the sizes from there.

subject: hostname and domain name server.
q: On SGI 3.3.1, running named forced us to set hostname to the fully qualified name, but elm expects hostname to return just the first part. Is anyone running named with a single-name hostname?
a: If you don't put your domain in /usr/etc/resolv.conf, the fully-qualified name in /etc/sys_id is a Good Idea. gethostname returns what's in sys_id, and hostname just echoes it. Use hostname -s to strip the domain. Honestly, that's not hard.

subject: Mountd keeps dying
q: On our SGI 4D/70GT running IRIX 3.2, rpc.mountd keeps dying whenever someone mounts or unmounts one of its disks, and we cross-mount filesystems with several hosts. How can I find out what's causing it? Do I need more nfsd processes?
a: Nfsd has little to do with mounting, so more of them won't help. Use rpcinfo -p to check that portmap is running and knows inetd will start mountd, and netstat -a to see inetd is listening on that port. Core files or dead portmap? Call the Hotline. Define "dying" first.

subject: DWB and PostScript
q: SGI removed PostScript support from DWB in Irix 3.2.2, and my printer is on a VAX, so I need a PostScript file I can copy over. Where do I go from here?
a: Get Transcript. SGI has always sold it separately from DWB. Its psroff front end has an option to write the PostScript to standard output instead of sending it to a printer, so you can ship that file to your VAX. Hardly rocket science.

subject: Function Keys on Iris Console
q: The pF3 and pF4 keys on our IRIS 4D/220 console running IRIX 3.2 got redefined to print strings. How do I get them back to the standard values?
a: RTFM on bindkey. Run bindkey -l f3 and bindkey -l f4. Bindings are per wsh, so do it in every wsh. Put the commands in your .cshrc if you want it permanent. The release notes don't mention it, naturally.

subject: VMS utilities
q: VMS lets you edit previous commands with the up arrow, which beats UNIX history commands. Has anyone written something to emulate this on UNIX, free or for sale?
a: MIPS boxes have an optional emacs-like line editor in csh and dbx, about the same function as VMS but with control characters, not arrow keys. The SGI Irises lack it. Learn control keys instead of whining about cardpunch-style ! and ^ editing.

subject: xdm
q: We run IRIX 3.3 and xdm doesn't seem to support XDMCP, so X-terminals can't use it. Has SGI fixed this bug in 4.0?
a: Yes, the bug has been fixed and will be available in 4.0. Took long enough.

subject: Third Party Disks for 4D/70GT
q: We want to add a third-party 760 MB disk to our 4D/70GT. Should it be ESDI or on the built-in SCSI bus, and does fx in 3.2 handle drives like the Fujitsu M2263 and Imprimis?
a: Go ESDI; it will outperform SGI's SCSI on that machine for now. Release 3.2 knows the 2263, the Imprimis and others. For an unknown drive, copy and modify a similar fx entry. Naturally the vendor says buy from them.

subject: color map lighting
q: What are the limitations of color map lighting in GL versus RGB, and which is better in the long run?
a: You're limited in colors, since each needs a color ramp the lighting indexes into. The ramp includes the light's color too, so no two differently colored lights. Many properties don't apply in color index mode. RGB is the way to go. Obviously.

subject: What is "pseudorgb()"?
q: What is pseudorgb() on the SGI? It needs -lgutil, but ar -t libgutil.a doesn't list it, and I can't find it in the man pages, includes or source.
a: Can't say what it does, but ar -t only lists object files, and one object file can hold several routines. Use nm to see what symbols a library defines. Basic stuff, really.

subject: spreadsheets
q: What spreadsheets are available for SGI machines, especially ones with hooks into Oracle?
a: Two exist. SQL*Calc is a curses-based spreadsheet written by and for Oracle. Wingz is a Motif-based spreadsheet from Informix, and you'd have to adapt it to Oracle yourself. Both come from your SGI sales rep, so go bother them.

subject: timetrim value
q: What value should timetrim in /usr/sysgen/master.d/kernel be so a 4D-80GT keeps better time? At -2000000 it still runs fast.
a: Lower. Mine is at -2570000. If you can run timed or timeslave, it will report a suggested value. Otherwise you're guessing.

subject: qdevice and stuff.........
q: When I qdevice keyboard keys on an SGI, I get two entries in the event queue for each key press, one for down and one for up. Can I get only one entry per press?
a: That's what the val is for: 1 when the button goes down, 0 when it goes up. Just test it and ignore the event you don't want. If all you want is ascii, qdevice(KEYBD) and val is the ascii value. RTFM.

subject: Kermit For 4D/25 Wanted
q: Where can I get a Kermit that's pre-set up for an SGI 4D/25 running 3.3.2?
a: Check /usr/people/4Dgifts. It has a kermit that worked when I tried it. You may need to reload it from tape as the gifts subset, or compile it, which needs the dev set. It's already on your machine.

subject: # of overlay planes
q: Why doesn't set indentprefix work in Mail, so my quoted replies get a tab instead of a prefix?
a: Because mailx source never checks it. Transmit() just does putc of a tab, and grep for prefix finds nothing related. Build a vi macro instead. Grumble, Berkeley Mail never did this properly.

subject: yp problem
q: Why won't an SGI yp client bind to a Sun yp master when a router is between them on the subnet?
a: ypbind finds servers with UDP/IP broadcasts, and routers don't forward broadcasts. You can often limp along by pointing the client at the server with ypset, using an IP number. It becomes unbound whenever anything hiccups, though. Sigh.

subject: 1000SL additions
q: Can I add a hard disk to a Tandy 1000SL by mail order, or do I have to buy a Tandy hard card?
a: Any drive and controller for a PC should work, but get a money-back guarantee in writing to be safe. Order a hard card sized for the Tandy and watch the ads. Not rocket science.

subject: 64k for CoCo2
q: Can I upgrade my CoCo 2 to 64K, and is Extended Basic needed to access more than 16K of RAM?
a: Get Rainbow Magazine, which covers memory upgrades often. As for Extended Basic, it's irrelevant: all three Basics, Standard, Extended and Disk, address only up to 32K on the CoCo II. Anything past that needs clever machine language or Basic extensions. Sigh, RTFM.
