subject: Hard Disk on a 1000TX (revisited)
q: Does enabling IRQ5 with the DIP switch on a Tandy 1000TX let most non-Tandy hard drive controllers work, given that Tandy used IRQ2?
a: Yes. IRQ2 was only used on the pre-1989 Tandy 1000 models, and on the TX (and SX too) you can enable IRQ5 with one of the DIP switches. Read the manual properly next time.

subject: TRS-80 Model I
q: I have a TRS-80 Model I whose monitor was wrecked in shipping. Can I get its output onto a TV or another monitor, or is there an RF modulator for it?
a: The Model I video out is plain composite video on a funky connector, so feed signal and ground into any composite monitor or RF modulator. The 5-pin DIN carries ground, video and 5 volts for the optoisolator. Use a cable with RCA ends, skip the 5 volt line, and it's a piece of cake.

subject: Model 1: how to get any $ recovery
q: I have a Tandy Model 1 I don't use anymore. How can I get any money back or let someone make use of it? Do schools want them?
a: Donate it. Schools get finicky about donations, but a charity, a home for the handicapped, or a place introducing people to computing might take it. Some nonprofit ships used computers to third world countries. Either way you get a tax writeoff, so stop pining for cash.

subject: What sort of support is there for Tandy 6000HD?
q: I'm looking at a cheap Tandy 6000HD with Xenix and no C compiler. Is a C compiler available, and what Xenix version is minimal for a USENET node?
a: Your dealer is dense. Tandy sells a run-time system and a separate development system, and the dev system has the compiler. Use Tandy's 3.2 core system; the 3.0 dev system will do. Look in the catalog.

subject: Harddisk swap (is it possible...?)
q: Is it possible to install a harddisk from an IBM PS/2 Model 30 into a Tandy RL1000? I need a larger harddisk.
a: No. The RL1000 uses a special low-current, low-voltage drive because Tandy refused to put a fan in it. A standard drive will probably overload the tiny power supply and hose it. Only the Tandy 20 meg, RS part 25-1047, belongs in there.

subject: Scroll Lock Key on 1000TX
q: My Tandy 1000TX has no Scroll Lock key, but Smartcom II needs it for VT100 emulation. What do I do?
a: On the original Tandy 1000A, Scroll Lock is emulated by pressing ALT-BREAK. I don't know about the newer ones, but try that first. Honestly, read your keyboard docs.

subject: MOUSE TROUBLE
q: My Tandy serial mouse on a Tandy 1000A says "MOUSE DRIVER NOT INSTALLED -- MICROSOFT MOUSE NOT FOUND". Is it the right software, and what's wrong?
a: Most mouse drivers default to COM1 unless told otherwise. Check which port the mouse is plugged into, COM1 or COM2. Basic stuff, but nobody reads the manual.

subject: RS 4000/4000LX with SCSI drives and XENIX 386
q: Tandy ships XENIX 386 2.2.4 on the 4000LX with SCSI drives because 2.3.1 doesn't support them. Is that a temporary glitch or permanent?
a: Probably temporary. Rumor from near Tandy is that a new Xenix, 2.3GT, is due soon, about 95% of the upcoming SCO Unix, with support for two SCSI controller cards. It's third-hand grapevine, so check with Tandy yourself.

subject: RF Modulator
q: Where can I get an RF modulator for a TI99/4A? Mine is trash, and I remember an ad for them at about $5.
a: Tenex was advertising them at $19.95 in MicroPendium, which is steep, and Tex-Comp probably carries them even if the ads don't say so. Ask your local users group. Your $5 memory is fantasy.

subject: Meiko User Group
q: Does a Meiko User Group really exist, and how do I join it? Are there publications from it?
a: It exists, though Meiko does a lousy job of advertising it. Two conferences so far, another coming up in Manchester, and about 5 or 6 issues of a newsletter called Surface Noise. Contact Peter Dew at the University of Leeds computer science school, or Meiko themselves.

subject: MemStart
q: What is MemStart in the INMOS Transputer Instruction Set compiler writer's guide? I can't find where it's defined.
a: It's not defined in the book, which is an omission. MemStart is the address of the first word above the special RAM locations at the bottom of memory, so it varies by chip. T212 is #8024, T414 is #80000048, T425 and T800 are #80000070. Read the datasheet.

subject: Taken ABAQ, back to the days of void and vapor.
q: What's the status of the Atari ABAQ transputer workstation running Helios? Does it really exist or is it vapor?
a: It exists. Atari UK handles it, not Sunnyvale. 47 Revision 3 beta units were built, mostly staying in Europe. Production may use those or wait for Revision 4. Helios comes from Perihelion Software in the UK, with X-Windows reportedly ported. Stop spreading vapor rumors.

subject: Programs for a Z-1OO
q: I have a Z-100 running DOS 3.1. Is there a version of Turbo C that runs on it, and what Sidekick-like popup utilities are there?
a: The command line Turbo C runs fine on a Z-100, though you may need a parameter to turn off line numbers. Get ZPC from HUG to run PC software. For popups, only Perks and Genie that I know of. Both cover most of what Sidekick does.

subject: Info about AT&T 630 MTG
q: Compiling a large program for the AT&T 630 MTG, mc68ccom gives "Dimension Table Overflow". Is there a flag to increase the dimension table size?
a: No flag. It happens when the compiler meets more than about 200 aggregates and arrays in a file. The limit is compiled in; raise DIMTABSZ from 800 in manifest.h and rebuild mc68ccom. Easier: break the application into smaller files.

subject: CIT101e terminfo?
q: Does anyone have a terminfo source or at least a termcap entry for a C Itoh CIT-101e terminal?
a: Yes, there's a termcap entry for it, derived from the Callan cd100 entry, with variants for 132 columns and for no auto-margins. Go find it in the net archives, the net's not your personal termcap file. Grumble.

subject: Wyse 50 terminal -- anyone have manual for block mode?
q: Does the standard manual for a Wyse 50 terminal say anything about block mode? I want to use it for error checking with a Unix driver.
a: The reference manual has a little, not much more than you'd figure out yourself. Block mode data is sent only when PRINT or SEND is pressed, nulls aren't sent, and attributes go as spaces. Turn it on with Shift Break or ESC B. No off sequence is listed. Dismal manual.

subject: Terminal link to PC
q: How can I hook a terminal to my 8088 PC's serial port and use it to run word processing and my other programs, rather than just talking via Procomm? CTTY didn't work for me.
a: Forget it. This is a neat idea that gets attempted constantly, but MSDOS software isn't written for it, and graphics programs won't work at all. At best, with a terminal ANSI/PC mode and a special driver, you run text programs. Or buy a keyboard/monitor extension, or just carry the thing.

subject: Televideo 970 Help?
q: How do I save changed setup settings like baud rate and parity to NVR on a Televideo 970 without documentation?
a: While still in the setup menu, hit ^S. That's it. Next time, find a manual before asking the whole net.

subject: VT-compatible terminal laptop?
q: I need a small laptop RS232 terminal with at least VT100 compatibility. Any pointers?
a: Almost any laptop will do. The trick is the choice of terminal program, so first try MsKermit. Sigh, you don't need special terminal hardware for this.

subject: ANSI codes
q: Is there a complete list of ANSI terminal codes available by email or ftp? Also, are there codes for redirecting data to a capture file, like redirecting to a printer?
a: There's a summary of the ANSI X3.64 control codes on anonymous FTP at CS.UTK.EDU, pub/shuford/ansi_x3_64.txt. For the full story read the actual standard. Capture-file redirection isn't in it; that's a private vendor extension, so don't count on it.

subject: ADM3+ terminal
q: Is there a way to make my ADM3+ terminal run like a vt100?
a: Definitely not. If your system uses termcap or terminfo, though, most simple software can handle the ADM3+ with its own control codes. Use the terminal for what it is, grumble.

subject: ESC key and the VT320 and vi (whew!)
q: On my VT320, when I finish editing in vi and hit the ESC key, it capitalizes or uncapitalizes the last thing I typed. How do I fix it?
a: Use the map command, like everyone told you. Put it in the EXINIT environment variable: map x ^[ and map! x ^[, where x is the sequence the F11 key sends. That's the key labelled Esc on the keyboard. Look it up in the manual, sigh.

subject: 5620 fonts for a Pyramid
q: We run AT&T 5620 terminals off Pyramid machines with Pyramid's DMD package. Has anyone ported the dlf font downloader and its fonts to the Pyramid?
a: Sounds like the loadfont utility that goes with Dave Prosser's myx environment for the 5620. It's in the AT&T UNIX System ToolChest as the dmd-pgmg package. Go look there instead of begging for ports. myx does a lot more than swap fonts, too.

subject: wyse 60 experience requested
q: What do users think of the Wyse 60 terminal? Is it fast enough to keep up with 9600 baud output without flow control, and is it a good terminal?
a: It's cheap and gives you 43x132 with real underlining and inverse, but it's no ANSI/VT100. The keypad is never reprogrammable, native mode is nasty, and it needs lots of padding at 19200. The 9600 rumor is true on at least one unit. Sigh, you get what you pay for.

subject: VT-240 Terminal attributes question
q: Why does the blink attribute go away on a VT240 while a QIOW is pending, so the cursor disappears waiting for keyboard input? How do I stop it?
a: Never seen it happen on any VT240 under RSX or VMS, so can't explain it. If you're doing a read with prompt and the prompt string has an escape sequence that disables the cursor, that would do it. Check your own code first.

subject: New mouse for 630MTG?
q: My 630MTG mouse, the standard Depraz red hemisphere with a DB-9, has no vertical tracking. Is there a plug-and-play replacement?
a: Not that anyone knows of. Common Mac or PC mice won't do. A Logitech 3-button serial mouse or an old Apollo mouse was suggested. If the cursor tracks horizontally only, a slight adjustment of the matching potentiometer will probably fix it.

subject: Huge Characters
q: Can LaTeX print very large characters like for posters? The biggest I get is 12pt with \Huge and it's not big enough.
a: TeX only ships fonts at a limited number of magnifications, so \Huge is where it stops. Use the font cminch, which gives characters one inch high at \magstep0. Or generate huge ones with metafont, of course. Read the docs.

subject: IPA in MF
q: Does anyone have an International Phonetic Alphabet font in Metafont, or any other format? Half-finished work is welcome.
a: Washington State University has a full IPA font, reasonably priced and good quality, and may be making it public domain. Contact the Dean Guenther guy there. Fair warning: no source. Bought it in 300, 118 and 1270 dpi.

subject: Changing Math subscript fonts in LaTeX...
q: How can I change the font size LaTeX uses for subscripts and subsubscripts in math? My thesis has 200 equations and fonts can't be under 10 points, and I don't want to edit every equation.
a: Just say \scriptfont1=\tenmi anywhere after \begin{document}. It's plain TeX, sure, but no LaTeX source lines need changing. Honestly, you'd have saved yourself the panic by knowing what's underneath.

subject: Printing 2 x A5 pages on A4 with LaTeX/TeX/DVIALW/AppleLaserwriter...
q: How can I print two A5 pages sideways on an A4 sheet with LaTeX, TeX, DVIALW and an Apple LaserWriter? Is hacking DVIALW the best way?
a: No need to hack DVIALW. Use a TeX output routine to put two pages side by side on each sheet, then print landscape, assuming DVIALW can do that. The LaTeX twocolumn option nearly does it unless you want headers and footers. Then more work is needed. Think before you hack.

subject: Tilde (~) in LaTeX
q: How can I put a tilde in text formatted with LaTeX, in a sentence and not in verbatim mode?
a: Most fonts have the tilde only as an accent, not a letter. So put a tilde accent over an empty character or over a space, like \~\ . Ugly, but that's TeX for you.

subject: how to FORCE a page break in troff?
q: How do I absolutely force a page break in troff with me macros? Even .rs before .bp doesn't give a blank page with headers and footers.
a: Put .bp, then a line containing just \& (a zero-width character) to put something on the page, then another .bp. That leaves one blank page with headers and footers. Simple, if you'd read the manual.

subject: Eroff: Lanscaping Header and Footers
q: In troff, how can I set different page offsets for odd and even pages, so headers and footers behave properly when printing for xeroxing and cropping?
a: Troff has built-in conditions for odd and even pages. Use .if e .po 1.0i and .if o .po 4.0i inside a macro, and set a trap at the top of the page to call it. Better yet, modify your macro package. Basic stuff, really.

subject: TRANSCRIPT licence
q: Is Adobe's TRANSCRIPT software freely available, or is it a normal product needing a site licence? I've seen it on FTP sites but the documentation says licence.
a: It's a normal Adobe product, meaning not free and not public domain. Whatever you saw on FTP sites shouldn't be there. Read the licence before you go downloading things.

subject: Request for Display PostScript Utility
q: Is there a commercially available PostScript previewer that can display troff/PostScript output in an X Open Look window?
a: Sun's pageview is a PostScript previewer: troff into dpost into pageview. The X11R4 tape also has xditview for previewing troff under X. Read the tape contents before whining about it, and check the earlier answer.

subject: Change bars in *roff
q: Is there a program that highlights the changes between two *roff files, with change bars, for printing man pages for review?
a: diffmk(1), any idiot knows that. Run diffmk old new change, and it puts change bars and deletion stars into the output file using troff's .mc directive. Then run that file through troff. Sometimes the result needs a bit of repair.

subject: Contour Integrals
q: Is there a reasonable way of drawing a contour integral sign with TeX?
a: Use \oint. It's in cmex10 at octal positions 110 and 111. Did you even look through the font tables? Sigh.

subject: refer and troff and TeX questions
q: Is there a way to use a refer database with TeX? I have a big reference database and would like to use it there.
a: The output of refer is just troff commands, so a sed script can convert them into TeX macro calls. Wrap it in a shell script that runs refer, runs sed, and makes a TeX input file. Works with LaTeX too. Not rocket science.

subject: verbatim macros in latex
q: The LaTeX verbatimfile style's listing environment doesn't number blank lines and handles tabs badly. Has anyone solved either problem?
a: Run the Unix command "expand" on the file first to deal with tabs. Doing it correctly in TeX is real hard, and it's much easier to expand the tabs ahead of time. Not what you wanted to hear, I know. Tough.

subject: AmS-TeX
q: What is the latest version of the AmS-TeX macros? Is there anything later than 1.1d from August 1988?
a: 1.1d is the latest. The AMS keeps promising new stuff, like an AmS-TeX style for LaTeX and new fonts, but judging by past timetables don't hold your breath. Maybe by summer, if then.

subject: What is the LaTeX license???
q: What is the license on LaTeX? I can grab latex.tex from our mainframe but don't know whether it is public domain.
a: It's freely redistributable but copyrighted, so it is not public domain. Learn the difference, it isn't hard.

subject: Tex 2.98(?) wanted.
q: What's the newest version of TeX? I know 2.95 but heard of 2.98. Where can I get it by ftp?
a: Latest TeX.web is 2.991. Try june.cs.washington.edu by ftp, though a European archive site should do just as well. Sigh, check the archives before asking what's newest.

subject: need pointer to sgml documentation
q: Where can I get documentation on SGML, the standard graphical markup language?
a: It's Standard Generalized Markup Language, get it right. Not much is published yet. Try the American Association of Publishers, which built its own standard on SGML, or the University of Chicago Press guide to electronic manuscripts at a local university library.

subject: AMS Euler Fonts
q: Where can I get the METAFONT description of the AMS Euler fonts? Only some pk files came with my new TeX.
a: You can't, not freely. The AMS still owns the sources and hasn't released them, just the low-resolution rasters. If you're willing to pay, contact the AMS. Sigh, not everything on the net is free.

subject: Publisher listing
q: I'm starting out freelancing. Is there an electronic listing of publishers anywhere, or any list at all?
a: Most large libraries carry the Gale Directory of Publications, which lists most if not all magazines. Otherwise try the yellow pages. Yes, paper. It still works, you know.

subject: Ascii Text from Ventura
q: Is there a way to get Ventura 3.0 to print out a file containing only ASCII text?
a: Print to an ASCII file, no. You can extract text with File Type/Rename under the Edit menu, changing the type to ascii. But you lose all the formatting, frame text has to be saved piece by piece, and you strip Ventura's commands yourself. That's the DOS/GEM version; don't whine about it.

subject: Text Movement Problems....
q: We get magazine submissions in troff ms format that must end up in QuarkExpress after editing, and some editors want Frame. Frame has no DCA output filter. How should we move text between these?
a: Why do authors need formatting at all? They're just pouring text into predefined formats. Have them use the tool of their choice and make the interchange format plain ASCII. Handle special formatting needs outside the normal loop. House style should cover fonts.

subject: Text going round in circles?
q: What MS-DOS packages can put characters at various angles and positions, say a logo with text in a semicircle? Do desktop publishing packages do this directly, or are graphics programs better?
a: TeX and MF can do it, and there's a TUGboat article detailing it. Otherwise, Adobe Type Align lets text follow an arbitrary path, but it needs MS Windows and wasn't out for the PC yet. Go read up before buying anything.

subject: Rotating Text at Arbitrary Angles
q: Can FrameMaker 2.1 or 3.0 rotate text at angles other than 90 degrees?
a: As I recall, no. That was a feature ArborText offered over Frame. Whoever picked Frame figured they'd rarely need it. Guess you did. Tough luck.

subject: How to hide fmconsole.log
q: How can I hide the fmconsole.log file when I start up FrameMaker 1.3? An alternate name like .fmconsole.log would solve it.
a: You can't suppress it, only redirect it. Edit fm_install_dir/bin/scripts/.maker_wrapper, search for "tee", and change the $HOME in the fmconsole.log path to somewhere else, or /dev/console. Unsupported, of course, and you'll want that log for troubleshooting anyway.

subject: autonumbering in anchored frames?
q: In FrameMaker 2.1X, I number figures with F:<n+>, each in its own anchored frame, and they all get number 1. If I put several figure paragraphs in one frame it works. What am I doing wrong?
a: You're not doing anything wrong, it's a known bug. Frame only looks at one text rect in an anchored frame for the counter. Select your text rect and use the Front tool from the Graphics Tools menu. Yes, a workaround for a bug. Welcome to Frame.

subject: Embedded PostScript?
q: Is there a way to embed PostScript commands in a FrameMaker document so they get executed rather than printed?
a: Sure. Put your PostScript in a TextRect, then mark it as PostScript Code in the Format Flow dialog box. It's in the manual, you know.

subject: Can't print large PS file derived from a dvi file..
q: I convert a dvi file to PostScript with dvi2ps, and a long document with PostScript figures stops printing midway on my LaserWriter. I assume the printer is running out of memory. Any ideas?
a: Probably not memory at all. The culprit was a stray space in the \psfig argument: it must be figure=psfilename,height=size with no space after the comma. That innocent space hung the printer. Check your syntax first, sigh.

subject: Questions on BNF.
q: Can someone characterize languages that are LR but not LL? Is there an example?
a: Easy. L = {x^n : n > 0} U {x^n y^n : n > 0} is LR but not LL. An LL parser must pick a rule before it sees the y's, and no fixed lookahead of k x's gets you past that. Sigh, any decent formal languages text covers it.

subject: RP Survey article
q: Can someone suggest a good survey article on randomized polynomial time algorithms?
a: Prabhakar Raghavan's IBM Tech Report, titled Randomized Algorithms, is a really good one. It covers analysis techniques too. Go read it instead of asking the net.

subject: Classification question
q: Complexity theory on NP-complete problems seems based on Turing machines, which are serial. How can the classifications be right for multiprocessors and other parallel machines?
a: First, NP-completeness is defined for problems, not algorithms. Get your terms straight before asking about parallel machines. Sigh.

subject: structure in DAG's
q: How can I formally recognise 'regular' DAGs, like the FFT, triangular solver, diamond or binary tree DAGs used for parallel algorithms? Are there criteria or general results about such graphs?
a: Regular structure is normally described by patterns or grammars, and for graphs that means graph grammars. Not much work exists on parsers for them. Look at the graph grammar workshops in Springer Lecture Notes in Computer Science, numbers 73, 153 and 291, and Brotsky's MIT thesis on parsing flow graphs. Do the reading.

subject: Info Request: LAWS OF FORM
q: Where can I find references on G. Spencer Brown's Laws of Form, especially its calculus applied to inference in computers?
a: Louis Kauffman devotes a section to Laws of Form in his book On Knots. That's the one pointer anybody gave, so go read it instead of asking the net to do your library work.

subject: Information request on a (possible) folk theorem
q: Where is the algorithm that determinizes, reverses arcs, and repeats for three conversions to give a minimal DFA documented? References?
a: The algorithm is given, without proof, in Beckman's Mathematical Foundations of Programming. A nice proof is in van de Snepscheut's Trace Theory and VLSI Design, which credits W. Peremans. It's the only handwritten LNCS volume, naturally.

subject: Lyapunov exponents
q: Is there any code or method other than Wolf's for finding Lyapunov exponents from a chaotic time series?
a: Not code, but references: Briggs, Phys. Lett. A 151 (1990) p. 27; Ellner et al., Phys. Lett. A 153 (1991) p. 357; Abarbanel, Brown and Kadtke, Phys. Lett. A 138 (1989) p. 401 and Phys. Rev. A 41 (1990) p. 1782. Go read them.

subject: bibliography
q: Any new bibliographical news out there in self-organizing systems research?
a: Subscribe to the Cybernetics and Systems mailing list, CYBSYS-L at BINGVMB.BITNET, by sending LISTSERV the single line SUB CYBSYS-L and your full name. That's where the current research is. Be more specific next time.

subject: Backing up AIX to a Sun tape drive -- can it be done?
q: I'm backing up an AIX box with rdump to an Exabyte on a Sun, using rdump 0unf csg:/dev/rst9 /dev/hd2. The tape rewinds and the data is corrupt on restore. What's wrong?
a: Read the manual. The BSD admin doc says the AIX v3 invocation is rdump -0 -unf csg:/dev/rst9 /dev/hd2, with a dash on the 0. And the Sun's bugs were fixed long ago, so suspect the AIX side.

subject: Serial-port -> Parallel printer
q: How can I connect a serial port on my XENIX box to a parallel-only printer? I don't have converters, so can I use special connector pins?
a: Buy a converter. Companies like Black Box make serial-to-parallel boxes, so check their catalog or call them. Wiring up special connector pins won't save you.

subject: NFS mounts over other files
q: Is it a bad idea to NFS-mount a filesystem over a directory that already has files in it, say /usr/lib/X11 so X can still start if the server is down?
a: No, it works. The files underneath are hidden and their disk space is wasted. Any open file blocks the mount, so users must exit X and leave the directory first. Hardly a mystery, though the manual never mentions it.

subject: Most commonly asked questions
q: Is there a file of most commonly asked questions for comp.unix.admin?
a: No. The closest thing is the comp.unix.questions FAQ posting. Nobody has bothered writing one for admin since the reorganization split it off. Feel free to volunteer, newcomer.

subject: Permissions needed to run 'su'
q: On our Sun 3/110 running 4.0.3, my ordinary account suddenly can't su to root, though my wheel group admin account can. What controls this?
a: Any BSD since 4.2 only lets members of the wheel group su to root. That's the whole mystery, and it's in the group file. Look at su2 if you want another account to get through. Read the man page next time.

subject: what is CERT?
q: What is CERT? I got a mail message from them and want to know who they are and where they get their info.
a: CERT is the Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Center, run out of the Software Engineering Institute at Carnegie Mellon in Pittsburgh. Advisories are on anonymous ftp from cert.sei.cmu.edu. And mail is trivially forged, so check before you trust it. Sigh.

subject: NTP - where?
q: Where can I find the source for NTP? I can't reach sunic.sunet.se because I don't have a nameserver running.
a: Grab louie.udel.edu:pub/ntp/xntp/xntp.tar.Z for the source and pub/ntp/clock.txt for the peer-picking instructions. Subscribe to comp.protocols.time.ntp for the discussion. Set up a nameserver while you're at it.

subject: WANTED: PNX (Unix) for a Three Rivers Computing Perq T-2
q: Where can I get PNX, the ICL Unix derivative, for a Three Rivers Perq T-2?
a: PNX is derived from 7th edition Unix, so you'd need a licence. Go ask ICL. And frankly, you won't like it much. Using PNX was no joy.

subject: Does anyone have nn running on IBM RS/6000?
q: Has anyone got nn running on an IBM RS/6000? What changes were needed, and which m- and s- header files did you use?
a: This belongs in the FAQ. No source changes needed: use m-vax.h and s-bsd4-3.h in config.h, and -Iconf -O -qnoro for CFLAGS. Make sure -lcurses is the only library when linking. That works for version 6.4 PL 4.

subject: X11R4 clients on AIX 3.1 (3003+) server
q: On AIX 3.1 with X11R4 clients, the twm menus show no selections until I mouse over them. Any hints?
a: Disable backing store. Add NoBackingStore to your .twmrc and the menus should draw properly. Sigh, the usual vendor X server breakage.

subject: Support for multiple C compilers
q: On an RS/6000 under AIX V3, what dependencies exist between the C compiler and the kernel if we want to build for older OS levels using separate compiler trees?
a: None between compiler and kernel. The dependencies are compiler to libc.a and libc.a to the kernel. Running a compiler on the same or later libc.a is fine, but an old libc.a on a back-level kernel will bite you. Use -I and -Z instead of chroot.

subject: Archive 2150s & Amiga UNIX?
q: Has anyone gotten an Archive 2150s tape drive working with an Amiga 3000 running UNIX?
a: Yes, but not well under Amix 1.0. Only QIC-120 tapes work and only one pass per tape, both fixed in 1.1. I write filesets from AmigaDOS and read them with dd to disk. Rebooting the kernel clears the problems. Beta software, what did you expect?

subject: NEC 5D (setting up)
q: I hooked a NEC 5D up to my A3000UX, but I only get 800x600 in X and standard overscan in AmigaDOS. What settings do I need to get 1024x1024 or 1280x1024?
a: You're confused. The stock Amiga display hardware only does NTSC-type resolutions, and the A2024 is a 4-level grey-scale trick at 10 or 15 Hz. For real 1Kx1K at 60Hz you need the A2410 TIGA board, which isn't out yet. Sigh.

subject: Unix rookie questions
q: On my Amiga Unix file server I have to type "share /mnt/amiga" after every boot. Is there a file I can put that command in so it runs automatically?
a: Put a line like "share -F nfs /mnt/amiga" in /etc/dfs/dfstab. It gets exported when the machine goes into networking mode. Do a "man dfstab" and read the R4 network admin guide for the gory details, as that's what manuals are for.

subject: Console Windows
q: When I log in to a Sun from the Amiga 3000 console windows, the terminal acts like a vt100 except the arrow keys don't work in vi. Can I make the console act just like a vt100, or tell the remote machine how to handle it?
a: Use ansi as the terminal type, it suits the Amiga Unix consoles better. Or infocmp your amiga terminfo entry and send it to the remote system. The real problem is the console keymap. Check /usr/amiga/lib/kmap and load one with sioc setkmap. And arrow keys in vi? Heresy.

subject: More questions on GCC for A/UX
q: Are the files in the gcc-1.35 A/UX binary distribution a complete build or just a stage, and how do I use them to rebuild gcc?
a: RTFM, or rather the README. It's a complete, ready-to-install stage3 build of gcc-1.35, because the native A/UX compiler's fixed-size tables choke on gcc. Put gcc in /usr/local/bin, the rest in /usr/local/lib, run sh config.gcc aux, then make CC=gcc install.

subject: Strange behaviour of Cnews rnews program on A/UX 1.1
q: Cnews rnews on A/UX 1.1 runs spacefor fine for thirteen batches, then fails silently on the fourteenth and rejects the batch. Raising MAXUP didn't help. What's going on?
a: Something is eating a resource and never giving it back. My guess is uuxqt opens the X. file and never closes it, so each child has fewer descriptors left until the spacefor pipeline can't open any. Old uucp had bugs like that. Change the per-process descriptor limit and see if the failure point moves.

subject: M.O. disks
q: Do magneto-optical disks work with A/UX 2.0, and do they need a special driver?
a: Seems so. A Microtech OR650 disk mounts fine as an A/UX file system, even dp partitions it, but it must be sectored at 512 bytes, not 1024. For HFS volumes you might need an INIT, which ships with the drive. Read the manual.

subject: AUX and XWindows
q: Does X-Windows on A/UX with a one-button mouse make you wince? Is there any way to make it usable?
a: The mouse button acts as the left button. The left and right arrow keys generate the center and right buttons. That makes it a lot more usable, if you'd read the docs before whining.

subject: Another A/UX question, re: rn
q: Does the A/UX distribution come with rn, and how easy is it to get running? Also, do Hayes-compatible modems work as dial-in devices?
a: No rn in the box, but it's very easy. Larry Wall's Configure script makes it compile on almost anything; type Configure, answer the questions, make. Modems are a mess: Microcom 2400 and 9600 work in AT dumb mode, smart mode is still broken, and carrier loss won't kill the shell. Sigh.

subject: dump.bsd & bad sblock magic number - Please Help!!
q: Dumping / with dump.bsd to a SyQuest cartridge gives "bad sblock magic number", and fsstat says the filesystem state is bad even though fsck is clean. What's wrong?
a: Use the raw device, like /dev/rdsk/c0d0s0 or wherever your root lives, instead of the name /. The problem only shows up when dumping root. Seen it before; it's a silly quirk.

subject: Anyone got NNTP/news running on A/UX and want to share it ?
q: Has anyone got NNTP news running on A/UX 1.x? Are there diffs needed?
a: No diffs needed. Run the included configuration scripts and install it as you would on a Berkeley-like system. It works fine on A/UX 1.1. Funny how reading the instructions solves things.

subject: 24bit vs 32bit
q: How does A/UX tell if an application is 32 bit clean? I get a crash warning on many applications that run fine, so how do I disable the warning for one I've tested?
a: The warning shows when the app lacks the 32BitCompatible flag in its SIZE resource. Set the flag with ResEdit, or use /mac/bin/changesize. No magic, no AI, whatever the marketing says.

subject: MODEM problems
q: I can't get my Hayes 2400 modem to work with A/UX; I get no device at 2400 baud even after changing inittab. Why?
a: Typical when the modem sits on the serial port running AppleTalk. Disable AppleTalk with the command in section 1M of the manual, or comment out its startup script in /etc/startup, or rebuild the kernel without it. Read the man pages.

subject: Timout errors
q: I get frequent SCSI timeout errors on the external Apple drive on a Mac II running A/UX 1.0 with an internal Quantum drive. Is this normal, and how can I reduce it?
a: Older Quantum drives, up to drive ROM level F, have bugs that cause exactly this. Only a ROM upgrade from Quantum fixes it. As for memory, a full ethernet/tcp/ip/NFS config with lots of NBUFs eats 3-4MB, so quit wondering. See kconfig(1).

subject: Questions about AU/X
q: I'm considering A/UX for my Mac II. What's in the 6000 page manuals that isn't on-line, can I run Usenet and add serial ports, and do third-party tape drives work?
a: The on-line stuff is just the man pages; the manuals add the Berkeley and System V books plus A/UX material. News should work since A/UX is SVR2, and uucp is already there. Add ports with 4-port AST or SuperMac cards. No tape drives are supported yet. Patience.

subject: MPW C++ under A/UX?
q: Is MPW C++ available under A/UX, or did I dream the press release saying MPW tools would work there?
a: You didn't dream it. Apple's A/UX Developer's Tools 1.0 press release lists MPW, MPW C++, MPW C, the assembler and Object Pascal under Macintosh OS tools, plus C++ for A/UX (beta). Read your press releases.

subject: MacApp->C++->A/UX
q: Is there a MacApp using C++ that I can use under A/UX instead of Object Pascal? If it's coming, when, and if not, why not?
a: Slight misconception. A/UX cc makes COFF files, while MPW tools make MPW object format. MacApp 3.0 uses a PascalObject base class so Pascal and C++ link with the MPW linker, which has nothing to do with A/UX. Only select developers have the alpha; real soon now.

subject: Rapidly degrading performance under A/UX?
q: My Mac IIcx under A/UX 2.0 slowed to a crawl overnight and the disk grinds. How can I tell what's going on, when vmstat and iostat don't exist?
a: Run swap -l to see how many blocks are swapped out. If it's bogged down, shut down, and once in single user mode, issue init 2 to bring it back up. That helps, though it doesn't cure it, I'm afraid. Welcome to A/UX.

subject: trouble with 2.0.1 ftp upgrade
q: Running shutdown from the command shell under A/UX 2.0.1 ends with an "enter run level" prompt and then logs me out. How do I get A/UX into single user mode?
a: Single user is "init s", not shutdown, which unmounts all your filesystems. Log in as root on the Console Emulator, sync a few times, run init s, wait a minute, then run killall and answer s if it asks for a run level. Basic stuff.

subject: fsck of root partition won't work
q: We ran fsck on / and got LINK COUNT TABLE OVERFLOW, CONTINUE? If we answer yes it just prints the same message again, and if we answer no it quits. What is wrong?
a: Keep answering 'y'. It'll eventually finish, then reboot and do it all over again, and after about six rounds it clears up. Run fsck from sash so you skip relaunching A/UX every cycle. Tedious, sure, but that's what you get.

subject: Free disk space that isn't there!
q: df as root shows over 10,000 free blocks on /usr, but as a normal user it shows 0, and I get out of disk space errors. Why is there free space only root can see but can't use?
a: Berkeley file systems reserve a 'dead zone' on each partition, a safety margin so the disk doesn't fill beyond a safe level. Older versions handled full file systems badly. Any idiot who read the FFS docs knows this.

subject: Cray YMP instruction timings?
q: How many clock cycles do scalar integer compare, add, and multiply and single precision multiply take on a Cray YMP, and where can I find similar timings?
a: There's no integer compare, just subtract. Scalar integer add/sub takes 3 clocks. 48 bit integer multiply uses the floating multiplier, and floating multiply is 8 clocks. For the rest, read the Symbolic Machine Instructions Reference, SR-0085B, from OSC.

subject: Get weird run time error when porting C code to Cray. Help!
q: My C program ported to a Cray X-MP running UNICOS compiles fine but dies with an "operand range error" that jumps around when I comment out code. Any ideas?
a: My first guess is your heap isn't big enough. Make any large arrays static and see what happens, which gets them off the heap. Also, the latest 6.x UNICOS libraries cause trouble with multitasking. Tough to debug, as usual.

subject: 386/ix V2.0.2 breaks awk
q: After upgrading 386/ix from 2.0.1 to 2.0.2, nawk became the standard awk and my script with the pattern ! /foo/ || /bar/ now gives a syntax error. Is this AT&T's or ISC's bug?
a: I saw the same on a 3B2 with vanilla SVR3.2, so it's AT&T's bug, fixed in SVR4.0. Meanwhile write it as $0 !~ /foo|bar/ and use print instead of printf, which is expensive. Sigh.

subject: AIX tty line sharing
q: Can AIX share a serial port for both dialin logins and uucp dialouts, the way SCO Xenix disables the line automatically when dialing out?
a: Yes, from AIX 2.2.1 on. 2.2 sort of worked, badly. Specify "share" for "ae" and "remote (modem)" for "dvam" in the devices command. Then use /dev/ttyx for incoming and /dev/lttyx for outgoing. Not hard.

subject: ESIX and X windows
q: Can ESIX X windows run on a Hercules adapter, and which mice does it support in Rev C? Will an ATI VGA Wonder work?
a: Rev C does NOT work with Hercules; only EGA and VGA, from 640x480 up to 1024x768 depending on the card. It supports Logitech bus and serial and Microsoft bus mice, with serial on tty00 and tty01 only. The ATI is untested but reportedly works at 640x480. Also, buy more RAM.

subject: uucp and Interactive 1-2 user license
q: Can I connect 4 or 5 uucp lines to Interactive Unix 386 with a 1-2 user license without buying more users? The lines would be for uucp only, not user logins.
a: Calling out on multiple lines is no problem. But ISC's user limit can't tell UUCP from user logins, so you can't have them all dialing in at once without subverting the limit. Whether they meant to forbid that is unclear. Vendors never write a clear policy.

subject: Vertical mounting of SCSI drives?
q: Can an Imprimis half-height 300 MB SCSI drive be mounted vertically, on its side? I know ST-506 drives can, but low-level formatting seems pointless on SCSI.
a: Sure. I've run plenty of Maxtor SCSI drives on their sides with no trouble, and yours should be fine too. Just format it in the position it'll live in. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: looking for problem reports with Unix or VP/ix on Micronics plus...
q: Does UNIX have problems on Micronics 25 or 33 MHz cache motherboards, and which ESDI controller is best?
a: You NEED Phoenix BIOS 10.10 and 100ns RAM or faster, since slow memory sometimes ships. Booting breaks if the video BIOS shadowing switch is moved. ESIX SysV 3.2 Rev C works fine. Use a fast controller: the WD is poor at 33 MHz, the Adaptec is fine.

subject: Chips in a Bell HUB card?
q: Does the Bell Tech HUB card use 16450 chips for serial I/O? Can I put 16550s in it and use Jim Murray's asy driver?
a: They're not 16550s, probably 8250s, and they're soldered in, so pulling them out would be a grade-A pain. Even if you swapped them, $195 plus $20 a chip puts you near the price of the cheaper smart cards. Do the arithmetic first.

subject: GNU Emacs deletes file without warning under ISC UNIX V.3.0.1
q: GNU Emacs under ISC UNIX V.3.0.1 seems to delete my Rec.humor.funn file when it saves it in Babyl format. Why does the original vanish?
a: Emacs makes a backup called rec.humor.funn~, which is 15 characters. System V truncates that to 14, so the backup name is the original file and it gets clobbered. Use shorter filenames, or a real OS. That 14-character limit is ancient brain damage.

subject: Anyone get GNU G++ 1.36.0 up on 386/ix v2.0.2???
q: Has anyone gotten GNU G++ 1.36.0 running on 386/ix v2.0.2? The link fails with unresolved externals for start, data_start and getpagesize.
a: Take the 1.35.1 COFF patches and apply the needed changes by hand, carefully. Your link errors say you haven't made the necessary changes to the crt0.c code. There's also a sysv patch to libg++. Get both from prep or tut.

subject: Prodigy on VPIX?
q: Has anyone gotten Prodigy to work on a 386 running VPIX? On a Sun 386i it dies trying to dial out through the modem.
a: It doesn't work on VP/ix, and Prodigy support stops talking to you once they hear you run it. My guess is they don't want it on anything that could capture their stuff. Typical vendor attitude.

subject: non AT&T mouse on 6386
q: Has anyone put a non-AT&T mouse on a 6386 running Unix 3.2? My Microsoft bus mouse on IRQ 2 or 3 shows Open Look but the cursor doesn't move or click.
a: The AT&T mouse is just a Logitech bus mouse. A Microsoft bus mouse works only if it's the old style card with the UART onboard. The newer InPort one has a specialized chip UNIX doesn't like. Expect trouble with only two buttons under OpenLook too.

subject: adding bad blocks using 386/ix
q: How do I add bad blocks to a SCSI drive on a 1542 controller under 386/ix? mkpart -A gives "No root partition" and I still get errors.
a: Why are you adding bad blocks to a SCSI drive at all? SCSI drives handle bad blocks internally and present an error-free face to the bus. If you're seeing errors, suspect the drive itself, not the partition table. Sigh.

subject: 386/ix 2.0.2 + PS/80 + WD8003ET/A = ?
q: How do I get TCP/IP running under 386/ix 2.0.2 on a PS/2 80 with a Western Digital WD8003ET/A card? The stock driver seems not to support the Micro Channel board.
a: Our problem was the board: we had the newer WD8003E/A, not the older WD8003ET/A. 386/ix's driver just hangs on it. We swapped in a WD8003ET/A and TCP/IP ran smoothly. Check the card revision before blaming the software.

subject: virtterm.c for bnews
q: How do I get virtterm.c from bnews to compile under 386/ix? Adding an include for sys/ptem.h didn't fix it.
a: Add #undef TIOCGWINSZ after the includes at the top of virtterm.c. It's a kludge, but it works. Or tweak the Makefile to skip virtterm entirely, since only vnews uses it and readnews works fine without it.

subject: Tape retensioning
q: How do I retension a tape under ISC 386/ix 2.0.2? The Xenix 'tape reten' command isn't there, and the man page only covers the driver.
a: RTFM, specifically the permuted index. Look up "tape" and you'll find tapecntl, which does retension, erase, reset, rewind and positioning. Works for QIC-150 too, since the ioctls are the same. No need to write a C program for that. Sigh.

subject: SCSI Tape on 386ix
q: I configured a SCSI tape on my 386ix with an Adaptec 1542 and the kernel builds, but there are no tape nodes in /dev. How do I get them?
a: kconfig does everything except create the /dev nodes, so you make them yourself with mknod. For a primary SCSI controller, /dev/ntape is c 41 0 and /dev/tape is c 41 8. Secondary uses 64 and 72. Don't kludge major numbers by hand, for crying out loud.

subject: Computone Problems??
q: I installed a Computone 4 port board on Interactive 2.0.2, and once a getty is respawning it cannot be killed, not even with kill -9. Any suggestions?
a: Classic driver bug. The driver calls sleep() and doesn't check whether the wakeup was due to an interrupt. A signal wakes it, it sees the resource still isn't available, and goes back to sleep. Blame the driver author.

subject: (s)RAM CACHES: WORTH IT?
q: Is a 64KB SRAM cache worth it on a 33MHz 386 running Unix? Can Unix even use it, given 80ns RAM and one wait state?
a: Cache will solve most of the problems, and makes a big improvement with slow memory. Even 16-bit memory ends up only 15-20% slower than 32-bit instead of 60% or so. The hardware does it, Unix needn't care. On a 486 with burst mode, don't bother.

subject: heretical SCO Open Desktop question
q: Is any third-party vendor planning to port Open Look to SCO's version of X in Open Desktop? I dislike Motif.
a: My guess is Open Look arrives on SCO with SVR4, same story at INTERACTIVE. To get it today you'd have to switch to AT&T's X. Motif has solid technical faults, and Open Look has Sun and AT&T behind it, though IBM's RISC boxes argue otherwise.

subject: tar & ulimit are pissing me off.
q: On Bell Tech Unix, ULIMIT stops me receiving files over 2 meg by uucp, and tar gives directory checksum errors on the gcc archive. How do I fix this?
a: ulimit is a Bourne shell builtin, RTFM. Raise the ULIMIT tunable and rebuild the kernel. Skip the temp file: zcat the archive into tar through a pipe. Your cat of the pieces used > and overwrote itself; use >> so you don't end up with just part 10.

subject: Console & Mouse Problems
q: On a 386 UNIX box, kernel messages to the console wreck my graphics. How can I stop the kernel sending messages to the console?
a: Do what most X servers do and switch to one of the VTs for your graphics. Console error messages don't appear on a VT. Don't go symlinking /dev/console to /dev/null like a newbie.

subject: Sendmail + Sites with names in uppercase = Argh!
q: Sendmail lowercases UPPERCASE uucp host names, so mail to user@SITE.uucp fails as unknown host "site". How can I fix it without breaking HDB uucp?
a: Add the "h" flag to F= in your uux mailer entry in sendmail.cf, which tells sendmail not to case-fold host names. Sigh, it'd be simpler if the vendor shipped sendmail.cf documentation. Naming machines in uppercase is asking for it.

subject: make(1)
q: Shouldn't make(1) be compiled so that -d works? Make -p isn't enough to debug my mistakes, and I found -d broken in Microport 3.0e and ISC 2.0.2.
a: Someone tried make -nd under ISC 2.0.2 and it worked fine. So what's the complaint? Sounds like an axe to grind rather than a bug. Check before you flame the vendor.

subject: X11 previewer
q: Where can I get X11 for 386/ix?
a: From Interactive, of course, or from the dealer or distributor you got the rest of the system from. If you mean the distribution source, that's MIT. Is this a serious question? Sigh.

subject: Xwindows on ISC, SCO, ESIX
q: Who has X Windows working between different 386 UNIX systems like SCO, ISC and ESIX, or with Sun and DEC? Does it work with one as client and another as server?
a: Yes, it works fine. An ISC 386 server with an SCO ODT client over thin ethernet worked like a shot. Reversed it left garbage, since the ISC box only had a Hercules screen. Other mixes with DEC and Sun work, but limited resolution or colors bite.

subject: Why no job control in 386/ix?
q: Why does the C-shell included with 386/ix, a System V UNIX for 386 boxes, have no job control? Is the kernel missing something, or was ISC too lazy to implement it?
a: Job control is a BSDism that never made it into vanilla System V, and it needs kernel support the 386/ix kernel doesn't have. csh relies on the Berkeley stop and continue signals. SVR4.0 is supposed to have it. Learn your Unix history.

subject: Question about IPC900 ports
q: Why is the modular wiring scheme on the IPC 900 card so different from the 3B2 and the ACE card? Does anybody know the story?
a: The pinout is identical to the DataKit wiring, so it's not totally off the wall. Not what you'd call friendly to the 3B2 crowd, but there's the reason.

subject: SVR4 HDB uucp G protocol and file recovery
q: Does anyone have a description of the G protocol in SVR4 HDB uucp, and how does file recovery work with it?
a: There's a full document on g protocol in a Unix archive. G is just g with packet and window size configurable from a file in /etc/uucp. Recovery is the same: the file is deleted only after a successful transfer. Or read the O'Reilly UUCP book.

subject: IPC keys
q: How do you choose System V IPC keys for msgget, shmget and semget so they don't collide with other vendors' software? Is there a standard key management scheme?
a: There's a hack based on device and inode numbers, but it's just a hack. SysV IPC was never meant as a general facility. It came from a special-purpose application moving to a generic kernel, and USDL stuck it in. Now you know.

subject: hiding files under a mount point.
q: If you mount a filesystem over a directory with files in it, they become invisible. Can this be exploited to hide files securely from mortals?
a: No, they can't be used until you umount the filesystem. We lost ages to a kernel copy backed up into an unmounted /tmp eating root disk space. Take heed, it's a trap, not a security feature.

subject: Scheduling of processes, and timers
q: My profiler uses sigitimer and ptrace to interrupt a process and copy its stack, but it gets scheduled mostly during system calls like ioctl, and the timer is only 100Hz on a Sparc 2. Is scheduling likely at system calls, and is there another timer?
a: Yes, scheduling happens at system calls, and no, you can't avoid it without major kernel changes. Probably just use gprof, or profil(2). The hardware counts microseconds. The limit is kernel software. SparcStations have a separate, faster profiling clock, but you need kernel source.

subject: Where is c.u.wizards ?
q: What happened to comp.unix.wizards? I thought comp.unix.internals was going to be renamed.
a: You'd know if you followed news.groups. The vote said remove c.u.internals, but the meta-voters wanted to keep it, and the control messages died when the feed had problems. Some sites also rewrite the aliased group name. Sigh.

subject: YASQ: ksh in 2.4 has forgotten about history
q: After installing Microport 2.4, ksh forgot about history on root's login only. ^P just rings the bell and /history stays empty. What did I forget?
a: Put HISTFILE=/.history and export HISTFILE in root's .profile. Apparently for root it doesn't use the default ~/.history. Why, who knows; ksh quirks, what else is new.

subject: ROM disk [ was Re: RAM disk ]
q: Could you build a transportable, shake-proof UNIX box with the root partition on a ROM disk, by modifying a RAM-disk driver? Can UNIX boot off a ROM disk?
a: It's been done. HP sold a portable called the Integral PC with most of the UNIX utilities in ROM, though it looked like a niche product. Some Toshiba DOS laptops like the T1000 keep DOS in ROM too. Hardly a new idea, kid.

subject: CLOCK PROBLEMS II
q: Did my Microport SysV system gain or lose an hour and make 'at' jobs fail with 'too late' on April 29th? Does SysV handle daylight savings itself?
a: Microport lists DST handling as a known bug in the release notes, blamed on federal law changes. My 3.0e box lost an hour that Sunday too, so that's when it thinks DST ends. SysV is supposed to track DST. Supposed to.

subject: Using sadp on uport V/386 3.0e
q: Has anyone got sadp working on uPort V/386 3.0e? It always just prints its usage no matter what device name I give.
a: You aren't doing anything wrong. A 386/ix vendor reported it's broken in the AT&T distribution, and it's also broken under uPort SysV/AT 2.3, as is sar -d. So much for disk tuning. Typical.

subject: 2.4 process size, how ?
q: How do I configure the process size on Microport 2.4? Is it set on the fly like ulimit or globally at boot time?
a: Run patch /system5 mmpatch with the size, then reboot. It does rudimentary checks that you have enough swap, so a very large size may mean reconfiguring your disk. It's a boot-time patch, not ulimit, so quit guessing.

subject: Help needed with using 'asy' with interrupts 9 & 10
q: How do I make interrupts 9 and 10 on the second PIC work with the async device driver under SYS/AT 2.3? Interrupts 3, 4 and 5 work, but on 9 and 10 the line opens and only the first character goes out before it hangs.
a: Set the fourth interrupt value in asy_conf.h to 0x0a before compiling asy.c. And the stock Microport asy.o is hard wired to 3, 4, 5 and 7, so don't bother with it. Typical vendor limitation.

subject: is microport alive or dead?
q: Is Microport still in business? I know they were in Chapter 11. If they came out of it, is anybody selling their stuff?
a: Yes, they're still in Santa Cruz selling product. A Sacramento company bought them just last week and plans to put money into them. Try keeping up with the net before declaring things dead.

subject: VGA with Microport?
q: Microport said uport '286 Unix works with the IBM VGA adapter, but it doesn't seem to. Does anyone have patches to make it work, and when does Microport plan to support it?
a: Microport says VGA cards aren't supported at present. Their console driver works with the IBM EGA card, and apparently somebody heard it wrong over the phone. Support for IBM VGA and register-compatible cards is planned, with no date. Typical vendor vapor.

subject: telebit on uBug 286 - update
q: My Telebit on a Microport 286 UNIX box gets 9600 bps until anything else uses another serial line, then throughput collapses. Why, and does anyone have interrupt-driven serial driver sources?
a: Nearly all Unix sio drivers are interrupt driven already, with a few arcane exceptions. The real problem is critical code elsewhere in the kernel, where interrupts are disabled while it drops its pants. Keeping those sections short takes serious kernel hacking. Sigh.

subject: microport mail(x) program
q: On Microport with its AT&T-style mail, how can I feed every received mail item to a program for a mailserver? Is there an internet-style mailer for System V/386?
a: Get smail, a smart mailer that handles internet addresses and gives you /usr/lib/aliases. Add lmail, a replacement for local delivery that does mail to programs. Elm replaces mailx. That combo works on V/286 and V/386. Don't reinvent the wheel.

subject: V/AT 286 help with vi and jove
q: On V/AT 286 2.3.0 with an EGA card, vi and JOVE show odd extra characters, random cursor movement, stray words, and blank lines, though normal command output is fine. What have I done? Should I reinstall?
a: No reinstall needed. I'd suspect the ANSI terminfo file for the console, or bugs in the console driver's ANSI handling. Upgrading to 2.4 cured the stray words for me, and a dumb pessimistic ANSI terminfo helped. Sigh, vendors.

subject: Microport 386 keyboard strangeness
q: On my Microport SysV/386 with a 101-key keyboard, the right-hand Alt and Ctrl keys are reversed. Anyone seen this, and is there a fix?
a: Use the cons(1M) utility. Run cons rawkey to see your scancodes, then cons swapkey 96 97, or whatever numbers fit your keyboard. Reading the man page would've saved you the post.

subject: Pathalias failing on Sys V/AT with much input
q: Pathalias fails on Sys V/AT on a 286 with the message 'Out of memory' when given more than a trivial amount of input, even with the large model. Is this common?
a: Yes. Pathalias needs lots of memory and expects it contiguous. One site ran it on a 286 with disk-based hacks, and it took about eight hours for the North American maps. A 386 handles it fine, in about five minutes. Quit torturing the 286.

subject: GNU 18.52 movemail problem
q: Running GNU Emacs 18.52 on Microport Unix, rmail gives "Movemail: error making lockfile". How can I fake movemail out or get mail locking it will respect?
a: It's a permissions problem, nothing more. movemail can't create its lock file in /usr/mail, which is 775 root, group mail. Run ~emacs/etc/movemail setgid mail and it can write its locks. Worked fine for a year on SysV R2. Think before you blame the OS.

subject: Running out of swap space in V/AT
q: Since my newsfeed started sending compressed news, uncompress eats lots of memory and I run out of swap on my V/AT. The system hangs in a perpetual swap state with unkillable zombies. Any fix besides a bigger swap partition?
a: Nope. Only fix I know is to make the swap partition bigger. I bumped mine to 8000 blocks and haven't had the problem in nine months. Sixteen-bit decompress is a pig on a small box, so don't run memory hogs next to it.

subject: missing 384K on V/386
q: Where did the missing 384K go on a 386 with 2MB? 386/ix reports 1703936 bytes, not 1664K plus the rest. Is it shadow RAM, and can the kernel use it?
a: It depends on the hardware's address decoding. Some machines remap the memory to start at 1 meg, while others lose 384K because the area is mapped to ROM and video RAM. On some it lurks at 0xE00000, enabled in 16K or 64K chunks. Don't touch it blindly.

subject: 3780 protocol
q: Does anyone know of a package, commercial or public, that supports the 3780 protocol on Unix?
a: NCR has a BSC 2780/3780 product for its Unix boxes, though their SNA RJE product is nicer. Rabbit Software makes well-regarded Unix/IBM integration stuff too. Whatever you buy needs a SYNCHRONOUS serial port, so check your hardware first.

subject: how are password encryped?
q: How are Unix passwords encrypted? The same password looks different in the password file each time I set it, so how can that even work?
a: Would you trust a password scheme you could figure out? Read crypt(3C) and crypt(3X) for the short discussion of DES encryption. Go read the manual before posting.

subject: Default Libraries using cc
q: How do I make cc on machine B use the libraries, includes and ld from Interactive's development package on machine A, NFS-mounted, without passing -Y flags every time?
a: Use gencc, in /bin on the machine with the SDS. Read its man page. It builds a cc front end with the new defaults, and you put that in your local path. Interactive's support couldn't tell you? Figures.

subject: ftp text conversion
q: I wrecked non-text files by ftp'ing them without the binary command, and the conversion didn't change the file lengths. What conversion happened, and can it be reversed?
a: Depends on the two OSes, which you didn't name. Usually newlines get converted, with CR LF as the standard. Sometimes it's reversible, sometimes not. Best tip: ftp the files back to the same or a similar system. Next time, type binary.

subject: man page suffixes?
q: I'm trying to isolate the X commands' man pages by naming them with an X suffix, like xterm.1X, but man can no longer find them even though it finds v and g suffixes. Are suffixes hard-coded into man?
a: Yes, very often. The sections, subsections, directories and man trees are frequently all or mostly hard-wired into man. Next time say which flavor of UNIX you're running, since that matters. A replacement man that isn't hard-wired can be had by FTP from tut.cis.ohio-state.edu.

subject: Can anyone make helpful suggestion?
q: In dbxtool on a Sun 3/60 I get BUS and SEGV signals in a function at a line of my C program. What causes this and how do I find it?
a: Look at the line it names. Most likely a pointer there points to an invalid address. Use the where command to see how you got there, and print the variables on that line. Still lost, trace with printf. Debugging 101, sigh.

subject: How to change an RCS log message ?
q: How do I change an RCS log message after checking in a file with the wrong one, short of editing the RCS file itself?
a: Use rcs -t file instead of checking in and out. Wait, that's the description, not the log message. It will prompt you for a description like when you created the RCS entry. Read the man page.

subject: Program Preprocessor?
q: I need a program preprocessor to substitute some Fortran calls for calls on a new machine when porting. Should I write it in C or awk, or has someone already done this?
a: If it's only simple substitution, use a sed script. Neither awk nor C is worth the bother. Sigh, people reach for the big tools way too fast.

subject: printing underlined text
q: Is it possible to print underlined text using printf() in C, and how?
a: This belongs in comp.lang.c. printf("Underlined text\015__________ ____\n") works on any ASCII printing terminal, using carriage return and overstrike. For CRTs you have to get hardware-specific or use termcap.

subject: Reading termcap database other than termcap
q: My program reads printcap with the termcap routines, but the file location comes from an environment variable. Can I set the file to be read from inside the program without breaking other programs?
a: Call putenv("TERMCAP=/etc/printcap") before using the termcap routines. Mind you, you mean TERMCAP, not TERM. TERM is the terminal type. Any child process you spawn will inherit that setting, so don't be surprised.

subject: Best way to determine originating host (rlogin/telnet)
q: What's the best way to determine the host a person remotely logged in from, like the Where field in finger? Do I have to plow through the wtmp file?
a: You mean utmp, not wtmp. How do you think finger does it? Read utmp, or if you want it faster than finger, just use who. Think a little.

subject: File Ownership Info ?
q: Where is file ownership and permission info actually stored? Is it in the first few bytes of the file?
a: No. It lives in the inode, along with the owner numbers and permission bits. You don't need to know that anyway; use stat(2) or lstat(2) to get ownership and permissions. This comes up every week.

subject: Changing Passwords From A Batch File
q: Can I change a user's password from a batch file by redirecting input to passwd? We're on SunOS 4.1 and want a cron job to reset about 40 temporary accounts.
a: You're root, so write your own program to edit the passwd file, though if you can't encrypt a password or avoid security holes, don't. Otherwise grab Dan Bernstein's pty package and pipe the new password twice into pty passwd username. Don't pass passwords on a command line, ps shows them.

subject: SCO junks long newsgroup names
q: Cnews on SCO UNIX can't link articles for newsgroups with names longer than 14 characters. Will the rest of my newsbatch still be posted, and is there a fix?
a: Articles are processed independently, so one failure won't affect the others. Nothing is planned in C News. Work around it by creating a short-named group and aliasing the long one to it with an equals sign in the active file. Lock the news system first, and blame SCO's filesystem.

subject: Does tail still need the 4K byte limit?
q: Does tail still need its 4K byte limit? Is it fixed in SVR4 or 4.3BSD, and has anyone written a public domain tail?
a: The limit is long obsolete. A trace on SunOS 4.0.1 shows tail reading the last 32K. And the GNU tail and head, written by me and Paul Rubin, have no buffer size limits at all, and GNU head is much faster than the BSD one. They're not yet widely distributed, but I'll mail them out.

subject: 4.2BSD / System V ioctl questions
q: How can CBREAK and no-echo be emulated in System V, and are there stty and gtty-like calls there?
a: RTFM, TERMIO(7). Disable ICANON, keep ISIG, set VMIN to 1 and VTIME to 0, and clear all four ECHO flags, via ioctl with TCSETA or TCSETAW. Old gtty and stty may exist, but they have no CBREAK bit. Avoid them.

subject: Allowing users to remove files in /usr/spool/at
q: How can I let users cancel their own at jobs in /usr/spool/at when only root can write to that directory, without opening the directory to the world or writing a setuid program?
a: You don't need setuid at all. Users own their at files, so have a script just empty the file. The daemon runs the empty job and deletes it. On BSD, at needs only write permission on the spool directory, so setgid to the directory's group does it. System V has at -r anyway.

subject: How do I tell if STDIN is a PIPE?
q: How can a C program tell whether stdin is coming from a pipe? lseek and fseek don't work on a pipe, so how should I seek on one?
a: Just try the seek. If lseek fails with errno ESPIPE, stdin is a pipe. As for seeking forward, getchar() reads binary bytes just fine, so a loop of it works. Whoever told you otherwise didn't read the manual.

subject: Accessing a VAX tape drive from a Sun 3
q: How can my Sun 3 running SunOS 3.5 use the 9-track tape drive on a VAX 785 running Ultrix over Ethernet, so the Sun treats it as its own drive?
a: Simplest is the remote tape facility, /etc/rmt, see the man page in section 8. You have to recompile your program to talk to the VAX rmt. No source and no alternate device name? You're out of luck. A pseudo-tape kernel driver is far from trivial.

subject: EBCDIC to ASCII conversion under ULTRIX
q: How do I convert an EBCDIC file to ASCII under ULTRIX? Is there a command or public domain program?
a: RTFM. dd does it: dd conv=ascii <infile >outfile. There are several flavors of EBCDIC though, so dd's table may not be 100% what you want, but it should be close. This comes up every week.

subject: changing TAB's to newlines?
q: I have a file of names separated by TABs and NEWLINES. How can I get the names one per line? Is there a sed regexp like s/TAB/\n/?
a: Use tr -s '\011' '\012'. The -s squeezes repeats so you don't get blank lines. Sed can't do a newline in the replacement the way you wanted, so quit hand-editing files, for crying out loud.

subject: Are pointers in a shared memory segment valid for a different process?
q: If two processes attach the same shared memory segment with shmat() at different addresses, are pointers stored in the segment invalid for the other process? Is there an accepted way to handle it?
a: Yes, you're right, pointers break if the segment maps at different addresses. Storing offsets is clumsy. The usual fix is to have both programs attach the segment at the same address, well above where either will grow. Any idiot knows this one.

subject: help with signals (ultrix)
q: On AT&T Unix a system call like read fails when a signal arrives, but on Sun and Ultrix it restarts. On the Sun I can use siginterrupt to make it fail. How do I make the system call fail under Ultrix 1.2?
a: Hack it with setjmp and longjmp. Put a setjmp around the call, and have the signal handler longjmp back to it. Take the handler down afterward, or you'll longjmp to the same spot on every signal. Ugly, but that's Ultrix for you.

subject: SUN to Metheus ethernet connect
q: Our Suns share an ethernet with a Metheus 4.1BSD machine. We put each other in /etc/hosts, but rlogin hangs and times out. Could the '200' in our 192.9.200.nnn network number be the problem?
a: Sounds like your 4.1 box doesn't answer ARP requests. Add the ARP table entry for it by hand on the Sun; read the arp man page. The network number isn't your trouble. Sigh, check the basics before blaming the address.

subject: What is it? (was Re: Current Run-Level: How can you tell?)
q: What is a run-level on Unix? I use a Sun and have never heard of it.
a: BSD has basically single-user, multi-user and halt. System V has many levels: 0 is halt and 3 is normal multi-user mode. Beyond that I'm hazy, so go read the manual instead of asking the net.

subject: A question on awk and sort.
q: awk and sort choke on files with records longer than their maximum length. Is there a command line option to raise the maximum record length?
a: No option, so stop hunting through man pages. Get gawk, the GNU awk, which has no silly restrictions. Or run the script through a2p and use perl, which has no line length limit and has its own sort, or use the new SysV sort if you have it.

subject: zsh question?
q: Has anyone ported zsh 2.00.01 to System V R3? Also, in an alias how do I include the filename from the command line?
a: Nobody's done the SysV port yet, as far as I know. It doesn't compile there. And you can't use command-line arguments in an alias, same as ksh or bash. Use a shell function instead. RTFM.

subject: command substitution
q: How can I nest backquote command substitution in one line, like basename of an awk output, in csh?
a: In sh, backslash the inner backquotes. In csh it can't be done, because the internals assume backquote expansion goes one level deep; use two statements. Better yet, just do it all in awk with substr and index. Also, your csh syntax was wrong.

subject: Matching words in regular expressions
q: How can I search an input stream for a word held in a shell variable, matching only lines where it appears as a whole word and not as part of another word?
a: Easy with grep: pipe to grep '\<'$VAR'\>' and you're done. Perl does it too with \b around the variable, if you must. Either breaks if the variable has metacharacters, but that wasn't in your spec. Read the man page next time.

subject: sh vars in awk scripts??
q: How can I use an sh environment variable inside an awk script, like user=me; awk '{ print $1, ${user} }' .rhosts?
a: Pass it on the command line as an awk assignment: awk '{print $1, user}' user="$user" .rhosts. Awk then sees it as a variable. This should be in a FAQ somewhere. Or break out of the single quotes, if you like fragile hacks.

subject: csh args
q: How does one pass more than two args to csh aliases, other than the !^, !* and !$ mechanisms?
a: Use the !:n syntax, escaped in the alias, like alias swap echo \!:2 \!:1. That pseudo-history mechanism is the only way to pass arguments besides taking them all intact. Very kludgy, and it's a shame csh has no shell functions.

subject: Need help
q: I can't print from one of my machines, so I wrote a csh script that copies the file, rlogs into another machine, prints, and returns. The script stops executing after the rlogin. How can I do this?
a: Quit rlogin-ing, that's what stops your script. Just pipe it: cat the file into rsh machinename with the print command and options. It works as long as the hosts.equiv files let the machines talk to each other. Dumb idea indeed.

subject: for loops
q: In sh, how can I do a BASIC-style for loop that runs $FILES times, where $FILES is a number?
a: The sh for loop only walks a list of words. For counting, use a while loop that tests the counter with [ ] and -ne, and decrement it with FILES=`expr $FILES - 1` each pass. Look up expr(1) before asking next time.

subject: Positional parameters beyond $9
q: In the Bourne shell, how do I directly access positional parameters beyond $9? $10 gives a0 and ${10} gives bad substitution.
a: You can't. The man page says a positional parameter is a digit, not a number, so $10 is $1 followed by a zero. Digit is not number. Shift or assign to other variables, like you did. RTFM.

subject: execute stdin ?
q: Is it possible in sh or csh to execute a program that is read from stdin, for example a compressed program piped from zcat?
a: Yes, use the -s option to sh. Feed the commands in on stdin and the arguments follow, like (echo 'ls -l $1'; echo 'wc $1') | sh -s /etc/motd. As simple as that. Read the sh man page sometime.

subject: How to do <cmd> file | hold file
q: Is there a one-liner in the shell to do something like "sort file | hold file", so I can sort a file and put the result back in the same file without a temp file?
a: For sort, just use "sort file -o file". It's in the man pages. Read them. In general you have to park the output somewhere suitable and mv it back, since buffering the whole file in RAM won't work for large files.

subject: search and replace string from a script
q: Is there a way in ex or another text utility to change only the nth occurrence of a pattern in a file, without writing a temporary file? I use the Bourne shell.
a: Use perl, since ex won't do it. Something like perl -pe 's/STRING1/STRING2/ if /STRING1/ && (++$n == 20);' <in >out, with 20 being your magic occurrence. Season to taste. Syntax is cryptic, but that's the price of getting the job done.

subject: Bourne shell functions
q: My Bourne shell on a Sequent running DYNIX doesn't support functions, so I stored the commands in a variable and used eval. Any problems with that work-around?
a: It breaks as soon as you need parameters. The real fix is to use /usr/att/bin/sh in the AT&T universe, which has functions. Why Sequent ships two shells, one missing half the other, is beyond me.

subject: (t)csh if query
q: What is the syntax of the if test expression in csh or tcsh? I want to run the alias X11 in my .login if HOSTTYPE is sun3 and TERM is sun, but my one-line if gives 'Expression syntax.'
a: Write: if ($HOSTTYPE == sun3 && $TERM == sun) then, X11 on the next line, then endif. Aliases won't work in the one-line if form, so use the multi-line form. It's all in the man page. RTFM.

subject: TCSH filename completion and !
q: When completing a filename with TAB in tcsh, I'd like the ! escaped, like spaces and semicolons. Was it left out on purpose, or do others want this too?
a: You should have checked the newer version before whining. In tcsh 6.00, the ! is quoted when you complete a filename containing it. Upgrade from 5.18.

subject: Looking for Dan Bernstein's pty program.
q: Where can I find Dan Bernstein's pty program? I was told it was in comp.sources.misc but couldn't find it.
a: Wrong group. It's in comp.sources.unix volume 22, available at uunet and many other places, and via anonymous ftp on stealth.acf.nyu.edu. Apply all the latest patches. Try looking in the right place first.

subject: Problem using multiple 'head' commands in shell script
q: Why does a Bourne shell script that runs head -200 several times on the same piped input lose lines after each head? How do I get around it, preferably still using head?
a: Yes, head reads a bufferful at a time, so the rest of the buffer is gone when it exits. This comes up every week. Use awk to print your markers at NR==201 and NR==401 and print every line, or use split -200.

subject: Stupid sed question
q: Why does my sed script editing /etc/ttytype barf with a garbled command when two ports like ttya1 and ttya10 both match my fgrep?
a: Because fgrep returns two lines, so $line holds a newline and sed sees a command with no ending delimiter. Anchor your match to the end of the line, or use sed to substitute on the tab-anchored pattern directly. Think before you grep.

subject: tcsh for root -- ok or not?
q: Will using tcsh as root's shell in the passwd file cause problems? Should I stick to sh or csh?
a: No problem, we do it here. Just make sure your tcsh binary is listed in /etc/shells. Don't skip that step and then whine about it.

subject: BAD HZ VALUE --- Error
q: After relinking SCO UNIX 386 3.2, some programs print 'Bad Hz Value, using 60 from /usr/include/sys/params.h'. I set HZ to 50 for Germany and relinked, but I still get the message. Why?
a: What has Germany got to do with it? HZ is not the line frequency. It's the hardware interrupt rate the kernel programs into the clock/timer chip. You can't just play with it, or timing goes off by 6/5. Sigh.

subject: Dual ethernet support (ISC 2.2)
q: Can I run dual ethernet cards under ISC 2.2 with a WD8003E or 3Com Etherlink II, and why won't they work at IRQ 7?
a: Two 3c503 cards never worked for me. A 3c503 plus a WD8003 does work, but you must edit the config files and /etc/netd.cf yourself, a small hassle. There's also a fix for the hanging streams, which has held so far. Didn't answer the IRQ 7 bit, though.

subject: Can Win 3.0 and X Windows Coexist?
q: Can Windows 3.0 and X Windows coexist on a network of X workstations and PCs? Are X servers for MS Windows effective?
a: They can. One outfit in Anaheim, Integrated Inference Machines, ported the MIT X server to Microsoft Windows. I saw an xterm to a Sun running under Windows, with X apps displaying, no problems. Pretty neat, for a PC.

subject: Q: GIF viewers for UNIX?
q: Do any GIF viewers exist for UNIX? I have a 33MHz 486 running SCO UNIX with the development system and an SVGA card and monitor, and I don't want to go back to DOS.
a: Yes, of course. Grab video_demo from the Games directory at sosco. Or get MetroLink's X11R4 package, which includes at least two clients that display GIF files. Honestly, no need to crawl back to DOS.

subject: Backup of DOS partitions
q: Does anyone have software to back up the DOS partition on the hard disk from Unix or Xenix, moving DOS data structures between machines and partition sizes? Please don't say dd.
a: On ISC you can mount the DOS filesystem and use find, cpio or tar, though one poor soul had tar repeat the first file endlessly. Emmet Gray's mtools reads files from the DOS partition. Not a complete solution, but a start.

subject: How to make a laserjet work with Xroff?
q: How do I get a LaserJet working with xroff on ISC Unix? Printing loses the l and i characters, and I don't know what utod does or how to set the stty settings for the printer port.
a: You probably don't need utod at all. Put "stty 9600 cs8 opost onlcr ixon <&1" at the top of the interface script for newline conversion and 8-bit mode. For font downloads use "stty 9600 cs8 -opost ixon <&1" so binary data isn't mangled. Then replace utod with cat. Sigh.

subject: EtherCard Plus vs. Digiboard PC/16i??
q: How do I get a Western Digital EtherCard Plus WD8003E to work in a machine that also has a Digiboard PC/16i? The Ethernet card collides with the Digiboard.
a: Set the WD8003 address to D0000, since it's only reliable there. Then change Digiboard jumper J3 from pins 2&3 to pins 1&2, which shrinks its dual-ported memory from 128K to 64K. The memory address can stay put. Cheap PC hardware, always fighting over addresses.

subject: larger/additional Hdrives under Vpix
q: How do I get a bigger pseudo C drive, or extra pseudo hard drive partitions, under VP/ix on SCO Unix 3.2.0? It seems limited to 20 MB.
a: Up to 32MB is guaranteed, past that you're into DOS version magic. Make a real DOS partition of the size you want, fill it, compact the free space to the end, and dd the used blocks into the Pseudo-C file. It's no mystery.

subject: name resolve
q: How do I turn off the name resolver on ISC 3.2? I only have loopback set up and can telnet to an IP address but not a name, even with resolv.conf set to no nameserver.
a: Simplest way: move /etc/resolv.conf out of the way, to resolv.bak or whatever. Then gethostbyname() falls back to parsing /etc/hosts. And how exactly do you expect to telnet anywhere with only loopback? Sigh.

subject: Math Co-Proc. usage
q: How does System V handle a 387 math coprocessor when two tasks want it? Is it locked as a resource, or is its state switched on a task switch, and isn't that slow?
a: The 387 is only tied to a process while that process is running it. On a task switch the kernel saves the state of both the 386 and the 387 and restores it later. If you have no 387, the emulator runs at about 2% of chip speed. That's the slow part.

subject: How to get past end of cpio archive on tape
q: I accidentally wrote a 20 MB cpio archive over the start of a backup tape. How do I get past the EOF marker at the end of the cpio archive to read the rest of the tape?
a: Use the no-rewind device. Whatever you read with closes the device and rewinds the tape, so find the no-rewind minor number in /dev, read the cpio part, then reopen it with dd for the rest. Rewind before pulling the tape. Also, if it's a QIC cartridge, forget it: writing track zero erases the whole tape.

subject: ISC2.2 having trouble with Zmodem file transfer
q: I can't upload from Procomm Plus to an ISC 2.2 host via ymodem or zmodem at 9600 or 4800; it dies about 20 blocks in. Is it true ISC's 1K tty buffer prevents 1K block transfers?
a: That claim is bogus, I've done it here without problems. Likely culprit is XON/XOFF enabled at one end, since block 19's header has an XOFF in it. Or blame Procomm, which has more bugs than a dog has fleas. Try Telix.

subject: Printer Problems
