q: I installed AT&T's Line Printer Spooler on SysV r4 2.1 and set /dev/lp as the printer by hand, but the mail says it can't be opened. What am I doing wrong?
a: Check that /dev/lp is owned by lp, since that error shows up when it's owned by someone else. Also check the parallel port driver is in the kernel, a Y in /etc/conf/sdevice.d/lp, and have the printer powered on when Unix boots. Basic stuff.

subject: ISC PANIC: namei() and POSIX appls.
q: I'm chasing an ISC panic in namei() with POSIX applications, 5 to 10 panics a day, probably a NULL pointer. Anyone have more info?
a: Ask ISC for a copy of SSU21. It took two or three months to get, but since running it I've had only one crash, and not the namei null dereference. Expect a wait, because vendors never hurry.

subject: ISC 2.2 Hangs on disk I/O
q: ISC 2.2 on my 386 with a WD1006V-SR2 RLL controller and Seagate ST-277 hangs solid with the disk light on during disk I/O, like boot scans or big greps. Any ideas?
a: Known problem with the 1006 and 1007 controllers; they can return interrupts in an odd way. SCO fixed it in their driver, ISC blamed the controller. Replacing the controller will probably fix it, and switching to SCO definitely will. Typical.

subject: ISC 2.2.1 on a 386 clone: PANIC ERROR
q: ISC Unix 2.2.1 on my 33MHz 386 clone panics with a kernel mode trap 0x0E under heavy load like compiling. Is it memory or the bus? How do I find the cause?
a: Sounds like a bad disk controller. Mine crashed under heavy compiles, a heavy disk load, and replacing the three year old controller card fixed it. Try borrowing someone else's controller for a while. Nobody here knew what trap 0x0E means.

subject: Coherent (Mark Williams Unix)
q: Is Mark Williams Coherent for the 386 any good? I hear it's based on an early Unix with a 64K limit on various things. Is anyone using it?
a: Go ask in comp.os.misc, where the Coherent Digest gets posted weekly. It's roughly Minix-like in capability but more stable, minus the sources. Much 4.3 software, most of the GNU stuff especially, won't run on it. Depends what you want, as usual.

subject: UNIX WordPerfect Terminal Database
q: Is curses so broken on enough platforms that WordPerfect had to write its own terminal database for UNIX?
a: Pretty much, at various points. People kept adding special fields to termcap that it and curses didn't support, so they ended up with their own files. Terminfo can't tell a shifted function key from a plain one, for instance. Sigh.

subject: ANSI-C compatible cc in SysV??
q: Is the cc in Interactive System V 3.2 ANSI C compatible? Mine choked on ANSI prototypes. Also, can root log in on a virtual terminal instead of only the console?
a: Plain cc isn't ANSI. ISC 2.2 ships LPI-cc, which is, but it has problems, so get GNU cc for the 386. For root, comment out the CONSOLE= line in /etc/default/login with a #, and do the same in /etc/default/su. Sigh.

subject: TCP/IP/Novell/terminal emulator for Wollongong
q: Is there a terminal emulator that works through interrupt 14 so I can use it with Wollongong's WIN/TCP for DOS instead of its buggy vt100 emulator?
a: MS Kermit 3.10 does it, and you probably already had it. Run telnet with -e kermit and the hostname, or rlogin with -e then kermit in a batch file, and put SET PORT BIOS1 in MSKERMIT.INI. Not exactly obscure.

subject: various bugs in ISC 3.2.2
q: On ISC with VP/ix, the system always prints umount: /usr busy at shutdown, though I can't find a process using /usr. What should I do?
a: Something is running on /usr or holding a file open there. Use fuser(1M) to see which processes have access to /usr. It's a basic tool, so use it before you whine about bugs.

subject: SCO 'date'
q: On SCO System V/386 3.2.1, why does `date `setclock`` advance the CMOS clock by 5 hours every time, leaving the time wrong at boot?
a: It's a timezone problem. date honors TZ and setclock doesn't. Temporarily unset it: TZ= date `setclock`. Honestly, this is a nasty bug and the sort of thing SCO ought to have caught.

subject: increasing number of xterms
q: Running ISC 2.2 with X 1.2, I raised the number of ptys from 16 to 24 and rebuilt the kernel, but I can't start more xterms. I get "X Toolkit Error: Can't Open display." What am I missing?
a: You only fixed half of it. Set node.d/pts to more pts terminals, and set both sdevice.d/ptem and sdevice.d/ptm to 32. Reading the X386 config file would have told you that, you know.

subject: Strings in Standard Library
q: The Interactive Unix development libraries have lots of useless header-name strings in each object module, bloating executables. Can they be removed?
a: Look up the mcs command. mcs -d deletes the comment strings, mcs -c removes duplicates, and mcs -p prints them. Besides, all the libraries hold only about 450K of them, so what's loaded is tiny. RTFM.

subject: `lpadmin' and `lpforms' in SCO SysV3.2
q: Under SCO System V 3.2 (ODT 1.0.1), lpadmin and lpforms complain about invalid scaled numbers and forms get corrupted. Are these utilities just broken, and is there a workaround?
a: Yes, they're broken. Get update unx249b from the SCO uucp BBS. It has fixed lpforms, lpadmin and lpsched binaries plus revised printer interface scripts. Should have shipped that way, but vendors never test anything.

subject: ISC kernel symbol 'machenv'?
q: What does the 'machenv' symbol do in the Interactive (ISC) kernel? My kernel build with the Archive Viper drivers on a non-ISC UNIX fails on the undefined symbol, and I need to know what it contains.
a: It's a structure holding the machine type and assorted machine configuration items, like display type and math co-processor and its type. The element settings are defined in <sys/machenv.h>. Go read the header before you dummy anything up.

subject: timing of functions
q: What is the most precise way to time how long a function takes to execute on a System V 386 box?
a: Ideally measure with a different machine, since timing code changes the performance. Otherwise use gettimeofday() on BSD, but microsecond precision isn't microsecond accuracy. System V often only gives 1/60 second. Or compile with -p and run prof on mon.out. Learn precision versus accuracy, kid.

subject: What mouse is better: serial ou bus?
q: What mouse is better for X on Interactive Unix 2.0.2: serial or bus, two or three buttons, Microsoft or Logitech? What about the Logitech trackball?
a: Depends on whether you'd rather give up a backplane slot or a serial port. Three buttons, definitely. The Logitech trackball works fine as a swap-in, though a mouse is still preferable if you've got the desk space.

subject: Compatibility lists
q: Why aren't current hardware compatibility lists from Esix, ISC, SCO and others available here, and how do we get them?
a: Call the vendor's sales rep and they'll mail you the list. Any idiot can dial a phone. Get the lists before you build a 386 box, then ask the vendors about anything not listed. Don't trust the lists too much.

subject: Take out memory to speed up kernel build!?
q: Why did my SCO Unix System V/386 kernel link go from 7.5 minutes with 4 megs of RAM to 5 minutes after someone stole a card and left me with 2 meg?
a: Probably that 2 Mb card was slow 16-bit RAM on the 8 MHz AT bus, while main memory runs at 20-25 MHz. Unix puts its kernel in high memory, so pulling the slow RAM forced it into the fast RAM. Irritating that it takes 4 Mb to install but only 2 to run.

subject: serial line goes bad when switching screens
q: Why does my serial line lose characters when I switch virtual screens? Is it the clists being dumped, or running out of them with NCLIST at 120?
a: Probably neither. The console driver doesn't allow a context switch while it copies the screen contents to video RAM, so a slow system or display card drops characters. It was a problem on a slow 286 but not on a 386. Get faster hardware.

subject: X terminals for System V
q: Will an NCD X terminal work with an ESIX System V 386 system?
a: Yes, it works. People have tried both color and b&w NCD X terminals on ESIX with no problems. Not exactly rocket science, you know.

subject: Ultrix 4.0 and automount
q: Automount on Ultrix 4.0 under YP sends my machine into an endless "NFS server not responding still trying" wait. Are there patches, or is it just inadvisable to run it?
a: Don't run it. It's a piece of junk that chokes on maps with several hundred entries and gives the same errors. Other admins advised against DEC's automounter and suggested amd, available by anonymous ftp from usc.edu. Typical DEC.

subject: ATT C++ Release 2.1 under Ultrix 4.0
q: Building AT&T C++ Release 2.1 on a DECstation 3100 under Ultrix 4.0, the make munch stage dies with "sh: illegal io" and the problem seems to be in the CC script. Any ideas?
a: Ultrix /bin/sh can't redirect I/O on certain built-ins like set and read, hence "illegal io". Run the script under /bin/sh5, which doesn't have the problem, by changing the #!/bin/sh line to #!/bin/sh5. Typical vendor shell breakage.

subject: Info wanted on 3rd party memory for 5810
q: Can I buy third-party memory for a DEC 5810 and avoid DEC's prices? I heard the memory is the same as the VAX 6000 series.
a: Yes, it's the same memory as the VAX 6000 series, but there's no third-party alternative. DEC keeps the XMI bus proprietary and nobody has reverse engineered it. Enjoy the price gouging, since competition only shows up once the margins get fat enough.

subject: Different dialing strings on the L.sys files possible (DS3100)?
q: Can I use different dialing strings for different calls in the L.sys file on a DS3100? I only see one ACU option, and some sites have modems that need different protocols.
a: Put multiple lines for the same system in L.sys, with a different prefix on the speed field, like tb9600 or v9600. Those pick lines in L-devices, which name modem descriptions in acucap. Not all uucp control fields are limited to their apparent meaning, so stop being confused.

subject: How to use uucp on a VAXstation 3100 via Telebit modem?
q: Can uucp work on a VAXstation 3100 through a Telebit modem, given the DECconnect port has no modem control signals?
a: Probably, but it's ugly. With no modem control the line is dedicated to either incoming or outgoing, and you must hack the modemcap to ignore carrier and rely on timeouts and status strings. Expect it to be flaky. Thanks, DEC.

subject: rodent allergy
q: Does the DEC puck/tablet (VSXXX-AB) work on a DS3100, and does the mouse driver make it look mouse compatible to higher-level software?
a: Yes, it works on DS3100/2100 and DS5000 as the X pointer under Ultrix 3.1D and 4.0. The tablet area is scaled onto the root window, and no raw absolute data is available. To get the 4th button, start the server with -btn 4. Read the release notes.

subject: Ultrix 4.0 Packet Filter Devices
q: Has anyone written a nice Ethernet monitoring program using the packetfilter devices in Ultrix 4.0? Something like Sun Etherfind would be great.
a: Use tcpdump from LBL, which is apparently just like Etherfind, only better. NNstat/statspy and nfswatch have also been ported. Honestly, most of the porting work isn't the packet filter, it's fixing the byte-order bugs. Sigh.

subject: Autobauding and modems
q: How can I set up Ultrix so a naive user dialing in on an autobauding modem gets the right speed automatically, instead of sending a break to change baud rates?
a: Tell getty in /etc/gettytab that the line can be speed sensed with a CR, and edit /etc/ttys to match. That works from 110 to 9600 baud. Otherwise make your gettydefs cycle from high to low speeds so repeated returns find the rate. RTFM, it's old stuff.

subject: How to get curses to handle SIGWINCH
q: How do I get curses to handle SIGWINCH? My program gets the signal but curses keeps using the old size. Is it safe to ioctl() the new size and stuff it into LINES and COLS?
a: No. Just updating LINES and COLS won't make curses allocate memory for the new screen locations. And vi predates curses and never used it, so it proves nothing. Learn your history.

subject: uVax 3600: Setting default boot device
q: How do I set the default boot device on a uVax 3600 after a CPU upgrade?
a: At the console prompt type SET BOOT DUA0, or whichever device you want. The new firmware has lots of commands, so try HELP. You'd know that if you'd poked around.

subject: Building X11R5 under Ultrix 4.2 - Help!
q: I'm building X11R5 on a DEC 5100 running Ultrix 4.2 and don't have the /bsd43 or /sysv include directories, so makedepend complains in server/ddx/mips. What should I do?
a: You're probably using the wrong configuration file. Sounds like you picked Mips.cf; use the supplied ultrix.cf instead, since the DEC configuration wouldn't be building the Mips servers. Begging for header files is the wrong fix.

subject: Do I need to install 2.2 and 2.3 before 3.0 (advanced installation)
q: I'm running Ultrix 2.0 on a VAX 11/750. Do I need to install 2.1 and 2.3 first, with advanced installation, before going to Ultrix 3.0?
a: There's no technical reason for it. Go straight to 3.0. Honestly, this is the sort of question the release notes answer. Skip the intermediate versions and save yourself the grief.

subject: Disk partitioning and cylinder boundaries
q: In BSD Unix, partitions are supposed to begin and end on cylinder boundaries, but newfs still says sectors are unallocated at the end, even with the default Ultrix partitioning. Is this normal, or am I wasting my time?
a: Normal. Filesystems are divided into cylinder groups, and newfs wastes sectors if the size isn't a whole number of groups, up to a megabyte. Make every partition except the last a whole number of cylinder groups. Newfs uses 16 cylinders per group; check with -v and /etc/disktab. Basic BSD.

subject: is landscape available for lno3r PostScript printer?
q: Is landscape available for the DEC LN03R PostScript printer under Ultrix? The -Olandscape switch to lpr isn't working.
a: The LN03R filter doesn't understand -Olandscape, and it's written wrong. Use -w132 and it defaults to landscape, like lpr -Pyourprinter -w132 filename. The Motif Print Widget passes only -O values, so you'd need a front end or a fixed filter.

subject: Is there a SLIP implementation for Ultrix?
q: Is there a SLIP implementation for Ultrix? I have a MacII without an ethernet card next to a DECstation 3100 and want to link them.
a: I'm pretty sure SLIP is on the unsupported tape. Look in /usr/new, where slattach and friends show up with man pages. Which subset they're in, go dig it out yourself.

subject: LK401 keyboard
q: My DECstation 5000/120PX has an LK401 keyboard with extra Alt Function and Compose Character keys that generate no X events. What are they for, and can I make them generate keycodes?
a: The Compose key works like on the old VT3xx terminals. In an 8-bit DECterm with a suitable editor, you hit a two-key compose sequence to make 8-bit multinational characters. It's all in the VT3xx document set. Sigh, read it.

subject: Ultrix DECnet
q: My Ultrix 2.2-1 TCP to DECnet gateway now gives insufficient system resources errors and mail11 can't create a socket, with no software changes. How do I increase system resources?
a: Try ncp define exec max links 80 and ncp set exec max links 80. The default is about 20 links, which you likely ran out of. If not, V2.2's mbuf pool is fixed size, so tune the config file. Don't ask me which.

subject: rand() ... works ??
q: On Ultrix 3.0, rand() returns values that seem way too high. Is there a trick?
a: Not too high: rand() returns 0 to 2^31-1, the largest signed integer, so nothing can exceed that. To limit it, take rand() % x. But use random(3) instead of rand(), because rand() this way gives non-random results. Read the man page.

subject: Setting up BIND Client
q: On Ultrix 3.1, setting up as a BIND client says I must change my hostname to the fully qualified name, but our UUCP neighbors know us by the short name. Do I really have to change the hostname, or is there a workaround?
a: No, you don't. As of 3.0, uucp knows about domain names and only uses the hostname up to the first dot as the uucp node name. So set the fully qualified name and relax. Try reading the release notes.

subject: Configuring terminal line for dial-out under Ultrix
q: On Ultrix, tip segfaults when I try to use my modem port, and my /etc/remote is configured. Is there a simple way to connect to a modem port?
a: Check for a .tiprc in your login directory and delete it; that may cure the segfault. As for simple, no. Tip, kermit or rolling your own program is the only way I know. Ultrix isn't known for elegance.

subject: DS 3100/Xwindows bug
q: On a DECstation 3100 my X application fails at link time with jump relocation out-of-range errors in libX11.a, and renaming a variable called index fixed it. What was going on?
a: index() is a standard UNIX string routine, so your global named index collides with it. Using a data item as if it were code gives that ugly error. The Ultrix RISC release notes document it: rename your data structure. Any idiot knows not to reuse library names.

subject: Swap Space Problems
q: On a DECstation 3100 with 16 MB of memory and Ultrix 4.1, I set up two 24 MB swap partitions as the guide suggested but get memory problems with SAS, MATLAB and X windows. Is that enough swap?
a: No. 48 MB is not enough for X Windows on 16 MB of real memory; other sites run 125 MB of swap and are heading to 200. The guide's rule only fits typical loads. Add more swap, and check pstat and ps. Sigh.

subject: ds3100/uws 2.x xon/xoff LAT problem
q: On a DECstation 3100 with UWS 2.1, xon/xoff isn't handled correctly when connecting from a LAT terminal server, so C-X C-S in Emacs stops output until C-Q is pressed. Is there a fix?
a: The olde LAT problem again. Patches exist for all flavors of Ultrix; call the Colorado support center, or install 3.1C as the kernel base. As a kludge, disable flow control on the port in the terminal server. Sigh.

subject: LAT printers shared between VMS/Ultrix hanging
q: Our LAT printers shared between VMS and Ultrix 3.1 keep hanging on the Ultrix side because it won't let go of the port. A DEC patch didn't fix it. Is there a workaround?
a: Make sure you have all the LAT patches and the latest server images in every server. For the DS200, 33D is the current one, not the distributed BL33. Server software is separate from Ultrix LAT, so call software support about both. Obvious, really.

subject: copying "a" partitions
q: Since the partition table lives on each disk, I can't dd the root "a" partition to another disk unless the partition tables match. Is there a good way to make disk-to-disk copies of the root file system?
a: Standardize partition sizes and drive types between the system disk and your backup disk. Otherwise do a pipe: umount, newfs, mount, then dump 0f - / piped to a cd and restore rf -. For a normal root it isn't slow and needs no operator. Restore r is silent; x asks silly questions.

subject: "Unsupported" Ingres
q: The Ultrix distribution has an "unsupported" Ingres on its tape, but I can't find any documentation. How can I use it?
a: Keep looking. There are two documents for the public domain Ingres, either with the Ingres files or in the Documents subset that came as a separate part of the Unsupported tape. Unsupported means what it says, so dig.

subject: compliers for DECsystem 5000
q: The VAX version of Ultrix came with Pascal, f77, Modula-2 and Franz Lisp, but the RISC version didn't. How or where can I get this software for a DECsystem 5000?
a: Modula-2 is on anonymous FTP from gatekeeper.dec.com in pub/DEC/Modula-2, as m2.mips.tar.Z for your box. There's also a Scheme-to-C system under pub/DEC/Scheme-to-C. Go fetch it, and quit waiting for the vendor.

subject: Hesoid & YP
q: Ultrix 4.0 is going to use Hesiod and Kerberos. Will I still be able to import YP passwd files on my DS3100 in a department of Suns?
a: Yes, RTFM. The Ultrix 4.0 docs say you can run Hesiod, YP, or both. /etc/svc.conf holds a search list per database, so passwd can try local /etc/passwd first, then Hesiod, then YP.

subject: Ultrix ver 4.2 'make' not passing commands to 'sh'?
q: Ultrix 4.2 make says "Cannot load bison" for a command that isn't in the standard directories but is in my PATH, though "true && bison" works. Why, and is there a fix?
a: Make chokes on path names with a '-' in them, such as /u/bison-1.14. It tries to be smart and searches for the first command's full path before handing it to sh. Rename the directory to /u/bison_1.14 and it works. Vendors, sigh.

subject: Why can't I start hesupd?
q: Under Ultrix 4.1, hesupd says it can only be run on a bind primary. Why can't I start hesupd?
a: RTFM: the server needs the alias "bindmaster" on its /etc/hosts entry, and put it last in the list or hesupd won't see it. Also check named.boot in your namedb directory to see what kind of server you really are.

subject: Problems with 'mail'
q: Users on our Ultrix system sometimes get 'mail' stuck in a CPU run state and the process stays after they drop the modem line. Has anyone seen this? Is mail sensitive to line garbage?
a: Seen it since the first Ultrix release. The cause appears to be mail's improper handling of EOF: at the prompt, EOF sends it looping forever and burning CPU. A dropped modem line gives EOF on input. SIGHUP it seems to handle fine.

subject: Decnet-tcp/ip gateway.
q: We have many VAXes, one DECstation with DECnet and the DECnet-TCP/IP gateway, and TCP/IP-only X terminals. Can DECwindows clients on the VMS machines use the X terminals as servers?
a: UCX on the VMS machines solves it, and it's part of VMS from about 5.3, so no extra licence cost. You might need extra fonts or aliases for the X terminals. It runs on the VMS side, which you didn't want. Tough.

subject: RA90's
q: What are the optimal rotational gap and blocks per cylinder for a DEC RA90 drive? I'm running SysV on a VAX 8600 and DEC hasn't been helpful.
a: Sigh. The V3.1 disktab entry for the RA90 gives 69 sectors per track, 13 tracks per cylinder and 2649 cylinders. As for the gap, an 8 KB block with an 8 KB gap works fine. Smaller or larger gaps made no real difference to sequential I/O speed.

subject: dump to 8mm tape
q: What values do you use for dump to an 8mm tape in terms of tape size, density and block size? I was given a script using 346 for size, 4137733 for density and 2097152 for block size.
a: Those are the values suggested by the TLZ08 manual, so they work. I've used them successfully at a customer site. Your script was fine, you didn't need to ask.

subject: Monitor program - latest version?
q: What's the latest version of the monitor program for Ultrix on decwrl, and is there one that supports V4.x RISC Ultrix?
a: It's V1.2 or V1.3, dated around November. Get monitor_v4src.tar.Z from gatekeeper.dec.com, the sources suitable for V4.x. You likely have the old full distribution, monitor.tar.Z, which only covers V3.x. Read the filenames before you complain.

subject: Source for cat available???
q: Where can I get the Ultrix source for the cat utility?
a: If your site has an Ultrix source license, you already have it. If not, use the Free Software Foundation's freely distributable cat, in the fileutils tarball under pub/GNU on gatekeeper.dec.com. Honestly, it's cat. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: svc.conf
q: Why can't I rsh to a host and run dxterm with a symbolic display name unless the display host is in that machine's /etc/hosts, even after fiddling with /etc/svc.conf?
a: Do you even have an /etc/resolv.conf? You need a domain line and a nameserver line with the server's IP address. Read the DNS (BIND) section of the System and Network Setup manual, since svc.conf alone won't do it.

subject: dxpsview quirk?
q: Why does dxpsview on Ultrix 4.2 say "Comments wrong, ignoring them for this file" unless the PostScript file ends with a %%Trailer line?
a: The file claims to use structured comments but the syntax is wrong, so the viewer ignores them. They're an optional convention for print queues and previewers. Your generator is emitting bad PostScript. Read the Adobe PostScript Language Reference Manual, it's not a secret.

subject: Amd & Ultrix
q: With amd, how do I avoid starting a separate amd for each mount directory like /piper and /eclipse? Running amd on / replaces the root directory, which is bad news.
a: Run a single amd on a directory like /am with one map, then make symbolic links in / pointing into it, e.g. ln -s /am/eclipse eclipse. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: Tiny bug in lockd. Dies if hostname too long.
q: lockd dies when the hostname is too long, because the hostname buffer in prot_libr.c is only 20 characters. How should it be fixed?
a: Don't just double an arbitrary number. Include sys/param.h and use the MAXHOSTNAMELEN macro, which is 64 on Ultrix 4.0. Hardcoded buffer sizes, honestly. Any idiot knows better.

subject: news/mail feed times
q: I feed news and mail to several uucp neighbors. How can I send only mail to them during the day and news batches only in the evening? I run SCO UNIX, MMDF, and C News.
a: The obvious way is to not run the news batcher during the day. Leftover batches from the night before will still trickle out. Some advanced uucp versions can also restrict by traffic grade, since news normally has a lower grade than mail. Check your manuals, sigh.

subject: sun 386i that wouldn't boot.
q: A Sun 386i hangs during the green-bar boot and restarts. Booting standalone and doing mount -a fixed it. What was the problem?
a: Nothing obvious from what you've told us. Turn on verbose boot by setting NVRAM location 494 to 1, which may tell you more than that green bar does. Try giving some actual information next time.

subject: STREAMS tty drivers for SysV
q: Can I make ttys and pseudo-ttys STREAMS devices on System V/386 Rel 3.2 so I can use I_SETSIG with S_INPUT, without rebuilding the kernel?
a: Not with the stock SVR3 stream head. It has no VTIM/VMIN support and handles non-blocking reads differently from SVID ttys, so a compliant tty can't sit under it. A vendor with an extended stream head can, but it's no small job. Sigh.

subject: ksh incompatabilities with sh?
q: Do people actually still use ^ for pipes in shell scripts? It breaks under ksh and ought to be eradicated.
a: Yes, sadly. Many customers with a dozen years of UNIX still use it, because old habits die hard. Some terminals, like the Wang 2236, have ^ but no |, so the synonym is a lifesaver there. Eradicate that, and you break real people.

subject: 4.3BSD Internals book
q: Has anyone heard whether "The Design and Implementation of the 4.3BSD UNIX Operating System" by Leffler, McKusick, Karels and Quarterman has come out yet? It was supposed to be from Addison-Wesley in late 1988.
a: Addison-Wesley says it's due out Dec. 15, just in time for Christmas, and it runs 448 pages. Sigh, that's all anyone knows; the rest is rumor mill. Go bother the publisher instead of the net.

subject: Microport Sys V. r. 3 for 80386 machines
q: How can I access particular real physical addresses using Microport UNIX on an 80386? Microport said it wasn't possible.
a: Create a shared memory segment at the address you want. I've used that to directly map the registers on an EGA card. Hardly impossible, whatever the vendor told you.

subject: Determining one's own IP address.
q: How can I determine my own IP address without looking it up in the hosts file?
a: Run ifconfig on the interface name, such as de0, and read the inet line. If you don't know the interface name, netstat -i lists them. Sigh, it's not in memory by magic.

subject: stat of i-node
q: How can I get stat information for an i-node when I already know the file number, without scanning a directory for the name?
a: Open the disk and read the on-disk copy of the inode, if you must. But fstat() is very cheap, and stat() isn't that bad with name caching. Quit optimizing what doesn't need it.

subject: How do I know my Q-KEY is unique ?
q: How can I make sure the 32-bit key I pass when creating a message queue is unique? Is there anywhere to register one?
a: Nobody registers IPC keys. Use ftok() with an agreed existing file and id, or create with IPC_PRIVATE and hand the id to the other processes through a file or command line. Hard-coding a key and hoping is the worst way. Grumble.

subject: How to delete a file with ^? chars in the name?
q: How do I delete a file with ^? characters in its name? ls shows ???H01.b and rm with quoting won't take it.
a: Use ls -i to get the inode number, then find . -inum that number -ok rm {} \;. Or edit an ls listing into an rm script. And read the newusers stuff on silly filenames before asking again.

subject: running out of inodes?
q: How do I find out how many inodes a filesystem has? Man pages give "Word overflow" and "Out of temp file space" on a SunOS 4.0 box, though there's plenty of disk space.
a: On any modern system, just run df -i. As for your errors, they come from n/troff, and the temp file space is in memory, a fixed-size region in most implementations. It has nothing to do with inodes or disk. Look elsewhere.

subject: What processes are on the ends of a TCP connection?
q: How do I find which processes are on the ends of a TCP connection shown by netstat -a on BSD?
a: Trivial it isn't. Use netstat -a -A to get the PCB address, then walk it in adb on /vmunix and /dev/kmem through the tcpcb, inpcb and socket. Then search every process's u area open-file array for that socket. Write a program for it, if you're masochistic.

subject: The whole prompt string thing (was: PS1 and the bourne shell...)
q: How do I get the current directory into the PS1 prompt of the Bourne shell? We've tried every suggestion on the net and nothing works.
a: The stock Bourne shell won't do it, any shell hacker knows that. You have to modify the source: in main.c change prs(ps1nod.namval) to prs(macro(ps1nod.namval)), rebuild, then set PS1 with single quotes and backquoted pwd. Or just use ksh, which already does this.

subject: using System V 'cu'
q: How do I slow down cu's tilde-put file transfer? A fast PC talking over a 1200 baud modem overflows the remote system's input buffer and the transfer fails.
a: Use a protocol-based transfer instead: start umodem on the remote and run it through the ~+ escape. That also handles binary files. Also make sure xon/xoff flow control is set on the destination with stty. Or write a slow cat that sleeps between 100-byte chunks.

subject: syncing passwd files for NFS
q: How do I sync up the password and group files of a 4.3BSD VAX and a DG/UX machine for NFS without chown-ing the whole filesystem with a slew of finds? I recall a program that walks the inode table making the changes.
a: Such programs exist. Grab pub/unify_uids.tar.Z by anonymous FTP from mimsy.umd.edu, and do it off-peak, not during east coast working hours. Sigh, no need to hand-roll finds for this.

subject: How does vi know?
q: How does vi know whether it's on a screen terminal or a paper or glass tty and come up differently? Does it check particular termcap capabilities, or what?
a: It's your $TERM definition plus your baud setting. Below a certain baud threshold, vi drops into a special mode so it doesn't spend years redrawing a full screen. No need to go hunting through source for that, sigh.

subject: cd in the background?
q: I accidentally typed cd /new/dir & and my directory stayed the same. What's going on?
a: Backgrounding runs the command in a newly spawned shell. The cd happens there, then that shell dies and your old shell's state is untouched. Any idiot who thinks about it can see why.

subject: Kermit (dated Apr 89) and /dev/tty01
q: I built Kermit dated Apr 89 with make sys5r3 on an ISC 2.0.1 box. After a binary receive finishes, the machine beeps and the modem drops the line, and uucico and cu on /dev/tty01 often complain about a dropped line on the first try. What's wrong?
a: It's a locking problem. HDB UUCP keeps locks in /usr/spool/locks and stores the ASCII PID in the lock file. Kermit supports HDB, but the sys5r3 rule in the Makefile doesn't define it right. Add -DATT3BX to that rule. Should've been called HDB, honestly. Read ckutio.c.

subject: UNIX publications wanted
q: I'm compiling a list of UNIX publications for a talk. Besides UNIX Review, UnixWorld, UNIX Journal and the usenix and /usr/group mags, what others are there?
a: Go read the article 'UNIX Resources' in the August issue of UNIX World. It lists the publications, so you don't need to poll the whole net to do your homework.

subject: A quick /etc/rmt question
q: I'm trying to use /etc/rmt on a remote tape drive, but sending "O /dev/rmt8" and then "2" gives E2, no such file or directory. What am I doing wrong?
a: The documentation lies. No space between the command letter and its argument: type O/dev/rmt8, then the flags on the next line, and later arguments go on separate lines. You get A0 back as the acknowledgement. Sigh, trust the code, not the manual.

subject: Redirect Output in the Middle of a Program??
q: If a dial-up connection dies in the middle of a big C program, can the program or shell detect it and redirect stdout and stderr to a file from that point on and keep running?
a: The tty driver sends SIGHUP when the modem hangs up. Catch it with signal(), and in the handler use fopen and freopen to reassign the output streams. Easier still, teach users to run jobs in the background. Sigh.

subject: System V / SIGCLD questions...
q: In System V, my SIGCLD handler reaping children misses a second child that dies while the handler runs, and there is no wait3 or non-blocking wait. How do I get around this?
a: Two options. Reset SIGCLD first thing and reap one child per call, which has a race and can lose a signal. Better, set alarm(1) before wait() so it can't block forever, then check the return and cancel with alarm(0). Sigh, System V signals.

subject: Is to safe to do shmat without shmget?
q: Is it safe, on all known Unixes, to shmat to an existing shared memory segment using a shmid read from a file, without calling shmget first?
a: Everybody who tried it says it works, and folks with AT&T SysV kernel source say so too. The SVID just says "a shared memory identifier", not that it must come from shmget. One guy muttered "dangerous" with no reason. Nobody had a counterexample.

subject: C Profiler Wanted
q: Is there a C profiler for an SVR2 platform that profiles at a lower level, like monitor(3C), automatically via a compiler option, beyond prof and gprof?
a: On AT&T 3B machines there's lprof, the line profiler, invoked with the -qc compile option. It gives an annotated source listing with per-line execution counts. It's part of AT&T's C Programmers Productivity Tools, so see your account rep. Other platforms, ask your vendor. And name your platform next time.

subject: BSD/SunOS Reference
q: Is there a book on BSD or SunOS internals as good as Bach's The Design of the UNIX Operating System is for System V?
a: A similar 4.3BSD book by Quarterman, Karels and McKusick is due in the fall. Until then, the best source is Quarterman, Silberschatz and Peterson, "4.2BSD and 4.3BSD as Examples of the UNIX System", ACM Computing Surveys, December 1985. Go read it.

subject: Unix file archiving
q: Is there a file archiving and retrieval system for Unix like Bsys on Tenex or Dumper on Tops-20?
a: There's a user file archiving program that dumps to tape, ARCH.TAR-Z in the UNIX-C.TAPES directory on SIMTEL-20. If you just want to archive to files, there are multitudes of programs for that, zoo being a good one. Look before you ask.

subject: Authenticating Unix Domain sockets.
q: Is there a guaranteed way to find the uid of a process that just connected to me over a Unix domain socket?
a: Define "the" uid; the other end of a socket may be open in several processes, so nothing is unique. Short of a secure protocol or grodying around in the kernel like fuser or ofiles, there is no way.

subject: pseudo-tty problems
q: On 4.3 BSD, when I telnet back into my own machine over a pseudo-tty I lose characters on output to my VT100. Don't ptys understand control-S?
a: Telnet sends the control-S down the connection, and it has to get through the server and into the pty before it counts as a stop. Meanwhile your VT100's buffer is flooded. Use rlogin, which does XON/XOFF locally. Not perfect, but far better than telnet.

subject: Non blocking connect using streams/TLI?
q: On 4.xBSD I can do a non-blocking connect and select on the fd. Is there a similar way to do a non-blocking connect with streams/TLI?
a: Use poll, which does much the same as select, and set the descriptor to O_NDELAY. The STREAMS and t_* man pages describe it. Poll only works on STREAMS devices in V.3, and vendors may vary, so don't count on more.

subject: questions on dynamic linking on SunOS
q: On SunOS 4.0, can a program generate a C function, compile it into a shareable library, call it, then regenerate and recompile it into the same library and call it again?
a: Won't work. You can't write to the shared library your program has loaded, same idea as "Text file busy". It's like writing to the text of your running program and expecting the code to change. It doesn't. Think before you fork cc.

subject: "text: table is full" error message
q: On stock SunOS 3.5 on a diskless Sun 3/60 I keep getting 'text: table is full' and processes get killed. How do I make the text table bigger?
a: Patch ntext in /vmunix with adb -w, say from 28 to 50, then reboot. It won't take effect in the running kernel. But it may only delay things, since a failed NFS server can leak text slots. Only cure is a reboot.

subject: micro-code upgrade
q: Our VAX 11/750 running 4.3BSD needs a microcode upgrade from rev 98 to 103, and the DEC rep knows nothing about Unix. How do I get the code from his tape onto the RA81s?
a: You don't. The microcode goes on the TU58 console boot tape, not the RA81. Back up the tape with the console COPY command first, then copy the new files over, or read the BSD docs on making a console boot tape. Obviously.

subject: pid rollover?
q: Our Xenix System V box seems to roll over pids at 32K even though int is 4 bytes. Why doesn't the kernel use a full int for pids, and should I worry about rollover with mktemp() or $$?
a: The rollover has been at 30000 since time immemorial. On the 16-bit PDP-11 a short would have broken past 32767, so the cutoff was probably chosen to make rollovers easy to count. It's a 1 in 30000 chance of trouble, so quit worrying. Sigh.

subject: hanging uvaxIIs
q: Our two uVAX IIs running Ultrix 1.1 with RFS hang in a tight loop with no panic. We have the upgraded DEQNA cards but the old driver. Has anyone seen this?
a: Yes. The DEQNA hardware upgrade is useless without the matching software upgrade. The deqna driver in Ultrix 1.2 and 4.3BSD has the needed fixes. The same hangs went away for us once we had both. Sigh.

subject: Problems with pathalias
q: Pathalias on SysV R2 on a 3B2 dies with 'rehash error' and 'cannot recover' when I feed it the whole map. It's not memory or kernel parameters, as far as I can tell. What's wrong?
a: Known bug in pathalias. In yylex() in parse.y, the declaration char buf[BUFSIZ] must be made static, because the buffer is used after the function returns. It bit people on the 3B series and elsewhere. Check your copy before blaming the kernel, genius.

subject: Occasionally lp cannot find my print file. Why?
q: Sometimes lp says it cannot find my file xxx, even though permissions are read/write for everybody. I have to cat the file into lp. What's going on?
a: Check the permissions of the parent directories. Under System V, lp is setuid lp and setgid bin, so an inaccessible parent directory gives that error. Just use "lp < xxx". Fixed in System V Release 3.2. Basic stuff.

subject: Noisy symbolic links.
q: Symlinks on BSD systems get mode 0777, which clutters ls -l listings, and the permissions are meaningless. What mode should symlinks have, and should their permissions be used at all?
a: Use 444, since symlinks already act as if they were 444: anyone can read the target path, and you can't write one, you have to remove and recreate it. If permissions were ever used, read should control lstat() and execute should control whether the kernel follows the link.

subject: OSF -- some more news
q: The OSF is supposedly basing its Unix-style OS on AIX, said to be System V release 2. Which AIX is that?
a: Good question, and nobody's said. By IBM's own specs there are at least three AIXs: AIX/370, AIX/PS-2 and AIX/RT. They're all different, and none is Sys V Rel 2 compatible. Marketing at work, naturally.

subject: Limiting Telnet Access
q: We have a 3B2 running Wollongong TCP/IP and need to limit telnet access for some users without disabling their accounts. Is there something like the ftp.users file for telnet?
a: No such file. Make a group called telnet, chgrp /usr/bin/telnet to it, and chmod it so others have no access. Add allowed users to that group in /etc/group. They must run newgrp telnet before telnet, and that can't be in a script. Clunky, but it works.

subject: bigger longs (64 bits)
q: What do people think about 64-bit longs? Applications and devices are breaking the gigabyte limits of 32 bits, and we may get stuck with too small an address space again.
a: That's a C question, not a UNIX one. 64-bit longs are fine, and preferred in that kind of environment. Many applications assume longs are 32 bits, but those are already broken. Market pressure may make you cater to them anyway, sadly.

subject: NBBY
q: What does the symbol NBBY in sys/param.h under 4.3 BSD stand for?
a: Number of Bits in a BYte, usually 8. Any idiot could guess that from the name. Sigh.

subject: SYS V - What is Inode 1 ?
q: What is inode 1 reserved for in System V? The root directory is always inode 2, and I recall a manual saying inode 1 is reserved for future use.
a: Historically bad blocks were linked to inode 1, back before controllers mapped out bad sectors, so root became inode 2. Nobody does that now, but numerous dump tapes assume it, so we're stuck with it. Sigh, legacy.

subject: termcap "sg#0" capability
q: What is the semantic difference, if any, between sg#0 and no sg capability in termcap? The BSD 4.3 manual gives a default of 0, but a program behaves differently with an explicit sg#0.
a: There's no official difference. Some people tried to give sg#0 special semantics, but it was never adopted in the termcap or terminfo docs. One reply admits using sg#0 for terminals whose cookies take no screen position. That's a hack, not the spec.

subject: Sun Shutdown(8)
q: Why does Sun shutdown send so many messages to every terminal and window, and can I get fewer of them?
a: Those come from rwall, an RPC program that shutdown calls to message remote hosts. Disable the rwalld entry in /etc/inetd.conf and SIGHUP inetd. Or run rwalld as something other than root so mesg n can silence it.

subject: Phantom CPU gobbler?!
q: Why does an orphaned shell with a PPID of 1, whose user is gone, sometimes eat all the CPU on my system?
a: Most likely it's the infamous trap/signal/EOF bug: trapping and signalling plus end-of-file on stdin sends the Bourne and Korn shells into an infinite loop on some Unix versions. Or the user left a never-ending background loop script running. Kill it and educate the user.

subject: moby bignum tty accesses in /usr/adm/wtmp
q: /usr/adm/wtmp on my Xenix box grows over 500K a day, with thousands of accesses to /dev/tty02 each night. What's going on?
a: Almost certainly getty spawning and dying over and over because there's no real carrier. A Hayes modem or unplugged cable that holds Carrier Detect high does exactly this. Check the modem's carrier-detect dip switch and the serial line, or use a smarter getty like uugetty. Basic stuff.

subject: Xenix/386 v2.2.1 on a TeleVideo...Help !
q: 386 Xenix 2.2.1 won't boot on my TeleVideo 386/16, though 286 Xenix and Microport boot fine and Xenix boots on a Compaq. How do I get around this?
a: The TeleVideo disk controller is a special track-buffered board, and Xenix 386 won't work with it. Swap in a WD1003, WD1006 or compatible controller. Microport only boots because it has special code for that board. Sigh, vendor lock-in again.

subject: Problem with Computone Intelliport AT-8.
q: A Computone Intelliport-8 hangs at kernel initialization under Xenix 2.3 on one Olivetti 386 with the message D5, but the same configuration works on another model. What is going wrong?
a: Likely motherboard wait states. The Intelliport, unlike the Advantage board, chokes on certain timings on certain motherboards. I got mine working by adding a wait state to memory refresh, though it may have been the I/O waits. Fiddle with the BIOS setup.

subject: Help: Device driver from Xenix within Unix...
q: Can I link a Xenix device driver into the SCO Unix kernel, or edit the binary driver?
a: No. Drivers at least have to be recompiled, and Unix has a completely different link kit and installation. Some need code changes too. Contact the vendor for a real Unix driver. Editing a binary driver, honestly.

subject: Suggestions on big screen display systems for Xenix & X
q: Does anyone have experience with really hi-res displays and SCO X windows on Xenix? Which bigger monitors work, and what do they cost?
a: Nobody has experience with that, because it isn't supported. SCO's Xsight gives you standard VGA only, not even 800x600 yet. If you pair a Multisync 3D with a VGA card, make sure the card does 1024x768 interlaced. Mismatched cards don't get along.

subject: Corollary ??
q: Does anyone know how to reach Corollary Inc., and what else they make besides serial multiplexers? Any experience with their products?
a: Phone (714) 250-4040. They also sell an OEM multiprocessor 386 AT box, with Zenith as the big customer. One user found their 8X4 mux board and terminal concentrator the best around, with the best XENIX and 386/ix drivers. Beats Computone, anyway.

subject: Korn Shell for Xenix??
q: Does anyone know if the Korn shell is available for Xenix?
a: Yes, Aspen Technologies makes one. Took you long enough to ask. Go bother them instead of the net.

subject: SLIP for SCO Xenix?
q: Does anyone know if there is a SLIP for SCO Xenix/386? I've only seen them for Berkeley-based Unix.
a: SLIP is part of SCO TCP/IP. Honestly, check what the vendor sells before asking the net.

subject: Array Processors and Frame Grabbers for Xenix
q: Does anyone know of array processors with Xenix drivers that can do a 2D FFT, and video frame grabbers that work with Xenix?
a: We use a Weitek XL-8032 array processor, which runs fine under Xenix 386 2.3.1 and comes with compilers or library routines. For frame grabbers we use the PC-Vision FG100 and Univision UDC-2600, but we had to write our own device drivers. Welcome to Xenix.

subject: Loading Excel under VP/ix
q: Excel 2.0 won't install under VP/ix because it thinks I'm short on disk space, though I have 7000+ blocks free. How do I fool the installation into thinking I have enough space?
a: Don't fool it, point it somewhere sensible. Direct the *.ini files to a filesystem with plenty of room, since the default ones usually need modifying. Whether Windows even loads under VP/IX is another matter. Fix the config, not the installer.

subject: Fsck uses short for inode number. (Sco xenix [23]86)
q: Has anybody made a Xenix filesystem with more than 64K inodes, given that fsck and other utilities use a short for the inode number?
a: Forget it. That's a kernel limit. A directory entry is 2 bytes of inode number plus a 14 byte file name, 16 bytes total, so 16 bits is all you get. Any idiot can see why the utilities agree.

subject: Smail 3.1 and Xenix 286
q: Has anyone compiled smail 3.1 on SCO Xenix 286? I'm not sure it's possible.
a: Compile it on a 386, and the resulting binary will run on a 286. Sigh, cross-compiling isn't exactly black magic.

subject: EMACS on 386 Xenix
q: Has anyone gotten JOVE or some other Emacs clone running on a 386 Xenix system?
a: Proper GNU Emacs compiles fine under SCO Xenix 386 2.3.1 with no changes beyond configuring it. uEmacs 3.9 works on 286 Xenix but gets buggy when compiled on 386, losing track of the cursor. Use the real thing, not toys.

subject: SCRATCH FILE
q: How can I get Xenix 386 with two hard disks to get past the prompt for a scratch file name during fsck after an autoreboot?
a: Move /bin/fsck to another name such as Fsck, and write a short script as /bin/fsck that runs fsck with -t/dev/scratch followed by its arguments. The -t flag names the scratch file, so it stops asking. Basic stuff.

subject: Question about SCO Xenix and stack size
q: How can I increase the stack size for a program on SCO Xenix 2.2.1 that dumps core with "Stack overflow"?
a: Use the -F option at link time to set the stack size. Otherwise the fixhdr program does the same thing. It's in the manual, which you left in another office. Sigh.

subject: SCO Foxbase
q: How can I move data between a SCO Xenix Foxbase app and the DOS version of Fox, easily and quickly, without crunching DBFs with PKARC? How does its performance compare?
a: Just copy the .dbf files over and reindex under the other version. Job done, no conversion steps needed, and we do it all the time. Performance is excellent. Put your money into the host machine, and a 387 helps. Quit crunching things for no reason.

subject: communicating with DOS boxes
q: How can Xenix boxes send ASCII data files to a DOS box over a 1200 baud modem link without buying TERM or some other commercial package? It has to be cheap.
a: For plain ASCII, capture on the PC with any terminal emulator and cat the file on Xenix, or use cu and ~$cat to send. For error correction, get Kermit for both sides, the price is right, or pcomm. Zmodem is faster if the PC calls. Bundle with zoo or arc first.

subject: Question on adding a second terminal to a PC running SCO Xenix
q: How do I connect a second terminal, an HP-2624B on COM2, to an AT286 running SCO Xenix? I made /dev/tty2a active but it didn't work.
a: You probably have to swap the send and receive pins on your connector. A PC COM port is wired like a terminal, so a straight cable ties send to send and receive to receive. Basic serial stuff.

subject: UDS V.32 not yet dialing out for me...
q: How do I make a UDS V.32 9600 baud modem work with SCO UNIX System V/386 r3.2? Is there a Dialer entry for one?
a: Read the configuration options in the manual and first get the modem to answer the phone. Then put the dialing string in /usr/lib/uucp/Dialers to dial out and connect. Same drill for every new modem; RTFM.

subject: extracting tar.Z BBS files
q: I download tar.Z files from a BBS, run compress -d, and then tar gives 'directory checksum error' on the result. What am I doing wrong?
a: Your xmodem download is the culprit. Xmodem pads files out to multiples of 128 bytes, so the tar file ends up longer than it should be and tar chokes on the junk at the end. Use YMODEM instead, which keeps the true file size. Any idiot knows xmodem pads.

subject: nswap and swplo in /etc/default/boot
q: I'm running SCO XENIX-286 2.2.1 on an AT. The /etc/default/boot file made by mkdev fd has swplo=1144 nswap=1000, and I can't find what those mean in the boot(HW) manual page. What are they?
a: Holdovers from the old Microsoft Xenix, where swap couldn't be changed after install. swplo is the starting block of the swap area and nswap is its size, both in 1k blocks. Sigh, read up on divvy before fiddling with them.

subject: Development system
q: If I buy a Xenix development system, do I get a Microsoft C based compiler or a PCC one? Is Xenix 386 available for the Compaq 386 yet?
a: You get Microsoft C-Merge, similar to Microsoft C 3.0 for MS-DOS, and it can target Xenix or DOS. Xenix 386 isn't out yet, announced for a few months out. Buy Xenix/286 with the 386 developers toolkit now. Patience.

subject: Driver for Jumbo+ Tape Drive
q: Is there a Xenix driver for the Colorado Memory Systems Jumbo+ tape drive?
a: Yes, the JTAPE driver. One vendor sells it for about $45 and you must ask for the JUMBO XENIX OPTION or they'll put you on hold forever. A mail-order house charged $20 extra, and CMS gave a free update to 2.02 when asked. Some people regret buying the Jumbo though.

subject: Disk duplexing w/SCO Unix/Xenix
q: Is there a way to get disk mirroring or duplexing, like Novell's fault tolerance, under SCO Unix or Xenix?
a: Get the DPT disk controller and forget about it. It does on-board shadowing, taking the operating system out of the loop entirely, and caches disk accesses too. A bit expensive, but fast. Software mirroring on SCO? Don't hold your breath.

subject: Help with hard disk recovery under xenix
q: My 286 Xenix system won't boot, panicking from iinit because it can't read the root superblock, and I can't make a bootable floppy root filesystem. How can I recover without reinstalling?
a: You can make a bootable floppy root disk for a 286. Find another 286 with an empty drive, install Xenix, make the floppy root there, and come back. Moving your disk into the second system works too, but that's a pain.

subject: Problems with HDB and XENIX V/386 2.3.1
q: My HDB UUCP Permissions file on XENIX V/386 2.3.1 doesn't seem to honor the tilde in READ and WRITE. Is that a bug or am I misunderstanding something?
a: Not a bug. The tilde expands to the public directory on a uucp command line, but nothing says Permissions understands it. Spell out full path names in READ and WRITE. And READ=/ and WRITE=/ hand the whole machine to anyone who can reach it. Think about that.

subject: Keyboards and Xenix
q: My friend's 386 clone running Xenix 2.2 locks the keyboard from time to time, usually at the login prompt, and he has to flip the keyboard between AT and XT mode to free it. Is the keyboard incompatible or does Xenix have a bug?
a: It's really a flaw in the hardware keyboard controller, and SCO documented it in the release notes under Keyboard Lock-up. The fix is to patch the kernel with adb and set ledspresent to zero. Fair warning: that kills your keyboard LEDs. RTFM, the release notes.

subject: corrupted files
q: On SCO 386 2.3.1, I have 15 to 20 corrupted files in the root directory that rm says are non-existent. How do I delete them?
a: Those aren't corrupted files, your root directory is damaged. Boot to maintenance mode and run fsck first. Otherwise you may have to reinstall, since ncheck and clri won't help. And have a backup before touching anything, sigh.

subject: cp on 386 xenix problem
q: On SCO 386 Xenix 2.2.1, cp * /safe hung the system when it hit a 4.9 meg file. Do I need to play with ulimit, is it memory, or is it a cp bug?
a: Ulimit is the likely culprit; the default is about 2MB, and I wouldn't raise it much unless you're sure you need to. Not really a bug in cp. Also, if /safe is on the same filesystem as /tmp, you may have run out of tmp space.

subject: load module errors induced by array sizes in c
q: On SCO Xenix 2.1.0, why does a main() with char f[31][127] run fine but char f[32][128] dies with 'Stack overflow, Segmentation violation -- Core dumped'?
a: The _stkgro routine can't grow the stack by more than about 4046 characters at once, and the second program wants 4096. Specify a fixed stack size with the -F option of cc and the problem goes away. Typical Xenix braindamage.

subject: SCO netnews problems
q: On SCO Xenix netnews, expire with -e 5 won't remove articles that are 3-4 weeks old, and the history file dates look wrong. What's going on?
a: History file dates are stored in GMT, so stop worrying about that. For expire, rebuild your history file and run it again. Expire has always been flaky, and my own fix was to install rn. Next time get the sources.

subject: Xenix probs...
q: Our Compaq 386 running Xenix with a Computone serial card trashes its tty drivers about once a week, dropping characters, losing echo, and saying 'not a character device', usually during a UUCP connection. Has anyone seen this?
a: Computone is the common denominator. Their software is tailored to each Xenix release and needs an exact match. Someone with the same trouble fixed it by getting the install software specific to his Xenix version from Computone. Read the manual next time.

subject: pathalias slowdown
q: Pathalias on Xenix slows to a crawl and swaps heavily when I add the newest maps, such as u.usa.ca.1. Why does memory use balloon, and is there a fix short of more RAM?
a: It's not your RAM. A bad entry in the ca.1 map and a New Mexico map makes older pathalias loop. A fixed pathalias is supposed to be out. This was all over comp.mail.uucp, so read the group before posting.

subject: RTS/CTS flow-control problem with Xenix386 2.3.1 & ArNet Multiport
q: RTS/CTS flow control isn't working with Xenix386 2.3.1 and an ArNet Multiport board. CTS toggles properly at the breakout box but Xenix ignores it and sends at full speed, even with stty ctsflow. What's wrong?
a: Call SCO and ask for the RTS/CTS/Handshaking Supplement, SLS number xnx105. It fixes the broken RTS/CTS handshaking. Of course the vendor shipped it broken. Typical.

subject: setvbuf()
q: SCO Xenix's setvbuf() takes its arguments in a different order than BSD UNIX and Turbo C, and there's no prototype in stdio.h to catch it. Why the difference, and why no prototype?
a: Sigh. It was fixed in the 2.3 Development System, and the odd order was inherited from Microsoft. Prototypes for all library and system calls are now in the include files. Old objects work with the -compat flag; otherwise fix your source and recompile.

subject: Wanted - PL/1 compiler for XENIX
q: We're looking for a PL/1 compiler for XENIX V. Who sells one?
a: Only one I know of for the Unix market is from LPI. It runs on various 68000/68020 and Weco32100 boxes, with a 386 version coming. You didn't say what hardware you have, which is the first thing anyone needs to know. Sigh.

subject: mailx and big files
q: When I mail a big file of 50K or more with mailx, I get errors that it can't append to /usr/mail/user or write dead.letter, yet the text shows up in both files intact. I'm on an AT-compatible running System V/AT. Why?
a: Sigh. It's a 16-bit machine, and the count of bytes written sits in a plain short int. Past 32767 it goes negative, and the code reads n<0 as failure even though the write worked. With source, make it a long.

subject: Best source for digiboards?
q: Where can I get the best price on a DigiBoard 4 port intelligent serial board? List price is $695 to $895, and I'd consider used.
a: Check the mail-order ads in Computer Shopper. One outfit advertised the DigiBoard PC-4e at $495 and the PC-8e at $665, far under what direct from DigiBoard costs. Why pay list price?

subject: Which Version Of Xenix to Buy??
q: Which version of Xenix should I buy for a PS/2 Model 50 (286) to log in to our 4.3BSD and SunOS machines, with windowing, a C compiler and debugger, and DOS or OS/2 program support?
a: Don't. Buy PC-SLIP and X for DOS and use QuickC or MSC with CodeView. A 286 under UNIX runs only well-behaved DOS programs, nothing runs OS/2 programs under any UNIX, and sdb is no CodeView. You'd wish for a 386 anyway.

subject: Disk IO under SCO
q: Why does SCO avoid DMA for disk IO and use program control instead?
a: Because on the PC/AT architecture, and the 386 clones built from it, DMA is slow. A processor string instruction with a repeat prefix improves performance tremendously over what the DMA controller delivers. Blame IBM, not SCO.

subject: Xenix Executables
q: Why would SCO not recompile Xenix 386 utilities like grep and find for the 80386 instead of shipping 8086 and 80286 binaries?
a: If it works, don't fix it. Many utilities never need more data space, and touching a program tends to break it, plus you skip running 47 tests. A 386 mark doesn't make a better program, just one that won't run on older machines. Deliberate decision, not sloppiness.

subject: disk-drive/controller combination
q: Will a Maxtor XT4170E ESDI drive work with a WD 1007A WAH/WA2 controller? I heard the Maxtor is soft sectored and the WD1007 needs hard sectored.
a: Reports conflict. The bigger 4380 can be set for soft or hard sectoring and runs fine on the 1007A, so the 4170 probably does too. But one fellow's soft-sectored EXT-4175 flat out would not work with it. Check the exact model before believing a salesman.

subject: trouble with expr
q: expr(C) won't multiply for me. Typing expr 2 * 3 just returns "2 * 3". What am I doing wrong?
a: The shell is eating your asterisk. Escape it from the shell with a backslash: expr 2 \* 3 gives 6. The man page says so, which you'd know if you'd read it. Quoting the whole expression makes it a single string, so that fails too.

subject: MINICARTRIDGE DRIVER
q: Does anyone have a Xenix driver for the Colorado Memory Systems Jumbo 60 minicartridge tape drive? The stock Xenix minicartridge driver only looks at the two drive select lines it knows about and says the drive isn't there.
a: Ask Colorado. They'll supply the driver when asked, or charge a nominal fee. We ran the Jumbo on a Wyse that way. Why you'd bother the net before calling the vendor, I don't know.

subject: nroff driver for LaserJet IIP
q: Does anyone have an nroff driver for an HP LaserJet IIP, for use with Xenix 2.3.3 and Text Processing System 2.3?
a: Not nroff, but uunet has a troff for the LaserJet II called psroff. Go fetch it and quit asking.

subject: Getting Fsanalyze to compile on Xenix
q: How can I get fsanalyze to compile on Xenix 2.3.x devsys? It's missing definitions like SUPERBOFF, FsOkay and BOFF.
a: Get an up-to-date version. Fsanalyze patchlevel 3 compiles fine under XENIX 2.3.0 and with harmless warnings under 2.3.1. The patches went through comp.sources.bugs two years ago. You don't need GNU C for this. Keep up.

subject: Hanging up + resetting the modem from a script file?
q: How can a cron job on SCO Xenix check whether anyone is logged in on the modem line tty1A and, if not, reset and hang up the modem? uuchat didn't give the right results.
a: Run disable tty1A then enable tty1A from cron. They refuse to act if someone's logged in, otherwise they drop DTR, raise it and set the line up again. Or kill the getty so DTR drops and the modem resets itself. Not rocket science.

subject: cwd help needed
q: How do I write the equivalent of alias cd 'cd \!* ; echo $cwd' under csh on SCO? Is there an equivalent of $cwd?
a: No $cwd, so use pwd in backticks. Put the directory in your prompt: set prompt="`pwd` : " and alias cd 'cd \!*;set prompt = "`pwd` : "'. Works fine, no fuss.

subject: how do you determine end of tape? (floppy)
q: How does SCO Xenix tar know when it hits the end of a floppy so it can prompt for another? I want to pipe a program's output across several floppies.
a: tar reads the media size from /etc/default/tar, or you give it on the command line with the k option for kilobytes. Better yet, use bundle, which already handles multi-volume. This was done years ago, sigh.

subject: Incomplete Xenix- Help?
q: I bought a used copy of Xenix 2.1 for my 286 and it's missing disks. Does Xenix let me open a DOS window to run MS-DOS tasks, and can I get just the missing disks?
a: Xenix 286 does NOT run DOS tasks. You need a 386, Xenix 386 and an extra package like VP/ix or DosMerge. As for the missing disks, the N1 boot disk and the activation card are your proof of purchase, so good luck. Buy used, get used.

subject: Simulating vfork under SCO Xenix
q: I'm porting tcl to SCO Xenix and don't know the Berkeley vfork. How do I simulate it?
a: Just #define vfork fork. That works if the child only execs another program. If code modifies variables after the vfork, you're out of luck, since Xenix can't emulate that cleanly. vfork is only a performance trick anyway.

subject: Need help with SLIP
q: Is anyone successfully using the SLIP package that comes with SCO's TCP/IP? Pings between two Xenix machines send data out the serial line but nothing comes back.
a: The old beta release has problems, but the version in release 1.0.1h works, albeit slowly and inefficiently. There's no RFC 1144 support, so dialup over slow modems is uncomfortable. Direct lines between two machines work, though dialup is iffy. Get the current release.

subject: cc available with Xenix System V?
q: Is the C compiler standard with SCO Xenix 386? Mine came with only about 12 disks and I'm afraid it's a toy version.
a: No. Xenix 386 is sold in separate packages: Runtime, Development System, Graphics, Text Processing and Networking. The C compiler and standard libraries live in the Dev System, which you didn't buy. Gcc won't save you, you still need the libraries and include files. Typical vendor nickel-and-diming.

subject: increasing pseudo ttys limit
q: Is there an easy way to raise SCO Xenix's limit of 16 pseudo ttys? A customer wants to run Xsight, mscreen and TCP/IP on one machine and 16 isn't enough.
a: Get Chip Salzenberg's PTY package for SCO Xenix and install it. Works just fine for a PTY session manager here. Sigh, check the archives before asking next time.

subject: C libraries/include files (Was Xenix Patch Kit)
q: Is there any way to get a set of public domain libraries and include files for GCC or some other C compiler that runs on SCO OpenDeskTop 1.1?
a: Not yet. A BSD networking release 2 tape with a complete C library is on order from UCB, once the US export people approve it. Then the Xenix system calls get added and libc gets built, maybe by November. Watch this space and quit nagging.

subject: Non-destructive backspace
q: My Wyse-60 terminal's backspace is non-destructive on SCO Xenix 2.3.2d, but my client wants it destructive. Is there a simple way to change termcap to do that?
a: Wrong place to look. Termcap isn't it; the backspace action is controlled by stty. Put stty erase "^H" in /etc/profile, and for vi use the sequence ^V^H. You did try RTFM, but apparently not the right page.

subject: Cron problems
q: On SCO Xenix 2.3.2, cron refuses to start each day's jobs automatically, so I have to run an "at" command every morning to kick it. The process is still resident. Why, and how do I fix it?
a: Well-known bug in SCO Xenix 2.X cron. It goes to sleep when no jobs are scheduled for long periods. SCO's recommended fix is a cron job that runs /bin/true once a minute. Yes, really.

subject: Panic at shutdown
q: On SCO Xenix 2.3.4, running /etc/shutdown gives a kernel panic, but sync;sync;haltsys doesn't. The panic also destroys disk mirroring. Any ideas?
a: Shutdown is a shell script, so put an echo with an incrementing number after each step and find the offending command. My guess is it kills a disk mirroring daemon, so filter that process out. Another SCO box panicked because /usr was on a separate partition. Sigh.

subject: Sys V386 binaries working under SCO Xenix 2.3.2 ???
q: Why do SysV386 COFF binaries, like groff built for ISC, run under SCO Xenix 2.3.2? Are there any limitations?
a: Not isolated at all. XENIX could do COFF before the SysV vendors could do XENIX, thanks to the binary compatibility agreements between the big players. Limits: no COFF 387 emulation, so you need a real coprocessor. Shared libs live under /shlib and work fine. Old news, really.

subject: groff binaries from anomaly (grodvi problems)
q: With the groff binaries, grodvi gives unreadable characters. Running groff -Tdvi on a one-line file of "Hello world" gives binary output. Shouldn't ditroff output contain only printable characters?
a: Not with groff -Tdvi. You get real dvi, which is a binary format. If you want ascii ditroff output, say groff -Z -Tdvi. Read the groff script in /usr/local/bin to see what it does. Honestly, RTFM.

subject: installing on SPARCstation running 4.0.3
q: Are there known problems installing InterViews 3.0 beta on a SPARCstation running SunOS 4.0.3? The cpp segfaults or bus-errors on several files.
a: That's the SunOS 4.0.3 cpp being broken. Add +i to the C++ driver, or use a better cpp, such as the one in 4.1.1, Sun C++ 2.0 or gnu cpp. Also 4.0.3 lacks waitpid(), so ibuild won't link. Upgrade already.

subject: help
q: I get undefined symbol errors linking my Unidraw application with InterViews using the AT&T C++ 2.0 compiler. What additional libraries do I need?
a: Your libraries are in the wrong order and you left out Xext. Use imake and it gives you the right list. Otherwise read the imake templates and copy the same libraries by hand. That's what they're for.

subject: Glyphs, Graphic, Unidraw, IV2.6 and IV3.0 !
q: I want a Glyph subclass like Background but that uses a Pattern instead of a solid color, in InterViews 3.0. Should I use Unidraw or go back to 2.6, and are there docs specific to 3.0 or Unidraw, and is the 2.6 reference manual available?
a: Just use a color with an alpha value less than one. Textures, which are more powerful than patterns, may come to Canvas someday. Unidraw man pages and a tutorial ship with 3.0, and the 2.6 reference manual is only the 2.6-specific man pages. Read what ships.

subject: COM-PORTS 3 & 4, TELIX
q: Does Telix for Windows exist, and can I get Telix 3.12 to work under Windows 3.0? Otherwise, what's a good comm program?
a: There is no Telix for Windows, so quit looking. Telix 3.12 runs fine as a windowed application from a PIF file, so make sure you made one. For another comm program, WinQVT is shareware on SIMTEL-20 or cica. Not great, but it's free.

subject: mgr questsions/notes
q: How can I iconify a window in MGR, fix the termcap entry so less works, and is there an MGR mailing list?
a: Can't help with icons or the mailing list. For termcap, use the entry generated by set_emacs and it works fine. Resizing doesn't notify programs, so emacs gets confused. Sigh, read the docs.

subject: SVGA on Windows 3.0
q: I set up Windows 3.0 for super VGA with a Diamond SpeedStar 1Meg card, but the logo appears and then the screen goes blank. If I remove HIMEM.SYS from CONFIG.SYS it runs fine, but only in real mode. What's wrong?
a: Probably a memory conflict in 386 Enhanced mode, where Windows grabs the address space your video card uses. Test with win /s first. Then add EMMExclude=A000-C7FF to the [386 Enh] section of SYSTEM.INI, trimmed to what your card really uses. Read the card manual, it's not magic.

subject: Window Toolkits and Systems for a bunch of systems.
q: I'm writing an interactive graphics program that has to port across VAX-VMS, VAX-Unix, Sun, Apollo and several window systems (X, NEWS, SunView, HP). Is there a graphics toolkit that gives a common interface so I only write the graphics code once?
a: Open Look is supposed to do that, with the same toolkit calls linked against an X11 or NeWS library, though nobody's seen it working yet. One shop uses Stepstone's ICpak-201 in Objective-C, which sits on a layer called Earthbase. Basic graphics, no GKS or PHIGS, and the vendor promises X11 someday.

subject: Windows 3.1? & also .GIF <-> .BMP
q: I've only heard rumors of a Windows 3.1. Does anyone have information on it, or know where I could get some?
a: Go read comp.windows.ms. There have been plenty of articles lately on the advancements in Windows 3.1. Rumors, honestly; try looking before you post.

subject: more help needed... : (
q: My AmiPro word processing document is nearly a megabyte. Is there a utility to split a file across floppies and restore it on the hard drive of my other computer?
a: Fastback Plus. It spans multiple floppies automatically and can compress the data to cut down on disks. Sigh, backup utilities have existed for ages; you didn't need to ask the whole net.

subject: "funny" languages; interfaces
q: Which windowing system gives the best support for languages like Arabic, Hebrew and Chinese, meaning proportional spacing, alternate wordwrap and extended character standards rather than just fonts?
a: The Mac is the only machine I know with direct support for all those, you just boot a different OS version. MS-Windows is much easier to customize than Motif, which is full of buggy, undocumented behavior. Don't expect miracles from X.

subject: Strange Error message
q: After installing Windows 3 on a 386SX under MS-DOS 4.01, starting it gives "INVALID COMMAND.COM, UNABLE TO LOAD COMMAND PROCESSOR, SYSTEM HALTED". Where should I look?
a: Set COMSPEC to your real command.com, for example set comspec=c:\dos\command.com. Make sure that command.com matches your DOS version and isn't a leftover from an older one. Another user fixed it by installing the DOS 4.01 corrective release. Basic housekeeping, kid.

subject: Opening screen disappeared...
q: After trying new Trident drivers from cica and switching back to the old VGA driver, I lost the opening Windows logo and only get a black screen with blue background. What do I need to do to get it back?
a: Don't hand-edit system.ini and win.ini. Run SETUP from DOS in the Windows directory and pick the change-drivers option; that switches Trident drivers cleanly. Many people use 'win :' to skip the logo, so odd that you'd want it.

subject: Unrecoverable Application Error
q: Can I run the Trident SVGA drivers for Windows in 640x480x256 mode with only 256K on the card? The screen got mangled.
a: Yup, you need 512K for that mode, since 640x480 at 256 colors is more than 256K. With 256K the card can only do 640x400x256, if memory serves. Do the multiplication before you blame the drivers.

subject: Can I use Quick C 2.0?:
q: Can I use Quick C 2.0 with the Windows SDK to write Windows apps, instead of paying for MSC 5.1?
a: Yes, the official Microsoft line is that QC 2.0 can build Windows apps. Some people on GENIE had trouble with it, but a fix was posted. Sigh, nothing is ever simple with Microsoft.

subject: Environment space for DOS appl. under Windows
q: DOS applications run from Windows get too little environment space, about 224 bytes in standard mode. How do I make Windows allocate more? I've already read TFM.
a: Change COMMAND.PIF to run COMMAND.COM /E:#### with the environment size you want. That's the one that worked. A hackish alternative is a long dummy SET variable run from a batch file. Ugly, but that's Windows for you.

subject: Windows Stat packages
q: Do standard stat packages like Minitab or Systat have a Windows version or announced plans for one, and do they support DDE?
a: SAS has announced a Windows version for late 1991 that will support DDE. Bring hardware: a 386, 6 MB of memory, a math coprocessor and a 110 MB disk. Typical bloated vendor nonsense. Nobody mentioned Minitab or Systat.

subject: DOS 4.0 Himem?
q: Does DOS 4.0's himem.sys work with Windows 3.0? I'm having trouble with himem on my 286.
a: No. Throw the DOS himem.sys away. Windows 3.0 documentation says plainly that DOS's HIMEM won't work and you must use the one that ships with Windows. The Windows one is about 15K dated 5-90. RTFM.

subject: Databases....
q: Does anyone know of a good, easy, powerful database program for Windows 3 under $200, something along the lines of Q&A for DOS?
a: Q+E goes for about $99 and handles dBase and a few other formats. Querying and editing are fine, but report generation is simple and there's no real programming. Superbase2 runs around $200 and lets you stick Windows graphics in. Don't expect miracles.

subject: Info on Languages
q: Does anyone know of very high-level language compilers or interpreters, like Lisp or Prolog, running under Windows?
a: Not much, but I believe ACTOR, an object-oriented language, runs under MS Windows. Go look it up, and stop expecting Lisp on a PC to be a big selection.

subject: About Multimedia Extension for Windows.
q: Has Multimedia Extensions for Windows been released, and how do I get it? Is it in Windows 3.1, and what software does it support, like Toolbook?
a: It's out now, but only with an MPC from vendors like Tandy or CompuAdd, or via an upgrade kit from the MediaVision or SoundBlaster folks. Windows 3.1 won't include it; its big feature is TrueType. Toolbook works. Everything that runs under 3.0 runs with it.

subject: What is the status of WFW 2.0 ?
q: Has Word for Windows 2.0 started shipping, and what enhancements over 1.1 justify the $120 upgrade price?
a: It's in manufacturing and should be on shelves next week. You get OLE apps for WordArt, graphing, drawing and equations, a grammar checker, mixed portrait and landscape, sections, shading and borders, new tables, the tech ref in help, and more macro features. Read the box.

subject: printing from terminal programme
q: Has anyone gotten printer transparent mode (ESC [ 5 i and ESC [ 4 i) working in the Windows 3.0 Terminal program? If it's broken, is there a Windows terminal program where it works?
a: Windows Terminal is too brain dead to bother with. WinQVT does work for this, I've used it. Try a real terminal program next time instead of the toy that ships in the box.

subject: Logitech mouse
q: Has anyone had problems with Logitech mice in Windows where the pointer stops moving as if it hit an invisible wall?
a: Have you tried cleaning the thing? Pop it open and clean the ball, and especially the little white rollers it rides on. They gum up and hang on one axis or the other. Basic maintenance, folks.

subject: C++ with Windows?
q: Has anyone used C++ with MS Windows? Would it be possible if you have a C++ translator that generates MS C?
a: Should be no problem, as long as the MS C you're feeding it uses link 4.0 or greater. That's the basic requirement, from what I've heard. Check your linker version before whining about it.

subject: Debugging with the Slow boot Windows
q: Has anyone used Codeview with the slow boot debugging version of Windows? There's no WIN.COM file to hand to the debugger.
a: Run Kernel.exe for the debug version, and Codeview works with that too. For a slow boot win/386, rename command.com to win86.com and win86 to win.com, then run Codeview from the v86 command.com. The 2.1 SDK update notes cover it. RTFM, people.

subject: SCSI drives with WIN3
q: Has anyone used a SCSI drive and controller with Windows 3.0 alongside an IDE drive? Which controller works, and are there compatibility problems?
a: Yes, it works. Adaptec AHA1542B with a CDC Wren IV, and a PLI Fast Card with Mac SCSI drives, run fine under Windows 3.0. Program Manager and File Manager see them. Disk utilities like Norton won't, since they hook the drivers. Obvious, really.

subject: Unix Windows under Win30?
q: Has anyone written a Windows 3.0 program that gives multiple independent Unix login windows over one connection, like Unixwindows on the Atari? I'd like it to work with any comm software.
a: If you've got an ethernet card, you can just log into the Unix machine several times. A shareware package for Win 3.0 called winqvtnet does it. Not quite what you asked, but nobody's written your fancy comm-software version.

subject: DOS batch files
q: How can I run a batch file in a Windows 3.0 window and then get a DOS prompt? With my PIF file, the window closes or goes inactive when the batch file finishes.
a: Turn off the Close Window on Exit check box in the PIF file. If that fails, use CALL and the batch name as the program name. Basic stuff, if you'd read the manual.

subject: Windows installation disk compression?
q: How do I get the compressed Windows documentation and program files back off the installation disks without reinstalling everything?
a: RTFM. Use the expand utility, something like expand a:foo.txt c: with the file name and destination. It's probably on the main setup disk. Doesn't anyone read manuals anymore?

subject: Win3, Netware, and swapfile
