q: How do I make a Windows 3 swapfile when running a shared copy from a Netware server? The swapfile program says other applications are running.
a: Use your hard disk, that makes sense. The culprit is NWPOPUP.EXE, an invisible application always running under Novell. Disable broadcast in the network menu of the control panel before running the swapfile program. It's not in the user manual, only in a document file. Typical.

subject: Windows Dialog Box
q: How do I make a modeless dialog box in Windows that also contains a menu bar? It fails when the dialog is a child window.
a: You can't. A child window can't have its own menu. Replace the main window's menu with the one belonging to the currently active child, and forward the menu messages to that child. Windows being Windows, it's a kludge.

subject: extended or expanded memory for codeview under win386
q: How do I run CodeView under Windows/386 with SDK 2.1 on a PS/2 Model 80 with 2MB, when CodeView wants expanded memory and I only have extended?
a: Read the README that came with the SDK. Rename WIN86.COM to WIN.COM in the windows/386 directory, then copy COMMAND.COM to WIN86.COM there. Run win386 and you get a DOS shell in a virtual machine where extended memory looks expanded. Run CodeView from that shell.

subject: Global Field Updates in WFW
q: How do I update all the fields in a WFW document at once, instead of pressing F9 after every field I insert?
a: Select the whole document, either by control-clicking in the left margin or with ctrl and keypad 5, then press F9. Any idiot with the manual would know this, but fine.

subject: Codeview for Windows problem.
q: I can't get CodeView for Windows working on my 386 with Windows/386 2.1. All I get is a blinking cursor, though commands still work. Do I need a second monitor, or does it work in a virtual DOS machine?
a: That blinking cursor is normal. You're in a 386 Windows virtual machine but the GUI hasn't started yet, an odd situation. Honestly, CVW is virtually unusable without a second monitor. Best used with Windows/286 and 386-to-the-max. Welcome to Microsoft tools.

subject: Standard Mode ... How?!?!?
q: I have a 386sx with 1M RAM and should be able to run Windows in standard mode, but himem.sys says no extended memory found. How do I set up himem or emm386 for standard mode?
a: Have you tried running it as "win /s"? With 2 megs I have to force enhanced mode, so you may have to force standard mode. Try the switch before fiddling with config files.

subject: Opening screen revisited
q: I have an RLE4 picture for the Windows opening screen, but COPY WIN.CNF/B + STRT.RLE/B WIN.COM gives no picture and goes right to Program Manager. What's the right command?
a: You left out the logo driver file. Use COPY WIN.CNF/B + [CEV]GALOGO.LGO/B + STRT.RLE/B WIN.COM, picking the right one for your display. The whole file must stay under 64k, since it's a COM file after all. Sigh.

subject: No drive D: in Windows-3
q: I installed Windows 3.0 on a single 40M drive split into two 20M partitions, and it can't see drive D:. Do I need a special device driver in config.sys?
a: No. With MS-DOS 3.30 or 4.01, DOS handles the second partition itself, no driver needed. Just create the partitions with DOS's FDISK. If you used some other program, back up, then repartition and reformat with DOS. Don't go cargo-culting drivers.

subject: win/r
q: I'm trying to set up a permanent swapfile in Windows, but I can't get Windows to start in /r mode. I only get the hourglass in the middle of the screen. What should I do?
a: Remove any load= or run= lines from your win.ini, then type win/r and it should start fine. Sigh, that's the usual culprit. Also, Microsoft quietly withdrew the blanket swapfile advice. Unless you run lots of DOS apps, skip the swapfile; on a slow disk it just drags Windows down.

subject: WfW Macro FileOpen Convertion confirmation
q: In a Word for Windows macro, FileOpen always brings up a dialog asking me to confirm converting the .RFT file. I tried SendKeys after FileOpen and it had no effect. Any ideas?
a: You put SendKeys in the wrong place. Issue it BEFORE FileOpen, since it stuffs the keys into the buffer and they hit the dialog when it appears. Use the {enter} mnemonic. Basic stuff, really.

subject: Anybody using Win3 with DOS 4.01?
q: Is anybody running Windows 3 under DOS 4.01 with one big partition? Should I avoid switching, and what problems will I run into?
a: Several folks run Win3 under 4.01 on big partitions with no problems at all, and it installs fine. Grumble: one says wait for DOS 5.0, which supposedly fixes the non-reentrancy problems. Those bugs in Word for Windows aren't DOS's fault.

subject: Windows term
q: Is there a DOS shell under MS Windows, like xterm under X? I want a normal shell-like window.
a: Just run COMMAND.COM in a window. Make a COMMAND.PIF with PIFEDIT, fill in the blanks at the top, and UNCHECK 'Directly writes to SCREEN'. Then start it from the MS-DOS Executive or with WIN COMMAND. You can run several at once. Hardly a pipe dream.

subject: Scheduler applications for Windows 3.0
q: Is there a Windows 3.0 scheduler with alarms and recurring appointments like Sidekick Plus Time Planner? Sidekick doesn't work as a scheduler under Windows 3, and I'm willing to pay.
a: Try Desktop Set from Okna Corp. It has a well-designed interface and an advanced mode that removes the window border, and PC Magazine reviewed it on Jan 30, 1990. Ask them whether any demo disks are left, and quit whining about TSRs.

subject: Windows communications packages that work?
q: Is there a Windows communications package that works without losing characters? Procomm and the SDK's TTY sample both lose characters. Is there a standard fix?
a: Try the Windows version of Kermit, on the Columbia Kermit archive in kermit/a, files starting with win. No lost characters here, though only at 2400 baud. Hardly a stress test, but it works.

subject: Displaying graphics in windows
q: Is there a way in Windows 3.0 to display graphics from a non-windows application, like a Kermit Tektronix terminal emulation, in a window instead of full screen?
a: On a 386, set the PIF settings to run it windowed, or hit Alt-Enter while it's running. Otherwise Windows just suspends a DOS graphics app unless it's full screen. Read the manual before blaming Windows for everything.

subject: Accessing a remote file server from Win 3.0
q: Is there a way to access a remote NetWare file server from within Windows 3.0, and can I do it while running QVT/Net at the same time?
a: Run the Windows install program to add NetWare support, then attach from the control panel or, somewhat, the file manager. You need Windows-compatible IPX and NET3/NET4/NET5. Running alongside QVT/Net generally can't be done; the Mark and Release utilities make it possible but ugly.

subject: Is there a Ultrascript PC driver for Windows 3?
q: Is there an Ultrascript PC driver for Windows 3.0?
a: Not yet. QMS/Ultrascript said there would be no Windows 3.0 upgrade for at least a couple of months, and the workaround is running it in real mode. Don't hold your breath, given how slow they've always been.

subject: ftp list for windows?
q: Is there any big ftp site for Windows software? Most ftp sites I know carry far less than an average BBS.
a: Grab the general ftp list, ftp.list, from pilot.njin.net by anonymous ftp. It's also posted to comp.sources.wanted and comp.misc, though it's not always current. For Windows 3.0 stuff, the best and only place is cica.cica.indiana.edu in pub/pc/win3. Read the list before asking.

subject: LINK4 problem
q: LINK4 aborts with a fatal error saying the line is too long when I list about 15 .OBJ files on the first line of my link file. Backslash at the end of the line didn't work as a continuation. How do I get around this?
a: Backslash? This isn't RC. Put a '+' at the end of the line instead. The '+' tells LINK4 the next line continues the list of objects. Renaming everything to one-character names, honestly. Read the linker docs.

subject: 386SX,HIMEM.SYS,SMARTDRV.SYS
q: My 16 MHz Gateway 386SX crashes with parity errors when HIMEM.SYS and SMARTDRV.SYS are loaded, but works fine when I turn off turbo and run at half speed. What's causing this?
a: Sounds like your motherboard is set to zero wait state with RAM that isn't quite fast enough. Get into the setup program at bootup and add one wait state. Marketing says 0 wait state, physics says otherwise.

subject: Trident svga card and the may91 drivers
q: My 1M Trident SVGA card (8900c) fails with the May 1991 Windows drivers. It complains vddtvga.386 is corrupt, and Setup hangs the machine. The older drivers work. What can I do?
a: Delete the old Trident drivers from the Windows directory and the Windows system directory, then try the new ones again. Sounds daft, and nobody can tell you why, but it fixed the same problem for someone else. Stale files lying around, I suppose.

subject: Couldn't get WinQVT 4.51 - Why?
q: My BITFTP request for WNQVT451.ZIP from cica.cica.indiana.edu got 'No such file or directory'. What did I do wrong?
a: You typed the file name in UPPER case. Unix is case sensitive, so use lower case. Those darn Unix systems, eh? Think before you mail the net.

subject: OmniPage and Windows 3.0
q: My OmniPage 2.12 won't work properly under Windows 3.0. Is that the latest version, and when is there a Windows upgrade?
a: No, it isn't the latest. OmniPage 3.0 is out, since I just got the upgrade notice in the mail. You should probably get mad at your dealer, like you said.

subject: 1024x768 Interlaced Monitors
q: My Super-VGA card and multisync monitor flicker terribly at 1024x768 interlaced under Windows 3. How can anyone use this, and do some card and monitor combos do worse than others?
a: Flicker depends far more on the screen redraw frequency than on interlacing. Keep it at 60Hz or above; a Paradise VGA-1024 does 1024x768 interlaced at 89Hz with no flicker. Also check the card is set up for the right monitor, since a wrong mode flickers badly.

subject: Problem seen in 286vs386 machine
q: My Windows program allocates about 2K from the global heap and keeps it locked for its whole life. On a 386 Compaq, the DOS window complains of not enough memory to display a directory. What's wrong?
a: Locking global memory for the life of your app is a HORRIBLE NO-NO. It puts a brick wall in memory and makes big allocations hard for everyone else. Unlock it when you yield control. The About box memory figure is only an approximation anyway.

subject: Windows and Floating Point
q: My Windows programs using floating point under MSC 5.1 and SDK 1.04 don't run at all, and nothing happens when I double-click the .exe. What's going on?
a: Likely your float parameters. Old-style K&R prototypes that declare floats cause a mere warning in MS C 5.10 but generate code that doesn't work. Change them to doubles or use ANSI prototypes (see Microsoft Q29686). Also check your math libs.

subject: XVTDRAW
q: My copy of XVTDRAW suddenly posts a scaling error window and now takes up the whole screen. Is there some .ini file it reads?
a: It doesn't play well with PostScript printers, and that's when the scaling error shows up. It works OK with lower-resolution printers. Pick a different printer driver.

subject: himem.sys problem
q: My himem.sys is incompatible with my 12mhz 286 clone. Is there a substitute I can get?
a: Make sure you're using the himem.sys that shipped with Windows 3.0, not the ones from various DOS distributions or Windows 2.x. Also, himem.sys only installs if you have extended memory, not expanded only. Check before blaming the machine.

subject: NDOSEDIT type utility that works with multiple Windows 3.0 DOS boxes??
q: NDOSEDIT makes Windows 3.0 kill my DOS boxes when I run two or more. Is there a DOS command line editor that works in Windows 3.0 DOS boxes?
a: Get 4DOS. It replaces COMMAND.COM, has a built-in command line editor, and works fine in multiple Windows 3.0 DOS boxes. Or don't load such TSRs in AUTOEXEC.BAT: have the DOS icon run a batch file that loads the TSR, then COMMAND.COM. Honestly, RTFM.

subject: Windows prints garbage on Novell
q: On our Novell 3.11 network, Windows prints reams of garbage from user accounts, though it sometimes prints fine as supervisor. What causes this?
a: One fix: edit win.ini by hand and replace all the LPT?: entries with LPT?.PRN:, or pick LPT?.OS2: in Control Panel Printers. Worked for me. Windows and its printer ports, what a mess.

subject: QEMM 5.11 / Windows 3
q: Running QEMM 5.11 on a 386SX with DOS 4.01, some DOS programs can't find enough memory, but they work with himem. What's wrong?
a: QEMM puts a 64K EMS page frame in the 640K range if there's no big enough gap above it. Run QEMM TYPE MAP to see. If you don't need EMS, put FRAME=NONE on the device=qemm386.sys line, or use a smaller 16, 32 or 48K frame.

subject: TurboP 5, TurboC 2, under Win3
q: Under Windows 3, how do I choose an icon for Turbo Pascal, which I run from a group? It only shows the DOS icon.
a: Turbo Pascal isn't a Windows application, so there's no icon in its .EXE file. Go to Change Icon and type the name of an .ICO file you want to use. Basic stuff, really.

subject: Copyright Symbol in AboutBox
q: Using the Windows dialog editor, how do I put the copyright symbol, the little c in a circle, in a dialog box?
a: It's character 169. Hold ALT and type 0169 on the numeric keypad. Or enter the string without it, then edit the .dlg and put a \251 where you want it. It's a screen character, so don't expect printing to match.

subject: DVI Viewer for Windows 3.0
q: Was a new version of DVIMSWIN announced that works under Windows 3.0, and where can I get it by FTP?
a: It's on c.scs.uiuc.edu, at 128.174.90.3. Go fetch it.

subject: .DLL files under Windows 3.0
q: What are .DLL files under Windows 3.0 used for?
a: Dynamic Link Libraries are subroutines linked at runtime instead of link time. Programs don't each carry their own copy, so .exe files stay smaller, and only one copy sits in memory when several apps need it. Statically linked libraries are the wasteful way.

subject: CorelDraw and Typefoundry - what can I do with them?
q: What can I do with CorelDraw's WFN-Boss and ZSoft Type Foundry fonts? Can I make PostScript fonts or Windows 3.0 screen fonts from them?
a: Yes. Publisher's Type Foundry makes PostScript, HP LaserJet and Windows screen fonts, plus Ventura/GEM ones. WFNBoss makes OTL files for it and for SoftType. PTF runs poorly under Windows 3.0, SoftType runs fine. Read the docs.

subject: Windows DataBases ?
q: What can you tell me about FormBase from Xerox and Superbase from Precision Software for Windows? I need a database that can relate a field to a file such as TIFF or EPS.
a: FormBase isn't a database at all, just a form maker for purchase orders and invoices. Superbase 4 is a fully relational database with its own BASIC-ish language. It handles WMF, EPS, PCX, TIF and BMP through external file fields, not stored in the database. Read the box next time.

subject: ScreenPeace--Where's Andersen?
q: What happened to the author of ScreenPeace, the charityware screen saver? My contribution check wasn't cashed.
a: ScreenPeace was bought by Icom Simulation and is now called Intermission, I believe. The author's no longer accepting payments and asked that it be removed from all electronic services. Keep your money.

subject: QEMM 5.1
q: What's the final word on QEMM 5.1 with 386 Enhanced mode under Windows 3.0? Is it completely compatible?
a: Not happily. 5.1 doesn't get along with Windows, but 5.12 works just fine. You have to ask Qdeck for the update. Honestly, any idiot reading the version numbers could've guessed that.

subject: Driver for Star NX1000?
q: Where can I find a Windows driver for the Star NX1000 printer that does color?
a: The manual lists printers it emulates, and one is the Epson EX-800, which does color. The driver in the Win 3 distribution supports it, though it won't use the printer's fonts. Microsoft's NX-1000 driver has no color, and it's on cica. Read the manual.

subject: Location of LAUNCH program?
q: Where can I find a shareware or public domain program called LAUNCH that puts up a menu you click on to start applications? It was mentioned in a recent PC Mag.
a: Can't say where LAUNCH lives, but go grab Usher or Backmenu from cica, once it's back up. Usher has redefinable menus for both buttons and sticky menus. Backmenu never worked for me. Do try reading the directory listing first.

subject: Looking for a OKIDATA 182 Driver
q: Where can I get a Windows 3 printer driver for an Okidata 182 printer?
a: Don't bother hunting for one. The ML 182 emulates an Epson, so use the generic Epson 9-pin driver that comes with Windows. Works fine. Ask the dealer first next time.

subject: Compuserve <---> Windows
q: Where on CompuServe are the Windows discussion groups and download sections?
a: Windows is covered in MSAPP, MSLANG, MSBASIC, MSEXCEL, WINNEW, WINADV, WINAPA, WINAPB, WINAPC and MSOPSYS, and occasionally MSDOS. The libraries are in those forums too. Hardly mundane, just read the forum list.

subject: 24bit Windows Cards
q: Which 24-bit color cards have Windows 3.0 drivers that actually display full 24-bit color at 640x480 or higher?
a: One that works is the Opta card: 4 megabytes of VRAM, a TI-34020, TIGA interface, and full 24-bit color up to 1024x768 under Windows 3.0. The driver is a little buggy, mind you, but performance is good. Nothing's perfect.

subject: Problem in using BMP files as background in enhenced mode
q: Why can't I use a 780K BMP file as the Windows 3.0 background in 386 enhanced mode when it works fine in standard mode? I have an Orchid ProII card.
a: Looks like a bug in the ProII driver that chokes on 1024x768 images in enhanced mode. Get PICLAB from cica and clip the image to 1023x768 with "clip 1023 768". You'll need WINGIF to convert the BMP to a GIF first. Nobody will notice the missing pixel.

subject: RegisterClass in DLL
q: Why does RegisterClass inside my DLL's LibInit work a few times (usually 3) and then fail?
a: Registering the class with the DLL's instance handle causes exactly this. Restart the app without exiting Windows and the second RegisterClass fails. Use the calling application's instance handle instead. Works fine if only one app uses the DLL. Skipping RegisterClass on re-init just broke CreateWindow.

subject: Problem with printing using 256-color driver
q: Why does printing on my NEC P2200 give a blank page and a form feed when I use a 256-color Windows driver on my Trident 8900 Super VGA card? 16-color drivers work fine.
a: The original Video7 256-color driver Microsoft handed to OEMs is full of subtle bugs, especially in monochrome bitmap handling. Printer drivers render into bitmaps through the display driver, so they get wrecked. Nag your video board vendor for newer drivers. Not much else to do.

subject: Why not PM ?
q: Why is there so little traffic about OS/2 Presentation Manager compared to MS-Windows in the Microsoft windowing newsgroup? Why did you choose Windows over PM?
a: Market, plain and simple. Most PCs out there are DOS machines, and with Windows you just type win app and it runs. Nobody's moving to OS/2 in droves, and it's unclear they ever will. Port to PM when the customers show up.

subject: Going Windows 3.0 without Going Broke - Cheap Apps, anyone?
q: Windows 3.0 costs way more than $90 once you buy apps. What cheap Windows 3.0 applications are there, like word processors, desktop publishers, and terminal programs, under $150 to $200?
a: Ami Pro goes for about $130 or less if you shop, and it may spare you a DTP package. JustWrite is reportedly a bargain. Windows Terminal is fine without scripting, plus shareware like UniComm and QVT on SIMTEL and cica. Spend $60 on ATM.

subject: Windows 3.0 crashing in 386 enh mode
q: Windows 3.0 in 386 enhanced mode crashes back to DOS when I run WordPerfect 5.1 in a window or Ventura Publisher. They run in standard mode. What's wrong?
a: The poster found the culprit by experimenting: disabling the RAM drive in config.sys let Ventura run in enhanced mode. Suspect your old ramdrive.sys. Try that instead of whining about it.

subject: Background image in Windows 3.0
q: Windows 3.0 picks a different background .BMP every time it starts, even though I put wallpaper=chess.BMP in WIN.INI, and it rewrites that line on exit. What's setting it at random?
a: Probably not Windows itself. If you run Screen Peace with random wallpaper checked, it picks a new one each start and rewrites your win.ini. Otherwise hunt for some other utility, usually a screen blanker, doing it. Check your own startup junk first.

subject: Corel Draw, AT&T 6300 problem
q: With CorelDraw 1.21 on Windows 3 on an AT&T 6300, the text box won't take multiple lines and the node edit menu shows 8 choices instead of 10. Why?
a: RTFM, specifically the addendum sheet: version 1.21 needs control-ENTER for multiple lines, and 2.0 no longer does. For the menu, check your screen driver. The Windows 3.0 EGA driver is low-res only, which may be cutting off the choices.

subject: metafile format???
q: Are Windows GDI metafiles just the library calls and parameters in ASCII text? Where can I find details on the format?
a: No, .WMF files are binary. The format is documented in the Windows SDK Reference Volume 2, section 9.5. Fair warning: there are record types in real files that the book doesn't list, though most are easy to decode.

subject: Having an EXE and DLL of the same name
q: Can a Windows program have an EXE and a DLL with the same name, like XYZPROG.EXE and XYZPROG.DLL? Link complains about a self-import.
a: No. Windows only allows either a DLL or an EXE with a given name. It's a documented feature in the SDK manuals, so read them. Rename one.

subject: Help: custom controls in a dialog box
q: CreateDialog() returns NULL when my modeless dialog contains a custom control from a DLL. What am I doing wrong?
a: Probably you forgot to RegisterClass the custom control's class name. Dialog creation fails when the class isn't registered. Happens to everybody once; check the basics first.

subject: Borland C++, any graphics classes?
q: Does Borland C++ come with graphics classes that wrap Windows controls like windows, buttons and scrollbars, or is it just a compiler that can call the SDK functions?
a: It's the latter. You get the Microsoft WINDOWS.H file and make the standard Windows calls, with no class library wrapping them. Time to reinvent the wheel, I guess, or go buy someone else's classes.

subject: RLE bitmaps
q: Does anyone have RLE encoded bitmaps? I'm writing a Windows BMP reader and want to test RLE4 and RLE8 files, but all the ones I found are non-RLE.
a: Use WinGif.EXE. It reads gif and bmp files and saves bmp files in both rle4 and rle8. Make your own test files, no need to go begging on the net.

subject: SCSI and Windows w/o real mode
q: Does anyone know of a SCSI adapter that works in protected mode Windows? We only got the Adaptec card working by switching to real mode.
a: The Adaptec works fine in standard and enhanced modes. You need two drivers, adaptec.sys and aspi4dos.sys, and you load them real early. Sigh, no need to drop to real mode.

subject: Non PASCAL DLL functions
q: Has anyone made a non-PASCAL function work in a Windows DLL? I need a variable number of parameters, but the linker gives export undefined error L2022.
a: Put an underscore in front of the function name in the EXPORTS section of your .DEF file, so myFunc becomes _myFunc. Anything declared cdecl, the C calling convention, needs that. Hardly a secret, though the manual buries it.

subject: Positioning a Dialog Box
q: How can I display a dialog box at a position I specify at run time? The dialog editor hard codes an X and Y location, yet Word for Windows centers its dialogs.
a: Handle WM_INITDIALOG in your dialog proc and call MoveWindow() to put the box where you want it. That's the whole trick. Read the manual before blaming the dialog editor.

subject: rotating text in TPW. Help !!
q: How do I rotate text in Turbo Pascal for Windows so that axis labels are parallel with the axes?
a: Read the online help for lfEscapement and lfOrientation in TLogfont. They take the angle in tenths of degrees, counter clockwise, so 900 writes south to north. Not all display or printer drivers support rotation; standard 16-color VGA doesn't. A type manager like ATM will do the trick.

subject: "button" class tracking cursor after leaving window???? how???
q: How does the Windows button class keep tracking the mouse after the cursor leaves its window while the left button is held down? Does it use some kind of hook?
a: No hook needed. Use SetCapture() and ReleaseCapture(). Read the SDK docs before inventing exotic mechanisms.

subject: my first windows program
q: I get unresolved externals like CreateWindow, FatalAppExit and OutputDebugString linking my first Windows 3.0 SDK program with link /NOD snap3,,,libw slibcew,snap3.def. What's wrong?
a: Link libw after slibcew. The linker makes only one pass to satisfy externals, so when it processes libw before slibcew it hasn't yet seen what slibcew needs. Swap the order, and learn how linkers work.

subject: Algorithm for arc
q: I need algorithms for drawing arcs and ellipses. Could someone help me?
a: Bresenham's algorithm. Plot a start point such as x=0, y=r, then step incrementally, picking the adjacent pixel with the least error. Scan-line by scan-line leaves holes. It's in Foley and Van Dam, Fundamentals of Interactive Computer Graphics. Go read a book.

subject: Latest Windows version
q: I'm about to develop with Windows 3.00a and C6.00. Is there a newer Windows version, and do I need it?
a: A new Windows 3 is coming soon but isn't here yet. Your real worry is C6.00, which is incredibly buggy. Get the C6.00a upgrade if you don't have it, though it still has about 70 listed bugs, mostly in optimization. Typical Microsoft.

subject: Borland C++ Bugs???
q: In Borland C++ I have to select text in the clipboard before I can paste it after a copy or cut. Is that a bug or can I configure it?
a: It's configurable. Go to Options/Environment/Editor and look at the Persistent Blocks option. You have it turned off. Next time, read TFM a bit harder.

subject: Exclusive Control
q: Is there any way to take exclusive control of the processor in Windows for a while, so I can do flicker-free animation?
a: Windows only multitasks when an app yields, so just don't yield. Avoid GetMessage, PeekMessage, Yield and ReplyMessage, and get your DC with GetDC rather than BeginPaint. Cooperative multitasking, what did you expect?

subject: Lining up rows and columns of characters
q: My Windows program draws maze-like rows of letters, but with TextOut or DrawText the letters don't line up in columns because of the font. How do I make them align?
a: Use a fixed-spacing font: select GetStockObject with OEM_FIXED_FONT, SYSTEM_FIXED_FONT or ANSI_FIXED_FONT into the dc. Or call TextOut once per column and keep proportional fonts. Petzold covers it; read the book.

subject: NMAKE: warning U4004: too many rules for target `foo.exe'
q: NMAKE gives 'warning U4004: too many rules for target foo.exe' on the SDK samples, and sometimes it gets confused and does nothing. How do I write the makefile to avoid this?
a: Use a double colon when a target has multiple rules. Write foo.exe:: foo.obj and foo.exe:: foo.res instead of single colons. Sigh, it's in the manual.

subject: Borland C++ _f... functions don't work under Windows. Any ideas?
q: Some of the _f functions in Borland C++, like _fstrlen, _fmemset and _fstrncmp, crash under Windows 3.0 in small model. I'm running real mode Windows on a 286. What's going on?
a: Real mode Windows is your real problem. BC++ 2.0 and 3.0 don't support real mode, and executables won't reliably run there, with no reliable workaround. One person found _fmemcpy fails in small model but works in medium. Use medium, or get a real machine.

subject: Source Code for dBASE III routines in C wanted
q: Where can I get C source code for handling dBASE III Plus files in a Windows program, such as create, append, sort and index?
a: Two C libraries ship with source: CodeBase 4.2 from Sequiter and AccSys for dBASE from Copia. Neither is Windows-specific. Everybody wants an Ashton-Tate DLL for this, and the vendor stays tight-lipped. Sigh.

subject: Strange things are afoot at the Win Kernel...
q: Why did popping up a MessageBox() from a dialog in Windows 3 change my desktop background to a screen listing the Win3 developers' names?
a: Those are the Windows 3 credits. One reply says it happens if the message string isn't static. The other says you can summon the credits by holding F3, typing win3, releasing F3 and hitting backspace. Click the desktop to dismiss. Supposedly gone in 3.1.

subject: Position of help menu entry. Was Re: ModifyMenu Bug?
q: Why did the Windows style guide move the help menu entry away from the upper right corner of the menu bar? Is there any reason other than IBM saying so in the CUA guidelines?
a: Mostly it's personal taste. Some people kept losing the help item visually when it sat apart from the other menus. It isn't anywhere either, since the guidelines still say it must be the rightmost item. Stop fussing over it.

subject: BitBlt question
q: Why would BitBlt redraw a large colored bitmap in slow horizontal strips, about four or five swipes? Is there a reason it does that?
a: BitBlt is implemented by the video display driver, not GDI. So go try the standard VGA driver and see if the problem goes away. Honestly, check your driver before blaming the API. I've never seen those symptoms.

subject: PeekMessage() question.
q: Will PeekMessage() in a yield loop remove a WM_QUIT message from the Windows queue, and can I requeue it with PostMessage()?
a: Set the PM_NOREMOVE bit and PeekMessage won't dequeue anything. Or yes, you can put it back with PostMessage, as you guessed. Basic stuff, read the docs.

subject: High-res bitmap from News
q: Can NeWS on a Sun render PostScript to a buffer or file at the equivalent of 300 dpi, the way Display PostScript on the NeXT makes a bitmap for its printer?
a: Untested, but try a retained canvas with the transformation matrix set for 300 dpi. That should do it, though I haven't tried it myself. Go and find out instead of waiting for a summary.

subject: Running NeWS on SG Iris workstations
q: My NeWS program driven from C via cps on a Silicon Graphics Iris dies with the loader error inet_addr undefined, though it works on a Sun-4. Any ideas?
a: Link in the BSD libraries with -lbsd and it should work. And don't use the example in the Iris manual; SGI admits it's wrong at the source, since they got it from Sun. Manuals, bah.

subject: Help key broken for tNt applications in OW2.0
q: My tNt application under OpenWindows 1.0 responded to the Help key, but under OW2.0 it doesn't get the key events. Uncommenting the HelpKey code in OLUI.ps changed nothing. How do I get Help to work?
a: Add to your .startup.ps: UserProfile begin /OLFunctions? true def end. That's on top of what you already did. Next time, read the docs instead of snooping around in system files.

subject: Emacs NeWS support
q: We have Gnu Emacs NeWS support from NeWS 1.0, but it refreshes the window constantly under XNeWS 1.0. Does anybody have revised support known to work?
a: Pointless. XNeWS, X11/NeWS or OpenWindows is both X and NeWS, so the X version of GNU Emacs runs fine under it. Why bother making Emacs support a proprietary window system that already supports it? Just use the X version.

subject: virtual olwm ftp site?
q: Does anyone know an ftp site that carries the virtual olwm, the one with a large virtual screen like swm?
a: It's on export.lcs.mit.edu as contrib/olvwm.tar.Z. Try archie before bothering the net.

subject: icons under olwm, xcpu no title
q: How do I display xcpustate or similar clients without a title bar under OpenWindows olwm? OpenWindows.MinimalDecor doesn't seem to work.
a: List the client names after OpenWindows.MinimalDecor in your .Xdefaults, e.g. xeyes xfd xlogo xbiff xclock xload xcpustate and so on, all on one line. If it doesn't work for you, check that the names match exactly.

subject: New to open-look, want info
q: I'm new to Open Look and XView on a Sun 3/60 and will have to program with them. What books should I look up?
a: Get the Open Look Graphical User Interface Functional Specification and the Application Style Guidelines, both Addison-Wesley 1989. Add the O'Reilly XView Programming Manual, and Sun's guide for converting SunView applications. An XView reference manual from O'Reilly is coming. Read them, don't ask for hand-holding.

subject: CM problems
q: I'm running CM on a SparcStation 2 with SunOS 4.1.1 and X11R4. It complains about missing lucida fonts and spews XView warnings when I view by month. xset fp+ on the OpenWindows font directory gives a BadValue error. What's going on?
a: Your fonts.dir lacks entries matching those lucida names. Copy the 80 line, change it to 90, and bump the count on the first line by one for each line added. And xset fp+ fails because OpenWindows uses a different font format than X11R4. Read the file.

subject: Questions about Open Look
q: I'm running OpenWindows on a Sun 3/60. How do I place icons where I want them, change the default icon for an xterm, and change the root menu? My .olwmmenu changes get ignored.
a: Use a geometry like 32x32-50-50; -0-0 puts the icon off screen. Set the icon with -xrm "*iconPixmap: bitmapfile". Your man page is old: OpenWindows 2.0 reads .openwin-menu, not .olwmmenu. Read the right docs next time.

subject: HELP! I need tool to make tools
q: Is there a tool for building X interfaces by dragging and dropping objects from a palette, like Interface Builder on the NeXT, for XView or OLIT?
a: It's called guide, and it ships with OpenWindows on a SPARCstation. You drag and drop objects and set properties, including event handlers. Sun's DevGuide product does the same for about $250. Learn what's already on your own machine.

subject: VT tools for openwindows
q: We have vttool for VT-100 terminal emulation under SunView. Is there something similar for OpenWindows?
a: xvttool, available by FTP from titan.rice.edu. Sigh, it's been out there for ages. Go fetch it.

subject: LeaveMouse after moving a window
q: After moving an Emacs window with the window manager, Emacs gets a LeaveWindow but no EnterWindow even though the mouse is still inside. How does xterm avoid this?
a: Something is eating the EnterWindow. Look for XSync calls that flush the Xlib buffer, or a window manager or server not doing its job. In xterm I just checked where the mouse really was. Debug your own code first.

subject: X on Amiga\?
q: Are there any ports of X to the Amiga, and where can I get one?
a: Yes, X exists on the Amiga. An Alpha version of X11R2 is being tested and looks very good. It will be a commercial product of Boing, Inc. Go ask them instead of the net.

subject: Question on building X11R4 on SCO Unix.
q: Building X11R4 on SCO Unix with gcc 1.38, I get 'bad include syntax' errors in the Imakefile. Does it matter, and should I have applied the level 15 and up patches?
a: Ignore the message, everything builds fine. The SCO patches are guaranteed after fix-14. Apply all the fixes to vanilla MIT code first, then the SCO patches. Expect to hand patch leftover files. Fix-15 through 18 are all Xt.

subject: Combining Two drawables (Pixmaps)
q: Can I XOR two color Pixmaps in X and still keep the colors? My overlay lines come out black.
a: Simple binary logic like XOR is not appropriate for multi-bit color pixel values; a little arithmetic on your pixels will show you why. Either combine pixels yourself using images, or set up your colormap so the logic functions give the results you want. The colormap trick is faster. Any decent graphics text covers it.

subject: Sun 386i and DOS
q: Can I run X (even OpenLook) and DOS graphics applications on a Sun 386i, or do I have to go back to SunView?
a: Two choices. Run the Sun OpenWindows server, which lets SunView and X coexist and so gives you the 386i DOS tool, or try SoftPC, if it exists for the 386i. Can't remember who makes it. Hardly rocket science.

subject: R4 clients on a R3 server
q: Can I run X11R4 clients on an X11R3 server, or did the X protocol change between R3 and R4?
a: Yes, works fine; people do it all the time. Your main headaches will be font mismatches and nonexistent cursors when running across platforms and revisions. Hardly a tragedy.

subject: Using Save-under
q: Can I use save-under to speed up popup menus over an HP workspace widget on the MIT X11R3 Sun 3 server, and does Motif support save_under?
a: Motif doesn't include a server, so that part is up to your X server. The Xt Intrinsics shell has a save_under field, and the Motif menu shell supports it too. Many save_under implementations are slow, so test it. Basic stuff.

subject: VENDOR symbol
q: Can I use the VENDOR preprocessor symbol in my .Xdefaults with #if VENDOR == 'MIT X Consortium'? cpp on the Sun chokes on the spaces in the strings.
a: Sigh. #if is for numerical comparison only. You can't compare VENDOR or any text-valued symbol that way; you get substitution and #ifdef or defined() tests, nothing else. Cpp isn't stupid, you just misused it.

subject: X and RPC libraries: Can they co-exist?
q: Can RPC libraries like Sun ONC or NCS coexist with the X toolkit event loop, given both block on sockets and weren't designed for each other?
a: Use threads. OSF DCE comes with a threads package, or use a POSIX 1003.4a or Mach C threads package. Sun's current threads won't help, since they're user space and one blocking syscall stalls them all. Why the two weren't designed together is anyone's guess.

subject: Alternative installation directories for X11R4
q: Can X11R4 be installed somewhere other than /usr/bin/X11 and /usr/lib/X11, such as under /usr/local, on Ultrix 4.1? Is that practical, and is it done in the .cf file?
a: Sure, it's routinely done. Build with the default paths, then make DESTDIR=/local/X11R4 install install.man, and symlink from /usr/bin, /usr/lib, /usr/include and the man dirs into it. Or put everything in /usr/local/X11 with symlinks. Works fine, but expect to rerun the link script whenever you add a tool.

subject: Sending a string to another Window using DECWindows
q: Can an X client send a string to another client's window so it reads it as if typed, to put a graphical front end on an existing command-line program? I'm on DECwindows under VMS.
a: Don't bother stuffing keystrokes into another window. Fork the non-X program from your X client and talk to it over pipes or sockets. Most public domain X front ends for mail and dbx do exactly that.

subject: PEX and X-terminals - out of luck ?
q: Can an X terminal that only has a stock X server, an 11.3 one, work with PEX or a PHIGS library? Is there any workaround?
a: No. PEX adds its own protocol to X, so the terminal must understand it. You can't make a stock X-only server executable do that. You'd need the X source and a workstation to build your own server. Some vendors are working on PEX terminals, so wait for those.

subject: Display Postscript and X
q: Can anyone give me information about the Display PostScript extension to X?
a: It's an X server extension plus a client library of callable routines that send data to the server extension for execution. There's also pswrap, which turns mixed C and PostScript into plain C. Ask Adobe Developer Support for the docs. Read them.

subject: complete X bibliography (was Re: Doug Young examples)
q: Can anyone give the publisher and ISBN for Douglas Young's X Window book on Xt programming? Are there other good X books I should know about?
a: Young's book is "X Window Systems: Programming and Applications with Xt," Prentice-Hall 1989, ISBN 0-13-972167-3. Also Johnson and Reichard's "X Window Applications Programming," MIS: Press, 1989, ISBN 1-55828-016-2. Its code is copyrighted, so don't count on free redistribution.

subject: X for Mac w/SLIP?
q: Can the Mac X products run over SLIP from home? Is SLIP bundled with them, or where can I get SLIP for the Mac?
a: This comes up constantly. There's no SLIP for MacTCP, which both X products use. Wait until around the end of October. TCP/Connect II has SLIP, SMTP/POP and NNTP, but no X.

subject: __udivsi3 : Undefined
q: Compiling X apps like epoch or awm with X11R4 on a Sun2 gives undefined __udivsi3, __divsi3, __mulsi3 and __modsi3, even with -lm. Where do I find these?
a: They live in gnulib, not the math library. Link against that. Sigh, this is a FAQ if I ever saw one.

subject: Help compiling XView 2.0 on decstation 3100
q: Compiling XView 2.0 on a DECstation 3100 fails because svc_fdset is undefined in the RPC headers. Has anyone ported it, and what's the workaround?
a: Your RPC implementation is lame. Build a newer RPC and have XView use that. You can get the latest by anonymous ftp from titan.rice.edu in the sun-sources directory. Vendors never ship anything current.

subject: Motif / Open Look Xt Questions
q: Do I need to pay for the Motif source code, or is the library and include files package enough for developing applications?
a: If you're doing serious Motif work, get the full source. There's a cheaper license for just libraries and headers, but it's inadequate. Three weeks in you'll need the source to see what's happening. Only needs to be accessible, not on every workstation.

subject: terminfo entry for xterm?
q: Does anybody have a terminfo entry for xterm? I have to telnet into a braindead sysV-ish machine that lacks one.
a: Just use vt100. The xterm entry is almost identical to it, with a few differences in dch, dl, function keys and rmcup. Unless you're on a SysV 3.2 system with color curses, or using function keys, you won't notice. Don't bother with the rest.

subject: AutoCAD under X?
q: Does anybody know if AutoCAD will support X Windows in the near future?
a: AutoCAD gave a talk at the June Xhibition about a port to DecWindows. Whether they'll ever make it a real product, nobody said. Vendors love a demo.

subject: xperfmon-like widget (xt)
q: Does anyone have a widget under Xt that draws a continuing graph like xperfmon does?
a: There's an undocumented load graph widget in the Athena widget set. Read the xload source for an example. Honestly, look at what ships with X before asking the net.

subject: Looking of a Select Widget.
q: Does anyone have a working copy of a Selection widget that puts a pixmap and text side by side in a command button? I need one now.
a: You don't need to hunt for it. The X11R3 Athena command widget already does this, via the XtNbitmap resource, which takes a Pixmap or the name of a bitmap file. Read the widget manual before begging the net for code.

subject: CC compiling of X11 under SunOS 4.1
q: Does compiling X11R4 with Sun's cc work better than gcc on SunOS 4.1, given Sun's optimiser was broken in places?
a: I've compiled the entire R4 through fix-18 at -O4 under SunOS 4.1. The compiler fixes in the release notes handle all the source, unlike the 4.0.3 compiler. One gripe: the server compiled -O4 under xdm dumps core when .xsession finishes.

subject: XView sample
q: Does the basic MIT X tape have sample XView programs, such as an image display or plotting program?
a: Just the online O'Reilly examples. Look in X11R4/contrib/toolkits/XView/clients/examples. Don't expect more.

subject: Xview Postscript
q: GUIDE for XView has a "PostScript" drawing model option for canvas windows that generates a PSCANVAS in xv_create(), but I can't find it documented. Does anyone know what it is or how to use it?
a: It's a front end to the NeWS side of the merged X/NeWS server, output only. It's not in the XVPM, naturally. Look in the xvps demos under share/src/sun/xview/demos for PSCANVAS examples, and read xvps.ps in the share directory. Sigh, read the shipped source.

subject: X11R5 on Sun386i OS 4.0.2
q: Has anyone gotten the X11R5 server to run on a Sun386i under OS 4.0.2? I compiled it with the stock compiler and BuildPex No, and the server seems happy, but nothing shows on the screen.
a: Quit using the stock compiler. The only decent way I found was to get gcc; 1.39 is fine, and I tried 1.40 too. BuildPex goes back to Yes then. It's on prep.ai.mit.edu and the proper GNU sites. Sigh.

subject: xtalk under X11R4 co-Xist on NeXT
q: Has anyone gotten xtalk to work compiled on a NeXTstation running X11R4 co-Xist? It builds and connects, but as soon as I send a character the window dies with a bus error.
a: Some X11R4 implementations choke on xtalk. I saw a malloc error out of the Ascii widget on an SGI. You'll probably need to get X11R5 built for the NeXT to fix it. Welcome to vendor X.

subject: X11 xpr for imagen?
q: Has anyone modified the X11 version of xpr to produce Imagen IMPRESS format?
a: Yes, xwdimp (bitimp) was updated for X11. It converts a window dump into impress code and sends it to the printer, and you run it with xipr. Should've been in comp.sources.x already.

subject: Using Different Compilers
q: How can I get Imake to use gcc as CC everywhere, including the server directory, when setting CC=gcc in an Imakefile gets undone by the top-level Makefile?
a: Quit fighting it per directory. Set CC and friends in util/imake.includes/Sun.macros, and the values propagate everywhere on a make Makefiles. Works fine with gcc 1.34 under SunOS 3.5.1. Imake isn't that hard, you just have to put it in the right file.

subject: Console output on a SUN 3/50 running xdm
q: How can I get console output on a Sun 3/50 running xdm, X11R3 and SunOS 4.0 to show up in a console window instead of hosing the screen?
a: Use the -C option on the xterm you want console output sent to. Mine is the last line of .xsession: exec xterm -title login -geometry 80x10+1+20 -rv -C -ls. RTFM, it's right there.

subject: MacX keypad escape sequences
q: How can I get emacs running through MacX to recognize the keypad keys as escape sequences instead of numbers? Has anyone done this with xmodmap?
a: Run xev and press the keys to see their keysyms, then remap with xmodmap. MacX keycodes are the Mac keyboard keycodes plus 8, and "xmodmap -pk" shows the defaults. The Command key adds more keycodes to the keypad and arrows. The docs never covered this, naturally.

subject: printing a selection from xterm
q: How can I print the current selection in xterm? Right now I type lpr and paste the selection into standard input, but it sometimes loses text.
a: Grab xselection from expo.lcs.mit.edu under contrib, or from a comp.sources.x archive. Then it's just xselection PRIMARY piped into lpr, and you can hang that on a button. Quit pasting by hand like it's 1983.

subject: Running X11 under Sun Overview
q: How can I run X11 under Sun Overview and pop back to suntools? The server freezes keyboard and mouse on my color Sun 3/110.
a: Don't compile the server with -DSUNWINDOWS. Run overview with the -W option to tell it another window system is running. For full function you'll also have to hack xinit or the server to handle stop and restart. No free lunch.

subject: FAQ Archives & FTP?
q: How do I access the comp.windows.x FAQ archive and the X export archive by FTP?
a: Sigh. The central distribution point for all things X is export.lcs.mit.edu, and the FAQ is contrib/FAQ.Z there. Caches also exist at uunet.uu.net and on der Mouse's machine. Figure out anonymous ftp.

subject: cutting text in xedit (X in general)
q: How do I cut or delete a selection in an xedit window under X? Is there an editor or twm feature that does it?
a: Cutting text is handled by the application, not X or twm. xedit uses the Athena text widget, where control-w deletes the selection. You can remap it through the translations resource, and many folks use the delete key instead. Read the docs.

subject: Draw color image
q: How do I display a color image in an X window with 256 colors? XDrawPoint seems to have no color parameter, and I can't find a routine to modify pixmap data.
a: Wrong. The GC in XDrawPoint(s) sets the foreground color, though that's an inefficient way to handle images. Use XPutImage to put the image into a pixmap and make it the window's background pixmap. O'Reilly volumes I and II have it all. Read them.

subject: how do you get correct window position?
q: How do I get the correct screen position of a Xt popup shell's window when twm adds a border, so I can recreate it in exactly the same place? XTranslateCoordinates with XGetWindowAttributes makes it drift each time.
a: With an ICCCM-compliant window manager, which the R4 twm should be, XtTranslateCoords should do the trick. Stop hand-rolling Xlib calls and fighting the window manager's border.

subject: Using Xlib calls in Xaw viewport
q: How do I get the window ID of the child in an Xaw viewport widget so I can use Xlib calls like XDrawLines inside it?
a: Look in the XtNchildren resource for the child not named clip, horizontal or vertical; that's your scrollable child. XtNameToWidget gets the others. And yes you can draw, but you must handle exposure, easiest with a core widget child with expose and resize handlers.

subject: XTERM keyboard translations
q: How do I make xterm translate the Delete key to ctrl-D in .Xdefaults? Where is this documented?
a: Use xterm.translations: #override <Key>Delete: string(0x4). You can give the ASCII code of the character you want. And string(d) should be string("d") anyway. Read the xterm and Xt docs before posting.

subject: IBM RS/6000 and Motif 1.1.3
q: I built Motif 1.1.3 on an IBM RS/6000 and linking the motifshell demo fails with unresolved symbols .regcmp and .regex. Any clues?
a: RTFRN. Those routines live in libPW.a, so add it as an extra load library. Or, if your libc has re_comp and re_exec, set -DNO_REGEX in StandardDefines, which is probably faster anyway.

subject: problem for building R4 for PS2 AIX 1.1 ...
q: I built the X11R4 server for PS/2 AIX 1.1, but it locks up the screen and dumps core when run. What's wrong?
a: Probably HasNdbm. If it's defined, the server dumps core opening the color database, because dbm on PS/2 AIX is not ndbm. Put an override in site.def that sets HasNdbm to NO for PS2Architecture. Read your config before blaming the code.

subject: Andrew Toolkit Installation - HELP !!
q: I can't build the Andrew toolkit with X11 R3. The Makefiles have hard-coded paths and the README's make AndrewMakefiles and make Makefiles steps fail. Do I have to edit every Makefile?
a: No, you don't edit every Makefile. Set the paths in the system macros file in the config directory under toolkits/andrew, check andrewenv.h there, then run make World in the andrew directory. Ignore the README bits that don't match. Documentation, bah.

subject: mwm
q: I can't find non-binary source for the Motif Window Manager, mwm. Is it dead?
a: Motif is proprietary, so you shouldn't find source anywhere. OSF will send you the source for about US$ 1000. That mwm.c you found looks like a home-brew clone, and the floating binaries will vanish soon. Read the FAQ.

subject: Dialog Value String problem
q: I have a Dialog Widget running, but XtDialogGetValueString() always returns the default value, not what the user typed. What's going on?
a: Looks like a widget flaw. The DialogWidget doesn't do anything on a set-values call for XtNvalue, so the string never updates. That's from reading the widget code, not gospel. Typical toolkit quality.

subject: xfig on SCO Open Desktop
q: I'm compiling xfig 2.0 on SCO Open Desktop and the X11 R3 include files like Command.h and Label.h are missing. Can I just copy them from the R3 tapes?
a: Depends on your patch level. If you have xfig 2.0 patch level 6 or 7, you need R4. With an earlier patch level, just use the include files from the R3 tapes. Whether it runs under SCO, no idea.

subject: SeeTeX-2.15 installation problem
q: I'm installing SeeTeX-2.15 and running imake -I/usr/lib/X11/config, then make Makefile gives "sh: ./config: bad directory" on target config/imake. What's wrong?
a: Your X is already installed, so tell imake so. Use imake -DUseInstalled -I/usr/lib/X11/config instead. It's in the docs, but nobody reads those.

subject: X application + data via sockets.
q: I'm writing an X Motif application that gets data over a socket from a machine not running X. Is a non-blocking socket checked in my main loop OK, or is there a better way?
a: Don't poll in your own main loop. Use XtAddInput and let the toolkit handle it, so you don't have to worry about the main loop. Worked for me, and it's what the toolkit is for.

subject: How do I block X events?
q: In my Motif X app, how can I show an hourglass cursor and ignore mouse and keyboard events while it does a long computation?
a: Create an InputOnly window covering the whole application. Set its do_not_propagate_mask so no events propagate, and give it an hourglass cursor. When the work is done, destroy or unmap it. Basic X, really.

subject: 2 Popdowns = lost focus
q: In my X/Motif app, popping down two popup shells in a row loses the keyboard focus, but a sleep(1) between them fixes it. Why, and what can I do?
a: There's no guarantee where the focus ends up. That's the window manager's job, and the R3 focus code on both the Xt and Motif sides is brain-dead and can't be relied on. R4 is better. Also, where's your mouse pointer?

subject: Multiple architecture's compiled out of a single source tree-- how
q: Is anyone compiling multiple architectures out of a single source tree? How are you doing it?
a: Keep one read-only source tree, then make a separate build directory per architecture and fill it with links to the sources using lndir, a script in the X R4 release at mit/util/scripts/lndir.sh. Build in each with make World, using NFS to share. Rm -fr the shadow tree to clean up.

subject: Looking for UIMS
q: Is anyone working on a toolkit-based UIMS or forms processor for X, especially Motif? OSF mentioned a UIMS as a future Motif product. What's the schedule?
a: OSF has said it will not release a UIMS for Motif. Several companies have announced such products, mostly for Motif, a couple for Open Look. Which is best depends on your requirements. Vendor rumors, sigh.

subject: Spy program
q: Is it feasible to put a program between the X server and a client that records the events and requests transparently, without affecting behaviour or slowing things down much? Is there ftp'able source for something like that?
a: Already done. Look at xscope in contrib/clients of the MIT X distribution. It sits between client and server and logs the traffic. Try looking in the distribution before asking the net to write it for you.

subject: Xwd to Tektronix 4696 printer program?
q: Is there a program to take a dumped X window from xwd to a Tektronix 4696 printer?
a: There's a public domain Amiga driver for the 4696 that works with the Amiga-based xpr from GfxBase. Of course, you need an Amiga too. Hope you've got one lying around.

subject: Is there a way to detrmine a window's current cursor?
q: Is there a way to determine the current cursor of an arbitrary window in X?
a: No. The Cursor ID may not even exist any more if someone freed it with XFreeCursor after attaching it. And even with a Cursor value you can't do much beyond recoloring it, setting other windows' cursors to it, or freeing it. What are you really after?

subject: Mac-style window managers in X?
q: Is there an accepted way to write a Mac-style window manager in X, with a border around each window holding controls to move, resize, delete and iconify it?
a: Yes, it's been done. Track the windows and embed each new one inside a window-manager window that carries the controls. Forcing apps to link a standard interface package is a very bad idea indeed. A simple prototype called wm ships on the V11 beta distribution. Go read it.

subject: Killing all clients except Me 'n' Root
q: Is there an easy way to get a list of all clients connected to the X server and kill them all except my application and the client that owns the root window?
a: No. You can't do anything to a client that creates no resources, and it's very hard even if it does. Windows aren't owned by clients, and nobody really owns the root. X never made client connections full protocol objects. Sigh.

subject: Athena Graphics Widget?
q: Is there some way of drawing graphics through an Athena widget?
a: Subclass an existing widget and add the graphics functionality you want. If no existing widget has anything useful, just subclass the Core widget. That's the correct way to do it, whether or not you like the work.

subject: MWM icon labels
q: MWM icon labels seem to come from XA_WM_NAME rather than XA_WM_ICON_NAME. Is that a bug, a feature, or configurable?
a: Feature. It lets you read the full window name without deiconifying. Not everything is a bug, you know.

subject: Motif on X11r4
q: Motif 1.0.A from OSF says it doesn't build correctly with X11 Release 4, but I've seen people using Motif with R4. Are there patches, or is a new release out?
a: Not yet. OSF says a version of Motif that officially works with R4 is coming this summer. Wait for it, like they told you.

subject: What mwm resource(s) is used to place the window icon?
q: Mwm puts my iconified windows along the bottom of the screen starting from the left. Which resource makes it place them on the right starting from the top?
a: That's iconPlacement, as in Mwm*iconPlacement: Top Right. The first value is the direction the icons run, the second is where the first one goes. Also set iconAutoPlace to true, or the icons stay put where you minimized them. RTFM next time.

subject: X server growing very quickly.
q: My X server grows by 1 to 4 Meg for each Motif graphics window, depending on screen configuration. Why, and how can I minimize the growth?
a: We saw the same leaking, and it went away when we turned off save-unders with the -su argument to the X server. We haven't dug into the server side yet. Fix the symptom now, grumble about the cause later.

subject: problem with C++ and X
q: My Xaw client with a C++ routine in the event handler list gets a segmentation fault when it uses cout or cerr. Any ideas?
a: Without more info it's a guess, but passing a C++ method to Xaw won't work. cfront passes 'this' as a hidden first argument, and Xaw expects a plain old C function. Pass a wrapper function that calls the method. Basic stuff.

subject: Xt toolkit and dec3100 window manager
q: My Xt toolkit application with Athena widgets (X11R3) runs fine on a Sun under uwm or twm, but on a DECstation 3100 it won't accept keyboard input in Text or Dialog widgets. Is there a patch, or some other bug?
a: This is the second most commonly asked X programming question. For ICCCM compliance you must set XtNinput to True on top level shells that expect input, or the window manager won't give them focus. See the intrinsics manual section 4.1.3 and ICCCM 4.1.7. RTFM.

subject: OLIT: Who distributes it?
q: OLIT is an Xt widget implementation of Open Look. Who distributes it and where can I get it?
a: Sun sells OLIT for Sun machines. It's a port of the AT&T Open Look toolkit, sometimes called Xt+, and AT&T sells that for some of its own systems. Sigh, read the docs next time.

subject: Sun4 4.0.3 and color resetting
q: On Sun4s running 4.0.3, the screen text color is pale and hardly readable after I terminate X11. How do I restore the colors?
a: Run clear_colormap. It works from the command line or as the last entry in your .xinitrc. Not exactly a deep secret, so read the man pages once in a while.

subject: PROBLEM with xterm & telnet........help.......wedged screens....
q: On X11R4 on a Sun 3/60, vi and more wedge my xterm screen when I telnet to a host, but they work fine over rlogin or rsh. What's the deal with telnet and xterm?
a: rlogin and rsh pass TERM along properly, so it stays xterm. telnet doesn't, and TERM may end up as something like "network". Just setenv TERM xterm after telnetting. Basic stuff.

subject: WANTED: R5 precompiled for Sun 4/110 SunOS 4.1
q: On my Sun 4/110 with a cg4, error messages written to the console appear before a console-trapping window comes up and can't be cleaned. The console runs on cg2 on top of the color screen, and xrefresh doesn't help. What can I do?
a: Try running "switcher -e 0". You can probably also get the server to manage both the color and mono screens, with the cursor moving across the left or right edge to switch. Look for the cgfour overlay planes thread for the 3/60.

subject: Is it possible to translate characters ?
q: Our eXodus X server on a Mac has German keyboards and characters like y and z are swapped. Can the X translation tables fix characters in all applications?
a: Wrong tool. Change the keyboard mapping with xmodmap, see section 7.9 of the Xlib manual. On a DECstation 3100, xmodmap -e "keycode 195 = y Y" makes the z key report y and Y. Translation tables are not for this.

subject: X Windows (tm)
q: Quest Systems is advertising their X server as QuestWindows and claims X Classic and X Windows are their trademarks. Has MIT lost the rights to the name X Windows?
a: Hardly. The name has been misused so much that nobody is likely to trademark X-Windows. IBM has called their version X-Windows for a year already. Marketing types never learn.

subject: twm 4.0 grabbing all keys
q: Running twm 4.0 on R2 and SunOS 3.5, I can't type into any window. twm gets events for every keypress, and disabling XGrabKey for window contexts fixes it. What's going wrong?
a: Check your .twmrc for a key like Clear that your server keytab doesn't define. XKeysymToKeycode returns zero, and XGrabKey treats zero as AnyKey, so twm grabs every key. Oops. Fix the keytab or drop the binding.

subject: Beginner needs help with XToolkit error messages.
q: Running xgdb gives X Toolkit warnings: translation table syntax error: Unknown keysym: Backspace. What's wrong?
a: Keysyms are case sensitive. Use BackSpace, not Backspace. Read the error message, it's telling you exactly that.

subject: Digital-logo in DECwindows
q: The VMS 5.3 New Features manual says the Session Manager can display a logo other than the Digital logo in the login box. How do you do it?
a: Write an application that puts up the window you want, say a bitmap made in DECwindows Paint. Make a .COM file that runs it, then DEFINE/EXEC DECW$LOGIN_BACKGROUND to that file. It must be executive mode. The manual won't tell you that, naturally.

subject: X copyright
q: The X11R4 copyright says "permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute... without fee". Does that mean I can't charge for a package containing modified copies of those files, or just that I owe the copyright holders nothing?
a: It means the latter. You owe Digital or MIT nothing for permission to redistribute, and you can do anything with the software, including reselling it, without restriction. Read the license before you whine about it.

subject: Dialogs in XView 2.0
q: There doesn't seem to be a dialog box in XView 2.0. What's the standard practice for making one? Is it a command frame, then a panel, then the items in the panel?
a: Two paths. The simple one is the notice facilities, notice_prompt(). For more interactive dialogs, use FRAME_CMD objects and manage the dialog yourself. The O'Reilly XView Programming Manual explains it, so go read it.

subject: Boring cursor on Mvax-2000 (X11)
q: Under X11 on my MicroVAX 2000 the cursor is a boring white rectangle and xsetroot has no effect, though it works under X10. Any ideas?
a: Add a line at the end of the qvDisplayCursor routine in server/ddx/dec/qvss/qvss_io.c, before the return TRUE: ioctl(fdQVSS, QIOWCURSOR, qvInfo->cursorbits); It's worked for a fortnight without problems. Not pretty, but it works.

subject: Need simple library for displaying Plots/Graphs
q: We need a simple high-level library for displaying plots and graphs, something like GKS or PHIGS. Are there X11 implementations of GKS or PHIGS, or other libraries that do the same sort of thing?
a: Digital has X11 versions of GKS and PHIGS, though PHIGS (PEX) may not be for sale yet. Or try CPLOT, with drivers for X10, X11, PostScript and Tek, from anonymous FTP at maddog.llnl.gov in pub/cplot. Not hard to find.

subject: Debugger?
q: What debuggers are available for C under X windows, something like dbxtool under SunView?
a: With OpenWindows you already have an X dbxtool in $OPENWINHOME/bin/xview. The nicest one is ups, from anon ftp at export.lcs.mit.edu. It's actually integrated with X instead of being a front end, and its author clearly debugged real code, unlike the xdbx crowd.

subject: X11 R5 NFS export
q: What happened to the exported file system /export/ftp from EXPORT.LCS.MIT.EDU? We can no longer mount it for X11 R5.
a: Nothing happened to it. It's still working for me, so the trouble is on your end. Go check your own setup before blaming MIT.

subject: Beginning use of Xlib
q: What is a good text for learning to write programs with Xlib only, with examples? The X Window System book by Scheifler, Gettys and Newman has none.
a: Get Oliver Jones's Introduction to the X Window System from Prentice Hall. It's about Xlib programming and deliberately bypasses the toolkits. O'Reilly's Xlib Programming Manual and Reference Manual are also out there, with example source on uunet. Your toolkit-free approach is fine.

subject: Most efficient way of managing children
q: What is the most efficient way to manage a tree of widgets in Xt/Motif, managing children first and then the parent before realizing? What does it cost?
a: Before realization it makes no difference at all: XtCreateManagedWidget is the same as XtCreateWidget plus managing later. After realization, batch management calls with XtManageChildren as much as possible. Read the Xt docs.

subject: HELP !!!
q: What's the best way in X to change the main part of the interface when the user picks an option from a menu bar? Say letter format shows one set of fields and fax format shows another. Should I map and unmap the widgets?
a: Use the XcuDeck widget from the Xcu set, on the contrib tape I think. It stacks children like a deck of cards, one on top at a time. Give it a letter child and a fax child, and raise whichever one is picked. No flashing, since it sizes to the biggest child. Stop hand-mapping everything.

subject: Drawing Widget for Athena Toolkit/Widget set
q: What's the best widget to use as a child of the Athena viewport widget to draw some lines? There's no drawing widget in the R4 Athena set, and I don't want to write a whole widget.
a: Look at the sample in the last chapter of the Athena widgets manual. Apart from the class structure and initialization, which you can mostly cut and paste, there's very little code to write. Asente and Swick's X Window System Toolkit has a good tutorial. Do your own homework.

subject: Fastest Text Display Method
q: What's the fastest way to display text in X? I'm getting about 19,200 chars per second.
a: Use XDrawImageString with the GC set to GXCopy, and time several screenfuls. It's mostly server speed, not your code. Scrolling adds 30 to 50 percent, and font width matters since odd widths are slow. Run x11perf instead of guessing.

subject: Creating X Window through EMACS
q: When I start EMACS under X it creates a window with characters so small it drives me nuts. Is there a way to get larger characters?
a: Set a font in your resource database. For GNU Emacs 18.54 under X11R3, an entry like *Font: *-courier-medium-r-*-*-*-120-*-*-*-*-*-* works and Emacs respects it. You didn't say what Emacs or X you run, which doesn't help anyone.

subject: DECwindows and X11R3
q: When an X11R3 client displays on my DECwindows VAXstation, I get "Xlib: sequence lost" messages. Is it trying to tell me something?
a: Yes, an old Xlib bug. It was in UWS2.0 and X11R2, and fixed in UWS2.2 and X11R3. Build your client with one of those Xlibs and see if it goes away. Next time say which release you run.

subject: Xt program resource files - How much is enough?
q: When writing Xt applications, should I put as much resource information as possible in an app-defaults file and only call XtSetValues for run-time values? Or am I going overboard?
a: It's the right thing if you distribute the program widely, since the program still works if users override nothing. But smart users only, mind you; others can screw themselves up, resources cost performance, and a resource file is no substitute for real preferences. Religious argument anyway.

subject: List of Xt resources
q: Where can I find a list of the core X Toolkit resource names and classes? I never use the Xt toolkit.
a: RTFM. They're in the "X Toolkit Widgets - C Language X Interface" manual. Page 6 lists the resources retrieved from the database by all toolkit widgets.

subject: Caps lock LED patch.
q: Where can I find the Caps Lock LED patch for the MIT X server on Sun? We run X11R4 on SunOS 4.0.3 on Sun3, Sun4 and Sun4c.
a: You'll have no luck, since SunOS 4.0.x doesn't support the keyboard LEDs. For the curious, the patch is at ftp.uni-paderborn.de in /local/X11/more_contrib/Sun_LED.patch.Z. Upgrade your OS.

subject: Source Code for xwd and xwud
q: Where can I find the source code for xwd and xwud?
a: It's in the MIT X distribution, under mit/clients/xwd and mit/clients/xwud. Sigh, it ships with the source tree. Go look there.

subject: Wanted: Sun Rasterfile to X11 bitmap conversion
q: Where can I find utilities to convert Sun rasterfile, PCX and other formats to X11 bitmap format?
a: PBMPLUS, in the standard X11 distribution, does it all. This comes up every week. Go look in the distribution you already have.

subject: olvwm
q: Where can I get olvwm, the apparent tvtwm/olwm cross I keep seeing mentioned?
a: It's on ftp.uu.net, in comp.sources.x/new or thereabouts. Go fetch it yourself instead of waiting for someone to hand it over.

subject: X WINDOW AND X WINDOW PROGRAMMING
q: Where can I purchase the Nutshell series X books from O'Reilly & Associates?
a: Buy them straight from the publisher using their 800 number, 800-338-6887, or send a written order. Most good technical bookstores carry them too, and the publisher will send a free list of stores. Phone books exist for a reason.

subject: X Server for Sun GX or GXP?
q: Where is the long-awaited Sun merged X server with the July FCS date?
a: It slipped to August, to the tune of great gnashing of teeth. Typical vendor schedule. Don't hold your breath, and don't plan around marketing dates.

subject: Viewport Widget
q: Which R3 X clients make the best use of the Viewport widget? We're having problems and want some working sample code.
a: Look on scam.berkeley.edu, in ~ftp/src/local/xtdemo/multiwidget. It's a decent instructional use of the viewport widget. Go read it instead of guessing.

subject: Running Open Look apps using other than OLWM
q: Why do Open Look applications fail under twm or any window manager other than olwm, complaining about missing fonts? Is there a workaround?
a: The window manager has nothing to do with fonts; that's the server's job. Your problem is running Open Look apps on a server other than XNEWS, which lacks the Open Look glyph and cursor fonts and the other XView fonts. Post the actual error messages next time.

subject: Gnu emacs under X.
q: Why does GNU Emacs under X not redisplay the screen after finding a file until I type something?
a: No idea of the root cause, but running Emacs as a subprocess of an xterm instead of from the window manager mostly fixed it. Probably an OS bug, since it didn't reproduce on Sun release 3.2. Ugly kludge, but it works.

subject: -g libs on System V
q: Why does a Motif program built with -g libraries run under gdb so slowly on System V (20 minutes, 40 Meg of memory), compared to a Sparc? Is this a System V or Motorola thing?
a: Not System V, it's gdb. On Berkeley dbx-style symbols gdb lazily reads symbol tables only as needed. Nobody has made that work for System V COFF symbols yet, and sdb presumably doesn't lazy-load either. So yes, be picky with -g.

subject: MOTIF on SUN - I give up
q: Why does the only way to get Motif libraries for linking on a Sun seem to be buying OSF source for $1000 or a compiled version from a third party for over $500?
a: Do the arithmetic. One engineer half time plus equipment at about $100K a year is $50,000 to release Motif, plus patches and support. With around 15 companies selling to developers, $500 a copy is hardly gouging. Not everything is a conspiracy.

subject: Why does xterm use $SHELL if available and not /etc/passwd
q: Why does xterm use $SHELL if it's set instead of the /etc/passwd shell? Our make uses SHELL and needs /bin/sh, so should xterm change?
a: Fix your Makefiles, don't break xterm. Put SHELL = /bin/sh in the Makefile. Using $SHELL is correct behavior, since people who run their own shell, like bash from a per-machine directory, want every new xterm to use it without extra switches.

subject: Large file (Andrew) at export.lcs.mit.edu
q: Why is a huge file like andrew.tar.Z on export.lcs.mit.edu not split into small chunks like X11R5? FTP keeps hanging on the 10 MByte transfer.
a: Nobody answered the splitting question. The suggestion was to mirror the /contrib directory on servers on your side of the pond, using the mirror package from src.doc.ic.ac.uk, which shouldn't be hard. Sigh, bandwidth doesn't grow on trees.

subject: is the mit R4 server for PS2 slower than ibm's R3 version ?
q: Why is the MIT R4 server on a PS/2 under AIX 1.1 so much slower than IBM's R3 server when running the ico demo with -dbl?
a: The R4 ico finds the double buffer extension and uses it, while IBM's server lacks it and fakes double buffering with the colormap. The extension is software, and memory-to-screen copies are slow on PS/2 displays. Disable the double buffer extension in the server. Not a compile error, relax.

subject: (none)
q: Will X run on a Moniterm vy6155 display for the IBM RT/PC, the new 19 inch monitor that uses the same adapter as the 6155?
a: Yes. All the software sees is the 4768 display adapter, so it works just like the IBM 15 inch monitor. Andrew has run fine on prototypes for ages. You can actually read the screen now, which is more than I can say for most vendors.

subject: Pyramid X11R4
q: Will the MIT X11R4 distribution compile on a Pyramid?
a: Yes, it's running on Pyramids here. As I recall the library and clients came up pretty easily. Just try it instead of asking the net.

subject: Problem with twm/InterViews
q: With InterViews and twm, running a program with -geometry WxH works and the window manager knows the window, but with -geometry WxH+X+Y the window is placed but the window manager doesn't know about it. Is this an InterViews bug or did I botch it?
a: It's an InterViews bug. It's being brought up to ICCCM conformance, and this and related bugs will be fixed in the next release. Join the InterViews mailing list for the latest news, and quit blaming yourself.

subject: Xfig 2.0 and transfig 2.1.1
q: With Xfig 2.0 and transfig 2.1.1, printing from xfig fails because f2ps has the wrong format. Also fig2dev -L ps output has %%Pages: 0 and no showpage at the end. Is there a patch?
a: Use the f2ps that ships with xfig 2.0. As for the missing showpage, read the fig2dev man page. Use the -P option, which says the figure is a full page, adds the showpage at the end, and leaves the coordinate system alone. No patch needed.

subject: Colormaps
q: With a 256-entry PseudoColor colormap under X/Motif for imaging, installing it loses the window manager's colors. How can I keep the Motif window manager's colors, reserving N entries for mwm?
a: Not easy. Instead, make mwm allocate only two colors by setting its resources to a monochrome setup, with the same foreground and background as the colors you use, and restart mwm. Then you get 254 colors for your image. Read the mwm resource docs next time.

subject: Event problems with OpenWindows2.0
q: With the OpenWindows 2.0 server, I get EnterNotify events on every mouse move and MotionNotify handling without buttons pressed. The code works fine under an X11R4 server. Why?
a: The xnews server in OpenWindows 2.0 is full of bugs. For one, events like LeaveNotify get discarded while a button is grabbed, and that breaks Motif toggle buttons. Sun knows about it but hasn't shipped a fix. Typical.

subject: Visual 640 term and colors?
q: With xterm colors in .Xdefaults, a Sun X11R2 monochrome server gives black on white but the Visual 640 terminal gives white on white. Which is correct?
a: Black on white is correct. The November product release of the V640 software will match the sample server. Until then, live with it. Vendors never ship it right the first time.

subject: XtCallActionProc && Motif PushButtons
q: XtCallActionProc isn't in any of my X libraries. How can I use it with Motif PushButtons, and how do I gray out a PushButton so it can't be armed?
a: XtCallActionProc is in X11R4 (Intrinsic.h, TMstate.c), not R3. You've got R4 docs and R3 libs, genius. For graying out, just call XtVaSetValues(w, XmNsensitive, False, NULL). Use it to call Arm(), Disarm() and Activate() from the program.

subject: Difficulty w/ xdm on Silicon Graphics w/ NCD.
q: xdm on a Silicon Graphics Personal Iris won't work with an NCD X terminal; debug output stops after 'creating socket 177'. Anyone else seen this?
a: Seen it. The geometry in the xdm Xresources file was too big for the NCD17c, since a full size login window suits the black and white portrait NCD terminals. Shrink it. Maybe an NCD17c bug, but read your own config first.

subject: Xlib with motif? ...
q: Has anyone mixed Xlib and Motif in one program? I want a window that doesn't use the default visual. Is XtCreateWindow a full substitute for XtRealizeWidget?
a: Don't bother. Make your own widget class and do the Xlib work in its methods; the Xt tutorial books cover it under subclassing widgets. If you just want a new visual, set the visual resource on your top level shell, supported in X11R4 and supposedly Motif 1.1.

subject: Oh boy! Troubles with Scrolled XmList
q: How do I get a scrolled XmList of a fixed width and height in Motif, letting it figure out how many items are visible? I usually get a list showing one item.
a: You're setting the wrong widget. Set the size on the list's parent, the scrolled window. Its name is the list name with SW appended, so in the resource file use the listname plus SW dot height. Or do an XtSetValues on XtParent of the list. Works in 1.1.2.

subject: How do you make a dialog appln-modal?
q: How do you make a Motif Information Dialog application-modal, so all user interaction with the application is blocked until the dialog is dismissed?
a: Set XmNdialogStyle to XmDIALOG_FULL_APPLICATION_MODAL, or XmDIALOG_APPLICATION_MODAL in Motif 1.0. In 1.0 it only works under mwm. It's in the manual, you know. Sigh.

subject: Problems using motif on DECStation 3100
q: I built Motif 1.1 on a DECStation 3100 under Ultrix 4.0, and every application I write core dumps with a message about fixed up unaligned data access. How do I solve this?
a: That error usually means you recast data wrongly, like using a variable as a structure when it was declared as a pointer to one. Run a debugger and find out whether the failure is in your code or Motif. Another build worked fine, so suspect -DSTRINGS_ALIGNED. Learn to use a debugger.

subject: wcl on vms again
q: I built wcl on VMS, but running mri on the example resource files gives 'No children defined in Xrm database'. Changing XAPPLRESDIR and decw$user_defaults does nothing. What am I doing wrong?
