a: You didn't apply fix-1 or read the comment in the DCL script. You most likely didn't rename the resource files to a .DAT extension, since DECwindows folks think a file without an extension is sacrilege. Or you're invoking Mri wrong; try MCR []MRI.EXE M01_Hello.

subject: 1st argument to callbacks in Motif 1.1
q: I noticed almost all widgets in Motif 1.1 invoke XtCallCallbackList() with a NULL widget argument, so under X11R5 callbacks get a NULL pointer. Is this a bug or a feature?
a: It's a bug in Motif 1.1, reportedly fixed in 1.1.1 and later. Until you upgrade, you can fix the roughly 150 XtCallCallbackList calls yourself, which gets most Motif apps running. Typical vendor quality.

subject: FormDialog and DrawingArea's children
q: I put a DrawingArea inside an automatic ScrolledWindow, and once I add a child widget like a button to the DrawingArea the scrollbars disappear and scrolling stops working. Why?
a: The DrawingArea shrinks to fit its children because ResizePolicy defaults to XmRESIZE_ANY. If it ends up smaller than the scrolled window, no scrollbars are needed and they vanish. Set ResizePolicy to XmRESIZE_NONE to keep the size fixed. Read the resource docs.

subject: Ignore my last posting, read this one...
q: In Motif, how can I turn off the window menu button without losing the other title bar and border elements?
a: Use a resource: Mwm*clientDecoration: -menu. Programmatically you need patch release 1.0.3. Mind that shift-esc and Btn3Down in the frame still bring up the menu; the safe way to suppress that is the protocol stuff.

subject: Pushbutton callback problem
q: In Motif, my pushbutton inside a form in a dialog shell runs my callback but also dismisses the whole dialog. Who is doing that, and how do I stop it?
a: That's the BulletinBoard resource XmNautoUnmanage, which defaults to True. It adds a callback to button children that unmanages the BulletinBoard. Set it to False. Stripping callbacks was the hard way, and yes, RTFM.

subject: MenuBar question
q: Is it legal to put a Motif menubar cascade button with no pulldown menu and attach a callback to it directly?
a: Yes. Leave XmNsubMenuId NULL and attach your activate callback, and it works like a pushbutton. Keyboard traversal won't reach it, though, since there's no submenu. That was Motif 1.0, and who knows what 1.1 broke.

subject: window group
q: My Motif 1.1 application needs a group of windows iconified and restored together, like the window_group field in XWMHints. Motif doesn't seem to support it, so how can I simulate that?
a: One way is to make all the windows in the collection child DialogShells of some top-level root window of your application. Whether that fits the style guide, who knows. Motif never does this properly, so you make do.

subject: problem on demo mre compile
q: On Motif 1.0.3 with X11R3 on a Sun4, why does compiling the mre demo give undefined symbols _regex and _regcmp? Also, why does mwm run in the background but let a user create no new windows until it's brought to the foreground?
a: In 1.0.4 the mre demo uses the same configuration flag as lib/Xm to pick the regex routines, so get the updated sources and read the README. For mwm, you probably suspended it with ^Z instead of backgrounding it. Type bg %job. Basic job control, folks.

subject: VMS, Motif and the Widget Creation Library
q: On VMS with DEC Motif 1.1, linking against the Widget Creation Library gives unresolved _Xm references like _XmManagerEnter and _XmGadgetArm, though they appear to exist in the shared library. How do I fix this?
a: They're private, undocumented Motif routines, and DEC didn't export them from the shareable library to avoid maintenance liability. The Motif Table widget in Wcl needs them. Either skip Table, or try the Xaw Table, which won't play well with Motif. Typical vendor nonsense.

subject: gadgets vs. widgets
q: What are the differences between Motif gadgets and widgets? Are they interchangeable, and can gadgets detect mouse enter events?
a: Not interchangeable. Gadgets use the parent's window, which cuts server requests, but they do NOT support event handlers, translations or popup children. They do support callbacks and accelerators, and suit menus. They derive from rectObj, not Core, hence the differences. Learn your class hierarchy.

subject: XmNcreateCallback -- what is it?
q: What is XmNcreateCallback in Motif, and why don't my Motif 1.0 packages have it?
a: It's a pseudo callback generated by uil/mrm when a widget is created, not by the toolkit. As of 1.0.A it was renamed MrmNcreateCallback, to stop people confusing it with the intrinsics, as the old name implied. Read the release notes.

subject: Black and White monitors
q: What's the simplest way to make mwm handle a black and white monitor so borders and buttons don't look like a bad negative, without setting -fg, -bg and -bd on every program?
a: You shouldn't need to. Mwm and the Motif toolkit default sensibly on monochrome, static gray or color, so run without any Mwm resources set. If it still looks like a negative, say which mwm version you run.

subject: Where do you get MOTIF for DECstations?
q: Where do you get Motif for DECstations? Does DEC sell it, or do we buy it from OSF, and do we need development software?
a: With an ULTRIX 4.0 license a Motif binary license is bundled, but you order the media separately from your sales rep. It's version 1.0. OSF only sells source licenses. Combine it with a UWS kit for the bulk of what you need. Ask your rep.

subject: .mwmrc errors
q: Why does mwm on my Decstation 3100 not read my .mwmrc, so buttons and menus don't get defined, when the MIPS mwm works fine over the network?
a: Likely your Mwm*buttonBindings and Mwm*keyBindings resources aren't set to match your .mwmrc. The remote mwm uses the local app-defaults file, and those differ between machines. Set both explicitly in your .Xdefaults. Basic stuff.

subject: Why won't XmCreateFileSelectionBox bring up widget?
q: Why won't XmCreateFileSelectionBox bring up the widget from inside a callback? I tried XtManageChild and XtRealizeWidget.
a: You want the Dialog version, XmCreateFileSelectionDialog. A dialog is a Box with a DialogShell parent, which an independent dialog window requires. Then XtManageChild works. Basic Motif, kid.

subject: grunch from external disk drive
q: My Mac's second disk drive barely ejects disks, then made a GRRUNCHH sound and called the disk unreadable, though the other drive read it fine. Anyone else had trouble?
a: Probably a bad drive or not enough power. Check the +5VDC and especially the +12VDC, since that runs the eject motor. Also see how freely the metal shutter on the cartridge moves. Basic troubleshooting.

subject: exec-path and process-environment in gnu-18.53
q: I'm running GNU Emacs 18.53 and need to change the PATH used when it spawns subprocesses, such as for compile. Changing exec-path and process-environment does nothing. Is there a way to change the environment of an already-running emacs?
a: Build emacs with MAINTAIN_ENVIRONMENT set, which gives you a setenv function. Or skip all that and prefix the compile command, like "PATH=extra/dir/:$PATH make -k", setting compile-command in your .emacs. Better yet, fix it in your Makefile, as any idiot would.

subject: cheatsheet
q: Is there a summary of Emacs commands I can keep handy?
a: Look in the GNU Emacs source area for etc/refcard.tex. Keep a printout in your desk drawer. No TeX? The FSF will sell you cards alone or with the manual. This comes up every week.

subject: coming up in auto-fill-mode
q: What do I add to my .emacs to come up in auto-fill-mode by default?
a: Put (setq default-major-mode 'text-mode) and (setq text-mode-hook 'turn-on-auto-fill) in your .emacs. That starts you in text-mode with auto-fill on. This comes up every week.

subject: Slide Show in AmigaVision?
q: How can I build a menu on the fly in AmigaVision for a slide show, so I don't hard code each image name and can click a name or brush to show it?
a: Use the database features, they're plenty. Keep titles and image names or brush names in a database, read entries into variables, and put the variable names in square brackets in the object editor. Text/Var objects work as hit boxes. You can't change response fields on the fly, though.

subject: Compiler Book
q: Does anyone know about a book called something like Writing a Compiler with C by Fisher and someone?
a: That's Crafting A Compiler with C by Fischer and LeBlanc, the C version of Crafting A Compiler, whose examples were in Ada. One reader rates it well above the Dragon book, especially on optimization. Spell the authors right next time.

subject: Rescue 911 Ad
q: A Rescue 911 ad claims "66 lives saved to date." How can they make that claim?
a: Most likely it means 66 lives were saved in segments aired on the show. Another take is that the show drills the 911 number into viewers, kids especially. Marketing math, don't expect rigor.

subject: The Edible Doormouse
q: Are there really edible doormice, and can they significantly reduce one's cholesterol levels?
a: Edible, sure; they're bred in England as a gourmet delicacy, sauce and all, but nobody called them health food. No magic potion lowers cholesterol. Eat less fat, balance your fats, exercise, take medication if it's high. Wrong group, too.

subject: Lat Spread
q: How do you do a lat spread? I read that pulling on a door knob helps, but it doesn't seem to help me.
a: Pulling on a door knob or a vertical pole only stretches the lats. The spread itself: hook your thumbs around your waist, lean back slightly, and get those shoulder blades as far apart as you can. Work on hand placement, lean and pull angles, and do lots of pull-ups and rows. Not rocket science.

subject: heart monitors
q: If I calibrate my heart monitor by how I feel, what's the purpose of using the monitor to gauge my effort? Why not just use perceived effort to begin with?
a: Once calibrated, the monitor watches you more carefully and consistently than you do, and warns you when you wander out of your zone. Effort isn't always proportional to heart rate either: sore legs feel bad even at a low HR. Not hard to grasp.

subject: Using Caffeine as a Workout Stimulant
q: Is caffeine intake before a workout in any way harmful?
a: It can help early in a workout by speeding fat usage, but it raises your heart rate and its diuretic effect can hurt hydration over time. Bodybuilders should skip it, since it helps you burn protein for energy, which is what you don't want.

subject: Cortizone (sp?)
q: My doctor may give me a cortisone shot for an injured shoulder. What results have people gotten, does it hurt, and is it dangerous?
a: Friends say it's the most intense pain outside a dungeon. My own shoulder took months to heal, and benching stresses it heavily. I'd see a physiotherapist instead of a doctor who just throws more medication at it. Ultrasound and electrotherapy worked for me. Don't be a hero before a competition.

subject: Ben Franklin's 200-year investment
q: Ben Franklin's thousand pound bequest to two cities grew to about 5 million and 2 million dollars over 200 years. Was that a good return?
a: You're missing the point. Franklin said to lend it to deserving apprentices, which lately means student loans. The principal had to stay untouched only for the first 100 years, after which the cities could spend some on useful things. He never meant them to squeeze out every penny.

subject: 401k and IRA
q: If I already have a 401k plan, can I still open an IRA?
a: Of course you can have both. Whether the IRA is deductible on your federal income tax depends on your income. Not exactly a secret.

subject: IRA Deduction
q: If I take a job in November with a retirement plan, can I still deduct IRA contributions I make before the hire date?
a: No. If you're eligible for a qualified plan at any time in the year, your IRA isn't deductible that year, and the IRS just checks a box on your W-2. Partial deduction applies if AGI is $35K to $45K. You might luck out if the plan has a waiting period. Read the rules.

subject: Can you reduce your property tax?
q: House values have dropped. Can a homeowner get property taxes reduced by requesting a reassessment?
a: Yes, ask the county, but be careful. They may find things not in the original assessment, like that deck you built, and you can't just say nevermind afterwards. If the value really dropped or they got something wrong, file a protest with the county tax department.

subject: Interface for C64-note Rick Stuart, Frank Prindle, BJH @ Rutgers
q: What is Supra Corporation's address? I need an interface for a C64 like the Cardco type they made.
a: Supra Corporation is at 1133 Commercial Way, Albany, OR 97321. Write to them instead of posting open letters to the net.

subject: FORTRAN subroutine mapper
q: Does anyone have a program to read the source files of a large FORTRAN program and list which subroutines each subroutine calls?
a: Don't reinvent the wheel. There's a Fortran cross-referencer, probably called INDEX, that's been on DECUS tapes for ages. It started on RSX and has likely moved to VMS. Go look at the tapes, it's not new.

subject: Plan 5 for Inner Space - A Sense of Mind.
q: What would it cost and how long would it take to design a portable intelligent system with color vision, speech, natural language, learning and strong servo control, all in one low-power enclosure?
a: About nine months, plus a few years training. Hospitals charge around $1000 and the upkeep costs more, but you get a tax break. Or the serious version: over 50 years and about a trillion dollars. Cute spec, amateur.

subject: Where are delayed branches handled?
q: On RISC machines with delayed branches, who rearranges instructions to fill the delay slot, the assembler or the compiler? Can the compiler do significantly better?
a: Mostly the assembler, in the experience of the one who answered; reorganizing happens after code expansion. The compiler can't get much the assembler can't. One dissenter says only the compiler can reasonably do it, but I've read thousands of lines of disassembly and say otherwise.

subject: equalizers
q: How do I calibrate a multi-band equalizer, and do SPL meters or equalizers with built-in analyzers exist at reasonable prices?
a: Forget calibrating by ear; it's notoriously unreliable. Get an equalizer with a built-in pink noise generator, octave analyzer and microphone, and a room takes under 20 minutes. Around $400 CAN buys a decent one, and calibrated SPL meters run about $250 CAN. Sliders also overlap neighboring bands, so mind that.

subject: Octane mixes...
q: Is it true that mixing gasolines of different octane ratings gives a mix with a higher rating than expected? Also, what are the two main methods used to rate octane?
a: Yes, it's true. One reader got about 94-95 octane from one part leaded regular at 88-89 and two parts super unleaded at 91-92. The two methods are the Research Method and another one I forget. They differ by about 4, and the pump shows the average.

subject: Commercial aircraft power-to-weight
q: Of the subsonic airliners flying now, which has the highest power-to-weight ratio? Is there a real difference in acceleration and climb, or is it my imagination?
a: Twins must have much better power-to-weight than three- or four-engine jets. FAR Part 25 requires a positive climb rate with one engine out, and a twin must do it on 50% power, a four on 75%. So twins climb well, and the 737 has always had good performance.

subject: Snow Traction
q: Does anyone have a solution to the snow traction problem on a bicycle? A friend suggested wrapping wire around the rear wheel. Has anyone tried that?
a: Nobody here has tried the wire. Back in Michigan I pushed thumbtacks through an old tire tread about an inch apart and rode on a frozen lake. Fun, but hopeless on pavement unless you enjoy swapping tires. Think it through, kid.

subject: plutonium
q: If you had enough plutonium to contaminate the New York City reservoirs and made bombs instead, what could you blow up?
a: Nothing, probably. Plutonium is very, very poisonous but not particularly explosive, and the amount needed for a bomb isn't easily transported. Honestly, any idiot who read a book would know that.

subject: Wizard of Oz question
q: In the L. Frank Baum Wizard of Oz, how long was Dorothy unconscious between being knocked on the head in the tornado and coming to after returning from Oz?
a: Sigh. That's what television does to you. In the actual book she was never knocked out and never dreamed anything. The tornado carried her to Oz for real, and she got home by flying over the Deadly Desert in her silver shoes, not ruby slippers.

subject: Pepper Grinders
q: Has anyone seen a good one-hand pepper grinder, either battery powered or with a slide or squeeze mechanism? I can't find one in catalogs or cookery shops.
a: They exist. I've seen both a battery grinder and one you run by squeezing the unit with one hand, in a cooking store in Atlanta. The battery one used a standard grinder. Go look harder.

subject: ?ground mole? (admission of ignorance follows)
q: What is ground mole in a chile recipe, and how do you pronounce it, like the animal or with an accent on the e?
a: It's a Mexican sauce made with chocolate and no peppers. Say MOE-lay. And no, nobody puts the blind rodent in a blender. Honestly.

subject: New 9600 baud modem
q: I heard Digital Communications announced a breakthrough 9600 baud modem that isn't the old half duplex kind. Does anyone know details?
a: PC WEEK for July 16 ran it on the front page. It uses multiple narrow channels and 'adaptive duplex' to fake full duplex, with internal CRC checking. It comes with a stripped-down Crosstalk, at $1995 for the PC card or $2395 stand-alone. Marketing fluff, if you ask me.

subject: Unix PC port
q: Where do I get the shortnames/remap.h file when porting Emacs to the Unix PC?
a: You don't get it, you build it. The remap.h file is created dynamically on the target system because it depends on defines in /usr/include. The shortnames directory has all the pieces. Look before you ask.

subject: FM - What is it?
q: I've seen people in Chess Life referred to as FM. What does that mean? Future Master? Fantastic Master?
a: FM is FIDE Master. That's a master recognized by the international chess federation FIDE, not just by their own country, who hasn't yet reached the norm for International Master. Not exactly rocket science, and no, not Fanatic.

subject: Why no renegade demons, etc.?
q: Why do you always hear of fallen paladins and good things turned evil, but never renegade demons or evil monsters raised to be good?
a: With a change-alignment magic item it's reasonable, but it won't happen naturally. Good characters don't really turn evil, they just go neutral. And a demon or an inherently evil orc protesting South Africa? Please. Red dragons raised from the egg are the only wrinkle.

subject: Why wasn't I invulnerable?
q: I had great armor and weapons from a wand of wishing in Hack but still had a hard time and died. Does armor class or weapon power wrap around at some level, or does the game boost monsters?
a: No wrap-around. Brute strength alone doesn't make a winner; use your head. Write Elbereth in the dust, throw missiles, and wish for gain level, gain strength, wand of death, wand of fire, genocide and tame monster. Think before dying next time.

subject: Demon princes & Lesser gods
q: In srogue I was a 16th level cleric on dungeon level 34 and met demon princes and lesser gods. How do I deal with them, and with black puddings and pit fiends?
a: Lead them into trap doors, or be tough enough to fight them. Best is a magic user who maxes intelligence early. Use your magic points to enchant armor and weapon when wraiths show up, and enchant your teleport scrolls. Spoiler, so don't whine.

subject: Star Wars Trivia
q: Who is the only minor character to survive all three Star Wars movies without dying, and how is that character related to a major character?
a: Wedge Antilles, the X-wing and snow speeder pilot who appears in all three and lives. As for relation, maybe none beyond flying with Luke. One theory: Captain Antilles of the Blockade Runner owned the droids, so if they're related, the droids could be his estate's.

subject: parametric equations
q: Is there an algorithmic way to generate parametric equations for a 3-D surface given in the form f(x,y,z) with ranges for x, y and z?
a: First, a single parameter t gets you a curve, not a surface. Basic stuff. You need two variables: fx(u,v), fy(u,v), fz(u,v), with u and v each running from 0 to 1.

subject: Why are these issues so low?
q: Can anybody shed some light on the recent price drops of Tandon (TCOR) and Denelcor (DENL) common stock?
a: For Tandon, the explanation was that they were grossly over-capitalized. Amateur investors also panicked when they laid off 1000 employees and closed most plants in L.A., though that was a move of manufacturing to Singapore. Fear and greed, kid, not supply and demand.

subject: Stock market is NOT a present value machine
q: Someone said the stock market is just a present value machine. That can't be right, since every stock with the same P/E ratio would then sell at the same price, and it doesn't. Comments?
a: You're mixing things up. Present value is the current worth of the future stream of dividends and capital gains. A P/E ratio is just a snapshot, historic, current or projected, so it's only indirectly related to the present-value idea.

subject: Unfunny things (Re: YABS)
q: Who wrote the limerick about the young man of St. Bees who was stung in the arm by a wasp? Is it George Bernard Shaw?
a: Not Shaw. It's W. S. Gilbert, of Gilbert and Sullivan. Sigh, check your attributions before posting them.

subject: ANSI C and function prototypes
q: With ANSI C prototypes, how can I declare a function pointer argument that points to a function returning anything, not just void?
a: If anything means pointers, declare int dispatcher(int code, void *(*disp_func)()). For scalars and structures you'd have to build a union and return that. And nobody has a prototyping compiler yet to check this, so good luck.

subject: question for a Common Lisp guru
q: Common Lisp says defun is a macro, but there seems to be no special form to implement it, and the book also calls it a special form. Is the book wrong?
a: If the book says it's a macro, it's a macro. Use the step function and you'll see functions get expanded into blocks with all sorts of stuff in them. Try (describe 'defun) for the absolutest right answer.

subject: Relative Number Theory
q: In relative number theory, what is N(a) for an ordinal a? It can't be Peano Arithmetic relativised to a, since induction fails and limit ordinals have no predecessor.
a: N(0) is the Peano postulates. For computable a, N(a) is Peano plus the Goedel sentences P(b) for every b less than a. Computability is required so that N(a) stays a formal system. Past the smallest uncomputable ordinal, Goedelization fails. Think before guessing.

subject: Is there a micro vi?
q: Is there a vi for micros? Has anyone built a vi-like editor for a micro, commercially or privately?
a: Yes, there's 'z' from Manx Software, a very good vi subset for the Macintosh with Aztec C and for MS-DOS PCs. Hard to find a vi command it lacks, only a couple of ex commands. Don't know about the Apple ][, though.

subject: Forget part numbers...
q: What is the state of National's GENIX 4.2BSD implementation? I know the 4.1BSD-based GENIX has been out a while.
a: 4.2 is running in-house and moving toward beta test, with a version in QA. There's more cleanup to do, but the software is in good shape. No final release date yet. Vendors and their dates, sigh.

subject: Defualt actions for System Requesters
q: Has Amiga Kernal 1.2 changed the system requesters so there's a keyboard shortcut for retry or cancel? Having to mouse over to the cancel gadget is a pain.
a: Yes, 1.2 has Amiga key shortcuts for Autorequest requesters. Not obvious, naturally: retry is LeftAmigakey plus B, and cancel is LeftAmigakey plus V. Go read the docs before complaining next time.

subject: windows
q: How do I create an Intuition window in C without a title bar? I can make a borderless window but can't get rid of the title bar without a custom ViewPort. Is there a flag to turn it off?
a: There's a flag byte, the one called type in the AmigaBASIC WINDOW description. The bit for decimal 2 decides whether you get a drag bar. You probably want all the bits off, maybe leaving bit 16 on for the redisplay buffer. Read the manual harder.

subject: 1.2 keymap woes
q: Why did the AmigaOS 1.2 keymap change so that ALT keys no longer send char+128 for MicroEmacs? Can I get the 1.1 behavior back?
a: The 1.2 keymap added dead keys for foreign language support. Software that assumed fixed ALT keycodes broke, foolish software. The final 1.2 release disk has a usa0 keymap just like 1.1. Run 'setmap usa0'. You need the release disk, not the beta.

subject: STwriter, Hard disks, and Will Hom
q: How can I get STwriter to print single-spaced on an Epson FX-80 on the serial port? Control-S variants haven't worked.
a: Check your printer's dip switches. One of them does an automatic line feed on each carriage return, which is what double-spaces you. It's the printer, not the word processor.

subject: How to photograph color monitor?
q: Any pointers or hints on how to photograph a color monitor display?
a: Use an SLR on a tripod and darken the room. Shutter at 1/2 second or longer, f-stop way down around f22, and check with a light meter. The long exposure blurs out scan lines. It's not rocket science, kid.

subject: 3b2/hayes problem
q: Can I get a Hayes-compatible modem to work as both dial-in and dial-out on a 3B2/300 with uugetty? Carrier detect switch settings only allow one direction.
a: No surprise, the Hayes was never designed to do that. AT&T's support center got it working with a kluge of moderate proportions, but the sane approach is buying a modem that does both, like the AT&T 2224B or the Penril. Don't kluge.

subject: 3B1, 32100, etc.
q: How does the AT&T 3B1 differ from the 7300?
a: The 3B1 is a 7300 with a larger disk, and I think an extra RS-232 port. Salesfolks still call it the 7300 or UNIX PC. For info, try a local computer store that carries AT&T. Marketing names, sigh.

subject: Putting a 1541 on its side??
q: Is it OK to put a 1541 disk drive on its side to save desk space?
a: No harm to the drive or disks. Keep it against a wall or something stable so it doesn't wobble when you insert and extract disks. Tipping wouldn't help the alignment. Honestly, buy a bigger desk.

subject: DBASE II
q: Is there a compiler for dBASE II? I don't want to give away my sources with a program, the way MBASIC programs can at least be protected against listing.
a: Last I heard there's no dBASE II compiler. Ashton-Tate does sell a runtime subset that runs your command files without giving the user the dBASE command level. Go ask them, and bring your wallet for the license, naturally.

subject: Updated Finder and MacWrite
q: I got a new Macintosh with Finder 1.1g and MacWrite 2.20, but the latest release is 4.0 for both. How do I upgrade? I hope I don't have to pay full price.
a: The upgrade should be free, and available from your dealer, or from some dealer in your area. Surprised you didn't get it with the Mac in the first place. Ask the dealer, don't pay.

subject: Pascal compiler for Mac needed
q: I need a Pascal compiler for the Mac to port PC-DOS Pascal source into a stand-alone program, since MacPascal only interprets. What do you recommend?
a: Buy the TML Pascal compiler. It gives full access to the toolbox and OS routines and can also run generic Pascal with a TTY window for standard I/O, which saves you porting headaches. Turbo Pascal for the Mac is only a rumor so far.

subject: Grow Box in Mac+ windows
q: I'm running System 3.0 and Finder 5.1 on a 512K Mac and don't see the new grow box on windows like on the Mac+. Should it be there, and how do I find the version of a System?
a: The grow box lives in the new 128K ROMs, so your 512K machine won't get it. See Tech Note #57. The system version is in a STR resource that says "System Version x.x". Just open them till you find it. Sigh.

subject: What is Latest Ver. of RMaker??
q: What is the latest version of RMaker? Mine, 2.2, doesn't match the REdit decompile output or support ICONs.
a: Who cares. RMaker was just a stopgap. ResEdit has gotten so good that I use RMaker only for STR resources, which are easier to edit in a text editor and then compile. I've yet to see a good Mac version.

subject: Help Wanted (Please!)
q: After I increased the environment size with SHELL=C:\COMMAND.COM /e:32 in CONFIG.SYS, AUTOEXEC.BAT doesn't run automatically. How do I fix this?
a: You left out /P. Use SHELL=d:\COMMAND.COM /P /E:62. The /P makes COMMAND.COM stay resident and run AUTOEXEC. Without it, typing exit locks the machine because there's no command interpreter. Read the manual.

subject: IBM tech support tele number
q: Does anyone have the IBM technical support number that they don't give out to non-dealers? I have hardware questions the local people can't answer.
a: The hardware-only tech support line was 1-800-428-2569, as of last year, anyway. There's no similar number for software, I think. The people were well-informed, but sent one caller on to a non-toll-free number in Boca. Try it yourself instead of begging the net.

subject: Lex for IBM PC-AT, is it available?
q: Is there a lex(1) program available for the IBM PC-AT under MSDOS 3.x, and which C compilers work with it?
a: The Austin Code Works sells Lex and Yacc cheap, plus a preprocessor called prep. It's compatible with DeSmet C and may work with Lattice or Microsoft. The C-kermit distribution also has wart, a free public domain lex-like preprocessor. Check the back of Byte.

subject: Vaporware prize
q: Is there an annual prize for vaporware in the computer world? Has anyone ever advertised and taken money for a software product four months before it was available?
a: Not this week, anyway. Ads six months to a year before the first unit ships are nothing unusual in the micro world. Four months is amateur hour. Where have you been?

subject: computer music
q: I can't find a computer music newsgroup. Where do I look? I also want to write music software for my Amiga, so is there any public domain source for staff-entry or wave-editing interfaces?
a: Sigh, look before you post. Computer-generated music is synthesized music, so the group you want is net.music.synth. People talk about computer music there all the time, so go ask the interested parties directly.

subject: Avatex 1200 bd modems for $99??
q: I saw an Avatex 1200 baud modem advertised for $99. Has anybody bought one, or do you get what you pay for?
a: Mine's been fine and reliable so far. It's a Hayes compatible with decent quality, missing only busy signal detection so it just times out after 30 seconds. Cheap 1200 baud is hardly rocket science, so stop clinging to your 300.

subject: Michael Cimino's first film - query
q: Somewhere I read that The Deer Hunter was Michael Cimino's second film. Does anyone know the name of his first?
a: Thunderbolt and Lightfoot, with Clint Eastwood and Jeff Bridges. Any movie buff knows that one. Honestly, this is what reference books are for.

subject: Springsteen demos?
q: A radio station played unreleased early Springsteen demo and audition songs. Where did they get them, and is that stuff a promo or a bootleg?
a: There's a bootleg floating around called DEMOS. The station almost certainly got the tracks from it, which is why they were so evasive when asked. Work it out yourself.

subject: IS SGT. PEPPER REALLY A CONCEPT ALBUM?
q: Is Sgt. Pepper really a concept album? What's the concept?
a: Loosely, love and friendship as antidotes to 20th-century alienation, hence the lonely hearts club. Little Help From My Friends is about friendship, A Day In The Life about everyday stress, and When I'm 64 about family as an antidote. Hardly a rigorous concept, mind you.

subject: Even Bismark, ND has a scene ... why can't Washington, DC?
q: What can you tell me about the band The Suburbs from Minneapolis?
a: They were one of Minneapolis's early post-punk bands, with two Twin/Tone albums and an EP that got them signed to Polydor, where they died quietly after one album. Now they're in the studio with REO Speedwagon's producer. Depressing.

subject: DICKIES!
q: What do you know about the band the Dickies, like where they're from and what albums they have?
a: They've been around since about 1978 and come from California. Albums include The Incredible Shrinking Dickies, with a great Paranoid cover, and Dawn of the Dickies, with the Nights in White Satin cover. There's a third with a Communication Breakdown cover, but I forget its name.

subject: Pathology of "Cannot install article as ..." ?
q: Our news errlog regularly shows "inews: Cannot install article as ...". What causes this, and have I set something up wrong?
a: Probably part of your news tree isn't writable by "news". Change the ownership of the directory and the error goes away. Check the news log file for the explanatory messages, which is where any sane admin would look first.

subject: Dasher to VAX
q: How do I get a Data General Dasher D211 terminal working properly with a VAX running VMS? It talks but things like the DELETE key don't work.
a: DG terminals in DG mode don't use ^H to backspace, so of course delete breaks. The D211 has an ANSI mode that looks like a vt100 without tabs. Early models didn't backspace right on ^H there, so you may need the latest firmware.

subject: cancelling forces
q: If two robots push on opposite sides of a box so the forces cancel, they still put in energy but the box doesn't move. Where does the energy go?
a: Heat, mostly, inside the drive devices of the robots, plus friction and slip losses. Strictly, force through zero displacement is no work, so only losses count. It eventually radiates away; entropy wins again. Go look up thermodynamics.

subject: grammars in physics
q: Since any calculation can be done by a Turing machine, and its language generated by an unrestricted grammar, what grammar describes nature? Is there one for quantum mechanics?
a: The premise is wrong. Nature does not have to perform calculations. Think before you post.

subject: Does checked baggage get x-rayed and if so what kind?
q: Does checked baggage get x-rayed, and with what kind of x-rays? Is it safe to put film in checked bags, or will even a Film Shield not protect it?
a: Don't put film in checked baggage. Airports are x-raying everything lately, and a film shield just looks like a suspicious lump, so they'll open your bag anyway. Carry the film in hand luggage, in a clear baggie, and ask for a hand check. Any idiot traveler learns this.

subject: question: how to prepare house surface for painting
q: My clapboard house has badly alligatored, peeling paint on two walls. After scraping, the surface is uneven where paint chips remain bonded. Is there a better way than hand sanding, like a drill attachment?
a: Forget the drill attachment. Rent a disc sander, very high RPM, about $15, though it leaves swirls. A water blaster works too, but it can gouge soft or rotted wood and soaks you. A belt sander kept wet won't clog. Prime bad spots with boiled linseed oil first.

subject: Earth's one immortal man
q: In Weapon Shops of Isher, there's a mysterious character called Earth's one immortal man who founded the Weapon Shops. Was he ever developed in another book, or was he just a plot device?
a: The author is Van Vogt, not whatever you typed. The theme gets developed further in The Weapon Makers. Read it before asking the net next time.

subject: Ulysses probe
q: How can the Ulysses probe go over the Sun's poles if it uses a Jupiter flyby? I figured a passive pass could only get it 26 degrees out of the ecliptic.
a: Ulysses leaves Earth about 2 degrees off the ecliptic. A hyperbolic Jupiter flyby at 141 degrees inclination, retrograde, flings it into a solar orbit inclined about 77 degrees, passing high over the south pole first. Later it passes the north too. Work the conics properly.

subject: double-spacing in TeX and LaTeX
q: Is there a simple way to get double-spacing in LaTeX or TeX? I've searched the manuals and found nothing, and my hacked style that bumps \baselineskip doesn't let me switch back and forth.
a: In LaTeX, put \renewcommand{\baselinestretch}{2.0} before \begin{document}. In plain TeX, set \baselineskip. Sigh, it's all in the manual if you look in the right place.

subject: "dot" file deleted!
q: Somehow the "." entry got removed from one of my directories, so I can't read or access anything in it, and I can't even rmdir it. How do I remove the directory or get at the files again? I'm on System V rel 2 on a VAX 11/780.
a: Get someone with the su password to write a little program that calls link(2) to link the directory to its own name slash dot. Only root can link directories. Or if you just want it gone, that same su'er can unlink it. Sigh, next time don't go poking around.

subject: C++ installation
q: Is it sufficient to change the C++ stdio.h header when the FILE member order differs from the system /usr/include/stdio.h on Amdahl UTS?
a: Leave stdio.h alone. FILE must match the one compiled into libc.a, i.e. the one in <stdio.h>, because C++ here is just a preprocessor over cc. If you mix a C++ library using FILEs with your native C library, you're out of luck. Elementary.

subject: need stereo viewer for 35mm slides
q: Where can I buy an inexpensive stereo viewer for 35mm slides, something like a ViewMaster where you put two slides in and look through two lenses?
a: We use the folding cardboard viewers from Taylor-Merchant Corp in New York. Cheap and very satisfactory, no need for fancy plastic.

subject: INEWS -C
q: I ran inews -C tropez to create a local-only newsgroup, and uucico then called my feed and sent something. Did I just litter some admin's disk?
a: Probably, yes. Inews usually defaults to world distribution. Use inews -d local -C tropez. Otherwise posts go out to any feedee wanting everything, and other sites may auto-create the group. One poster accidentally spawned a silly alt group that way. Be damn careful.

subject: city ? [city] (was Re: ... map latitude/longitudes)
q: In comp.mail.maps location entries, should approximate positions be flagged with the word city or with [city] in brackets?
a: Plain "city", no brackets. The brackets in the readme just mean the word is optional. A grep through the maps shows "city" is by far the most popular form, and the map software wants to see exactly that word. Florida's [city] is simply wrong.

subject: Net saturation
q: UUCP Usenet is getting saturated by binaries and talk postings. Wouldn't it be a good fix to get more sites onto the Internet and use anonymous FTP instead of posting binaries everywhere?
a: Ah, if only it were that simple. Sites connected to the Internet have a clause in their contract forbidding them from hooking up someone else and passing that traffic. Hearsay, mind you, but that's the catch. Nobody just gets on.

subject: USENET protocols
q: Where can I find a definition of the USENET protocols so I can put USENET up on other platforms?
a: RFC 1036 tells you just about everything that's documented. It says nothing about the underlying transmission, like uucp, so you'll have to sort out getting data from A to B yourself. Usenet is a logical network, not a physical one. Read up.

subject: Miscellaneous C-News Questions
q: Why doesn't C News expire update the start-of-articles field in the active file, so users see messages like 2000 new messages in a group? And where can I FTP the latest C News and patches?
a: Because that field showed up after expire was written, and the whole concept is an unworkable botch. If you insist, use upact or updatemin. The distribution is on ftp.cs.toronto.edu in pub/c-news, patches in pub/c-news/patches. Not during their peak hours, please.

subject: crossposting to moderated and unmoderated groups
q: With nntp/cnews, when I post to both a moderated and an unmoderated group, the article goes to the moderator but not into the batch for the unmoderated group. Is this a problem?
a: No, that's correct behavior. There's only one article, not separate copies. The moderator posts it to both groups if approved. Honestly, think before you call it a bug.

subject: Bitnet service is free (?)
q: People say Bitnet service is free, but someone must pay for it. Where does the money come from?
a: Membership is by institution, not per node. A university pays one fee regardless of how many nodes it has, scaled to its budget as a measure of its potential use. Nothing is free, kid; someone's budget just eats it.

subject: IN MODERATION
q: Was the announcement about IN MODERATION legit? It seemed satirical in parts, and the spokesperson's name and the company name seemed phony.
a: It's real. The man, his MIPS machine and his company are all legit, and the service probably is too. The tone was a parody of high-tech press puffery, but larger firms do it with a straight face. Some people have no sense of humor.

subject: adding and feeding news at the same time, can this be done
q: Can I run two batch jobs at the same time with ANU News, one adding news items from the nntp batch files and another running nntp_xmit to the sites I feed? I'm using the NX option in news.sys for the feeds.
a: Yes. Been doing exactly that for about a year with no problems. Sigh, try it before asking next time.

subject: Moderator Functions from remote node
q: Can you issue moderator functions from a non-local NNTP node for ANU News on VMS, or do you have to be on the node with the news database?
a: No. The NNTP protocol doesn't support it, so you do your moderating on the local node. Sigh, it's a news transport protocol, not a remote admin shell.

subject: Running News clusterwide
q: I run ANU-News V6.0-3 with Multinet on one VAX in a cluster, but Multinet is licensed only on that node. Is there a way to run ANU News clusterwide?
a: Yes, it's easy. Build the main NEWS.EXE with no TCP, and build only the NNTP server programs, NNTP_WINMULTINET.EXE and NNTP_XMIT, with Multinet support. Incoming TCP only reaches the Multinet host, so run the NNTP_XMIT batch queue there too. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: availability of V6.03 on mailserv or fileserv nodes
q: Is V6.03 of ANU-NEWS available from any mailserver or fileserver? I don't have FTP access.
a: Yes, the MRCserv mailserver at Janus.MtRoyal.AB.CA has it in the [.VMS.ANU_NEWS] directory. Fair warning: the three save sets total over 12,000 blocks, so default 100-block parts means 120 pieces. Enjoy the busywork.

subject: news ITEMS display question-- 'from' column?
q: Is there a way to disable the 'from' column in the ANU News newsgroup items display, so the subject lines don't get chopped off?
a: Simple: SET PROFILE/FROM=0. It takes effect next time you enter NEWS. Any number after FROM= sets how many characters of the from address are shown; the default is 19. It's in the docs, you know.

subject: Problems with controlling NNTP access
q: My NNTP_ACCESS.NEWS entry for a client gives read and post, but NNTP insists I have no posting privileges after going to V6.0-2. What am I missing?
a: The client name format depends on which server you run. For TCP clients use the full domain name, and always put a wildcard or group list in the newsgroup field, because an empty field means no groups. Names aren't case sensitive. Read the instructions in the file itself.

subject: Waikato Menus?
q: When I start ANU-NEWS I see a line mentioning "Waikato Menus - Press ESC at NEWS> prompt". What are the Waikato Menus?
a: Press ESC or F11 and you get a series of small menus; pick with the arrow keys. The code came from the University of Waikato in New Zealand, hence the name. Not hard, try it again without panicking.

subject: Building ANU-News for Multinet
q: When compiling ANU-News for Multinet I get time_t declaration conflicts in NEWSREMCLIENT, NNTP_XMIT and NNTP_XFER. What is the problem?
a: It's a conflict between the definitions in Multinet and the ones DEC uses. Ignore the messages; they don't cause any problems. This comes up every time, and it's harmless noise.

subject: Cnews: Who should own news articles?
q: After installing Cnews on a new news server, articles are owned by root instead of news, and expire reports permission errors. Who should own the articles, and what did I do wrong?
a: Articles should always be owned by news. Check how nntp is run. If it runs as root, which is naughty, it runs relaynews as root and everything ends up owned by root. Run it as news. Don't run things as root.

subject: C News: dbminit called more than once
q: After upgrading C News from 14Sep89 to 12Mar90 I get occasional errors saying dbminit may only be called once, and articles repeat. What causes this and is a fix coming?
a: Sigh. Relaynews flushes caches before running a child for a control message, using dbmclose() then dbminit() again. That fails where dbmclose() is our do-nothing fake and dbminit() refuses a second call. We overlooked it. A fix is imminent, along with official dbz support.

subject: CNEWS expire leaves history owned by root
q: C News expire leaves the history file owned by root if I run it as root, and updatemin does the same to the active file. Shouldn't it seteuid to the news user or chown the files?
a: Not trivial, and we decided not to bother. Once you fix the C programs you'd have to fix the shell files too, and that gets tricky. Policy is that news admins run things as the news uid. It's documented. We won't burn code space defending against every newsadmin blunder.

subject: Cnews version of inews with nfs server
q: C news inews runs relaynews remotely with rsh and PATH=$PATH, which fails under csh and for users without accounts on the news server. Is there a fix not involving NNTP?
a: Already fixed. The 14-Sep-1989 patch significantly revised inews's rsh handling. Apply the patches before complaining; this is what they're for.

subject: Cnews ihave/sendmes
q: Can Cnews still run ihave/sendme with a Bnews site? And how do I get Cnews to put a Lines: header in locally posted messages, like Bnews used to?
a: Ihave/sendme works fine with Bnews sites, no problems known, though it's a spooky area even for the Cnews authors. For Lines:, uncomment the 7 lines in inews that start with the comment about a sop to msb. Cnews doesn't rewrite headers, read the docs.

subject: addmissing dies with assert in histslash (Cnews)
q: Cnews addmissing dies with an assertion failure in histslash, "last != NULL", after an hour of CPU time. Would it be safe to change histslash to ignore blank lines?
a: Don't bother patching histslash. The bug is in histdups, the previous stage of the pipeline, which emits a blank line when no articles are missing at all. It's fixed in the next patch, and meanwhile it's harmless apart from the annoying message and core dump.

subject: Problem compiling latest C-news under Ultrix 4.1
q: Compiling C News with the fast stdio routines on Ultrix 4.1 fails in rdwr.c with 'redeclaration of fread' and 'fwrite'. Can I coax the compiler into accepting them?
a: Try changing those char pointers to void pointers. Fair warning: that means more work inside the routines to make it all come out right, so it's not a trivial fix. Welcome to portability.

subject: News software: binary files and distributed DB's
q: Has anyone used news software to carry a distributed database, using message-IDs as product numbers and owners?
a: No, message-IDs must be unique per message. A duplicate won't show up on your system, and that's vital for loop prevention with redundant connections. News works fine as a transport for database updates, though. Put the product and owner info in an X- header or the body. Think before you hack.

subject: How to Create Local Moderated Groups (cnews site)?
q: How do I create a moderated local newsgroup on a cnews site?
a: Create the group with addgroup. Then add a line to NEWSCTL/mailpaths with the group name and the moderator's address, like our.local.group itsmoderator@here. That's all of it.

subject: "Problems with my active file"
q: I got an automatic news message saying my active file has invalid newsgroups and I should delete them, but it listed all thousand-plus of my groups and they're all valid. What generates this message, and what is it based on?
a: That's a checkgroups control message arriving, and C News mails you delete instructions for every group it dislikes. There's no clear spec for the message contents and the C News checkgroups code is known to be buggy. Ignore the mail. Sigh, this gets fixed eventually.

subject: Patch, patchlevels, Who's on first?
q: I just got C News running on my Xenix box but don't know what patchlevel it is. Is there an easy way to find out?
a: Look at the PATCHDATES file in the source directory. Sigh, it's sitting right there in the source tree; try looking before posting.

subject: Corrupt history file?
q: I keep getting a mail message from expire saying a garbled name is not a directory. Is it a corrupt line in the history file, and what's the fastest cure?
a: No, it's not the history file. It's a corrupt line in your explist file. That message appears when an archiving directory, given in explist or the -a option, can't be found. Fix explist and leave your 6 MB history alone. Read the error before rebuilding things.

subject: cross-posting to moderated and unmoderated groups
q: If I cross-post to a moderated group and an unmoderated one, the article gets mailed to the moderator and isn't posted to the unmoderated group. Will the moderator post it there, or should I post separately?
a: The multi-group Newsgroups line is a request that the moderator cross-post it once approved. Don't post twice yourself, let the software work as designed. The moderator may skip groups that don't fit, or if it's a digest.

subject: Why am I still getting stale/misdated news?
q: If UUNET has upgraded to C News, why do I still get stale or misdated news? What version of C News are they running?
a: First, are you sure it comes from UUNET? They ran B News before, which had similar date filters. Their idea of stale may be more generous than yours. They run a newer, greater C News with mods for their odd setup. Expect surprises.

subject: SCO Bnews, C News, and ihave/sendme woes
q: My SCO B News posts an ihave to my C News machine, but C News never sends back a sendme. Is something wrong with SCO B News?
a: Probably not your B News. Nobody has seen ihave working under C News on any site they feed. The feature likely isn't quite functional yet. Don't waste a week debugging it.

subject: Problems getting map articles added to Batch file for uuhosts
q: My news sys line for comp.mail.maps doesn't append filenames to the Batch file, though a similar line for local.test works. What's the difference?
a: Both the newsgroup and the distribution have to match the sys line, and map postings go out with distribution world. So write it as maps:comp.mail.maps,world:F:... and add na or usa too if updates use those. It's in the manual.

subject: C News, 386/ix, assorted questions/experiences
q: What does expire -c do in C News, and how do I deal with nn expiring from the active file's third field?
a: Expire -c just does expire's startup processing, reading and parsing the control and active files, then exits. It's a debugging aid. Readers that expect contiguous article numbers between min and max are broken, pure and simple. Run upact nightly in the wee hours.

subject: uucp: PERMISSION (DENIED) - why?
q: Why do I occasionally get a uucp PERMISSION DENIED on a news batch when most batches arrive fine?
a: Usually you've already received that batch. If the link drops after the data file is sent but before the command file is acknowledged, the other end retries the data file, and you reject it because it's already there. Then the command file goes through and all is well. Harmless.

subject: Another CNews Question
q: With CNews, if I run df -t before and after expire, will the drop in inodes equal the number of articles expired? I'm trying to tell whether CNews is throwing away incoming news.
a: Yes, roughly, since an expired article means a reclaimed inode. Allow for directories created by archiving and for incoming news processed during expire, since a running expire doesn't lock out incoming processing. Also, df -iv is more informative than df -t.

subject: Unwanted News groups
q: How do I stop my feeding site from sending me unwanted newsgroups like ba.* and ca.* when I run nntpxfer? Editing the batch file at his site makes NNTP barf.
a: Look in the news spool directory, usually /usr/spool/news. The file is called nntp.REMOTE, where REMOTE is the name of the site you nntpxfer from. Edit that one, not the batch file you were mangling.

subject: news feed over Ethernet: how?
q: How can I get a news feed running over Ethernet when my 9600 bps hardware doesn't look like any standard modem? I was thinking of rlogin'ing into the feed and running uucico from there. Is there a better way?
a: Your rlogin kludge will be a pain, since rlogin won't run transparent without an escape character unless you have source. 4.3 uucp can run over a TCP connection, though Sun is probably sluggish about picking it up. NNTP is a Good Thing; some feeds can use it without forcing all of them to. Sigh.

subject: How do I register my node ???
q: How do I officially register my node in the UUCP maps? I tried in December and heard nothing, and we're not in the Pennsylvania map.
a: The addresses posted with the maps are wrong. Use uucpmap@rutgers for map changes and dpz@rutgers for Pennsylvania. Mail to uucpmap@cbosgd gets forwarded badly and bounces. Send your entries there and you should show up within a month.

subject: ** Asking Bnews 2.11 for Patchlevel **
q: How do you ask Bnews 2.11 inews what patch level it is?
a: You can't, I think. But each release has a unique SCCS ID, so run what on inews. For example, inews.c 2.92 9/1/89 means B 2.11.18, and 2.91 1/24/89 means 2.11.17. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: Public/student terminal/PC rooms
q: How do you keep the equipment in public student terminal and PC rooms clean? Are keyboard covers common, and what cleaning solutions do you use?
a: Windex works pretty well on the keyboards. Another site uses an occasional weekend, a molecular cleaner called FD, and some student assistants, a couple of hours' work. Don't trust the janitors, they'll hit BREAK on the console. Peanut butter is a clientele problem.

subject: Help! My history files are taking over!
q: My news history files are huge and /usenet/lib is over 15000 blocks. What can I do to reduce this?
a: On 2.11 news, expired article IDs stay in history for four weeks by default to stop old articles reappearing. About 1.5 meg is right for that. Change the HISTEXP define in defs.h to something smaller, like 3 weeks. Rebuild, obviously.

subject: keeping canister tubing clean?
q: How do I keep the tubing of my new canister filter from clogging with algae?
a: Pull a small square of cloth through the tube on a string, weighted at one end with a sinker or bit of coat hanger wire so you can drop it through. Do it every couple of months. Or force compacted filter floss through with a hose. Bleach works too.

subject: Tank light too bright ?
q: My fish head for the bottom and hide when I turn on the 25 watt, 24 inch fluorescent tube over my 3 foot tank. Is the light too bright, and what light should I have?
a: The light sounds fine. Some fish just don't like light. Switch it on and off at the same times each day, only once a day, and add floating plants so they have cover near the surface. Not every fish wants a tanning bed.

subject: pH fine tuning
q: My water is pH 7.2 and 70 ppm hardness, and my community tank fish like about 6.8 and 120-140 ppm. Should I lower the pH with buffers and worry about hardness?
a: Leave it. Don't increase the hardness; 70 ppm is just fine for these fish and most plants. Buffers are a temporary stop-gap that you must keep using. If you really must lower the pH, use peat. Stop fiddling.

subject: Something is killing my fish.
q: Something killed my kuhli loach and pleco, with a white film around their bodies. The other fish look fine, the temperature is steady at 79 F, and it doesn't look like ich. What is it?
a: Ich is granular, not filmy, so probably not that. Likely ammonia or other toxins built up and hit toxic levels, and plecos are the most sensitive. Fungus moves in after death. Change a third of the water, and do it regularly next time.

subject: Post-nuclear fiction
q: When was the first post-nuclear-war novel or short story published, the kind with society collapsed and survivors struggling afterward?
a: As far as anyone here knows, it's The World Set Free by H. G. Wells, published around 1905. Wells knew nothing of fallout, but he handled the social collapse well. Nobody has contradicted this yet, so go read it.

subject: Lobo/Wolverine; DC/Marvel (was Re: Who'd Win ? # 2)
q: Has Marvel ever shown Wolverine getting his clock cleaned, big time, the way Lobo gets beaten up in DC comics?
a: Thanos in the Infinity Gauntlet. Wolverine gets clobbered big time there. Go read it.

subject: X-Men #1 -- How much?
q: How much will the new X-Men series sell for? I know issue #1 is $1.50. Will that price hold through the series?
a: No. The deluxe cover edition, out the second week of September, is $3.95, or $4.95 Canadian. Typical comics gouging, if you ask me.

subject: Nagging at my brain
q: I saw a Superman cover where he's punched by a big orange scaly guy with a mohawk, with a 'Vote for' sign behind. Who is the orange guy and which issue is it?
a: Sounds like Rampage, the Doctor Faulkner issue. Poster only thinks they have that issue, so no promises on the number. Check your own longboxes next time before nagging the net.

subject: Fisher King and Mage
q: In the comic Mage, wasn't the evil guy called The Fisher King? How does that fit with the movie of the same name?
a: No, no. The bad guy was the Umbra Sprite. The Fisher King was the good man whose blood the villain wanted for his ritual. The name in both Mage and the Gilliam film comes from Arthurian mythology. Get it straight.

subject: "Rocketeer", the comic NOT the FILM, query
q: Is the Airboy comic from the 1940s still published? How can the characters still be around when they'd be in their 70s or 80s now?
a: The recent Airboy is the son of the original, and the series is on the shelf for now. Can't speak for the Blackhawks. Do the math before you ask.

subject: Captain America Movie???
q: Was a Captain America movie made last year, starting with Rogers before he became Cap, fighting the Red Skull and getting frozen? Has it been released?
a: Yes, Marvel showed it at the Chicago ComicCon last summer, and a European movie poster was dated summer 1990. It looked halfway decent, better than the Punisher movie. Rumor says it hits video this winter. Don't hold your breath on a theater release.

subject: Sandman #28 Cover
q: What do the kanji on the cover of this month's Sandman #28 say? The 2nd and 3rd look like 'new' and 'life'.
a: The whole phrase translates to 'Newborn Baby', and it refers to Nada. The first and last characters are parentheses. The wording is a bit unconventional for modern Chinese, as if the cover artist was more into Japanese.

subject: LEE and PORTACIO first works??
q: What were the first comics that Jim Lee and Whilce Portacio ever did?
a: Nobody here knows the very first, but early work includes Jim Lee on Alpha Flight around issue 51 and a Mockingbird story in Solo Avengers number 1. Portacio's earliest pencilling was the Punisher, from issue 8 I believe. Go dig through the back-issue bins.

subject: More X-Questions
q: Whatever happened to Wolverine's hallucinations of Nick Fury and Carol Danvers? And why didn't the Shadow King detect the creature in Psylocke's mind that kept the Hand from fully brainwashing her?
a: The hallucinations were just Wolverine's fevered mind, and they vanished once he healed and got his head clear. As for Psylocke, that was Mojo, and he wasn't around when the Shadow King mind-controlled her. Pay attention, will you?

subject: New Titans
q: Why can't Jericho in the Teen Titans talk, when the evil Jericho in New Titans 75 does?
a: Back story, as I recall: terrorists kidnapped him to get at his father Terminator and cut his vocal cords. So he can't talk, unless he takes over the body of someone knocked out, and then he speaks with that person's vocabulary. Read your own comics.

subject: CORNER BOX on COVERS
q: Why can't comic publishers remove the corner box on newsstand covers, when the direct-sales editions put a Spider-Man head there instead?
a: Cover stock is preprinted with a blacked-out box for the artist's reference. What shows in the box is only on the black plate; it's blocked out on the red, yellow and blue plates. Running full art there would cost great extra expense. Printing 101, kid.

subject: Those guys who shoot rays from their hands
q: Why do so many super-heroes with ray powers fire them from their hands?
a: Likely aiming. Arms and hands are easier to point than a belly-button. One theory: their energy goes out in every direction, and training lets them direct it through the hands. Strikeforce: Morituri even had a character wearing focusing cylinders on his hands. Honestly, it's comics.

subject: Audience control
q: Are Disneyland people told not to do anything about guests who ignore the no-flash requests during shows? The Disney person at the back of the Tiki Room did nothing while someone took flash pictures all through it.
a: Not so. Attendants are supposed to give the spiel and then enforce it as necessary, up to calling security. Half the offenders don't speak English anyway, and the rest just don't listen. Sigh.

subject: Looking for a Movie title
q: I saw an animated clip with a mouse named Basil, his friend Dawson, and an evil rat named Ratigan. What was the book, who wrote it, and what's the film called?
a: The book is Basil of Baker Street, though I don't know the author. The Disney feature is The Great Mouse Detective. Sigh, that one's not hard.

subject: Movie 'Willow' ?
q: What is the movie 'Willow'? Is it a Disney release, recent, live action, or connected to The Wind in the Willows?
a: Not Disney, and nothing to do with Wind in the Willows. George Lucas made it, directed by him too, and it's about a dwarf's adventures, the title character. It wasn't well received, just a shade better than Howard the Duck. Do your homework.

subject: water colour painting
q: I've started water colour painting classes. Can anyone suggest good references, and any words of wisdom about techniques, papers and colours?
a: Get Painting What You (want to) See by Charles Reid, with lots of reproductions and critiques. Buy GOOD quality paints, since cheap ones are chalky and not transparent, and tubes beat cakes. Get a ream of paper and experiment. Watercolor is demanding stuff.

subject: Cherryh - Forty Thousand In Gehenna/Cuckoo9s Egg
q: After reading Cherryh's Chanur books, Cuckoo's Egg and Forty Thousand in Gehenna, what should I read next?
a: Read Merchanter's Luck next, since it fits well with what you've read. Then try the Faded Sun trilogy. Do your homework before asking for a sequel.

subject: A for Andrommeda (was SF plots)
q: Does anyone have info on Fred Hoyle's "A for Andromeda" and the BBC TV series it was supposedly made into?
a: It started as a BBC serial, seven 45-minute episodes from 3 Oct to 14 Nov 1961. Hoyle did the plot, John Elliot wrote the scripts, and Hoyle novelized them. A sequel, Andromeda Breakthrough, followed in 1962. Never shown in the US, as far as I know. It was Julie Christie's first pro job.

subject: Rollerball - the movie and the book
q: Does anyone know about the book Rollerball, the one that shares its title with the movie? Who wrote it, when was it published, and did it end differently from the film?
a: It's a collection called Rollerball Murders, and only the title story is science fiction or got filmed. William Harrison wrote it and the screenplay too. Hardcover 1973, paperback a year later. Nobody remembers the ending; go read it yourself.

subject: Dickson's "Childe Cycle"
q: Gordon Dickson began the Childe Cycle in the 50's with a grand plan, yet he's only written a half dozen books. Why are people in awe of its scale?
a: Your premise is off. The plan was nine books: three historical, three contemporary and three science fiction. He never wrote the historicals or contemporaries, and the sf triad grew well past three. That sums it up.

subject: Tim Powers: "The Drawing of the Dark" - comments?
q: Has anyone read "The Drawing of the Dark" by Tim Powers? OtherRealms gave it five stars. Do you agree with that rating?
a: Five stars? Hardly. Of Powers' books I've read, it's the weakest, though still a fun read. Try The Anubis Gates or On Stranger Tides first. Ratings in those magazines are inflated anyway.

subject: Wanted: parodies of Dune and Covenant
q: Has anyone written a parody of Donaldson's Thomas Covenant books or of Herbert's Dune, as a book, story or machine-readable text?
a: Yes, plenty. Dave Langford wrote both the Covenant and Dune sendups, collected in a book of his parodies, though it's hard to find now. Joanna Russ's story about May the Unpregnant and the Harvard Lampoon's Doon are also mentioned.

subject: Joan Vinge/Catspaw
q: I just read Catspaw and was impressed. Can anyone tell me about Joan Vinge and her work? Did she win a Hugo for The Snow Queen, and is she Vernor Vinge's ex-wife?
a: Yes on both counts. The Snow Queen won the Hugo, around 1981, and Vernor is her ex-husband. She's also written Mother and Child, The Crystal Ship and Eyes of Amber. Not prolific, but what she writes tends to be very good. Do some reading.

subject: Piers Anthony - A question
q: I liked the first Xanth books and the first Apprentice Adept books. What other Piers Anthony books are worth reading?
a: On a Pale Horse is his best, and the Incarnations of Immortality series is good. Omnivore and Steppe are decent too, and the first Kirlian Quest books are fine. The later Adept and Xanth books just work the ideas to death. Skip Bio of a Space Tyrant.

subject: Day of the Triffids
q: I'm tracking down all versions of The Day of the Triffids: the 1950 book, a 1963 black-and-white movie, and a 1981 color movie. Did I get the dates right or miss any?
a: The 1981 one was a six-part BBC TV mini-series, filmed in color, shown on PBS and Arts & Entertainment. And Revolt of the Triffids is no sequel, just a retitled paperback edition of the original. Read the cover, people.

subject: The Devil's Day (spoilers)
q: In Blish's The Devil's Day, what do the closing lines mean: Domenico thinks, Baines believes, Ware hopes, Ginsberg loves?
a: You've got it backwards, sigh. Each has learned to do what he says: Ginsberg learned to love after random sex proved unsatisfying, Ware the black magician regained hope, and Baines the nihilist came to believe in something. Domenico's conclusion is left to the reader.

subject: Sauron (Question about.)
q: In the Second Age when the Ring was cut off, why did Sauron leave Middle Earth, and how did he come back in the Third Age if he needs the Ring?
a: He didn't leave. He lost his form and was greatly diminished, so it looked that way. He didn't need the Ring to take shape again, only to regain all his former power, since he'd put so much of it in there. Read the books.

subject: A next yet another Tolkien question...
q: Is Glorfindel from Lord of the Rings the same person as the Glorfindel in the Silmarillion who dies fighting a Balrog? How come?
a: No, they're different people. The Silmarillion one dies well before LOTR, so the answer is hardly a mystery. Apparently it's stated plainly somewhere in the text. Maybe read the books again instead of asking the net.

subject: Particolored Unicorn (review)
q: Is Jon DeCles, author of The Particolored Unicorn, really Diana Paxson?
a: No. Someone who met both Diana Paxson and the author at the last MythCon says they are different persons. Check before you post guesses.

subject: Piers Anthony
q: Is Piers Anthony the American version of Michael Moorcock? I disagree, since I think Moorcock is a lot better, but I'd like to hear opinions.
a: Only in quantity of books, and that's about it. Moorcock beats him on quality any day, has serious artistic intent, edited an SF magazine and helped drive the British "Next Wave". Anthony just inflates a few neat ideas into five-book sets. Sigh.

subject: The Fall of Hyperion
q: Is _The Fall of Hyperion_ out in paperback yet, or when is it due out?
a: It's been out for months as an oversized trade paperback. No pocket paperback yet, so quit asking and go buy the trade one.

subject: Mithril?
q: Mithril silver in Lord of the Rings turns blades. Wouldn't happen to be depleted uranium, would it?
a: No. Mithril is a fantasy metal, and Tolkien was a philologist, not a metallurgist. It's described as light, so uranium is out. Gamers argue aluminum, but that's too soft; titanium is the best match on strength and lightness. Sigh, people love this game.

subject: Where Are They Now?
q: Robby the Robot from Forbidden Planet turned up in the video box for Phantom Empire. What else has this venerable robot been in?
a: At least one Twilight Zone episode, plus a Mork and Mindy episode, believe it or not. He also showed up in Gremlins at a toy convention, in a kids' film, and in Earth Girls Are Easy during a dream sequence. Sigh, the poor tin can works cheap.

subject: Dickson's Childe Cycle Question
q: Wasn't Dickson's "Soldier, Ask Not" rereleased as "Dorsai!"?
a: No. Sigh. "Dorsai!" was a redo of "The Genetic General," just as "Necromancer" redid "No Room for Man." The Hugo-winning novelette "Soldier, Ask Not" was padded out with extra material into the middle third of the novel of that name.

subject: Panglos?
q: What or who is "Panglos"? A friend of mine, heavily into SF, used it as a password and said it was something to do with classic SF.
a: It's Pangloss, the optimistic philosopher-teacher in Voltaire's satirical novel Candide, source of "the best of all possible worlds." It's not really SF, though it has fantastic bits like El Dorado. Go read a book, heathen.

subject: Sequels - when can I expect them?
q: When can I expect the paperback sequels, like Magic's Promise, Magic's Price, Prince of the Blood, Sorceress of Darshiva, Phoenix and Waterdeep? I'm getting anxious.
a: Magic's Promise is out already, and Waterdeep too, I believe. Magic's Price is due this summer, as is Prince of the Blood, though that publisher waits a year after hardback. Sorceress of Darshiva is a guess for late summer or fall. Patience, kid.

subject: Highlander II: Release Date???
q: When is Highlander II going to be released? I thought it was supposed to be summer of 1990.
a: A friend with a supposedly accurate source says this winter. Whether it actually happens is another question. Don't hold your breath, Hollywood schedules are fiction.

subject: SF Writer Characters in 'Footfall'
q: Which real SF authors are the characters in Niven and Pournelle's "Footfall" based on? I only spotted Robert and Virginia Anson as Heinlein and his wife.
a: This gets asked once or twice a year. As I remember: Nat Reynolds is Larry Niven, Wade Curtis is Jerry Pournelle, Sherry Atkinson is C. J. Cherryh, Bob Burnham is Robert Forward, and Joe Ransom is Joe Haldeman. Put it in the FAQ already.

subject: Casting the Fionavar Tapestry
q: Who was the actor who played the dwarf lawyer on L.A. Law? What's his name, anyhow?
a: That was David Rappaport, also of Time Bandits fame. Sigh, he committed suicide last year, so you can forget casting him in anything.

subject: The Coat that Eats People (was Re: THE TOMORROW PEOPLE)
q: Who wrote the story about the coat that eats people, which appeared in an Omni collection of semi-SF horror stories?
a: It was Michael Swanwick, the fellow who wrote In The Drift and Vacuum Flowers, and it's a funny story. It was definitely not Philip K. Dick, whatever the guessers claim. Check before you post a guess, people.

subject: Cover illustration fluke?
q: Why are there two copies of The Madness Season with the same text and ISBN but front and back cover illustrations swapped?
a: It's intentional, just a marketing gimmick. The author's first book has the same trick, with the blonde girl in white and the dark-haired guy in black swapped front and back. Publishers also do it with different background colors. Marketing, sigh.

subject: Crowley (was: Re: Five Best Known SciFi Fantasies)
q: Why do people rate Crowley's Little, Big so highly? I kept waiting for something to happen and it never really did.
a: Something is always happening in it: interwoven subplots and lives that tie into the conclusion. You probably wanted a climax with bells, whistles and fireworks. Crowley doesn't write that way; his style is simple and elegant. Not every book is a Lord of the Rings.

subject: Hooked on Yesterdays Ent.
q: After the Enterprise-C went back through the time rift in Yesterday's Enterprise, wouldn't Tasha Yar have disappeared when history went back to normal, so she never made it back to the C's time?
a: No. The Yar from the C and D warship timeline was still alive, so she goes back as that Yar, not the peace-time one. Think Back to the Future. Though time-travel fans will argue it forever.

subject: The Klingon Sign in Data's Room in "Silicon Avatar"
q: Did anyone notice the large sign with Klingon writing next to Data's room door in the episode "Silicon Avatar"? What does it say?
a: It's a joke, as usual. There's a little picture of Sylvester the Cat laughing like mad, and the Klingon reads "You want it WHEN?!?" Sigh, the set dressers have more fun than the viewers.

subject: TV ratings
q: Does anyone have Nielsen TV ratings for Star Trek: TNG this season, and how do they compare to other shows?
a: TNG gets a consistent 9-11% of US TV households. That puts it around 40th-60th compared to primetime, and third among syndicated shows with new episodes, fourth or fifth in reruns. Syndicated and primetime get listed separately, so compare carefully.

subject: Info help
q: How many Star Trek: TNG episodes have aired in the USA, how does it do in the ratings, how does it compare to the original series, and is an end in sight?
a: Number 194 airs this week, counting from 101. It's the number one syndicated drama and number three overall, behind two game shows. Better than the original, especially in stereo. Six seasons looks like the end, about 152 episodes. Sigh.

subject: all these GIFs
q: I decoded and uncompressed the romulan warbird and 1701D GIFs, but my program doesn't recognize them. What am I doing wrong?
a: You're doing nothing wrong. They aren't GIF files at all, they're in PostScript format. Look at the file before you blame your program, sheesh.

subject: Data and Central Computer
q: In 'Booby Trap', the crew fears turning the Enterprise over to the computer, yet Data is a computer third in command. Why the double standard?
a: Because they stopped thinking of Data as a computer. After four years he's a friend, and a computer on two legs is easier to trust than a disembodied voice. Also, he's sentient and the ship's computer isn't. Obvious, really.

subject: The Title of "The Drumhead"
q: In TNG's "The Drumhead" the episode title was spoken in the dialogue, as often happened in TOS. Can anyone remember other TNG episodes where the title was used in the story?
a: Not exactly what you mean, but "Up the Long Ladder" was originally titled "Send in the Clones", and that line shows up near the end of the story. That's all I've got, trivia hound.

subject: What did the Horta get out of it?
q: In the Star Trek episode The Devil in the Dark, what did the Horta get out of the compromise with the colonists?
a: Think harder. The way the Horta find minerals is by eating, which they no doubt want to do anyway. A later novel, My Enemy, My Ally, even has a Horta Starfleet officer who eats through a door to save some Vulcans.

subject: Mr. Sulu
q: Is George Takei a good guest at conventions? I'm going to my first Star Trek convention in Philly.
a: He's one of the best. He loves his fans, speaks well, and chats with every single person in his autograph line, signing until the last one. The line crawls, so bring patience. Also expect fanatical attendees at your first con.

subject: Season 5 Finale - Are the Borg going to return?
q: Is it true the Borg are returning in a three-part episode as the season 5 finale?
a: No, the three-part episode was a hoax. An episode called I, Borg will most likely appear later in the season. Believe every rumor you read and you'll go nuts.

subject: Is there a Klingon dictionary, or: Are those Klingons really saying anything?
q: Is there a Klingon dictionary, and are the Klingons really saying anything on Star Trek: TNG?
a: Yes, The Klingon Dictionary by Marc Okrand, Pocket Books 1985. The Klingon on screen has been checked against it since ST3, so they're speaking real Klingonese. Go to the bookstore and look, it's not hard.

subject: Pollocks on Star Trek
q: Was Polaski the only Polish name used on Star Trek? I seem to remember a Kowalski in engineering somewhere.
a: It's Pulaski, for starters. I don't recall any Kowalski in Star Trek, though that proves nothing. There's a Kowalski in the old series "Voyage To The Bottom Of The Sea", which is where you probably saw the name. And the word is "Pole", by the way.

subject: How to bring Yar back for good!
q: Was there really a Star Trek V marshmallow dispenser, and what was it for?
a: Yes, there was. A marshmallow company offered it for a few bucks plus a couple of UPCs. It was a molded plastic tube with decals, holding only 4 marshmallows. Hardly a great idea.

subject: IDIC
q: What does IDIC stand for?
a: Infinite Diversity in Infinite Combinations. Any Trekkie knows this, and a blank brain is no excuse. Honestly, this comes up every week.

subject: klingon language
q: What is the book on the Klingon language mentioned on the Star Trek anniversary show, and who wrote it?
a: It's called The Klingon Dictionary, by Mark Okrand. This comes up every week. Go find a bookstore.

subject: Strength of Characters
q: What is the relative strength of Data versus a Borg, a Klingon, a Vulcan and a man?
a: Data is much stronger than Worf ("Datalore") and presumably than humans. Klingons and humans aren't MUCH different, and the Borg seem much stronger than humans. Beyond that there's no evidence on screen, so quit guessing.

subject: What was said?
q: What was the line Kirk used in the third Star Trek movie as he kicked the Klingon over the cliff? It was something like "I grow tired of you."
a: It's "I have had enough of you." Followed by a kick, of course. Another respondent thought it was "I am getting tired of you," but nobody could check the tape. Honestly, go rent it yourself.

subject: Turbolifts
q: When did the Star Trek turbolift stop being an elevator and become a turbolift?
a: Probably when it learned to move horizontally as well as vertically, so it wasn't just about elevation anymore.
