Also, Starfleet is a naval outfit, and navies insist on different names for everything: overhead, bulkhead, lines. McCoy calling it an elevator is just a grumpy old man twitting people.

subject: Battlebridge
q: Where on the Stardrive section of the Enterprise is the battlebridge located?
a: Separate the saucer first, genius. The battle bridge sits on top of the goose neck of the stardrive section, in the very center, right where it joins the saucer. It stays hidden when the ship is in one piece.

subject: WHO was David Rappaport?
q: Who was David Rappaport, and what roles was he in?
a: He was the leader of the Time Bandits, his best known role. He also played an opponent of a lawyer on LA Law, and had a short-lived CBS series called The Wizard. Surely you can look this up yourself.

subject: TNG Episode numbers
q: Why do the TNG episode numbers differ by one? Is the 90-minute Encounter at Farpoint episode one, or are the two 45-minute halves one and two?
a: The 90-minute version was production number 721. Split in half it became 101 and 102, but 103 aired as the second episode shown. So by order first shown, Allegiance is the 65th, not the 66th. Sigh, it's bookkeeping.

subject: Why a JunkYard???
q: Why would Starfleet operate a junkyard? Wouldn't they just melt old ships down into materials for new ones instead of keeping the junk floating?
a: Same reasons we have junkyards today. It's a place to strip parts as needed, or a mothball fleet, and you wouldn't melt ships down if you aren't building new ones. Also, it wasn't a Starfleet yard anyway. Sigh, pay attention to the snotty proprietor.

subject: Who knows anything about "Leader of the Pack" ?
q: Our amateur musical theatre company is considering the musical Leader of the Pack, about the life of Ellie Greenwich. Is it a good show, and what is it like?
a: It's a lot of fun, with lots of great songs. It's a nostalgia trip, and the story isn't too corny. It was directed and choreographed by Michael Peters. Ellie Greenwich wrote pop songs in the Brill Building. Go see it before asking the net.

subject: Battlestar Galactica: Rules to Pyramid?
q: Does anyone know the rules to the Pyramid card game from Battlestar Galactica, and whether a special deck is needed or where to buy one?
a: If I recall correctly, New Eye Studio sells a pyramid deck and rules for around six bucks. They advertise in Starlog. I don't remember the address, so go look.

subject: BA I - "Mad Gerald"
q: In the first Black Adder series, episode 6 "The Black Seal", was Mad Gerald, credited as "Himself", played by Rik Mayall?
a: Yes, it's Rik Mayall. He was moving from the Comic Strip crowd and apparently wanted to save his stardom for later, so don't ask me why. Gerald then became Lord Flasheart in BAII and Flash in BAGF. Pay attention.

subject: Question: Name of this show??
q: What was that TV series about an American cop named Dempsey sent to the UK to work with a policewoman named Makepeace?
a: It's "Dempsey and Makepeace." Sigh, you had both names right and still needed the net to tell you the title.

subject: Trumpton
q: What were the names of the firemen in Trumpton and Camberwick Green?
a: Pugh, Pugh, Barney McGrew, Cuthbert, Dibble and Grubb. Cuthbert always went up in the bucket, and Grubb was the driver, I think. The captain was Captain Flack. Can't vouch for the spellings.

subject: Peter Jones(?) in Hitchhiker's GTTG
q: Who or what did Peter Jones play in the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy series?
a: He played The Book, the voice of the Hitch-Hiker's Guide itself. I think he also did the overall narration for the series. Any fan knows that.

subject: Choosing Op-Amps
q: Are there better op-amps these days than the LM540 and MC1556 for a hi-fi preamp with RIAA phono, tone control and line gain stages?
a: Yes, your ten-year-old design book is stale. The Signetics NE5534A is the low-noise pick, with 13V/uS slew rate and low cost. The PMI OP27 has less noise but a slew rate of only 0.5V/uS. The LM318 gives 70V/uS if speed matters more than noise.

subject: Remote Control <-> Computer Interface
q: Does anyone know of an IBM PC compatible card that receives and transmits IR remote control commands, learns codes from my current remotes, and signals a program when commands arrive?
a: I can't name a card, but Wozniak's CORE universal remote is reportedly an option. Crutchfield advertised it, and as I recall it had an RS232 interface for hooking up to a computer. Nobody here has posted real details, naturally.

subject: Adcom?
q: How good is Adcom power amp really, such as the GFA-535, for a bass lover? I've heard its capacitance and current reserves are weak.
a: If you're a real bass lover, get a servo powered subwoofer. A powered sub crossed over around 80 Hz means your amp doesn't waste power driving a huge woofer cone. Use two for stereo bass. Throwing watts at it with a small amp is the wrong approach.

subject: Speaker Stand Advice Needed Please
q: I built some small "midi" monitor speakers and need stands about 30 to 32 inches high. Are Target stands good quality and reasonably priced, and are there other brands to consider?
a: Target stands are generally considered acceptable. Another trick is to find a commercial speaker of similar size and see which stands its maker recommends. That's how I ended up with Mission-Cyrus stands. Not hard to figure out.

subject: Punch 45 --> Punch 10"
q: I have a Rockford Punch 45 amp bridged mono driving two 8 ohm 10 inch woofers in parallel, and I'm adding a second Punch 45. Is it worth swapping the 8 ohm speakers for 4 ohm ones to get about 70 watts each rather than 45?
a: Yes. Currently each 10 inch gets about 35 watts. With a second Punch 45 and 4 ohm speakers you double that to 70 watts into each one, so it's worth unloading the 8s. Basic Ohm's law, people.

subject: Req. for Microphone info
q: I have an older Neumann microphone, a U64 with a solid state phantom source, and someone wants to borrow it. Is it valuable enough that I need to worry about it?
a: Yes, worry about it. Even a cheap Neumann is like a cheap Rolls Royce. Used ones rarely go for under about $250, and new ones list from $600 to $4000. Treat it carefully. They're repairable and never really retire, so handle it with care.

subject: Magnepan Speakers
q: I liked the Magnepan MG 1.5/QR speakers but the lack of bass troubled me. Would proper placement in a room add more bass?
a: Placement isn't what the replies say. The smaller Maggies are a bit lacking in bass, and you'll get slightly deeper bass after they're broken in. If you want one-note boom bass, buy something else. Live with it.

subject: Rotel amps
q: What do people think of Rotel amps? I'm in Australia where all imported hi-fi gear is taxed about equally, and they seemed good value in listening tests.
a: The British magazines rate them well: of six Rotels HiFi Choice reviewed, three got Best Buy and three Recommended. Good, solid midrange stuff, strongest in the middle of the line, though newer designs are catching up. Hardly junk, so stop fretting.

subject: Dem DAT's
q: What exactly is the copying inhibited stuff everyone is talking about with DATs, and when will they be sold in the US?
a: It's the Serial Copy Management System, which the RIAA wants in all consumer DATs. You can copy a CD or prerecorded tape, but the copy can't be copied again. Pro decks supposedly skip it. Rumor says XLR connectors mark a pro deck. Ugh.

subject: Dolby HX Pro - explanation please.
q: What is Dolby HX Pro, and does it replace or work with Dolby B and C?
a: It varies record bias and equalization dynamically to suit the signal, since higher bias lowers midband distortion but cuts highs. It's meant to be used along with normal B or C noise reduction, not instead of it. Read up on bias, kid.

subject: Concert hall. Power requirements
q: What speaker power in watts and dB output is typical for a big hall like Carnegie Hall, and where should the speakers go? How do PA systems for halls differ from home systems?
a: Too much for a post. Go read "Sound Reinforcement for the Amateur" by Glen Ballou, in the March '84 issue of Audio. It covers all of that and more. Do your homework.

subject: Dynaudio in San Francisco?
q: Where can someone visiting the San Francisco Bay area buy Dynaudio drivers?
a: Try A & S Speakers, alias Just Speakers, on 23rd Street in San Francisco. They carry Dynaudio drivers and kits. Failing that, Madisound at (608) 831-3433 definitely has them, shipped from Wisconsin. Dynaudio's expensive anyway, deal with it.

subject: Ported Speaker Designs
q: Why do ported speakers all seem to have a bass bump around 70-100 Hz and nothing below 45-50 Hz? Can a ported enclosure be designed without that?
a: Sure it can. Mid-fi makers fake bass with a midbass emphasis, and that's not just vented designs. Consumers lap up the warm sound instead of real 20-40 Hz bass. Clean bass below 45-50 Hz is hard in a small box, but not impossible. Just not cheap.

subject: Buying a used "new" car
q: A dealer has a used 1991 VW Jetta GL with about 16,000 miles, asking $9,995 against a $13,300 list. What is a fair price to pay?
a: Figure VW rebates put a new one near $10,800, then knock off about ten cents a mile and some for no new-car smell. That's roughly $8,700 at most. I'd offer $8k and pay no dealer prep nonsense. Never get attached to a car.

subject: Fog Lights
q: Are my mother's BMW's front spoiler lights really fog lights, or just driving lights that merely reflect off fog and make driving more dangerous? They aren't yellow.
a: Colour isn't the point, and even that's disputed. Driving lights are a narrow long-range beam that works best mounted high. Fog lights are like a low beam, throwing plenty of light under the fog and little into it. Low mounting is correct for fog lights.

subject: Serengeti Driver's Glasses - Question
q: Does anybody know a mail order outlet that sells Serengeti Driver's glasses at decent prices? My local mall kiosk wants $85.
a: No mail order name, but try a warehouse chain like Price Club in California. They've carried the drivers on and off for $39.95, in a few styles. Stop paying mall-kiosk prices, for crying out loud.

subject: Breaking In New Engines / General Engine Care
q: How do I break in the engine of a new car? Friends say to rev to redline in each gear, or to take it easy. Is revving high bad, and will changing the oil more often prevent damage?
a: Take it easy. Break-in lets the parts wear in compatibly, and high revs raise the forces before that happens. Limit RPM at first, raising the limit every couple hundred miles until you reach redline. Oil changes can't hurt but won't prevent that damage. Yes, it's frustrating.

subject: Tire question, never been asked?
q: I have whitewall tires on my car with the whitewalls turned in, because I figured the walls of whitewall tires are stronger than non-whitewalls. True or false? Should I keep buying whitewalls?
a: False, as far as anyone can tell. Some whitewalls may have stiffer sidewalls than some blackwalls, but you can't make a general rule out of it. Buy tires on their specs, not on the colour of the stripe.

subject: door mounted seatbelts (was Re: GM Seatbelts)
q: I heard on a TV news show that a door-mounted seatbelt isn't a safe design because the door might open in an accident. Any thoughts?
a: Think about it: the problem is the door latch, not the seatbelt. In an accident the door should stay SHUT. Mercedes Benz put a lot of effort into their latches and they're the best. Obvious, really.

subject: -= $2000 Fine For Running A Header =-
q: I live in California and heard you can be fined $2000 for having a header on your car. Is that true? I'm about to buy one.
a: Why ask a newsgroup? Call the California DMV. They're the ones who'd know, and a rumor from some guy isn't evidence. Sigh.

subject: Help with a speeding ticket requested
q: I was cited for 74 in a 55 and admit it. Will this ticket raise my insurance rates, and how can I keep it off my record without hiring an expensive lawyer?
a: Just pay the fine. You admit you were speeding, and getting out of it means perjury or hoping the cop doesn't show up. Paying is cheaper than a lawyer. My own insurance never rose. Grow up.

subject: port and polish
q: I've heard the terms porting and polishing used for improving engine performance. What do they mean and how does it work?
a: It means reworking the intake and exhaust ports in the cylinder head to maximize gas flow: smoothing, enlarging or reshaping them. Doing it right takes a flow bench, a dyno and a pile of ruined heads, which is why shops charge hundreds of dollars. Not magic.

subject: Repaint and Pealing
q: If I get my car repainted without having the windows and molding removed, will the new paint peel around the windshield after a couple of years even if I keep it clean and polished?
a: Quite possibly, yes. Sanding around the trim is hard, so the paint gets a poor surface to stick to, and masking leaves obvious lines. Chipping there is the first sign of a cheap repaint. Pay for the windows to come out, grumble all you like.

subject: Jeep Cherokee, how much ??
q: If I spend $3000 to $3500 on a Jeep Cherokee 4.0 liter in good condition, what year can I expect to find?
a: Dream on. You won't find a 4.0L Cherokee at that price. The 4.0 straight six only came back a few years ago. The older 3.9L V6 is far less reliable but might fit your checkbook. Sigh.

subject: Traffic Law lookup
q: If I think a traffic ticket was issued wrongfully, where do I look up the law? Would a normal library have the traffic lawbooks, or do I need a law library?
a: Call a library and ask for the Vehicle Code for your state. Only the larger ones carry it. DMV offices and police stations keep copies too, and in California the DMV sells it for $3. Sigh, a phone call settles this.

subject: Porsche 944
q: Is a new '89 Porsche 944 Turbo at a big discount a good deal, given it was the last year of the Turbo and the dealers say it will hold its resale value?
a: Be skeptical. The Turbo was dropped from the US because Porsche decided the 944S2 suited American driving better, and it doesn't hold its value nearly as well as a 911. Being discontinued could even hurt resale. Dealers pushing you to double your budget? Be very suspicious.

subject: * Toyota Recall *
q: Toyota recalled the 1982 Celica because the seatbelts wouldn't retract when the door opened. Can I still get that fix now, and two dealers say they never heard of the recall?
a: Dealers never know anything. Call the federal Auto Safety Hotline at (800)424-9393 and ask about your year, make and model. If a recall applies you get a printout. Take it and the car to a Toyota dealer, who must fix it or prove it was done.

subject: Here is one for those Chevy fans
q: Was a 1919 Chevrolet ever made, how many still exist, and what is a fully restored one worth?
a: Yes, Chevrolets were made in 1919. No idea how many survive; ask an antique Chevy club. For prices, check Hemmings Motor News or an old car price guide. One 1919 FB sedan was listed at $13,000. Check the wood frame; it was used until 1936.

subject: Top speed question
q: What do they mean by top speed of a car? The most it can do without harming the engine, or the fastest it can go even if the engine blows up after two seconds?
a: Top speed is the absolute fastest the car can go. Thanks to the gearbox, you needn't worry about the engine blowing up, since redline is chosen so cars can run near it for long periods. Stock cars usually hit top speed in 4th or 5th without exceeding redline.

subject: New Celica model
q: Will there be a new Celica model in 92?
a: Doubtful. Haven't heard anything, and the current Celica is only a couple of years old. The convertible is in its first year with the new skin. Give it a rest.

subject: Disadvantages of the semi-auto gearbox
q: Doesn't a semi-automatic gearbox in F1 hurt the driver, since he has to go through every gear to downshift instead of dropping straight to 2nd for a chicane? Does the McLaren also shift itself at the rev limit?
a: Most likely it's no disadvantage at all. You do your downshifts in the braking zone before turn-in, with the clutch in, and there's plenty of time to click through three or four gears with your fingertips. You don't brake with the engine, so stop worrying.

subject: Help needed with Centerforce clutch!
q: I installed a Centerforce II clutch in my '87 Starion and the clutch only disengages with the pedal at the floor. I wrecked a master cylinder seal from pushing the piston so far in. What's wrong and how do I fix it?
a: Sounds like the wrong throwout bearing. They come in different lengths, and a too-short one gives exactly this. Same thing happened on a Trans Am and an El Camino, and a longer bearing fixed both. Also check it's installed right, and bleed the system. Basic stuff.

subject: Can I add some pep to my Jetta GLI without being a stinker?
q: Can I swap a 16 valve head onto my 8 valve Jetta GLI engine to get more power, or add a cam and exhaust, without being illegal in California?
a: Not a head swap. You'd need a whole new long-block, plus the knock-sensing ignition, engine computer, clutch and flywheel. Better to get a 2.0 liter 8V block, add a cam and a legal exhaust (everything but the catalytic converter) and enjoy 130-plus hp. Sigh, no free lunch.

subject: HELP! Can I convert an AUDI 5000 to VW 4cyl.
q: Can I swap a VW 1.6 four-cylinder into my 1980 Audi 5000 with a dead 5-cylinder, bolted to the 5-speed with hydraulic clutch?
a: Not without major modifications. The Audi five uses different transaxles, and engine mounts, ignition, wiring, intake, exhaust, fuel injection and cooling would all change. No US Audi 5000 had a four. Find a used engine or just repair it.

subject: Following up on a rumour
q: Is it true that some VWs in Germany have a G-Lader supercharger on a 16V engine making 210 hp, or is that a myth?
a: Real, not myth. Some 60 or so GTi syncros, four-wheel drive, got that engine and were sold in Switzerland. Very rare. VW is putting its effort into the V6 for powerful models rather than the G Lader, which makes sense.

subject: More on hesitation, please....
q: My '87 GTI 16v has a rough idle on start-up and hesitates when accelerating at low RPM. What are the most common causes?
a: One fix was carbon buildup on the intake valves, which the dealer's injector cleaner cured after two or three treatments. It's heavy duty and expensive stuff. Go figure. Quit swapping parts at random.

subject: Stop light switch on Golf
q: Where is the brake light switch on an '85 VW Golf? My brake lights quit, and the fuse and bulbs are fine.
a: It's on the master cylinder, which sticks out of the firewall. There are two 3-prong switches, each under a black rubber boot. Peel one back carefully, since a wire has probably come loose. Reconnect it and tape it up, and you're in business.

subject: ATA in FAR/AIM
q: Everyone knows you should call the tower before entering an airport traffic area, but where does the FAR/AIM actually say this?
a: FAR 91.129, sections (b) and (c): two-way radio contact is required in the airport traffic area at a towered airport. The old numbering was FAR 91.87, and the AIM's ATA definition says it too. Learn to read the index.

subject: FAA-approved Check Pilot?
q: FAR 61.57 lists an FAA-approved check pilot among those who can give an Instrument Competency Check. What is an FAA-approved check pilot?
a: Air carriers under part 121 and air taxi operators under part 135 have designated check airmen, approved by the FAA, who evaluate other pilots on flights. If you don't work for one of those outfits, that option isn't available to you. Read the regs.

subject: P-51
q: How common are constant-rpm engines in aviation, and what are the advantages and disadvantages?
a: It's constant-speed propellers, not engines. Nearly every aircraft except the lowest-performance ones has one. Different airspeeds need different pitch, so a fixed prop is a compromise that only works when cruise and climb speeds are close.

subject: Passengers in clouds
q: Now that I'm flying in clouds, how do my passengers react? Do they get claustrophobic, disoriented or airsick, and how do I relieve their fears?
a: Passengers only spook if you're spooked or the turbulence is bad. Brief them on route and weather beforehand, point out instruments, and keep it light. Mine just get bored and read. It's no big deal unless you hit sparks, bumps or ice.

subject: soaring records
q: What are the soaring records for undeclared flights: straight-line distance, out-and-back, and duration aloft?
a: Straight distance is, I believe, still Hans Werner Grosse's 900-odd miles to Spain in an ASW-12. Goal-and-return was about 1008 miles, Lock Haven to Knoxville and back, in ridge lift. Duration records aren't kept anymore because pilots nodded off past 24 hours. Predictable.

subject: Localizer Delta
q: What does 'localizer delta' mean on the Gillespie Field ATIS in San Diego?
a: Some approaches, typically circle-to-land only ones, are named by a letter after the navaid instead of a runway number. So LOC-D is just that approach. Look in the book of Instrument Approach Procedures for details. It's cheap. Read it.

subject: That first solo landing...
q: Why is the first solo landing usually the best a pilot ever makes?
a: Two theories: you'll never concentrate so hard on a landing again, and the euphoria of first solo floods you with endorphins so it feels like your best. Intense moments make for good landings too. Spare me the romance.

subject: Cassette player affects instruments?
q: Will playing a cassette or CD on a portable stereo in the cockpit interfere with my instruments or radios, such as ADF, VOR and comm?
a: A cassette is most unlikely to cause trouble. A CD player is another story, with digital edges and harmonics that can get into radios. Check by holding it near the panel or antenna, or copy to tape. Also watch the speaker magnets near the compass, obviously.

subject: dial indicators ??
q: Are dial indicators useful for truing bicycle wheels? Where do I buy them, how much do they cost, and how accurate do they need to be?
a: Useful, not essential. Get one at a machine tool or automotive tool supplier for roughly $10 to $50. A 0-20mm range with 0.01mm or 0.001 inch resolution is plenty. Truing to about 0.1mm is already true, so don't obsess, perfectionist.

subject: Road bikes on track
q: Are road bikes with gears usable on the track for pursuit or kilo, and is it true the new records for time trials in New Mexico were set on fixed gears?
a: Yes, the senior men's 40 km record was broken on a fixed gear, reportedly a 53x13. The course suits it if you start early before the wind picks up and can spin the gear down the slight downhill finish. Geared bikes lagged.

subject: Are there any natural sources of glucose polymers?
q: Are there natural sources of glucose polymers? Bicycling magazine touts them over single glucose molecules.
a: Starch is a glucose polymer: potatoes, bread, corn meal. The lo-tech name for the hyped stuff is maltodextrin, made by partially digesting corn starch, and it's cheap from wholesalers or home-brew suppliers. Skip the designer prices; it's marketing hype.

subject: Replacing HyperGlide Question
q: Can I replace my Shimano HyperGlide chain with a Sedis ATB chain and reuse the pin? Do I need a special tool, or can I get the old chain off without one?
a: Yes, the Sedis works and several people have done it. And you don't need a special tool, an ordinary chain tool does the job. I've reused the pin four or five times and it never fell apart. Stop fretting over marketing.

subject: basic fix-it book needed
q: Can someone recommend a good basic book on fixing and maintaining 10 speed bicycles? I've never even changed a tire.
a: Try Anybody's Bike Book, Richard's Bicycle Book, or Compton's Complete Book of Bicycle Repair. The first two get you started and go deep enough that you can eventually fix anything short of welding. If you can handle a screwdriver and wrench, you'll manage.

subject: Buying bicycles at Poice Auctions
q: Does anyone have experience buying bicycles at police auctions in the San Mateo and Santa Clara counties area? What kinds of bikes and prices?
a: I went to one in Santa Clara. Mostly junk. Dealers were there buying up lots of stuff, and they know enough not to let any steal slip by. Don't expect a bargain.

subject: Advise on purchase
q: I commute 8 to 10 miles a day over hills, wind and gravel, and I'm small at 5'5" and 115 lbs. What kind of bike should I buy to replace my department store mountain bike?
a: Try a hybrid like last year's Specialized Rock Combo. Drop bars, bar-end shifters that thumb-shifter fans will like, and 26 inch wheels that take skinny tires or knobbies. It got bad press, but it's a decent bike. Skip this year's models.

subject: Chainwheel question
q: I have 52 and 42 tooth chainwheels and am thinking of replacing the 42 with a 28 for hill climbing. What are the pros and cons, and will I need a new front derailleur?
a: A 28 is awfully extreme and loses a lot of versatility. A 39 or so makes a bigger difference than you'd think. Better to put a freewheel with larger sprockets on the back. Shifting is easier and it's cheaper, since chainwheels cost plenty.

subject: Chondromalacia info request
q: I have pain behind both kneecaps while riding after about half an hour. How is chondromalacia of the patella treated?
a: One poster got rid of it in two days with sports-medicine advice. Take lots of aspirin or ibuprofen to cut the swelling behind the patella, and keep the knee from flexing under load. Biking is out, sorry. Swelling feeds friction, which feeds more swelling.

subject: Wheelbuilding
q: I keep breaking spokes on my touring bike's rear wheel and want to rebuild it. Can anyone recommend a good book on wheelbuilding?
a: Read Jobst Brandt's book, The Bicycle Wheel. It covers building a durable wheel and then some. Sigh, go read it before breaking more spokes.

subject: What to do in an accident?
q: I ride a bike in the city and read that juries often side with the motorist after an accident. What can I do to improve my chances, and is there any bicycle organization that helps?
a: Try the League of American Wheelmen, a lobbying outfit for cyclists; the address is in the FAQ, which you evidently didn't read. Many local bicycle groups also give members legal counsel after an accident, such as Transportation Alternatives in New York and the Boston Area Bicycle Coalition.

subject: What were they doing?
q: I saw four cyclists in team jerseys riding two by two very close behind a small car with its hatchback open and flashers on, at about 20 mph. What were they doing?
a: Motorpacing. You draft behind a vehicle at constant high speed to work on sheer speed, good prep for criteriums and some flat road races. Twenty mph is slow for it, though.

subject: Bent chain ring
q: I slightly bent the 28 tooth chain ring on my mountain bike and spares are hard to find. Can the ring be straightened?
a: Depends where it's bent. For bent teeth, set an adjustable wrench as close to the metal thickness as possible, put the chainwheel in a bench vise, and GENTLY bend the tooth back in line. Don't bend it back and forth, genius.

subject: Avocet 40 ?
q: I was about to buy the Avocet 30 when I heard a model 40 was coming. When is it out, what does it cost, and what features does it add?
a: Read Bicycling Magazine, it's not useless. It's called the Cyclometer 40: lightest full-function computer, average speed, the PaceArrow display, nine colors. Think of a smaller Avocet 50 minus altimeter and cadence option. It shows current speed alongside max or average. Nobody gave a price.

subject: SPECIALIZED ALLEZ - FRONT-END SHIMMY
q: My 1990 Specialized Allez carbon bike gets bad front-end shimmy over 15 mph when riding no-hands. Should a bike do that? Is it frame alignment?
a: Try a different tire first, since out-of-round tires are guilty more often than you'd think, and it's cheap. Then fiddle with weight on the front wheel and fork, then have the frame checked. A carbon frame with an aluminum fork also just feels twitchy. Don't panic.

subject: Tire & Rim Questions
q: My Michelin Hi-Lite Comp 700x23 tires blow off my Durex Ambrosio rims near 110 psi and they puncture a lot. Are these rims suitable, and what's going on?
a: Michelins want hook rims, and if yours are non-hook, they'll keep blowing off. Also, pinch the tube up into the tire cavity when mounting so it doesn't sit under the bead. Punctures usually mean sloppy rim taping over the spoke holes. Basics, people.

subject: Time pedals are sticky!
q: My Time pedal's left shoe doesn't float like the right one and my left foot gets sore. Should I swap cleats between the shoes?
a: Don't do that. The cleats are directional, and swapped ones may not release at all. Check for burrs on the cleat and sand them down. Shoes also wear in after a couple of weeks, which eases clicking and rotation. Learned that the hard way.

subject: bent chainring
q: My mountain bike chainring is bent like a potato chip and the chain drags on the front derailleur cage. What should I do?
a: Replace the chainring. Take it off and lay it on a flat surface to check it's really bent. If it's not, suspect the spider, or even a slightly bent bottom bracket spindle. Torque the chainring bolts evenly. Not hard if you're handy; otherwise pay the shop.

subject: Schedule for 1990 RAAM?
q: What's the route and schedule of this year's 1990 Ride Across America?
a: It leaves Irvine, California on August 6 and should finish in Savannah, Georgia around August 13 or 14, depending on competitors. It's 2920 miles, via I-10 to Arizona, Colorado, Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and Georgia. It skips New Mexico.

subject: roller bearing replacement
q: When I overhaul a headset with roller bearings, do I need to replace the bearings if they look okay? The replacements cost $16.
a: Not necessarily. Clean everything and inspect under a bright light for pitting and flaking. Rub the old grease on a white rag; tiny shiny metal flakes mean lost material and new rollers. Headsets barely turn, so they don't wear like other bearings. Don't waste $16 needlessly.

subject: Cyclometer for Cannondale Pepperoni Forks...
q: Where can I get a cyclometer for my mountain bike with Cannondale's huge pepperoni forks? Pickups don't have a clamp large enough for the chain-stay or fork, and I'd prefer wireless.
a: Don't buy anything special. Take a Cateye Micro pickup and drop the threaded insert from its strap, then run a tie wrap through both strap holes around the fork blade. If it slides, a dab of silicone adhesive holds it. Sigh, not hard.

subject: Flexstem
q: Will a 0.2 mm difference between a 22.2 mm Flexstem post and my 22 mm post cause a problem? Also, do I need the $8.95 Spring Washer Kit?
a: Your stem should measure 22.2mm unless you have an oversized steerer, which would be nearer 25.4mm. The washers are spongey stuff that sets the damping. Too soft and you soak up your climbing effort. Measure properly.

subject: Help w/bird identity: KS
q: I saw a slim, cardinal-shaped bird in Kansas, yellow underneath with dark wings, black on the face but not under the chin, and a clear four-note whistle. It isn't in my Audubon guide. What is it?
a: Sounds like a first-year male orchard oriole. Check the Robbins Golden guide, around page 302. They're all over the place right now, and your description fits it right on the beak. Next time look in a guide that has it.

subject: bird book - Australia
q: I'm going to Queensland, Australia this winter. What's the best bird book for Australia?
a: Slater, Slater and Slater, "The Slater Field Guide to Australian Birds", 1986. All 756 species described, maps and text facing colour plates, and it fits a pocket. Simpson's book has bigger pictures but won't fit your back pocket. Pick one and go.

subject: Crossbill movements
q: There was a big influx of Crossbills in Holland, Denmark, the UK and the USA this year. Are Crossbill movements a global phenomenon? Surely not all spruce forests had a bad year.
a: Can't say it's global, but spruce are especially vulnerable to acid rain or some common air pollution. They've been sickening and dying in upstate NY, New England and Canada, and all recent years have been bad. Spruce and sugar maples go first.

subject: Vagrants
q: Would someone post the rare bird hotline numbers? I'm especially interested in the San Francisco area one, and who runs these hotlines?
a: Northern California Rare Bird Alert, run by Golden Gate Audubon and covering the whole Bay area. Weekly summary is 415 528 0288, updated Tuesdays; daily updates are 415 524 5592. Write them down this time.

subject: Spinning Dog Hair Try #2
q: Does dog hair make a good yarn? Can I spin and knit my collie's shed undercoat, and how much hair do I need for a sweater?
a: Collie undercoat spins very easily, easier than angora, and makes warm, soft yarn. The catch is it smells like a wet dog when wet, so stay out of the rain. Estimate by weight: a hat is 2-4 ounces. Learn on wool first, and watch for moths.

subject: Need Recipe for honey-based Mead
q: Does anyone have a tested recipe for honey-based mead? A friend wants to sell it as a marketable beverage at a medieval fair.
a: Forget the recipe, mead is alcohol, and selling it takes a very expensive license. Making it for yourself or giving it away is no problem. I wouldn't call homebrew a marketable beverage anyway.

subject: hbd died?
q: Has the HomeBrew Digest stopped? I haven't received any since #614.
a: The digest is alive and well, since #619 showed up already. You probably have a path problem and the bounces are going to the editor. Resubscribe via the request address, homebrew-request%hpfcmi@hplabs.hp.com. Check your own mail first, geez.

subject: Irish Whiskey
q: I want to buy my boyfriend a bottle of Irish whiskey for Saint Patrick's Day, $20 or less, and we like single malt Scotch. I'm in southern California. What do you suggest?
a: Stick with the two blends you can find anywhere and that won't kill you: Bushmill's and Jameson's. Black Bush, the longer-aged Bushmill, is nicer if you can find it. Tullamore Dew is another favorite. Skip Paddy's, for pity's sake.

subject: What is "moderation"
q: Wine books say it's healthy in moderation, but none say how much is moderate. Is there any research on what counts as a moderate or safe amount to drink?
a: Most medical studies set moderation at about two six-ounce glasses of wine a day, roughly half a bottle. Food in your stomach slows absorption, and wine absorbs slower than beer or spirits. Australian figures are lower: 1-2 glasses for women, 3-4 for men. Pick your poison.

subject: Influencing those you love to eat less meat
q: How do I influence my husband and mother to eat less meat without it becoming a power struggle? They keep serving or ordering meat even though I'm trying to cut it out.
a: You won't browbeat anyone; they just get stubborn. Her house, her cooking, so just don't eat it. Keep cooking meatless meals for your husband, and lead by example. Or let them watch the Diet for a New America video, no force. Sigh, people learn from example, not lectures.

subject: Curry Leaf
q: Is the curry leaf the same as Daun Massala in Indonesia and Malaysia? The dried leaf I can get in Hawaii is almost flavorless.
a: Real curry leaves are close to impossible to get in the US, and dried ones are nearly useless since they need to be fresh. Used like bay leaves for subtle flavor. The spice mix called curry has little to do with curry leaves. The reply never says whether it's the same as Daun Massala.

subject: Vegetarian eating on Airlines
q: My vegetarian meal request for an airline flight got lost and they offered kosher instead. How can I make sure I get the meal I ordered?
a: Call the airline to confirm the flight, then confirm your meal and seat so it's actually in their computer. Ask again at check-in and boarding if you're thorough. Even then they botch it sometimes, so bring your own food. Airlines, sigh.

subject: Blue Corn
q: What is blue corn? I saw ads for blue corn chips and blue popcorn. Is it just food coloring, or is there something special about it?
a: It's corn that grows naturally blue, so no food coloring. It's a grain originally cultivated by the Aztecs. The chips have a more subtle corn flavour than the yellow ones. Nutrition, no idea, so don't ask me.

subject: Count Frequencies for 4 Deck BJ
q: Does anyone have count frequencies for the 4 deck blackjack game, like Thorpe has for one deck?
a: From Fundamentals of Blackjack, true count frequencies for four decks: 0 to 0.5 is 0.151, 0.5 to 1.5 is 0.137, 1.5 to 2.5 is 0.086, 2.5 to 3.5 is 0.051, falling to 0.007 at 6.5 to 7.5. Look it up yourself next time.

subject: Some craps observations and questions
q: In craps, should I have my odds bets on or off during a come out roll? Is there a rule of thumb?
a: Leave them working. It's still the best bet on the table, and turning them off is just a ploy the casinos use to pad their edge a bit. Not rocket science.

subject: BJ: Card Counting In AC
q: Is it true that blackjack in Atlantic City is too tough to beat by counting, and that it's illegal for the casinos to throw out counters or even shuffle up on them?
a: With shoes, your typical maximum edge with a 1-8 spread is about 0.5%, and high counts are rarer than in single deck, so AC is poor. The shuffle-up thing is too good to be true: casinos can and do shuffle up, and a mandatory penetration rule was only ever short-lived. Wishful thinking.

subject: VW BJ question
q: What is the disadvantage of playing single-deck blackjack at Vegas World, where they deal down to the last card? It looks like a big edge for counters.
a: They probably pay only even money for blackjack, which hands the house about a 2.5% edge. Vegas World is not known for giving the player a fighting chance. Sigh, the deep dealing is bait, so stay away.

subject: Newbie question (gambler)
q: In Cosmic Encounter, if the Gambler bluffs a 5 card as a 15, the other player has nothing to lose by calling the bluff. Isn't that broken?
a: Read the Gambler power again. It also costs you tokens outside the challenge, so calling the bluff can cost eight tokens, not just the four. Nothing to lose indeed. Read the rules before inventing house rules.

subject: Looking for chess-related software
q: Is there an X11 interface to a chess program, ideally one supporting two human players?
a: There are two: xchess and xboard. xchess has been around ages, is in the contrib directory of the X11 release, and supports two players and uses gnuchess against the computer. xboard is new, posted in comp.sources.x, and probably has no two-player mode.

subject: Best Chess Program?
q: What is the best chess program? Is it Deep Thought?
a: Yes, Deep Thought won the 1989 world computer chess championship in Edmonton and the recent ACM computer chess championships. Worse for the competition, it's still getting faster.

subject: education
q: What level of education have Karpov and Kasparov achieved?
a: Both are college graduates. Kasparov has an undergraduate-level degree in languages, and Karpov has a Masters or Doctorate in economics, as I recall. His professors were disappointed he picked chess. Both were exceptional students. Not exactly dropouts, so spare me the speculation.

subject: what happened?
q: I got a country on Merc III and before I could do anything it killed me, I think, and I can't get back on the game. Could I have been killed off that soon?
a: Yes, you could. All sanctuaries were removed at about 8:55 pm EDT on Thursday, the 10th of October. That's what happens to a country that sits there with its sanctuary gone.

subject: Questions regarding exploring sea sectors
q: In Empire, how do you build a multi-span bridge from one bridgehead, and how can you see the resources of a sea sector for oil drilling without bridging over it?
a: You can't. Bridges extend only one sector from a bridgehead, so every span must touch one. For oil, nav an oil rig onto the sector and the content shows next to the rig's mobility reading. No other way that I know of.

subject: food distribution
q: My Empire agribusinesses are stuck at 955 food and 18 mobility and can't ship out all their food. Also, how can I set a threshold in a warehouse so it won't distribute below a certain level?
a: Set a delivery threshold in the aggie, like dist f 0,0 (120) j, which moves food over 120 into a road. Distribute out of several roads to reach the warehouse, or just sell the surplus. Warehouse threshold? No real way. Read the manual.

subject: plague problems
q: Plague in our bsd-empire 1.1 game keeps killing 100% of the same sectors, which happen to be a player's warehouses. Is that a known bug or a feature?
a: Feature, not a bug. Too much iron sitting around raises the odds of plague, and a warehouse is exactly where iron piles up. Another player dug through info and plague and found it. Read the docs before blaming the code.

subject: Battletech: New Clan Sourcebooks
q: Has anyone seen the new FASA Battletech Clan sourcebooks, such as the Wolf Clan one? Are there reviews?
a: Nobody's reviewed it because it isn't out. Four Clan books are planned, but the Star Trek copyright mess shook FASA up and delayed everything. Only the Wolf Clan book is on distributors' lists, and it probably won't show until late summer.

subject: Gurps Fantasy world Yrth, MAPS ??
q: I can't find any maps of Yrth in my GURPS Fantasy books. Is my copy missing something, or do I have to pay for more?
a: You've got a messed-up copy, or you didn't look. There's supposed to be a fold-out glossy map of Yrth, about 16x11 inches, stuck to the inside back cover. If it's gone, the SJG address is in the book. Check the cover before whining.

subject: Sonic Booms? What damage if any!
q: I have a speedster who can hit mach one in a phase. What damage does the sonic boom do to the area, and how do you handle it in the game?
a: You buy it as a separate power, kid. Make it a continuous explosion linked to running, only going off at a certain speed, no range, 0 END, persistent, always on. Expect roughly 7-8d6 with a hole in the center, maybe double knockback. Expensive, but nothing is free.

subject: ok, what is it...
q: I keep seeing TORG discussed but still don't know what it stands for. What does it stand for?
a: Nothing. It's just a name, and the designers don't specify any expansion. It's the ultimate title, godship for the possibility raiders, and the name of the game. Not everything is an acronym, kid.

subject: CHAMPS: How not to get killed?
q: I'm joining a grim Champions game where killing is common. What powers and skills are best for not getting killed?
a: The three D's: damage resistance of any sort, desolid, and dexterity. Regeneration is nice, and Danger Sense and Luck help. Better yet, make a character that death enhances, like a tragic hero, because the GM has more points than you do.

subject: Elementals in GURPS
q: In GURPS, a summoned elemental must remain an hour unless dismissed, but if a second mage takes control of it with Control Elemental and tells it to leave, what happens? Can elementals be Banished?
a: My ruling: whoever controls the elemental can dismiss it, so the controller can send it away and the summoner can't. If the controller dies, it's free to do as it pleases. Banish probably works, since it sends back anything not native to the plane. I haven't got my books, so check them.

subject: more GURPS rule fudging
q: In GURPS, the pacifism/self-defense disadvantage: if a thug with a contract to kill my character shows up armed, do I have to wait for him to swing first? And do I have to stop fighting if he turns and runs?
a: He can draw his sword or prepare defenses, but must let Joe take the first swing. If Joe runs, he can try to capture him, but no deadly force unless Joe uses deadly force again trying to escape. Seems straightforward, what's the confusion?

subject: SHADOWRUN: Virtual Realities Question
q: In Shadowrun's Virtual Realities, the chart on page 42 says an attack program's size is rating squared times 2 in MP, but the examples say rating squared times 4. Which is it?
a: Go with the chart, rating squared times two. Charts get referenced and fixed more often, and the example boxes show no calculation, so errors slip past proofreaders. Another copy lists times two in both places. Check your printing.

subject: Cyberweapons
q: In Shadowrun, is it possible to have retractable spurs as well as cyberguns?
a: You bet. One character has both. The rules don't forbid it as far as anyone recalls, and rules are only guidelines anyway. Don't be the rules lawyer quoting page 72 at the GM.

subject: PALADIN
q: In Unearthed Arcana a Paladin gets the Cavalier abilities plus the Players' Handbook Paladin abilities. Cavaliers raise Strength, Dexterity and Constitution by percentile dice on leveling, and Paladins raise Charisma. Does a Paladin raise all four?
a: Yes. UA paladins, as a Cavalier subclass, get the bonus rolls for all four abilities. It was changed in 2nd Edition, where cavaliers are gone and raising abilities that way is not allowed. Too munchkin, even for TSR.

subject: Magical Deflected armor in GURPS
q: Is the cheap magical Deflect for armor and shields in GURPS unbalancing? It costs $100 per +1, and my dwarf has a Block of 16, so combats will take forever. Any suggestions?
a: Deflects shouldn't stack; two +1 Deflects give +1. Block values are supposed to be high anyway, so use the Feint maneuver, slams and tackles, and mages, since defenses don't help against magic. You can also make enchanting costlier by GM discretion. Quit whining.

subject: GURPS vs. Shadowrun: Which?
q: Should I get GURPS or Shadowrun? Is Shadowrun only a cyberpunk game, and is GURPS better if I want to play any kind of adventure?
a: Play both. But if you can only afford one, buy GURPS. Definitely. Absolutely. Don't waste time agonizing over it.

subject: AD&D Fantasy Battles - How?
q: What's the basic premise TSR uses to resolve mass fantasy combat in Battlesystem?
a: Each troop has a combat rate, damage rate and so on depending on how good it is. One counter can stand for one man, ten men or a thousand. If you've played Warhammer 40K, it's a lot like that. Go buy it.

subject: Another Map Question
q: Where can I get blank map paper with a Mercator or other projection printed on it, so I can put my maps on it? Art supply stores just gave me funny looks.
a: Try a drafting and engineering supply store, not art. Cartography is basically engineering, any idiot knows that. Or the geography section of a university bookstore. Don't hold your breath, though, there's probably not enough market for standard projection paper.

subject: Exasperating NPCs
q: Why do some modules feature an NPC who is rude and tries to make the PCs hate him, yet the adventure expects them to do as he says? Has anyone made such a scene work?
a: It's really a jab at an old relic of role-playing games. In real life you put up with a rude person who has something you want, usually vital information. Most PCs just blow such a person off, which is the problem.

subject: Openning (moyo? mayo?), middle phase, and endgame
q: I always do pretty well at the opening of a go game, but my play gets worse and worse after that. Why would that be?
a: Usually it means you don't understand the fuseki as well as you think. Only really big mistakes show up in the opening. Most fuseki mistakes show up later, when your game crumbles because of a weak foundation. Of course, this may not apply to you personally.

subject: "Hiraki" and "Gozuni" -- anyone know what they mean?
q: What do the Go terms "hiraki" and "gozuni" mean, and how do they relate to the game?
a: Hiraki is an extension on the third or fourth line along a side of the board. Gozuni is unknown to me, but it resembles guzumi, a move that is bad shape but a very good move nonetheless. Check your spelling.

subject: What is the result here (rules)
q: What do the Japanese rules say about this Go position with a bent four in the corner, triple ko and an outside ko?
a: If played out, it's a seki: neither side can capture the other, but neither has two eyes. Each position is judged independently, so the triple ko doesn't matter. You score it as a seki plus a dead group. Not hard.

subject: Another Go variant
q: What would happen if three players played Go with three colors? Has this been discussed?
a: Probably too hard to live on a standard board. Try a hexagonal board lined with triangles, six lines at each intersection. That might be interesting, though I doubt anyone seriously tried it.

subject: dumb beginners question
q: Why are there 180 black stones and 182 white stones in my Go set? I'd have expected more black, since black plays first and handicap stones are black.
a: White stones are often slightly smaller than the black ones for aesthetics, so the counts needn't match. Sets packaged for Chinese counting have more carefully controlled numbers, and many include a few spares. Sigh, it's not a conspiracy, just packaging.

subject: #dipping things in fountains
q: Dipping things in fountains with #dip hasn't done anything for me. Am I missing something?
a: Yes. Dipping an item once usually won't do the trick, so keep dipping it repeatedly. Sigh, read up before you waste a perfectly good fountain.

subject: credit card
q: How do I use a credit card in NetHack 3.0? A shopkeeper just said no cash, no credit, and a closed shop stayed closed.
a: Try applying the credit card to the door. As for real credit, the shop code has some provision for cards that hold credit, but don't expect it in 3.0; maybe 3.1. Read the source before whining.

subject: Help!!!!!!
q: In Hack, I get killed when I enter the vault and the Quantum Mechanic transports me. Is there a way to get away with the money and past the guards?
a: You don't die entering the vault. You die when you try to leave with the guard's money. Tunnel out or teleport out. Or polymorph the guard into something harmless like a jackal. Read up before whining, newbie.

subject: Possible Store bug???
q: In Hack, the storekeeper wanted 240 Zorkmids for food, but when I ate it without picking it up it only cost me 12. Bug or feature?
a: Feature. They say price tags aren't fixed. Go read the sources instead of whining.

subject: Getting to lower levels of hell.
q: In NetHack I can't get to the lower levels of Hell: no teleport scroll, no wishes left, and wands at 0 charges. I have teleportitis but even confused I only teleport within the level. How else can I go down?
a: Intrinsic teleport doesn't care about confusion. You need a scroll of teleportation, cursed or read while confused, or a level teleporter trap, plus teleport control, and no magic resistance for the trap. Also 0 charges isn't empty: keep zapping the wand for one last wish. Honestly.

subject: Unzipping
q: My PKUNZIP can't unzip the NetHack files. How were they zipped?
a: They're a self-extracting archive, so you don't need PKUNZIP at all. Rename the file to nethac.exe (any name, but the extension MUST be .exe) and run it as a program. It extracts itself. Try reading the directory listing before posting.

subject: How do you wake up a pet?
q: My cat is sound asleep on a sleeping gas trap. How can I wake her up?
a: A couple of slaps will do it, but unwield your weapon first. Throwing lightweight things like gems at the pet works once in a while. Applying a leash and dragging it off the trap works better. Basic dungeon manners.

subject: Unicorn (nh3.0p6)
q: My pet killed a unicorn in NetHack 3.0 and left a horn. I tried wielding it, dipping it and blessing it and nothing happened. What is it good for?
a: It's a decent weapon if you wield it. Apply it and it cures blindness, confusion, sickness and so on. Nothing happens when you dip it, genius.

subject: Snickersnee
q: What is the origin of the name Snickersnee? Does it come from a fantasy or science fiction novel, or folklore?
a: No, it's from High Culture. It's the executioner's sword belonging to Ko-Ko, the Lord High Executioner of Titipu, in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado. Go listen to some real music.

subject: doors, straight through
q: Why do doors in NetHack sometimes let you move through diagonally and sometimes not?
a: Is it a door or just an entryway? An open door can only be entered straight in. A doorless entryway, a gap in the wall, can be crossed any way you like. Read the docs, kid.

subject: What's so good about wizards?
q: Why do people like playing a wizard in NetHack? I usually go barbarian, since wizards are hard to keep alive. Can wizards tell whether an object is cursed?
a: Wizards start with a blessed +1 athame and a cloak of magic resistance, and they have to think through the early game. Some find barbarians too easy. They can't identify curses, though; priests can. And don't confuse wizard class with wizard mode, newbie.

subject: Commander Kenn ][
q: Any word on when Commander Keen II comes out? Hasn't it been long enough?
a: Apogee says it's been delayed because id wanted to add more features. It's supposed to have 256-color VGA and AdLib sound, $39 for all three episodes, with a new expected date of December or January. Be patient, kid.

subject: games like Fool's Errand
q: I loved Fool's Errand. Can anyone recommend similar games where puzzle-solving is the central theme, preferably on the PC?
a: Try Sokoban for the PC, published by Holobyte Spectrum, and there's a public version with C source in the games archive. You push cubes around a maze into place, with 50 levels plus an editor. Fiendish, though not an arcade game, so don't whine.

subject: BeyondZork
q: In BeyondZork, how do you get the jewel out of the idol?
a: Think about the mouth, it's like a kids' park ride. Anger the mother so she chases you and gets stuck on the ramp. You'll fall into the crocodile, so use the right wand from your medical gear on her. Carry the lamp, and skip the elven cloak. Figure the rest out yourself.

subject: Drakkhen: help
q: In Drakkhen, how do I cast spells like heal when I'm not in combat? It seems silly to start a fight just to heal.
a: Line up the caster and the recipient on a 45 degree diagonal, and the light heal spells will work outside combat. Otherwise it just drains your magic points. A walkthrough with a map is on anonymous ftp. Try thinking diagonally.

subject: Might & Magic 3 BUG?
q: In Might & Magic 3, Brother Delta in the Wildabar caverns sends me to Zeta, but gives no trinket and Zeta won't recognize me. Is this a bug? Also, do the Quatloo coins do anything?
a: Yes, it's a bug. New World said to ignore the quest, and the missing brother riddle is obvious once you see Zeta is the last brother. The Quatloo coins are about as useful as a Froboz of Misfortune, though there's a slot machine somewhere.

subject: Does Red Baron have a UFO in it?
q: In Red Baron I keep seeing a red and yellow graphic floating in the distance in the sky, and it jumps around and vanishes. Is it a UFO, a beacon, or a bug?
a: Seen it too. It looks exactly like bullet tracers coming at you, but it does nothing. Sounds like a minor bug to me. Don't lose sleep over a harmless glitch.

subject: Secret of the Silver Blades
q: In Secret of the Silver Blades, all my spells always work, dragon breath does max damage, poison always works and enemy spells always work. Anyone else seen this?
a: Check whether you set the Veteran difficulty. If so, your characters are just too awesome for it. Try the pre-generated characters that come with the game instead. Sigh.

subject: Shadow Gate
q: In Shadow Gate, how do I get past the big demon statue in the fiery abyss?
a: Operate the large book from the study room on the statue. If you've actually read the book, the solution isn't strange. As for the other talismans, nobody here knows either.

subject: Space Quest IV * Help! *
q: In Space Quest IV at the mall, I need a disguise to use the teller machine but the clothing store clerk won't help me. What do I do?
a: Try the ATM before you shop at the store, and you should have no problem. Do it in that order. Hint hotlines aren't always right.

subject: Spell Casting 101 (Sorcerers Get All The Girls, IBM)
q: In Spell Casting 101, I'm stuck on the Island of Lost Soles. A nymph says I have some of the soles and won't let me leave, and the mayor Blaise seems to be human. How do I solve it?
a: Read the menu back at the restaurant; something on it should look familiar. The mayor's no exception: he's a lost soul too, which is why his sign ends abruptly. You need a spell from back at SU. Try skonn; it doesn't work like the frat boys think.

subject: Spellcasting 101
q: In Spellcasting 101, I'm at the island of the gods and can't get in. I've tried throwing things and praying. Do I need another spell?
a: You need something from the Island of Lost Souls. Go get it instead of throwing things at the door. Sigh.

subject: Adlib Gold question and a WC II question
q: Should I bother with the original Wing Commander or go straight to Wing Commander II? Also, is the Adlib Gold available to buy yet?
a: Start with Wing Commander I; the early missions are much easier, and it'll keep you busy while Origin stabilizes WC II. Adlib Gold isn't out, and from what I hear it won't be for a couple of months.

subject: M.U.L.E., Lode Runner & Archon
q: Were MULE, Lode Runner and Archon released on the PC, and are they still available?
a: Lode Runner and Archon were definitely released for the IBM-PC by their original companies. Lode Runner should be in any software games store for about $7.50. Not sure about MULE, never heard of it, and I don't know if Archon is still around.

subject: HELP!
q: How do I protect myself from ghosts and wights draining my experience in Moria? Also why is there only one spell in the third magic book?
a: Carry dispel undead scrolls and restore life levels potions, use a Slay Undead weapon, or fight from a distance with fire. Third book has more than one spell; you just haven't reached the level to see them. Level up, newbie.

subject: How to raise stats?
q: How do you raise stats in Moria when gain stat potions are mostly at 1250 feet and my character can already wipe that level easily?
a: Go deeper. My 33rd level priest likes 1900 feet, and below that the monsters get a wee bit too powerful. Clone-and-kill grinding is for the bored. Try some actual danger.

subject: Hickory staff
q: I found a hickory staff in Moria that I couldn't use, so I sold it for 51 gp, and it was a staff of *Destruction*. Why wouldn't it work and what did I pass up?
a: If a staff or wand always says you fail to use it properly, identify it. It's always a good one, worth stacks of money. You'd need about level 30 to use Destruction competently. Always identify what you can't use, genius.

subject: Compiling umoria 5.1
q: I'm compiling umoria 5.1 and exceed my disk quota at link time, and I can't get more quota. Any suggestions?
a: Move everything to /tmp or /usr/tmp, which is what temporary directories are for. Make a subdirectory first, and expect it to get wiped within a few days. Copy the final executable home. Basic Unix, kid.

subject: Losing Dex with a +4 to Str. HA... Why!!??
q: I'm running umoria 5.2.1 on a PC and found a Holy Avenger weapon with +4 to Str. I thought HA sustains dexterity, but a Death Quasit bite still drained my Dex. Is that a bug?
a: Not a bug. An HA weapon sustains one stat, but which stat is random. One may sustain DEX, the next INT or something. Annoying, but that's the way it is. RTFM next time.

subject: God mode
q: In Moria's wizard mode, when creating an object, what do tval, subval, number, p1, and flags mean? And is the name the actual name or just what I want to call it?
a: Tval is the general group of the object, like sword or food, and subval is more specific. For the rest, read the wizardmode source. The name is just a label; it has nothing to do with the damage, so a Bastard Sword can be renamed anything. Sigh.

subject: questions, questions...
q: What is a Staff of Starlight good for that a Wand of Light isn't? I'm playing a priest.
a: It damages creatures that are sensitive to light, like giant bats. Read the item descriptions, will you.

subject: Secondary weapon
q: What is the use of a secondary weapon in Moria? I've reached 26th level without one.
a: It's convenience, mostly. You can carry another weapon without using pack space, and switch quickly with the X command instead of digging through inventory. Handy for swapping a defender for a holy avenger, or keeping a shovel for tunneling. Not essential, as you've noticed.

subject: Medusas
q: Does anyone know a good way to kill Medusas in Rogue? They keep getting me. How can I keep from getting confused by them?
a: A staff of cancellation, if it is a staff, will cancel a medusa's magic when you zap her. Good luck finding one. Otherwise, git gud.

subject: weapons compared
q: If I have a mace that's up to +4,+4, is that better than a +0,+0 two handed sword? How do they compare?
a: Higher numbers are better, period. The +4,+4 mace beats a +0,+0 anything. The first number is to-hit, the second is damage done. Not exactly rocket science.

subject: Treasure (was Re: "Masquerade")
q: Does anyone have information on the book Treasure by Dr. Crypton, similar to Masquerade? I pieced together some of the clues but got nowhere.
a: Time ran out, the golden horse was dug up, and the organizers wouldn't say where. Later two guys from the L.A. area claimed they solved it and dug at Tennessee Pass, where a note congratulated them. Their solution smelled fishy to me, but whatever.

subject: Words beginning with S ending with X
q: I know 7 words that begin with S and end with X. Can anyone do better? Sax isn't allowed.
a: Easy. Syntax, suffix, six, sex, suplex, simplex, surtax, plus sox, sioux, sphinx, salpinx, sardonyx. Obscure ones: scolex, silex, smilax, spadix. Seven, ha. Try harder.

subject: Back to the Future Question
q: In Back to the Future Part I, the Twin Pines Mall becomes the Lone Pine Mall after Marty returns from 1955. Why did the name change?
a: Marty runs over one of the two pine trees the farmer had managed to grow when he crashes in the barn in 1955. Kills a pine, and you get Lone Pine. Pay attention to the movie.

subject: Help With Super Mario World
q: Does anyone have a file on where the yellow, green and red switches are in Super Mario World?
a: Any idiot with a newsstand can find this. The November issue of GamePro lists where all the switch palaces are, plus some other tips. Go read it instead of begging the net for files.

subject: Budokan help needed!
q: How do you beat the guy with the Kusari Gama in Budokan for the Genesis, and the opponents after him?
a: Use the Bo, and save it for him by not using it on earlier opponents. Stay in a back stance and use the long-range attacks, like spin-forward-and-poke-in-the-eye, then back off. Do it fast as he closes in. Not rocket science.

subject: Need Help on Metal Gear
q: I need help on Metal Gear: where is the rocket launcher, where is card 7, how do I get through the maze zones, and when should I get captured?
a: Contact Jennifer in the rooms NE and E of Arnold and the items appear in the room north of her. You need the rocket launcher to kill Arnold, which gets you card 7. Mazes are W, W, N, W. Use the truck in building one to get captured. Do some work yourself.

subject: Crysalis question.
q: In Crystalis, what are those walls that spit fire and won't let me pass, and where is the ball of thunder hidden?
a: Go to Sharon first and buy everything you want there, like the battle shield and sacred shields. Then go to Goa, walk up to the fire-spitting metal thing and shoot it with the sword of thunder. A sad message follows that leads you to the ball of thunder. Read the hints.

subject: Electrocop (Lynx) help wanted
q: In Electrocop for the Lynx, is there a shorter way to level 5 than 1-2-3-4-11-12-8-6-5? Is there an EMP weapon on level 8 or 6? I lose everything by level 8 and arrive at level 5 naked.
a: Nope, no shorter route. Your memory's rusty but mine's fine: there should be an EMP or Shoulder Cannon on level 6, right near the door to level 5. It's enough to keep you alive, and you don't need as much weaponry as you think. Sigh.

subject: Another Ghouls & Ghosts Question
q: In Ghouls and Ghosts, what does it mean when the game tells me to put on the magic armor and open a box to find the goddess of magic? Will I keep the magic weapon after I die?
a: Second time through, wear the gold magic armor and open a chest. If you're lucky, the goddess shows up and hands you the magic weapon. Don't get excited though, it's weak against the slug, so grab the dagger first. Read the message properly next time.

subject: Zelda II Help
q: In Zelda II I've finished 5 of 6 palaces and found Old Kasuto, but can't find the 7th magic container or the magic key. What do I do next?
a: There's a magic container on maze island, maybe that's your missing one. The magic key is in the hidden town of New Kasuto, not Old Kasuto. Go to the end of the town and use Spell. The cross is, I think, in the 6th palace.

subject: Link (Zelda II) help needed
q: In Zelda II, The Adventures of Link, how do I kill my own shadow? I have max hearts, magic, sword and all spells.
a: Stand on the left side of the screen, kneel down and just keep stabbing. He runs into your sword and dies. Not exactly rocket science. The angel of death was the hard one.

subject: Checkered Flag
q: Is Checkered Flag on the Lynx really in stereo? I have a Lynx II and it sounds mono to me.
a: Stereo only kicks in once you're on the track, when somebody's passing you or you're passing them. Everywhere else the game is pretty much mono. Your headphones are probably fine. Read the fine print next time.

subject: EA Music/Rob Hubbard
q: Is the music in the Electronic Arts games for the Genesis written by Rob Hubbard?
a: Read the manual for the game in question, any idiot can do that. EA credits its staff there, unlike everyone else who makes you finish the game to see the credits. Not hard to find out.

subject: NES 'Galaga' (or equiv) info wanted
q: Is there an NES version of Galaga, and how does it play compared to the arcade game?
a: Yes, two of them. Bandai's US release is said to be an exact copy of the arcade game and goes for about $10 used by mail order. Galaga '90, around $20, is a faithful translation of Galaga '88. Honestly, it's not hard to find.

subject: R-type
q: The arcade R-Type claims to be a Nintendo game, so why is there an R-Type cartridge for the Sega Master System but not for the Nintendo?
a: R-Type is made by Irem, an independent software maker, not Nintendo. Nintendo is merely distributing the arcade game in the US. Look at the maker before theorizing, will you.

subject: Genesis Spider-Man Questions
q: Who are the villains in the Genesis Spider-Man game, and is it really 8 Mbits? The box doesn't say.
a: The bosses are proper Spider-Man rogues: Dr. Octopus, the Lizard, Electro, the Sandman, the Hobgoblin and Venom, all led by the Kingpin. As for size, the cart never claims 8 meg, and one review reckoned it was only 2 megabits. If it were 8, they'd be shouting it.

subject: Strider (Stryder?)
q: How do I get past the part in the last level of Strider where gravity reverses and I keep falling in the hole or getting hit by missiles and spikes?
a: When gravity switches, wait and kill the droids, then jump over and kill the wall-walker. Run down the upside-down hill, jump at the end and swing your sword at the stuff below you. Keep jumping right and up to the ceiling. Reflexes, kid.

subject: CW for pilots
q: Do pilots need to know Morse code? Station identifiers used to be sent in Morse.
a: No civil requirement exists to know Morse as a pilot. Many VOR stations have voice identifiers, but ILS nav-aids only send three or four character Morse idents. The dot-dash pattern is printed on the chart, though a rudimentary knowledge is handy. Sigh.

subject: ICOM IC-735
q: Has anyone used the ICOM IC-735? I want a shortwave transceiver and am also considering the FT-757 or TS-440.
a: Plenty of people like the IC-735. It has a great receiver, clean transmitter, intuitive controls, and it's small enough for mobile or portable use without cramped controls. Transverter jacks are still there, with optional narrow filters. Short of megabuck rigs you won't do better.

subject: RTTY and/or Packet with a TS-440s
q: How do I hook a Kenwood TS-440s to a PK-232 or similar TNC for RTTY and packet? Do I use the AFSK ports or ACC-2, and do I mute the mike?
a: Use ACC2 and the mike mute lead too, driving PTT and mike mute from the PK-232 PTT output through 2 switching diodes. The 440 wants more audio, so turn mic gain up to about 50%. Mind the 13-pin DIN plastic; it melts. Use less heat.

subject: (none)
q: What exactly is a "techie" or "ultra-techie" in ham radio? Is it someone who builds superhets, strings computers together, or designs antennas?
a: A techie is someone more interested in the technical side of radio than in operating. A builder, not a DXer, who likes novel circuits or software and operates mostly to try out ideas. An ultra-techie is so far gone he won't even talk to the techies. Sigh, it's not hard.

subject: kam wefax mode
q: How can I write a Mac II program to display fax and wefax from a Kantronics KAM or AEA PK-232? Where's the documentation on how the TNC sends pixel data over the serial port?
a: On the PK232 the only real way is host mode, so cough up about $20 for the AEA tech reference manual. And the fax is fake: the TNC just returns bytes of on/off pixels, no gray scale, no color. FF00FF means 16 on, 16 off, 16 on. Don't expect miracles.

subject: Packet software for 386/Unix?
q: Is there any packet radio software available for Sys-V Unix?
a: Yes. There's a Sys-V version of KA9Q's net program, plus a PBBS written for it. Both are on vax.cs.pitt.edu. Go fetch them.

subject: Where can I get KA9Q for IBM PC Compatible ??
q: Where can I get the KA9Q software package for an IBM PC compatible?
a: It's on plenty of machines. Try the pub/ka9q directory on thumper.bellcore.com, tomcat.gsfc.nasa.gov, hpcsos.col.hp.com, or ucsd.edu. Honestly, this comes up every week; try anonymous ftp before asking the whole net.

subject: Token-ring? Ethernet? Why not use the parallel-port?
q: Why not use the parallel printer port instead of slow RS232 to connect a computer to a TNC?
a: Because the PC can't feed it fast. My 4.77 MHz laptop manages only 10-20 Kbytes/sec with hand-optimized assembly, since x86 I/O is a pain. Many printer ports aren't bidirectional either. That beats RS232 but is nothing next to DMA like a LAN or SCSI.

subject: Another engine problem!
q: My Magnum 25 engine splutters and takes several seconds to reach full power when I open the throttle from idle. It has an air bleed adjuster I haven't touched. How should I fix it?
a: You're running rich. Lean out the idle setting, and check that the air bleed hole is clear. Set the screw end to cover about half the hole, and adjust 1/4 to 1/2 turn. Turning it out leans, in is richer. Opposite of the needle valve, naturally.

subject: Gentle Lady construction
q: The plans for the Gentle Lady use the covering as the hinge for the elevator and rudder instead of real hinges. Is that secure enough, or should hinges be added?
a: The covering hinges work great. I'd go with them over nylon hinges on this plane, so quit fretting and build it.

subject: New Paul McCartney album?
q: I saw a new Paul McCartney album listed for May 21st. Is it a new album, what's the title, and is it the same band?
a: It's called "Unplugged" and mostly has the same cast. It has some old Beatles, some McCartney, including the first song he ever wrote. The poster read that a couple of weeks back, so don't quote me.

subject: DC + G ??
q: A friend got a CD player for his TurboGrafx-16 that can show the graphics from CD+G discs. Does anybody have a list of discs that have graphics encoded?
a: Not a full list, but Information Society's first CD was a CD+G. So were Lou Reed's New York and Fleetwood Mac's Behind the Mask. Go dig up the rest yourself, I'm not your discography.

subject: Silly (was Re: Double-Sided CD's Do Exist!)
q: Can a CD be made as a picture-disc like a record, say by putting metallic dyes on the surface before stamping in the pits?
a: Picture CDs exist, but not like picture-disc records. They just paint the whole label side. Look at the Beatles' White Album CD, all white, or an Australian import with the cover painted on. Nobody is printing pictures into the data side.

subject: Tubes CD ordering info needed
q: Can anyone give me the order numbers for the Tubes CDs T.R.A.S.H. and Young and Rich on A&M? Stores want an order number. Also, has Love Bomb come out on CD yet?
a: T.R.A.S.H. is A&M 3244.A and Young and Rich is A&M 3222.A. Nobody turned up Love Bomb in the catalogue. Stores carry the Schwann catalogue, which lists all this, so ask them to look it up instead of making them beg you for numbers.

subject: Hithhiker's Guide, Firesign Theater ?
q: Has Firesign Theater's How Can You Be In Two Places At Once been released on CD?
a: Yes. Mobile Fidelity put it out as MFCD 834, and Don't Crush That Dwarf is MFCD 880. I believe the Bozos album is also out, and Rhino has newer ones. Check a catalog once in a while.

subject: CD pressing plants
q: How easy or expensive is it to have CDs pressed? What minimum order is needed, and do the plants print the artwork?
a: Easy enough. Give them a Sony 1630 format tape and timing paperwork. Roughly $2500 for 1000 CDs with the most basic labeling, and you box them yourself. Check ads in Electronic Musician magazine.

subject: Lou Reed recomendations?
q: I liked the Lou Reed cut Last Great American Whale from the Greenpeace CD set. Which of his albums would you recommend for similar songs?
a: Get NEW YORK, the album that song comes from. Many cuts are similar, and it's one of the greatest albums of the 1980s. If you also want Reed and Cale, try Songs For 'Drella, the Warhol tribute. Do your homework next time.

subject: Queen finally out?
q: I've been looking for Queen's 'A Night at the Opera' and 'A Day at the Races' on CD and just found them as imports for about $18. Is that a normal price, and will they be released domestically?
a: Eighteen bucks is standard. Nearly the whole Queen catalog has been around as European imports for 3+ years, and I've never seen one under $17. Do some legwork and you'll find any title, if you're willing to shell out the big bucks.

subject: CD rot
q: I've heard that CDs lose quality over time because the molecules move around and the pits fill in. Has anyone heard this?
a: Sigh. Everything decays eventually; thermodynamics is the law. The real question is how long. My oldest CDs are close to 10 years old with no detectable decay, and I expect them to outlast my money's worth. Stop worrying.

subject: Art Zoyd
q: Is any Art Zoyd available on CD?
a: Yes, mostly French imports. Titles around include Le Mariage du Ciel et de l'Enfer, the Les Espaces Inquiets/Phase IV/Archives II double CD, Berlin, and Nosferatu. Wayside's catalog lists several, singles around $18-20 and the double about $36. Do some digging yourself.

subject: Current BMG offer - was Re: BMG CD Catalog
q: Isn't the BMG offer of buy one, get two free just paying full price for three CDs?
a: Wrong. Somebody took the offer and paid US $21.64, shipping and handling included, for one full-price CD plus two free ones. That's nowhere near three CDs at full price. Do the arithmetic before you go accusing people of pulling a fast one.

subject: Holes in CDs
q: Some of my CDs that my player has trouble with have lots of little pinholes in the aluminum layer when held up to the light. Is that normal?
a: Pinholes aren't unusual, most discs have one or two. The constellation-sized ones turn up on CD club pressings, especially discs made under license. Whether your player chokes depends on its error correction and tracking, so a cheap player will gripe. Buy a better one.

subject: Mike Nesmith CD's
q: What Mike Nesmith recordings are available on CD, and where can I get them?
a: Just one that anyone knows of, a compilation called The Newer Stuff on Rhino, R2 70168. Any decently stocked store should have it. His real albums aren't out on CD, since there's no market. Sigh.

subject: 2001 CD? 2010 CD?
q: What is the Khachaturian piece used in 2001 for Discovery's approach to Jupiter? Is the 2010 soundtrack available?
a: It's from Khachaturian's Gayne ballet suite, heard as Bowman jogs around the centrifuge in the Discovery sequence. I believe the performance was Rozdanevski's on Deutsche Grammophon. Check your own record shelf for the rest.

subject: info request on "The The"
q: What's happened to "The The"? Three great albums and that's it. Have they split?
a: Don't forget those three albums spanned something like seven to ten years. Each one is a product of one man's personality, so it takes him a while to build up material. Meanwhile, hunt down his solo album Burning Blue Soul, reissued by 4AD. Patience, kid.

subject: Operatic Duets
q: It's ensemble week in masterclass and I need lovely, beautiful duets for soprano or mezzo-soprano and baritone, from Broadway or opera. Any suggestions?
a: Mozart is the obvious place to look: La ci darem la mano from Don Giovanni, Se a casa madama and Crudel, perche fin'ora from Figaro, and Bei Maennern from The Magic Flute. On the Broadway side, All I Ask of You and the Mountain Duet from Chess. Sigh, you could've opened a score.

subject: cockroaches and allan sherman
q: Where can I find the lyrics to Allan Sherman's 'The Cockroach that Ate Cincinnati', and which Sherman song uses the tune 'Conspiracy'?
a: The cockroach song is on Dr. Demento's Delights. For the tune, I can only guess it was 'The Continental', which became 'The Painless Dentist' on My Name Is Allan. Otherwise I'm stumped, and so are you.

subject: Exetensial blues edited?
q: Why was the line about dreaming the impossible dream edited out of the Existential Blues song on Dr. Demento?
a: As I understand it, copyright problems forced the line's removal for airplay. It was already cut back in 1987. Yes, it's annoying. Lawyers ruin everything.

subject: what's this song?
q: What's the name of the song that goes "1-2-3 shake your body", and who does it?
a: Probably "Use It Up and Wear It Out". One version is by Pat and Mick, but it's surely a redo of the 1980 song of the same title by Odyssey, the Going Back to My Roots people. Kids these days and their covers.

subject: pogues
q: Can anyone recommend some good Irish bands, other than the Pogues?
a: Scottish will do, you philistine. Try Capercaillie, the Bothy Band, De Dannan, Silly Wizard, the Tannahill Weavers, and anything with Phil Cunningham. Green Linnet Records sells them all and their catalog has accurate descriptions.

subject: Where are all the blokes?
q: I realize my music collection is mostly women artists. Can anyone suggest some male solo artists in the rec.music.gaffa vein?
a: Try Adrian Belew, Warren Zevon, Lou Reed, Brian Ferry, They Might Be Giants, Johnny Clegg, Michael Hedges, Dave Stewart. Prince too, though you can forget him. Honestly, you needed the net for this?

subject: Blizzards of Glitter!!!
q: Is there a full version of the video with the long shot of the tree-lined road shown on VH1, and are there other videos floating around?
