a: It's not hard, and the limit was about $7500 a year. The catch is that the forms use last year's 1040, so if you earned a lot working, the computer may disqualify you. See an FA rep and prove your income dropped. Read the fine print, kid.

subject: Studying in Maryland
q: Can my girlfriend take a few individual courses at a US university near Washington, like the University of Maryland, without paying the full fee?
a: Yes. Stay part-time, up to 8 credits or about two courses, and you pay by the credit, roughly $150 each plus maybe $50-100 in misc. fees. Maryland is five minutes from Goddard. Call the university and ask, it's not hard.

subject: GRE and Applying to Grad School
q: I'm taking the GRE in early February but many grad schools have a Feb 1 application deadline. Do the scores have to be in by then?
a: Basically yes, though it depends on the school. Most want December as the last date, and schools don't get scores for a month or so. Call the department and ask their official policy; otherwise take the December test. Should have planned ahead.

subject: Beltaine and Samhaine pronounced?
q: How are the Gaelic words Beltaine and Samhain pronounced? I've seen them said at least ten different ways.
a: Spell them Bealtaine and Samhain. In Irish they come out roughly "bell-tah-nuh" and "sow-in", with sow like the pig, not what you do with oats. Scots Gaelic varies a bit. Ten different ways, honestly, people should learn the language.

subject: Celtic art
q: I'm planning to make celtic-design metal jewellery as a hobby. I already have Celtic Art, Celtic Knotwork and the Book of Kells. Any other reference books on celtic art for ideas and guides?
a: Try Early Medieval Designs From Britain by Eva Wilson, Dover Publications, 1987. Each design is presented separately so you can photocopy it, and the source of each one is listed. Hardly obscure, you know.

subject: Another question for celtics (was: Re: 3 boats down from the candy)
q: What is a mogadon? My dictionaries tell me nothing. Is it a Scottish expression?
a: It's a brand of sleeping pill or tranquiliser, like valium. Usually prescribed to stressed housewives, and it screws you up if taken for long. Not Scottish slang, so quit blaming the dictionaries.

subject: Irish vs. Gaelic
q: What is the difference between Irish and Gaelic? Are the language tapes labelled Gaeilge the same thing as Gaelic?
a: Gaelic is the generic name for the group covering Irish, Scottish Gaelic and Manx. Gaeilge is just Irish, so it's the same thing as Irish. A bare "Gaelic" could mean the Scottish variety. Check what you're buying, for pity's sake.

subject: (was: Who's out there?) who has netnews access ?
q: Does having access to the network (ARPA, BITNET and so on) guarantee you have access to netnews? Some machines seem to be on the net but never show up in netnews.
a: No, it doesn't. A machine can be on the net and simply not have the netnews software installed. Plenty of non-UNIX sites, like VMS boxes, don't run it. Net access and netnews are different things, obviously.

subject: Radio Broadcasting from HK
q: Has anybody in the midwest been able to pick up broadcasts from Hong Kong on a shortwave radio? What frequencies and times should I try?
a: Sigh. As far as anyone here knows, Hong Kong has no shortwave broadcasts to speak of. You can pull in Radio Beijing and Radio Free China from Taipei, around 9.3 MHz near 11 pm Eastern. Fiddle with the dial like everybody else.

subject: trip to New York
q: What should I know about crime and safety before visiting New York City?
a: Be street-smart. Don't look like a stranger or flash money. If you drive, pay for guarded parking, which is cheaper than a broken window or a stolen car, and leave nothing in the car, not even a shopping bag. Out-of-state cars get vandalized. Obvious, really.

subject: Dansk Rugbrod in the US
q: Does anyone know where in the U.S., preferably on the east coast, I can buy Danish rugbrod?
a: Try the larger food shops in New York City, like Zabars. They carry Iversen rugbroed, presliced and wrapped in plastic. Tastes decent, but it's not fresh-baked, so don't whine that it isn't Copenhagen.

subject: Jeg er ikke noget berliner!
q: Is 'Berliner' an Americanism, and is the term used in the U.S. or Canada for a jelly doughnut, or does it connect to Berlin?
a: Never heard it used in North America. It's the German word for a jelly-filled roll, seen in bakeries in Northern Germany. Some Americans say 'bismarck' for a filled doughnut. Sigh, this old Kennedy joke gets nitpicked to death.

subject: Finnish language and history.
q: Is Finnish spelling really phonetic, and are there Finnish dialects? How close is Finnish to the other Finno-Ugric languages?
a: Spelling really is phonetic, with exceptions, though you pay with about 15 noun suffixes. Dialects exist, mostly different words and tone, and they're fading thanks to TV and radio. Hungarian is as far off as English from German or French, but Estonian and Karelian are quite close.

subject: Wanted: Tech info to build Pal : Ntsc converter box
q: Where can I find technical info to build a PAL to NTSC converter box?
a: Forget it, it's only of theoretical interest. PAL framing is 50 Hz, 625 lines, and no commercial TV set shows that with NTSC color. Converting the framing takes a scanconverter with at least 1.5 MB of RAM and a fast signal processor, around $20,000 ready-made.

subject: Buddha's names
q: Can somebody post the names used for Buddha and the bodhisattvas, with their meanings? What does Tathagata mean?
a: Tathagata means the One Gone Thus, or one who has come from or returned to thusness. That is, passed beyond normal conceptuality and the afflictions and obstructions into complete enlightenment. Manjusri is the embodiment of wisdom, and a bodhisattva as I recall.

subject: Zen Buddhism (Is a teacher necessary?)
q: Is a teacher really necessary to practice Zen? Does a person have to be involved with a teacher or a group to consider themselves a Zen Buddhist?
a: No teacher is needed to practice Zen, though you may need one to learn how to practice. Joining a group isn't the test either. If your zen never shows up in daily life, you merely study about it. Sigh, stop worrying about labels and just practice.

subject: Byelorussia Help
q: Where is the town of Chumsk (Xhumsk?) in Byelorussia?
a: It's probably spelled Chomsk. Look west of Pinsk and south of Kartuz-Bereza. Next time, spell the place right before asking the whole net, and get a decent map.

subject: trial net fragmentation
q: Is the trial.* test hierarchy dead everywhere, or just here? I see few messages in trial.test and none in trial.rec.metalworking.
a: It's not just you. trial.* has generated hardly any traffic yet. The structure is appearing, but the groups haven't reached enough sites to produce postings, and metalworking isn't popular among news readers. Be patient.

subject: UNIX PC, 110V-> 220 and "Norwegian" UNIX verion. (questions)
q: Does anybody know if there are adaptors converting from 110V to 220V for computers, since I'm taking my UNIX PC to Norway?
a: Not an expert, but if Norway runs the same 60 Hz, just buy a transformer with a 2:1 winding ratio that's hefty enough for the wattage your machine draws. Check your frequency first, genius.

subject: System 5 socket driver (uipc)
q: Has anyone gotten the System V uipc socket driver for the Unix PC working, with BSD-style socket programs or DNET?
a: Don't I wish. DNET uses raw mode, and this package doesn't support raw mode, or at least it didn't last time I checked. So no, not with DNET. Don't hold your breath.

subject: "anon ftp" -- just how does this work, anyway?
q: How does anonymous ftp work? I can ftp to a site but it wants a login, and anon, ftp and anonymous don't work. Is there a standard login?
a: Login is ftp, password is ftp. That easy. Sigh, and you thought it was a big joke on Unix types.

subject: Why is my 2nd ksh (only) owned by sys?
q: On my 3B1, why is my second ksh window always owned by sys instead of the usual user?
a: Your links between /dev/syscon, systty and window are broken. They should all be links to the same device as the window driver. Fix it by changing /etc/rc to delete syscon and systty and relink them to /dev/window at boot. Wonderful feature, that.
